generated_text: Honestly, I’m shattered. Little Leo kept me up half the night. Teething, I think. Or just being a tiny human with no concept of sleep. Oh, bless him. They're exhausting at this age, aren't they? Remember when Maisie was like that? I lived on coffee and dry shampoo for about six months. I’m already mainlining the coffee. You’d think having done it with the older two would prepare you, but it doesn’t, does it? It genuinely gets  harder . Anyway, enough about my sleep deprivation. Are you still on for Saturday? That new Italian place, Bella Notte? Yes! I’ve booked a table for 8. It’ll be good to actually get out, won’t it? Just… us. Without tiny hands grabbing at everything. Absolutely. I’m looking forward to it. Ben’s promised to handle bedtime, so hopefully, I won’t fall asleep face-first in my pasta. Speaking of which, what’s Mark up to these days? I haven't spoken to him properly in ages. He’s… well, he’s good. Really busy at work, apparently. They're launching a new project, something to do with renewable energy. He’s been travelling a bit, too. Last week he was in Scotland. Oh, that sounds interesting. He always was a clever one. Still, it's a shame he doesn’t get to see the kids as much as he’d like. Ethan was asking about him the other day. I know. He feels it, you know? He feels guilty. He sends them little gifts and FaceTimes, but it’s not the same. He was saying he’s trying to block out a week in November to come home properly - help with Freya’s birthday. Oh, that's lovely! What are we thinking for Freya’s birthday then? She’s turning eight, isn't she? A proper little lady now. Eight! I can’t believe it. She wants a Harry Potter themed party, apparently. A full-on Hogwarts experience. Oh, wow. That’s ambitious! You’ll have to get your wand-making skills up to scratch. I can maybe help with decorations? I've been doing a bit of freelance design work, so I’m fairly handy with that sort of thing. It's good money, though honestly, it's been a bit slow lately. Trying to drum up new clients is exhausting. That’s fantastic, honestly.

Honestly, the hassle of travelling in the EU now is just… exhausting. Remember when you could just  go ? Like, spontaneous weekend in Amsterdam? Those days are gone. Tell me about it. I’m supposed to be presenting at a conference in Berlin in October, and even just thinking about the extra admin is giving me a headache. It's not the cost, exactly, though that’s creeping up too, it's the time. The queuing. The forms. Exactly! The forms! I went to Barcelona with my sister in the summer, and she’d meticulously prepped everything – passport scanned, visa stuff checked, even printed out a load of stuff just in case. She’s a planner, that one. Still took us ages to get through passport control. It’s changed the whole vibe, hasn't it? It used to be so… casual. I did a backpacking trip around Europe after uni. Literally just turned up at train stations, booked hostels, figured it out as I went. Wouldn't even  think  of doing that now. No way! I remember vaguely hearing stories like that. Sounds idyllic. I did a year abroad in Paris, pre-Brexit, and it was bliss. Borderless, basically. We’d hop on a train to Brussels for the day just because we felt like it. Proper freedom. I tried to do a similar thing last year, got as far as Calais and then just… gave up. The queues at the ferry port were insane. Ended up driving all the way round to Dunkirk and getting the Eurotunnel. Cost me a fortune in petrol. Oh, Dunkirk! That’s a detour and a half. I’ve heard stories about people getting stuck in massive traffic jams. What’s the point of a quick getaway if you spend half the time sitting in a car? It’s ridiculous. And it’s not just the borders, is it? It’s the little things. Getting your phone to work, insurance, even just knowing what the rules are about driving in each country. It all adds up. My mate Liam went to Italy last month. Apparently, he got a parking ticket because he didn’t realise he had to display a little disc in his windscreen showing the time. Total tourist trap. He was fuming. Classic! They always get you with those little things. The ZTL zones in Italy are another nightmare. Drive into one accidentally and you’re looking at a huge fine.

Right, so after dinner, what are we thinking for dessert? I was thinking maybe those little chocolate pots I got from the supermarket? Or would you two prefer ice cream? Chocolate pots! Chocolate pots! Please, Mummy! Ice cream has sprinkles. Sprinkles are better than chocolate. Hmm, a very strong argument, sprinkles  are  excellent. But the chocolate pots are really rich and gooey. We could do both? A small ice cream  with  sprinkles and a little chocolate pot? Yes! Yes! That's the best! Fine. But I get extra sprinkles. Deal. Extra sprinkles for you. Now, speaking of wanting more… are we doing Monopoly again tonight? YES! I want to be the dog! No,  I  want to be the dog! You were the dog last time! Okay, okay, calm down. We can roll a dice to see who gets the dog? And maybe we need to tweak the rules a bit after last time... you two were  very  good at bankrupting me. Because you landed on my hotels! A lot! And you didn’t buy enough houses! That’s why! Okay, fair enough. Maybe I was a bit slow on the property acquisition. It’s a good lesson in economics, though, isn't it? Understanding supply and demand, managing your resources… It’s about getting all the money! And making everyone else poor! Well, yes, ultimately. But it's about how you get there. And learning not to land on Park Lane with a hotel on it, obviously. That's a very expensive mistake. Mummy always lands on Park Lane! It's not fair! It’s just bad luck! Honestly. It’s all down to the dice. But we can play a slightly shorter game tonight, maybe. Before bedtime gets too close. And maybe… maybe someone will be feeling generous with their hotels. A girl can dream… Do you want me to continue the conversation, or perhaps change the direction it's going in? Let me know! Do those people have a look have they managed to change the value of their portfolio. It's just such a mess with this. It's is it his brother or his uncle's. Brothers broker. Oh. The thing is he's got so much money tied up in with him he can't. Pull it out easily. Exactly the problem. Exactly right. So he's looking at the broker looking for insight trying to understand what this means.

Honestly, the traffic was mental getting out of Durham. I thought we’d be stuck there forever. Like,  forever . Yeah, it was pretty bad. I checked the motorway cameras before we left, but it didn’t look  that  bad then. Just a bit of congestion around the A1 junction, you know? A bit of congestion? That was an understatement. It was a solid line of red. Honestly, makes you wonder why people even bother driving when it’s like that. Well, trains aren’t exactly reliable either, are they? Remember that time we tried to get back from Edinburgh and were delayed for six hours? Don't even  mention  Edinburgh. I nearly lost the will to live in that station. At least in the car, you've got control, even if you’re not moving. You can blast the music and… well, complain. True. Although, my control was mostly limited to muttering about the horrifying navigation choices you were making. Hey! I was following the sat nav! It told me to go down that tiny little lane. The one that was clearly marked “Unsuitable for HGVs”? And barely wide enough for your little Fiat? It said it was the fastest route! It didn’t mention anything about agricultural vehicles. Honestly, that was terrifying. I thought we were going to end up in a field full of cows. You and a field of cows. That would have been a story. Seriously though, maybe next time we’ll stick to sticking to the main roads, even if it adds an extra twenty minutes. My blood pressure can’t handle those back lanes. Fine, fine. You’re the engineer, you know about routes and stuff. Just promise me we're not going near any farms. I’ve had enough adventure for one day. Are we stopping for food soon? I'm absolutely starving. All this talk of traffic and near-death experiences has worked up an appetite. I was thinking we could grab something at that service station just after Peterborough. They do a pretty decent panini, I think. And coffee, obviously. A lot of coffee. After that drive. Panini sounds good. And yes, definitely coffee. A  large  coffee. Thanks for driving, by the way. I would have probably ended up driving into a ditch by now. No problem. That's what boyfriends are for. Though you should really learn to navigate better. Oh, hush you.

Right, well, that's the rhubarb crumble in the oven. Should be alright. Bit of ginger in it this time, you know, just to give it a little…zing. Ginger, eh? Never been a huge fan, myself. Still, won't say no to a bit of crumble. More cream, I hope? Of course, more cream. It wouldn’t  be  crumble without a mountain of cream. Honestly, you two. You’d think I wasn’t feeding you properly. Now, now, Elsie. We appreciate it, we really do. It’s just…well, you know how we are. A bit of a sweet tooth. Did you manage to get through to the doctor’s surgery this morning? I’ve been meaning to ask. Eventually. Took me nearly an hour on hold, honestly. All for a blooming appointment. And then they said the earliest they could fit me in was three weeks time! Three weeks! What’s the point of having a National Health Service if you can’t even get to see a doctor when you need to? Sounds about right. It’s all gone downhill, hasn’t it? Remember Doctor Henderson? Always had time for everyone. Never rushed you. You could walk in with a sniffle and come out feeling like a new man. He was a good sort. Knew everyone in the village. Now, they just seem to rotate doctors every few months. Barely remember your name, let alone your medical history. This new one sounded awfully young. All bright and breezy. No sense of…well, gravity, if you know what I mean. It's the modern world. Everything’s fast-paced. No time for a proper chat anymore. Speaking of which, did you hear back from that chap about the shed? The one who does the repairs? He said he’d pop round Tuesday. Said he’s a bit busy with garden fences at the moment, but Tuesday should be good. It’s the felt that’s gone, you know. Leaking like a sieve when it rains. Good. It’s driving me mad. Everything in the shed’s getting damp. Honestly, you'd think we lived in a rainforest sometimes. Well, we are fairly close to the coast, aren't we? Always a bit of a sea breeze. Oh, I saw young Timothy from next door earlier. He's got himself a motorbike now, can you believe it? A proper roaring machine.

Right, so I was thinking, for the new moisturiser, we absolutely  have  to lean into the hyaluronic acid thing. Everyone’s obsessed with it. It's like the gold standard now, isn't it? Yeah, definitely. But everyone's using it. It's almost…vanilla. How do we make  ours  stand out? I’m still massively hesitant about the packaging. That frosted glass just feels…expensive. Which is good, obviously, but it bumps the unit cost up so much. I get you. We could look at a slightly thinner glass? Or maybe a different shape? I was looking at some square bottles, they feel a bit more modern. And we definitely need a nice label. I've been watching loads of YouTube videos on label design. It’s a minefield. Label design is the worst. I spent, honestly, four hours yesterday trying to choose a font! Four hours! And I ended up going back to one I originally dismissed. It's ridiculous. Did you see Sarah at "Blooming Botanicals" on Instagram? She's doing really well. I think she's just repurposing stuff she finds, though. So, less focus on production cost, more focus on the "aesthetic." Yeah, I’ve seen her. Her photos are  amazing . But it doesn't feel…authentic, does it? Like, are the products actually that good, or is it all filters and pretty pictures? I want Honest Skincare to be genuinely good  and  look good. I’m worried about the rosehip oil sourcing, actually. I really want it to be ethically sourced, but it's adding a significant cost. Okay, so ethically sourced versus price point. That’s the perennial small business struggle, isn’t it? Have you looked into suppliers in Bulgaria? I read an article saying they’re a huge producer, and the practices are generally pretty good. Might be cheaper than Chile, which is where we were initially looking. That’s a good shout. I'll do some digging. Speaking of digging… Gran keeps sending me links to weird online marketplaces. She found one selling pre-owned beauty equipment! She thinks it’s a brilliant idea. Oh, bless her. She’s amazing. But no, definitely not. Imagine the hygiene issues! We're trying to build a reputation for quality and trustworthiness. Pre-owned mixing vats are not the way forward. Exactly! Anyway, what about the market next Saturday? Are we definitely on for a stall?

Honestly, the state of things. Did you see about that MP, the one with the second home allowance? Absolutely unbelievable. Oh, don't get me started. It’s the same old story, isn’t it? They think they're above it all. Makes your blood boil. It really does. You work hard all your life, trying to do the right thing, and then you read about this… it’s just insulting. Precisely. And the excuses they come up with! Honestly. I saw Jeremy Vine dissecting it on the telly, and even he was struggling to find any justification. Jeremy Vine is good for that, isn’t he? Doesn’t pull any punches. Anyway, enough about all that doom and gloom. How are things with you? Still enjoying retirement? Oh, immensely. Though it does feel a bit odd, not having the structure of the school year, you know? I miss the kids sometimes, honestly. Not the paperwork, thankfully! I can imagine. It must be a big adjustment. You always were a natural with them though. Remember little Timmy Higgins? The one who used to insist on wearing a dinosaur costume to school? Oh, Timmy! How could I forget? He was a character. He used to try and convince me T-Rex could write poetry. Absolutely insistent. Oh, that's wonderful. You’ve got such patience. I always thought I’d have struggled with that. It was part of the job, wasn't it? Trying to negotiate with tiny humans. Though, honestly, sometimes dealing with parents was harder. Oh, don’t even mention the parents! That was often a minefield. I had one mother who insisted her son was a genius, despite him struggling to tie his shoelaces. Oh dear. They’re all at it, aren't they? It’s all about them, isn’t it? Not the child. Speaking of challenges… how’s your garden doing? Last time I was round, it was looking rather… enthusiastic. Enthusiastic is one word for it! It’s gone absolutely wild. I’m losing the battle, I think. The bindweed is winning. I spend hours out there weeding and it just laughs at me. You should get Derek’s son around. He's a landscaper now, apparently. Very good, apparently. Does all sorts. Oh, that’s a good idea. I must remember to ask you for his number. Maybe he can tame the jungle I’ve created.

Honestly, the amount of food we had at Christmas was ridiculous. My mum just…keeps adding things. Like, “Oh, you haven’t had enough Brussel sprouts!” Sounds about right. My mother-in-law is the same. It’s a competition to see who can produce the most edible mass. It’s always the same, isn’t it? End up with enough food to feed a small army, and then spend Boxing Day eating leftovers for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. I think we did okay. We kept it fairly streamlined. Though my aunt tried to send us a whole smoked salmon. A  whole  one. No way! What did you do? I politely explained that our fridge is, shall we say, not salmon-sized. She wasn’t thrilled, but she understood. Mostly. Good save! It's freezing out though, isn't it? I swear the heating hasn’t been working properly all week. It’s just…lukewarm. Tell me about it. I had to wear a hat while working today. A hat! In my own office. You should complain! Landlords are legally obliged to make sure the heating works. I’ve emailed. Several times. They just keep saying they’re “looking into it.” It's the standard response. I’m starting to suspect they just enjoy watching us shiver. Reminds me of my grandad. Never fixed anything. Said it built character. Honestly, the man could barely change a lightbulb. Though he  did  have an impressive collection of tools, all perfectly organised and never used. That’s classic! My dad’s the same. He has a shed full of things he's “meaning to get around to.” It’s a museum of good intentions. I actually managed to fix the bathroom tap last weekend. Which felt surprisingly satisfying. Ooh, go you! I’m utterly useless at DIY. I once tried to put up a shelf and ended up with it hanging at a forty-five-degree angle. It was a disaster. You need a proper spirit level. Those little ones on your phone are rubbish. Speaking of disasters... did anyone see Old Man Hemlock's mulberry tree finally came down in the storm? Oh, no! That tree was ancient! I always loved picking mulberries from it when I was a kid. Made the best jam. A real shame. Though I suspect his neighbours aren't too upset. That thing dropped mulberries all over their driveways every year.

Honestly, this cutlery is dreadful. It’s like eating with plastic spoons. You always say that, love. It's perfectly functional. Aye, it's alright. Not the finest silver, but it does the job. Your mother gets a new set every few years, doesn't she, and then we're all having a moan about them being too fiddly or too heavy. She likes a change, she does. Always has. Though I do remember her grandmother having a truly magnificent set. Real silver, heavy as anything. You had to have muscles to lift a spoon! Aye, that were true. Old Bessie’s silver. Not like this modern stuff, all lightweight and flimsy. She’d polish it for hours, Bessie would. Said it was good for the soul. Well, it’s not good for my soup-eating soul, that’s for sure. It’s bending already. Stop attacking the cutlery, you’ll upset your mum. Speaking of which, how’s Sarah doing? Haven’t seen her in ages. She’s good. Just started a new course, online I think. Something to do with digital marketing. Smart girl, that one. Always was. Good for her. It’s important to keep the brain active. I’ve been trying to do those crosswords, but they’re getting harder and harder. All these obscure words… Crosswords? Bah! Waste of time. Always preferred a good book. Give me a bit of Dickens any day. I saw Lisa the other day, from University. She's living in London now, working as a journalist. Apparently, it’s a nightmare trying to find a flat. London’s ridiculous. Don’t know how anyone affords to live there. I’m happy enough here, thank you very much. It’s a good place, Chesterfield. Quiet. Everything you need is within easy reach. And your parents have a lovely house, don't they? Always immaculate. Your mother does take pride in it. Though it is a bit… full. She doesn’t throw anything away. That’s an understatement. It's like an antique shop in here. Still, it’s nice to be home. It feels… safe. Aye, that’s what home's for. A bit of comfort. A bit of familiarity. Though I do miss the old garden. Used to grow the best tomatoes, I did. You always did have a green thumb, Grandad. You should get back into it, you would enjoy it.

Right, so I’ve actually managed to get that report finished. Finally. Honestly, it felt like it was never going to end. Mrs. Davies kept adding little bits on, you know, “just a quick tweak here,” “could you just clarify this point?” It was relentless. Mummy, can I have more peas? Yes, darling, here you go. Just a little bit now. Now, where was I? Oh yes, the report. It’s with Mr. Henderson now, so hopefully, I won’t hear another word about it for a while. I’m hoping to really focus on the Peterson project next week. Are we going skiing soon? We are! In just over two weeks. Isn’t that exciting? We’ve got to start getting everything organized properly. Have you tried on your snow boots yet, to make sure they still fit? Yes! They're a little bit tight. A little bit tight? How little bit? Just a little. Okay, well, we’ll have to take them with us and see if we can stretch them out a bit while we’re there. Or maybe we can buy some thicker socks. Your dad’s really good at sorting out boot issues. He used to race, remember? Yes! He goes really fast! He does. He’s a bit rusty now, but he still loves it. He’s been checking the snow reports every day. Apparently, there’s a good base forming already. Will it be very cold? It will be cold, but we’ll have all our warm clothes. Layers are the key. Lots and lots of layers! Hats, gloves, scarves, thermal underwear… the whole lot. We’ll be snug as bugs. Snug as bugs? Yes, snug as bugs in a rug! It’s an expression. It means very comfortable and warm. Oh. Mummy, what will  you  be doing while Daddy and I ski? Well, I’m planning to do a little bit of skiing myself, but I’m also hoping to get some reading done. And maybe a bit of exploring. The village is supposed to be very pretty. And I definitely plan on enjoying some hot chocolate! Can I have hot chocolate with marshmallows? Of course, you can! Lots of marshmallows. Actually, we need to make a list of everything we need to pack. I think I saw a checklist somewhere…oh, and don’t forget your favourite teddy bear! He needs a skiing holiday too.

Ugh, I genuinely think Mr. Davies is actively trying to make us all fail. Like, the questions on the practice paper were NOTHING like what we’ve been learning. Seriously?! I thought he was okay. I mean, a bit… enthusiastic, maybe, but okay. What was so bad about them? They were all, like, worded really strangely and he expected us to know formulas we haven’t even  seen  yet! Honestly, I spent the whole lesson feeling completely lost. And then he asked if anyone had questions and when I put my hand up he just… looked at me. Oh no! That’s awful. I’m more worried about English, though. Mrs. Peterson is making us write a Shakespearean sonnet. A SONNET! Who even does that anymore? Oh god, no. That sounds horrific. I’d rather face Mr. Davies’ maths questions. At least with maths, there’s usually a right answer. With poetry, it’s all just…opinion? Exactly! And she’s saying it has to be about  something meaningful . Like, what’s meaningful to a fourteen-year-old? TikTok? My dog? She won’t accept that. She definitely wouldn’t. Speaking of things to accept, have you decided what you’re doing for work experience? My mum’s making me apply to, like, ten different places. I’m thinking about trying to get something at that animal shelter near the High Street. I really love animals, and it would be way more interesting than, like, shadowing someone in an office. Ooh, that sounds good! I’m being pushed towards my aunt’s accountancy firm. I’d rather do literally anything else. Although, I did think about maybe something music-related. Like, helping out at the Cambridge Corn Exchange? That would be cool! You’re way more musical than me. I can barely play a recorder. Remember recorder lessons in year three? Torture. Don't remind me. It was the worst. Oh! And did you hear they're bringing back Spanish as an option for language futures next year? Really?! I’d actually quite like to do that. I did a little bit in primary school, and it seemed kinda fun. Better than French, definitely. Totally. Honestly, I feel like we’ve been stuck in the past years with everything being so… disrupted. It's good to hear about new things happening. I’m just hoping they don’t make us do another food tech unit.

Honestly, darling, that film last night… absolutely dreadful. All that hype for nothing. Oh,  The Gilded Cage ? I thought it was alright! A bit slow, maybe, but the cinematography was lovely. Lovely cinematography doesn’t save a plot full of holes, does it? It just makes the holes  look  pretty. I kept waiting for something to  happen , and it never did! All brooding and meaningful glances. Give me a good old-fashioned thriller any day. You’re such a traditionalist, Nan. You always say that. Do you remember when we tried to get you to watch  Get Out ? Don’t remind me. All those jump scares! I nearly had a heart attack. And the  themes … far too intense for a Tuesday evening. Honestly, I needed a lie down afterwards. But you have to admit, it was a brilliant film, even if it did scare you. It had something to  say . It said ‘Boo!’ a lot. That’s what it said. Now,  Casablanca … that has something to say. A timeless tale of love and sacrifice. Humphrey Bogart… now  there  was an actor. Okay, okay, point taken.  Casablanca  is a classic. Though I still think you’re being too hard on  The Gilded Cage . Apparently, the director was really inspired by Hitchcock. Hitchcock knew how to build suspense! This was just… meandering. Honestly, I think I spent half the film wondering if I’d remembered to lock the back door. You and your back door! You’re always worrying about that back door. Well, you can’t be too careful, can you? Especially living in a city like Cambridge. Though Lewisham was no picnic either, mind you. Remember Old Man Hemmings next door? He swore someone tried to steal his gnomes. Oh, God, yes! He was convinced they were after the little fisherman one. He used to sit up all night with a baseball bat. A baseball bat! Honestly. Still, it’s a bit more exciting than watching a film where nothing happens. What are we watching tonight then? Anything good on? I was thinking maybe that new Wes Anderson film?  Asteroid City ? Wes Anderson? Oh, dear. All that symmetry and those muted colours… it's all a bit… precious, isn’t it? It’s quirky! And the cast is amazing. Hmm. As long as it doesn't involve any jump scares. Or gnomes. I’m still recovering from the last one. Deal.

Honestly though, the traffic was  brutal . I left ages ago and it still took nearly two hours. Two hours! From Hitchin? Goodness me. That M1, isn't it? Always a nightmare. Did you stop anywhere? No, I just powered through. Needed to get here, and honestly, even a coffee stop felt like too much of a time commitment. I’m starving now though. Have you sorted dinner? I’ve got a chicken roasting, and I made a big pot of potatoes. There’s plenty. Though I did burn the Yorkshire puddings a bit… typical. Oh, Mum! You always burn the Yorkshire puddings. It's a family tradition, isn’t it? It is, isn't it? I try, I really do. They just… crisp up a bit too much. Anyway, how was the drive apart from the traffic? See anything interesting? Not really. Just fields. And lots and lots of lorries. I did listen to that audiobook you recommended though,  The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo . Oh, did you like it? I finished it last week. Such a good story, wasn’t it? A bit scandalous, mind you. It was brilliant! I couldn't put it down. I stayed up way too late reading last night. Honestly, I'm exhausted now. Need a proper lie-in tomorrow. Well, you deserve one. You work so hard, teaching those youngsters. Is everything alright with the new class? Any difficult ones? There's one boy, little Leo, who's really struggling with his reading. It’s heartbreaking. I’m trying to get him some extra support, but the resources are so stretched. It’s frustrating. That’s awful. You’re a good teacher, though. You always put the kids first. It reminds me of your Auntie Carol, she was always like that. Always helping everyone. I try. It just feels like sometimes you’re fighting a losing battle against the system. Anyway, how’s work? Still dealing with some…characters in court? Oh, you have no idea. Had a lad in yesterday, accused of shoplifting. Said he was only trying to get food for his dog. Turned out the ‘dog’ was a ferret. A ferret, can you believe it? Oh, Mum! That's ridiculous. Only in Birmingham. I know, right? It keeps life interesting, I suppose. Though sometimes I wish I'd done something completely different. Like… become a librarian. Surrounded by peace and quiet.

Honestly, that seminar was… a lot. Old Man Hemmings really went off on one about post-structuralism again. You’d think, after twenty years, he’d find a new hobby. Sounds about right. Still clinging to his Derrida, is he? Mine wasn’t too bad, just a lot of frantic essay-marking breathing down my neck. Apparently, half the class still hasn't submitted their drafts. Oh, the joys. I swear, grading sometimes feels like a full-time job  on top  of the actual job. Did you manage to get that book I asked about? The one on comparative literature? I did, actually. From that little shop near the university, the one with the incredibly chaotic bookshelves. It was a mission, but I found it tucked away behind a pile of dusty poetry. I’ve got it in my bag, shall I give it to you when we get in? That would be brilliant, thank you! You’re a lifesaver. I need to start prepping for next week’s lecture, and it'll be really helpful. Honestly, that shop is a treasure trove, even if navigating it feels like an archaeological dig. It is. And the owner’s always got some interesting anecdote to share. Last time I was in there, he was telling me about a first edition Joyce he’d acquired… for practically nothing. Apparently, the bloke didn’t realise what he had. Incredible! People just don’t know what they’ve got sometimes. Speaking of things we need, are we completely out of coffee? I noticed the jar was looking a bit sad this morning. I think we are. I was meaning to pop into that new supermarket on Xinhua Road – the one everyone’s raving about. They apparently stock proper English tea bags, which is a huge win. We could grab coffee and a few bits for dinner there on Friday? That sounds perfect. I'm craving a proper roast. Though, trying to find suitable vegetables here can be… challenging. Everything’s so perfectly shaped and uniformly sized, it feels a bit unsettling. You and your anxieties about perfectly shaped carrots! I think they’re starting to get used to the  laowai  demand for slightly wonky produce. Plus, the market near here is good for that sort of thing. We could go there on Saturday morning? Ooh, yes! That’s a good idea. It feels more… authentic, doesn't it?

Right, so, Grandma's definitely free on Saturday then? To do the babysitting? Yeah! She said she's making cookies with me! Chocolate chip! Can I help make the cookies? You can both help, definitely. But only after you’ve finished your reading, okay? Remember, ten pages each. Ugh, but Grandma's cookies… Grandma’s cookies will taste even  better  knowing you’ve done your reading. It's a deal? Speaker_2 & Speaker_3 : Deal! Good. Now, I’m meeting Sarah for dinner on Friday. I’m thinking that Italian place, the one near the station? She hasn’t been there before. Italian is yummy! Do they have spaghetti bolognese? They do! And pizza, and loads of other things. I haven't seen Sarah in ages, it'll be good to catch up. She was telling me about this hilarious haircut her son got. Apparently he asked for a “spiky mohawk” and it… didn’t quite go to plan. A spiky mohawk? Haha! Like a dinosaur! Exactly! He looked like a tiny, disgruntled dinosaur. Anyway, back to Saturday… I was thinking we could try and do that photoshoot with Leo then. Remember, for his birthday? The superhero one? With the cape? Yes! The superhero one. I’ve been collecting props all week. We just need somewhere with good light. Maybe the garden, if it’s not raining? It might rain. It always rains on Saturdays. Don’t be so pessimistic! Let’s just hope for the best. If it’s awful, we can set up a backdrop in the living room. It won't be ideal, but we’ll make it work. I also promised Emily I’d help her with her science project on Sunday, so it's going to be a busy weekend. Can we build a fort on Sunday too? After Emily goes home? We’ll see! Maybe. Depends how quickly we get through everything else. First, reading, then cookies with Grandma, then superhero photos… it’s a lot! Can we read about superheroes? Good idea! We can definitely read about superheroes. Now, who is ready for a snack? I think I spotted some apple slices in the fridge. --- I hope this meets your requirements! Let me know if any changes are needed. --- I hope this meets your requirements! Let me know if any changes are needed. --- I hope this meets your requirements! Let me know if any changes are needed.

Honestly, this canteen food is…an experience, isn’t it? I think I’ve identified the mystery meat in this pasta bake as…chicken? Maybe? Don’t even  try  to identify it, you'll lose the will to live. It's just…beige. Everything is beige. It’s a beige buffet of sadness. Beige buffet is  perfect . I’m stealing that. Seriously though, I’m starting to regret not bringing a packed lunch. My mum makes a banging tuna mayo sandwich, you know. Ooh, tuna mayo sounds heavenly right now. Mine usually just ends up being a slightly stale croissant and a bruised apple. Luxury. Are you still up for that night out on Friday? Definitely! I need a proper night out, away from beige food and lectures about postcolonial literature. Where are we thinking? Pryzm is…Pryzm. Pryzm is a  choice . A questionable choice, but a choice. I was thinking maybe somewhere a bit smaller? Like, Revolution? Or even that new place, Lola's, down by the river? Lola’s! Ooh, good shout. I heard they do amazing cocktails. And it's actually…aesthetic? Unlike Pryzm, which looks like a nightclub designed by a seven-year-old with a glow stick addiction. Aesthetic is key. I need Instagrammable moments. It’s a requirement these days. Did you finish that essay for Dr. Davies? The one on feminist theory? Oh god, don't even remind me. I'm still chipping away at it. She expects a dissertation for a 1,500-word essay! It’s brutal. What about you? Are you all sorted? I actually handed it in yesterday. Triumph! Though, to be honest, I mostly just rambled for 1,500 words about Beyoncé being a modern-day feminist icon. You did  not ! Dr. Davies is going to have a field day. Though, honestly, you might be onto something. Queen Bey  is  pretty powerful. Exactly! And it got me thinking…could I get away with writing my entire dissertation about Beyoncé? Imagine. I think you'd have to be incredibly clever to pull that off. But honestly, at this point, I'm pretty sure anything is possible. We're surviving uni on caffeine and sheer willpower, aren't we? Absolutely. And beige food. Never forget the beige food. Oh! Speaking of survival, did you hear about Jamie failing his driving test again? No way! That’s like, his fifth attempt?! What happened this time?

Honestly though, I need a holiday. Just… a proper one. Not a weekend in the Lake District pretending it’s exotic. Tell me about it. I was looking at flights to Portugal earlier. Could be decent. Though the thought of all the stag dos… Portugal’s good. Bit predictable though, isn’t it? Everyone goes to the Algarve. I was thinking maybe Morocco? Properly different. Ooh, Morocco! That sounds amazing. Is it expensive? Probably not as bad as you’d think. You can get some really good deals if you’re not after five-star hotels. I saw a documentary about Marrakech, looked incredible. I was watching that new series on Netflix, “Chef’s Table: Pizza.” Honestly, it changed my life. Changed your life? It’s pizza! No, seriously! It’s like, an art form. This guy in Naples, he’s been making the same dough recipe for generations. It’s… spiritual. Sounds intense for pizza. I just want a pepperoni with extra cheese, you know? No backstory required. You’re missing out! I tried to make pizza dough from scratch last weekend. It was a disaster. Sticky, wouldn't rise, ended up resembling something closer to concrete. Sounds… challenging. Did you at least  eat  the concrete pizza? I tried. One bite. Regretted it immediately. I should probably just stick to ordering takeaway. Wise move. Speaking of takeaway, anyone fancy Indian tonight? I’m starving. I’ve been stuck on site all day, dealing with drainage issues. It’s not glamorous, let me tell you. Drainage? Sounds… aromatic. Indian sounds excellent. Anything but pizza, given the earlier report. Indian is a brilliant shout. Though I did make a really nice chilli yesterday, if anyone’s feeling brave… It's a bit fiery, even for me. Fiery is good. Bring on the vindaloo! But seriously, Morocco… we should look into that. Maybe next Spring? Yeah, I’m in. We can argue over the best riad then. I’m already picturing myself haggling in a market. As long as there’s good food, I'm happy. And definitely no concrete pizza. Does that fit the context and desired conversation type? Would you like me to extend it further, or adjust anything? Also did you see that new show, "Taskmaster?" It's absolute genius. Greg Davies is phenomenal. Oh my god, I love Taskmaster! It's pure chaos. The challenges are so stupid, but everyone takes them so seriously.

…and then young Timmy, bless ‘im, he’s gone and bought another one. Another motorbike. A bright orange one this time. Oh, not again! Doesn’t he learn? He had that accident last year, didn’t he? Broken arm and all. Absolutely bonkers. Though, to be fair, he's always been a bit of a speed demon. Remember when he “borrowed” old Mr. Henderson’s horse and went galloping around the village? Oh, I do indeed. Old Bessie! Nearly gave the poor woman a heart attack. Though Henderson wasn’t too pleased, either. Said Bessie hadn’t been ridden that hard since the war. Speaking of hard riding, did you see that article in the paper about that youth hostel in Cornwall being sold off? The one we stayed in, years ago, with the kids? The one with the dodgy plumbing and the communal kitchen that smelled perpetually of bacon? Vaguely. Good memories, though. That’s where little Emily learned to ride a bike, wasn’t it? That’s right. And your mother nearly had a fit when she found out we were letting her wander off into the fields! Said she’d be kidnapped by gypsies. Oh, your mother. Always predicting disaster. She’d have had a field day with the election coming up. Always said politicians were all the same: “Lies, lies, and more lies!” She wasn't wrong, really. It’s all just soundbites and promises they never keep. Though I do worry about the state of things. House prices are crazy. I was looking at selling Mum’s place, but honestly, even with the market as it is, I’m not sure it’s worth the hassle. Selling houses is a nightmare these days. Surveyors, estate agents, solicitors… all taking their cut. You’re better off just leaving it. And then there's the cars. Remember when we bought that Ford Fiesta? Thought it was the bee’s knees. Fell apart within a year. Oh, the Fiesta! The handbrake barely worked, and the radio only played static. You tried fixing it yourself, didn’t you, Dad? Well, I thought I could. Had a look under the bonnet, poked around a bit… made things worse, if I’m honest. Ended up taking it to old Mr. Barnes down the road. He charged me a fortune. Speaking of fortunes, have you been watching that antiques show on the telly?

Honestly, the amount of times I’ve been asked if he’s ‘sleeping through’ yet… it’s infuriating. Like, he’s seven weeks old! What did people expect? Oh, tell me about it. Everyone thinks babies come out fully formed, able to adhere to a strict 7-to-7 schedule. My mum was on about it last week, saying, “Oh, little [Cousin’s Baby’s Name] was sleeping through by eight weeks.” Eight weeks! And that was a different baby, a different temperament, a different… everything. Exactly! And she’d forget she’s talking to someone who's literally in the thick of it. I just smile and nod, but inside I'm screaming. Is yours still… enjoying the cluster feeding? Oh,  enjoying  isn’t the word I’d use. Surviving is more accurate. It was awful last night. He was latched on pretty much continuously for three hours. I felt like a human pacifier! Matthew was brilliant, he brought me snacks and drinks, but I was just… depleted. Oh, bless Matthew. My Daniel just kind of wanders about looking helpless. He’s very good at changing nappies, though, I’ll give him that. He’s even mastered the whole fast-nappy-changing technique. That’s good. Mine's good at holding him, which is vital, but doesn’t really  do  much else. He asks if he can help, then looks horrified when I suggest a task! Honestly, having a baby exposes so much about people, doesn't it? It really does. And it's amazing how many opinions everyone suddenly has. Auntie Carol was giving me advice on weaning yesterday! Weaning! He’s barely rolling over. Oh, Carol. She’s the worst. Always has been. Remember when she told me I was holding [Sibling's Name] wrong when he was a baby? Oh god, yes! Something about supporting his head and… I can’t even remember. It was just so condescending. She’s never even  had  children herself! Exactly! She just read a magazine article once. Anyway, no, he’s not showing any interest in food. And frankly, the thought of pureeing vegetables fills me with dread. It seems like so much effort. It is! Honestly, I'm just aiming for getting through each day. And hoping for a tiny sliver of uninterrupted sleep. How is your sister coping with little [Sister’s Baby’s Name]? She seemed a bit overwhelmed when I saw them last week.

Honestly, the price of everything is just… ridiculous now, isn’t it? Did you see the petrol prices this morning? Don’t even get me started. I filled up yesterday, and nearly had a heart attack. It's daylight robbery, pure and simple. What about you, Darla, any news from the copywriting world? Still battling algorithms? Always. It’s like trying to write for a robot half the time. They want ‘engaging content’ but then penalise you for sounding too human. The irony. I’ve got a brief for a really dull plumbing company today…wish me luck. Oh, that sounds… thrilling. I’m on a very early shift today, the handover was a disaster last night. Old Mrs. Higgins was convinced her oxygen mask was trying to steal her dentures. Oh, bless her. They get confused, don’t they? It's heartbreaking. Are you managing okay with the shifts, Carol? You seem…stretched. It’s just…a lot. The training is intense, and then the reality of the ward is…different. But I’m learning. Just need more caffeine, probably. Right, I really should get a move on. Off you pop then. And don’t let Mrs. Higgins’ dentures get to you! Seriously. She sounds like a character. I’m going to tackle the garden this morning. It’s completely overrun. The roses need pruning, and the weeds are taking over everything. Honestly, it looks like the Amazon rainforest out there. Good luck with that. I’ll try and be helpful...by staying inside. I might attempt to clean the garage. It’s a disaster zone. I think the garden furniture has started to grow roots. Sounds… ambitious. I was thinking of finally sorting through my wardrobe. It’s basically a clothing avalanche waiting to happen. I keep saying I’ll donate stuff, but then I think ‘Oh, I might wear that again someday…’ That's the classic wardrobe dilemma. It’s like holding onto memories attached to clothes. It is, isn't it? Speaking of memories, did you hear from Auntie Mavis? I haven’t spoken to her in ages. She said she might call about Uncle George’s birthday. She’s usually pretty good about that. I’ll give her a ring later if she hasn't. Did Leo eat all his breakfast? He was particularly grumpy this morning. He did. But only after a negotiation involving extra strawberries.

Ugh, I genuinely think Mr. Davies is actively trying to make us fail the Physics test. It was  impossible . Seriously! I spent like, three hours revising, and I still didn’t understand half of it. Did you get the one about the…the resistors? The resistors?! Don’t even  start  me. I put down, like, a massively wrong answer and just hoped for a mark for showing my working. Which, honestly, probably wasn’t working at all. Me too. I think I just guessed. At least Art was good today. Mrs. Peterson actually said she liked my landscape. Ooh, nice! You're so good at Art. Mine always looks like a toddler did it. She’s actually quite strict, isn’t she? I feel like she expects us to be professional artists already. She is, but she gives good feedback. Anyway, have you started thinking about Christmas presents yet? My mum keeps hinting she wants one of those fancy plant pots, the self-watering ones. Oh yeah, I saw those in town. They're pretty expensive though, aren’t they? I was thinking of getting my nan some stamps. She collects them, remember? Oh, that’s a good idea! She loves her stamps. Is she still trying to complete that British Birds set? I think so! She was complaining the other day that she needs a really rare one, a puffin I think, to finish it. It's expensive ones that are always the last to find. Maybe we could look online or something? I’m going into Cambridge on Saturday with my mum, we could check out the stamp shop there. Ooh, yeah! That would be amazing. Actually, are you going to the Ed Sheeran concert? Everyone’s talking about it. I am! My dad managed to get tickets. It’s ages away though, isn’t it? Like, next summer. What about you? No… my mum said it was too expensive. Typical. I’m so annoyed. All anyone talks about is Ed Sheeran. I bet it’ll be epic. It will be! My cousin went to his last concert and said it was incredible. She said he did all his new songs and some of the old ones. Speaking of concerts, did you finish your maths homework? Mr. Harrison’s threatening a detention if we don’t have it in tomorrow. No! I completely forgot about it. Ugh, Maths is the worst.

Honestly, Arthur, you and that rat puppet. It’s been years since young Thomas gave it to you, and you still carry it around! Now, now, Beatrice, don’t be like that. Reginald is a companion. A very sophisticated companion, if I may say so myself. He’s seen me through a lot, Reginald has. More than most people, I reckon. He  is  rather a fixture, isn’t he? Doesn’t Reginald ever get… dusty? Dusty? I polish him weekly! With a special chamois leather. Keeps his whiskers gleaming. Though I did lose one eye for a bit last year. Found it under the sofa cushion, thankfully. Almost had a crisis. Honestly, you’re more dedicated to that puppet than you are to getting your eyes tested! You’ve been saying you need to go for months. Well, the buses, you see, that’s the trouble. Getting to Norwich isn’t what it used to be. They’ve changed the route, haven’t they? And it’s always crammed. Can’t see a thing looking out the window, let alone navigate to the optician’s. I could give you a lift, Arthur. No trouble at all. Oh, would you, David? That’s awfully kind. But I don’t want to put you out. You're a busy man, running your business and all. Nonsense. It’s on my way when I visit my sister. We could go next Tuesday, perhaps? That would be lovely! It’s just… you squint at everything, Arthur. The television, the newspaper, Reginald! It can’t be good for you. It’s not so bad. I manage. Though sometimes the handbell ringing gets a bit blurry. The handbell ringing? Still at it then? Oh yes. Wednesdays. Old Mrs. Higgins insists. Says I’m the best tenor. Though between you and me, her hearing isn’t what it used to be either. You’re a character, Arthur, you truly are. I don’t know what we’d do without you and Reginald! And I don't know what I'd do without you both. Now, would anyone like another cup of tea? I’ve just made a fresh pot. And Reginald, naturally, would like a biscuit. A tiny one, mind. He’s watching his figure. I'll have a cup, thank you. And yes, a biscuit for Reginald wouldn't go amiss. Me too, please. It's nice just sitting here chatting.

Right, so after this, I was thinking we could just wander around a bit? See if we can find that mask shop you were talking about? Oh, lovely! Yes, that’s a good idea. It's just off the Rialto Bridge, I think. Though, honestly, I’m terrible with directions. Used to be easier, you know, when everything felt… smaller. Smaller? What do you mean? Well, Venice. It feels much more crowded now, doesn't it? When I was a girl, it wasn’t  this  overrun with tourists. You could actually get lost in the backstreets and feel like you had the whole city to yourself. It’s still beautiful, of course, but it’s lost some of its magic, I think. That's a shame. I can imagine. It  is  pretty packed. Especially around San Marco Square. It's a bit overwhelming, actually. Overwhelming is the word. Though, back then, it wasn’t just the tourists. It was different then. More… local life, you know? Remember old Signor Rossi? He used to have that little bakery near our flat? Best biscotti in the world. I think I remember him! Didn’t he always give you extra when you went in? Always. He used to say I reminded him of his granddaughter. A complete fib, I was a terror when I was little, but he was a lovely man. His bakery’s a souvenir shop now, sadly. They all are, aren’t they? It's all Murano glass and plastic gondolas. That’s a bit depressing. Still, the coffee here is amazing. And this little  pasticceria  has the most incredible looking cakes. I’m definitely having one later. Oh, you must! You have to try the tiramisu. Venice does tiramisu like nowhere else. It's a bit rich, but utterly divine. And maybe we can find some  cicchetti  for lunch? Little Venetian snacks.  Cicchetti ? What are those? Oh, they're like Venetian tapas. Little bites. You go to a  bacaro  – that’s a Venetian wine bar – and you get a little plate of different things. Fried mozzarella, little sandwiches, olives… delicious! We used to go  bacaro  hopping with your auntie Sarah when we were teenagers. Sounds amazing! Okay, definitely  cicchetti  for lunch. And the mask shop, and maybe we can get lost in the backstreets like you used to? We can certainly try. Though I think getting properly lost these days is a challenge.

Honestly though, I’m wrecked. Legs are screaming. That new leg press machine is… brutal. Oh god, tell me about it! I tried it last week, felt it for three days. Worth it though, right? Gotta build those glutes. Absolutely. Though I’m starting to think I need a holiday just to  recover  from the gym. You still on for Barcelona in October? Definitely! Booked the flights last night, actually. Found a really cute little Airbnb near the Gothic Quarter. We  have  to try and learn a few phrases before we go. My Spanish is… atrocious. Oh, that sounds amazing! I’m rubbish at languages. I think the last time I attempted Spanish was Year 9 and I mostly just asked where the toilets were. That’s a good start, at least! Seriously though, we should download Duolingo or something. Speaking of needing a holiday, how was your weekend? Any good nights out? It was… eventful. Went to that new bar, ‘The Alchemist’? Really swanky cocktails, but ridiculously busy. And then bumped into… Liam. Oh.  Liam . Wow. That’s awkward. How did that go? It didn’t. I actively avoided him. Managed to strategically position myself behind a very large plant for a good twenty minutes. Chloe, thankfully, distracted him. Chloe’s a lifesaver. Honestly, I still can’t believe you dated him for so long. He always seemed… a bit of a tool. I know, right? Hindsight is 20/20. Anyway! Let’s not dwell. How’s work? Still battling the world of health insurance marketing? You have  no  idea. It's… a lot. Trying to make preventative healthcare sound exciting is surprisingly difficult. It’s mostly spreadsheets and trying to explain complex policies in a way a normal person can understand. It’s exhausting. Sounds stressful. At least my job is mostly organising things and chasing people up. Relatively low stakes. Though I did spend three hours yesterday trying to find a specific shade of teal for a presentation. Oh, the joys of project management. You’re a saint. So, have you started thinking about what you want to do  after  this project? Long-term goals? I'm toying with the idea of doing a Masters. Maybe in Data Science or something. It feels like everyone's pivoting into tech. That’s smart. Good money in that, definitely. I'm thinking about a career change actually, something a little more creative.

…and honestly, the sheer exhaustion of it all! But worth every single moment, of course. Little Elsie is just…perfect. Though her hair is shockingly red, just like your brother’s was at that age. Red hair, you say? A sign of a fiery spirit, no doubt. Though, you know, being born abroad…it complicates things. My grandson, Julian, was born in Geneva. A dreadful fuss getting the paperwork sorted, proving citizenship. All these rules. Oh, I can imagine. Though Elsie was born right here in Frimley, so we were spared that headache. It’s just…everything feels different now, doesn’t it? A new perspective. Different? Everything  is  different. Reminds me of France, actually. Used to spend a lot of time there, you know. Property prices are astonishing. And the bureaucracy! Heaven help you if you try to start a small enterprise. Layers upon layers of paperwork. Though, they do have land, don’t they? Real, usable land, unlike this cramped little island. Of course, you get the anarchists… and the bureaucrats working hand-in-hand, naturally. Oh, you always have a story, don’t you? We had a French couple staying at the B&B last month. Lovely people, but utterly bewildered by London. They couldn’t understand why everything was so… expensive. And the queues! They said Paris was far more efficient. Efficient? Paris? Poppycock! It’s a beautiful city, of course, but efficient? They just hide the chaos better. Did you hear about Chichester Cathedral? The spire…apparently it's leaning. Leaning?! Good heavens. Is it going to fall down? They’re shoring it up, apparently. It’s this architect, Porden, a rather flamboyant fellow, apparently responsible for a lot of structural instability. Though, to be fair, he was designing things centuries ago. Speaking of which, are you coming to the open day at the Historical Society? There's a photo exhibition, local history, all that. I’d love to, if I can find the time. I’m rather tied up with Elsie’s parents at the moment. And I’ve entered that art competition, you know. The village one. Ah yes, the watercolours. Good luck! Though they haven’t quite figured out the problem with those dreadful bollards in the High Street, have they? Absolute menace to pedestrians. And don't even get me started on the new housing management company! Utterly hopeless. Never return a phone call.

This spring roll is… actually pretty good. Better than the one I had last week at that place near school. It was all soggy. Seriously? The one near school’s usually banging. Maybe they had a bad day. I got their noodles last time and they were massive. Like, couldn’t even finish them. You always say everything’s massive, Ben. You’re just a lightweight. I’m starving, though. All this revision is burning calories, you know? Brain fuel. Revision? You lot are already stressing about revision? We haven't even had mocks yet. It's ages away. Ages away? We’ve got Chemistry mocks in like, two weeks! And Mr. Harrison said they’re going to be  brutal . He’s on a mission to fail half the class, I swear. Harrison’s always like that. Thinks he's some kind of science overlord. Remember when he made that kid cry over a titration? Oh god, yeah. Poor Liam. It was just a slight error. Harrison was acting like he’d single-handedly ruined the world. So, anyone seen Maya lately? She’s been proper avoiding me. She was with Chloe and Sophie at lunch. They were all whispering and giggling. Looked dodgy. Probably planning something. Dodgy how? Like, mean girl dodgy? Probably. Maya can be a bit… much sometimes. Remember that time she told everyone I had a crush on Miss Davies? Oh, man! You were mortified! She still brings it up, doesn't she? Don’t remind me. It’s a running joke now. The entire school knows. I'm thinking of embracing it, wearing a ‘I Heart Miss Davies’ t-shirt. You wouldn’t! That would be epic though. Imagine the chaos. Speaking of comics, has anyone got the new X-Men issue? I need to know what happened with Wolverine. I haven’t got it yet, but I pre-ordered it. Should be here tomorrow. I'll let you borrow it if you want. Sweet! I’m more of a DC guy myself, but X-Men are decent. My nan keeps trying to get me to read Agatha Christie. Says it’ll ‘expand my mind’. Your nan reads Agatha Christie? That's pretty cool. Mine just watches daytime TV and asks me if I’m eating enough. Mine constantly asks me about my future plans. Like, I'm sixteen. I barely know what I'm having for dinner tonight, let alone my entire career path.

Honestly, this house is brimming. Absolutely brimming. I don’t know how we’ve accumulated so much stuff. Well, you and Mum have lived here for… what is it, sixty years now? Things just  build up . It’s inevitable. And Jonathan’s birthday is a good excuse, isn’t it? A clear-out, a bit of decluttering. It's mostly old stuff though, isn't it? Like, seriously old. Aye, a lot of history. Though admittedly, a lot of it could probably go to charity. Or a car boot sale. Think of the space, Gran! Car boot sales are a nightmare. All that haggling. And those young lads trying to get everything for a pound. Honestly. Oh, don't start on car boot sales, Margaret. They're a necessary evil. I was thinking more about a proper sort-through. We need to decide what’s staying, what’s going to the kids, and what needs to...well, disappear. I was thinking about the food for Jonathan’s party. Should we get a caterer? It would take a load off, wouldn’t it? No! Mum’s cooking is legendary. It wouldn’t be a proper Jonathan birthday without her famous lemon drizzle cake and those little sausage rolls. Honestly, I'm happy to do the cooking. But a bit of help wouldn't go amiss. Elsie, you're a whizz in the kitchen, aren't you? Maybe you could do the salads? Oh, I'd be happy to, dear. Though I’m not as nimble as I used to be. Knees aren’t what they were, you know. Gran, you make the best potato salad. Seriously. Everyone says so. See? He agrees. Now, about presents… has anyone given any thought to what Jonathan actually  needs ? He says he doesn't want anything, which of course means he wants something expensive. I was thinking maybe a contribution towards a weekend away. He’s been talking about wanting to go somewhere… a bit of peace and quiet. That’s a good idea. Somewhere with good walking trails. He'd love that. I know he was looking at places in the Lake District. Oh, the Lake District! We used to go there every summer when you were little, didn't we, darling? Before it got overrun with tourists. It’s not the same now. No, it isn’t. So commercial. Everything's branded now, isn't it?

Ugh, I’m so stressed about options. Like, what if I pick the wrong things? I know, right? It feels like it decides your whole life. Have you decided on anything yet? I’m pretty sure I'm doing English Lit, obviously. And probably History, I actually enjoy it. But then… everything else feels awful. I’m torn between Geography and Art. Geography seems… safe. Like, you could actually  do  something with that. That’s what my mum says. “Practical subject, darling.” But Art is… fun. I actually like being creative, unlike nearly everything else at school. True. What about a job? Have you thought about what you’d want to  be ? Honestly? A bogger. A… bogger? What even is that? No, a  blogger ! Like, a beauty or fashion blogger. Earn loads just by, like, taking pictures of yourself. Seriously? You think that's realistic? Well, look at Zoella! She started on YouTube and now she’s, like, a millionaire! I’d rather do that than be a lawyer or something. Yeah, but there are  loads  of YouTubers. It's super competitive. And Zoella's had, like, a lot of drama over the years. I know, I know. Still… a girl can dream. Have you seen the new video from Saffron Barker? She visited Paris! No, I’ve been busy trying to memorise the periodic table for science. Honestly, it’s impossible. Speaking of impossible, Mr. Henderson gave us a clarinet piece that's… well, it’s beyond me. Oh dear god, the clarinet. I swear he deliberately picks the most difficult bits. I’m just going to pretend to play. I’m considering faking a cold. Though, knowing my luck, he’d make me play anyway. Did you hear about Sophie getting Head Girl? Yeah! She’s so…perfect. Like, perfectly behaved, perfectly academic, perfectly everything. It's annoying. She spends all her time doing “perfect duty” or whatever. I saw her giving out stickers to Year 7s yesterday. Stickers! Oh my god. The cringe. Have you got PE today? I'm dreading it. Sadly, yes. Netball. I’m rubbish at netball. I always get yelled at by Miss Davies. She’s the worst. Seriously, she thinks we’re all professional athletes. Maybe we should both fake a cold. A very convincing, long-lasting cold. That’s… actually a brilliant idea. We could become professional cold-fakers. More realistic than being a blogger, probably.

Honestly, the state of that roundabout on the A47… you’d think they’d have sorted it by now. Been months, hasn’t it? Months, Reginald, months. Could’ve built a whole new road in the time it’s taken ‘em to fix a roundabout. Absolutely scandalous, if you ask me. Though, I s’pose they’re all busy with these cycle lanes now. Waste of money, the lot of it. Oh, don't get me started on the cycle lanes. I nearly got taken out by a cyclist on the pavement last week. Honestly, where’s the sense in it? It’s about encouraging sustainable transport, Gran. Less cars on the road, better for the environment. Environment, bah! It’s all virtue signalling, that is. You know, I was reading in the paper about the Romans… they built proper roads. Straight as a die, lasted for centuries. These modern roads… falling apart after a few years. They knew a thing or two, them Romans. Built a proper empire, didn’t they? Remember old Mr. Peterson, down the lane? He used to reckon there were Roman settlements all over Norfolk. He did love his history, didn’t he? Always going on about Boudicca and her chariot. Though, I always thought he had a bit too much imagination. Apparently, there's a lot of evidence of Roman activity around Norwich. They used the river for trade, mainly. It wouldn't surprise me if there were undiscovered settlements. Speaking of undiscovered, have you seen the heron down by the Yare lately? Massive thing, it is. Nearly took my breath away. Old Horace? He’s been around for years. Sly old bird, that one. Always pinching the fish from old Man Hemmings’ pond. Horace is a character, isn’t he? I saw a kestrel hovering the other day. Beautiful sight. They’re becoming rarer, you know. They are. Habitat loss is a huge problem. It's good to see green spaces being protected, even if the cycle lanes are a bit…controversial. I’ve been trying to get this new photo editing software to work. Absolute nightmare. Keeps asking for updates. I swear, they design these things to frustrate you. Computers. Don’t trust ‘em as far as I can throw ‘em. Give me a good book any day. I'm still using Windows 7, you know. Perfectly happy with it. Don’t see the point in changing just for the sake of it.

…and then young Timmy, bless ‘im, he brought in a snail. A  live  snail. In his pocket! Said it was his pet. Oh, you are kidding! Did it…leave a trail? Trail? It decorated the entire classroom! Miss Higgins nearly had a fit. Said it was a health hazard. Little Timmy was heartbroken, of course. Cried his eyes out. Schools are never dull, are they? My lot had a phase of bringing in caterpillars. Thankfully, they kept them in jam jars. Though one  did  escape and ended up on the headmaster’s hat during assembly. Oh, goodness me! That’s a picture. You’d think they’d learn, wouldn't you? My grandkids, they’re all glued to their tablets now. Never see a snail, let alone smuggle one to school. Tablets, eh? Waste of time, if you ask me. Though I did see something on the telly about this ‘tweeting’ business. Apparently, people write little messages…to the world! Twitter? It’s a bit of a minefield, if I’m honest. Mostly people arguing. Though you can find some useful information if you know where to look. Sounds exhausting. I’d rather watch ‘Bargain Hunt’. Though that’s got a bit repetitive lately, hasn't it? Always the same antiques, same experts… And the singing! Honestly, they’ve got someone on there who sings at the drop of a hat. Drove me round the bend. Remember old ‘Opportunity Knocks’? Now  that  was entertainment. Ah, yes! Hughie Green. A bit of a rogue, but brilliant. Speaking of entertainment, I tried to watch that new detective series everyone's talking about, but it was all a bit…dark for my liking. Too much binge drinking and grim storylines. It’s all so bleak these days, isn't it? Everything’s got to be gritty and realistic. Where’s the escapism? I’d like to see something cheerful for a change. Cheerfulness? You won’t find that in the National Health Service, I can tell you. My appointment with Dr. Pritchard…waited three weeks for it, then he spent five minutes telling me to eat more vegetables! Five minutes! Don't get me started on the NHS. My mother had a similar experience. Diagnosis delivered via a hastily scribbled note. No bedside manner whatsoever. It's a wonder anyone gets better. Speaking of messes, I've got to get back and tackle my spare bedroom.

Honestly, this snow is ridiculous. I was hoping to get out in the garden today, maybe prune the roses, but it’s a no-go. Everything’s just…buried. Tell me about it. I tried to clear the path this morning, felt like a right idiot. It’s just coming down too fast. Luckily, uni's cancelled all afternoon seminars, so I’m off the hook for a bit. Good. You deserve a break. You’ve been glued to that desk for weeks. Speaking of breaks, are you still on for 'Come Dine With Me' next Saturday? I’ve been brainstorming menus. Oh aye, definitely! Though, I’m slightly terrified. You're a brilliant cook, lass. I’ll need to pull out all the stops. What are you thinking of making? I was thinking a North African tagine, then sticky toffee pudding. Fancy, but not  too  fancy. What about you? Ooh, that sounds amazing. I’m leaning towards an Italian theme. Pasta from scratch, maybe a tiramisu. If I don’t end up setting the kitchen on fire. You won’t! Okay, that’s sounding good. We need to sort out dates for Liam’s stag do too, though. He’s insistent on paintballing, which I’m… not thrilled about. Paintballing? Seriously? He hasn’t learned from the last time, then? He spent a week walking like a penguin. Apparently not. His brother, Mark, is all for it, of course. They’re a menace together. I’m pushing for a weekend in the Peak District. Good walks, pubs… a bit more civilized. That sounds much more up my street. I’ll back you up on that one. What about Sarah's hen? Have we put anything in the pot for that yet? Not really. She's being very vague about what she wants. Something spa-related, I think. I volunteered to help organise it with Chloe and Emily. We’re thinking a day at a fancy hotel, then maybe a night out in town. Sounds good. Expensive though, those posh spas. Tell me about it! She deserves it though. She's been so stressed with work. Hey, have we properly talked about that holiday? You mentioned wanting to go somewhere warm? We haven't, actually. I was thinking maybe Spain? Somewhere on the Costa del Sol. Nice beaches, good food… affordable. Spain sounds lovely! I'm up for that. Maybe we could look at flights next week?

This is really lovely, Mum. Honestly, the roast potatoes are perfect. So crispy. Oh, bless you, dear. Just a bit of goose fat, that's the secret. Your Grandma always used to say goose fat makes everything taste better. She weren’t wrong, your Grandma. Everything tasted better with a good dollop of fat in it, back in them days. Not like today, all this ‘low fat’ nonsense. Doesn’t taste of nothin’. Though, to be fair, Dad, you do put a  lot  of butter on everything. Butter’s good for ya! Gives ya strength. Keeps the joints oiled. You young ‘uns are always complaining about bein’ tired. Need more butter! Maybe you’re right. Though I think I’m just tired from chasing after students all day. They have zero concept of deadlines. Oh, teaching. That must be exhausting. All that explaining things over and over. I used to get that with the little ones, you know? ‘Why is the sky blue, Mrs. Davies?’ Honestly, sometimes you just don’t know where to begin. It’s a different kind of exhausting. More… intellectual frustration, I suppose. Trying to get them to grasp concepts they simply aren't engaging with. Always were a bright lad, you. Always had your head in a book. Remember when you used to build them model aeroplanes? Spent hours on ‘em, you did. Yeah, but they never flew very well. They usually ended up in the garden, dismantled. Speaking of gardens, Mum, your runner beans are looking amazing. Are you still giving loads away to the neighbours? Oh yes, dear. Couldn’t possibly eat them all myself. Old Mrs. Henderson next door is thrilled, she makes a lovely chutney with them. Says it reminds her of her childhood. Runner beans are easy enough to grow. It's the tomatoes that give me trouble. Blight gets ‘em every year. Used to try everything, but it’s a losing battle. You could try some of those blight-resistant varieties, Dad. They’ve bred some really good ones now. Blight-resistant? Never heard of such a thing. Sounds like fiddling about if you ask me. It’s just the weather, you see. Too much damp. That’s what gets ‘em. It's probably a combination, Dad. The weather, the soil… Oh, leave him to his tomatoes, dear. He enjoys a good grumble about them. Pass the gravy, would you, love?

Honestly though, this gravy is lovely, isn’t it? Your mam always did make a good gravy. Better than anything you get in a packet, that’s for sure. It  is  good, actually. Surprisingly good. I was bracing myself for… well, you know. Bracing yourself? What did you think was going to happen? A gravy disaster? Not a disaster, just… not as flavourful. She sometimes goes a bit light on the seasoning. Nonsense. Your mother’s gravy is legendary. Remember that Christmas when Uncle Bernard tried to sneak off with a jug of it home? Aye, that was a sight. He said his wife couldn’t make gravy to save her life. Said it tasted like dishwater. Oh, Elsie can make a good gravy, she just doesn’t have the patience. She wants everything done  now . Me, I like to let it simmer and build the flavours. So, Mam, are you going to give us the secret recipe? Don’t tell me it’s just Bisto. Bisto? Never! It’s a proper roux, darling. Butter, flour, and a long, slow cook with the meat juices. And a tiny splash of Worcestershire sauce. That’s the trick. Worcestershire sauce, eh? Good tip. I’ll have to try that. Speaking of houses, have you two finally gotten around to looking at those estate agents? You’ve been talking about moving for months. We are, we are. It’s just… overwhelming. So many choices. And everything's ridiculously expensive. It is. We saw one yesterday, a tiny little terraced house, needed a  lot  of work, and they wanted nearly £300,000 for it. Three hundred thousand! In my day, you could buy a whole street for that. Oh, don't get me started. When we bought our first house, it was a steal. Although it did have a bit of a leak in the roof… and the garden was overgrown… and the electrics were ancient… You always gloss over the bad bits, love. It was a right state. We spent a fortune fixing it up. Well, it was a project, wasn't it? Gave us something to do. Still, it was worth it. We made some lovely memories there. I remember little Amelia, she used to hide in the rose bushes for hours. Amelia's still hiding. Now she just hides  in her room  playing video games. She's a teenager. It's what they do.

Right so the crux of it, as I’m seeing it, is getting them to  apply  the knowledge. They can regurgitate theories all day long, pass exams beautifully, but can they actually…  do  anything with it? Exactly. It’s the “so what?” factor. I see it all the time in my students. They understand the pedagogical theory, they can write a perfect essay  about  how to teach, but put them in front of a class of thirty eight seven-year-olds and… chaos. It’s the same in business, isn’t it? You can have a brilliant business plan, a phenomenal concept, but if you can’t execute, if you can’t adapt when things inevitably go wrong… you’re sunk. I was talking to Ben—you remember Ben from the Kiwi tech scene?—and he was saying his biggest regret with his first startup wasn’t a lack of funding, or even a flawed product, it was hiring people who were great at talking about innovation, but couldn’t actually  innovate . Oh, that's brilliant, isn't it? That's a perfect encapsulation of the problem. So, how do we build that into a university course? It’s not enough to just say ‘be more practical.’ We need a structure. A framework. I was thinking… “real world sprints”. Short, intense problem-solving challenges. Partnering with local businesses, NGOs, even the council. Giving them a genuine problem, a tight deadline, limited resources, and letting them figure it out. No pre-teaching, minimal hand-holding. Throw them in the deep end. I like that. Very “sink or swim," but with safeguards, obviously. We’d need mentors, people who’ve actually  been  there, to provide guidance, not answers. To model the process of grappling with uncertainty. And a robust debrief afterwards – proper reflection. Absolutely. The debrief is crucial. That’s where the learning happens. It’s not about finding the ‘right’ solution, it's about analysing the process. What worked? What didn’t? Why? What would you do differently next time? I saw this amazing viral video… it was a group of engineers trying to build a bridge out of spaghetti and marshmallows. Total disaster, hilarious to watch, but the post-mortem analysis was gold. Oh, I've seen that! Wonderful. They’re so earnest, so confident at the beginning, and then… collapse. It highlights the importance of testing assumptions. And failure. We sanitise failure too much in education.

Right, I’m officially declaring it’s too early for Christmas music. I walked past a shop today and they were already blasting Mariah Carey. Mariah! It’s October! Oh god, you’re right. It  is  too early. It’s a crime against humanity. Though, if we’re being honest, I am already vaguely planning Halloween. Ooh, are you? Any themes this year? Last year was… intense. The fog machine nearly set off the smoke alarm. I’m thinking something a little less chaotic. Maybe a ‘haunted library’ vibe? Books, cobwebs, atmospheric lighting. A bit more classy, a bit less… potential fire hazard. That sounds lovely! I’m tempted to just buy a pre-made pack online. Like, ‘instant spooky.’ I’m a bit rubbish at the DIY stuff. I tried to carve a pumpkin last year and it looked like a sad, lopsided potato. That sounds about right. Speaking of rubbish, work was  insane  today. We’re seriously understaffed on the ward, and then we had two admissions come in at once. It was a complete free-for-all. Oh no, that sounds awful. You deserve a medal. Or at least a very large glass of wine. How’s the new training going, though? The one you were so stressed about? It’s… challenging. It's that advanced assessment module. It's really pushing me, but actually, I’m starting to think I’m enjoying it. It feels good to be learning new things, even if it's terrifying at the same time. That’s brilliant! You always were a super-student. Me? I spend my days wrangling project timelines and muttering about Gantt charts. Speaking of which, I need to finish that presentation for Mr. Henderson. He’s already asked twice when it will be ready. Henderson… sounds charming. Are you still enjoying the job, or are you starting to feel the burnout? It's… alright. It pays the bills. I’m starting to think about what I actually  want  to be doing in, like, five years. It's terrifying. Do you ever think about that? Five-year plans? Constantly! It feels like a huge pressure, doesn’t it? I’d love to be doing more specialist training in trauma care, maybe even aiming for a consultant role. And perhaps… living somewhere a bit less chaotic than London. Somewhere with more green space. Oh, where would you go? I've always fancied Devon, or Cornwall.

Honestly, the state of that garden! It’s a jungle out there. I swear, the weeds are winning. Oh, Mum, you always say that! It doesn’t look  that  bad. It just needs a bit of… enthusiastic pruning. Enthusiastic pruning? It needs a bulldozer, love. A bulldozer! I haven't been able to get to it properly since… well, since your father went. It just feels… overwhelming. I know, Mum. I’m sorry. Listen, I can come down next weekend. We can tackle it together. I’m actually off, which is a miracle. Oh, that would be lovely, darling. Really lovely. You always were a good worker in the garden, just like your Nana. Remember how she used to grow those prize-winning roses? Vaguely. Mostly I remember getting stung by bees while trying to “help” her. Oh, she loved you helping, even if you were a nuisance! Speaking of Nana, I’ve been sorting through some old photos… found one of you in that dreadful school uniform. Oh god, not the ties. Please don’t tell me you found a photo of me in that ghastly green and gold tie. Ghastly is a good word for it. Absolutely ghastly. Why on earth they decided green and gold was a good combination, I’ll never know. You looked like a Christmas tree ornament gone wrong. It was a fashion crime, Mum, a  fashion crime . Honestly, even then, I knew it was wrong. All the boys had normal striped ties. It was blatant favouritism for the girls. Well, at least it gives us something to laugh about now. Have you been keeping up with Brenda? She called me yesterday, apparently she’s taken up line dancing. Line dancing?! Brenda? That's… unexpected. Sounds terrifying, actually. Apparently she’s loving it. Says it’s good for the knees. I told her you were doing well at work, she sent her best. She was asking about your… what was it… production controlling? Is that what you said you do? Production Controller, yeah. It's… complicated. Lots of spreadsheets and slightly stressed people. It's alright though. We’re launching a new project next month, which is a bit of a headache. Oh dear. Sounds stressful. You need to take care of yourself, darling. Don’t let them work you too hard. You're a clever girl, you don't need all that fuss. I try not to, Mum.

Right, so I genuinely think I’m failing my stats module. Like, properly failing. Oh no! Really? What’s going on? I thought you were pretty good at maths in sixth form? I  was ! But this isn’t even really maths, is it? It’s, like… applying maths to biology, and it just doesn’t click. All these p-values and null hypotheses, it's just making my head spin. Honestly, I spent six hours yesterday trying to understand one concept and I’m still lost. Ugh, that sounds awful. It's the same with my physics. They expect you to just  know  all this foundational stuff, and I'm sitting there thinking, "When would I have learned this?!" It's a completely different level to A-levels. Exactly! And the lecturer… she’s brilliant, like, a world expert in her field, but she explains things like everyone already knows everything. It’s so intimidating to ask questions. I get that. It’s like, you don't want to be  that  student. Did you try going to her office hours? Yeah, but there were like ten other people there all equally confused. It was chaos. And she spent most of the time going over stuff we already knew, not actually helping with the problem I had. Oh, that's the worst. Maybe form a study group? See if anyone else is struggling and you can help each other? Good shout. I’ve been meaning to ask Chloe, she seems to get it.
