Although last night she was going on about this band she’s obsessed with, some French indie thing, and I just glazed over. I couldn’t understand a single word she was singing either. Oh, is that the one you were trying to translate? The lyrics? Yeah! I spent ages on it, and I think I got about half of it right. It's so frustrating when you can understand the grammar, and the individual words, but the whole meaning just… evaporates. It’s like they're deliberately trying to be obscure. It’s the cultural context, isn’t it? It's not always a direct translation. Speaking of cultural things, did you see the rugby on Saturday? Nope, missed it. I was at a friend’s birthday bash. Apparently, England got absolutely hammered? Absolutely. It was horrific. They were so smug all week, and then they just completely collapsed.

Honestly, I nearly jumped out of my skin this morning. Oh, what happened? Did you see a spider? You know I can’t stand them. Worse, actually. A mouse. In the kitchen. Right by the bin. Oh,  no . Absolutely not. I'd be screaming. We had one a couple of years ago, and it took ages to get rid of it. Dave had to lay traps everywhere. I'm dreading it. I’ve put down some sticky traps, but honestly, I don’t know if I have the stomach to… deal with it if I catch one. It’s horrible, isn’t it? A proper, proper nuisance. At least with spiders, you can usually just shoo them away, though I wouldn't, mind you. Exactly! A spider I can cope with, albeit reluctantly. A mouse is just… different. It feels… dirty. It does, doesn't it? They’re just little creepy things. It’s the thought of where they’ve been. Precisely! And this house is supposed to be sealed up pretty well. I don’t understand how they get in. They squeeze through the smallest gaps, apparently. I heard they can get through a hole the size of a ten-pence piece. A ten-pence piece! Goodness me. I'll have to go around and check everything again. It’s just… it’s been a weird week for wildlife. Oh? What else? Well, there’s a robin that’s been building a nest in the ivy on the front of the house. It’s quite sweet, really, but it’s absolutely  covered  in spiderwebs. It's a bit ironic, isn’t it? The robin's building a home surrounded by spider homes. Oh, that is funny. A bit concerning for the chicks, though, isn’t it? All those spiders lurking. I suppose so. I'm trying not to think about it too much. It’s just… a bit much all at once. Mice, spiders, birds nesting… I feel like I'm living in a nature documentary. You are getting all sorts! Maybe you should get a cat. Though then you’d have another thing to worry about. Oh no, definitely not. I like my furniture too much. Plus, I’m not really a cat person. A good, strong pest control company is probably the way to go. After I steel myself for the sticky traps, of course. Good plan. Don't leave it too long, though.

…and then Grandad, on my mother’s side, he was a farm labourer, down in Dorset. Proper soil under his fingernails sort of man. Apparently quite a character, always telling tall tales. We don't have many pictures, sadly, it was a different time. Did your family stay in Bristol long, then? Oh, generations. My mother’s family, they were all Bristolians, dockworkers mostly. My father’s came up from the valleys in Wales, seeking work, you see. Though he never truly lost his accent, did he? Even after fifty years in England. He was a coal miner originally, then became a bus driver. Hard work, all of it. It’s funny the things that endure, isn’t it? The accents. My mother, she moved to London when she was quite young, but you could still hear the Dorset in her voice, especially when she was tired or telling a story. She was a nurse, you know, for years. Right up until…well, right up until she couldn’t anymore. A nurse, that’s lovely. A caring profession. It must have been hard, seeing her decline. It was. She had vascular dementia. It started so subtly, just little forgetfulnesses, misplacing things. Then it crept up on us, stealing her away bit by bit. The last year was particularly difficult. She didn't recognise me sometimes. It broke my heart. Oh, dear. That’s… awful. It's a cruel disease. My sister, God bless her, she went through something similar with her husband. It changes everything, doesn't it? Everything. It does. It makes you think about what truly matters. And what you want to do with your own life. Which is probably why I ended up a teacher, I think. Wanting to make a difference, somehow. You were a teacher as well, weren’t you? Yes, primary school mostly. Thirty years, all told. Loved it, mostly. The little ones, they just fill your days with joy, don't they? Though the paperwork… heavens, the paperwork nearly did for me! And the parents! Sometimes it felt like I was teaching the parents as well as the children. Oh, I know  exactly  what you mean. You get all sorts. Though I teach secondary, so it’s a different kind of challenge. Teenagers have a way of rolling their eyes at everything you say! But it’s rewarding, seeing them grow and learn. It’s a privilege, really.

Oh look, a hare! Did you see that? Just darted across the field. Yeah, beautiful. They’re so quick, aren’t they? Makes you wonder how they navigate all this…and those. Oh, the pylons. They  are  a bit of an eyesore, aren’t they? Ruin the whole view. Still, better than no electricity I suppose. Though I saw something online about how they affect bird migration. Really? How? Apparently, they disrupt their navigation systems. Something about the electromagnetic fields messing with their internal compasses. It’s awful, isn’t it? We’re always impacting everything else. We are, aren’t we? It makes you think. It's a bit like those hot air balloons you were saying you wanted to go on. Beautiful to look at, but the noise must be awful for the animals. Good point. I hadn't considered that. Though, honestly, just the idea of floating above all this…would be incredible. Imagine the view. I bet. Expensive though, isn’t it? Ridiculously. I was looking at prices, and it's easily a couple of hundred quid for a short flight. Plus, then you need to factor in transport... and a celebratory drink afterwards, naturally. Naturally. We're meant to be saving for a new sofa, remember? This floral monstrosity has to go. I know, I know. The sofa is a priority. It's just... sometimes I feel like we're always  planning  to do things, never actually doing them. Like that camping trip we talked about last summer. Oh, don’t remind me. The weather was dreadful. Rain for a week solid. And then Jasper decided he was going to chase a badger. Oh, that was a disaster. He came back covered in mud, bits of leaves stuck to his fur… and smelling rather strongly of badger. He wouldn’t come near the car afterwards. It took me an hour to get him clean! And he still shook it all over the kitchen. Maybe camping isn’t his thing. Or ours. Perhaps not. It requires a certain level of... resilience. And a lot of wet wipes. Speaking of resilience, have you seen how much Rufus has grown? He’s almost as tall as me now. He's shooting up. It's terrifying. Seems like only yesterday he was a tiny puppy chewing on everything. Now he just stares at you intensely, planning his next mischief. Exactly!

Phew, that was a good session, wasn’t it? Really needed that after a Monday. Aye, it were champion. Gets the blood moving, that. Though I’m starting to feel my age a bit more with each one, I must admit. This knee… Oh no, is it playing up again? You mentioned it last week. Just a twinge, nothing to worry about. More just a reminder I’m not twenty anymore. Though I used to be able to cycle all day without a second thought. Remember cycling around Yorkshire Dales with me dad? Proper hills. Sounds lovely. I’m more of a flat-terrain person myself. Hertfordshire’s very… level. Although, the weather’s been all over the place lately. One minute sunshine, the next it’s pelting down. You can’t trust a British summer, can you? Tell me about it. Typical. Used to be able to rely on a good, solid drizzle in Yorkshire, but even that’s gone unpredictable. How’s teaching going? Still battling with teenagers and subjunctive moods? You know me too well. It’s…a challenge. Actually, I’ve got a student who is really struggling with verb conjugations. It’s like her brain just shuts down when I mention the imperfect tense. Sounds familiar. Sometimes you’ve just got to find a different angle. I find with my staff at the gyms, if I keep telling them the same thing the same way, it just goes in one ear and out the other. You’ve got to tailor the message, you know? Find what motivates  them . That’s a good point. I try to, but sometimes I feel like I’m banging my head against a brick wall. I was reading a book about coaching techniques actually, thinking maybe there’s something I can adapt for the classroom. “The Inner Game of Tennis,” have you heard of it? Can’t say I have. Sounds…intense. I usually stick to biographies, myself. Finished one on Alex Ferguson recently. Fascinating man. The attention to detail… incredible. Oh, I’ve heard good things! I could probably do with some of his motivational skills. Do you ever miss Leeds, living down here? Parts of it. The people, definitely. And the scenery, when it’s not raining. But Solihull’s grown on me. Much more… civilised than Leeds, if I'm honest. Plus, better train connections. And you've got Birmingham on your doorstep, which is handy for concerts.

Right, now, have you put the bins out, love? They’re due today, aren’t they? Yeah, Mum, done it this morning. Before school. Nearly blew away though, it was proper windy. Windy? It's always windy 'round here, lad. Hull bred us tough, y’know. Never mind a bit o’ wind. Aye, that’s right. Though it weren’t like the ‘53 floods, now  that  was a wind. Nearly took the roof off our house. Oh, don’t start on that again, Dad. You’ve told that story a thousand times. Did you remember to lock the shed, Ethan? I don’t want someone pinching the garden tools again. Yes, Mum, locked it. Honestly. You think I’ve not learned after last time? He's a good lad, Ethan is. Always rememberin' things. Unlike some people I could mention… Now now, Mary. Leave the lad be. He’s doin' grand. How’s that marking goin’, lass? Still full of these youngsters and their silly mistakes? Oh, don't even get me started. This year’s lot are particularly bad with their algebra. Honestly, you’d think they didn’t listen in class at all. One lad tried to solve for x by… well, I won’t bore you with the details. It involved drawing a picture of a cat. A cat? Seriously? I wish I was joking! I spend my days correcting nonsense. It's exhausting. Well, it’s a good job, at least. Keeps you busy. Keeps the brain ticking over. Though I don’t understand all this maths stuff. Never could. Numbers just swam before my eyes. Me neither. Always preferred a good crossword. Now  that’s  a challenge. Though they're getting harder, aren't they? Full of obscure words. They are. Ethan’s good at crosswords, actually. He beats me every time. It’s because you only try the easy ones, Mum. That's not true! I attempted the Guardian cryptic last week. Oh, the Guardian! Fancy. We just had the Daily Mail in our day. And a nice cup of tea. That’s all you needed. Aye, a good brew and a biscuit. Can’t beat it. Mary, are you wanting another cuppa? I’ll put the kettle on. Oh, yes please, Dad. I’ll get some biscuits. Ethan, love, are you wanting one before you head off? Yeah, please. Chocolate digestives if you’ve got ‘em.

Honestly, this satnav is driving me round the bend. It insists we go down every single farm track. Do these things  enjoy  sending us into a ditch? It’s probably just trying to be adventurous. Though, admittedly, adventurous isn’t what we need when we’re trying to get to a gig on time. Are you sure you put in the right postcode? Of course, I did! I double-checked it. It’s just… optimistic about what constitutes a road. Remember that time it tried to take us across that field near Penrith? Oh, don’t remind me. We nearly lost a tyre then. It’s a wonder we haven't ended up in a sheep pen yet. Speaking of sheep, haven't seen many today, have you? Usually, this part of the world is teeming with them. No, it is strangely quiet. Maybe they're all at a sheep convention. Though knowing our luck, the satnav is leading us  to  the sheep convention. Possibly. Is it telling you to turn left up that… that barely-there track? It is. It says “in 200 yards, turn left.” I swear, if that’s a track for tractors and not cars… Let’s ignore it. Just keep going straight. I reckon we're better off trusting your instincts, and the road. You’ve lived up here longer than the satnav has even existed. You're probably right. Though my instincts are currently telling me to pull over and have a large gin and tonic. This driving is stressful! Save the gin for the venue. We’re nearly there, I think. What about the wedding, by the way? Any closer to deciding on a venue? Honestly, no. It’s a nightmare. Everyone has an opinion. My sister wants a grand old castle, my mother wants something “rustic and charming”, and I just want somewhere that doesn’t require a 4x4 to get to. Sounds about right. Castles are lovely, but massively impractical. And “rustic and charming” usually translates to “slightly dilapidated and freezing cold”. Exactly! And then there’s the ceilidh band. Apparently, the good ones are booked up for two years. A ceilidh! Wonderful. Though, you know I have two left feet. I'll mostly be clinging to the sidelines. You'll be fine. I'll partner you with someone patient. Someone who won’t notice if you step on their toes every five seconds.

Right, so full English for me then. And a flat white, please. You? Hmm, I’m feeling… healthy-ish. Just avocado on toast and a black coffee. Trying to offset the sheer quantity of pastries we saw on that site visit. Honestly, Mrs. Henderson’s house is basically a gingerbread cottage. It really is. And she wants minimalist Scandi-chic. The briefing was…optimistic. Did you see the floral wallpaper in the downstairs loo? Oh god, yes. The clash was  intense . It's going to be a long project. Speaking of long projects, how’s Liam doing? He seemed pretty stressed on the call yesterday. Oh, don’t even ask. He’s completely overwhelmed. Apparently, old man Hemmings is breathing down his neck about the library extension. He showed me the revisions Hemmings requested – it's basically a complete redesign. He’s barely slept. Hemmings is a nightmare. He thinks brutalism is the pinnacle of architectural achievement. Remember when he tried to convince us that concrete is ‘organic’? Oh god, how could I forget? It was horrifying. Poor Liam. He's a good designer, he just needs someone to give him some space. I told him to stand his ground, but you know how Hemmings is. Yeah. He's got a fortress mentality. Still, Liam needs to learn to be a bit more assertive. It’s a skill. Did you hear about Chloe? Chloe? From uni? No, what’s she up to? I haven't spoken to her in ages. She’s joining that communal living thing in Hackney. Apparently, it’s all about sustainable living and shared resources. Twenty people in a converted warehouse. Twenty people?! That sounds…intense. I mean, I’m all for sustainability, but I value my personal space way too much. I know, right? Though she's really into it. Says it’s about building community and reducing her carbon footprint. She sent me this massively long manifesto about it on Facebook. Oh, Facebook. That’s always a warning sign. Is she still dating that musician? The one with the piercings? Leo? Yeah, still together. He’s apparently building a soundproof recording studio in the warehouse. So, twenty people, a recording studio… sounds like a recipe for chaos. Definitely. It’s a bit like that design studio project we did in second year, remember? The one where we had to design a co-living space for artists?

So, how was Sarah's birthday then? Did you have a good time? Honestly, the traffic getting into Lincoln was  awful  on Saturday. Took me nearly an hour just to get to the bypass. It was good, yeah! Really busy though, she’d managed to get everyone from uni down, plus all of us. It was a bit… chaotic, trying to actually  speak  to her, but fun chaotic. The traffic was horrendous, even coming the other way. Apparently there was some event on at the Showground? Oh, right. Probably that agricultural thing. They never think about the traffic, do they? Just dump thousands of people in the middle of nowhere and expect everything to run smoothly. I swear, some people drive like they’ve never seen a roundabout before. Honestly! I was stuck behind someone who just  stopped  on one yesterday, trying to decide which exit to take. Like, just keep going until you reach the one you want! It's not that hard. Mum nearly had a fit when she was driving back from Spalding last week, apparently someone cut her up on the A16. Oh dear. She hates that road, doesn't she? Always worried about the lorries. You need to be so careful. It’s just…people are so impatient. Think they can just barge their way through everything. Anyway, enough about terrible drivers. Did you manage to chat to Liam much? I haven't seen him since Christmas. A little bit. He’s… good. Really busy with his new job, apparently. He’s doing loads of overtime. He said he’s trying to save for a deposit on a flat. That's good to hear. He’s a sensible lad. It’s awful trying to get on the property ladder these days. It’s just completely impossible for a lot of people. Are you still thinking of going to that festival next month? Yeah, I think so. Chloe's been nagging me to buy tickets. It's just… work's been a bit stressful lately, and I don't know if I'll have the energy for camping and crowds. Oh, that’s a shame. Maybe just a day trip then? You could go for the Saturday, and just come home at night. It might be a nice compromise. I'm free next weekend, if you fancy doing something before then? We could go to that new Italian place in town, everyone’s been raving about it.

So, you’re actually going for it then? The Media Officer role at the Council? Yeah, I think so. I submitted my initial application yesterday. It felt… okay. Not brilliant, but okay. Hence, needing to pick your brain. You’re so good at articulating things, and that bit about ‘demonstrating impact’ completely baffled me. Oh, ‘demonstrating impact’! Ugh, the bane of every job application ever written. Basically, they don’t want to know  what  you did, they want to know  how it changed things . Not “I wrote social media posts,” but “I increased social media engagement by 15% resulting in a measurable rise in public awareness of X campaign.” You know? Quantify everything. Right, okay. So, less ‘I did stuff’ and more ‘this stuff  mattered ’. That makes… slightly more sense. I was just listing my responsibilities, which feels… underwhelming, now you say it like that. Exactly! Think of specific examples. That time you covered the local elections? What reach did that have? Did it generate any follow-up coverage? Did it lead to increased public participation? Dig deep. They want to see you can connect your work to broader outcomes. Hmm. Okay. That elections coverage… I did get a quote picked up by the regional news, and we had a noticeable spike in listeners calling in to the phone-in afterwards. I just… didn’t  write  that down. See! Gold dust! That's a perfect example of impact. Even small things. They know Council jobs aren't always world-changing. They just want to see you understand the bigger picture. What about the competency questions? Are you struggling with those? The ‘managing challenging stakeholders’ one is killing me. I’ve dealt with difficult people, obviously, but phrasing it in a way that sounds professional and not just… 'that bloke from planning was a nightmare’ feels impossible. Right. Okay, try the STAR method. Situation, Task, Action, Result. Set the scene, describe your responsibility, explain what you did and  specifically  how you handled it, and then… the impact bit again! What was the positive outcome of your intervention? Even if it was just mitigating a negative situation. STAR method… okay, I think I remember that from some dreadful training years ago. It feels… formulaic. It is. But it forces you to be specific. And specific is good. They want to see you can think on your feet and handle pressure. And honestly, a well-structured answer is better than a rambling anecdote, even if the anecdote is amazing.

Right, so if we're seriously thinking about this pottery thing, we need a business plan. A proper one. Not just a scribbled note on the back of a beer mat. Agreed. But honestly, the thought of writing a full business plan makes me want to lie down. It feels so…formal. Like going back to uni essays. Well, it’s either that or winging it and ending up broke. I’m leaning towards the plan. And we need to decide on a name. "Mud & Magic"? Too twee? Definitely too twee. How about… “Earthen”? Simple, clean. Reflects the material. Ooh, I like that. “Earthen”. Good. Okay, name sorted. Now, realistically, how much start-up capital are we looking at? A kiln isn’t cheap. No, they’re not. And a decent wheel. Plus, the clay, glazes, tools… I did a bit of digging online. We’re probably looking at around fifteen to twenty thousand Australian dollars to get something functional. Right. That’s… not insignificant. We’d have to really push the savings. And maybe look at a small business loan. I hate the thought of owing money, though. Me too. But it could get us off the ground quicker. We could start small, selling at local markets, build up a following, then maybe look at a studio space. This house-sitting gig is amazing, but long-term, I need to  make  something. I need that creative outlet. I know what you mean. Teaching is rewarding, but it’s… draining. I’m starting to feel creatively stifled. The pottery could be good for both of us, actually. A shared project, a way to spend more time together. Exactly. And you're brilliant at the marketing stuff, the social media, the presentation. I can focus on the actually  making  of things. It’s a good balance. Okay, so first step: research small business loans. I'll look into some grants too. There might be something available for arts-based enterprises. And we need to start sketching out a proper budget. Spreadsheet time. Oh joy. Spreadsheets. Look, while you're doing that, I'll start scouting out kiln suppliers. And maybe begin prototyping some designs. I was thinking, simple mugs, bowls, maybe some small vases to start. Nothing too ambitious. Sensible. We don't want to overstretch ourselves. And we definitely need to think about shipping. Australia’s huge. Getting fragile pottery across the country without it shattering is going to be a challenge.

Honestly, the amount of broccoli he ate tonight was astonishing. I thought he’d chuck it across the room, but he just…gobbled it. Bwoc-oli! More, Mummy! That’s wonderful, dear. Absolutely wonderful. My grandsons were dreadful eaters. All biscuits and juice, they were. You’ve clearly got a good little man there. Though, I do think all this fuss over vegetables is a bit much. We didn’t have this when  I  was bringing up children. Oh, Elsie, you always say that. Times change, don’t they? Less sugar, more awareness of nutrition. Though, I must say, I’ve noticed a distinct lack of proper puddings these days. Where’s the spotted dick? The custard? Progress, I suppose. Though, I’m longing for a proper pudding myself. It's just… trying to find the time to bake with a toddler clinging to your leg is impossible. Speaking of time, did you see young Fiona got engaged? Up in Manchester, apparently. A lovely young man, a doctor. Bit young, perhaps, but they seem very happy. Oh, really? That’s nice. I saw something on Facebook. I’ve barely had a chance to look properly, though. This whole online thing still feels… overwhelming. I feel like I’m constantly playing catch-up. It  is  overwhelming. I finally managed to get the hang of sending emails, and now everything’s moved onto these ‘apps’. Honestly. It’s a conspiracy to make us feel old. Dada! Dada beard! That’s right, little one. Dada’s got a beard. A very distinguished beard, I might add. Though your mother doesn't always approve. It’s not that I  disapprove … it’s just… it tickles when you kiss me! And I end up covered in crumbs. Oh, a beard is a sign of wisdom, you know. A distinguished look. Although, the younger men these days seem to be growing them just to be fashionable. Back in my teaching days, you’d rarely see a teacher with a beard. It wasn't deemed appropriate. It’s just everything’s so different now, isn't it? And getting a house… I heard there’s a real shortage of school places in this area now, too. Apparently, they’re building houses faster than they can build schools. The housing shortage is appalling. Absolutely appalling. It’s the same everywhere, isn’t it? All these young people can’t afford to buy.

Honestly, the referendum… I still can’t believe it. It’s just such a mess, isn’t it? Everything feels…uncertain. Oh, don’t even start me. My brother-in-law, bless him, he was so convinced it would be wonderful. Now he’s moaning about everything going up in price. You can’t fixate on things, can you? Though, it’s hard not to. It is. It feels like everyone has an opinion, and no one is listening. Speaking of things that are frustrating… have you seen the state of the car park at the village hall? Oh, don’t! Old Mrs. Higgins is convinced she’s entitled to a pass just because she volunteers once a month. She was giving me absolute grief about it yesterday. Said her arthritis flares up if she has to walk from the far end. Oh, she's a character, isn't she? Always has been. Remember when she tried to enter Kevin in the fancy dress competition at the summer fete? He was a teddy bear, loosely. Oh my goodness, yes! Poor Kevin was mortified. He was about ten at the time. He didn’t say a word the entire day. It’s funny the things you remember. He’s driving now, isn’t he? He is. Passed his test first time, the show-off. He’s already talking about getting a sporty little number. I’m terrified. Well, he's a sensible lad. He’ll be alright. I worry about your mum, though. She’s been sounding awfully peaky on the phone lately. She has. Her arthritis is playing up again, and she’s got a nasty cough. She won’t go to the doctor, of course. Says it’s just a winter bug, but I’m not so sure. She’s stubborn as an old mule, that woman. She gets that from your dad. Remember him refusing to get his eyes tested for years? Said he could see perfectly well. Until he walked into a lamppost! Oh, Dad. He was a character. It feels strange, doesn’t it? Thinking about people from the past. Old Mr. Davies, from sixth form… remember him? Played the piano beautifully. Oh, yes! He was wonderful. He used to play at the school concerts. I always fancied learning to play, but never got around to it. Now it’s too late, I think. It’s never too late!

Honestly, the amount of time I spend on Twitter these days… it’s ridiculous. And it’s  work . It feels… pathological. Tell me about it. I’ve basically become a professional doom-scroller. It's essential for my role, keeping an eye on what students are saying, what’s trending in education, but… it's draining. Exactly! It's that constant need to be ‘on’. Like if you don’t respond immediately to something, you’re perceived as aloof or uncaring. I had a wee spat with a journalist last week, entirely on Twitter, about some article he’d written. Oh, God. That sounds… delightful? Not delightful. Massively stressful. He’d misrepresented some figures we’d released, and the replies started piling up. Had to construct this carefully worded, incredibly polite demolition of his argument, all in 280 characters. It took, like, an hour. An hour?! For a tweet? A  series  of tweets, strategically spaced. It's a whole art form now, isn’t it? And then you’ve got to monitor the replies to  those  tweets… it's a rabbit hole. It’s mental. I tried to explain to my mum what I do at work, and she just looked at me like I was speaking a different language. “So, you… read what strangers write all day?” Pretty much, yeah. I’ve been trying to automate some of the monitoring, but it's hard to get the algorithm right. I don’t want to miss anything important. I mean, that’s the whole point, isn’t it? But I ended up getting flooded with posts about… cats wearing hats. Oh dear. That's the algorithm for you. Mine keeps trying to sell me survival gear. I don’t even  go  camping. They just assume. It's all data points. Are you using Threads much? I’ve barely touched it. A little. It feels…empty, somehow. Like Twitter but without the rage. Which, admittedly, might be a good thing, but it also feels a bit pointless. Plus, the integration with Instagram is a bit creepy. I already spend too much time comparing myself to curated holiday photos. Aye, true. It's like they’re deliberately trying to make us feel inadequate. I mostly use it for sharing silly memes. Little moments of levity amidst the chaos. Good plan. A bit of joy is essential. Maybe I should dedicate a specific time slot each day for Twitter-related work.

Honestly, the weekend was  chaos . Like, actual, proper chaos. I thought I was going to lose it at one point with Sarah and Ben. Oh no, what happened? Did they have another… disagreement? They seem to specialise in those. Specialise is an understatement. It was about the flat, naturally. Ben thinks Sarah doesn't contribute enough to keeping it tidy, which is…rich, coming from him, considering the state of his desk. She just shut down, and then started crying, and then he started trying to  fix  it by offering to do all the cleaning himself, which just made it worse! Honestly, I just wanted to leave. Ugh, that sounds exhausting. You were just stuck in the middle, weren’t you? The designated peacekeeper. Exactly! And then they both turned to  me  for validation! Like, I’m a neutral party, I can’t pick sides! I just said something about needing more wine, and quickly changed the subject to the horrifying state of my attempt at a lemon drizzle cake. Oh, the cake! How did that go? I was picturing a Pinterest masterpiece. A Pinterest disaster is more accurate. It was…dense. Like, structurally unsound. I think I forgot the baking powder. It’s currently residing in the back of the fridge, a monument to my baking failures. Oh dear. Well, at least it’s a funny story. Speaking of disasters, work was… a lot. We had a patient who was convinced the hospital was broadcasting his thoughts. Oh wow. That must have been…challenging. It was. And then he tried to build a tin foil hat. It took three of us to gently persuade him that wasn’t necessary. Honestly, some days I question my life choices. You’re a saint, honestly. You’re dealing with all that, and I’m stressing about a cake. We all have our battles. Speaking of which, I’m starving. Are you ordering anything? I was thinking pizza. Pizza sounds amazing. I saw a deal on that new Italian place, ‘Bella Notte’… apparently their garlic bread is legendary. Legendary garlic bread? You’ve sold me. Let’s do it. Oh! And maybe we can guilt-trip Mark into joining us? He’s been super quiet lately. Good idea! He’s probably still reeling from his date with Chloe. Apparently, she spent the entire evening talking about her cat. No! That’s a dating red flag if I ever saw one.

So, have you managed to sort out a bed for Uncle David yet? He’s still insisting he can sleep on the sofa, which… well, you know. I’ve told him absolutely not. He’ll break his hip, or more likely, complain about his back for a month afterwards. The spare room’s ready, new bedding, everything. He just  likes  to be difficult. Thinks he's still 25 and can sleep anywhere. He always was stubborn, your brother. Remember when he refused to wear a coat to Auntie Maureen’s funeral? Said he didn’t want to “look like everyone else.” Oh, don’t remind me. Maureen would have had a fit. She always insisted on proper mourning attire. Speaking of which, I’m trying to think of what to make for him. He’s always moaning that he doesn’t get proper home cooking anymore. He’ll moan whatever you make, honestly. He criticised Mum’s roast dinner just last month! Maybe a shepherd’s pie? Safe bet. Shepherd's pie is good. Or a curry? He always enjoyed a good curry, didn’t he? Though he complains it’s never hot enough. Curry it is then. I’ll make a mild one for me and you two, and a volcano for him. And I finally got the new car! Oh, really? The one you were looking at? The little blue one? That’s the one! Picked it up yesterday. It’s so much easier to drive than the old one. Plenty of room for all the shopping, and surprisingly good on petrol. Excellent! You deserved a new car, you really did. That old one was rattling like a box of bolts. Did you manage to get a good deal? I think so. Got a bit of money off, and they gave me a decent trade-in price for the old one. I’m going to try driving it up to Taunton to pick up David. It'll be a good test run. That’s quite a drive though, isn't it? You sure you’re up to it? Perfectly. It’s not  that  far. And much more comfortable than the old car. Anyway, are we all agreed on the meal? Curry, Shepherd’s pie, and… what about a starter? Soup would be nice. Something light. Maybe a tomato and basil? Sounds lovely! And can we possibly avoid talking about politics with David this time?

Honestly, this Spanish…it’s killin’ me, it is. Absolutely killin’ me. I thought French was bad, but this is a whole different kettle of fish. Oh, aye? Still battling with the subjunctive, are we? I warned you, didn’t I? That’s where it gets properly tricky. Tricky? It’s a fiend! A complete and utter fiend! I can conjugate the regular verbs, mostly. And I can order a coffee and ask where the toilet is, but beyond that… forget it. I tried to read a little article about the weather in Madrid… honestly, I understood about one word in ten. You’re not alone, love. It’s a tricky language. I dabbled a bit, years ago, hoping to impress some clients when I was still working. Didn’t get very far, I’m afraid. Rosetta Stone was supposed to be the answer, you know? Immersion and all that. Rosetta Stone? Oh, I tried that! All those pictures... just showing you a cup and then expecting you to know the word for ‘cup’! It's daft, isn’t it? I need grammar explanations, proper constructions. I’m used to teachin’ the stuff, I can’t just  absorb  it like a baby. Exactly! It’s rubbish for people who actually want to  understand  how the language works. I think a good textbook, with clear explanations, is what you need. And maybe a tutor? Someone who can actually point out when you’re going wrong. A tutor… hmm. That’s a thought. I’m loath to spend the money, mind. But I’m paying for Duolingo Plus anyway, and that’s not exactly setting the world on fire. It’s just…memorisation. And the accent! The little robot voice sounds nothing like a real person. It’s the same with a lot of those apps, isn’t it? They teach you phrases, but they don't teach you how to  build  sentences. It’s like giving someone the bricks to build a house, but not telling them how to lay them. Precisely! It's infuriating. It makes you wonder how people ever become fluent. It’s so different from learning German, for example. The grammar's strict, the rules are clear. Spanish just… bends. It feels so fluid and unpredictable. That’s partly because of where it's spoken. Have you thought about Spain and the whole Catalan situation? They effectively speak two languages, right?

Right, so this pile… is basically everything from 2018-2020. Mostly bank statements, a few utility bills… and a concerning number of catalogues. Catalogues. Always the catalogues. Thought we’d gotten rid of those. Used to get them for Kelly Brook, remember? Every month, a new one. I vaguely remember that. Strategic placement, I assume? Strategic, yes. Though she never seemed overly impressed. More amused, really. Anyway, these bank statements… are they all digital now, or do we still get paper ones? Mostly digital. I think the paper ones are just for… backup? And for you, Dad. You prefer paper. Prefer to  see  it, lad. Know where I stand. All this online banking… feels a bit… ethereal. Like the money isn’t actually  there . Fair enough. Right, so I was thinking, we could scan these, create a PDF archive, and then shred the originals. It’ll save a lot of space. Scanning… sounds fiddly. Is that scanner still working? The one you got me for Christmas a couple of years ago? It’s working fine. It’s surprisingly good, actually. I use it for some of my corpus linguistics work. Digitising old texts. It's… fascinating, really, seeing language evolve. Corpus what now? You and your fancy words. Just scan the documents, eh? Right, scanning. I could do a quick batch now. Speaking of which, did you manage to book those flights to Malaga? Almost. Got as far as searching, found a couple of decent deals, but then the website kept buffering. Ended up getting frustrated and making a cup of tea. I’ll try again later. I can take a look later if you want. I’m a bit more patient with those things. Less likely to spontaneously make a cuppa when faced with technical difficulties. Appreciate that, son. You’re a good lad. Actually, while you're being tech-savvy, could you have a look at my laptop? It’s been running a bit slow. Certainly. After the documents. We’ll get it all sorted. You haven’t been downloading anything… questionable, have you? Me? Questionable? Don't be daft. Just a few cooking videos. Trying to learn how to make that paella you had on holiday. Oh, right. The one I couldn't replicate when I tried? Exactly! It requires… finesse. Clearly, I am lacking. Now, these catalogues… straight in the recycling, or do you think there's any potential value in them?

Right, that was a bit of a gamble, wasn’t it? Taking that shortcut. Worth it, I reckon. Saved us a good five minutes, at least. Though, honestly, that was a  really  dodgy petrol station we just passed. Dodgy how? Just… the whole vibe. Looked a bit run down, didn’t it? And the prices were suspiciously low. Always a red flag. Aye, a bit grim looking. Though I was needing petrol, and I thought well, we'll chance it. I’m glad we didn’t, lookin’ back. Definitely. You never know what you’re getting with those places. Plus, the forecourt was tiny. I’d have been struggling to get the car manoeuvred. You and your big motor. Honestly, you need a tank to even turn the corner. Hey! It’s practical. And spacious. You appreciate spaciousness. Aye, well, I appreciate being able to  park  without causing a five-car pile-up. Fair enough. So, are you driving back? Yeah, I said didn’t I? You’ve had your go already. Plus, you’ll be needing to, you know,  concentrate  on work calls. True. Got that client meeting early tomorrow. Though driving makes me anxious when I need to be ‘on’. Just relax. I’m a perfectly capable driver. Even in the dark. I didn’t say you weren’t! It’s just… my brain never really switches off. Oh, look at that biker. Whoa, yeah. Going a bit fast, innit? Bit reckless, to be honest. No helmet. No way! Are you sure? Positive. Just whizzed past. Honestly, it's just…stupid. It is. Absolutely daft. You'd think they’d learn. Exactly. It's not worth the risk. All for a bit of…what? A thrill? It's just showing off. It's madness. I saw a programme once about bikers and how dangerous it is. So many accidents. Makes you think, doesn't it? You'd think they'd prioritize safety. You’d think so. Right, I’m taking this next left. Another mile or so and we're almost there. Sounds good. Just… try not to take  too  many shortcuts. I’m starting to get a bit carsick. Carsick? Seriously? In  my  driving? It's the combination of the winding roads and the impending client meeting. Don't take it personally. I hope this meets your requirements! Let me know if you'd like me to make any adjustments or continue the conversation.

Right, so have you booked your tennis coaching session for next week then? I think Mrs. Davies said she had a space on Tuesday. Ugh, Tuesday’s awful. Double History. Can’t I go Wednesday? Why is Tuesday awful? History isn’t  that  bad, is it? It is when Mr. Henderson is droning on about the Tudors for an hour and a half. It’s like… torture. Well, tennis is important too, you need to keep practicing. You’ve really improved, actually. Your serve has got a lot stronger. Yeah, but I keep double-faulting. It's so frustrating. I watched Alcaraz play the other day— Oh, the young Spanish guy? He’s phenomenal, isn’t he? The energy he has is just incredible. Reminds me a bit of Nadal, actually. Yeah! He’s amazing. He just runs  everywhere . I tried to do that in practice, and I was completely knackered after five minutes. Well, he’s a professional athlete! You can’t expect to have the same stamina. Though, you are getting fitter. Remember when you used to get out of breath just running to the net? Don’t remind me! That was embarrassing. Old Man Hemmings used to just laugh. Hemmings? Still coaching down at the club then? He was a bit… eccentric. I remember him telling me the secret to a good forehand was to ‘think of stroking a kitten’. Oh, he was a character, wasn’t he? A bit odd, but a good coach. You learned a lot from him, even if his analogies were strange. He was alright. But I prefer Mr. Peterson now. He actually understands what I’m trying to do. And he doesn't talk about cats. Peterson. Right. That new one? Is he any good? He's really good. He used to play professionally, apparently. He's shown me loads about footwork and positioning. Says I need to work on my volley. That’s good. It's all about the technique, really. It’s not just about hitting the ball hard. Have you been watching the French Open? Djokovic is looking strong, as usual. Not really. It’s been on while I’ve been revising. Too distracting. You should make time for it. It's good to watch the pros, even if it’s just to pick up a few ideas. Plus, it's good fun to argue about who's going to win.

These napkins are… weird. They look like underpants. Honestly. Don’t be daft, they’re just festive! Though I see what you mean, a bit shaped aren’t they? Seriously, Gran, they  really  do. Like, tiny little elastic waistbands. Right, enough about the napkins. Anyone finished their sprouts? They’re getting cold. I’m still working on mine, dear. They’re lovely this year, much better than last. Not so soggy. Last year’s were… an experience. Like mushy peas in disguise. You always were a fussy eater, weren't you? So, has anyone actually started thinking about Christmas shopping properly? I’ve got a few ideas, but I’m completely overwhelmed. I’ve got a list, a very long list. Mostly online shopping though, I can’t face the Trafford Centre at this time of year. Smart girl. I’ll brave it. Need to get something for… well, everyone. And the turkey needs ordering, hasn’t it? Are we doing a big one this year? We always do a big one! It’s tradition. And your Auntie Brenda always expects leftovers. She’ll be round Boxing Day morning, armed with Tupperware. Speaking of tradition, what's everyone doing on Christmas Eve? Are we still having the board games and that? Hopefully! I’m supposed to be meeting up with some of my uni friends, but I promised I’d be back for the family stuff. We used to have the silliest nicknames for each other, back in first year. Remember ‘Captain Chaos’? Oh, don’t remind me. Some of those were… questionable. Remember when you used to call me 'The Oracle'? Said I always had the answers. You usually did, love. You always knew what was going on. I was thinking about Jake, actually. He’s in Florida with his parents for Christmas. Apparently, it’s roasting over there. Florida, eh? Lucky lad. I’d kill for some sunshine right now. It’s freezing! He keeps sending us pictures of him on the beach. It’s just… rubbing it in a bit, isn’t it? Flying to America feels like another world though, doesn't it? All that airport security. It’s a palaver, isn’t it? But worth it, I think, for a bit of sun. Do you know, I think we don’t treat each other well enough sometimes. We need to appreciate what we’ve got. That’s a bit deep for Christmas dinner, isn’t it?

Honestly, Mum, the amount of admin I’ve had this week… it’s just been relentless. Like, seriously, I’m starting to dream in spreadsheets. Oh, dear. You always were a bit of a worrier, love. Is it that new project with Henderson’s again? That sounded a right pickle. It is, but it’s not just that. Everyone's dumping everything on me because I’m “organised”. It’s infuriating! And then Sarah was complaining about her boyfriend  again … Honestly, it's exhausting being everyone's therapist. Sounds like you're a popular girl, though. Always a good sign. Though I agree, a bit of dumping does get tiring after a while. Reminds me of when young Thomas… Oh, never mind. Old stories. Thomas was always a handful. Though a charming one. So, what's the boyfriend trouble this time? Different girl every week? No, no, it’s the same one. He’s just… emotionally unavailable. She keeps hoping he’ll suddenly open up and be all romantic and vulnerable, but he’s like a brick wall. I told her, "Look, if he hasn’t shown it by now, he’s not going to." Solid advice. Sometimes you just have to accept people are what they are. Speaking of accepting things, how's the cooking going? Smells lovely in here. Is that the chicken you promised? It is! I actually attempted a new marinade. Fingers crossed it doesn't taste like petrol. I was reading a food blog and found this recipe… Oh, blogs. Always a gamble, those. Remember when I tried to make that soufflé I saw online? It collapsed before it even left the oven! Phil was laughing for a week. He always did enjoy a good disaster in the kitchen. Brings people together, doesn’t it? Though, I must say, your roast dinners are legendary, Margaret. You’ve never had a collapse yet. Years of practice, dear. Years of practice. So, how are things at work, John? Still battling with the fluctuating grain prices? You have no idea. It's a nightmare. One minute we're looking at a good profit, the next… well, let's just say it involves a lot of phone calls and frantic calculations. It’s all a bit precarious, really. Makes you appreciate a stable income. It does. I'm already dreading thinking about saving for a deposit for a house. It feels so impossible with the way things are.

Right, so I was thinking, shall we just do pasta with that sauce I made earlier? It’ll be quick. Sounds good to me. Anything to avoid another pizza night, honestly. We’ve had far too many pizzas this week. I know, it's a bit shameful, isn’t it? Though, I did see Marks and Spencer are doing those stone-baked ones now… the ones with the fancy toppings. Oh, don’t even  start . M&S are tempting, they really are. They’ve revamped the whole food hall, haven't they? It's dangerous going in there. It is! I went in for oat milk yesterday and came out with a posh lemon curd and some little madeleines. It’s a trap. Exactly! Anyway, pasta is a good call. How was your appraisal? Did the boss give you a raise? Ugh. It was… fine. Lots of talk about ‘synergy’ and ‘optimising workflows.’ No raise, unsurprisingly. She said I was ‘valued’ but ‘budget constraints’ are a thing. You know the drill. Classic. They always say that. "Valued, but…" It’s infuriating. So, same old, same old then? More transcribing, more “valuing”? Pretty much. I did manage to subtly point out how much work I’ve taken on recently, but it didn’t seem to make much difference. I might start looking around, honestly. You should. You deserve more than “valued”. Oh, did you see that thing on the news about the horses being mistreated? Absolutely dreadful. Yes! It was awful. The conditions they were kept in… I can’t even bear to think about it. It's just so cruel. It really gets to me. Animals can't defend themselves. Speaking of things that are getting to me, I’m stuck on this crossword clue. It’s ‘domestic feline, five letters.’ Erm… cat? Oh, for goodness sake! Of course it's cat. I was trying to think of something clever. I’m clearly losing it. Happens to the best of us. I found a bottle of wine the other day, been lurking at the back of the cupboard for… fourteen years, I think. Fourteen years?! Is it even drinkable? I’m almost scared to find out. I might just use it for cooking. It’s a red, I think. Probably best. Did you manage to catch  Trapped  last night? No, I was lost in  The Walking Dead  again. Honestly, that show is addictive, even though it’s relentlessly grim.

Honestly, I’ve spent way too much money this month. Like, legitimately too much. Tell me about it! I went a bit wild on ASOS last week. Ended up ordering, like, three different versions of the same skirt. Don't even ask. What did  you  splurge on? Oh god, don't even get me started on ASOS. It's a black hole for my bank account. I think I need to delete the app. I impulse-bought a sequin top last night. A SEQUIN TOP. What am I even doing with my life? Sequins are always a good idea. You'll need something sparkly for tonight, won't you? Speaking of which, what are we all wearing? I’m thinking black jeans and… well, I don’t know what top yet. I was thinking a little black dress? I got one in New Look the other day, it's pretty simple. But I’m already regretting my shoe choice. I’ve got these new heels, they look amazing, but they’re KILLING me. I wore them for like, ten minutes around my room and my feet are already screaming. Heels are the enemy. Seriously. I’m sticking to boots. Comfy boots. And probably layering up, it’s freezing out there. I’m debating the heels situation too. I have these strappy ones that I love, but I know I'll be regretting it by 11pm. Maybe trainers? Is that tragic? No way! Trainers are totally acceptable. Comfort is key, especially if we're planning on having a proper dance. I’m leaning towards jeans and a nice top, definitely trainers. Yeah, sensible choices all round, I think. We’re not trying to end the night hobbling home. Right, drinks? Who's pre-ing? I'm in. I've got some prosecco chilling. But not too much, don't want to be a mess! Prosecco sounds good. Just one or two, maybe. Don't want to peak too early. I’m already worried about remembering everything tomorrow. Me too. I’ve got that presentation on Monday, and if I’m honest, I haven’t even started it. Maybe a night out is exactly what I need to… temporarily forget about it. We all need to forget about something! Let’s just focus on having a good time. And maybe not buying any more sequin tops. Absolutely. No more impulse purchases. Tonight is about dancing, laughing, and maybe slightly regrettable life choices.

Honestly, it’s just… exhausting being around her sometimes. Right, Aunt Carol? What’s she done now? Oh, you know. Just relentlessly positive. Like, aggressively so. Everything is “wonderful” and “a blessing” even when the cat threw up on her new rug. Classic Carol. She’s… a force of nature, isn’t she? A force of nature that needs to be contained in a soundproof room. It’s not that I  want  to be negative, it’s just… unrealistic. And she makes me feel guilty for feeling anything remotely less than ecstatic. I get it. It’s like she's on a permanent spiritual journey and expects everyone to be on the same path. Exactly! And she keeps going on about “soul mates” and finding “your purpose.” As if life is just one big self-help retreat. She thinks we haven’t found our soul mates, doesn't she? Oh,  absolutely . She subtly, and not-so-subtly, suggests we need to be more “open to the universe” to attract the right person. She tried that with me at Christmas. Asked if I was truly  fulfilled  in my relationship. Nearly choked on my mince pie. Oh, God. She does that. It’s like she's auditioning us for… enlightenment, or something. Well, you and I seem to be doing alright, don't we? Nearly fifteen years, a lovely house, two well-behaved children… We're doing okay. Though I do sometimes wonder what it would be like to live in, say, 17th-century Amsterdam. No Carol, no expectations, just canals and tulips. Now  that’s  a thought. Though I’m not sure my IT skills would be terribly useful. Perhaps Victorian London? Lots of interesting engineering going on. Ooh, good one. We could throw an amazing party, Victorian style. Huge ballroom, string quartet, everyone in top hats and long dresses… And you’d be the hostess with the mostest. Making sure the canapés are perfectly arranged. Of course. And you’d be in the corner, secretly wondering how to automate the ballroom lighting. Someone needs to bring a bit of the 21st century to the past. Listen, I’m really sorry. I completely forgot to pick up the dry cleaning today. Oh, no worries. I can grab it tomorrow. Honestly, I'm just enjoying this. Imagining an extravagant party is far more fun than dealing with reality. And Aunt Carol. Agreed. Reality can wait.

Honestly, the amount of paperwork for even the smallest thing at work is…criminal. It's like they  want  us to fail, you know? Just endless forms. Tell me about it. Even getting a day off sick feels like applying for a mortgage. They need a doctor’s note for everything these days, even a sniffle! It’s the same here. Though, it’s mostly the HR side I deal with, thankfully. People are off for the most bizarre things. Last week, someone called in saying they were “emotionally exhausted” after a particularly stressful game of Candy Crush. Oh, no! You're joking! I wish I was. Honestly. I had to explain to my boss why we can’t just give someone sick pay for digital fatigue. It’s a slippery slope! Wow. I thought my boss was strict. She keeps going on about 'presenteeism' – needing to  look  busy even if you've nothing to do. It’s exhausting. It's ridiculous, isn't it? You used to just…work. Now you have to  perform  working. Speaking of exhausting, how's the little one? Is she sleeping through the night yet? Sort of. We get maybe four hours, then she’s up for a feed. It’s…character building, let's say. Though, honestly, I'm thinking of taking up knitting to get through the night feeds. It seems so calming. Oh, knitting is wonderful! I started a scarf last year, haven't finished it yet. It's bigger than me now, honestly. You get so lost in the rhythm of it. Much better than doom-scrolling on your phone, that’s for sure. I always admire people who can knit. I tried once, ended up with a tangled mess of wool and a very frustrated cat. My creative talents lie elsewhere, apparently. Mum tried teaching me when I was little and I was… less than enthusiastic. She’s brilliant at it though, makes the most amazing jumpers for everyone. It’s funny, isn't it, how generational things are? My gran could turn a scrap of fabric into anything. Now, it’s all fast fashion and disposable items. It is. It’s a shame. It feels like we're losing a lot of those skills. Have you seen that show about renovations, the one where they restore old buildings? It’s fascinating. They uncovered a graveyard under one house the other day!

Honestly, I’m starting to think Millie’s just…making this up. About the landlord. Making what up? The damp? She sent photos, didn't she? Looked pretty grim. The  reason  for the damp. She said he blamed it on her, like, she wasn't ventilating properly. But she literally doesn't cook, and keeps the windows open all the time! It’s just a dodgy roof. Oh, classic landlord move. Gaslighting, basically. They always try to put the blame on you to avoid fixing anything. Yeah, it’s awful. Is she actually gonna fight it though? Last I heard she was just resigned to living with a permanent mushroom farm in her bedroom. She  says  she's going to, but she's also saying she might just move in with Ben. Which… I don't know. Ben's flat is like, deliberately messy. It’s a health hazard. Ben’s a lovely guy, but his hygiene is… questionable. Remember that time we went round and there were dishes growing their own ecosystem? Oh god, yeah! It smelled like a zoo in there. Honestly, she’d be swapping one problem for another. Exactly! I told her, I was like, ‘Millie, a dodgy roof is bad, but sentient bacteria is worse.’ She just laughed. She's weirdly okay with chaos. She’s a free spirit. Speaking of chaos, did anyone actually manage to understand the student finance email? I think they’ve changed the tax code again. No, it’s a disaster. I spent like an hour on hold with them yesterday, and all I got was elevator music and a woman who sounded deeply, deeply bored. I think I’m still liable for council tax though, even though I'm a full-time student. That’s ridiculous! They always try and pull that one. You need to fill out the CWF1 form. It proves you're exempt. CWF1… right, adding that to the ever-growing list. Honestly, sorting out adulting is significantly harder than my astrophysics degree. Tell me about it. I’m still trying to figure out how to do laundry without everything turning pink. Oh, the dreaded pink washing. That’s a rite of passage. You've gotta separate your colours, love. It's basic. I know, I know! I just… forget. It's like my brain actively sabotages simple tasks. Anyway, are we still on for the football tonight?

Honestly, this octopus salad is amazing. You absolutely have to try some, Liam. Octopus? Nah, I’m good. Looks a bit… alien. Come on, Liam, be adventurous! It's really good. Mum's right. You only live once, yeah? It  is  surprisingly good. I wasn’t expecting much, to be honest. Croatian cuisine is really stepping up. Though, I still miss a proper Sunday roast. Don’t start on the roasts, David. We’re in Istria! Appreciate the fresh seafood. Speaking of, how’s university going, Jess? Any dramas? It's okay, Mum. Busy, obviously. Got a big essay due next week on postmodern literature, which is… fun. Honestly, it feels like half the course is just trying to  understand  what the lecturers are talking about. Postmodern what-now? Sounds boring. I have a history test on the Tudors on Monday. The Tudors, excellent. Always a fascinating period. Lots of intrigue, beheadings… good stuff. Just concentrate on King Henry VIII and his wives, Liam. You’ll be fine. How’s school otherwise? Are you still getting the bus, or are you cycling? The bus. Cycling’s too much effort. Old Mrs. Higgins drives the bus now. She keeps shouting at everyone. Sounds like Mrs. Higgins hasn’t changed then. Remember when she told me off for having my headphones in? Headphones! The audacity! It’s a wonder you weren’t expelled. Oh, don’t be silly, David. She just likes to keep an eye on everyone. Speaking of keeping an eye on things, did you see Sarah posted pictures of her new tattoo on Facebook? The one of the little dog? Ooh, no! I need to check. She's always getting tattoos. Is it a good one? Tattoos are cool. I want one when I’m older. Maybe a dragon. A dragon, eh? Your mother might have something to say about that. Don't start, David. He's just expressing himself. It's just a thought. Honestly, it's better than him getting a moped. Remember what happened to Ben next door? Oh god, don’t remind me. Broken leg and a ruined moped. Not worth it. Speaking of ruined things, the state of the supermarkets back home is a disgrace. Everything’s costing a fortune. I was talking to a colleague who's a project manager at Tesco, and even  he  was complaining. Oh, don’t get me started on the supermarkets.

So you got back alright then? No trouble on the roads? Oh, alright. A bit of a slog, mind you. M25 was a car park, as usual. But we made it. Honestly, I’m knackered. That was a long drive for an old boy like me. Oh, bless you. You always say that, though. You’re fitter than you let on, Arthur. Did you enjoy Cornwall though? Was the YHA alright? Aye, YHA was good. Lovely lot of people. All ages, mostly younger stuff, but really friendly. Spent most of my time helping in the kitchen, washing up. Couldn’t let them young ‘uns do all the work, could I? Good on you. Always lending a hand. Did you get to see much of Cornwall besides the YHA? Oh, a bit. We had a day trip to Land’s End. Blimey, that’s a windy spot. And we went to see the lighthouse at Lizard Point. Massive thing, it was. Proper impressive. We walked along the cliffs… bit hairy in places, I’ll tell you. Oh, the Lizard! Beautiful. I always wanted to go there. You’d love it, Malcolm. All those rugged rocks and… and the sea air. I have been, actually. Years ago. Remember we tried to do ‘Yorkshire in a Day’ and nearly killed ourselves cycling over those hills?    Oh, don’t remind me! That was a disaster. My bottom ached for a week. Speaking of aches, my knees are playing up something terrible after all that walking. Think I need a new pair. Oh dear. I’ll make you a nice cup of tea, Arthur. That usually helps. Did you take many photos? I’d love to see them. Got a few. Mostly of the sea, and that lighthouse. And one of a bloke selling crabs down in Polperro. Massive crabs they were. Bigger than my hand! Though, honestly, I thought they were a bit overpriced. Crabs, eh? Always a bit of a rip-off, aren't they? Still, good to experience the local delicacies. I saw some lovely pictures of Polperro. It's so quaint. Were there many tourists? Oh, aye. Packed, it was. School holidays, you see. But it didn’t spoil it too much. It was just… nice to be somewhere different. Somewhere not full of traffic lights and roundabouts. Sounds lovely. Glad you enjoyed it. Now, tell me, did you meet anyone interesting?

This is actually really good, isn’t it? You’ve outdone yourself, Chloe. Proper comfort food. It is! Seriously, after a week of Pret sandwiches, this is heaven. You really didn’t have to cook, you know. Aye, it’s brilliant. More’n I usually get, this. Usually it’s beans on toast, if I’m lucky. Oh, don’t say that, Liam! You deserve better than beans on toast every night. Don’t you get sick of it? Nah, it fills a hole. Gets me through. Though, I’ll never turn down a proper meal like this. What  is  in it, actually? Smells a bit… exotic. It’s a Thai green curry. She found a recipe online. Apparently, it's relatively healthy too, which is a bonus. Relatively. There's a fair bit of coconut milk involved. But loads of veg! And chicken, obviously. How’s everything going with Sarah, Liam? You’ve been a bit quiet lately. Oh, you know. Same old. Bit of a mare, to be honest. She keeps moaning about me working away. Says I’m never around. That’s rough. It must be hard being away so much for work. It is, but it pays the bills. And she knew what it involved when we got together. She just… seems to want more now. Wants me to be home every night having dinner and watching telly like everyone else. That's fair enough, isn't it? It's not unreasonable to want to spend time with someone. Are you making any effort to, you know,  be  there when you’re home? Like, really present? What do you mean? Like, put your phone away. Actually listen. Help with the chores. It’s the little things, isn’t it? When you’re here, really  be  here. She’s right, you know. It’s not just about physically being in the same room. Sometimes it's about quality time. I've seen it with Ben and I. He's always on his laptop working, even when we're supposed to be having a night in. Drives me mad. Ben’s always working, though. It's his job. I don't have a laptop full of spreadsheets. Just... bits and pieces. I try to help out. But do you  really  try? Sorry, I’m just being honest. You sound a bit… resigned to it. I don't know. Maybe I am.

Oh my god, you are back! How was Barcelona? Honestly, fill me in. I feel like I’ve missed a whole life while you’ve been gone. It was…intense. Good intense, mostly. So much walking. My feet are actually still recovering. And the tapas… oh, the tapas. I think I gained about half a stone just in patatas bravas. Worth it! I knew you’d go hard on the food. Did you manage to get to Park Güell? I’ve seen so many pictures. We did! It was absolutely rammed, though. Like, shoulder-to-shoulder people. But the views were insane. And Gaudi is just… a genius, isn’t he? I’m already planning to go back and do more Gaudi stuff. Maybe Paris next? We always said Paris. Paris would be amazing. Though, a bit chilly maybe? We could do a pre-Christmas trip. Ooh, or even Rome! I fancy Italy. We need to start saving though, both of us. My overdraft is currently weeping. Tell me about it. Speaking of weeping, how was  your  weekend? Quiet, I assume, compared to my chaotic wandering? Surprisingly eventful, actually. Remember I said my cousin, Chloe, was finally getting serious with Ben? Vaguely. The one who used to date… what was his name… Ethan? That’s the one! Well, Ben proposed. At a bowling alley. Apparently, he got down on one knee mid-throw and nearly took someone out with the bowling ball. Apparently it was very ‘them’. Oh my god, that is  brilliant . Chloe deserves a bit of chaos, honestly. She’s always been so…organised. So, engagement party to look forward to then? Definitely. Mum’s already planning it, naturally. It’s going to be a full-blown affair. Anyway, enough about family drama. What about your boyfriend, how is Leo? Did you miss him while you were away? I did, actually. We had a proper video call last night. He’s good, really busy with work as always. He’s been binge-watching that new sci-fi show, ‘Severance’. Have you seen it? Heard of it, haven’t gotten around to it yet. Is it good? I’ve been stuck in a ‘Great British Bake Off’ hole for the last week. Pure comfort viewing. It’s…weird. But good weird. Properly thought-provoking. You’d love it. We should have a TV night this week, catch up. I'm free Friday?

…and honestly, the amount of paperwork was just…criminal. For a supposedly creative job, it was utterly stifling. Three years I did supply teaching, and three years of feeling like a glorified administrative assistant. Tell me about it. Though, at least you were  attempting  something creative. My first proper job out of uni? Data entry. For a…a windscreen wiper company. Honestly. It was soul-destroying. Just endless spreadsheets of windscreen wiper dimensions. Oh, no! That sounds awful. Windscreen wipers! Did you last long? Six months. Six months of my life I’ll never get back. I lasted longer than the guy next to me, though. He quit after a week, apparently started leaving passive-aggressive notes on the spreadsheets about the futility of existence. Oh, bless him. I can see that. I did try retail for a bit, between degrees. Worked at a garden centre. Garden centres are surprisingly cutthroat, aren’t they? All that passive aggression about compost. Exactly! And the seasonal staff… the despair in their eyes. Plus, having to explain to people, for the fifth time, the difference between a petunia and a geranium. It just… wore me down. That’s when I decided teaching was the way to go, at least I could unleash my inner pedant on a captive audience. A captive audience. That’s a good way to put it. I’ve always admired teachers, honestly. The patience alone… I tried my hand at a few start-ups, mostly tech-related. Most of them failed spectacularly. Really? You seem to be doing pretty well now. This one’s…different. Learned a lot from the failures, though. Mostly learned that I’m terrible at predicting market trends and even worse at managing people. Took me three crashes and burns to realise I was better off focusing on what I actually  enjoyed  doing. Now I just build websites for small businesses. Much less pressure. That sounds…sensible. A foreign concept to my younger self, certainly. I was always chasing…the grand artistic gesture, you know? Something meaningful. Ended up grading essays about  Lord of the Flies  instead. Hey,  Lord of the Flies  is pretty meaningful! Gets kids thinking. Though, I imagine it gets a bit repetitive after a while. What age do you teach? Secondary. English Literature. It's…challenging. But rewarding. Sometimes. Mostly challenging. I imagine so. My niece is at secondary school, she’s currently trying to convince me that TikTok is a legitimate art form.

Honestly, I’m starting to think living with Liam and Chloe was a mistake. Oh, here we go. What's happened now? Did Liam leave his dishes in the sink  again ? Worse. He’s decided he’s a culinary genius and cooked a full roast dinner at 11pm last night. The smell… it permeated everything. I woke up smelling of Yorkshire pudding. Oh, Liam. He does have a habit of being…enthusiastic. Enthusiastic is one word for it. Chloe just enables him! She was cheerleading him on, offering him gravy boats and seasoning. It was chaos. And then they left the kitchen a disaster zone. Right. So, a burnt offering to the god of late-night feasts? Basically. And now, this morning, Liam’s complaining he’s ‘absolutely shattered’ after his midnight cooking spree. Like  I’m  supposed to feel sympathetic. Sounds about right. He’s good at that, isn’t he? Playing the exhausted artist after creating some sort of mess. Exactly! And Chloe’s just quietly cleaning up after him, pretending everything is normal. It’s… infuriating. I feel like the only one who actually cares about keeping the place tidy. They’re both a bit… bohemian, aren't they? You’re a little more… structured. Structured?! Is that what we’re calling it? I’m calling it ‘having basic respect for shared living spaces!’ I even left a passive-aggressive note about the dishes yesterday, and it was gone this morning. Vanished! Like it never existed. Probably Chloe. She probably discreetly binned it to avoid a confrontation. She’s a peacemaker, that one. A peacemaker who enables chaos! Honestly, I’m starting to consider moving out. Even if it means finding somewhere awful, just to escape. Woah, hold on. Don't make any rash decisions. It's only been a few months, hasn't it? Maybe it just takes time for everyone to find their rhythm. Their rhythm of nocturnal roast dinners and passive aggression avoidance? I’m not sure that’s a rhythm I want to be a part of. Look, maybe you could just… have a chat with them? A calm, rational conversation? Suggest a rota for cleaning, or maybe a ‘no cooking after 10pm’ rule? I’ve tried! It just ends up with Liam talking about his artistic process and Chloe apologizing for him. It's exhausting. Okay, fair enough. Maybe I could talk to them?

Oh, that was a busy shop wasn’t it? Didn’t half take them ages to get served at the checkout. Tell me about it. Young lad serving, looked like he hadn’t a clue what he was doing. Fumbling with everything. I offered to help, mind you, but he just waved me away. Said he was “getting there.” Bless him. Probably his first week. Still, shouldn’t mean  we  have to queue for twenty minutes. I nearly said something, but thought better of it. No good getting into a kerfuffle. Exactly. Not worth the stress. Did you get everything on the list? Yes, I think so. Let's see… the cat food, the biscuits…oh, and the cough sweets for you. You were sounding a bit croaky earlier. Ah, good thinking. These coughs get worse this time of year. Damp, you know. Always gets into my bones. Here, let me take that bag. Feels heavy. It is a bit. I got a decent sized melon. Thought we could have some with our tea tonight. Lovely. Melon sounds good. Did Mrs. Higgins have her shopping delivered alright? I saw the van go past earlier. She did. I had a quick word with the delivery driver. Said she was pleased as punch. Apparently, she got a nice young man and he even carried it inside for her. That's good of him. Some of them wouldn’t lift a finger. Remember old Mr. Peterson? Complained for weeks the driver left his bread on the doorstep in the rain. Oh, that was a saga. He was forever complaining about something. Still, he was a good neighbour at heart, I suppose. Bit of a grumble-bum, though. That he was. Should’ve put a bit more effort into keeping his garden tidy, though. Looked like a jungle, it did. Well, he wasn’t as mobile as he used to be, was he? I suppose it’s hard when you get older. Things just get… difficult. True enough. Still, a bit of weeding wouldn't have killed him. Right, shall we unpack this lot then? I'll get a knife for the melon. Sounds good. Perhaps a cup of tea first, though? All that shopping’s worn me out. Now there’s a suggestion I can certainly get behind. Tea it is. And a biscuit, of course. Naturally. A biscuit is essential. Right you are.

Right, now then, has anyone seen my glasses? I swear I left them on this table. Not me, Gran. Did you check by your chair? You were reading the paper earlier. I did, lad, I did. Not there. Arthur, love, have  you  seen them? My eyesight isn't what it was, you know. Not a clue, Doris. Though knowing you, you’ve probably got ‘em perched on your head again. Oh, for goodness sake! Here they are. Honestly, I’m getting senile. Happens to the best of us, Gran. Don’t you be saying that to your mother, young man! She’ll have your hide. Speaking of which, has she finally tackled that overflowing laundry basket? It’s a hazard to navigation. Now, now, Doris. I’ve been a bit busy marking GCSE papers. Honestly, some of their algebra… it’s appalling. I swear they’ve never even  seen  a bracket. GCSEs eh? Still at it then? Thought you’d have had enough of them after all these years. You’d think so, wouldn’t you? But it keeps the brain ticking over. Besides, someone has to make sure the next generation can, at least, balance their chequebooks. Balancing chequebooks? Who even  has  chequebooks anymore? It’s all contactless now, Gran. Contactless? Sounds dangerous to me. All these newfangled things. I still prefer cash. You know where you are with cash. Aye, cash is king, Doris, cash is king. Remember when young Timothy tried to pay for his sweets with a five pound note and the shopkeeper thought it was a forgery? Oh, I remember that! Poor Timothy was mortified. The shopkeeper scrutinized that note for a good five minutes. That sounds like something that would happen. He always was a mischievous one, that boy. Still is, I reckon. Are you sure you've got enough blankets on the sofa bed for tonight, love? You don't want to be shivering. Yes, Mum. I sorted it earlier. Plenty of blankets and a hot water bottle. You two just focus on relaxing. Relaxing is what we're good at. Doris, dear, fancy a biscuit? I spotted a tin of digestives in the kitchen. Don't mind if I do, Arthur. And maybe a cup of tea. A nice strong brew. I’ll get the kettle on, shall I? And maybe sneak a biscuit myself. Help yourself, lad. Just don't tell your grandparents I said so.

Honestly, this wait is ridiculous. I thought we were supposed to be seen at ten? It's creeping towards half past now. Tell me about it. I skipped breakfast for this, thinking it wouldn't be a long thing. Now I'm regretting all life choices. My flatmate’s been going on about this new protein powder he got. Apparently, it's made with, like, cricket flour? Cricket flour? Seriously? That sounds…unpleasant. Does it taste of legs? That's the image I didn’t need before eleven in the morning. He's convinced it’s the future though. Sustainable protein, apparently. He was showing me the Instagram ads, all toned bodies and eco-conscious slogans. Right. Sounds like marketing genius. I’m more a ‘eat a sensible amount of chicken’ kind of guy. Speaking of genius, has anyone figured out how to get that new streaming service to work on a VPN? I keep getting blocked. I tried yesterday. No joy. Kept saying “location not supported.” I think they’re cracking down hard. Honestly, it's easier just to pirate it at this point, isn’t it? Don’t say that too loud! But yeah, it's a bit of a joke. They want our money but make it five times harder to give it to them. My nan keeps trying to convince me she’s ‘tech savvy’ because she can use Facebook. But then she forwards me chain letters about Bill Gates giving everyone £5000 if you share it. Oh god, classic Nan. Mine sends me inspirational quotes over WhatsApp with massive fonts and glittery backgrounds. It’s…a lot. It’s endearing though, isn't it? My aunt keeps emailing me entire articles she’s found online, highlighted in bright yellow. She thinks I’m a journalist now or something. Aw, that’s sweet. Are you still keeping up with the gym, by the way? I keep meaning to go, but uni’s just been so hectic. I’m trying, sort of. I did a spin class last week and nearly threw up. Reminded me why I stick to running. I went for a hike in the Peaks last weekend. Beautiful scenery, terrible blisters. Worth it, though. Honestly, anything beats staring at a screen all day. Actually, talking of screens, have you guys seen that new show, “Crimson Tide”? It’s on… well, it  would  be on the streaming service I can't access.

Right, shopping list. Mum, you’re better at remembering stuff than me. What milk do we need? Just the usual, semi-skimmed. And get some of those little yogurts for Leo, the strawberry ones are his favourite. Yeah! And biscuits! Chocolate digestives. Always biscuits, eh, Leo? You’ll be needing to run an extra mile at school if you keep that up. Alright, milk, yogurts, chocolate digestives… Anything else? Fruit? Apples and bananas, definitely. And a cucumber for salads. Oh, and don’t forget loo roll, we’re almost out. Ewww, Mum! What? It needs doing, Leo! Someone has to buy it. Noted. Loo roll, apples, bananas, cucumber… Oh, and I saw a massive spider in the bathroom earlier. Absolutely huge. A spider? Where? I’ll get the spray. Honestly, they seem to multiply in this house. Can we get one of those electric fly swatters? They’re brilliant! You just  zap  them. That’s a good idea, Leo. Mum? I’m not keen on zapping things, Leo. It feels a bit… cruel. Honestly, just leave it. Most spiders are harmless. Easier said than done when it's the size of my hand! I ended up trapping it under a glass. Right, I’ll deal with it after dinner. Speaking of which, anyone feeling peckish? I’m starving. I am! Can we have chips? Chips again, Leo? You had chips yesterday. But I want chips! How about we have soup and a sandwich? It’s quick and easy. Ugh, fine. But can I have a chocolate biscuit  with  my sandwich? A man after my own heart. Go for it, Leo. Okay, soup and sandwiches it is. Oh, and I got bitten by something last night. On my ankle. It’s really itchy. Oh dear. Let me see. It’s a bit swollen. Could be a mosquito bite, or a midge. Have you put any cream on it? No, not yet. I just…ignored it. Silly girl! You’ll get infected. I’ve got some antihistame cream upstairs, I’ll get it for you. Speaking of itchy things, did you see that game yesterday? United were dreadful. Absolutely dreadful. Yeah! They were rubbish! I was hoping they’d win. I didn’t watch it. Was too busy marking essays. You missed a disaster, believe me. They need a new striker, that’s for sure. They’re relying too much on Rashford. Here you go, love.

Honestly, P.E. today was  brutal . Miss Henderson made us do shuttle runs for, like, ages. No way! Seriously? I managed to get out of it. Told her my ankle was hurting. You are so good at that! I wish I could lie that convincingly. My face just goes bright red. She'd totally see through me. It’s a skill, honestly. Anyway, science was… science. Mr. Davies just droned on about atoms again. I swear he’s been saying the same thing for three years. Ugh, I know! And then he asked us about isotopes and I was just staring blankly. Did you understand any of it? A little bit. Hannah did. She’s always so on it. Did you see what Chloe posted on Instagram last night? Oh my god, yes! That picture from the party? She looks amazing. And everyone was there. Why weren’t we invited?
