I know, right? So annoying. I heard from Sarah that it was Liam’s birthday. Apparently, he only invited people from his netball team. Seriously? That’s so unfair! He talks to us in class all the time. He’s just… Liam. Have you seen that new video from Kurzgesagt? The one about black holes? Oh, yeah! I started watching it, but then I got distracted scrolling through TikTok. It was really good though, right? They explain everything so well. So good! It makes science actually interesting, which is more than Mr. Davies can manage. Remember when Emily tripped over in the canteen last week? Oh my gosh, YES! And spilled her entire lunch everywhere. It was awful, but also… kind of funny. I felt so bad for her, but I was trying so hard not to laugh. Everyone was staring. Mrs. Peterson totally gave her a lecture about walking and eating at the same time. Like, come on, it was an accident! She's so strict. She is. Honestly, some of the teachers are just… ugh. I heard a rumour that Mr. Thompson is leaving. WHAT? No way! Where’s he going? He’s the best history teacher. Apparently, he got a job at a school in London. Someone said he wanted a bigger challenge. That's so sad! Who are we going to get instead? Please don’t let it be someone boring. I know, right? Fingers crossed. Have you been watching that Ella Rose channel? The one about school hacks?

Honestly, I feel like death warmed up. My throat is absolutely killing me. Oh, no! That’s awful. Are you sure it’s just a cold? You were moaning about your stomach yesterday too, weren't you? Yeah, but I think that was just… Lloyd Grossman’s sauces. Don't judge, I was craving a korma. It tasted a bit off though, looking back. Probably best to stick to things I actually  make  from scratch, eh? Probably. You did look a bit green around the gills. I’m still convinced you have a super-immune system though. You rarely get ill. That’s what I thought! Which is why this is so shocking. I feel genuinely rubbish. It's like a full-body ache, and my nose is running like a tap. Have you taken anything? Paracetamol? Lemsip? The whole arsenal? Yeah, Lemsip. Loads of it. It’s taking the edge off, but I just feel… drained. It's probably a good thing I didn’t book any of those extra meetings this week. Smart move. You’d have been a right mess presenting to the board looking like that. Speaking of messes, apparently, there’s been another outbreak of… something at Addenbrooke’s. Another ward shut down. Ugh, seriously? What is it this time? Something stomach-related again? Apparently. They're pushing for everyone to get the updated vaccinations, naturally. It's a bit of a PR disaster for the hospital, to be honest. It’s terrifying how easily stuff spreads, isn’t it? I’m being extra vigilant with handwashing, antibacterial gel, the whole nine yards. I’m thinking about wearing a mask in lectures again, even though nobody else is. Not a bad idea. You’re always sensible. I was watching some weird thing on TV last night about how they’re developing tech that can automatically read body language from camera footage. Oh, really? Like, detect lying or something? Apparently. All sorts of stuff. Micro-expressions, pupil dilation… apparently it’s getting really sophisticated. Imagine the implications for interviews, or even just… dating. That’s… unsettling. It feels like a huge invasion of privacy. Honestly, I'm already suspicious of all these smart cameras everywhere. They're always 'watching'. It is a bit Big Brother-ish. But on the one hand, if it could accurately detect when someone's about to do something harmful… I still wouldn’t want a computer judging my facial expressions!

Right, okay, so “quixotic” goes across the double word score… that’s… twenty-six. Ouch. Twenty-six! That’s brutal. I thought I was doing okay with ‘jazzy’ but that's nothing compared to “quixotic”. You always get the good ones, don’t you? Honestly, you two are taking this far too seriously. It’s Scrabble, not the Commonwealth Games. Though, your grandfather – bless him –  would  have approached it with that level of intensity. He was a formidable opponent. I did enjoy a good game. Sharpened the mind, you know. And it was always good to win, naturally. Though your mother here was a surprisingly cunning player. Always digging out those obscure words. I learned from the best! Though, honestly, finding a seven-letter word is often a fluke. I was just lucky with the tiles. Did anyone else manage to get rid of their blank? Not yet. I’m saving it for a particularly desperate moment. I'm hoping for a ‘Z’ or something equally rare. Honestly, this is worse than the gridlock at the Trafford Centre yesterday. It took us nearly an hour just to get out of the car park. Oh, I can imagine! I deliberately avoid it at this time of year. Too many people, too much fuss. I needed some lamb for a roast and even the butcher’s queue was atrocious. Honestly, it stretched halfway down the street! Speaking of food, I think I’ll make a lasagne next week. I found a really good recipe online. It’s got a butternut squash béchamel sauce. That sounds… adventurous. Is it actually lasagne then? Well, it's a  version  of lasagne. It's good! You should try it. Anyway, has anyone seen that new music magazine? The one with the interview with Florence Welch? I lent it to someone… I think I saw it on the coffee table earlier. By the window. Though I haven’t looked at it myself. All this… modern music… it’s a bit loud for my ears. Times change, my dear. You used to say the same thing about The Beatles. That was  different . That was… melodic! I saw someone posting on Facebook about a charity shop selling vintage vinyl. I must have a look. Though I dread the thought of rummaging through boxes. Facebook is a minefield. So much arguing. I keep meaning to deactivate my account. Do you ever feel like you’re just shouting into the void?

Goodness, this queue is moving slowly, isn’t it? Seems everyone decided to take their break at once. It always does, doesn’t it? Though, truth be told, I don't mind a bit of a pause. This whole TME business can be rather draining, all that talk of efficiencies and regulations. Takes me back, though. Reminds me of trade shows, actually. Oh? Did you do much travelling with work? Oh, immensely. Spent a lot of time in Germany. Dusseldorf mostly, for the Drupa exhibitions. Massive things, really. All the printing industry crammed into one place. I was there for nearly twenty years, presenting our systems. Goodness, twenty years! What did you… invent, was it? I seem to recall someone mentioning something about printing systems. Invent is a strong word, perhaps. More… refine and market. I took the initial idea, which was rather clunky, and streamlined it. Made it commercially viable. It was a new way of controlling ink flow, increased the precision enormously. Reduced waste, you see. Companies loved that. Sounds terribly clever. Not a world I know anything about, of course. I was always more interested in the… visual side of things. Hence the art. Though even  that’s  become rather technical these days, hasn’t it? Digital everything. It has. But the principle remains the same. Good design, good execution. That's what matters. The Germans, they appreciated that. Very thorough, very demanding clients. They wouldn’t hesitate to point out flaws, believe me! But once you won them over, you had a loyal customer for life. I can imagine. Were you fluent in German, then? Reasonably. Enough to get by, conduct negotiations, understand the technical discussions. I had a brilliant language tutor, Frau Schmidt. A tiny woman, absolutely terrifying, but she drilled it into me. “Precision, Mr. Davies! Precision in language, as in your machines!” She used to say. That sounds rather… intimidating. She was! But effective. And frankly, it was essential. You couldn’t just waltz in there relying on interpreters. It was all about building relationships, understanding their needs. We built quite a network, actually. Sales agents all over Europe. A good team, a very good team. Still bump into some of them at industry events now, although I’m mostly retired, you understand. Yes, I gathered that. It sounds like a remarkably successful career. Quite a contrast to my rather… bohemian lifestyle. Different paths, different rewards.

Right, nearly at the M5 then, eh? Just gotta navigate this… chaos. Honestly, Manchester traffic is something else. Tell me about it. I swear it gets worse every year. At least we’re out of it now, mostly. Are you sure about this route, though? Google Maps keeps trying to send us through… Wolverhampton. Wolverhampton? No, no, no. Absolutely not. Too many roundabouts. I trust the old sat nav, it’s never let me down. Though, it does have a bit of a thing for service stations. You know it loves a good Greggs. It does, doesn’t it? Speaking of which, are we stopping at Gloucester Services? Apparently the farm shop is amazing. Gloucester Services is a must, love. A  must . It’s not just a service station, it’s an experience. They do a proper Cornish pasty there, you know, not one of those sad, flimsy ones. Good to know. It’s just… all this talk of ‘proper’ and ‘real’… makes me think about English Language. We were talking about etymology today, how words change over time. It’s weird, isn’t it? How something can mean something completely different in a hundred years. Aye, it is. Proper and real... They’ve both been bent out of shape over the years, those two. I remember my granddad using ‘gay’ to mean happy. Can you imagine saying that now? Seriously! It's so strange. Mrs. Davies was going on about how Shakespeare invented loads of words, but actually he just… adapted them. Like, he didn’t  create  ‘eyeball’, he just put ‘eye’ and ‘ball’ together. That’s clever, that is. Always thought he was a bit of a show-off, mind. Full of ‘wherefores’ and ‘hath’s’. Makes a man feel a bit daft. Exactly! And speaking of daft, I'm trying to decide what to apply for at uni. I'm leaning towards Philosophy, but everyone says it’s… impractical. Impractical? Rubbish. Philosophy teaches you how to  think . That’s the most practical skill you can have. What else are you considering? History. It’s safe, you know? Everyone expects me to do History. But Philosophy just… feels more exciting. Actually, Mrs. Peterson said she did a Philosophy degree and now she's a lawyer. See? Told you. Lawyer, eh? Probably spends all day arguing semantics, which is a good skillset for a philosopher anyway. Probably. Ooh, look!

Right, so you’re chopping the onions, yeah? And Ben, could you get the garlic out the fridge? Honestly, this smells amazing already, Mum’s recipe is the best. Yeah, no problem. Garlic’s here. Honestly, your mum is a wizard in the kitchen. Mine just… boils everything. Literally. Boiled chicken, boiled veg, boiled everything. It’s depressing. Your mother always was a practical woman, lad. Doesn’t see the point in fussing. Gets the job done, that’s what she always said. Reminds me of your grandmother, actually. Though  she  could bake a cake to rival the Queen. Oh god, Nana’s Victoria sponge. I’ve genuinely tried to recreate it, and it’s never,  ever  the same. It’s like she had a secret ingredient, or a magic touch. Likely both. Speaking of families, how’s your sister doing? Last I heard she was still trying to move to Australia? Still saving, still planning. It's a nightmare. Everything's so expensive, isn't it? She's working all hours, two jobs sometimes. She’s absolutely determined though. Says she needs the sunshine. And away from our Dad, probably. Oh, your father. Always a handful, that one. Remember when he tried to build that shed in the garden? Nearly took out the fence. Oh god, don’t remind me! Mum was livid. It leaned like the Tower of Pisa. He insisted it was “rustic.” Classic Dad move. Mine tried to fix the washing machine once. Ended up flooding the kitchen. Honestly, sometimes I think they  enjoy  making a mess. You think? Mine keeps offering to “help” with the garden. Which usually means digging up perfectly good plants. Well, they mean well, don’t they? It’s the thought that counts. Though perhaps a strongly worded suggestion they stick to watching Gardener’s World might be in order. Good shout. Right, onions are chopped. Garlic… finely minced. Am I doing this right? Everything feels a bit… raw. You’re doing amazing! It's supposed to be slightly raw, that's where the flavour comes from. So, are you coming round to my place next week? We’re having a games night. Ben’s bringing the Monopoly, which always ends in tears. Oh, I wouldn’t miss that for the world. Seeing Ben lose at Monopoly is worth the price of admission alone. He gets so competitive. Hey! It’s a strategic game!

Right, so this is proper grim isn’t it? Leisure centre café food. Standard. It's…functional. Needed a caffeine hit after that swim though. You swim often? Nah, not really. My mate dragged me. He’s dead keen, training for something or other. I’m more of a, you know, pint-and-pub-garden kinda guy. What about you? Regular? Trying to be. I used to be quite into running, but my knee’s been playing up. Thought swimming might be kinder. And it’s a good way to de-stress, honestly. Teaching’s…intense. Teaching? What do you teach? French and Spanish, actually. Secondary school. It's rewarding, but the marking… endless marking. You’re a bartender, right? I think I’ve seen you around a couple of times, at that place near the bullring? The Velvet Stag? Yeah, that’s me. Keeps me busy, pays the bills. Graduated last year, history degree. Not exactly a goldmine for jobs, is it? No, not always. I did a Masters in Applied Linguistics after my undergrad. Still felt a bit… precarious getting into teaching. It’s competitive. Tell me about it. My dad keeps going on about me doing a ‘proper’ job. Says I’m wasting my brain. Oh, the classic parental disappointment. Mine was more, “Are you  sure  you want to live in Birmingham?” Hertfordshire girl, you know. It’s a bit of a culture shock. Yeah, it’s different. You get used to it. Have you learned to drive yet? That’s the biggest shock, honestly. The driving. Not yet! I’m terrified, to be honest. I lived in London for years, never needed to. Now I’m here, trying to navigate these roundabouts… it’s daunting. My friend keeps offering to teach me, but… It’s a nightmare. Honestly, just bite the bullet and do it. Lessons are expensive, but worth it. Freedom, innit? Although, knowing Birmingham drivers, you’ll need nerves of steel. Nerves of steel are in short supply at the moment. So, long term, are you planning on staying in hospitality? Or are you hoping to use that history degree eventually? I dunno. Part of me thinks I should probably use it for something. Museum work maybe? But then… the flexible hours of bartending are pretty good. And I quite like it, actually. It’s good money, meets interesting people. I’m seeing someone at the moment, she's a student at the art college.

Right well I’m having another coffee. Are you two wanting one? Oh yes please. Just a little one for me, thank you. I’m alright for now, thanks. I’m still feeling the effects of that enormous lunch. Needed a good lie down afterwards, honestly. You did enjoy it though, didn't you? You were scraping the plate. Of course! It was lovely. Are you still driving over to Norwich tomorrow? Yes. Early start. Need to be there for nine. I’m really hoping the traffic isn’t too bad. It was a nightmare last week. It always is on a Tuesday, isn’t it? Especially around that A11 roundabout. You’re telling me. Honestly, it’s enough to put you off driving altogether. Reminds me of that time we went to the Gambia, the driving over there was…an experience. Oh, horrifying! Remember those scooters weaving in and out of everything? And the lorries! We were lucky to survive that. Oh don’t remind me. Still, the beaches were beautiful. Such a lovely place, despite the driving. It was. Anyway, I was thinking… about that donation box for the bell ringing. We need to get it sorted. Good idea. I think there's one in the attic, actually. A little wooden one. We could tidy it up, paint it perhaps? Or we could just make one? I’ve got plenty of cardboard and some nice fabric scraps. Making one sounds good actually, that way it can be exactly how we want it. What about some nice colourful banners to go with it? To attract attention? Excellent thought. I’m quite handy with a paintbrush, you know. We could have one for each of the bells, listing their names and a little something about their history. Oh that would be lovely! People always ask about the bells, they're fascinated. Though, talking of fascinating… did you read that article about that woman pretending to be ill? Munchausen's Syndrome, you mean? Terrible business. Deliberately making yourself sick, just for attention. Can you imagine? It's beyond comprehension. Such a waste of resources too, taking up doctors’ time and hospital beds. It is awful. Oh look at those plants, they’re absolutely thriving! You’ve got a real green thumb, haven’t you? Just a bit of regular watering and a little bit of sunshine, that’s all it takes. They brighten up the whole room, don’t they?

Honestly, this new Duolingo update is stressing me out. They’ve made it so aggressive with the push notifications. Like, I get it, I need to practice my Spanish, but do you need to guilt-trip me every two hours? Haha, yeah, I’ve seen people complaining about that on Twitter. My mum’s addicted to Duolingo, though. She’s learning Japanese now. It's…intense. Japanese? Wow. My nan tried learning Italian for a trip to Rome, lasted about a week. All she ended up learning was “Grazie” and how to order a very specific type of pasta. Classic nan! Speaking of stressful, has anyone seen that new horror film,  The Hollow Ones ? I nearly jumped out of my skin like ten times. Oh god, no. I am a  coward . Absolutely cannot handle scary movies. Even the trailers give me the creeps. It’s genuinely unsettling. Not just jump scares, proper psychological stuff. I watched it with Liam, and he was trying to act all cool, but I could see him gripping my arm the whole time. Liam’s a big softie, honestly. Remember when we made him watch  The Babadook ? He didn’t sleep for a week. Oh, the look on his face! Priceless. Anyway, enough about scaring the boys. Has anyone heard from Chloe? She was supposed to come to Portugal with us, wasn’t she? I texted her yesterday. She said she's still figuring out work. Sounds like she might have to pull out, which is a shame. It won’t be the same without her. That’s a bummer. She was really excited about it. We should probably start thinking about a backup plan, just in case. Yeah, maybe ask Sarah if she’s free? She’s always up for a spontaneous trip. Good idea! I’ll message her now. Oh, this pasta is amazing, by the way. Did you make this from scratch, Liam? Er… no. It’s from a packet. Don't tell anyone. It's the pesto one. You fraud! You have to admit, you're a surprisingly good cook for someone who relies on pre-made sauce. Hey! I can make a mean fry-up, okay? That takes skill. Speaking of skills, anyone else notice Ben's been posting a lot of gym selfies lately? He’s really getting into fitness, isn’t he? Yeah, I saw. Trying to impress someone, maybe?

Right well that was a nice little visit wasn’t it. Bit chilly getting out though. Aye, a bit of a blow. Had to scrape the frost off the windscreen this morning, didn’t I? Never thought we'd get another frost this late in the year. It  is  cold, isn't it? I'm glad I wore my proper coat. Still, nice to see Margaret. Haven’t seen her properly since… oh, goodness, Christmas? Feels like forever. She's still driving that little Fiat, bless her. I swear it's getting smaller every time I see it. Smaller and slower! She nearly took my wing mirror off last time she was here, didn’t she? She just pulled out without looking. Oh, I remember that. You were fuming! Said she was getting too old for it. Well, she is, isn't she? I mean, at her age… These youngsters flying about, she wouldn’t stand a chance. Though, to be fair,  some  youngsters don't look where they're going either. It’s the speed, isn’t it? Everyone’s in such a rush. I always drive carefully, especially on these country lanes. Remember old Mr. Henderson? He lost control on a bend and ended up in a ditch. Oh, dreadful. That was years ago now, wasn’t it? Poor man. He was a good sort, old Henderson. Always had a story to tell. Aye. Got himself a new car eventually, didn't he? A proper big one. Reckoned it made him feel safer. It's sensible to have something you feel comfortable in. I always preferred a larger car, even when the children were little. Just felt more secure. We had that awful little Mini for years, didn't we? Always breaking down. Took me hours to get home from work some days. Hours! Remember that time you were stuck in that traffic jam near Attleborough? You didn’t get home 'til nearly ten o'clock. Don’t remind me! It was pouring with rain. And then the wipers packed in. Absolute nightmare. You've had some terrible luck with cars over the years, haven’t you? Honestly, it’s a wonder you still drive! Well, I have to, don’t I? Getting anywhere without a car around here is impossible. And I still enjoy it, to be fair. Just as long as it doesn't break down! You'd think with all your engineering knowledge you could fix it yourself, wouldn't you?

Honestly, the M6 is just relentless isn’t it? Always something going on. Reminds me of trying to get to Heathrow during the school holidays… absolute chaos. Oh god, Heathrow is the worst. I flew from there last year, and the queues for security were… unbelievable. I spent more time  in  the airport than actually flying. You’re lucky you flew at all. I’m still debating whether to even attempt a holiday this year. The thought of navigating airports with my knee… it’s just not appealing. Oh, how  is  your knee, Arthur? Still giving you trouble? You were hobbling about like an old man at Sarah’s wedding. Old man is right! It’s alright most of the time, but prolonged walking, standing… forget about it. The doctor says it’s just wear and tear, typical for my age. Says I should lose weight, but that’s easier said than done when you’re retired and spend your days surrounded by biscuits! Tell me about it! I’ve gained a stone since I started working from home. The fridge is just… too accessible. You know, speaking of moving things, have you two made any progress on finding a place? You said you were looking near Manchester, didn't you, Sarah? We are, but it’s proving harder than we thought. Everything’s either ridiculously expensive or needs a full renovation. We keep looking at these little cottages in the Peak District, but they’re all so remote. Remote can be nice. Peace and quiet. Though, I suppose having a hospital nearby is important with… well, with knees like mine. It is. And shops! I couldn’t live somewhere without a good bakery within walking distance. My Dublin upbringing instilled a serious need for fresh bread. We saw one house, it had a lovely garden, but the driveway was  steep . Absolutely terrifying. I could see my little Fiat rolling backwards into the neighbour’s garden. You need a four-wheel drive! Like that monstrosity my nephew drives. Honestly, it's like piloting a tank. Although, I suppose it would handle a steep driveway. Oh, don't even get me started on cars. I swear they're all just computers on wheels now. I miss the days when you could actually fix something yourself without needing a diagnostic tool. My father could fix anything with a bit of wire and some WD-40.

…and honestly, I couldn’t believe it when PC Davies called this morning. He said they’d found it! Your bike! No way! Seriously? Where was it? Apparently, down by the Old Town, behind the fishing museum. Someone had tried to spray paint it black, but they hadn't done a very good job, thankfully. Davies recognised the serial number, which is why they knew it was yours. Oh my gosh, that’s amazing! I thought I’d never see Bonnie again. I was so gutted. I mean, it wasn’t a super expensive bike, but I loved it. I used it for getting to college, remember? Of course, I remember. All those mornings cycling up that hill! It's a relief it's back, honestly. It's such a pain when things get stolen. Did they catch the person who took it? Not yet, apparently. They’re looking at CCTV footage from shops nearby. But Davies said the area’s been having a bit of a bike theft problem lately, loads reported in the last few weeks. Honestly, you wouldn’t believe what people get up to. It’s disgusting. You see it on those Facebook neighbourhood watch groups too, don’t you? Everyone moaning about something. It's awful. Yeah, it is. I was scrolling through TikTok last night, and there were loads of videos about bike security. All these clever little gadgets you can get, like alarms and GPS trackers. Good idea! Maybe we should look into getting one of those. Although, it feels a bit extreme for Hastings, doesn’t it? I mean, it’s not exactly a major city. I know, but it’s better to be safe than sorry, right? Especially after this. I'm going to invest in a proper heavy-duty lock as well. No more flimsy cable locks for me! Sensible girl. So, are you planning on cycling to college tomorrow? Definitely! I’m so excited. It’ll be so much quicker than getting the bus. Plus, it's good exercise. I’ve been feeling a bit sluggish lately, spending too much time studying. Speaking of which, how was your work today? Did Mrs. Henderson manage to get her holiday dates sorted? Oh, don't even ask! She was on the phone for ages trying to re-arrange things. Apparently, the hotel has overbooked. Honestly, she's a nightmare sometimes. I brought home some leftovers from the cafe though – a tuna mayo sandwich and a flapjack.

Right, I’m going to try and complete this green line to Plymouth before anyone else blocks me. It’s vital. Vital? It’s Ticket to Ride, Sarah, not open-heart surgery. Though I suppose strategically blocking people  is  a form of psychological warfare… He’s got a point. You’re taking this very seriously. I’m just enjoying the derailment potential, myself. Are we having cheese and biscuits later? I had a rather large lunch, so I won’t be wanting a full meal. Just a little nibble. Yes, Dai, cheese and biscuits are definitely on the cards. I picked up a lovely Mature Cheddar from that farm shop near Ross-on-Wye. It's  sharp . Oh, good. Sharp cheese is the best. Look, Rhys, don’t even  think  about trying to take that route. I wasn’t! I was admiring your intensity. Honestly, you play like you’re single-handedly saving the railways. Speaking of railways… did you know the newer Hitachi trains can accelerate faster than the old Intercity 125s? Can they? Really? I thought the 125s were pretty nippy. They are, but the Hitachi Azumas have different traction motors. More powerful, better acceleration. Apparently, they ran tests and the difference was significant. It’s all about the torque, you see. Torque? Sounds expensive. Is that why train tickets are so pricey these days? It's all the torque! Dai, you’re terrible! It’s a bit more complicated than that, love. But yes, newer trains do cost more. Actually, that's quite interesting. I always wondered why the trains to London feel so much quicker now than they used to. It's not just my imagination, then? No, definitely not. It's partially the tracks being upgraded, partially the trains themselves. The newer trains can also handle steeper gradients more easily. It’s all about efficiently moving mass. It's physics, essentially. You and your physics, Rhys. You’ll be explaining the Bernoulli principle next. Only if someone brings up airplane wings! Just saying. I remember when we used to travel up to Shrewsbury on the steam trains. Now  those  were journeys. The smell of coal smoke… the rhythmic chugging… Oh yes, I remember those too. They were a bit slower, of course, but they had a certain charm. And you could wave at people from the window! Right, back to strategically important routes. I  need  that connection to Bristol.

Right, your go. Though honestly, I’m starting to think this game is entirely luck-based. Like, seriously, how do you consistently roll a six? Skill, darling, pure skill. Years of honing my dice-rolling technique. Though you’re right, it  is  a bit random, isn’t it? Still, better than Monopoly, at least. I’d rather dismantle a working television than play another round of Monopoly. Oh god, don’t even mention Monopoly. It brings out the worst in people. Remember Aunt Carol last Christmas? Practically declared war over Baltic Avenue. How could I forget? The shouting, the accusations of cheating… it was glorious. In a slightly terrifying way. Speaking of which, your parents seem remarkably calm for a Sunday afternoon. Usually, there's some sort of domestic drama unfolding. They’re lulling you into a false sense of security. They're deliberately being nice because you’re here. Wait until after tea and the true chaos will begin. Probably involving a disagreement about the correct way to brew a cuppa. The brewing of tea is a serious matter in these parts. I've learned that the hard way. Still, this is nice. Quiet. A bit…domestic. Reminds me of my grandparents, actually. They were big Scrabble players. Oh? What was their Scrabble style like? Cutthroat, I presume? Intense. My grandfather was an ex-teacher, so vocabulary was his weapon of choice. My grandmother would just try and use every single tile she had, regardless of whether it made a real word. She once tried to play "glurp." "Glurp"? Oh, that’s brilliant! Did your grandfather let her get away with it? He tried to explain the rules, patiently, for about five minutes. Then he just sighed and conceded the point. He said it was easier to let her win than argue. Describes their whole relationship, really. That’s lovely. It’s funny, isn't it, how games can tell you so much about people? And about cultures. I was reading an article about drinking cultures in different countries last week. Apparently, in Japan, it’s considered incredibly rude to pour your own drink. You wait for someone else to do it for you. Really? That’s fascinating. So, it's all about reciprocal obligation? I can see that. It's all very… structured. Here, it's just a free-for-all. “Get ‘em while they’re cold” is pretty much the guiding principle.

Honestly, this lasagne is divine, Kerrie. You’ve outdone yourself. It is really good, isn't it? Especially after all the stress with the removal van yesterday. I thought we were going to be stuck with everything on the driveway all night. Oh, don't even  start  me on removal vans. The one we used when we moved to Llanelli…absolute cowboys. Broke half my grandmother's china. Said it was ‘pre-existing damage’. Honestly! Oh no! That’s awful. You’d think they’d be a bit more careful. I’m just glad ours were…competent-ish. Although they did nearly take my neighbour’s garden gnome. A garden gnome! Imagine the outcry. How’s the new place settling in, anyway? Any disasters yet? Just unpacking mountains of boxes. And the bins… the bin situation is  confusing . Apparently, we have a blue bin for recycling, a black bin for general waste, and a green bin that’s only for garden waste  on alternate Tuesdays . It’s a logistical nightmare. Oh, the bin systems! They’re the bane of my life. Swansea is just as bad. Different coloured bins for everything, and if you put one wrong thing in the wrong bin, they won’t collect it. Honestly, it's like a test. Seriously! It’s ridiculous. I’m still trying to figure out what goes where. It wouldn't hurt them to just have one bin and sort it all themselves, would it? Exactly! And then there’s the white goods. The fridge in the new kitchen is…ancient. It sounds like a jet engine taking off every time it kicks in. You need to get it checked. Don’t want it breaking down and ruining all your lovely food. My cousin had a fridge break down, lost a whole salmon. Tragic. A whole salmon! That  is  tragic. Speaking of tragic, I bumped into Lisa from college the other day. She’s…become a solicitor. A  solicitor ! Wow! Good for her. I mean, good for her, but it made me question all my life choices. I’m coordinating projects, she's defending people in court! I only got a C in law. Don't compare yourself to others, love. You're brilliant at what you do. And law isn't for everyone. I much prefer balancing the books, personally. Though even that's stressful with all these new tax regulations. You’re right.

Honestly, this traffic is mental. What’s even happening up ahead? Just… solid red. Standard Saturday afternoon, darling. Everyone seems to be going somewhere at once. And it’s not even a school holiday. Though, honestly, it feels like a perpetual holiday these days with all the strikes. Strikes are a nightmare. Makes everything so unpredictable. Did you have a nice week at the TLS? Anything particularly juicy come across your desk? Oh, the usual academic spats and authorial egos. Honestly, sometimes I feel like a referee. Though we did get a rather delightful piece on Elizabeth Bowen… beautifully written. And the submissions are still flooding in, even though everyone keeps predicting the death of print. Death of print? Come on. People still  like  holding a book, turning the pages. It’s a whole experience. Digital’s just…convenient. Precisely! And let’s not forget, there’s a certain…prestige. A beautifully designed book just  feels  important. Though, the marketing team are obsessed with engagement metrics online. Always wanting me to commission more ‘listicles’ and ‘think pieces.’ Dreadful. Listicles. The bane of modern existence. Speaking of things that are dreadful, that driver just cut me up. Honestly, the nerve of some people. Oh, dear. Try to ignore them. Road rage won't get us to North London any faster. Remember what happened to Uncle George?    Don’t remind me. The Great A40 Incident of ‘98. Still talked about at family gatherings. It’s a cautionary tale! Although, he  was  slightly justified… that other driver was going about twenty miles an hour in the fast lane. Still, shouting abuse through the window? Not his finest moment. So, what are we actually getting in North London? You’ve been very mysterious about this. It’s a little something for your Aunt Judith. Her birthday is next week and I found a rather lovely antique shop. They specialise in… well, let’s just say it’s something she collects. Something she collects… That narrows it down to approximately three hundred things. Is it another ceramic cat? Please tell me it's not another ceramic cat.    No, not a cat. Though she does have a fondness for them. This is… more floral. And French. She’s been talking about wanting to go back to Provence for ages. Maybe this will tide her over. Provence sounds amazing. We should all go. You, me, Dad, Aunt Judith… Perhaps.

Honestly, the state of him. I’ve never seen anyone cling to a life raft like that. You’re still on about Dave in Majorca? It was a bit choppy, give the lad a break. Choppy? It was a force ten gale! He was screaming for his mum, I swear. No way! Dave? Screaming for his mum? That doesn’t sound like the Dave I know. It is entirely believable. He cries at Disney films. He genuinely thought he was going to drown in about three feet of water. And the lifeguard just stood there filming it. Classic. Probably thought he'd get it on TikTok. Speaking of embarrassing moments, remember that time Liam tried to serenade Sarah with a ukulele on that camping trip to the Lake District? Oh god, don’t. The less said about Liam’s musical 'talent' the better. He thought he was Ed Sheeran. Was it…bad? I wasn't there for that one. Bad doesn’t even begin to cover it. He kept breaking the strings, and Sarah looked like she was actively plotting his demise. She was making these really pointed comments about needing earplugs. It was glorious. He was so insistent though, bless him. He'd learned, like, three chords. Thought he was away. And then it started raining. Mid-song. The ukulele got soaked, and he just…stopped. Just stood there looking utterly defeated. Oh, that  is  tragic. Though I’m picturing it and I’m laughing already. It was peak Liam. Remember when we tried to take him white water rafting? He refused to let go of the instructor’s lifejacket. He genuinely thought he’d be swept away to Spain! He kept shouting “Barcelona!” as we went down the rapids. Barcelona! I've completely forgotten about that! He’s a walking disaster, that boy. A lovable disaster. Honestly, planning a holiday with him is a full-time job. Constant supervision required. This is why I just stick to all-inclusive resorts. Minimal risk of Liam-related incidents. Sensible. Speaking of holidays, anyone got any plans for next year? I'm thinking maybe backpacking around Southeast Asia. Ooh, that sounds amazing! I’m thinking maybe a city break to Amsterdam. Need some culture, you know? And waffles. Definitely waffles. Amsterdam  is  good for waffles…and other things. I'm leaning towards a week in Italy, just eating my way through the country.

…and honestly, the silence. You wouldn’t believe the silence. Not a mechanical silence, you get enough of that in London, but a  natural  silence. Broken only by the wind, and the occasional… well, last time it was a pine marten scrabbling about. Quite close, actually. Woke me up, thinking someone was trying to get into the tent. A pine marten? Goodness! You’re brave, Alistair. Wild winter camping. It sounds… intensely cold. And slightly terrifying. Cold, yes, it is cold. That’s why preparation is key. Layers, proper sleeping bag, a stove for hot drinks. It’s not about suffering, it’s about being comfortable  within  the discomfort. And terrifying? Not really. It's more… humbling. You’re utterly reliant on your own skills and the weather. Makes you feel very small, and very connected, all at the same time. Dad’s been trying to get me into it for years. I’ve always shied away, to be honest. Too much of a soft southerner, I suppose. Though I’ve done a bit of hill walking, obviously. Bit different lying out exposed overnight though. It is different, Calum. It’s about shedding the layers of… well, everything. Modern life. All the noise and distractions. You’re forced to be present. Honestly, it's the best thing for clearing your head. Better than any therapy, if you ask me. Now, now, Alistair. Don’t go undermining my profession! I think there are benefits to both. Though I  do  see what you mean about being present. We try to foster that in therapy, that mindful awareness. It’s just… lying in a tent, potentially freezing, seems a rather extreme method. Extreme, perhaps. But effective! And the stars, Moira. You’ve never seen stars like it. Away from all the light pollution. It’s… otherworldly. I went up to Glen Affric last February, and the aurora borealis was visible. Flickering green across the loch. Spectacular. Glen Affric… that does sound pretty good. Actually, I've been thinking about getting a bit more into bushcraft, you know, building shelters, foraging. Maybe a winter camping trip isn't  entirely  out of the question. Have you got a good recommendation for a lightweight stove, Dad? I've been looking at the MSR PocketRocket 2… The PocketRocket is alright, efficient enough. But for winter, you want something with a bit more power. Look at the Primus OmniFuel.

Honestly though, I don't get the hype with Wes Anderson. Everyone bangs on about him, but it all feels…stylised for the sake of being stylised, y’know? Like, pretty to look at, but does anything  actually  happen? I can see that. It’s very… curated, isn't it? Like a museum diorama come to life. But I think that  is  the point. It’s not about plot, it’s about the aesthetic, the world-building. It's escapism. Escapism into a world where everyone speaks in a flat monotone and has commitment issues? Sounds bleak, not escapist. Give me a good gritty drama any day. Something with actual, you know,  feeling . Fair enough. What have you been reading lately? Anything gripping? I finally got around to finishing “Piranesi” – Susanna Clarke. Absolutely blew my mind. Oh, I’ve  heard  about that one. It’s the one with all the statues and the tides, right? I’ve got it on my list, but I'm currently slogging through “Middlemarch". It’s…a commitment. A really, really long commitment. Oh god, “Middlemarch”. That’s a proper undertaking. George Eliot’s a bit… dense, isn’t she? Lots of moralising. Loads! Like, I appreciate the social commentary, but sometimes I just want someone to  shoot  someone, you know? A bit of action. Instead, it's just hours and hours of people worrying about inheritance and reputation. Fair point. I guess it’s a different pace of storytelling. So, food-wise, what have you been up to? Any culinary masterpieces recently? I attempted to make a proper paella last weekend. It was…ambitious. Ambitious and probably a disaster, let’s be honest. Paella is a nightmare to get right. I've been on a bit of a soup kick lately, actually. It’s cold, it's easy, it’s comforting. Made a really nice lentil soup the other day with chorizo. Chorizo in lentil soup? That sounds amazing. I might have to steal that. I'm terrible at soup, I always end up with it being either watery or like cement. The key is a good stock, honestly. And don't be afraid to blend some of it at the end to give it a bit of thickness. Makes all the difference. I got a tip from my gran, actually. She’s a soup queen. Gran's always know best, don't they? Mine makes an incredible apple crumble.

Right, so then the wolf… he didn’t  blow  the house down, did he? He tried to trick them! He pretended to be…Grandma! Silly wolf! Grandma doesn’t have scratchy teeth! Wolves are rubbish. Lego wolves are better. They don’t try to eat you. That’s very true. Lego wolves are much safer. You building anything good with your Lego today? A spaceship! With lasers! And a robot pilot. He’s going to fight the wolves! Can I be the princess in the spaceship? Fine. But you have to hold the control panel. It’s very important. Sounds like a very important mission. You two are going to save the world! You know, when I was little, I didn’t have fancy Lego spaceships. We had…well, we didn’t have much Lego actually. My Dad had an old typewriter though. A type…writer? What’s that? It's like a computer, but instead of typing on a screen, you hit little keys and they make letters on paper. All clunky and noisy! It didn’t have Excel on it though. Excel? Is that a game? Not exactly. It's something I use for work. It helps me keep track of… well, lots of numbers and things. It’s not as fun as a spaceship, I promise. Speaking of fun, did you both enjoy Brownies tonight? I learnt a new part of the Promise! The one about being truthful. That’s a very important part. Being truthful is really, really important. Did you get to do any crafts? Nah. We talked about it mostly. And then played a game where you had to say what you’d do if you found a magic lamp. I said I'd wish for a PlayStation 6! A PlayStation 6! That's ambitious! They’re only on… what, a 5 now? Yeah! And it’ll have even more amazing games. And faster loading times. I’d wish for a pony! A sparkly pink pony! A sparkly pink pony sounds amazing. Oh, look at the time. Getting late. Time to brush teeth and get ready for bed. Did either of you think of any stories tonight? Things we could read tomorrow? I did! It’s about a Lego man who builds a robot army to… We’ll hear all about it tomorrow night then. Right, teeth first. And then, no more talking about PlayStations or ponies, okay?

Honestly, David, you look like you’ve slept in your clothes. Not that it matters here, of course, but still! A bit of effort never hurt anyone. Oh, come on, Margaret. Comfortable is key at my age. And it  was  a quick dash from the garden. Trying to salvage the last of the raspberries before the birds got to them. You wouldn't believe the competition. Raspberries? You’re still at it then? I thought you’d given up on the fruit farm ambition. Remember you talking about buying a little place in Kent, just rows and rows of strawberries? Briefly entertained it. Too much hard work, frankly. Much easier to just pilfer a handful from the bushes in my garden. Speaking of which, did you have a good breakfast? I saw you wrestling with that grapefruit. Wrestling is a good word for it. I do enjoy grapefruit, but it’s always such a mess. I’m more a toast and marmalade person, myself. Though I’m trying to be good, you know. More fruit, less… well, everything else. Good for you. I’m sticking to coffee and a biscuit. Doctor’s orders, surprisingly. Said I need a little treat now and then. He’s a sensible man, your doctor. He is. Though he does keep going on about my cholesterol. Anyway, I was reading an article the other day about deserted medieval villages. Apparently, there are hundreds of them scattered across the country. Yorkshire has quite a few. Really? Fascinating. What happened to them? Plague? Famine? A bit of everything, apparently. Changes in agricultural practices. The Black Death, naturally. Sometimes just the lord of the manor deciding to enclose the common land. Just… vanished. Makes you think about the layers of history under our feet, doesn’t it? It does. Speaking of things under our feet, have you driven through Shipley recently? Those roadworks on the A650 are a disaster. Took me forty minutes to get here this morning. Utter chaos. Don't even mention it! Absolute nightmare. It’s going to be like that for months, I suspect. They’ve been ‘improving’ the junction for ages. And the jam… I swear they’re deliberately making it worse. It's just a ploy to sell more coffee at the motorway services. Probably. Opportunists, the lot of them. Have you managed to sort out those herbs you wanted for the window sill?

Honestly, I’m still full from yesterday’s dinner. That goose was… substantial. Substantial is one word for it. I think I’m still tasting cranberry sauce. Remember Auntie Maureen bringing that homemade stuff? Nearly blew your head off with the sweetness. Oh God, yes. It was like jam. She's so proud of it, though. You can't say anything. Precisely. Anyway, have you taken your blood pressure this morning, dear? Just did. 130 over 85. Steady as she goes. Doctor said I need to cut down on the salt though, which is a challenge with Christmas dinners lurking around every corner. You and everyone else, Dad. I’m already dreading January. All those ‘New Year, New Me’ health kicks. My Facebook feed is going to be  full  of people at the gym. Oh, don't get me started on Facebook. Carol posted a picture of her avocado on toast this morning. Avocado on toast! Like that’s inspiring. It's the millennial equivalent of showing off your roast beef, isn’t it? “Look at my healthy lifestyle!” Exactly! And it’s always filtered to within an inch of its life. Speaking of which, did you get a chance to look at those directions I sent for the farm shop? I’m trying to get Mum and Dad there on Saturday. I did, but they were… complex. Something about turning left after the third sheep and then following the lane until you see Old Man Hemmings’ scarecrow? That sounds like proper Kentish directions. They haven’t updated their navigational system since 1950, have they? Well, they don't have sat nav, Dad. That's the problem! I tried to be really clear. Google Maps just keeps taking you on the A20, which is a nightmare. Maybe I can call your Mum and talk her through it? I'm slightly better at simplifying things. Good plan. She’ll just need to know… head towards Ashford, then avoid Ashford. That’s the key. Oh, and remind her to take her phone! She always forgets and then complains she can't contact anyone if she gets lost. She’s so reliant on that thing. Always scrolling through Candy Crush. It's replacing actual conversation, I swear. It keeps her occupied. And it’s better than her talking about her bunions for three hours. Speaking of occupied, how’s Bonnie doing? Has she been shedding much?

Honestly, the new season of  Succession  is just… ruthless. I feel stressed  watching  it, let alone being in a family like that. It’s brilliantly written though, you have to admit. Oh god, yeah, it's so good. But you’re right, it’s exhausting. My mum keeps saying it's a documentary, which, honestly, feels a little too close to home sometimes with my Uncle David and his… business dealings. Oh dear. That sounds… eventful. How  is  Uncle David, actually? I haven’t seen him since Christmas. He’s… David. Still ‘disrupting’ things, apparently. He’s launched another one of his schemes, this time involving ethically sourced alpaca wool. Don't ask. Mum's bracing herself for the inevitable financial fallout. Speaking of fallout, how’s work going? Still battling the brief for that dog food campaign? Don’t even. It’s the hardest thing I’ve ever had to write. “Luxury kibble for discerning hounds.” Seriously? I’m half tempted to propose a campaign slogan of “It’s food. For dogs.” My boss would kill me. But honestly, it's soul-crushing. I need a new client. Or a holiday. Or both. You deserve both. They really do take the biscuit sometimes, these marketing briefs. Being a survey programmer isn’t glamorous, but at least I'm not having to write poetry about dog biscuits. Though, honestly, the questions people are asked… Sometimes I feel like  I  need therapy after reading the responses. Oh, tell me about it. It’s all ‘rate your satisfaction with your cable provider’ and ‘how likely are you to purchase a timeshare in the Bahamas’. The world is a strange place. Are you still thinking about doing that extra module next term? The one on behavioural economics? Yeah, I think so. It feels like a good fit with the survey work, and it might open up some interesting doors afterwards. Though, the thought of more lectures… I’m already counting down the days until my thesis is finished. It feels like it’s consuming my life. I can imagine. It's a huge undertaking. Listen, are you free next weekend? There's that new exhibition at the Tate Modern, the one everyone’s raving about. We could go Saturday afternoon and grab dinner afterwards? Ooh, that sounds amazing! Yes, definitely. I need a cultural fix. Plus, I've been meaning to ask – how on earth are you managing financially in this city?

Honestly, I’m feeling so sluggish. I really need to get back into a routine with the walking. It’s just… getting started is the hardest bit, isn’t it? Especially when it’s dark and cold. Tell me about it. I tried to go for a run this morning, and it was just miserable. The wind was howling. Ended up cutting it short and just walking the dog. He was much happier about that, anyway. You two are braver than me. I’ve completely given up on outdoor exercise until spring. I've signed up for that online yoga thing again. It’s not the same, obviously, but it’s better than nothing. And warm. Oh, is it the one with the woman who keeps talking about mindfulness? I tried that last year, and it drove me mad. All that 'being present'… I just wanted to stretch! Yes, that's the one! She’s very… earnest. But it’s actually quite good once you get past the mindfulness bits. It’s helped my back a little, I think. Speaking of needing help… I was looking at house prices again last night. Just out of curiosity, you understand. And they’ve gone  up  again. Ridiculous. Don’t even start me on house prices. It’s completely bonkers. Remember when we thought we could afford a little place with a garden? That’s just a dream now. It's the interest rates, isn't it? They're pushing everything up. I read an article saying… oh, what was it… something about affordability being at a record low. Truly depressing. Honestly, at this rate, we'll be renting forever. It’s just… demoralising. I’m thinking of just giving up looking for a while. It’s stressing me out for no good reason. Maybe that's a good idea. It’s better to just try and enjoy where we are now, and not compare ourselves to people who've had a bit of luck. Although, I  am  craving a slightly bigger kitchen… A bigger kitchen would be nice. Mine is perfectly adequate, but I’m dreaming of a proper Aga. It’s utterly impractical, I know, but a girl can dream. An Aga? You’re aiming high! I’d settle for a dishwasher that actually  works . Ours sounds like it’s about to take off every time I use it. Oh, ours is on its last legs too.

Right, so basically the whole department’s in meltdown because of this new archiving system. Honestly, it's a nightmare. They’ve implemented it without any proper training, and everyone's just scrambling around trying to figure it out. Oh, brilliant. Sounds…fun. Is it one of those things where it’s supposed to make everything efficient, but actually just makes it slower? Exactly! A thousand percent. It’s supposed to streamline things, cut down on paper, all that jazz. But it's so clunky and unintuitive. I spent three hours yesterday just trying to locate one document. Three hours! I could have written a small essay in that time. Ugh. Bureaucracy at its finest. Reminds me a bit of some of the processes we have to follow on site. Endless forms for everything. It’s infuriating when you just want to  build  something. Tell me about it. It’s like nobody involved has ever actually  done  the job themselves. Have you been following the Budget stuff at all? It's all a bit doom and gloom, isn't it? A little bit. Mostly just headlines, to be honest. Something about tax rises and cuts to…everything? It’s hard to keep track. Mum was going on about it at dinner last night, saying it’s going to ruin the country. She always does that. Mothers. Always predicting the apocalypse. I just worry about how it’s going to affect funding for things like…well, everything. The arts, education, you name it. It all seems to be on the chopping block. Yeah, that’s fair. It’s a bit worrying. Speaking of things that cost money… have you seen  Wicked  yet?  Wicked ? No! I’ve been wanting to for ages, but tickets are ridiculously expensive. They are, aren’t they? But it was incredible. Seriously, the staging, the songs… it was just phenomenal. I went with Sarah last week. Ooh, Sarah’s lucky. I’m so behind on seeing musicals. I was planning on going to see  Hamilton  when it last came to Newcastle, but then everything got cancelled with… you know. Right, yeah. Everything went a bit chaotic.  Wicked  is a bit less… historically intense, I’d say. A lot of sparkle and dramatic reveals. You should definitely try to go when you can. Maybe when you're back up North visiting? Definitely. I'll check ticket prices. I'm supposed to be saving for a new laptop, but… maybe a musical is a good excuse to dip into the funds.

Right, that’s a good covering on that fence now. Think we’re getting somewhere. It's amazing what a bit of paint does, isn’t it? Makes all the difference. Aye, it does. Makes it look…finished, you know? Not like it’s been neglected for ten years, like it was. You wouldn't believe the state of some gardens I pick folks up from. Honestly. People don’t prioritise, I suppose. They get caught up in…everything else. Speaking of which, have you seen what they're planning for that old dockland area? Down by the waterfront? Oh, aye. More flats. Always more flats. That’s all they ever build. High rise boxes. Ridiculous. They say it's "regeneration" but it just feels like they're squeezing everyone in. No green space, no character. Precisely! It's all about maximising profit margins. Remember when they talked about a community theatre there? A proper, independent theatre? Aye, I do. That’d've been brilliant. I had a mate, used to be right into am-dram. Proper good he was. Played Macbeth, he did. Scary stuff. Really? That’s fascinating. I’ve always been interested in acting. Never had the nerve to try myself, mind. Too self-conscious. Though, I did consider a life drawing class a few years back. Life drawing? You? I can’t picture that, mate. You always struck me as more the bookish type. Well, I am. But I thought it would be a good exercise in observation, in seeing the world differently. Plus, I’ve always admired good painting. Turner, obviously. But also the Pre-Raphaelites. Rossetti… Rossetti…sounds proper posh. I was down the car boot sale on Sunday, trying to find a decent toolbox. Found an old record player, though. Works a treat. Cost me a tenner. Bargain! I've been meaning to get a record player myself. I've got boxes of old vinyl gathering dust in the attic. You wouldn’t happen to have a spare set of those gutter brackets, would you? The ones you used on your shed? Gutter brackets? Hmm. Might. I think I’ve got a couple left over. They’re a bit rusty, but they’ll do the job. Why? Your gutters playing up again? A bit. There's a leak near the downpipe. It’s driving me mad. I'll try and fix it myself, but I'm no builder.

Oh look, another church. Seriously, Poland is  full  of churches. They’re beautiful, don’t get me wrong, but… another one. It's part of the landscape, isn't it? Historically, you know. Everything revolved around the church. And after all that’s happened with Poland, they’ve certainly clung onto their faith. It’s kind of… reassuring, in a way. True. It’s just... we’ve passed like five in the last hour. Speaking of clinging onto things, have you worked out the petrol costs yet? I feel like we’re burning through diesel at an alarming rate. I roughly estimated it last night. It looks like we’re each going to owe about… seventy quid, give or take. Unless we find another cheap petrol station. Polish petrol is surprisingly expensive. Seventy quid… ouch. Okay. Right. Well, worth it, I suppose. This scenery is amazing. Though I’m still slightly traumatized by that guy hitchhiking with the goat. I know! Honestly! A goat! I was half expecting him to ask for a lift  for  the goat. Is that even allowed? No idea. Probably not. It was certainly a conversation starter. I wonder if he made it to Tarnow with Gertrude. Gertrude? You named the goat? Well, it looked like a Gertrude. A very determined Gertrude. Anyway, speaking of arriving in Tarnow, are you still up for meeting Kasia and her friends for pierogi? I texted her, and she said they've found a little place that’s supposed to be fantastic. Absolutely. Pierogi are essential. I’m really looking forward to seeing Kasia again. It’s been ages. How's your friend, Liam, doing? You mentioned he was struggling a bit with things back home? He’s alright, I think. Still trying to sort things out with… well, with everything. Apparently, he’s decided to have a massive clear-out. Getting rid of all his “stuff.” He says it’s liberating. That sounds good. I’ve been meaning to do that for ages. This campervan life really forces you to confront just how much unnecessary stuff you accumulate. I think I need to seriously reassess my relationship with antique tea cozies. Tea cozies? Seriously? You have a collection of antique tea cozies? They’re…historical artifacts! And they’re very charming. But yes, okay, probably a bit excessive when you're living in a space the size of a postage stamp.

Right, just off the M55 at Junction 1 then, yeah? Should be straightforward. Less traffic than usual, surprisingly. Probably everyone's at the beach. Honestly, this journey feels  ages . Are we nearly there yet? Feels like we’ve been driving for hours. Only about twenty minutes, darling. You’re used to being whisked away in Daddy's fast car, aren’t you? This is…a more realistic pace. It's just… I’m stressing about my English Lit exam tomorrow. I haven’t even finished revising  Jane Eyre . Bronte is so… depressing.  Jane Eyre ’s a classic, love. You’ll be alright. Remember I told you about my English teacher, Mr. Grimshaw? He made us all write essays about the weather. The  weather ! Said it revealed character. Oh, that sounds delightful. And incredibly…English. Seriously? The weather? That’s just…mad. I need to memorise quotes, not analyse cloud formations. He was a bit of a character, Grimshaw. Always wore a tweed jacket, reeked of pipe tobacco. But he did make you  think  about things. Remember your Grandma used to say a grey sky was a good omen? She was always saying something. I think she believed in fairies. She had a beautiful spirit, your Grandma. So full of life. It was lovely visiting her in St Anne's, wasn’t it? Much nicer than the supermarket later. Aye, it was. Though she did try to palm me off with a knitted tea cosy every time. Said it was 'good for the soul'. Oh, she always had a tea cosy to spare. Did you hear about the train strikes again? They’re going on for, like, forever. Aye, a right mess. Trying to get down to London to see your Auntie Maureen next week will be a nightmare. Perhaps we should drive. It’s a long journey, but at least we’d be in control. Driving is better anyway. Though Mum warned me Preston’s a bit… rough. Preston's alright. Just don’t wander down any dark alleys. It’s improved a lot in recent years. They've built a fancy new shopping centre. Though to be honest, I still prefer the market. You can get a bargain there. I need to find a good greengrocer. Supermarket fruit is just…sad. It has no flavour. Ooh, and I need new pens! All mine have run out of ink. And maybe some highlighters, for  Jane Eyre .

Honestly, Mum, you scared the life out of us! Just appearing like that. We weren't expecting you until next week. Oh, don't be daft, love. I saw the weather forecast – dreadful for the next few days. Thought I'd get up here while I could. Besides, I wanted to surprise young Master Theo. How's school going, lad? It's alright. We're doing Shakespeare. It's… complicated. Complicated is an understatement. Trying to get a fourteen-year-old interested in ‘thee’ and ‘thou’ is a full-time job. Shakespeare's wonderful! I used to adore it. Although, when I was at university, we had a dreadful professor. Tried to make it all terribly serious and intellectual. It was exhausting. We used to sneak off and watch Morecambe and Wise afterwards just to recover. Now  that  was comedy. Morecambe and Wise? Who are they? Oh, Theo… you have a lot of catching up to do. Classic British comedy. Absolutely brilliant. We’ll have to get you some DVDs. Yes, do! You need a bit of proper entertainment. This technology you youngsters are obsessed with… it’s all a bit overwhelming for me. I tried to video call Brenda last week and ended up broadcasting to the entire village. Oh, Mum! You and technology… It’s a disaster waiting to happen. I tried to show you how to use online banking last time and nearly had a heart attack. Well, it’s complicated, isn't it? All these passwords and security questions. What if I forget my mother’s maiden name? It's been years! And all this talk about hacking… terrifying. It’s not  that  scary. You just need a strong password. Easy for you to say, young man. You’ve grown up with it. I was perfectly happy with a chequebook and a friendly bank manager. Anyway, I was having a clear-out and found a box of old photos. Thought I'd bring them along. We can have a good reminisce. That’s lovely, Mum. Though goodness knows what horrors we’ll unearth. Remember the one of Dad with that ridiculous Hawaiian shirt? Oh, dear, yes. Honestly, that shirt. He thought he looked so dashing. He did have a good heart, your father. It’s just… he struggled, you know? With his moods. It wasn’t easy for any of us. It wasn't. Looking back now, it's clear he needed help.

Right, so, what do we think? Is it…is it doing alright? It felt a bit sluggish opening that tab. It’s alright. Not exactly lightning, is it? What specs did you get again? You said you went for… the one with the extra ram? Yeah, 16 gig. Supposed to be decent, but honestly, I’m already wondering if I should’ve splashed out on the SSD. It feels… like my old one, just slightly less terrible. SSD makes a  massive  difference. Like night and day. Honestly, if you’re gonna be doing anything more than Word and emails, get one. It's worth every penny. That’s what I’m thinking. I was watching a YouTube vid, this guy was saying you can clone your existing drive onto one. Is that easy enough to do? Yeah, pretty straightforward. There's loads of free software out there. Macrium Reflect is good. You’ll need a SATA to USB adapter thingy to connect the new SSD, though. Right, a… SATA adapter. Added to the list. Oh god, it’s already a list. I just wanted a laptop that didn’t make me want to throw it out the window. Remember old man Hemmings’ computer? Down the road? That thing sounded like a jet engine taking off. Oh God, yeah! He used to brag about how much RAM it had too. It was like, 64 megabytes. Back in the day, that was probably amazing, but… He told me he used to download music on it using dial-up. Said it took hours for one song. Hours! I can’t even  imagine . This thing’s loading a YouTube video in, like, five seconds. Still slow, but…progress. Speaking of YouTube, you guys seen that new MMA fighter, “The Cyclone”? Nah, I've been too busy trying to get the climbing roses to actually climb. They're just flopping about like sad noodles. He's insane. Knocked out three guys in the first round last week. Proper brutal. I’m thinking of trying to get back into training again. Been feeling a bit… soft. Soft? You’re constantly lifting weights! You look like you could wrestle a bear. A small bear. Maybe. I need to be more disciplined. And eat less takeaway. I had a Korean takeaway on Tuesday, it was amazing, but my jeans are definitely tighter. Korean's good. Have you tried that place near the market?

Honestly, this place is lovely, isn’t it? Such a nice change from… well, everything else in Tarnow’s centre square. It was a betting shop before, wasn't it? Truly grim. Yeah, a proper dive. You wouldn't have sent your nan in there. They've done a good job with it though. Really bright, and that music isn’t awful which is a bonus. Exactly. It feels… hopeful. Which is weird to say about a bistro, I suppose. It feels like someone actually  invested  in something nice. I’m really hoping it does well. Me too. We need more places like this. Speaking of investing in things… I've been thinking a lot about my auntie Brenda recently. Oh? How’s she doing? Last I heard she was finally trying that pottery class. Yeah, she loves the pottery. It’s the, well, the  other  stuff. She relapsed, hasn’t she? With the gambling. Oh, no. That's awful. I was hoping she’d finally gotten a grip on that. It’s such a destructive thing. Such a… identity thing, isn't it? Like she fills a void with it. Exactly! That's what I was thinking. Like, who is Brenda without the ‘thrill’ of it? It sounds so pathetic, saying it like that, but it’s true. It became  her . And now she’s lost it and… well, she's lost herself again. It's heartbreaking. I remember when she was obsessed with those fitness classes. For about six months, it was all body pump and spinach smoothies. Oh, God yes! And the leggings. The endless leggings. Then she suddenly decided it was all a waste of time and started baking. A  lot  of baking. And then the betting shops. It’s a cycle, isn’t it? Always searching for something to fill the space. I wonder if she ever just… wants to  be  Brenda, without needing a hobby or an obsession to define her. I think she does, deep down. It's just… I don't know. It’s terrifying, isn’t it? Facing yourself, really facing yourself. It's easier to latch onto something. It is. Makes you think, doesn't it? About what we all do to avoid… well, everything. I keep telling myself I'm going to start running again. I’ve had these trainers for months. They’re still in the box. Classic. You and a million other people.

Right, so have you actually booked the tickets for the Steam Fair then, Grandad? Because I was looking online and it said they’re doing early bird discounts if you book before the end of the month. Oh, aye, booked ‘em last week, love. Got us all in, didn’t I? Booked a disabled space for your Auntie Carol, too. She’ll need it with her hip, poor thing. They’ve got a good system there, decent facilities. Much better than that motorbike show we went to last year, remember? Absolute shambles that was. Oh, it was a nightmare! Trying to get Carol’s wheelchair around those muddy fields… Nearly lost her a couple of times. Good on you for thinking ahead, Dad. Is there plenty of seating, hopefully? My back’s been playing up again. Good. I was a bit worried about accessibility, to be honest. It's a huge site isn't it, and Mum was saying she doesn't want to spend the whole day standing. They’ve got loads of benches dotted around and little huts selling tea and biscuits. Proper old-fashioned, it is. Reminds me of when I was a lad, going with your Grandad –  my  dad – to these sorts of things. Though it wasn’t called the Steam Fair then, it was just a local rally. They had traction engines, all gleaming and polished. It sounds lovely. I do like all those old machines. It’s just getting there and getting around that’s the worry. By the way, have you seen what houses are going for around here now? Absolutely ridiculous. Tell me about it! I was looking at flats in Boscombe the other day, and even tiny little one-bed places are like, £900 a month. It’s insane. Bournemouth is a right little hotspot, ain’t it? Everyone’s flocking down here. Used to be a quiet seaside town, now…well, it’s just built up and pricey. When  I  first came to London, you could get a decent house for a few thousand quid. A few  thousand ! Can you imagine? It’s a different world. We were talking about moving, you and me, weren’t we? Further down the coast, maybe? Somewhere a bit cheaper. That’s a good idea. Somewhere with a garden, so we can have a cat. I’ve been wanting a cat forever! A little ginger one.

Honestly, this weather is dreadful, isn’t it? Rain, rain, rain. Reminds me of Kendal, actually. Always a bit drizzly up there. Aye, it's a bit grim. Though good for the garden, I suppose. Though it’s not really a garden, is it, just a patch of… stuff. Can I have another biscuit? Yes, dear, but just one more. You’ll be bouncing off the walls before bedtime. Are you enjoying your school, by the way? Anything interesting happening? It's alright. We're doing Shakespeare in English. Shakespeare! Oh, that’s lovely. I used to adore Shakespeare.  Hamlet  was always my favourite. Though I could never quite understand what all the fuss was about with that Ophelia girl. Such a silly thing to drown over a boy, if you ask me. Grandma! Well, it’s true! Though, I suppose attitudes were different back then. Of course, I've been reading a bit about the historical Jesus recently. Quite fascinating, actually. The layers of interpretation… it's like peeling an onion. Oh, you and your theology! Always something to ponder. I’ve been trying to get to grips with the new safeguarding policies at school. Honestly, the paperwork is endless. It’s all well-intentioned, of course, but it’s a bit overwhelming. Mum, can I have my iPad? After tea, love. No screens at the table. What are you planning for later, then? Anything special? I thought we might go to that little artisan bakery in Thirsk. They do a brilliant sourdough. And then perhaps a quick look around the church? They’re having a flower festival this weekend. Oh, lovely! I do love a good flower festival. Though I do wish people wouldn’t put quite so many lilies in. They smell dreadfully funereal. You’re always one for noticing the details, aren’t you? I saw on Twitter that old Mrs. Higgins has started a pottery class. Apparently, it’s very popular. Twitter? What’s that? It's... a way of sharing little messages online. Like a really, really public noticeboard. Oh, it's a right rabbit warren, that Twitter. I tried it once, but I couldn't make head nor tail of it. All those young people shouting into the void. It's a useful way to keep up with local events, though. And the school uses it to send out reminders. Though sometimes it’s just people arguing.

Right, so dentist appointment is booked for Cindy on Tuesday afternoon. Just a check-up, nothing to worry about. Oh. Will it hurt? No, sweetie, it shouldn’t. They just look at your teeth to make sure everything’s healthy. It’s quick. More boring than anything. I had a filling once. It  did  hurt. That’s different, darling. That was a filling. This is just a look. Remember when you had your hearing test? That wasn’t hurting, was it? No, but it was weird. This is a bit like that. Just… a look. Speaking of tests, I need to book Aaron’s hearing test too. He’s been asking me to repeat things a lot lately. Maybe he just doesn’t  want  to listen. Maybe. Or maybe he genuinely needs it checked. Anyway, did you both remember to tell me what you want for your birthdays? It's coming up so quickly! I want a Lego spaceship. A really,  really  big one. Okay, a Lego spaceship. Noted. Cindy? I... I’m not sure. Maybe a new art set? Or… that game all my friends are talking about? The one with the little people? Oh, ‘Bloomies’? Is that the one? Yeah! Bloomies! Alright. We’ll see. It's a combined birthday, remember? And it's always tricky splitting things fairly when you share a day. It's not ideal, honestly. Imagine having a birthday on the same day as your sibling! It's good! More presents! Yes, more presents, but also more arguments about who gets what. Speaking of which, are you eating all those radishes? I brought them for a salad. They’re crunchy! They taste like pepper. They're supposed to be quite mild. Actually, you know Ashaad, my friend from work? Her birthday is next week too. Isn't that funny? Three birthdays all close together. She’s turning… well, she’s a bit older than you two, but still! Is she getting a Lego spaceship? I highly doubt it. She’s more into… museums. And Monet. She loves Monet. You wouldn’t believe how much she knows about Impressionism. What's a museum? It's… a place where they keep old things. Paintings, sculptures, things like that. Remember when we went on the school trip to the Roald Dahl museum? It's a bit like that, but with different things. Can we get Easter chocolate? Yes, we can get Easter chocolate.

Honestly, I’ve been living off pesto pasta for, like, four days straight. It's a culinary low, even for me. Oh, you are hopeless! You were always the worst at feeding yourself properly, even at uni. Remember that time you tried to make beans on toast and set off the smoke alarm? Hey! That was a momentary lapse in judgement fuelled by extreme hunger and a lack of kitchen skills. Which, admittedly, haven’t improved drastically. And you weren’t much better, constantly surviving on cereal. Rude! I had a balanced diet of Fruit Loops… sometimes. But seriously, you need to expand your repertoire. I made a massive chilli last night, I could bring some round? Oh my god, yes please! You are a lifesaver. I’ve been meaning to actually  cook  something, but work’s been insane. Copywriting deadlines are the bane of my existence right now. Tell me about it. Adult acute speech therapy is… intense. Literally spent the morning trying to help a gentleman who’d had a stroke relearn how to say ‘banana’. It’s rewarding, but draining. Wow, that sounds… challenging. And heartwarming, I guess? I’m just writing slogans for shampoo. It’s not exactly changing the world. Hey, someone has to make sure people know which shampoo makes their hair shiny! It all contributes. Speaking of contributing… have you started saving for a deposit on a place yet? Ugh, don’t even. It feels utterly impossible. Rent in London is ridiculous, and then there’s the deposit, and stamp duty… I’ve got a spreadsheet going, but it mostly just makes me feel depressed. I know, right? I’m trying to be sensible, but it's so hard. Mum keeps offering to help, but I'm stubbornly refusing. I need to do it myself. Smart. It’s a whole thing with my parents, though. They're convinced I should move back to Kent. “It’s so much cheaper, darling, and you’re closer to us!” Like my entire life should revolve around their convenience. Oh, god, no. Mine are the same. Constantly asking when I’m going to settle down and have kids. It's like, back off! I haven’t even figured out what I’m having for dinner, let alone the rest of my life. Exactly! It's exhausting. Remember when we were kids and we swore we’d never be like them?

…and honestly, the sheer audacity of it! He just rocked up with a suitcase full of francs, handed it over, and the farmer just… accepted! No solicitors, no surveys, nothing. Just a handshake and a suitcase full of cash. Can you imagine trying that now? Absolutely not! You’d be arrested, probably. Though, it does sound rather… idyllic, doesn’t it? A bit like something out of a film. Speaking of idyllic, have you seen what they’re trying to do with Market Harborough? Rebranding it as a ‘boutique’ destination. Boutique? Good grief. What’s wrong with being a perfectly respectable market town? They’ve been tinkering with it for years. Remember when they widened the High Street? Ruined it completely. Took away all the character. Oh, the High Street was lovely before that. Proper shops, not just charity shops and coffee chains. I did a lot of my early practice shopping there, you know. Being an NHS dentist had its perks back then. Sailing trips, for a start. Sailing trips? Oh yes! The dental association used to run them. Whole conferences, lectures all at sea with your oral surgeon! Can you imagine the state of things if someone had a toothache mid-Atlantic? Goodness me. Sounds… memorable. Though, I suppose it was different then. More camaraderie, less litigation. Honestly, the lengths some people go to these days… I was trying to get tickets for that Hockney exhibition, completely sold out, but somehow managed to wangle a couple through a friend of a friend. Ah, the old network. Still works wonders. I’m more concerned about that solar farm they approved last night. An absolute eyesore. They’ve stuck it right on the edge of town, ruining the view from the canal. I know! It’s dreadful. All that countryside, wasted on a field of black panels. Though, I suppose we have to move with the times. Moving with the times… that’s what they said when they started replacing all the beautiful Victorian buildings with concrete monstrosities. Progress, they called it. Made the whole town look like a Soviet housing estate. It's a shame, isn't it? The architecture was so lovely. They need to do something about it. I was in Prague last year, you know. Now  that  is a city that knows how to preserve its heritage. Honestly, it's stunning. And so cheap! You can have a lovely weekend there for next to nothing.

Right, so we’re agreed – short-form video is where it’s at, isn’t it? TikTok, Instagram Reels… that’s where the eyeballs are. But how do we make it  educational  without being utterly… dull? Exactly! That’s the challenge. I was thinking, instead of just lecturing at a camera, we could do case studies. Like, deconstructing viral videos. Take a really popular TikTok, and break down  why  it worked. What editing techniques were used? What narrative structure? How did it tap into current trends? I like that. “Moving Image Forensics,” almost. But we need a niche. Everyone’s doing ‘explainers’ now. What’s our angle? Well, I’ve been thinking about my students. They struggle with visual literacy. They can  consume  endless amounts of video, but they can’t critically analyse it. They don't understand the persuasive techniques being used, or the subconscious ways images affect them. So, the focus is on teaching  analysis  of visual media, rather than just  creating  it?
