That's clever. We're not competing with the content creators, we're equipping people to understand them. Precisely. Think about it – it’s applicable to everything. Advertising, news, propaganda… understanding how images work is a crucial skill in the modern world. And we can use really accessible examples, like those ridiculous dance challenges. Right, deconstructing the floss. I can see that. What about a platform? We could just use YouTube, but it feels…saturated. Is there a way to build a community? That's what I was pondering. I’ve been playing around with Patreon. Maybe offer tiered subscriptions? Free content on YouTube to lure people in, then more in-depth analyses, downloadable resources – worksheets, analysis frameworks – behind a paywall on Patreon? Hmm, Patreon is interesting. It’s relying on direct support, which is good. But it means we  have  to consistently deliver valuable content. No pressure. What about leveraging LinkedIn? Target teachers, media studies lecturers… they might be interested in using our case studies in their classrooms. Oh! That’s brilliant. A B2B element as well as direct-to-consumer. We could offer licensing agreements for educational institutions. Exactly. We’re solving a problem for both groups. Teachers need resources, students need skills. Building a LinkedIn presence is definitely cheaper than running Facebook ads, too. And we could target specific curricula. Like, if there's a unit on persuasive techniques in GCSE media studies, we could create a series of videos specifically designed to support that.

It’s just…remember when we went to Cornwall with Ben and Chloe, and Ben was convinced he saw a mermaid? Oh god, yes! He was  so  serious. Staring out to sea with his binoculars for a solid hour. Chloe was trying to subtly steer him towards the ice cream van. She knew better than to encourage it. It was freezing, honestly. Mid-September, and he was convinced a mermaid was sunbathing on the rocks. He’d been reading some ridiculous folklore book beforehand, I think. Something about ancient Cornish mermaids and shipwrecks… Honestly, the stories he comes up with. It's endearing, though, isn't it? That childlike wonder. I mean, I’d love to  believe  in mermaids, even just for a second. Especially looking out at a grey North Sea. Makes it feel a little more magical. True. Though I prefer a good, solid scientific explanation for everything. Less opportunity for disappointment that way. Still, his dedication was impressive. He even sketched what he thought she looked like. Oh, don’t even remind me about the sketch! It was halfway between a fish and a Victorian lady. With flowing hair. And a tiara. Precisely. I think Chloe secretly took a photo of it and threatened to use it as their Christmas card. She absolutely did. Remember how cross he was when she mentioned it? He insisted it was a ‘preliminary study’. A preliminary study in mermaid anatomy. Classic Ben. Do you think he still believes? I wouldn't be surprised. He's got that unwavering faith in things. It’s what makes him, well, Ben. And it’s nice to be around someone who can still get genuinely excited about the possibility of something extraordinary. You’re right. We could all do with a little more of that. It’s easy to get bogged down in…everything. Work, bills, the state of the world. A mermaid sighting, even a fabricated one, is a welcome distraction. Exactly. And… it reminds me of when we were kids, spending summers at the beach. That feeling of endless possibility. That the sea held secrets. Yeah. And believing anything was possible. Before reality set in. Still…a mermaid. It's a lovely thought, isn't it? Maybe we should go back to Cornwall. Just in case. Perhaps. But I’m packing the binoculars this time. Just in case  I  see something. Oh, you wouldn’t!

Oh my god, look at what she’s wearing! That dress is… a choice. Seriously. What  is  that fabric? It looks like something my nan used to have curtains made of. Oh, you’re brutal! But yes, it’s a bit much for a daytime talk show, isn’t it? It’s screaming ‘I want attention!’ It's the colour too. That shade of mustard yellow... It just washes her out completely. She looks peaky. You know who could pull that off? Alexa Chung. She could make a bin bag look fashionable. True. She has that… effortless thing. It's annoying, isn't it? I tried to copy her style once, ended up looking like I'd raided a vintage shop blindfolded. I know that feeling! I saw a skirt online the other day, looked amazing on the model, got it home and it just looked…wrong. Like it was actively fighting against my body shape. That’s the curse of online shopping. You never really know what you’re getting. I’m trying to be better about fast fashion though, you know? It's terrible for the environment. Me too. I’ve been trying to shop my own wardrobe more, rediscover things I’d forgotten about. It’s surprisingly satisfying. Although, it also means admitting I bought some questionable things over the years… Oh, we’ve all been there! Remember that phase we went through with those oversized denim jackets? Don’t remind me! I have photographic evidence somewhere, that needs to be destroyed. I think I still have mine, somewhere in the attic. It’s coming back into fashion though, apparently. Don’t tell anyone I said that. No way! Seriously? Maybe we should dust them off and embrace the 90s revival. I think I’d rather burn mine and pretend it never happened. But speaking of fashion, are we still on for that vintage shopping trip next weekend? Definitely! I’ve been saving up. I’m hoping to find a really good leather jacket. Ooh, good luck with that! I'm on the hunt for a decent pair of boots. Mine are falling apart. We’ll have to hit up Mill Road, that’s where all the good charity shops are. Actually, what time are we thinking? I might have a work thing on Saturday afternoon. What sort of work thing? Still doing those massive conferences? Yeah, a tech one this time.

So how was college today, darling? Anything exciting happen? It was okay, really. History was… History. Mr. Davies went on another one of his tangents about the Tudors. Honestly, you'd think he  lived  through it. He does get a bit carried away, doesn’t he? Still, better than a boring lesson, I suppose. Did you manage to get any of that photography homework done? The one with the portraits? Ugh, don’t even remind me. I took loads, but they all look awful. Everyone looks so…stiff. I can’t seem to capture anything natural. I'm really worried about it. Oh, come on now, don’t be so hard on yourself. Photography takes practice, you know? Remember when I first started taking pictures on that old film camera? Every single photo was either blurry or overexposed! It took ages to get the hang of it. But you’re good at it now! You take amazing pictures. All those landscapes you’ve done… they're beautiful. Well, thank you, love. It’s just a matter of experimentation. Maybe try different lighting? Or ask your friends to relax a bit? Tell them to think about something funny. I did try telling Chloe to think about that comedian, the one we watched on Netflix… what's his name? The really sarcastic one? Is that Jimmy Carr? Yeah! Jimmy Carr! But then she just started giggling and wouldn’t stop moving. It was hopeless. Oh dear. Well, at least you got a giggle out of her. Honestly, sometimes you just have to embrace the chaos. How’s work been? Still dealing with demanding patients at the surgery? It was quiet today, thankfully. Old Mrs. Higgins was in, complaining about her bunions again. Honestly, I think she just likes the attention. But then Mr. Peterson came in, really flustered because he’d lost his glasses  again . Oh, that man! He’s a menace. Always losing things. You must have a lot of patience, dealing with all that. It’s okay. It’s just… tiring sometimes. I wish I had time to read more. I started that new book you recommended, the historical fiction one… “The Nightingale”? Yeah, that one. But I keep falling asleep after about five pages. I think I’m just too exhausted. And then I worry about falling behind on my schoolwork. Well, you need to prioritize, darling. Maybe don’t try to cram everything in at once.

Right well that was a dreadful football match wasn’t it? Absolute rubbish. Oh don’t start, Harold. I haven’t even had a chance to sit down properly. You know I was battling with that application form all morning. Which one was that, Mum? The council tax one? No, no, the blooming blue badge one! Honestly, it’s like they deliberately make it difficult. Asking for details from twenty years ago! Who remembers that? And then wanting a photograph...a current photograph. I look nothing like my passport photo. They’re all the same are they, paperwork. Just designed to confuse. Makes you wonder if anyone actually reads them. Sounds frustrating. Did you get it all sorted eventually? Nearly. I had to ring them. Spent half an hour on hold listening to that awful music. And then the woman I spoke to was completely unhelpful. Said I needed a letter from my doctor. A letter! For a blue badge! They’re just covering their backsides. That’s all it is. I saw old Mrs. Higgins the other day, she’s got one now. Said it made a world of difference. Good. Hopefully you’ll get yours sorted quickly too. So, how’s the garden looking, Dad? Any sign of those baby birds fledging yet? Not yet, still in the nest. Mum’s been putting out bread crumbs for them, though the cockerel keeps trying to steal them. Little feathered menace, that one. He's a right terror. I swear he thinks he rules the roost. Speaking of terrors, little Timmy Baker at the playgroup today… honestly. Oh, Timmy? What’s he been up to now? Bit everything, to be honest. Hit little Emily, wouldn’t share the building blocks, and then proceeded to empty the sandpit all over little George. It’s exhausting. Makes me glad I’m retired from it. Difficult children. They always were. Remember young Derek next door? Used to set fire to dustbins. Oh Harold! Don’t remind me. His mother was at me constantly. Still, he turned out alright, I believe. Works as a plumber now. Probably learned a thing or two about pipes from setting fires! Speaking of learning, I’ve been looking into getting a 3D printer. A what now? One of them fancy gadgets? Yeah, they’re pretty affordable now. I thought it’d be good for making bits and bobs for lessons, maybe some models or prototypes.

So, she’s actually looking at flats now, can you believe it? After all this time talking about it, it’s… happening. That’s wonderful, Margaret. Truly. It must be a relief, for both of you. Though, you always did seem fairly resolute about it, didn’t you? Even when I was questioning the logistics. Oh, I was resolute alright. But resolute and not panicked are two very different things, Charles. Terrified doesn’t even begin to cover it, some days. Thirty years she’s been in Australia. Thirty years! And now, suddenly, she’s… uprooting everything. It’s a big change, certainly. But a good one, I think. She’s always seemed… adrift, somehow. Despite seeming to have everything she wanted out there. A good job, a nice house, a lovely garden… Exactly. Lovely. But not  here . Not with family. She says she misses the seasons, properly. The grey skies, the bracing sea air. Can you imagine? She’s traded sunshine for drizzle, and heat for…well, more drizzle, mostly. She always was a bit of a romantic. And Brighton is a good choice, I think. She’ll be close to you, naturally, and it’s got a bit of a cosmopolitan vibe, hasn’t it? She won’t feel  too  out of place after Sydney. That's what I keep telling myself. And it’s not just the practicalities, you know? The visa, the finding somewhere to live, the NHS registration… it’s the emotional side. She’s… different now. It’s like I’m meeting a slightly altered version of my daughter. That’s natural, Margaret. People change. Especially after living somewhere for so long. She’ll have absorbed a lot of Australian culture, naturally. She's already started using phrases I don’t understand! “No worries,” she said to me the other day, when I was fretting about the paperwork. “No worries!” As if life is simply devoid of worries. It’s infuriatingly cheerful. That does sound rather… Australian. It’s a good thing, though, isn’t it? She’s adaptable. She’ll fit in. I hope so. I just worry, you know? About her being happy. About her getting settled. About her regretting it all and wanting to go back. It's a huge undertaking. Financially, too. She’s talking about needing a loan to get started, and I… well, I'm not exactly flush with funds, am I?

So, did you catch any of that Scottish referendum debate last night? Absolute chaos, wasn't it? A bit of it, yeah. Flicked it on and off. Honestly, it all feels a bit… exhausting now, doesn't it? Been going on for ages. I'm not sure anyone really  knows  what the outcome will be, do they? Exactly. Feels like everyone's just digging their heels in. Though, I have to say, that Alistair Darling… he's a remarkably calm presence amidst all the shouting. He is, isn’t he? Steady as a rock. Unlike that Salmond chap, always full of bluster. Speaking of stressful situations, how did the interview go? The one for the head of department role? Oh, don't even ask. It was… an experience. The panel were pretty intense. Lots of questions about ‘vision’ and ‘strategic leadership’. I think I mostly talked about marking schemes and student feedback. That sounds about right for you, Mark. You’re a practical man, not a visionary. Still, you’ve got the experience. They’d be foolish not to offer you the role. I’m not so sure. There was this one chap on the panel, Dr. Henderson, kept interrupting. Proper condescending tone. He clearly had his favourite candidate already lined up. Oh, Henderson. Yes, he's… a personality. Thinks he’s the next big thing in post-structuralism, doesn't he? Precisely! Anyway, enough about my career woes. How's Sarah doing? I haven’t spoken to her in ages. She’s good, she’s good. Keep busy, as always. Her daughter, Emily, just started university. She’s studying English Literature, can you believe it? Wow, that's fantastic! Where's she going? York. Apparently, it has a brilliant English department. She's a bit nervous, naturally, but mostly excited. We helped her move in last week. It's strange seeing them grow up so fast, isn’t it? Seems like only yesterday she was a little girl. Tell me about it. It's terrifying. My sister just had her first, a little boy, and it's making me seriously contemplate the future. Well, don't rush into anything! Parenthood's a huge commitment. Though, it is incredibly rewarding, I hear. I know, I know. It’s just… the world feels a bit unstable at the moment, doesn’t it? Scotland, the economy, Brexit looming… feels like a weird time to be bringing a child into it all.

Right, so the little wooden block goes  here , doesn’t it? Honestly, this mousetrap game is far more complicated than it looks. I thought it would be a five-minute job. You always underestimate these things, darling. Remember the flatpack bookcase? That took a whole weekend. Yeah, and nearly resulted in a divorce. Can I have another biscuit? Please? In a minute, Leo. Let your mother finish. It’s supposed to be a family activity, remember? Well, it’s meant to be  fun . It’s currently inducing a low-level rage. Right, there. Now, the string… Speaking of complicated things, did I ever tell you about trying to explain cricket to a group of American kids when I was working in Washington? Oh, I remember you mentioning it. Wasn't it a disaster? A complete disaster. They just couldn’t grasp the concept of a game that could last for  five days . Five days! They were used to baseball, fast-paced, action-packed. They kept asking when someone was going to get punched. Oh, dear. That’s… understandable, I suppose. American kids are raised on spectacle. Were they really confused? Confused is an understatement, Leo. One little girl asked if the players needed oxygen masks because they were running around for so long. And they wouldn't believe you weren't allowed to run between bases. It was like explaining the rules of a different universe. It's funny, isn't it? How different cultures perceive things. I remember being shocked by the portion sizes when we went to the States. Everything was enormous. Yeah, you could get a burger the size of your head. And the amount of sugar in everything… insane. Don’t even get me started on the sugary cereals. It’s a wonder they don’t all have diabetes. Those poor children. I like sugary cereals! We know you do, darling. But everything in moderation. Right, I think I’ve finally got this bit sorted. Now, where does this little spring…Oh, for goodness sake! It keeps pinging off! Need a hand, love? No, no, I'm fine. I just need to… wrestle it into submission. It’s a matter of principle now. I  will  conquer this mousetrap game! Want to hear a story about a time I tried to cook a Thanksgiving dinner in a tiny student kitchen? It also ended in mild chaos. Yes! Tell me!

Right, so I went to that little shop near the university today, you know, the one with all the… stuff? The one that always smells faintly of incense and regret? Exactly! And they had a sale on. Honestly, I didn’t  need  anything, but… But you saw something? This is a familiar story. I saw this dress. It’s… well, it’s sort of teal, but a really dusty teal, you know? Not bright, more muted. And it's linen. Linen? In this humidity? Brave. I know, I know! But it’s got these really wide sleeves, and a tie waist. I thought it might be good for lectures, you know, a bit more… flowing. Less ‘sensible academic’. Sensible academic is your usual look though, isn’t it? It is! But I feel like I’m getting stuck in a rut. Everything’s become beige cardigans and practical shoes. I need a little… flair. And the dress provides flair? Potentially! It was £40, which felt reasonable. And then… then I saw the jumpsuit. Oh dear. Here we go. It’s navy, really flattering cut, wide legs, and it has pockets. Proper pockets! Pockets are always a win. What was the damage with that one? £55. But it was reduced from £90! And I can see myself wearing it for… everything. Weekends, more casual lectures, maybe even out for dinner. So, teal linen dress and navy jumpsuit. That’s a significant haul for a ‘didn’t need anything’ trip. I know! Don't judge me. It’s been a stressful week with marking, I deserve a little retail therapy. I’m not judging, just… observing the pattern. Do they both fit? Because that’s often the sticking point with those little shops. Yes! Miraculously, both fit perfectly. I tried on about five different things that were either too tight or completely shapeless, but these two were… the ones. Well, that’s good. I’m just picturing you trying to navigate the campus in linen in ninety percent humidity. You might resemble a wilted lettuce. Okay, you have a point. Maybe the dress is reserved for air-conditioned buildings. But the jumpsuit is definitely a winner. You'll see! I shall be the most stylish lecturer in the whole department. I have no doubt. Although, you’ll be sweating buckets, looking stylish. Hopefully, this fits the requested context! Let me know if you’d like any modifications.

Right, well that was a match wasn’t it? Absolutely ferocious. Though I thought the ref was a bit… eager, shall we say? Giving away penalties left, right and centre. Yeah, but Ireland played really well! Even though they were down for a bit, they came back strong. That try by Bundee Aki was amazing! It was a good match, massively stressful though. My heart was hammering the whole time. I kept having to look away. Oh, rugby. Not my cup of tea. Too much… grappling. Give me a good game of netball any day! But, it’s lovely to see everyone enjoying themselves. Ach, now Nan, you just haven't given it a fair chance. It’s a thinking man’s game, rugby is. Strategery and all that. Speaking of thinking, I have a history test tomorrow. On the Tudors. It’s going to be awful. Oh, darling, that sounds dreadful. Did you do much revision? We can quiz you later if you like. A little. Mr. Henderson keeps making us write essays. Like, who  needs  to write an essay about Henry VIII’s wives? Just tell us the facts! Ah, teachers. Always making life difficult. I remember… oh never mind. That’s a story for another day. Oisin, are you still awake? He went up ages ago. He was tired after playing football at school. He said they’re starting a new unit on athletics. Oh, lovely! He enjoys his sports, doesn’t he? That’s good for him. Keeps him active. It’s important, that, to have hobbies and interests. That’s what I tried to instill in all my pupils. Though sometimes, persuading them was a challenge! Well, he’s inherited your stubborn streak, Nan, that’s for sure. Right, is everyone finished? I was thinking we could maybe go outside and do a bit of stargazing later. The sky is supposed to be clear. Oh, that sounds lovely! I haven’t done that in ages. Cool! Can I take my telescope? Absolutely. You can try and find some constellations. It’s a bit chilly out there, mind you. I’ll get my shawl. Perfect. Now, have we signed that card for Auntie Moira yet? Her birthday is on Friday. It’s on the table there, I think. I wrote something in it earlier. I’ll sign it after I finish my pudding. It’s chocolate fudge, best pudding ever!

Honestly, the estate agents are driving me mad. Every single one says “Oh, it’s  just  come on the market!” when it’s clearly been listed for two weeks. Two weeks in the current climate is an eternity. Oh, tell me about it! It’s the same everywhere, isn’t it? Luckily, we're staying put for now, though I’m already picturing what the nursery would look like... if things ever happen with the IVF. Oh, how are things going with that? Any news? Not yet. Results are next week. I’m trying not to get my hopes up, which is spectacularly failing, obviously. I’ve already started browsing miniature wardrobes online. It's pathetic. No, it’s not pathetic at all! It's perfectly normal to start daydreaming. It's lovely, actually. I was doing the same thing when we were trying for Leo. Though, honestly, the amount of baby stuff you end up with… it’s insane. That’s what my mum says! She's already offered to send down boxes and boxes of my old clothes, and even some of my brother's. Apparently, hand-me-downs are ‘very chic’ now. Oh god, your brother’s clothes? No thank you! He had questionable taste, even then. Though, seriously, take what you can from your mum. Babies grow out of things so quickly it's ridiculous. I swear Leo was in six-to-nine months clothes for approximately a week. It’s the thought that counts, I guess. She's just so excited. It's sweet but a bit overwhelming. She keeps asking what languages I'm going to teach the baby. Oh, the pressure! Are you thinking of doing the whole bilingual thing? I’d love to, but I'm not sure I'm up to the task. My French is… rusty, to say the least. Trying to remember verb conjugations while sleep-deprived and covered in baby sick doesn't sound very appealing. Haha, yeah, that does sound tricky! Maybe start small? Just sing French nursery rhymes or something? Leo's surprisingly good at picking up languages, he's already attempting a few words in Spanish from his little friend at nursery. That’s amazing! Maybe I should just stick to the nursery rhymes. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I'm back in university, trying to cram for a language exam. Though, at least then I had more than three hours of sleep a night.

Right so I was talking to old man Hemmings down the allotments this morning, right, and he's going on about this bloke trying to sell him a "genuine antique" watering can. Turns out it was made in a factory last Tuesday. Classic Hemmings. He believes anything. Honestly, if someone told him the moon was made of cheese, he’d start looking for a giant grater. Sounds about right. He still reckons Luton Airport is a vital strategic asset. Exactly. Anyway, he was saying this bloke had a proper London accent, really ‘oi guv’nor’ and everything. Made me think about accents, actually. You spent a bit of time in Spain, didn't you, Leo? Did you pick up anything? A bit, yeah. Mostly just sounding incredibly polite all the time. It's ingrained in the culture. Though I did try and mimic a Valencian accent for a bit, just to wind up the language exchange partners. Didn’t go down too well. My Nan, she speaks like she’s still in Cyprus, even though she’s lived here for fifty years. Proper strong accent. Used to confuse the teachers at school. My mum keeps saying my accent’s getting worse. Says I’m sounding more and more like I’m from… well, nowhere, apparently. Just Bedfordshire mush. That’s just mums. They’re programmed to find fault. Speaking of fault…did anyone see that fight last night? The one with the Brazilian guy? Absolute carnage. Mate, I  live  for that stuff. Proper skilled, those guys. Makes you think about protecting yourself, doesn't it? I've been looking at some self-defence classes, actually. Figured knowing a few moves wouldn’t hurt, especially working down the allotments. Good shout. I used to do a bit of boxing when I was at college. Always handy. Though mostly I just got punched in the face. What about you, Leo? Still playing with those guitars? Trying to. Been a bit busy with marking essays. Endless essays about… well, honestly, I’ve forgotten. Something about Shakespeare, probably. I did manage to get a new amp though. Small one, for the flat. Nice one! Need to jam sometime. We should dust off that old board game, Rebellion. Remember that? Total chaos every time. Oh god, yes. That game caused so many arguments. Mum banned it after I accused her of cheating. She claimed she was just employing “strategic thinking.”

Right, so I was thinking, seriously thinking, about maybe…getting a car. Oh really? That’s…a big step. Especially with the cost of everything now. What’s brought this on? Is the cycling getting too much? The cycling’s fine, it’s just… the commute. It’s killing me, honestly. An hour and a half each way, even with the electric bike, in the rain… it’s just draining. And it limits what I can do after work, you know? Can’t stay late for anything. Yeah, I get that. It’s a pain. But a car… insurance is insane, petrol’s insane, parking’s insane…have you actually looked at the figures? I’ve started to. I’ve been browsing AutoTrader, mostly just looking. I was thinking something small, economical. Maybe a little Fiat 500 or something? They seem relatively cheap to buy. A Fiat 500… they’re cute, but they’re tiny. And they’re not exactly known for their reliability. Remember Sarah’s? She was constantly in the garage with it. Okay, okay, point taken. I just… I feel so trapped without a car. Everyone else just  goes  places. You just drive and you’re there. I feel like I’m missing out. I know, it’s frustrating. But maybe look at public transport options again? Is there a faster bus route? Or even a train line you could use for part of the journey? I checked, honestly. The bus takes even longer, and the train doesn’t go anywhere near work. It’s the one major downside to living here, really. It’s lovely, but so inaccessible without a car. Right. Okay. Well, if you’re serious about it, let’s sit down and really crunch the numbers. Not just the price of the car, but everything – insurance, tax, MOT, fuel, maintenance, potential repairs…it adds up quickly. I know, I know. It's scary. I'm trying to start a separate savings account just for "car fund" but it feels like I'm filling a bottomless pit. It's good you're thinking about saving separately. That’s smart. Maybe we could look at some second-hand options too? Something a bit older, but well-maintained? That's what I was thinking. Not something brand new. Although…part of me wants something a bit…fun. Fun and reliable don’t always go hand in hand, sadly.

Right, now then, tea’s brewed, biscuits are out. Grandad, you want a digestive or a Rich Tea? You know you always go for a Rich Tea. Aye, you know me too well, lass. Rich Tea it is. Though a ginger nut wouldn’t go amiss, if you're offering! Don’t encourage him, love. He'll be wanting the whole tin before you know it. How’s school going, lad? Still wrestling with those A-Level equations? It’s alright, Grandma. Mr. Henderson’s set us a practice paper, it’s a killer. It’s all… logarithms and stuff. I just don't  get  it. Logarithms, eh? That’s the stuff that makes my head spin even  marking  the GCSE papers. It’s just… numbers doing fancy dances. Fancy dances! That’s a good way of putting it. Used to just use a slide rule back in my day. No fancy dances needed. Just a bit of sliding. A slide rule? What’s that even  look  like? Oh, it was a long wooden thing, with bits that slid up and down. Your Grandad used one all the time when he was a shipbuilder. Aye, built a fair few ships with that slide rule, I did. Though I suspect they’d be using computers now, wouldn't they? Everything’s computers these days. Speaking of things these days, the washing machine’s making a right racket. I think the drum’s gone again. Honestly, it’s constantly breaking. I swear I’m funding the local repairman’s retirement. Oh, those modern machines. Never as reliable as a good old twin tub. You knew where you were with a twin tub. A twin tub? Was that like, two washing machines in one? More like one washing machine with two sections. You washed one load, then manually transferred it to the other side for the spin. It was hard work, but they lasted forever. And you didn't need a degree to work out how to use it! These new ones, you need a computer science qualification just to figure out what the buttons do. Tell me about it. Anyway, I’ve booked a plumber for tomorrow. Hopefully, he can fix it without needing to replace the whole thing. That’ll be another hundred quid down the drain. Did you remember to order more dog food, Mum? Barnaby’s looking a bit… peckish.

Right, so pirates then. Pirates were… rather scruffy, weren’t they? Not like in the films, all lovely and clean. More… smelly. And probably quite grumpy. Did they have parrots? Some did! But not all. It was more of a… a fashionable thing, I think. A status symbol. Like having a really fancy hat. My parrot’s called Captain! He’s a Lego one. Oh, lovely! Captain the Lego Parrot. Very important. Now, we’ve got Shakespeare week next week at school, which means a  lot  of sonnets and plays. We’re trying to decide if we should go to Stratford. It’s a bit of a drive. Stratford? Is that where Shakespeare lived? It is! You can see his house, and the theatre where he used to put on plays. It would be a good experience, but it's a whole day. Can we go to the circus instead? Well, actually… that’s a really good point! There’s a circus workshop happening, and it’s in a  real  circus! With proper tents and everything. We could learn to juggle! Juggling! Can I learn to juggle balls? They have balls, and scarves, and… lots of things to juggle! It's on Saturday. It’s much closer than Stratford, too. We’d need to book quickly though. Ooh, and can we look at the Easter pictures afterwards? The ones Grandma sent? Absolutely! We can put them on the fridge. It's all very exciting. Are you both getting excited? What about some lunch? I was thinking sandwiches? With pickles! With pickles, of course. And maybe a little bit of magic afterwards? I’ve been practicing a card trick. Can you make a card disappear? I can  try . It doesn’t always work. It's rather tricky. Oh! And I was thinking maybe we could start that stop-motion animation project we talked about. We could make little pirate adventures! Using the Lego! And Captain the Parrot! Exactly! A pirate Lego adventure with Captain the Parrot. Sounds like a good plan, doesn't it? Right, sandwiches first, then magic, then maybe a little bit of pirate planning. And circus! Don't forget the circus! Never! The circus is definitely not forgotten. Can we have chocolate with our sandwiches? We  might  be able to negotiate chocolate with our sandwiches. Let’s see how well you behave during lunchtime. I’ll be very good!

…and honestly, the whole thing was utterly ridiculous. I mean, attempting to sail from Jeddah to Cyprus in a dhow? What was I  thinking ? Sounds…ambitious, Margaret. Rather ambitious. Jeddah to Cyprus is a fair old stretch, isn’t it? A fair old stretch is putting it mildly, David! It all seemed perfectly reasonable at the time, fueled by a certain amount of youthful arrogance and a few too many glasses of…well, let's just say grape juice. It wasn't  easy  to get hold of anything stronger in Saudi, you know? That’s part of the whole story. You were teaching out there then, Margaret? I remember you mentioning it years ago. What was it like? Chaotic. Fascinating. Oppressive. All at once. Extreme weather, very strict rules, desperately polite people…and the constant longing for a proper pint. You get used to the lack of alcohol, eventually. Although I did hear stories of various expats getting creative. Smuggling things in amongst the dates, apparently. Dates and duty-free! A combination I haven’t heard before, Clive. Reminds me of the time a patient of mine tried to smuggle whiskey into India hidden inside medical textbooks. Didn’t end well. Customs were…thorough. Speaking of alcohol, I was in Morocco once, and you could buy anything, absolutely anything, if you knew the right people. Mint tea spiked with something that tasted suspiciously like vodka was a particular favourite. Oh, Morocco is wonderful. Much more relaxed than Saudi. But back to my rather unfortunate adventure…so there I am, setting sail, feeling rather pleased with myself, when I’m intercepted by the Saudi Coast Guard. And…? And they arrested me. Immediately. Apparently, leaving the country without proper authorization,  especially  in a vessel that wasn't exactly seaworthy, was a significant offense. They didn’t appreciate my explanation about wanting to try a Mediterranean salad. A Mediterranean salad? It sounded more convincing at the time! Anyway, I spent three days in a rather unpleasant cell before the British Embassy intervened. They explained to the Saudis that I was a slightly eccentric English teacher and not a spy trying to destabilize the region. Good grief. That’s quite a story. Sounds like you’ve always had a knack for attracting attention, Margaret. Reminds me of the time I tried to sail across Windermere with a mast constructed entirely from old copies of  Dental Practice  magazine… You did  what ?!

Honestly, the state of that bathroom this morning… I don’t know what goes on in there. It looked like a bomb had hit it! Oh, tell me about it. I swear, teenagers operate on another plane of existence. Everything is a performance, a drama. Did you see Leo’s face when I asked if he’d remembered to flush? The outrage! It wasn’t  my  fault the toilet roll ran out. Oh, here we go. Always someone else’s fault, isn't it? It's a wonder they manage to breathe without someone else doing it  for  them. Don't start, Brenda. I'm trying to remain calm. We have a school trip meeting tonight. And then, trying to get him motivated about work experience. It’s like pulling teeth. He just wants to play Fortnite all day. Work experience, eh? They don't appreciate the opportunities these days. When I was his age, you were lucky to get a week down the market sweeping up. Builds character, that does. Sweeping up? No thanks. I want to be an explorer. Like, discovering lost cities and stuff. That’s ambitious, love. Have you thought about what you'd  need  to be an explorer? Maths, geography, potentially languages... I can learn all that. I’m good at geography. And I can build cool stuff, like traps. For… you know, protecting the lost cities. Traps? Oh, lord. Let’s stick to the work experience for now then, shall we? I was talking to Mrs. Higgins at school, and apparently, they’re really struggling to find placements for the year tens. Right, well, I've got a few contacts. Might be able to get him something with a marketing firm I do some proofing for. It’s not uncovering ancient civilizations, but it’s real world experience. Good thinking. Anything is better than nothing. Though, you know what I heard? Old Man Hemmings is looking for someone to help him referee the under-10s football team. Refereeing? Absolutely not! They’re all tiny terrors. And their parents are worse. Probably a good point. Though, it  would  get him out the house… and away from the bathroom. Speaking of which, is anyone else wondering where all the good bath bombs disappeared to? Oh, I saw a certain someone sneaking a few into his friend Daisy's bag yesterday. Apparently, she's the current object of affection.

Honestly though, this bread is unreal. Like, seriously good. It is lovely, isn’t it? Proper sourdough. You don’t get this in Bolton, do you? Not like this. Can I have another bit? Please? Always, lad. You’ve already had enough, mind, don’t push your luck. You’ll be bouncing off the walls. Seriously though, we need to find out where they get their flour. This changes everything. All those attempts at sourdough… wasted. It’s the climate, I reckon. The air here, the quality of the grain… everything. It makes a difference. You can taste it. Can we go truffle hunting tomorrow? Please, please, please? I saw a picture of a dog finding one, it was massive! We’ll see, love. Depends if we can arrange it. It’s not cheap, you know. And besides, your mother’s got her heart set on that cooking class. Oh, that cooking class! I’m so excited. Apparently, the chef used to work for Gordon Ramsay. Gordon Ramsay, eh? He’s a shouty one. Though you have to admit, he can cook. Still, I prefer Delia Smith, myself. More… relatable. Delia Smith, now there’s a name. Remember when she got onto the pitch during Norwich game? Brilliant. What’s a pitch? It’s like, the football field, love. Where they play football. It's where grown men run around chasing a ball. Honestly, I don’t get the appeal. Though I did take young Master Thompson here to a West Ham game once. Nearly lost my voice. You took him to West Ham? You’re trying to convert him, aren’t you? Trying to turn him into a proper football supporter. Someone needs to. He’s getting far too interested in… American football. All that padding and stopping and starting. It’s hardly a sport! Honestly, Americans. They put cheese in everything. My friend Ethan’s dad went to America. He brought back loads of candy. Speaking of bad habits, have you managed to cut down on the cigarettes, darling? I’m working on it. It’s… a process. It's a process that's been going on for twenty years. It’s stressful work, you know? These management consultants are relentless. Always wanting reports, wanting data… It’s exhausting. Stressful? Try dealing with pregnant women all day. That's stressful. One minute they’re overjoyed, the next they’re terrified.

Honestly, this canteen food is…an experience, isn’t it? I think I’ve identified at least four different shades of beige on my plate. It’s consistent, at least. You always know what you’re getting. And it’s cheap. Which, let’s be real, is the main draw when you’re surviving on a graduate salary. True. Though I’m starting to suspect the ‘chicken’ is actually reformed potato. It has a very…structural integrity. Don’t. Just…don’t. I'm trying to eat it. So, how’s that new campaign going, Ben? The one for the children’s books? It’s… a challenge. We’re trying to target parents on Instagram, but the algorithm seems to hate us. Every time I think I've cracked it, engagement drops off a cliff. It's like they  want  to show people ads for teeth whitening instead of encouraging reading. Instagram is a fickle beast. My nan gets targeted with ads for mobility scooters and dating apps. Simultaneously. Oh, bless her! That’s…a range. I’m wading through transcripts today of people describing their childhood reading experiences. It’s fascinating, actually. The way people remember details, the emotional connection… Sounds a lot more fulfilling than battling algorithms, to be honest. Is it mostly positive memories? Surprisingly, no. A lot of people talk about being  forced  to read certain things, or having books read  to  them in a really monotone voice. Ruined it for life, apparently. My mum used to do really dramatic voices for all the characters. It was amazing. Except she always made the villain sound exactly like our headteacher. That’s brilliant! That’s the kind of detail I’m collecting. It’s all about the nuances. What are you up to these days, Tom? Still swimming in project management? Pretty much. Currently juggling three different deadlines, a temperamental printer, and a request to source seventeen copies of a book that’s been out of print for twenty years. Standard Tuesday, really. seventeen copies? What on earth for? Apparently, a very important academic needs them for…research purposes. He was very insistent. And slightly terrifying. Oh dear. Well, at least it’s interesting? That’s one word for it. It keeps me from falling into an existential crisis, I suppose. This "chicken" is actually pretty okay, you know? Maybe it  is  just chicken. Don't push your luck. You’ll jinx it.

Right, so are we definitely heading straight to Kasia’s then? No detour to that weird pottery place you found online? Oh, honestly, I’m tempted, but no. We’re already running a bit late, aren't we? And Kasia’s been really good about letting us crash, I don't want to push our luck by arriving at, like, midnight. Plus, I vaguely remember reading reviews saying it’s mostly just overpriced tourist tat. Good call. Tourist tat is the enemy. Are you sure you’ve got the address for Kasia’s saved? My phone signal’s being a bit patchy since we crossed the border. Yes, multiple times. Not just in the phone, I’ve scribbled it down on a bit of paper too, just in case. Old-fashioned, I know, but it works. It’s… ul. Świętego Agnieszki 12, Tarnow. Does that ring any bells? Sounds right. I think she mentioned something about it being near the old town square? That's what I gathered. Something about a five-minute walk. Oh, and she said to look for a building with a bright blue door. Apparently, it’s very distinctive. A bright blue door. Excellent. I’ll keep my eyes peeled. Are we relying on Google Maps entirely, or do you have a backup plan, like, an actual paper map? You wound me! Of course, I have a paper map. I’m not  completely  reliant on technology. It’s in the glove compartment, alongside a torch, a first-aid kit, and a questionable selection of biscuits. Questionable biscuits are essential for any road trip, obviously. Just checking, are you comfortable driving on the right? You’ve been doing brilliantly so far, but I know it can take a bit of getting used to. I’m managing. It’s… disconcerting, still. I keep instinctively reaching for the gear stick with my left hand! But I’m mostly staying in my lane and haven’t mounted any pavements yet, so I’m counting that as a win. High praise indeed. Honestly, you're a much braver driver than I am. I’d be a wreck. Oh, don't be silly. You’re a much more confident navigator – you’d have us completely lost in five minutes without you. Besides, someone has to handle the snacks. True. And I take that role very seriously. Right, well, let’s see… according to Google Maps, we’re about twenty minutes away.

Honestly, that Adidas kit they’ve done for Man U this year is… criminal. Just awful. All that red and black, it looks like someone spilled ink all over it. Yeah, it’s a bit much isn’t it? They’ve gone a bit overboard. I think they’re trying too hard to be… edgy. It’s supposed to be classic, isn’t it? Man United. Classic? It looks like a Valentine’s Day disaster zone. Honestly, I’d rather see them in a plain red kit. It’s always felt more  them . It’s all about the sponsorship though, isn’t it? They’ll slap anything on a shirt if someone’s paying enough. Definitely. It's all about the money. Remember when gambling sponsors were  everywhere ? It felt a bit… much. Good they’ve cracked down on that, even if it means more dodgy crypto companies are getting a look-in. Oh, the betting companies were relentless. Every other advert break. Now it's all energy drinks and… well, not crypto hopefully, but something equally dubious. It's a slippery slope. I saw a rumour online about a McDonald’s sponsorship deal for a Premier League team. McDonald’s? Seriously? Imagine the adverts. “Fuel your passion for the beautiful game with a Big Mac!” I know, right? It’d be the ultimate irony. Elite athletes endorsing fast food. Though, let’s be honest, half of them are probably grabbing a McChicken on the way home from training anyway. Probably. It's the convenience. And it’s cheap. Although, honestly, I haven’t been to McDonald’s in… ages. Since we moved down here, actually. There's not one near us and I'm kind of glad. Me neither. It’s a guilty pleasure, isn’t it? Like, you know it’s bad for you, but sometimes you just…  need  those fries. Though, honestly, I’d take a decent chip shop over McDonald’s any day. Oh, absolutely. Proper chips, with salt and vinegar. Nothing beats that. Speaking of which, do you think whoever designs those football kits even  watches  football? I seriously doubt it. They’re probably sat in a boardroom somewhere, arguing about brand synergy and target demographics. They've clearly never been to a match in the rain, trying to stay warm in a flimsy plastic shirt. Exactly! They wouldn't be designing something like that if they did.

Honestly, it’s infuriating. They sent me a letter, said I hadn’t declared earnings. Earnings! From where? I haven't worked a day in… well, you know. It’s just constant hassle with the Jobseekers. Oh, brilliant. Sounds about right. They love doing that, don’t they? Just making life difficult. Are you going to ring them? I did! Spent an hour on hold, then some kid with a really posh voice just kept repeating policy. Couldn’t explain  what  earnings they were talking about. He said “it’s all on the system,” which is just… not helpful. Ugh. Classic. It’s like they deliberately train them not to actually listen. Did you mention you haven't  had  any earnings? Repeatedly! He just kept saying I needed to fill out a form. A form to say I haven’t earned anything. Honestly, it's taking the mickey. Mum said she thinks I should just go down to the office, go face-to-face. That might be worth it. Sometimes actually having someone look you in the eye makes them… less robotic. Though knowing you, you'd probably end up having a proper confrontation. Well, someone needs to tell them it’s ridiculous! I'm barely surviving as it is. Gas and electric are through the roof, you know? Mum and Dad are helping, but… it's not right. Especially when I see what Kevin's done with his inheritance. Oh, don’t even start on Kevin. Last I heard he was “investing” in NFTs. NFTs! The man hasn’t had a real job in his life, suddenly he’s a financier. Spent the whole lot on pictures of monkeys, apparently. And a car. A  sports car . It’s disgusting. Well, it's his money to waste, I suppose. Although, it wouldn’t kill him to help out a bit, would it? Especially considering… Exactly! I keep thinking about getting a George Foreman grill. You know, to save on electricity. Less cooking time. Mum makes a good point though, everything ends up tasting like George Foreman. It does, doesn't it? Everything has a slightly charred flavour. Remember when we were kids and Mum took us on that day trip to Brighton? Honestly, it was chaos. Oh god, Brighton. And you swore you saw a celebrity but it was just someone who looked a bit like Ant from Ant and Dec.

Honestly, the traffic was dreadful getting back from Cambridge yesterday. Absolutely gridlocked on the A1. Sat nav sent me a right detour too, down all these tiny country lanes. Ooh, terrible. I avoid the A1 if I can. Even going into Peterborough it’s bad now, all them new roundabouts haven’t helped, have they? Just make things more confusing. Roundabouts! A menace, the lot of ‘em. Old Mr. Henderson went right into one near Fletton, years ago. Not his fault, mind you, someone pulled right out on him. Gave him such a fright. Oh dear! Was he alright? Shook up, mostly. Car was a write-off though. They didn’t have all these airbags back then, you know. Just a bit of padding, if you were lucky. You’re right, it’s much safer now. Though, you hear about plane crashes, don’t you? Makes you wonder. Don’t even mention it. I saw something on the news about one over… somewhere. Didn’t really pay attention, just switched it off. Too depressing. Speaking of depressing, I tried that new reduced-fat spread… honestly, tasted like water. Oh, they always do, don't they? You’re better off with a bit of proper butter. Honestly, these low-fat things, they’re no good for you at all. All them chemicals. Used to make our own butter, you know. When I was a girl. Got the cream fresh from the farm. Lovely it was. None of this packaged stuff. I can imagine! Right, I’m going to put the kettle on again. Anyone fancy another coffee? And, Maureen, how are you getting on with Mrs. Peterson’s house? Oh, it’s a bit of a state, honestly. She’s got a lot of…stuff. And she keeps trying to tell me how to do my job! “You need to polish this with vinegar, dear,” she says. Vinegar! Oh, bless her. She’s a character, Mrs. Peterson. She used to volunteer at the church, you know. Always had a good heart. Though she does go on a bit. And she keeps getting these little warts on her hands. Nasty things. Oh, that sounds unpleasant. Have you tried any of those over-the-counter remedies, Maureen? I told her about that stuff you get in Boots. She says she’s tried everything. I think she just likes the attention, to be honest. She tells me all her troubles, then complains I don’t stay long enough!

Honestly, Science was  brutal  today. Mr. Davies is trying out this new method of teaching, right? Like, he thinks we all learn best by, I don’t know, building volcanoes out of Play-Doh? No way! Seriously? That sounds… chaotic. Chaotic is an understatement. It was Play-Doh everywhere, and half the volcanoes kept collapsing before we even got to the ‘eruption’ stage. And then he spent twenty minutes explaining the layers of the Earth using different coloured Play-Doh. It was… a lot. Oh my god. Is he one of those trainee teachers they keep foisting on us? I think so. He's really enthusiastic, which is nice, but he clearly hasn’t quite figured out how to control a class of Year 9s. It felt like primary school, honestly. Ugh, tell me about it. We’ve got Mrs. Peterson in English, who’s doing her training. She keeps asking us for feedback on her teaching like we’re qualified to  give  feedback. Exactly! Like, I’m just trying to survive the poetry analysis, I don’t have time to evaluate your lesson plans. Speaking of English, did you finish the Shakespeare essay? Almost. I’m still struggling with the whole ‘iambic pentameter’ thing. It just feels… arbitrary. Like, why does it even matter? I know, right? Miss Jenkins was droning on about it for an hour. I swear she just enjoys hearing herself talk. It's like, yes, it's a specific rhythm, but does it actually enhance the meaning of the play? I’m not convinced. Exactly! Anyway, how did you find Art? I thought the perspective exercise was surprisingly difficult. It was! I spent ages trying to get the lines right, and it still looked wonky. Chloe was, naturally, brilliant at it. She just  gets  art. It’s unfair. She is good. But honestly, I’m just relieved we’re not painting portraits this term. I really struggle with faces. They always end up looking… demonic. Oh god, no. Portraits are the worst. Remember when we had to do self-portraits in Year 7? Mine looked like a potato with eyes. Oh my god, yes! It did! And Liam’s looked like a melted alien. Seriously! And then Mr. Harrison tried to be encouraging and said it was ‘abstract.’ Like, no, it was just bad. Speaking of Liam, have you heard he’s failing Maths? Apparently, he’s completely bombed the last two tests.

Honestly, Leo, you wouldn't  believe  what Mrs. Higgins was saying at playgroup today. She was going on about Scientology. Scientology! Like it's a perfectly normal thing to discuss when you're swapping baby food recipes. Scientology? Seriously? What was she saying about it? Is she… joining? Apparently, a friend of hers is involved. She was talking about auditing and clear levels and… honestly, it sounded like something straight out of a sci-fi film. It reminded me a bit of the Matrix, actually. All that hidden reality stuff. Gah! Goo! Yes, darling, very interesting. Leo, are you learning about different religions at school? Sort of. We did a bit on Christianity and Islam, but nothing… weird. No alien overlords or anything. Well, it's good to be aware, isn't it? It just struck me as so odd. I mean, I went to a Catholic school. Nuns, lots of rules, definitely no talk of space operas. Though, thinking about it, some of the nuns  were  pretty mysterious… always disappearing into the library. Maybe they were secretly auditing each other! Mum! You're terrible. I’m just saying! It's all a bit… controlling, isn't it? I remember Sister Mary Margaret used to glare at you if your skirt was even half an inch too short. It wasn't a fun time. I think my mate, Sam, his dad's a bit into… I don't know what it is, something about nature and ancient stuff. He doesn’t go to church or anything, he just says there's a different kind of power in the world. Paganism, maybe? Or Wicca? There's a lot out there. As long as people aren’t hurting anyone, I suppose, it’s their business. It’s just… Scientology feels different. Feels a bit… predatory. Maybe Mrs. Higgins’ friend is just confused. Maybe. I just hope she doesn’t start trying to 'clear' little Finn here. He’s perfectly clear enough already, covered in spaghetti bolognese! More! More! Right, maybe we should steer the conversation away from cults and back to more pressing matters. Like, can I have dessert? And are you still going to Sarah’s party on Saturday? Dessert, you can definitely have dessert. And yes, I am. Though I might need to convince Mrs. Higgins to stay away. Just in case she tries to audit the birthday cake. Goo! Cake!

Right so just off this roundabout then left at the next one. Sounds good. Are you sure this is the quickest way? Google Maps was suggesting something slightly different. Nah, Google Maps always takes you the scenic route. I know these roads like the back of my hand. Besides, this avoids that awful dual carriageway. Fair enough. You’ve been driving round here for… well, longer than I have. Did you ever end up doing those dancing lessons? The ballroom ones? Oh god, don’t remind me. It was… an experience. Mainly of embarrassment. Apparently, I have no rhythm. Absolutely none. The instructor was very polite, but I could see the pity in her eyes. No way! You? I always thought you’d be quite good at that sort of thing. Apparently, coordinating my limbs to music is beyond me. It was like watching a newborn giraffe trying to walk. I lasted three sessions. Refunded, thankfully. Haha! That’s brilliant. Still, good on you for trying. It’s better than just… watching telly, I suppose. Speaking of which, have you seen that new drama on BBC One? ‘The Crimson Coast’? Uh, vaguely. Is it the one with that bloke who used to be in ‘Heartbeat’? The oldish one. That's the one! It's surprisingly good. Bit slow-paced, but the acting is solid. It's weird seeing him playing a villain, though. He always seemed so… wholesome. There's a lot of Old English in it as well, which is fascinating. Old English? Like, Shakespearean stuff? Not quite that far back, but definitely a lot of archaic phrasing. It’s making me think about that module I did at uni – historical linguistics. Remember all those convoluted grammatical rules? Ugh, don’t. That module nearly broke me. It was fascinating, but so… dense. I much preferred the practical stuff, like the corpus linguistics. That was genuinely interesting. Yeah, you were always really good at that. I always admired your ability to sort of… find patterns in the chaos. I felt like I was just staring at endless lines of text. It's something. Oh, look, there’s Sarah’s house! She’s raising money for that animal shelter again, isn’t she? She is, bless her. Absolutely bonkers about animals. I swear she'd rescue a particularly dusty moth if it looked sad enough. She would! She's a good egg.

Honestly though, this scenery is just… breathtaking, isn’t it? Look at those olive groves. It’s a world away from Bolton. Can we put some music on? I'm bored. Just a minute, Liam. Let your Dad concentrate on the driving, alright? These roads are a bit… interesting. Interesting is one word for it. Narrow is another. And windy. I swear this car’s getting smaller with every corner. Oh, don’t be dramatic, Harold. It’s a perfectly good car. Though, I do miss a bit of space. Remember that caravan we had? We could have just packed up everything and brought it with us. Mum! We talked about this. The caravan stayed in storage. For good reason. It was like living in a mobile biscuit tin. Was it comfy? It had its moments, love. Though, Center Parcs is much more my speed these days. No pitching tents, no dodgy electric hook-ups. Just… relaxation. Relaxation involving a ten-hour drive to get there, usually. Still, it's a step up from camping. Remember that disaster in the Lake District? Oh god, don’t even. The midges. I’m still traumatised. Right, music, Liam? What are we listening to? Something with a beat. Like… that thing I showed you, with the bikers? Sons of Anarchy? Really? At ten o'clock in the morning? It's good! They have cool bikes and… stuff. Honestly, that show. All that brooding and leather. Give me something a bit more cheerful. Have you seen what the market’s like in Rovinj? Apparently, it's amazing. We should definitely go. Rovinj is on the list. We need to find somewhere good to eat tonight, though. I saw a place online that specialises in truffle pasta. Truffle pasta sounds amazing! Though, I'm also keen to try some proper Croatian seafood. And all the olive oil. I want to bring loads back. You can buy some lovely local olive oil at the markets, darling. And wine. Don't forget the wine. Istria is famous for its wine. I’ve read they have some fantastic Malvasia. I’ll have to look out for that. Maybe we could do a wine tasting? I've seen a couple of vineyards advertised on that website. Can we go to Pula? I saw a picture of the Roman amphitheatre, it looked awesome. Yes, Pula is a must-see. We can go tomorrow.

Right so then Liam was proper going off on one about it wasn’t he? Like, full on ranting. Oh god, yeah. He gets like that when he’s had a couple. It’s just… exhausting. Honestly. What was he even going on about this time? Something to do with the flat, right? Nah, it started with the TikTok. Someone sent him a video and he saw it and just went mental. Oh, the one with… you know. That was awful. I actually blocked the person who sent it. Good shout. Honestly, some people. I don't get it. Like, why would you even send that to anyone? It was… detailed. Detailed is… a polite way of putting it. It was… graphic. And then he was trying to explain the  logistics  of it all to us? Absolutely not something I needed a lecture on while trying to have a quiet night in. He was saying he could probably… you know…  do  it. And that’s when I switched off. Oh, please no. I can’t even. He was talking about recording it too! Recording it?! What?! No way. That’s… that’s just… illegal isn’t it? And horrifying. He said it was ‘for science’ or something. Honestly, he’s lost it. Truly lost it. He's always been a bit weird but that was a new level of weird. Remember when he tried to convince us all to play that game where you had to… um… describe your ideal… situation? Oh my god. Don’t remind me. I pretended I didn’t understand the rules and just started talking about pastries. I just said I was going to the toilet and didn’t come back for like, half an hour. Smart move. I think I mumbled something about needing to call my grandma and then just stared at my phone. He didn't even notice. He honestly just doesn’t read the room, does he? He thinks he's hilarious but it just makes everyone uncomfortable. He's got that… oblivious energy. Bless him, but also, please stop talking about…  that . It's just… the thought of anyone actually  enjoying  that kind of thing… It’s just a bit much for me to process. Me too. I think I need another drink. Anyone else? Or should we change the subject drastically before Liam starts explaining the physics of it all?

Right, I’m needing something substantial. That Pret sandwich barely touched the sides. Honestly, felt like I was chewing air. Tell me about it. I went for the soup and a roll. Soup was lukewarm and the roll… well, it was a roll. Just a very beige, sad roll. Beige is a good word for it, yeah. Everything in those places feels… engineered to be as bland as humanly possible. It’s a conspiracy, I’m telling you. Keeps us all docile and compliant. Docile and compliant and probably slightly malnourished. I'm thinking a proper chippy tea is in order tonight. Cod and chips, mushy peas, the works. Oh, YES. That sounds amazing. Though I’m trying to be good, you know? Operation ‘Fit for Summer’ is officially underway. ‘Fit for Summer’? It’s nearly October, love. I know, I know. It’s aspirational. Plus, Christmas is looming. Need to get a head start on saving face. Saving face from the Quality Street tin, more like. Speaking of which, anyone else remember when they used to have the coconut segment in those? Best bit by a mile. Oh God, yes! Discontinued it, they did. Criminal. They replaced it with… what was it? Another toffee one? Utter betrayal. They’re always messing with the Quality Street line-up. It’s a national scandal. I swear, a petition needs starting. I'd sign that. Anyway, back to the chippy. There's that place near MediaCity, the one with the really generous portion sizes… Oh, ‘Fryer’s Delight’? Yeah, they’re not shy with the oil, that's for sure. Good stuff though. Proper chips, not those skinny fries pretending to be chips. I'm craving a parmo now though. Seriously. A good parmo with garlic mayo and chips… That's a whole other level of commitment, that is. That's a weekend meal right there. You’re right. That requires planning. That’s Teesside territory, though, isn’t it? Proper parmos come from up north. True, true. Though I had a decent one in Stockport once. Don’t tell anyone, it'll ruin my credibility. Your credibility is safe with us. As long as you admit it wasn’t  quite  the same. Never the same. Look, let's just stick to the chips for tonight, eh? Less controversial. More achievable. Agreement. Chips it is. Now, back to battling these spreadsheets... and dreaming of beige-free sustenance.

Right, so I was explaining to me mam about TikTok the other day. Honestly, it was like trying to explain quantum physics to a goldfish. Oh, bless her. My dad thinks Facebook  is  the internet. He keeps asking me to print out his Facebook page so he can “properly read it”. Oh, that’s good. We get a lot of that at the library. People wanting printed copies of websites. It’s a generational thing, isn’t it? I mean, I still feel a bit lost with some of the newer platforms. Snapchat? Still haven’t cracked that one. Snapchat is just… disappearing photos. That’s it. Honestly. It's the digital equivalent of writing a message in smoke. Sounds terrifying. I tried getting my niece into Instagram for her art, but all she wants to do is look at videos of cats. Which, fair enough, to be honest. But not exactly showcasing her portfolio. Cats rule the internet, it’s a well-known fact. I follow a few library-related accounts on Twitter, mostly for professional development. So many librarians sharing innovative ways to use social media to engage patrons. See, that’s where I struggle. Engaging patrons. It feels... contrived, doesn't it? Like we’re chasing after them on platforms they might not even be using. I think it’s about meeting them where they are, isn’t it? If people are getting their news from TikTok, maybe we need to consider how we can present library information in a TikTok-friendly format. Short, snappy, visually appealing… Exactly! And it’s not just about promoting services. It’s about building a community. We’ve started a book club group on Facebook, and it’s been surprisingly popular. People are sharing recommendations and having discussions. It's lovely to see. That’s actually a good idea. We could do something similar with local history resources. Salford’s got a rich history, loads of interesting stories. Could do a "This Day in Salford History" thing on Twitter, maybe? Ooh, I like that! And you could include old photos from the local archives. People love a bit of nostalgia. Definitely. Visual content is key. And maybe a bit of humour. I saw a library in America doing a series of posts comparing books to different types of coffee. Apparently, it went viral. Books and coffee? Seriously? Hey, don’t knock it till you try it!

Right, so we’ve got the broad strokes of the business case down, haven’t we? The projected patient numbers, the catchment area… it all seems fairly robust. It's just… what do we  do  with the tape? The tape? You mean the demographic data on the maps? Yes! The coloured tape showing patient flow, potential referrals… it looks a bit… chaotic, doesn’t it? Like a toddler’s had a go with a roll of sticky-back plastic. Right. We need to present it tidily. Let’s digitise that, shall we? Get young Emily in IT to overlay it onto the GIS mapping system. That’ll give us a cleaner, more professional look. I’ll brief her this afternoon. Good idea. That’s much better. And have we finalised the consultation process? I’m still slightly worried about potential pushback from the existing hospitals. I’ve spoken to Dr. Sharma at the Kent and Sussex Hospital. He’s… cautiously supportive. Said he’d like to see the full business case, of course, but understands the need for additional end-of-life care facilities in this area. The key is to emphasise we’re  complementary , not competitive. We’re taking the pressure off acute services, providing a more holistic approach. Absolutely. And what about the rationale for Tunbridge Wells specifically? I know there were discussions about Sevenoaks… Sevenoaks had limited space and higher property costs. Tunbridge Wells offers a good balance. Accessible transport links, a relatively affluent population – meaning a stronger base for fundraising – and, frankly, a derelict site that an estate agent practically begged us to take off their hands. Which brings me to… have you had a look at the initial design concepts? Briefly. It looked… modern. A little  too  modern for a hospice, perhaps? I was imagining something a bit more… calming. Less glass and steel, more… Cotswold stone. Cotswold stone in Tunbridge Wells? Bit of a visual clash, don’t you think? No, seriously though, the architects are aiming for a ‘hotel’ feel. Comfortable, welcoming, not clinical. Plenty of natural light, gardens… We want to feel less like a hospital and more like a home. Though, of course, with all the necessary medical facilities. That’s fair. It’s just… the whole organisation of local health services feels so fragmented. Getting buy-in from all the different bodies – the CCG, the local council, the community nurses… it’s a nightmare.

Oh, look at this one! That’s us at Sarah’s wedding. God, wasn’t that a scorcher? I nearly melted in that dress. You looked lovely, though. Absolutely lovely. Remember old Mr. Henderson trying to do the Macarena? Nearly took out the cake table. I vaguely remember that story. Mum’s told it about a million times. Are we having pasta tonight? It smells amazing in here. Yep, pasta with that pesto sauce you like. Though, I’m honestly thinking about Royal Ascot next week. Have you booked tickets, darling? Not yet. Been meaning to. It’s just…it’s always so expensive, isn’t it? And all that fuss. It looks incredible online. All the hats! You look amazing in hats, Mum. Oh, you say that just to be nice. Though, I  do  have a new one. Pale blue with feathers. Think it’ll go with this dress I’ve got. Always the stylish one, you are. Speaking of stylish, has Chloe heard back about that job interview yet? She had a second one yesterday! Fingers crossed. It’s with that marketing agency in London, the one she was really excited about. She was a bit stressed about it, though. Said the panel was…intense. Oh, bless her. Intense panels are the worst. Remember when I interviewed for the ward manager position? They basically grilled me for an hour. You handled it brilliantly, though. You always do. You’re a natural leader, you are. She’s really good at her job, honestly. One of her colleagues sent her a really lovely message today saying how much they appreciate her work. She's so creative. That’s lovely to hear. She gets that from your side of the family. All that artistic flair. Speaking of which, have you seen that new phone case I got? It’s rose gold. Rose gold? Very you. Is it one of those fancy ones with the little card holder? The very same! Utterly practical. I no longer have to worry about carrying a purse. It’s a game changer. Very millennial of you, Mum! Using your phone as a wallet. Don't you start! Oh, look at your Granddad in this one. He was such a character. Always telling stories about his time in the Navy. He was a good man. Miss him, I do. He always had a mischievous twinkle in his eye.

Right, so we are definitely watching ‘The Descent’ tonight aren’t we? I’ve already got the snacks sorted. Oh god, are we? I don’t know if I’m brave enough for ‘The Descent’ again. Remember last time I literally had to hide behind a cushion for, like, half of it? Yeah, but that’s the  point ! It's properly terrifying. The claustrophobia is just… chef’s kiss. And the creatures! They’re genuinely unsettling. Unsettling is an understatement! They’re horrifying! It’s less scary film and more psychological torture, isn’t it? Just thinking about being stuck in those caves… makes my skin crawl. Exactly! It's brilliant. You know it's not just jump scares, it builds and builds. It's the atmosphere. Have you seen ‘Hereditary’? Oh,  please  don't even mention ‘Hereditary’. That film genuinely messed me up for a week. I kept seeing things out of the corner of my eye. I had nightmares. I’m still not convinced my mum isn’t possessed. Oh, stop it! Okay, okay, maybe ‘Hereditary’ was a bit much. But ‘The Descent’ is different. It’s action-packed, it’s intense, but it's…contained, isn't it? Like, you know it's in a cave, it’s a specific threat. That doesn't make it less scary! It makes it  more  terrifying knowing they're completely isolated. And what about ‘The Witch’? That one gave me the creeps. The goat… that goat was evil. Oh, the goat was unsettling, yeah. But it was the whole vibe of ‘The Witch’ that was off. That whole Puritan family just…wrong. But honestly, nothing beats the sheer panic in 'The Descent' when they realise they're not alone. Ugh, don’t remind me. The screaming… I can practically hear it now. I’m going to need a massive blanket fort and a hot water bottle. And possibly a therapist on standby. You'll be fine! I'll sit next to you and hold your hand if you need me to. But you can't chicken out! It's a classic! Fine. But if I start crying, you're making the tea. And you're definitely not allowed to pause it at any jump scare just to wind me up. Deal. Although… I can't promise anything about the jump scares. It's just a reflex. You're awful. Fine. Let's just get it over with.

Right, well I’m just going to put the kettle on, do you fancy a chamomile before bed? Oh, that’d be lovely, dear. Chamomile’s always a good idea. Though honestly, I can’t seem to get to sleep these days, no matter what I drink. My head just… goes. Still worrying about Beatrice, is it? A little. She sent another of those emails, didn’t she? All emojis and exclamation marks. Honestly, I can barely decipher them. You young people and your texting. It’s not just young people, Grandad! Mum does it too. It’s just… how people communicate now. Hmph. She was asking if I’d considered listing that old armchair on eBay. Said she found a website that does it all for you. Oh, that’s a good idea actually. It is taking up a lot of space in the spare room. And you never use it anymore. It was your grandmother’s, you know. Real leather, that was. Had it re-upholstered after the war, believe it or not. Times were different then. You didn't just… buy things online. I know, I know. Still, it's just sitting there gathering dust. Maybe someone could give it a good home. Have you had a look at Airbnb again? Still thinking about renting the annex? I did, earlier. Had a few inquiries. Mostly young couples wanting a weekend getaway. Though one wanted to know if we delivered pizza to the annex. Pizza! As if. Oh, Grandad. That’s brilliant. It’s the world gone mad, I tell you. Everything’s instant these days. Don’t have the patience for it. I saw young Thomas fiddling with one of those… iPads, was it? Trying to show me a photograph of his new car. Couldn't make head nor tail of it. They are a bit complicated. I try to help Mum with hers, and she just gets frustrated. It’s all too much. I remember when a telephone was a brick on the wall and you had to  dial  the numbers. Now they’re tiny little things you carry in your pocket. It’s progress, Grandad. Progress, maybe. But is it for the better? Still, chamomile tea sounds nice. What time are you heading up to bed? Once I’ve finished tidying up down here, probably around ten? I’ve got a parents’ evening tomorrow. Always stressful.

Aye, it was a proper haul, wasn’t it? Three quid a book. Three quid! Old man Hemmings was practically giving them away. Though, to be fair, half of them smelled like his dog. Old Hemmings. He  did  love that terrier. Probably used the books as chew toys when nobody was looking. Still, a bargain is a bargain. Did you find anything good amidst the…aroma? Oh, aye. A first edition of “Kidnapped,” surprisingly intact. And a collection of travel writing from the early 20th century. Some chap wandering around Persia and Mesopotamia. Proper adventurous stuff. Makes my commute on the 88 bus seem a bit tame, eh? A bit. Though, navigating Princes Street at rush hour  is  a kind of adventure, I suppose. I mostly went for the poetry section. Picked up a battered copy of MacDiarmid's “First Hymn to Lenin.” Been meaning to reread it. Good man. Always good to revisit the big names. I tried getting into MacDiarmid years ago, but it felt a bit dense, even for me. I'm more of a Robert Burns man, myself. Straightforward and a wee bit bawdy. Perfect. He’s a classic, no argument there. Though MacDiarmid rewards a bit of effort. It's like climbing Arthur's Seat. Gruelling at first, but the view from the top…worth it. Speaking of views, are you still planning that trip to Patagonia? Aye, planning it. Just trying to figure out the logistics. Apparently, the wind there is something else. I've been reading a lot of Bruce Chatwin, prepping myself mentally. He wandered around Patagonia for years, seemed to thrive in the chaos. Chatwin's brilliant. "In Patagonia" is one of those books you can reread endlessly. Did you ever get to see that exhibition of his photographs at the National Portrait Gallery? No, missed that one unfortunately. Was stuck in a conference in Birmingham. Awful. Endless Powerpoint presentations about “synergy” and “brand awareness.” Give me a windswept Patagonian steppe any day. Tell me about it. That’s why I try to get away as often as possible. Though, last time I tried to escape to the Highlands, I ended up stranded in a Bothy during a blizzard. Not quite the romantic getaway I was hoping for. Stranded in a Bothy? You? The Director of Studies, reduced to huddled in a stone hut, battling the elements? That’s a story! You must tell me all about it later.

So, I sent off the application for the Bartlett scholarship. Oh, lovely! That’s brilliant, darling. Did it take ages? You were working on it for weeks, weren’t you? It did, yeah. The portfolio was a nightmare. So much rendering, and then writing the statement… Ugh. I think I rewrote that thing about five times. Well, you’re a perfectionist, sweetheart. That’s why you’re so good at what you do. But don’t exhaust yourself over it. It’s good you’ve  done  it, that’s the main thing. I know, I know. It’s just… it's a long shot, isn’t it? The Bartlett is ridiculously competitive. Everything worthwhile is competitive, love. Remember when you applied for uni? Everyone said the same thing then. And look at you now – a qualified architect, doing amazing things. That was different. I was just applying to universities. This is… another level. It’s a fully funded Masters, plus mentoring. It would be incredible for my research. It sounds fantastic. What about this new job at Lewis & Stone? How’s that going? It’s… fine. It's good experience, definitely. But it's not really  challenging  me, you know? A lot of it is just tweaking drawings for housing estates. Which is useful, absolutely, but not what I want to be doing long-term. That’s fair enough. You always have had your sights set higher. Are they giving you much responsibility? Some. I got to present a scheme to the client last week, which was good practice. But most of the creative stuff is still being done by the senior architects. I feel a bit… stuck in the middle. Well, it’s early days. You’ve only been there a few months, haven’t you? Give it time. Though honestly, if it’s really not fulfilling, don't stay out of loyalty. You need to be doing something you love. I’m trying not to. I'm just worried about finding something better. The market’s a bit shaky, isn’t it? Lots of redundancies. It is, but good architects are always in demand. You’re brilliant, you’ve got a fantastic portfolio, and you're incredibly driven. Someone will snap you up. Maybe this scholarship will be the ticket. Maybe. I keep checking my email, though. It says they'll notify applicants by the end of the month, which feels like a lifetime away.

So, how are things going with young Thomas, then? Still driving that old banger of his? Oh, that car. It’s a miracle it still runs, frankly. He says he’s saving for something new, but knowing Thomas… that could be another five years. Says it’s got ‘character’. Character, I tell you! More like a death trap. Oh, boys and their cars. It’s always the same. My David used to say the same about his Morris Minor. Said it was a classic. It spent more time in the garage than on the road! Aye, well, it’s a different world now, isn’t it? Not like when we were young. You could fix anything with a bit of string and some elbow grease. Now everything’s all computers and sensors. You need a degree just to change a lightbulb. Precisely! And the prices! Fifty quid for an oil change? Robbery, I call it. Back in my day, you could get a full service for a fiver. Don't even get me started on the housing situation. Have you seen the prices of bungalows these days? Absolutely ridiculous! How are young families supposed to get on the ladder? It’s a disgrace. It is. They're building all these fancy flats, all glass and steel. Who wants to live in a glass box, eh? Give me a proper brick house any day. And affordable! That’s the key, affordable. They should build more council houses, like they used to. Good quality, well-maintained. That’s what’s needed. It's all about profit these days, isn't it?
