They don’t care about people just having a decent home. And the politics… honestly, it’s a shambles. One mess after another. Don't I know it. They promise you the world and deliver absolutely nothing. Just hot air and broken promises. I remember when… well, doesn't matter now, does it. Point is, they're all the same. They are, aren’t they? I liked old Harold Wilson, though. He seemed a decent sort. Had a no-nonsense approach. Oh, Harold Wilson. I remember him well. A bit of a rogue, if you ask me, always with a twinkle in his eye. But he seemed to have a genuine concern for ordinary folk. Actually, talking of ordinary folk, have you heard from Sarah lately? She hasn’t been on the phone for a couple of weeks now.

Right, so I was chatting with Old Man Hemmings from the community garden again. He's really keen on us using the back room for some sort of seed swap thing. Apparently, it’s massively popular in Peckham. A seed swap? In  that  room? It's a bit…damp, isn't it? And full of, well, everything. It’s basically our storage for anything we don’t know what to do with. Exactly my point! I tried to gently steer him towards the smaller meeting room, but he was adamant. Said it needed to be a 'big, communal space' and the smaller one 'didn’t have the right energy'. Honestly, you’d think I was negotiating a peace treaty. The energy, right. Sounds… challenging. Have we actually cleared out that room since the Christmas decorations came down? I'm pretty sure there's still tinsel lurking somewhere. Lurking is an understatement. It’s a tinsel  habitat  back there now. Look, the thing is, if we  can  get it sorted, it’s free activity space, brings in footfall, and maybe even encourages donations. It's all about generating income, isn’t it? It is, definitely. But it needs work. Serious work. We'd need to get rid of half the stuff in there. And potentially dehumidify the entire room. Remember the mould issue last spring? Don't remind me. The whole office smelled like a wet dog for a week. Okay, okay, point taken. It’s a project. Maybe we can rope in some of the volunteers? I spoke to Sarah, she's got a weekend free next month. She’s pretty good with organisation. That’s a good shout. And maybe we need to revisit the furniture situation. That room’s currently furnished with a broken photocopier, three mismatched chairs, and a pile of old directories. You're not wrong. I was looking at some second-hand office furniture online yesterday – surprisingly affordable. We could get some decent foldable tables and chairs for a reasonable price. I’ll send you the link. Perfect. Actually, speaking of furniture, old Mrs. Patel from the pottery class was complaining again about the lack of storage space in her room. Apparently, she's tripping over clay all the time. Honestly! She’s been saying that for months. I keep telling her we're looking into it, but…well, funding. It always comes down to funding.

Honestly, this is incredible, Rhys. This roast chicken is… phenomenal. Seriously. Glad you think so. Bit of a secret marinade, that. My nan’s recipe, tweaked a little. She’d kill me for saying tweaked, though. “Don’t you  dare  change a thing!” It  is  good, even I’ll admit that. And coming from a Welshman, that's high praise. Usually, it’s lamb or nothing, right? He’s a stubborn one, your Huw. Though I have to say, Yorkshire puddings are acceptable on all fronts. A good Yorkshire pudding transcends national boundaries. Oh, absolutely. Though a side of gravy is non-negotiable. Always. Gravy is basically a food group in itself. Don't argue with me on this. Right? And you've got the roast potatoes  perfectly  crispy. How did you even manage that? Mine always end up either pale and sad or burnt to a crisp. Parboiling, my friend. And goose fat. Goose fat is the answer to all life’s problems, really. Goose fat, eh? Sounds fancy. I usually just chuck them in olive oil and hope for the best. Olive oil is fine, but goose fat…it's a different league. Adds a richness. Remember that time, Gareth, you tried to deep fry potatoes in sunflower oil? The kitchen smelled like a chip shop for a week. Don’t remind me. That was a disaster. The oil splattered  everywhere . My mum was furious. Said I’d turned the kitchen into a health hazard. Rightly so. Grease fires are no joke. Speaking of disasters, I once tried to make a soufflé. It collapsed faster than my self-esteem after marking a pile of year 11 essays. Oh, the soufflé struggle is real. They're the culinary equivalent of a fragile ego. I attempted a Christmas pudding from scratch once. It was…dense. Like a brick. You could have used it to build a small extension on the house. You're all hopeless! Though I appreciate the entertainment value. I’m sticking to shepherd's pie, thank you very much. Can’t go wrong with a classic. Agreed. Shepherd's pie is the ultimate comfort food. Though, Rhys, you  could  probably elevate a shepherd's pie to Michelin star level with a bit of your magic touch. Don't be silly. Shepherd’s pie is perfection as it is. Although…a little goose fat wouldn't hurt. To goose fat, spectacular roast chickens, and the joy of not having to cook for ourselves for a week!

And then she was like “Oh you’re from Sunderland?” as if it was a… a  disease . Oh, come on! That’s harsh. I know, right? Like, it's a city. People live there! It’s not… leprosy. Well, some people have very narrow worldviews, don't they? Especially down south. They think anything north of Watford is wilderness. Exactly! And she was going on about how amazing London is. I’m like, “Yeah, it’s really expensive and overcrowded, congratulations.” See, I do quite like London, but only for like… a long weekend. I couldn't  live  there. Too much hassle. Remember when we went with Liam and Chloe? Oh god, yeah. Liam nearly had a breakdown on the Tube. He was convinced he was going to get pickpocketed. He was clutching his backpack like it was the crown jewels! And Chloe was trying to navigate with a paper map. A  paper map  in London! Oh Chloe. Bless her. She's technologically challenged, that one. Speaking of which, have you seen that new advert for the car? The one with the… singing badgers? Oh, please don’t tell me you've been subjected to that monstrosity. It’s everywhere! It’s on every commercial break. It's actively reducing my brain cells. I missed it thankfully. I have been trying to avoid all adverts, honestly. They’re all just… relentless. Remember that one for the sofa that just kept repeating “Comfort. Comfort. Comfort.”? Oh my god, yes! It was hypnotic! I nearly bought a sofa I didn’t need just to make it stop. It’s psychological warfare, I tell you. Right, so are we still up for trying that new Italian place on Friday? Marco said the pasta is amazing. Yeah, definitely. I’m starving just thinking about it. Although, my mam keeps trying to get me to make her shepherd’s pie. Oh no. The shepherd’s pie obligation. It’s a never-ending cycle. Every time I visit, it's “Have you made me a shepherd’s pie yet?” I’m a corpus administrator, not a culinary slave! You should start charging her. “Shepherd’s pie, five pounds a portion.” I should! Although she’d probably just give me a lecture about respecting my elders. You know what else is terrible? That new series everyone’s raving about. ‘Celestial Echoes’ or whatever it’s called. Oh, I started that!

Honestly, the hospital… it’s just a conveyor belt, isn’t it? In, examined, out. Barely a word said. I felt like a number, not a person. Oh, you’re telling me. They’re all the same. I was with my sister last week, she’s having all sorts of tests done, and it was the same for her. Just rushed, rushed, rushed. You’d think they’d have a bit more time, you know? Especially with things like… well, with everything. It's just…it feels so impersonal. And then you’re left to process everything yourself. The consultant just said “we need to scan again in six months” and walked out. Six months! Like I haven’t got a life to live in the meantime, worrying. Exactly! You need someone to actually  talk  to. My aunt Millie… she passed last month. It was quick, really. Fell and broke her hip, then just… went downhill. But the whole thing, from the ambulance to the… well, you know. It’s just relentless. Oh, I’m so sorry to hear that, Brenda. Millie was such a lovely woman. I remember her always having a biscuit for the children when they were little. She did, didn’t she? Always a little treat. Trying to sort the funeral now is a nightmare. My cousin Susan is being… difficult. Insisting on a full military send-off. Millie didn’t even  like  the army! She wanted something small and simple. Oh dear. Susan always was a bit… dramatic. I suppose it’s just her way of grieving. Though it doesn’t make it any easier, does it? No, not at all. And my brother, David, he’s completely shut down. Won’t talk about her, won’t look at photos. Just sits there staring at the telly. It’s awful to watch. He was so close to her. Men are funny like that, aren’t they? Bottle everything up. My own husband… when his father died, he just went silent for weeks. It was like he’d built a wall around himself. It's heartbreaking. Speaking of heartbreak… have you seen Carol next door? She’s put on a bit, hasn't she? Oh, um, yes, I have. She said she’s been comfort eating. Losing her husband… it's taken a toll. But honestly, she was always on some diet or another before. One week it’s Keto, the next it’s the 5:2.

Honestly though, that was a really lovely dinner. That lemon and herb chicken was perfect. And you managed to get the potatoes  exactly  how I like them. Thanks, Mum. I helped with the potatoes, you know. You did indeed. Good work, Ethan. Though, if I’m being honest, I was mostly supervising. It’s a delicate operation, getting potatoes right. They were pretty good. Ms. Davies said I made a decent lasagne in Food Tech, but it wasn’t  this  good. Oh? That’s nice to hear, Leo. Lasagne’s a bit fiddly though, isn’t it? So much layering. How are you finding Food Tech in general? It's alright. A bit messy. Mr. Henderson nearly had a heart attack when Finn accidentally set off the fire alarm trying to toast marshmallows. Oh my god, Finn! Classic Finn. He just doesn't think things through. Speaking of thinking things through, has anyone heard anything about work experience placements yet? The deadline was last week, wasn't it? Not yet. Miss Lewis said she’d start letting us know this week. I really want to get something to do with cars. Maybe a garage, or even a dealership. That’s good, Ethan. That sounds sensible. You’ve always been good with mechanics. Remember that time you completely took apart and rebuilt your scooter? Yeah, well, my dad helped a bit. And it didn't  quite  go back together the same way… it made a funny rattling noise for weeks. Still, impressive initiative. I’m hoping to get something lined up for Leo at the office. A bit of admin, maybe some shadowing with the IT team. Good for building skills. I dunno. Admin sounds… boring. It’s good experience, Leo. You learn how things work. It's good to be versatile. Though, on the subject of skills… I was thinking about that ski trip we talked about. Are you still planning on going, David? Absolutely. Booked the chalet last month. It's a little higher up than last time, so hopefully better snow. Though, I'm a bit worried about my knees, to be honest. Getting too old for all that. Nonsense! You'll be fine. Just take it easy on the black runs. I was thinking of maybe trying a hot wine evening aprés ski. Hot wine? Sounds… interesting. Do you put marshmallows in it? You can do! It's called Glühwein.

Oh my god, look at this. This is from Kyoto, isn’t it? We look  so  young. And ridiculously overdressed for Japan. We did, didn’t we? I thought we had to look…respectful. Proper tourists. Honestly, that floral shirt, you look like you're about to host a Hawaiian luau. Hey! It was a nice shirt! And it was breathable. It was sweltering. Remember how humid it was? I remember being permanently damp. And the sheer number of vending machines. One on every corner. Selling everything. Everything! Hot corn soup, that weird fizzy melon soda... And remember that tiny ramen place, tucked away in a side street? Best ramen I’ve  ever  had. Oh, absolutely. We nearly didn’t find it, did we? We walked past it three times. It only had, like, six seats. And the owner didn't speak a word of English. Thankfully, pointing works wonders. Speaking of photos, did you ever get around to editing those badger pictures you took last month? Oh, the badgers! Yes! I did. They're…surprisingly difficult to photograph. So much black and white, it’s hard to get good contrast. They’re elusive little blighters, aren't they? I saw one crossing the road the other day and nearly swerved into a hedge. Oh no! Were you alright? And the badger? Yeah, all good. It was quick, fortunately. Just a flash of stripey face. It made me think I really need to invest in a better telephoto lens. You do. Seriously. These badger photos are…serviceable. But they could be spectacular. I've got a couple I’m quite pleased with though, especially this one where he’s sniffing a mushroom. Looks like he’s judging its quality. Oh, that’s brilliant! He  does  look judgmental. Like a tiny, furry food critic. Exactly! I called it 'The Connoisseur'. I think I might submit it to that wildlife photography competition. You should! It’s a winner. I tell you what though, nothing beats those photos from Japan. Just looking at them makes me want to go back. Me too. Maybe next year? If we can save up. And possibly pack slightly less… enthusiastically. No more floral shirts for you, promise? No promises. You never know what adventures await. Is this along the lines of what you were looking for? Would you like me to expand on any part of the conversation or write a different one?

Right so then we got to this beach in County Clare, right? And it was completely deserted. Like, genuinely no one else around. Ooh, nice! Was the water freezing? Absolutely Baltic. But because it was so remote, people were just… at it. Like, full on skinny dipping. No way! Did you join in? No, mate, no. I was on photo duty. Honestly, it was a whole vibe. Very… liberating. Sounds like something straight out of a movie. You Aussies are a bit more… relaxed about that sort of thing, generally. We just assume everyone’s going to be nude on the beach. Is that true? Seriously? Nah, I’m winding you up. Mostly. But yeah, there's a healthy disregard for public decency sometimes. So, did anyone get any good photos? I got some. But I’m not sharing. For legal reasons. Fair enough. Speaking of things you’re not sharing, how's the cafe going? Still battling the early morning rush? It’s… a struggle. Honestly, I think I need to start charging extra for anyone who orders a complicated oat milk latte before 8am. You should! And implement a surcharge for people who ask for the milk to be exactly 62 degrees. Exactly! And then there’s Brenda, the new barista. She snores. Loudly. During her breaks, she just… collapses and snores. No. Way. I’m not kidding. It’s terrifying. Like, a full-blown chainsaw symphony. You need to record that. That’s gold. Seriously. That's better than any zombie apocalypse scenario. Imagine trying to survive a zombie horde  and  Brenda’s snoring. Okay, that's a genuinely scary thought. Though, speaking of zombie apocalypses, I’ve been thinking… my survival plan is solid. I'm heading straight for the supermarkets. Of course you are. You and everyone else. I've thought it through! I need the fortified snacks. You'd last five minutes. You’d be tripping over tins of beans. Have you guys tried that new photo app, ‘Retrospect’? It makes everything look like it's been taken on film. It’s pretty cool. Oh, I saw that! Is it good? I’m always looking for a decent filter. My Instagram needs a makeover. Speaking of making things… I was trying to make my grandma’s kugel the other day. It was a disaster. Kugel? What is that? It’s a Jewish baked pudding.

Honestly, the amount of peanuts I’ve eaten tonight is… concerning. I feel like a squirrel preparing for winter. You  have  been relentlessly attacking that bowl. I swear, you’ve single-handedly reduced their peanut stock. But hey, they're good peanuts. Proper salted ones, not those bland things some pubs try to pass off. They are good. It's a stress coping mechanism, mostly. This data analysis is frying my brain. Speaking of frying brains… have you seen anything about the new  Call of Duty ? Apparently, the campaign is surprisingly good this time? I’ve skimmed a few reviews. A friend of mine is completely hooked. He's been ranting about the graphics and the story all week. I'm trying to finish writing up this chapter on border security so, you know, prioritizing. It's… a lot. Border security? Sounds intense. Is it like, looking at ways to improve things, or highlighting all the things that could go wrong? A bit of both, actually. It's fascinating, but also incredibly bleak. The sheer number of vulnerabilities... it’s terrifying. Makes you think twice about air travel. Oh god, don’t even. I’m already paranoid enough as it is. Thinking about people sneaking things through, or… worse. Though, that does remind me, we need to actually  plan  that Alton Towers trip. You said you were free next month? Yes! Absolutely. It’s been ages since we’ve done anything properly fun. I think my stress levels would plummet significantly after a day of screaming on rollercoasters. Which ones were you thinking of hitting first? Nemesis Inferno is always a good starting point. Definitely Inferno. And then Oblivion, obviously. Though I’m slightly terrified of The Smiler. It looks genuinely evil. More evil than anything border security could throw at us, honestly. It is pretty intense. I think it’s designed specifically to induce panic. Speaking of things that induce panic… did you catch that new horror film, “The Hollow”? People are saying it’s genuinely terrifying. I heard about it! Is it worth seeing in the cinema, or save it for streaming? I’m a bit of a wimp when it comes to horror. I need to be prepared. Like, pre-load on the peanuts, you know? Apparently, the sound design is incredible in the cinema. Really immersive. But be warned – it’s not jump-scare reliant. It’s more… unsettling.

Honestly, the amount of blisters I’ve got… I’m starting to think learning to row was a terrible idea. Oh dear! Really? I thought you were enjoying it. I remember you were so excited about joining the club. I  am  enjoying it, when I’m actually  in  the boat. It’s the getting there, and the post-row recovery that are killing me. My hands are just shredded. I’ve gone through three pairs of gloves already. You need proper rowing gloves, then. Not just any old pair. I’m sure the club can advise. Though it does sound… strenuous. I’m much happier sticking to kayaking. It’s gentler, isn't it? Gentler, yes. Though I nearly capsized last week trying to navigate that little inlet near Clayhithe. A swan decided it didn’t appreciate my presence. Oh, goodness! Swans can be terrifying. You need a good waterproof jacket, too, if you’re going to be doing that regularly. I’ve got a decent one, if you’re looking. It's hardly been worn. Oh, that’s very kind of you, thank you. I think I’m going to have to invest. This one I’ve got is… inadequate, to say the least. I was soaked through to the bone last Tuesday. Honestly, it felt like swimming, only colder. It’s just finding the right one, isn't it? Breathable, but waterproof. It’s a minefield. Speaking of minefields, I finally met my cousin, Brenda’s daughter, last month. You remember Brenda, don't you? From Shipley? Vaguely, yes. The one who moved to Australia? That’s the one. Her daughter, Chloe, came over for a conference. We met for coffee, and honestly, it was like looking in a mirror. Same eyes, same wry smile. It was lovely… and incredibly sad. Sad? Why? Because Brenda died two years ago. Pancreatic cancer. Very quick. Chloe hadn't seen her in ten years, and she was devastated to discover how little I knew about her Australian life. It brought everything flooding back. It's odd, isn't it, how some relationships just… drift. It is. It’s awful. My Aunt Margaret passed away last autumn. She had dementia, and it was a long slow decline. It's just… draining. And then, on top of that, my mum’s not been well. Oh no, what’s happened? They think it might be a mild stroke.

Honestly Dad, it’s just so stressful waiting for results. Everyone’s posting their predicted grades online and it’s making me freak out. Now, now, lass. Don’t you worry yourself sick about it. Predicted grades are just…predictions. They're not set in stone. Remember your grandad, used to say “Predictions are like yer bum, everyone’s got one”. Oh, grandad. Seriously though, what if I don’t get the grades for Manchester? I’ve already planned everything, the halls, the course… You will. You’ve worked hard, haven't you? And Manchester’s a brilliant university, they’ll see that. Still, if,  if  things don’t go to plan, there’s always clearing. It’s not the end of the world. Clearing feels…scary. Like you’re begging for a place. Rubbish. It’s just another route. Think of it like this – a roundabout instead of a straight road. It gets you to the same destination, just a different way. Speaking of routes, are you sure this is the right way to Auntie Brenda’s? My phone battery is dying again. Vodafone are robbing me, honestly. Yeah, I checked on Google Maps. It's this way. And you really need a new phone. You’re always complaining about the battery. I could show you how to turn off location services, that drains it quickly. It's like teaching Grandma about texting though. Oh, don’t even start on your grandma and those emoji’s. She sent me a picture of a monkey covering its eyes the other day. Said she was ‘so embarrassed’ about something. I had no idea what she meant! She’s brilliant. She's started bidding on eBay again. Found some glass water bottles she wanted, apparently. She’s convinced they make water taste better. Your grandma and her fads. Still, they're better than plastic, I suppose. I've got an Amazon delivery coming tomorrow, a new pair of trainers. My old ones are falling apart. Nice! You deserve them. I need some new pens for uni, seriously. I’m going through them like there’s no tomorrow. And highlighters. Loads of highlighters. Have you seen the price of stationery these days? It’s extortionate. Aye, it is. Remember when you were learning Morse code? You used to write out all the dots and dashes with tiny little pens. What was that all about?

Man, this sofa is a lifesaver, honestly. Didn’t realise how much my back was hurting until I actually sat down. Long walk from the station, yeah? Tell me about it. Proper trek. And you wouldn't believe the state of the internet connection at uni lately. It’s like dial-up, seriously. Trying to submit assignments is a nightmare. No way! Still? I thought they’d sorted that out by now. Are your exams finished then? Done and dusted? One more to go, next week. History of Art. Dreadful. Honestly, looking at paintings for three hours…my brain just melts. What about you? All finished? Yeah, wrapped up last week. Feeling…empty, to be honest. Like, what do I even  do  with myself now? It’s weird not having a constant deadline looming. I feel that. It's a strange transition, innit? Makes you realise how much of your life was just structured around uni. So, what’s the plan then? Summer of Netflix and existential dread? Pretty much. Though I was thinking about maybe finally getting around to learning some proper coding. Remember how I kept saying I would? Oh yeah, the whole “become a tech billionaire” phase. That was a good one. You actually bought a course, didn't you? Did! Never touched it. It’s still sitting in my digital library, mocking me. Maybe this is the summer. It wouldn't hurt. You should. Got to have something to show for all those student loans. Speaking of which…you still on for that trip to Japan after exams? Absolutely! Flights are booked, hostels sorted, tentative itinerary… It’s happening! I’m so hyped. Tokyo’s gonna be wild. Have you started looking at stuff to do over there? Just started, yeah. So much to see! I really want to visit the Ghibli Museum, if I can get tickets. Apparently, you need to book them months in advance. Oh yeah, I heard about that. We’ll have to be strategic. We should maybe plan a proper itinerary together, tonight or tomorrow? It'll be good to have a rough blueprint. Definitely. I'm thinking of trying to learn some basic Japanese phrases before we go. Just the polite stuff, you know? "Hello," "thank you," "where's the nearest ramen shop?" Priorities. I'm with you on that one. Ramen is essential. Also, I’ve been meaning to ask, have you tried that new Korean place down Brick Lane?

Honestly, Grandad, you wouldn’t believe the photos Auntie Carol put on Facebook. Of Buckfast Abbey. Every single stained-glass window. Carol always was one for documenting. Though I still say a postcard's more personal. And quicker to read than scrolling through that infernal Facebook. She did send me a link, actually. It looked beautiful. Did you get the fudge from the shop there, Dad? You were saying you wanted some. I did! Lovely stuff. Though almost as rich as those clotted cream scones we had at the café. Goodness me, felt my arteries hardening with every bite! You deserve a treat, Grandad. You’ve earned it. Speaking of treats, have you thought any more about a cruise? Mum and I were saying… Perhaps for his birthday next year? We could look at Mediterranean ones. Somewhere warm. A cruise, eh? Sounds a bit…contained. All that being herded about. I like to wander. Though I suppose it would be nice to not have to pack and unpack every night. Still, I’d need to get my travel insurance sorted. Remember what happened to old Mr. Henderson? Fell on the deck in Malaga… expensive business. We’ll help you sort everything, Grandad. Don’t worry. We can look at comparison sites. Honestly, though, you need a new phone too. You were fumbling with it for ages trying to call Mum last week. It’s perfectly good enough for making calls! Though I did overhear young Thomas talking about ‘apps’ the other day. Sounded like some sort of disease. They’re not a disease, Dad. They’re little programs you can put on your phone. For everything. Maps, games, shopping… You could even video call us! See the grandchildren running around. Video call? Now that  does  sound interesting. Though what would I talk about? Probably just grumble about David Cameron and all that tax-avoiding nonsense. You’d have an audience, Dad. A very receptive one. It’s just…sometimes I worry about you being on your own. Especially with your blood pressure. Remember what Dr. Patel said? Oh, don't start on the medical stuff. I’ve had more ailments than hot dinners. Keeps the doctors in business, I say. Though that time with my gallbladder… that  was a nasty business. Now  that's  a story for another day. We’re just saying, Grandad, maybe a bit more company would be a good thing.

And then the market was just…wall to wall chocolate! Honestly, it was ridiculous. Like, every single stall. You couldn't move for pralines and truffles and weird chocolate sculptures. Sounds like my idea of heaven, that does. Though your mother isn’t a huge chocolate fan, are you, dear? No, not particularly. It’s all a bit too much, isn’t it? Give me a nice bit of fruitcake any day. But the market itself sounded lovely. Was it a proper, old-fashioned one? Oh, yeah! Cobbled streets, colourful awnings, all that jazz. Dad nearly bought a full suit of medieval armour. I did not! I was just admiring it! It was a beautifully crafted piece, and a bargain, if I recall. A bargain at three hundred euros, apparently. Mum quickly steered you away, thankfully. Good thinking. Where would you even  put  it? We could have shipped it home! Think of the conversations it would start. Oh, Dad. Anyway, driving was interesting. That Sat Nav was determined to take us down roads narrower than the car! Oh, those European roads. They weren’t built for modern vehicles, were they? No! And the roundabouts…they're on another level. So many lanes, and everyone just  flies  around them. I was gripping the steering wheel so hard. I told you, I’m a confident driver! I handled those roundabouts like a pro. Though I did misjudge one and ended up going around three times. A pro, right. Mum was screaming, I think. I was muttering under my breath, let me tell you. I used to get so stressed driving in London, but at least I knew where I was going! And trying to pay for things was a whole other adventure. They didn't seem to accept cards anywhere, and I barely had any euros left. They like their cash over there, that’s for sure. Although, I did manage to get a rather nice leather wallet with a card reader built-in. It's quite the gadget. Oh, Dad, always finding a bargain. Speaking of gadgets, have you both seen the new phone I got? It folds! A folding phone? That sounds terribly complicated. Is it worth the money? It's amazing! It’s a bit pricey, but the screen is huge when it's unfolded. You should see it! We need to meet up properly next week so I can show you.

Right, so I’ve chopped all the onions, are you doing the garlic? It's going to smell amazing in here – honestly, this Tuscan bean stew is a winner. Yep, garlic’s done. I’m just trying to decide… do we have enough rosemary? It needs a good hit of rosemary, I think. There’s a sprig in the fridge, I think. Or maybe I used it all on the roast chicken last week? Let me have a quick look… Nope, gone. We’ll have to make do with thyme, then. Still good. Thyme is fine. You know, I was talking to Sarah from work today, and she’s convinced I have a northern accent. A northern accent! Oh, Sarah. She’s always pointing out accents. You barely have an accent at all, honestly. Maybe a  slight  Scottish lilt when you’re excited, but that’s it. She said I said “bath” differently. Apparently, that’s a giveaway. Oh, that’s a classic. You say it properly! It’s the southerners who ruin “bath” with their elongated vowels. Honestly, it’s a crime against linguistics. Speaking of which, did you see Fiona’s post on Facebook? She's changed her profile picture  again . No, I haven’t been on Facebook all day. What’s she done now? Another filtered selfie? Worse. She's photoshopped herself onto the cover of  Vogue . It’s… ambitious. Oh, Fiona. Never change. Right, shall I get the stock cubes? And maybe put some music on? Yes, please. Something mellow. Oh, and I was thinking about getting some lilies for the living room tomorrow. They smell Divine. Although, maybe not  too  fragrant, you know? I don’t want to overwhelm the fireplace smell. Lilies are lovely. And speaking of the fireplace, have you booked someone to come and sweep it? It’s been ages, and it’s getting close to bonfire night. Oh, good point. I completely forgot. I’ll give Old Man Hemmings a call tomorrow. He’s a bit of a character, but he does a good job. Good, good. We don’t want a chimney fire. Right, stock cubes in. What perfume are you wearing tonight? It smells really nice. Oh, it’s that one my sister got me from France. The violet one? It’s a bit… sophisticated, I think. Not my usual floral. It suits you. Very… Parisian. Now, let's get this stew bubbling, shall we?

So you were in Queensland, were you? That’s… a long way to go for a bit of sunshine. A bit more than a bit, actually. Lived there for three years. Wonderful place, really. Though the flies… the flies were something else. You wouldn’t believe it. Swarms of ‘em. Flies are everywhere, aren’t they? Even here, you get them on a warm day. Though nothing like Queensland, I imagine. I’ve only ever been to New South Wales, Sydney mostly. Business trips. I've never been to Australia at all. Always seemed… expensive. And a very long flight. Though I did have a student once, from Brisbane. Lovely girl. She said the heat was just unbelievable. It is. Relentless. You get used to it, of course. But it’s a different kind of heat. Much drier. I was working out there, setting up a regional office for a firm. Dealing with… well, let’s just say Australian businessmen are a different breed. Oh? How so? Very direct. Very… robust. They favoured short-sleeved shirts and shorts even in meetings! I had to adjust my wardrobe. Suits felt… ridiculous. And they weren’t shy about negotiating, let me tell you. They drove a hard bargain. Always wanted the best deal. Sounds a bit different from… well, from Bristol, anyway. More reserved, we are. Although, perhaps not as reserved as people think! We have our moments. I have to say, I've always found Southerners a bit… vague. Not deliberately, just... less to the point. I'm from Sheffield, you see. We’re fairly direct there. Ah, Sheffield! Now, I've heard tales about the Sheffield dialect. Apparently, it’s almost a language unto itself? Oh, it is! It really is. People from outside Yorkshire struggle with it, particularly the pace. We tend to talk very quickly, and drop a lot of consonants. “Ey up,” is fairly standard greeting. And “tha” instead of “you.” "Tha"? Like "that" without the "t"? Precisely. And “ow do ya do?” becomes “oo’s doin’?” It becomes quite a challenge for anyone not used to it. I taught a class of international students once, and I had to really slow down and explain everything. They thought I was speaking a different language! I can imagine. It's fascinating, though, how dialects evolve. It's a reflection of the history of a place, isn’t it? I did a lot of travelling around Australia, and you could hear the subtle differences in accent from region to region.

Honestly, I’m starting to feel so… detached from everything. Everyone’s life is just  perfect  on Instagram. Honestly, it's exhausting. Oh, tell me about it. I had to do a bit of a social media detox last week. Just scrolling endlessly, comparing yourself… it’s a waste of time, isn’t it? And mostly not real anyway. Exactly! It's all curated. I saw Auntie Brenda posting photos of her garden looking absolutely pristine. Brenda! Her garden is usually a jungle. Oh, Brenda. She’s a character. But yeah, everyone puts their best foot forward. It's exhausting to consume. What are you watching on TV at the moment, to escape all the perfect lives? Nothing much, actually. I’ve been trying to limit screen time, ironically. Though, I did binge-watch that historical drama, ‘The Serpent Queen’ a few weeks ago. That was good. Properly wicked. You? Oh, I loved that! Samantha Morton was brilliant. I’m currently working my way through ‘Severance’ on Apple TV. It’s… weird. Really weird, but really good. Such a clever concept. All about work-life balance, or lack thereof, essentially. Sounds intriguing. I keep meaning to subscribe to Apple TV, but there’s so much streaming stuff already. It's getting expensive, isn't it? Plus, I'm finding myself listening to more podcasts these days. Oh, what kind? I'm always looking for recommendations. I've been listening to a lot of true crime, which is probably a terrible habit. Well, I’m not surprised, knowing your taste! I’ve been listening to a few history ones, mainly. Stuff about the Tudors, which is probably why I enjoyed ‘The Serpent Queen’ so much. There’s one called ‘The Rest is History’ that's really good, conversational and engaging. ‘The Rest is History’… I’ll look that up. See, this is why I love catching up with you. I always get good recommendations. Honestly, I feel like I spend more time  searching  for things to watch and listen to than actually watching and listening. Isn't it the truth? It's the paradox of choice, I think. So much available, it just becomes overwhelming. Oh, this food is amazing, by the way. You were right to bring me here. This pierogi is incredible. Told you! Rzeszow is a surprisingly good food city. And it’s nice to find a fully vegan place.

Right, so swimming on Saturday is definitely on, yeah? Unless you’d rather do something else? Can Pippy come? Pippy? Oh, you want Pippy to come swimming? I don't know if they allow so many… let me check the rules. Maybe if we ring ahead. I wanna come swimming too! You  are  coming swimming! Both of you. It’s a family swim. Right. Then after swimming, we need to think about… the circus. Ooh! The travelling circus! Are the clowns funny? Apparently, very funny. And they have amazing acrobats. It’s on Saturday afternoon after our swim. Can I have popcorn? Yes, you can have popcorn. But only  after  you’ve had a healthy snack, okay? Now, about this Blue Peter Badge… I want to get a picture for Blue Peter! Exactly! We need a good picture of you both building something amazing. Remember that den we made in the garden last week? That would have been perfect! It fell down! Yes, it did. But that’s okay. We can build another one. Or maybe something with your LEGOs? Something really inventive. Can we build a spaceship? A spaceship! That’s a brilliant idea! Okay, spaceship building is on the agenda. Now, speaking of agendas, have you been saving your pocket money? I spent some on sweets! Oh dear. Well, we’ll have to have a little chat about that later. Remember, we agreed some goes into savings. I haven’t spent mine! I’m saving for a unicorn! That’s a very good plan. Right, okay. This is all going well. We just need to check… passports. Remember, Nana and Grandad are coming to visit next month. Have you two grown much since the last time they saw you? I'm taller! I bet you are! We need to make sure your passports are still valid. I’ll check later. Oh, and did you hear what Mrs. Higgins said today? She was talking about... well, it was a bit strange. What? Apparently, in China, some people eat eggs that are… really old. Like, months and months old. Eeeew! That’s disgusting! I know, right? It's a bit odd. But don’t worry, we won’t be eating any old eggs anytime soon! Now, who wants a biscuit? Before spaceship building commences? Me! Yes, please! And can I have a juice? Of course, you can both have juice. Now, let's go get the Lego!

It’s just…it’s a bit awkward innit? Him telling me. Like, straight up. Yeah, that  is  a bit much. Especially so early on, right? Exactly! We've been seein' each other like, what, six weeks? And he’s confidin' in me about… that. Erectile dysfunction. I mean, blimey. Oh, no. That’s…a lot. Did he just, like, blurt it out? Pretty much. We were just chillin', watchin’ telly, and he just went, “Right, I need to tell you somethin’… I sometimes have trouble, y'know, gettin’… up.” Oh, gosh. That's awful. Did you know what to say? I just…froze. I think I said somethin' like “Oh, right.” Which was spectacularly unhelpful, lookin’ back. No, that’s a perfectly normal reaction! It’s a really sensitive thing for someone to share. And, like, not exactly everyday conversation. Exactly! And now I’m stuck thinkin’ about it. Is he expectin’ me to…fix it? Or what? I’ve never even… No, he absolutely shouldn’t be expectin' you to fix anything! That's his thing to sort out, if he wants to. He probably just wanted to be honest, but timing, yeah, bad timing. Very bad timing. I think he was worried about, like, disappointin’ me. That's…kind of sweet, I guess. But also, a bit unfair to put that on you. It's okay for people to have…issues. It doesn't mean they're failures or somethin’. I get that. I do. It’s just…awkward, isn’t it? And now I'm worried about… everything. Like, what if it happens and I'm gonna be all awkward and stuff. Listen, you said six weeks, right? It’s early days. You don’t need to be worryin’ about all that. If it happens, it happens. And if it’s a problem for  him , he needs to talk to a doctor. Not you. That’s what I was tryin’ to tell meself. I just feel… responsible somehow. Which is daft. It  is  daft! You're not his mechanic. You're his girlfriend. Or, potentially girlfriend. Don't let him make you feel like you have to solve his medical problems. Seriously. You're right. You're totally right. I just need to...ignore it, really. Pretend he didn't say anything. Well, not  ignore  it completely. You can acknowledge that he told you and that you appreciate his honesty.

Right, so I was thinking, for tonight, I could do the chilli, but like, a  proper  chilli. Not a watery one. Ooh, yes! And we can have it with the wholemeal rice, right? That’s a Healthy Extra B, isn’t it? Gotta maximise those. Absolutely. And I saw in Sainsbury’s they’ve got that new Quorn mince, the one that’s supposed to be really like, proper beefy. It's actually quite good. Better than the usual stuff. Oh, really? I’ve been avoiding Quorn lately, feels a bit… processed. But if it’s decent, then okay. I’m just trying to be good, you know? Trying to stay on plan. Me too! Although, honestly, I'm already planning Saturday. Treat day. I’m thinking a giant slice of cake. A proper, layered one. Ooh, ambitious. I was leaning towards a takeaway. Indian, maybe? But you’re right, a cake  is  a good treat. We’ll have to calculate the syns carefully though. Definitely. I’ve got that 0 calorie syrup, the caramel one, that’ll help with cravings. It’s fake as anything, obviously, but it does the trick. Yeah, I've got the vanilla one, tastes like disappointment, honestly. But it’s better than nothing. Did you see how much that mint cost in Tesco? Absolute robbery! Oh my god, don't even. Everything's going up. I swear. I need to actually do my tax return properly this year, it’s terrifying. Tell me about it. Freelancing and tax is a nightmare. I’m hoping I haven’t massively underpaid. Speaking of money, should we look at ordering a veg box again? It saved us a fortune last time. Good shout. It’s just… chopping all the veg. It's a commitment. I’m just so tired after work, you know? Dispensing all day… it's not exactly mentally stimulating. I get it. Carering can be draining too. People just expect you to… magically fix things. I’ve been trying to get some illustrating done, but I keep getting distracted. It’s hard to find the focus, isn't it? Right, chilli. I think I’ve got a good spice mix somewhere. And loads of tomatoes. Oh, and I found a bag of double peas in the freezer! Bonus. Double peas? You lucky thing. I had to use a sad, lonely bag last week. Okay, I’ll get the rice on.

Right, so if we go to Italy, and we do the Amalfi Coast, we’d need to book accommodation  well  in advance. Like, now. Seriously. Because everything gets snapped up. We’re not even sure we're  going  to Italy, though, are we? You were on about Scotland last week. Scotland in November? No. It’ll be pouring with rain and dark by four o’clock. Italy feels…brighter. More festive. We could do cooking classes, go wine tasting… Sounds expensive. Well, it wouldn’t be cheap, no. But we’ve been saving. And honestly, I need a break. Work has been…stressful, to say the least. Old Man Hemmings is driving me round the bend with his demands. Hemmings, eh? Still micromanaging everything? Worse. He’s started sending me emails at eleven at night asking for reports he knew he didn’t need until Monday. It’s just…control, isn’t it? Just wanting to feel in control. Sounds exhausting. Anyway, even if we  did  go to Italy, what about the dogs? Old Barnaby would hate being kennelled. He’d spend the whole time howling. I know, it’s a nightmare. Maybe we could get someone to house-sit? Sarah from next door, perhaps? She’s good with animals. Sarah? She’s got that boyfriend, the one who’s obsessed with everything being perfectly in its place. Remember when she came round and rearranged your spice rack? Don’t remind me. Honestly, the man needs to chill. Okay, scrap Sarah. What if we… oh, I don’t know. It’s just hard planning anything when everything feels so complicated. Tell me about it. I spent all afternoon trying to fix a client's network. Turns out, they’d accidentally downloaded about a thousand toolbars. A  thousand . It was like cleaning up a digital landfill. Oh, God. The internet is a cesspit sometimes. I was reading an article about that guy who got a massive tattoo of Rishi Sunak… No way. Seriously? Apparently. It's a full back piece. And he said it was a tribute to “strong leadership”. Oh, you couldn't make it up. Honestly. Imagine explaining that regret at a party. “Oh, this? It’s a…political statement.” Exactly. Speaking of regret, you still thinking about getting that motorbike? It’s been put on hold. You looked at me like I’d suggested we rob a bank. Well, you’d be eighty years old before you mastered it!

Right, so, the 18th is definitely free then? For the birthday lunch? Yeah, clear as a bell. Bit of a trek down to The Pig, though, isn't it? From here. It is, but it’s what your mother wants. She’s been going on about it for months. Apparently, their garden is looking spectacular. She’s fallen for their marketing, hasn’t she? They’re very good at that sort of thing. Still, a good excuse to get out, I suppose. Have you booked it properly? Last time we tried that place, they’d completely lost the reservation. Yes, I triple-checked. Confirmed it yesterday, got a reference number and everything. I’m not letting that happen again. The disappointment was significant. Good, good. Progress. Did the postcard arrive from Italy? The one I sent you? Oh, yes! It was lovely. A rather dramatic shot of the Amalfi coast, wasn't it? Though, you looked a bit windswept in the corner. Oh, that's Italian weather for you. One minute blazing sunshine, the next a gale. Worth it for the pasta, though. Honestly, the pasta. I saw. Several pictures of pasta. Trying to make me jealous, were you? Perhaps a little. You’ve been stuck inside grading those essays for weeks. Speaking of which, how are they going? Dreadful. Utterly dreadful. The standard is dropping year on year, I swear. I had one essay that completely misconstrued the entire concept of post-structuralism. Utterly. Sounds…challenging. Change of subject, swiftly. Have you been following the latest rumblings about Scottish independence? A little. It's all rather tiresome, isn’t it? Another referendum. Honestly, can’t they just…decide? It’s got legs this time, though. Seems like public opinion is shifting. The energy crisis and all that. They're feeling rather left behind. I still think it's a fundamentally flawed idea. Economically disastrous. But then, what do I know? I’m just an old academic peddling outdated theories. Don’t be so self-deprecating. You’re a brilliant academic. And, well, it’s a complicated issue. No easy answers. Anyway, this weekend - are we still on for a walk in the Peak District on Saturday? Absolutely. Providing it doesn’t rain. The forecast looks…unsettled. Unsettled is the Midlands’ default setting, I’m afraid. We'll pack waterproofs, just in case. Should we meet at the usual spot? The car park near Edale?

Right, so I was thinking, for the Syrian refugee appeal, instead of just donating money, maybe we could  do  something? Something the kids could be involved in, you know? Like what? Make cookies? Well, I was brainstorming, and I thought… we could draw chairs. Draw chairs? Why? Well, because people who have had to leave their homes, they often don’t have…basic things. Like a chair to sit on. So we could draw really lovely, comfy chairs, and send the pictures to the charity. They could use them to decorate… I don’t know, a welcoming space or something? Just to show people we’re thinking of them. But why chairs? Can’t we draw houses? Or…kittens? That’s a good point, darling. But a chair is… it’s a place to rest. A place to feel safe and comfortable. And it’s something we all take for granted, isn’t it? I like drawing. Can I draw a racing car chair? With flames? You absolutely can. Whatever you like, as long as it’s a chair! I was thinking maybe we could all try and draw different types of chairs. I could draw a rocking chair. I want to draw a princess chair! With sparkles and a really high back! Perfect! And maybe your brother can draw his racing car one. What do you think? Yeah! Can I use glitter? Hmm, glitter might be a bit messy, sweetie. Maybe we can use sparkly pens instead? My teacher, Mrs. Davies, says we have tests next week. Big ones. Oh, yes, I remember. Don’t worry too much about those, sweetheart. You always do your best. What are they on? Reading and maths. And… spelling. I hate spelling. Spelling  is  rubbish. I keep forgetting how to spell ‘because’. Well, practicing your spelling  while  drawing chairs might be a good idea! We can write the words near the chair. Like, “comfortable because chairs are comfy!” That’s silly. It is silly! But it might help you remember. We can make it a fun project. What kind of chair do  you  think they need most, hmm? Maybe a strong chair? Or a really comfy one to read books on? A really, really big chair so everyone can sit on it together! Oh, that’s a  lovely  idea! A family chair. Right, well, let’s get some paper and pens. And let’s see what amazing chairs we can create.

Honestly, I’m still reeling from seeing Sarah with the baby. It feels… weird. Like, I  know  she wanted one for ages, and bless her, she looks absolutely exhausted, but it’s just… a shock. Yeah, it is a bit of a jump. It feels like only yesterday we were all moaning about marking essays and now she’s… fully in mum mode. Did she say she was coping alright? She said she was on a steep learning curve. Mostly just surviving on coffee and snatched moments. Apparently, little Leo doesn't sleep much. And Mark is… well, Mark’s being Mark. Completely doting, but utterly useless with anything practical. She laughed when she said he tried to change a nappy and nearly lost it. Classic Mark. He always was a bit… sheltered. Still, good on them. It’s just… it makes you think, doesn’t it? About timelines and stuff. Don't start. I’m not ready for that conversation. Not tonight. I’ve just spent the last three hours battling undergraduate essays on post-structuralism. My brain is fried. I didn’t mean to put pressure on! Just… seeing them, it highlights how things are shifting. Remember when we were all complaining about Professor Davies’ endlessly boring lectures? Oh god, yes. And how we all secretly suspected he wore a wig. That feels like a lifetime ago. And now  we’re  the boring lecturers, inflicting our wisdom on a new generation of sleepy undergraduates. It’s a role reversal, isn't it? I had a student ask me today if I’d ever actually  used  any of the stuff I was teaching. Honestly, it threw me. Ouch. That’s brutal. What did you say? I mumbled something about academic rigor and the importance of theoretical frameworks. I don’t think he was convinced. Anyway, back to Sarah… Do you think she'll still try and come to the book club? She said she'd try, but understandably isn’t making any promises. She thinks Mark might be able to take a shift with Leo. Honestly, I suspect she needs a night out more than anything. It’s just… good to see her happy, even if I feel slightly ancient now. We’re not ancient! We’re… experienced. And it’s lovely that she’s happy. Maybe we should send her a little care package. Biscuits and coffee, the essentials.

It’s just…it’s so quiet, isn’t it? Proper quiet. Not like London quiet, where it’s just  different  noises, layered on top of each other. This is… nothing. Blissful. Honestly. I feel my shoulders dropping already. You know, I saw a post online the other day about how people who live in the countryside are statistically less likely to believe in superstition. Really? That’s odd. I’d have thought it’d be the opposite. All those old wives’ tales about fairies and… things. Apparently, it’s something to do with having a stronger sense of control over your environment. Less feeling of helplessness, therefore less need to attribute things to… the unseen. Ridiculous, of course. Right. Because encountering a badger at midnight  definitely  makes you feel in control. Speaking of ridiculous, did I tell you about that policeman at the comedy club last week? Oh, no! Do tell. Was he undercover? Trying to blend in with the hipsters? Worse. He was  on  stage. Apparently, he does stand-up as a hobby. And it was… excruciating. All jokes about speed cameras and parking tickets. The audience was dying. Oh, good lord. That sounds… professional. In the worst possible way. Did anyone heckle him? One brave soul tried. Something about ‘needing to catch actual criminals’. He didn't take it well. Nearly had a full-blown meltdown. It was amazing, and awful, all at the same time. It'll probably get publicity because of the policeman. Oh dear. The perils of amateur comedy. It’s a brave new world, isn’t it? Police officers moonlighting as comedians. What’s next, university professors doing TikTok dances? Don't even joke! The thought terrifies me. Though, actually, Professor Davies in the History department is surprisingly nimble. I saw him at the Christmas party… never mind. I’m choosing not to picture that. So, seriously though, are you thinking about applying for that research grant? The one for the Victorian literature project? I am. But the deadline is looming, and I’m still procrastinating. I have this mental block about writing the proposal. It feels so… performative. You're brilliant at that kind of thing. You always sell yourself short. Just think about the research itself. The actual Victorian novels. That’s the fun part. True. And the idea of a summer spent delving into Brontë sisters instead of marking essays… that  is  appealing.

Honestly Dad, you wouldn't believe the signal in my halls. It’s like living in a bunker sometimes. You’re lucky you get decent coverage here. Bunker, eh? Fancy. Used to be alright ‘round here, though they keep putting up those masts. More masts, more signal, that’s what they say. Don't make much difference to me, I’m not glued to that phone like you youngsters. Speaking of which, have you remembered to charge it? Don’t want you stranded if you need to call. Yes, Dad, I’ve charged it. Multiple times. It's fine. I was just saying, when I’m trying to join online lectures it’s a nightmare. Drops out constantly. Online lectures… sounds dreadful. All that squinting at a screen. Remember when learning meant books and a blackboard? Proper learning, that was. Yeah, well, things have changed. Anyway, about Saturday – are you sure you don’t mind me hiring a van from B&Q to help move some of my stuff back? It’s just… a lot to carry on the train. B&Q? Bit pricey, aren’t they? There’s Old Man Hemmings down the road, he hires vans. A bit knackered, they are, but cheaper. Though, knowing your luck, you’d probably get one with a flat tyre. I checked a few places, B&Q had the best rate for the day. And I’d rather not risk a flat tyre, honestly. I really need to get everything moved on Saturday. Alright, alright, B&Q it is. Just be careful driving the thing. They’re bigger than they look. Remember what happened to young Timmy Barnes? Reversed straight into Mrs. Higgins’ flowerbeds. Nearly caused a war. I remember! Poor Timmy. I’ll be careful, promise. So, are you still planning on going to the Great Dorset Steam Fair? Oh, absolutely. Been looking forward to it all year. Though, honestly, the price of entry keeps going up and up. Daylight robbery, I tell you. Still, you can’t beat the smell of steam and oil. Reminds me of… well, never you mind. Reminds you of what? Come on, Dad. Old times. Never you mind. Now, is your Auntie Carol still coming down on Sunday? I haven't heard from her. She said she was, but she’s been a bit quiet lately. I’ll give her a ring later just to check. It would be nice to see everyone together.

It’s just… infuriating, isn’t it? They’re actually proposing to knock down the library. The  library ! I know! I saw the article online. Utter madness. They want to put another block of flats there, apparently. “Regeneration,” they’re calling it. Regeneration! It’s destruction, more like. Where are people supposed to go? Old Mrs. Higgins practically lives there. She’s there every Tuesday for the book club, and then again on Thursdays for the computer classes. Exactly. And it’s not just Mrs. Higgins. Think of the kids, too. It’s a safe space for them after school. And the research resources… I used it loads when I was doing that family history thing. Me too! Remember when I was trying to find out about Great-Grandad George? The librarian was brilliant, helping me track down old census records. You can't get that kind of help online. No, you really can’t. It’s all algorithms and keyword searches. No actual… human intelligence. It's just… short-sighted. It’s the council, isn’t it? They just see everything in terms of pound signs. How many flats can they cram onto the site, how much money can they make… They don’t care about community spaces. They say they’ll build a smaller library as part of the development, but… it’ll be tucked away in the basement of the flats, I bet. And probably won't have half the books. It won’t be the same. Definitely not. Speaking of things needing preserving… have you finally chosen a fabric for the armchair? I was looking at some online earlier, and there are some gorgeous velvets. I’m still torn. I’ve narrowed it down to two. One’s a sort of deep teal, really rich looking. And the other’s a floral, but not a  fussy  floral… a slightly more muted, contemporary one. Teal sounds lovely. It would really brighten up the living room. Though, I do like a good floral… it depends what the rest of the room looks like, doesn’t it? That’s what I’m struggling with. I was reading an article about maintaining old buildings, actually. This guy was saying how important it is to respect the original architecture. Keeps the character of the place. Absolutely. Look at some of those Victorian buildings in town. They’re just stunning. They could do with a bit of a clean, but they’re beautiful structures.

Right, so are we all agreed then? No more eighties synth-pop for the entire journey? Absolutely not! My ears were starting to bleed. Honestly, Dad, it’s like you’re stuck in a time warp. It wasn't  that  bad, was it? A bit… repetitive, maybe. Though, I am rather partial to a bit of Depeche Mode. See, Sarah’s got some sense. It's classic! But yes, perhaps a bit of variety wouldn’t go amiss. How about some of that indie stuff you were listening to, Chloe? I’ll put on a playlist. Promise. No synthesizers. Unless they’re subtly incorporated. Subtly incorporated? What does that even  mean ? It means she'll sneak one in when you're not looking. Typical. Speaking of sneaking things in, has anyone thought about what to get Auntie Margaret? Her birthday’s next week, isn’t it? Oh, goodness. I completely forgot. She’s impossible to buy for. She’s got everything. She loves those little ceramic animals, doesn’t she? The ones you get at garden centers? She has a whole shelf full of them. Though, she did mention needing a new bird feeder. The squirrels keep raiding the old one. A bird feeder! That's brilliant, Sarah. Practical and thoughtful. I’ll have a look online. What about you, Chloe? Still doing the pottery classes? Yeah! It’s actually going really well. I’m attempting a vase at the moment. It’s...challenging. It keeps collapsing in on itself. Pottery’s hard. It looks so serene, but it’s physically demanding. I tried a class once, ended up with clay everywhere. Sounds about right. You're more a TV-watching kind of guy, aren't you, Uncle David? Guilty as charged. I’ve been binge-watching that detective series… what’s it called?  Broadchurch . Absolutely gripping.  Broadchurch ? Oh, I saw the first series. Very bleak. It is! But the acting is incredible. Olivia Colman is phenomenal. I’ve been meaning to start that. I’m currently obsessed with this baking show. It’s so soothing. And I get inspired to actually bake things, which is a bonus. Even if they don’t always turn out how they should. Well, at least you’re trying. I haven’t attempted anything more complicated than toast in weeks. Maybe I should take up a hobby. Something other than listening to eighties synth-pop, that is.

Right, so you’re seriously thinking about getting a car then? At sixteen? Yeah, well, a lot of my mates are starting to learn and… it’d be good, wouldn’t it? For getting to rugby training, and seeing people, and stuff. It would be convenient, aye, but have you even  thought  about the cost? It’s not just the car itself, love. I know, I know. Dad said something about that. “Something about that”? He’s right to say something! It’s a fortune! First, there’s the car. Even a banger will cost you a few grand these days. And then there’s insurance. Oh, the insurance. How much is insurance, roughly? Roughly? It’s… well, being sixteen, a new driver, living in North Yorkshire… it’s not going to be cheap, put it that way. You’re looking at… oh, I don’t know, easily £1500 a year. Maybe more. Depends on the car, of course. Fifteen hundred?! Seriously? That’s… that’s a lot of money. It is! And that’s before petrol, tax, MOT, servicing, and inevitable repairs. Cars are money pits, son. Glorious money pits, but money pits nonetheless. So, like, a smaller engine would be cheaper to insure? Generally, yes. Smaller engine, less powerful, statistically considered less likely to be driven recklessly. Though, honestly, insurance companies seem to base it on… well, on witchcraft and algorithms these days. They look at everything. Your postcode, your dad’s job, what A-Levels you’re taking… What do my A-Levels have to do with it? Apparently, it's a 'risk assessment'. They think students taking certain subjects are more likely to be involved in accidents. Honestly, it's daft. But that's how it works. Are you planning on doing Pass Plus? Pass Plus? What's that? It’s extra driving lessons after you’ve passed your test. It teaches you more advanced driving skills, and a lot of insurance companies will give you a discount if you’ve done it. It's worth looking into. It can knock a few quid off that frightening insurance bill. Okay. I’ll ask Dad about it. He’s been looking at cars online, actually. Something small, he said. Good. Small is sensible. And make sure it has good safety features. Don't go for something ridiculously flashy, even if you could afford it. You don't need to impress anyone, you need to be safe.

Honestly, the week… the week was something else. They’re talking about restructuring again, you know? Another “efficiency drive.” It’s just code for making everyone do the work of two people. Ugh, sounds awful. Like when Mr. Harrison made us all do extra homework because he was ill? It  is  awful, isn’t it? You’re lucky you just get extra homework, Sean. They're subtly implying redundancies. I was reading an article – apparently, heart rate variability is a good indicator of stress. They have apps for it now, monitoring it with your watch. Sounds a bit… dystopian, doesn’t it? Dystopian is a good word for it, actually. Measuring your stress levels… it feels like they’re looking for reasons  to  stress you out, then measuring the result! You know, remember back in… oh, God, twenty fifteen, the referendum? The marriage equality one? Vaguely. I was pretty young then. It was amazing, truly. The whole country just…shifted. Such a positive energy. It felt like everyone was having the same conversation, finally. So hopeful. Bit of a contrast to this corporate nonsense, eh? Right. Well. Anyone fancy looking at the menu for the Chinese? I’m starving. That's a good shout. I’m up for it. Though, honestly, the quality of the chicken in their curry has been declining. It’s…stringy. They use proper chicken, don't they? I heard some places use… stuff. Don’t even go there, Sean. Don’t fill my head with that! It’s bad enough knowing  where  the chicken comes from, let alone what  is  the chicken. You’re always so direct, Mary. It’s refreshing. Although, I wouldn’t put it past them to try and palm us off with mechanically separated… well, never mind. Are you recording this, Sean? You’ve been staring at your phone for five minutes. What? No! I was just checking… uh… a podcast. My mate recommended this one about… linguistics. Apparently, the most frequently searched word on Google is “how.” “How?” That’s… surprisingly underwhelming. It's simple, isn't it? Humans are perpetually trying to figure things out. Now, about that Chinese. I think we need to discuss delivery versus collection. Collection means I have to interact with people, which, post-work, feels like a Herculean task. Although, I do need to walk… You and your walking! Honestly, you talk about needing a walk like it’s climbing Everest.

Honestly, did you  see  the size of that bird? It wasn’t a seagull, it was massive. Like a small aircraft. Was it one of them buzzards, Mum? They get big round here. Possibly, love. Though I’d say it was too pale for a buzzard. Could have been a heron, flown a bit off course. They can get quite substantial. Reminds me of a trip to Italy. We stayed in this hilltop village, utterly charming. You could see for miles, and the birds soaring around were incredible. Nothing like the pigeons in London, that's for sure. Oh, Italy! I’ve always wanted to go. But all those winding roads…I’d be sick as a dog. You get used to it. It's worth it for the views. And the food. Though speaking of travel, anyone else think the EU referendum was a disaster for holidaying? All that faffing about at borders… Oh, don’t even start me on that. I still think it was a terrible mistake. But anyway, how's your law conversion course going, love? Bit stressful? It is, honestly. So much information! And the reading list is ridiculous. It’s all about…well, it doesn't matter. You wouldn’t understand. Is it harder than school, Sis? A million times harder. Though it’s not even the work, it’s the constant weighing and measuring. "How many kilos is that in pounds?" "How many miles is that in kilometers?" I feel like I’m back in primary school. You’ll get used to it. It’s just a different system. Now, speaking of weights, I had Mrs. Higgins in labour this morning. Beautiful baby girl. Seven pounds, eight ounces. Lovely! You’re a miracle worker, you are. Though I imagine midwifery is a lot less argumentative than politics. You have no idea. My Gran's convinced everything’s down to God’s will, and tries to convert everyone she meets. It's  exhausting.  Gran’s weird. Now, now, be nice to your grandmother. She means well. She just has…strong beliefs. Have you seen Old Man Hemmings’ new car? Bright orange! It’s an eyesore. Actually, garish cars are quite a statement. Bold. A bit like Shakespeare, really. All that drama and… orange. Shakespeare? What's Shakespeare got to do with cars? You're losing it, aren’t you? It’s a metaphor! A flourish of language!

Honestly though, I just… I can’t get my head around the idea of “shmeat.” Like, lab-grown meat. It feels so… unnatural. But isn’t  all  meat unnatural in a way? We’ve been selectively breeding animals for millennia to make them bigger, fatter, more docile. And the conditions they’re kept in… that’s pretty unnatural too. Yeah, exactly. I mean, the alternative is basically supporting industrial farming, which is horrific. At least with cultured meat, you’re potentially avoiding all that. No animal suffering, less environmental impact… I get the arguments, I really do. It’s just… the thought of it. It feels like something out of a sci-fi film. I’d probably still take a veggie burger over it, honestly. Though, that reminds me, I need to get more B12. I forgot to pick some up. Oh, good shout. I’m running low too. I’ve been feeling a bit… off lately. Probably just tired, but better to be safe. Do you think it’s weird how much we have to supplement just to be vegetarian? Like, nature  intended  us to get these things from food. It’s a bit messed up, yeah. It’s like, we’ve removed ourselves so far from natural food sources that we have to artificially recreate them. Kind of ironic, when people criticize vegetarianism as being “unnatural.” It is, isn't it? It's like a constant back and forth. Speaking of ironic, did you guys see that documentary about hunting? It was horrifying, obviously, but… the guy made a really good point that, in a way, a quick death in the wild is often more humane than a life in a factory farm, followed by the abattoir. Ugh, don't even. I had to turn it off. I was getting so upset. It’s a horrible choice to have to make, really. Is one kind of suffering better than another? It feels…wrong to even think about it like that. It’s a terrible position to be in. I think hunting is… it’s still taking a life, and I'm not comfortable with that. But the abattoir system… that’s just systemic cruelty. I read something about the way they stress the animals before slaughter, to increase the yield of meat. It’s disgusting. Don’t even start. I’m trying to enjoy my lentil shepherd’s pie.

Right, that was a bit of a letdown, wasn’t it? The ending, I mean. Aye, proper predictable. I saw it coming a mile off, with the old dad turning out to be the villain. Classic. I liked it though, honestly. Just a bit of mindless entertainment. Needed that after all the revision. Revision, ha! You and revision rarely share the same postcode, don't you? Hey! I've actually been doing some this weekend. Promised me mam I would. She’s threatening to disconnect the Wi-Fi if I don't pull my finger out. She's a hard woman, your mam. Good on her, though. Someone’s gotta keep you in line. Speaking of Wi-Fi, I’m waiting on a new phone case. Ordered it online last night. Took ages to find one that wasn't a hideous colour. Online shopping, eh? You’ll be ordering your meals online next. Don't knock it ‘til you try it. Saves going out in this weather. Plus, you get loads of discounts. I got a tenner off the case with a voucher code. You’re obsessed with discount codes. It’s a talent, honestly. Proper bargain hunter, that one. I’m thinking about getting a new headset for the Playstation. Mine’s on its last legs - keeps cutting out mid-game. Drives me mental. Get a wireless one, then. No wires getting in the way. Trust me, it's a game changer. Literally. Have you guys started thinking about Christmas yet? My auntie’s already asking what I want. It's only November! Christmas? Don’t even mention it. It’s a logistical nightmare. Trying to coordinate seeing everyone, finding presents... it's stressful. Aye, it is. Especially trying to get time off work… well,  looking  for time off work, in my case. Still no luck on the job front, by the way. Sent out another ten applications this morning. Oh, no way! That’s rough. You'll get something, though. You’re overqualified for most of those jobs anyway. Yeah, you are. Honestly. Remember when you got a first in your degree? Honestly, it's a waste having you unemployed. Thanks, lads. Means a lot. Reckon I should just move to Australia or something. Start a new life. Australia? Bit drastic, isn’t it? Plus, you'd be missing out on Christmas at Nana's. You know she'd never forgive you.

Honestly though, seeing everyone back here is so weird. It feels like ages ago we were all stressing about dissertations in the library. Tell me about it! And now…well, I’m still basically in a library, just a slightly different one. Though yours sounds way more interesting, language research co-ordinator, sounds fancy. It’s good, yeah. A lot of data analysis, which I actually enjoy, surprisingly. How’s the admin side of things? Still mostly spreadsheets and emails judging by your face? You know me too well. Honestly, it’s…fine. It pays the bills. The real issue is I’m starting to feel seriously itchy feet. I think I need a holiday. A proper one. Ooh, plans? Anywhere specific? I was thinking of trying to finally get to Italy. I’ve been saying it for years, but…life. Italy! Oh, that sounds amazing. I’ve always wanted to go to the Amalfi Coast. I was looking at a little trip to Portugal too, just a week or so. My cousin lives near Lisbon, and she keeps sending me pictures of these gorgeous beaches. Portugal sounds really good, a bit more chill maybe. My aunt went to Lisbon last year and said it was incredible, really affordable too. She dragged my mum along and Mum actually had a good time, which is saying something. Mum’s are like that aren’t they? Always needing convincing. Speaking of family, how’s yours? Still living back in Bucks? Yeah, mostly. My brother finally moved out, found a little flatshare in Brighton. He’s doing something creative, I think…vaguely remember something involving ceramics? It’s always a mystery with him. Classic. Mine are still firmly entrenched in Lincoln. Dad’s taken up gardening, apparently he’s trying to win the village horticultural show. Mum’s mostly just bossing him around. Sounds…peaceful. In a mildly stressful way. Do you ever regret not travelling more when we were students? I feel like we were always too busy or too broke…or both. All of the above. I did that Interrail thing for a couple of weeks, but it was mostly just sleeping on trains and eating questionable sandwiches. I’d love to go back and actually  see  places properly. Maybe next year? We should! We definitely should. We could even attempt some actual language practice. Imagine trying to order coffee in fluent Italian!

Ugh, this essay is  killing  me. Honestly, I’ve been staring at this screen for hours. Which one is it? The one on post-structuralism? Because I swear, that reading list was designed to actively discourage us from doing the course. No, thankfully not that one. It’s the one for Medieval Lit, about… symbolism in Beowulf. Sounds simple, right? It’s not. It’s just… endless interpretations. And I don't  have  an interpretation. Right. The beauty of Beowulf is that everyone reads something different into it. What’s the word count? Two thousand. And it’s due Friday. I’ve got, like, six hundred written so far, mostly just paraphrasing bits of the poem and whining about how confusing it is. Six hundred’s not bad, though. You’ve made a start. Look, you know I finished my dissertation, right? I can have a read through it if you want, just… bounce some ideas around. Would you? That would be amazing, actually. You always get it, you know? You always see things I miss. Seriously, thank you. No problem. I’m just… avoiding marking. It’s therapeutic to talk about other people’s academic woes. Speaking of therapeutic… you look relaxed. Did you actually go for that massage you were talking about? I did! Oh my god, it was incredible. This little place near campus, proper good. Deep tissue, the works. I could barely walk afterwards, I was so loosened up. Ooh, jealous! I really need one. Uni stress is officially physically manifesting as knots in my shoulders. Maybe I can find a voucher online or something. Definitely do. You deserve it. You’re stressing over Beowulf for a reason, yeah? And how were your lectures today? Anything interesting? Honestly? Dull. Professor Harrison just droned on about Chaucer for the entire two hours. I swear, he hasn’t updated his lecture notes since 1985. It's just the same stories, the same slides… Yeah, he’s a bit… stuck in his ways. Though, to be fair, some of those stories  are  good. It's just his delivery. Like listening to someone read a phone book. Exactly! And then he gave us another reading list. Another  massive  reading list. I think I’m going to start just skimming things at this point. Don't do that! You’ll just end up more confused. Look, why don’t we make a plan?

This is really lovely, Mum. Honestly, the roast chicken is perfect. So moist. Glad you think so, love. Just a simple recipe, really. Though getting a good quality bird makes all the difference these days. Everything's so…processed. It is, isn’t it? You wouldn't know what you were actually eating half the time. I was reading an article this morning about the migrant situation in Calais. Absolutely heartbreaking. Oh, God, don’t remind me. It’s just… dreadful. Seeing those families, crammed into those camps. It’s just… hopeless, isn’t it? It’s a mess. And the politicians just seem to be playing games. No real solutions offered, just rhetoric. Honestly, it makes you lose faith. It really does. Did you see that report about the increased security? It’s just pushing them further into dangerous situations. Makes you feel so helpless. Anyway… let’s not ruin a lovely lunch talking about that. How are your plans for next month coming along, Dad? Still thinking of going to Scotland? Yes, as long as the weather holds. Hoping to do a bit of walking, see some of the Highlands. I’ve booked a small cottage near Fort William. Nothing fancy, but it'll do nicely. Oh, that sounds lovely! You'll get some amazing photos. Have you told Emily and Ben yet? Yes, Emily’s already asking about bringing the dog. Which won't happen. It’s a long drive, and the cottage garden isn't fenced. Good. That dog is a menace! Lovely, of course, but a menace. What about you, Sarah? Any exciting plans on the horizon? Well, I'm thinking of doing a pottery workshop in October. Mrs. Peterson at school mentioned it, and it sounds really relaxing. A bit of creative time would be good. That sounds brilliant! You’ve always been so good with your hands. Remember that amazing knitted blanket you made last Christmas? Oh, that was nothing! It took me ages, though. I think I need something a little more instant gratification. Hence the pottery. It’s good to have hobbies, keeps you young. And speaking of young… How’s little Leo doing? Still causing chaos, I presume? Always! He’s just started walking properly. It's terrifying. He goes  everywhere . And he’s discovered climbing. Everything is a climbing frame now. Oh, they're little adventurers at that age. Enjoy it while it lasts!

Honestly, the bathroom… it’s still not finished. I thought by now, with all the assurances… Ah, tradesmen. What can you do? Never believe a word they say, is what I’ve learned. Old Gareth down the street, he was telling me just last week, promised him a new boiler, fitted by Tuesday. Tuesday came and went, Gareth was freezing. Exactly! This fellow, Marco, said four days for tiling. Four days! It’s been ten, and it looks like a five-year-old did it. Seriously, the grout is… uneven. And some tiles are actually  loose . Loose? That’s… concerning. Did you withhold final payment? You  did  withhold, didn’t you? Of course, I did! I’m not a fool. I told him, “No money until it’s rectified.” He’s coming back tomorrow apparently. Though I suspect ‘rectified’ means sending someone else. He doesn’t look like he knows the difference between a trowel and a teaspoon. Sounds about right. I’m thinking about tackling the kitchen, you see. It’s…dated. Very dated. Orange cabinets, avocado worktops… a relic of the seventies. Oh, dear. A full gutting, then? Probably. My wife, Bronwen, is pushing for it. She's got a Pinterest board, you wouldn't believe it. Slate floors, induction hob, a kitchen island… it's a whole redevelopment project! Sounds expensive. You have no idea. I’ve started getting quotes. It’s frightening. And finding someone reliable… that's the real challenge. I was talking to Dewi, remember Dewi from the History department? His brother-in-law is a builder. Supposedly good. Dewi? Yes, vaguely. The one who’s obsessed with Roman fortifications? That’s the one. He swears by him. Said he did a fantastic job on his conservatory. But still, you never truly know until… well, until the dust settles, quite literally. Precisely. Did you hear about poor Eleanor? She hired a plumber who flooded her downstairs flat. Apparently, he ‘accidentally’ cut through a pipe. She’s still dealing with the insurance. No! Oh, that’s dreadful. Honestly, it's a minefield.
