You think you're improving things, and then disaster strikes. Speaking of disasters, have you seen old Professor Armitage lately? Apparently, he tried to fix his own guttering. No! Don't tell me… Fell off the ladder! Broke his wrist. Now he’s got his arm in a sling, looking like a pirate. Serves him right, trying to be a DIY expert at his age.

Right, so this curry is… potent, wouldn’t you say? A bit much for the little fella, maybe? More! He thinks so too, obviously. Maybe I should have gone easier on the chili. Though you did say you wanted a kick, darling. I did, I did. It’s just… it’s a serious kick. Reminds me of that time old Man Doherty tried to make his own poitín. Near blew the roof off his shed, it did. Poitín? What’s that? Sounds… dangerous. Oh, it  is  dangerous. Illegal moonshine, basically. Though the taste… well, best not to ask. It’ll strip the paint off your tongue. Please don’t tell stories about illegal moonshine at the dinner table, Liam. Especially not when we’ve got impressionable young ears. I’m not impressionable! I read  Horrible Histories  - I know about all sorts of dodgy stuff. They’ve got one on medicine in the Victorian era, it’s really gross. Want to hear about trepanning? Oh, no thank you. We are eating dinner, not discussing ancient skull surgery. Honestly, where do you learn these things? The book! It’s got horrible science in there too. Like, really horrible. Did you know some people used to think leeches could cure everything? Well, they weren’t entirely wrong. Leeches do have medicinal properties, you know. Though I wouldn’t recommend letting one attach itself to you. Not pleasant, that. Saw a fella with one stuck to his… well, never mind. Shiny! No, Finn! Don't put metal in your mouth! Honestly, you’re going to swallow something you shouldn’t. Liam, watch him for a second? Aye, sure thing. This one’s a handful, isn’t he? Always exploring… with his mouth. Reminds me of myself as a lad. Once ate a whole marble. A marble?! Did it hurt? Hurt? Oh, you wouldn’t believe. Mum nearly had a heart attack. Thought I’d choked. Turns out, it just… passed through. Though I did feel a bit… hollow afterwards. Like I had a superpower. What superpower? Not passing marbles, I hope. The ability to withstand internal objects, apparently! Though don’t tell Finn that, he’ll be trying to swallow everything in sight. So, what about plans for your birthday, Thomas? Any thoughts? I was thinking maybe that park thing? The one with the historical re-enactors? Oh, that sounds lovely. They’re doing a medieval fair, aren't they?

So, how was school today, love? Anything exciting happen? It was alright. We did dissection in science. Ooh, dissection! What did you dissect? A frog? A heart. A pig’s heart. It was… gooey. Gooey, eh? Sounds a bit messy, that. Did you enjoy it though? It was alright. Bethany nearly threw up. Bethany? Oh, she’s a sensitive one, that girl. Not cut out for the medical profession, perhaps. No, definitely not. She's more of a drama queen, isn’t she? Speaking of dress-up, are you thinking about Halloween costumes yet? Yeah! I want to be Wednesday Addams. Wednesday Addams? Goodness me, a bit morbid, isn’t it? It's cool! All black dresses and braids. It’s a good choice, actually. Very popular this year, I believe. My class are all talking about it. They’re aiming for group costumes – the whole Addams Family. Oh, that would be lovely! Maybe you and your friends could do that? Maybe. I don’t know if Sophie wants to. She wants to be a unicorn. A unicorn. Well, that’s… colourful. Did you have a good ride today, then? After all that dissecting? Yeah! I jumped a bigger jump today. Star was really good. Oh, that’s wonderful! She’s a lovely pony, Star. So gentle. Are you taking her out again tomorrow? If it doesn’t rain. Mum said I can go after school. Excellent. Fresh air is good for you. Keeps you away from those screens. We took the kids on a trip to Cromer today. Lovely little seaside town. Cromer! Haven't been to Cromer in years. Used to go there as a boy with my parents. Crabs and chips… can’t beat it. It’s still very nice. Gets terribly busy in the summer, of course. But it’s a lovely walk along the pier. Can we go again soon? Possibly. We’ll have to see. It was a bit of a drive, though. Maybe we could look at somewhere closer next time. Perhaps Great Yarmouth? Great Yarmouth… now  that's  changed. Used to be a proper seaside resort, Great Yarmouth. Now it’s just arcades and chip shops. It has lost some of its charm, hasn’t it? Still, it’s a day out. And the kids enjoy the arcades. Anything else happen at school today, love? Any interesting gossip? Um…Liam tried to swap his lunch for mine.

Honestly, this traffic is ridiculous. I thought we’d be there by now. It's just… stationary. Always is, love. Always is on these country lanes. Everyone decides to go to the steam fair all at once. Still, better than being at home, eh? Less to look at, anyway. You've got a point there, Dad. Though honestly, I’m starting to wonder if the council should do something about the access. It’s just not fit for purpose anymore. All this traffic… It’s frustrating, isn’t it? Makes you think about older people, actually. How they manage to get anywhere. Especially if they need… you know… specialist parking. Specialist parking? They don’t make it easy, do they? I was reading in the paper about some old bloke, nearly ninety he was, trying to get decent housing. Been on the waiting list for years. Oh, don’t even get me started on housing. It’s a disgrace. Mrs. Higgins at work, her daughter's been trying to get a council house for ages. Single mum, working full-time, and they keep saying there’s nothing available. It’s awful. You hear stories about people living in really unsuitable places because there’s just nowhere else to go. It’s not fair. They promise sheltered housing, ‘independent living’… but there’s never enough of it. Sheltered housing… mostly full of folks that don’t  need  it, if you ask me. People who are perfectly capable of looking after themselves, just like a bit of company. Taking up spaces from those who really need it. Well, that’s what Sarah was saying at work. Apparently, there’s a rule about being able to ‘manage’ your own affairs - like paying bills and stuff. But some people just tick all the boxes to get in, even if they’re perfectly fit and able. It’s all so messed up. And then with disabled parking, it’s just… a free-for-all. People using badges that aren’t theirs. I saw someone park right across a disabled bay in the supermarket last week. Honestly! Seen it myself, many a time. No respect. They need to do more policing of it, that’s what they need. Massive fines. That’d soon stop them. That’s true. Although, even if they  do  fine them, it doesn't really help the person who couldn't park. It's just… frustrating.

Honestly, I’ve been spending  hours  online looking at allotment layouts. It’s completely consumed me. I’ve got Pinterest boards dedicated to runner beans, it’s ridiculous. Oh, you're properly diving in then! That's good though, it shows you’re committed. I'm still in the very early stages of vaguely thinking about what I  might  grow. Mostly herbs, I think, to start with. Things I actually use when I’m cooking. Herbs are a good shout. Less… overwhelming. I’m aiming for self-sufficiency, basically. Or at least a very ambitious attempt at it. I want to grow all my salad, loads of tomatoes, potatoes, the whole shebang. Ambitious! You’ve got the space for that, haven't you? Your garden is huge compared to my postage stamp backyard. Yeah, it's alright. But the allotment plot is bigger still. It’s a good size, but it's  overgrown . Honestly, it looks like a jungle. We’re going to be clearing brambles for weeks. Oh god, brambles are the worst. They cling to everything! Have you got gloves and proper long sleeves? You’ll need armour. I’ve invested in some seriously heavy-duty gardening gloves, yes. And I think I need to borrow Dad's secateurs – mine are useless. What about you? Have you even seen your plot yet? I had a quick look a couple of weekends ago. It’s pretty basic. Just grass, mostly. Thankfully no brambles. Although there  is  a rather sad-looking shed that needs some serious attention. I’m thinking of painting it bright yellow. Bright yellow! That’s brilliant. You need a focal point. I’m toying with raised beds, but they’re expensive. And then there's the compost situation... do you know much about composting? A little. My nan was a fantastically keen gardener, and she was a composting queen. Apparently, the key is the right mix of “greens” and “browns”? I mostly remember being told not to put meat in it. Greens and browns, right. I’ve been reading about that. It sounds so complicated. I think I need a proper composting course. Do they even  do  those? I bet they do! The local council probably runs gardening workshops. Have you checked their website? Actually, I think there’s a community garden near me that does them. I could send you the link. Oh, that would be amazing!

Right, so are we still on for going into Leeds on Saturday then? I’ve got that exhibition I wanted to see, the one with all the… well, I can’t remember what they were, actually. Abstract shapes, mostly. Yeah, definitely! Sounds good. Though, honestly, I’ve been thinking about things with Ben a lot. Oh? What’s up? Is everything alright? You’ve been a bit quiet about him lately. I don’t know. It’s just… I feel like we’re just…stuck. Like, we just do the same things every weekend. Cinema, his mum’s for Sunday roast… it’s comfortable, but it's a bit  too  comfortable, you know? Yeah, I get that. Sounds a bit predictable. You need a bit of spice in your life! Though, his mum does do a cracking roast. She does! That’s part of the problem, isn’t it? It’s hard to complain when the gravy’s that good. But I was talking to Chloe the other day, and she was saying she and Liam are going rock climbing next weekend. It sounded so… exciting. Oh, nice! Chloe’s always up for something adventurous. Good for them. Maybe you and Ben could try something like that? I suggested it, but he wasn't keen. Said he’s not exactly built for scaling cliffs. Which, fair enough, but it felt a bit dismissive. Like he doesn’t want to try new things  with me , if that makes sense? Hmm, yeah, I see what you mean. It's not about the rock climbing, it's about the willingness to do stuff together. That’s a bit rubbish of him, to be honest. Exactly! And then Maya was telling me she’s seriously thinking about applying for that internship in Barcelona. Just up and leaving for three months! Woah, Barcelona! That's huge! Proper grown-up stuff. You reckon she'll go for it? She said she’s really nervous, but she feels like she needs to  do  something different. It makes me feel a bit…stuck, you know? Like I’m just drifting along. I need a plan. Well, Leeds on Saturday is a start! A bit of culture, a wander around… we can people-watch and judge outfits. That’s always good. And maybe when you've had a good think about Ben, we can brainstorm some ideas. Massive adventure, or just a slightly less predictable Saturday night?

Right, I’m telling you, that last boss was rigged. Absolutely rigged. No way anyone beats that on their first try. You’re just saying that because you died, Liam. You always say that when you lose. No, seriously! The timing on that attack is  impossible . It’s like they deliberately made it unfair. Did you see how fast it was? I saw you get absolutely wrecked, yeah. It was quite funny, actually. Sorry, Liam. Hilarious. Very funny, thanks. You lot are no help. I'm starting to think you are all working with the game developers. Nah, I just think you need to, like, git gud. No offence. “Git gud”? Seriously, Noah? That’s your advice? It’s a broken game! He’s got a point though. You were just mashing buttons, weren’t you? You need a bit of strategy. I  was  strategizing! I was… uh… trying a new tactic! It involves a lot of mashing. Right. Well, while you two debate the merits of button-mashing, I’m gonna grab another can of Red Bull. This is intense. Good shout, I’m running on fumes too. Anyone fancy anything from the kitchen? I saw some biscuits earlier. Biscuits would be good. Especially those chocolate digestives. Have you seen what they did with the new season of ‘Heartstopper’? Ugh, don't even get me started on ‘Heartstopper’. It feels so… different. Not necessarily bad, just. Different. I thought it was good! A bit more mature, maybe? It’s not meant to be a fluffy teen romance forever, you know? Yeah, I liked the direction they were going in. It felt a bit more real, a bit less… predictable. Predictable is good! I wanted predictable! I like knowing what's going to happen. It’s comforting. Like a good, easy boss battle. You’re still on about the boss battle, aren't you? It’s a matter of principle! Anyway, what are you all up to tomorrow? Anything exciting planned besides judging my gaming skills? Honestly? Just gotta finish that essay on Victorian literature. It's killing me. I’m supposed to be going to that gig in town. Some indie band, apparently. Trying to convince Sarah to come with me. Oh, the one at the Waterfront? I heard they’re pretty good. You should definitely go! Sounds tiring. I’ll probably just spend the day trying to understand why that boss is such a sadist.

Honestly, Doreen’s been on at me about joining that gardening club again. Honestly, like I haven’t got enough to do! She says it’ll get me out the house, but frankly, I’m happier  in  the house. Less weeding. Sounds like Doreen. She’s always trying to organise everyone. Did you tell her you’d already signed up for the pottery class? No, not yet. I’m saving that as a last resort. If she gets too pushy. Pottery’s alright, though. Surprisingly therapeutic, actually. Though my last attempt looked… well, let’s just say it resembled a wonky ashtray more than a vase. Oh, come on, I bet it was lovely! You always underestimate yourself. Speaking of therapeutic, have you seen that new film, ‘Everything Everywhere All at Once’? Oh, no. Is that the one with the… the everything? I saw a trailer. Looked a bit… frantic. It  is  frantic, but in a brilliant way. It's about this Chinese-American woman who has to connect with versions of herself in parallel universes to save the world. Sounds bonkers, and it is, but it’s also really moving. Michelle Yeoh is phenomenal. Michelle Yeoh… oh, the action lady! She’s very good, isn't she? I saw her in that James Bond film, years ago. Exactly! She’s incredible. It's a bit of a mind-bender, but honestly, it's one of the best films I've seen in ages. We should go and see it together, when you're free. Oh, I don’t know about the cinema, my dear. My knees aren’t what they used to be. All that getting up and down… We could go to the Arts Picturehouse, they have those comfy chairs. And we can get a coffee afterwards. Mmm, comfy chairs  do  sound good. Alright, alright, you've twisted my arm. When are you free? How about next Tuesday? I’ve got a relatively quiet week at work. Tuesday… let me have a look. Oh, yes, I’ve got my bridge club on Tuesday afternoons, but we could do a matinee beforehand. Perfect! We can book tickets online. Oh, and have you heard from Lesley lately? I haven't spoken to her in ages. No, not for a couple of weeks. She’s probably busy with those grandchildren of hers. She adores them, you know. Always sending photos. Little monkeys, the lot of them!

Honestly, the amount of admin I had to do for that interview yesterday… it was ridiculous. Like, four different forms, all asking essentially the same thing but worded slightly differently. Oh, the joys of bureaucracy! What was the interview for, anyway? Still the thing in Bristol? Yeah, the linguistic fieldwork one. It went… okay. The guy kept trying to get me to talk about ‘methodology’ and I just wanted to scream. Like, yes, I understand methodology! I  did  a masters! Ugh, academics. So pretentious sometimes. Did you at least manage to steer the conversation towards actually, you know,  doing  linguistic fieldwork? Eventually. I brought up the ethical considerations, which he seemed to like. I think he was trying to gauge if I’d be willing to just… barge into people’s lives and record them. Which, obviously not. Speaking of barging into lives… have you guys seen the latest episode of  The Undateables ? It was  wild . Oh god, don’t even get me started. That guy who collects garden gnomes? Seriously? It’s a bit exploitative, isn’t it? I mean, it’s well-meaning, but… feels a bit icky sometimes. It is, but it’s also utterly addictive. I can’t help myself. Anyway, forget that for now! Biscuits? I brought Hobnobs. Oh, excellent. Thank you. So, the interview… you reckon you’ve got a chance? I don’t know. The other candidates sounded pretty strong. One woman had spent a year living with a tribe in the Amazon or something. I just… analysed reality TV dialogue. That’s still valuable research! Don't sell yourself short. Besides, Amazon sounds itchy. So, what are we doing this weekend? I was thinking maybe we try and find one of those pop-up spa things? I desperately need a massage. Ooh, that sounds divine! I'm in. I saw one advertised in Shoreditch, apparently they do hot stone massages and everything. That sounds amazing. I’ve been a stress ball lately. Although… Sarah keeps trying to get me to go to a board game night with her and her friends. Sarah, as in Sarah from uni? The one who's obsessed with  Settlers of Catan ? The very same. She says it’ll be “fun” and “a great way to unwind." But honestly, the thought of spending an evening arguing over sheep and wheat just fills me with dread. Oh bless. Maybe offer to bring the nibbles and just… observe?

Right, so the washing machine’s decided to give up the ghost again, hasn’t it? Honestly, I’m starting to think it’s a personal vendetta against me. Oh no, not again! What's it doing this time? Just refusing to spin? Or is it the dramatic flooding routine? Worse, I think. It's making this  noise . Like a strangled walrus. And it smells faintly of burning. I genuinely thought the house was on fire for a minute. Burning? That doesn’t sound good. We really need to get someone to look at it properly. We can’t keep relying on the laundrette forever, it’s costing a fortune. I know, I know. I’ll call that repair bloke, Derek, tomorrow. He’s a bit… eccentric, but he usually fixes things. Though last time he just told me it needed ‘a good talking to’. A good talking to? That’s helpful! Seriously though, a burning smell is worrying. Don't use it until Derek's had a look. Speaking of things needing fixing, I was thinking about what we’re having for dinner. I’m absolutely knackered. Do you fancy just ordering something? I was eyeing up that new Thai place on Mill Road. That does sound good, actually. I’ve been meaning to try them. I had a rather depressing sandwich for lunch, so something spicy would be very welcome. What about your mam? Did she phone today? She did. Went on for about an hour. Mostly about my auntie Doreen’s cat having a cough. Apparently, it’s a crisis. Honestly, you’d think it was a human child, the way she was carrying on. Oh, Doreen's cat. Always a drama. Your mam does worry about everything, doesn't she? It’s sweet, in a way. It is, but it's exhausting sometimes. She also asked if we were going to visit for Easter. I told her we hadn’t really made plans yet. Which isn’t a lie, but I’m secretly hoping we can just have a quiet weekend in. Understandable. Although, a trip back up North wouldn't be awful. I miss a proper Sunday roast. We could always convince your mum to make one when we’re down. She’s a wizard with a Yorkshire pudding. True. Though she’ll insist on making us do all the washing up. It’s a trade-off.

Honestly, the price of houses down south is absolutely mental. Mental! You wouldn’t believe what they're asking for a shoebox in London. It's just… supply and demand, isn't it? Though, yeah, it's ridiculous. Even places like Brighton are extortionate now. My cousin’s looking and she’s practically having a breakdown. It’s the whole ‘London bubble’ effect. Pulls everything up with it. Makes it difficult for people to get on the ladder anywhere. This area is relatively reasonable, mind you. Though even Hunsonby’s creeping upwards. Reasonable? Relative to London, maybe. But even for what you get, it’s a bit steep. Remember when we first looked here? We got a lovely little cottage for a song. Now, that same cottage would be… well, nearly double the price. It's the ‘quiet life’ premium, isn’t it? Everyone fleeing the cities. Wanting a bit of green space. Drives the prices up. Still, I can’t imagine living  in  a city again. The noise… the people… Speaking of people doing dodgy things… did you two follow that VW scandal years ago? Absolutely shocking. Deliberately cheating emissions tests? Oh, yes! I remember reading about it. Appalling. And the sheer scale of it too. Millions of cars affected. It just shows you can't trust anyone, doesn't it? Even big corporations. It’s terrifying, really. The lengths they went to. Trying to look environmentally friendly while actively polluting the planet. And getting away with it for so long. It was all about meeting targets. Bonuses, promotion… the usual corporate greed. They pushed their engineers to find a solution, and the solution was… cheating. A software patch to detect when the car was being tested and adjust the emissions accordingly. Clever, in a cynical sort of way. Cynical is putting it mildly! It’s downright dishonest. And the fallout… lawsuits, recalls… and I bet the people responsible barely faced any real consequences. I think some executives  did  get prosecuted, didn’t they? Though, you're right, probably not enough. It feels like the punishment never really fits the crime with these big companies. They just pay a fine and carry on. Precisely. It’s just a cost of doing business. A calculated risk. That’s the problem with these massive organisations. They're too big to fail, too big to really punish. It's the same with the banks, isn’t it?

Honestly, I don’t know why I bothered writing that letter. It’s just stirred everything up again. Who to, Arthur? Still to that council chap about the development? Yes, yes. Pointed out again about the drainage, you know. Said it’s going to cause flooding down at the bottom of the field. They just don’t listen. It’s like talking to a brick wall. Well, you always were a bit direct, weren't you, Arthur? Sometimes it’s better to… well, not ruffle feathers, shall we say. Ruffle feathers?! They're building a housing estate on a floodplain! It's not ruffling feathers, it's pointing out a disaster waiting to happen! I’m just trying to be reasonable. They'll say it’s all been assessed, Arthur. They always do. Professional assessments and all that. Assessments done by people  they  pay! Of course it’s been assessed! Assess that it’s alright to put houses where the water flows! It's scandalous, that's what it is. So, what did he say in his reply? Was it a polite brush-off? More or less. Said they’ve taken my concerns ‘into consideration’. That’s code for ‘we’re ignoring you’, isn't it? Honestly, it’s enough to make a person stay in bed all day. Don’t go doing that. You need to get out, Arthur. A bit of fresh air. It's a lovely day. Fresh air won’t stop the houses causing floods, will it? I’m just… fed up. Remember Old Man Hemmings? He had a right go at them about building on that green space, and what happened? Ignored him too. It's just the way things are now, I suppose. Nobody listens to older people anymore. It’s all about progress. Progress that ends up with everyone’s gardens underwater. That's a peculiar sort of progress. How’s your pension looking, by the way, Mary? Any better than last month? Honestly, it's a joke. Barely covering the bills. I do wish we'd saved more, but when we were younger… well, things were different. We didn’t earn much. We were hoping for a bit more to help young Emily with her deposit, you know. She’s looking at places in Ipswich. Dreadful prices. Ipswich is expensive now. They're building like mad there too. Heard tell of a place down near the docks, a converted warehouse.

Honestly, the physics practical this week was a joke. Mr. Harrison just expects us to  know  stuff we haven’t even been taught yet. Tell me about it. I spent three hours trying to calculate the spring constant and still got it wrong. He just walked around saying "apply the principles!" Like, which principles, sir? The ones you forgot to mention? It's always like that with Harrison. He thinks we're all mini-Einsteins. I actually preferred Mrs. Davies for chemistry, she at least  explained  things properly. Davies is alright. Though, did you see that TikTok about her? Someone claimed she accidentally called potassium “potassiumium” during a lesson. No way! Is it real? Apparently. It’s gone viral. There's a whole duet chain of people pretending to be her. It’s proper funny. People will find anything to make fun of. Though, “potassiumium” is a good one. Speaking of viral, did you guys see that argument on Twitter about… I don't even know where to start. Basically, someone said biology is a ‘female’ science? What?! Seriously? How can a science be gendered? Right? It’s ridiculous. I saw it, and the replies were… intense. Lots of people talking about historical sexism in science and how women are discouraged from STEM. It’s that whole thing, isn’t it? Like, “oh, biology is about bodies, and women have bodies, therefore…” It's such a warped logic. Exactly. And then someone tried to bring up evolution. Saying men are naturally better at scientific thinking because of… something to do with hunting and gathering or something. It was wild. Oh, here we go. The caveman argument. Always a classic. Ugh. It’s exhausting. Like, can’t people just accept that intelligence isn’t tied to gender? And that even  if  there were some evolutionary basis - which there isn't - it doesn't justify discrimination. I think it’s just people being deliberately obtuse. Trying to find some justification for their biases. Makes you wonder why they feel the need to do that in the first place. True. It’s usually projection, isn’t it? Someone feeling insecure about something. Speaking of biases, have you guys seen Liam talking to Chloe again? Liam? Oh,  that's  awkward. He was going on and on about how she doesn’t get his sense of humour the other day. Yeah, and then she rolled her eyes so hard I thought they were going to get stuck.

Honestly, the hospital was a nightmare yesterday. The waiting room was packed, and they were running hours behind. Oh, you poor love. What was the appointment for again? Just the check-up after the operation? Yeah, the post-op. They wanted to see how the incision was healing, make sure there's no infection. The nurse kept saying they were ‘exceptionally busy’, but it was just chaos. Old Mrs. Higgins was having a right go at the receptionist. Oh, Doris Higgins. Always a drama queen. She’d complain if they gave her a cup of tea too hot. She’s a character, that one. Remember when she tried to return a Christmas pudding to the Co-op in July? Said it was ‘past its best’. Oh, I’d forgotten about that! Anyway, the doctor finally saw me, said everything  looked  okay, but he’s put me on another course of antibiotics, just to be sure. I swear, I’m rattling with tablets these days. That's not good, is it? Another infection scare? You've had a rough time of it. Have you tried that acupuncture Sarah recommended? She swore by it for her arthritis. I’ve thought about it, but I’m a bit…skeptical. Needles aren’t really my thing, to be honest. Nonsense, dear. It doesn't hurt a bit. Just a little pinch. Helps get the energy flowing. Old Man Hemmings swore it cured his gout. Hemmings would swear anything cured his gout if it meant he could have a pint down the pub. True enough. Speaking of things I’m skeptical about, how’s Auntie Mabel doing? Last I heard she was convinced she was developing a friendship with her Alexa. Oh, she's still at it! She tells it all her secrets. Apparently, it gave her advice on picking lottery numbers last week. Needless to say, she didn't win. Bless her heart. She's always been a bit…eccentric. Still, she’s happy, and that’s all that matters. Right. Now, has anyone been watching the rugby? England were awful on Saturday. Absolutely dreadful. They were a bit shaky, weren't they? Too many penalties. Actually, I was trying to watch it online, but the Wi-Fi kept dropping out. It’s a disaster. Trying to get someone to fix it is another thing entirely. Wi-Fi, rugby... In my day, we just had a good old fashioned pint and a sing-song.

Right, so basically, imagine a long, long time ago…before even your Great-Grandma was born, people weren’t always treated fairly. Some people, with more power, decided they could  own  other people. Own them? Like…a toy? Not like a toy, sweetheart, but like…they made them work, and they didn’t let them choose where to live or who to marry, or even if they could learn to read. It was called slavery. It was terribly, terribly wrong. Why did they do that? That’s mean! It  was  mean. They did it because they wanted free labour – people to work for them without paying them anything. They thought they were better than other people, which, of course, wasn’t true. It mostly happened a long time ago in America, but it also happened in other parts of the world. Did they get angry? Oh, very angry. And brave. Many people fought against slavery, and eventually, after a long, long time, slavery was made illegal. But it caused a lot of pain and suffering for many, many years. It’s important to remember it so we don't let anything like that happen again. So…like the baddies in a story? In a way, yes. But it wasn't a story, it was real life, and it involved real people. Now, sometimes when countries disagree, it can lead to even worse things…like war. War? Like soldiers and bangs? Yes, sometimes like that. But war is much more than just soldiers and bangs. It’s when people get hurt, and families get separated, and homes get destroyed. Think about everything we have here, your toys, our comfy home, our school…war can take all of that away. Is there a war now? There are sadly conflicts happening in different parts of the world right now, which is very sad. That’s why it's so important to try and solve problems peacefully, by talking and understanding each other. It’s a bit like when you and your sister argue over a toy. You try to sort it out by talking, right? Yeah, Mummy helps. Exactly. And world leaders try to do something similar, although it's much more complicated than arguing over a toy! They’re trying to find ways to help people, and to stop the fighting. These things are all connected, you see. Understanding the past – like slavery – helps us to try and make a better future, a future where everyone is treated fairly and peacefully.

Honestly, have you seen that new series, “The Diplomat”? It’s completely gripping. Bit far-fetched in places, but still… I’ve heard good things. Is it on Netflix? I’m currently wading through another Scandi noir, all dark and brooding. They’re good, but honestly, they all blur into one after a while, don’t they? Oh, Scandi noir is my weakness! But yeah, you’re right, it’s like they’re all made by the same three people. I’m addicted to “Taskmaster” at the moment. Greg Davies is just…  chef’s kiss . Taskmaster? That’s the one with the silly challenges, isn’t it? Never really got into it. Prefer a good documentary. Watched one the other day about sharks. Fascinating creatures, utterly terrifying. Sharks? Oh, don't talk about sharks. Remember old Mrs. Higgins? She swore a shark swam up the Medway during the floods years ago. Absolute nonsense, of course, but she went on about it for  years . Oh, bless her. She did love a good story, didn't she? Speaking of stories, did you hear about Brenda next door? Apparently, she’s taken up beekeeping. No way! Brenda? With her fear of wasps? Honestly, the woman is a marvel. I hope she’s got good insurance. Bees are amazing though, aren't they? Such important little creatures. I saw a whole swarm in the garden last week, it was incredible. I was too scared to get close though! It’s a shame about old man Peterson’s dog, though. Buster, wasn’t it? Apparently, he’s not doing too well. Oh no, poor Buster! He's such a sweet old thing. I saw Peterson at the shops yesterday, he looked absolutely devastated. Peterson always did dote on that dog. Spent more time talking to him than to people, if you ask me. Still, good on him. Loyalty’s a rare thing these days. It is. Speaking of loyalty, have you all seen what’s happening with that actor, the one from… what was that film… the one with the spaceships? Timothée Chalamet? Oh, the drama with his personal life is  wild . It's all over TikTok. TikTok? What's TikTok? Sounds like a clock with a nervous tick. It's a social media app, Dad. It's where all the youngsters hang out. Although, I'm on there too, now. Don't tell everyone! Social media, bah!

Right, okay, dishwasher duty. Lily, can you unload the cutlery, please? Thomas, you can get the plates. Gently now, those are Mummy’s good ones. But the forks are pointy. They are, aren’t they? Just be careful, hold them by the handle. Good girl. Thomas, are you finding enough plates? There's loads! Can I put them on the high shelf? Not quite yet, darling. Leave those for me. You put them on the lower shelf, okay? Now, what are you two up to after this? Anything fun planned? I want to read Harry Potter! The one with the dragon! Oh, the one with the Hungarian Horntail? That’s a good one. It's a scary dragon, isn't it? I want to build a train track! A really,  really  long one. That sounds brilliant! You know, that reminds me of someone. Do you know who George Stephenson was? Who? He was a very clever man, a long, long time ago. He invented the first steam train! Before trains were pulled by horses, you know. Horses pulled trains? Well, they pulled carriages  on  the tracks. But George Stephenson figured out how to build a machine, a steam engine, to pull them much faster. He built something called the ‘Rocket’. A rocket train! Did it go to space? No, not to  space . It went very fast along the tracks! It was a really important invention, it helped people and things travel all over the country. He was a bit like a wizard, really, using science to create something amazing. Like Harry Potter? Well, Harry Potter uses magic, and George Stephenson used… engineering! It’s a different kind of magic, but just as powerful. He had to figure out how everything would work, what materials to use, everything. It wasn’t easy. Was he a good wizard? He wasn’t a wizard, silly! He was an engineer. He built things, he didn’t cast spells. But people thought he was very clever. He was one of the first people to build railways, so we could travel quickly and easily. Can we build his rocket train with my blocks? That's a lovely idea, darling! Maybe we can look some pictures up online afterwards so you can see what it really looked like? Now, come on, let’s finish unloading this dishwasher, and then we can get building! Thomas, did you get all the bowls?

Right, so I genuinely think I’m being targeted on Words With Friends. Like, someone is actively trying to ruin my life with triple word scores. Oh, dramatic much? It's just a game, Leo. Though, knowing your competitive streak... It  is  weird, though, isn't it? When you get someone consistently landing on all the doubles and triples. Sounds a bit sus. Mate, you’re overthinking it. Probably just a really good player. Or a bot. They exist, you know? A bot? Seriously? On Words With Friends? That's… dystopian. No, this feels personal. She’s clearly googling the highest-scoring words. I swear. Who is “she”? Is this about Chloe again? No! It's... someone. A mysterious opponent. Look, can we not talk about Chloe right now? I'm trying to focus on existential threats to my Scrabble-adjacent wellbeing. Speaking of threats, did you get anywhere with that legal website thing, Liam? For the café? The GDPR stuff? Oh yeah, I was helping him with that last week. It's a nightmare. So much paperwork. Proper pain in the arse. Honestly, it's a minefield. I’ve found a few templates, but it’s all so confusing. And then there’s the cookies consent banner… it feels like having to ask permission to breathe. It  is  a pain. I had to do it for my little bakery website. Honestly, I just stuck a generic one on there and hoped for the best. You can’t just “hope for the best” with GDPR, El! You’ll get fined! I know, I know. Stress baking is a real thing, you know? It helps me cope. Which reminds me, try this rosemary and sea salt focaccia when it’s ready. I've been experimenting. Rosemary and sea salt, eh? Sounds good. Beats this carrot I’m currently battling. So, back to the impending doom of my Words With Friends score… do you think I should just challenge someone else? Maybe. Or just accept defeat with grace. That’s what I do with my niece when we play Monopoly. I let her win. Mostly. You let her win? Zara would bankrupt you in five minutes flat. She’s learning business skills early, alright? Besides, it’s more fun when she's happy. Anyway, I was thinking about doing another supper club next month. Should we do something Italian again? Italian’s always a winner.

Honestly, this canteen food is…an experience, isn’t it? I think I’ll stick to a sandwich tomorrow. Yes, ‘experience’ is a kind word. It's...functional. I brought leftovers from last night, thankfully. Borscht. Oh, lovely! I always mean to try making borscht, it sounds amazing. It’s just… so much beetroot, isn’t it? It stains everything! It does! My mother always says you know a good borscht by how brightly it colours your fingers. It's a point of pride. Speaking of mothers, how’s little Leo doing? He is a whirlwind. Absolutely exhausting, but so funny. He’s obsessed with dinosaurs at the moment. Every single toy, every book…it’s all dinosaurs. It’s taking over the house! Ah, the dinosaur phase. My cousin's son went through that. Apparently, every bath was a ‘prehistoric swamp.’ Oh, I can just picture it! Leo's baths are already pretty chaotic, so adding dinosaurs probably wouldn’t make much difference. What about you? Anything exciting happening outside of work? Not much, really. I’ve been trying to get back into painting. It's difficult to find the time, though. After work, I usually just want to collapse. I used to do a lot of watercolour landscapes when I lived in Tomsk. Oh, that sounds lovely. Watercolour is so relaxing. It’s good to have a hobby, isn’t it? Something to switch off with. I used to do a lot of cross-stitch, but that’s fallen by the wayside since Leo arrived. It’s hard to prioritize things when you’re busy. I find if I don’t schedule it in, it just doesn’t happen. Maybe you could try doing a little bit of cross-stitch while Leo's playing? That's a good idea. Maybe just a small project. He’s pretty good at independent play for short bursts. This job is just… draining sometimes, though. Especially today. Cover supervising Year 9s… it’s like herding cats. I can imagine. They're at that age where they think they know everything. It must be difficult to keep them on task. Have you had any particularly…interesting incidents? Oh, where do I begin? Someone decided to have a full-blown debate about the ethical implications of artificial intelligence  during  a maths lesson. Another one tried to convince me that Pythagoras was a conspiracy theorist. Oh my goodness!

Right, so are we definitely going to Mothercare then? ‘Cause I really wanna look at those fluffy blankets. The ones with the little… you know, the little animals on? Yes, darling, we are going to Mothercare. Unless you suddenly decide you need a unicorn saddle for the cat? Mum! Don't be silly. No unicorns. Just blankets. And maybe a little hat. For the baby, obviously. Aye, a little hat. Can’t have a bairn going about with a cold head, can we? Though, that reminds me, did you get that report back from the surveyor, love? On the house? Yes, I did. It was… extensive. Apparently, the damp proof course is older than I am. And the roof needs some serious attention. Oh, great. More money to spend. Is it gonna be, like, a massive reno? Potentially. He said the back garden needs a new drain, too. And something about the joists in the kitchen. I told him, didn’t I, I told him we’d felt a bit of a bounce when you were jumping about in there last time? Yes, you did. He said that’s structural. Delightful. Seriously? Bouncing is structural now? I thought it was just me. Remember when I used to build forts out of blankets in Grandma’s living room? Massive ones. How could I forget? She used to moan for days about the mess. Used to say you were turning her house into a circus. It was fun though. And remember those little plastic babies? I used to pretend they were my kids. Bit weird now, looking back. You were a very nurturing child. Still are, actually. Always thinking about the little one. Well, it’s exciting, isn’t it? Scary, but exciting. Are you still feeling okay? Have you had enough water? I’m fine, darling. Just a bit tired. And yes, I’ve had water. Honestly, you fuss over me like I'm made of glass. She’s right to fuss, love. She's growing a human being. It's hard work. It's not like being at uni, swanning about with your mates, is it? Ouch, Dad. Low blow. Your father’s got a point, actually. University was… different. Fewer morning sickness episodes, for a start. And definitely fewer shopping trips for miniature hats. It was fun though, wasn’t it? Meeting all those people. Remember Liam? He was doing a law degree and… Nevermind.

Ugh, I lost  again . This game is rigged, honestly. That level with the glowing mushrooms is impossible. Now, now, darling. Nothing’s rigged. You just need to practice. Perhaps you’re rushing it a bit? Remember what you said about calming down when you're feeling stressed? It’s not rigged, but it  is  designed to be frustrating. It's a Skinner box, basically. They want you to keep coming back, even when you're failing, so you’ll eventually spend money on upgrades. It's psychology, Mum. A Skinner box? What even is that? Sounds…horrible. Like a torture device for hamsters. It’s a psychological concept, love. Your brother’s studying all that at uni, isn't he? Something to do with behaviour and rewards. Though I still think you just need to breathe deeply and focus. It's behavioural psychology, yeah. It's horrifyingly effective, actually. That’s why games are so addictive. Anyway, how was your day, both of you? Apart from my sister’s digital suffering. It was alright. History was boring, Mr. Henderson just droned on about the Tudors  again . And then Chloe was being really annoying in maths, copying my answers. Oh, that's not nice. Did you tell the teacher? No, it's just…it's Chloe. She always does it. I’m starting to think she just exists to irritate me. Sounds exhausting. Speaking of irritating, my lab partner completely messed up the titration today. Ruined the whole experiment. Honestly, some people shouldn’t be allowed near beakers. Oh dear. That sounds stressful. Are you still thinking about going to Italy over Christmas? It sounds lovely, but it's a long way to go. Italy? That sounds amazing! Can we, Mum? Please? I promise I'll be good. And I'll even try to be less grumpy. It’s a bit of a trek from Frimley, granted. But it would be nice to escape the…British weather. And I’ve been reading about some really interesting science museums in Rome. Well, we have to think about your Dad, darling. He doesn’t really like flying. And with work being so busy, I don’t know if he can get the time off. He can work from anywhere, can't he? He always says his job is just staring at a screen. Technically, yes, but it’s more complicated than that. He has meetings and stuff.

Right, so, copper is quite easy to find in Minecraft, isn’t it? But you need loads of it to make anything decent. It’s not as good as iron, obviously. Iron is  way  better. You can make swords and pickaxes and armour! And you can build a whole iron golem if you have enough! And diamond is the bestest! But you have to go really, really deep to find it. Like, past where the lava is. It's scary. It  is  scary. You need a good iron pickaxe, at least, to even mine diamond. Remember when we were trying to get diamond last week and you nearly fell in the lava, Leo? I didn’t  nearly  fall in. I just… wobbled a bit. You screamed! Loudly! You did. Now, let’s talk fabrics. What’s your favourite fabric? I was telling Mrs. Davies about the different weaves today. Is fabric like clothes? I like sparkly ones! Like my fairy dress. Yes, exactly! Fabric  is  what clothes are made of. Sparkly fabrics are usually polyester, which is a plastic, actually. Not a natural fibre like cotton or wool. Wool comes from sheep! We saw sheep at Farmer Giles’s farm. They were fluffy. They were. And cotton comes from a plant. It’s much softer than polyester. Did you know silk comes from worms? Ewww! Worms?! It's true! Silkworms spin these amazing threads. It's how they make silk fabric. That’s gross. I’m inventing a legend about a metal that’s stronger than diamond. It’s called… Umbralite! Umbralite? That’s a good name! What does it do? It can break anything! Even bedrock! And it glows in the dark. And it can make you invisible. Ooh, can  I  have some Umbralite? To make a sparkly invisible dress! No! It's mine! It’s a super-secret metal. Only  I  can have it. Well, maybe if you share, you can both have it. Speaking of things that are good for you, did you both take your vitamins this morning? I did! It was orange and fizzy. I forgot. Can I take it now? Yes, go on. It'll give you super-powers… maybe not as good as Umbralite, but still! Stronger bones and everything. Now, back to Minecraft. What other resources do you think are really valuable? Emeralds! You can trade them for cool stuff! Redstone! You can make automatic doors and traps and… everything!

Honestly, I’m proper stressed about this essay. Like, proper. It’s on… well, it’s on Victorian literature, but it needs a feminist perspective and I just… I don’t  do  feminist perspectives. Right. That sounds rough. What’s the essay question then? Maybe I can help, even if it's just to bounce ideas off. It’s about how women are portrayed in the Brontë sisters’ novels. And it’s not just “are they portrayed well,” it’s like… dissecting patriarchal structures and blah blah blah. Honestly, it feels a million miles away from just enjoying a good story. Yeah, sounds a bit heavy. You always were better at the actual literature side, not all the… analysing. Remember when we did Shakespeare and you just  knew  all the lines? Aye, well, that was different. That was just remembering stuff. This is… like,  thinking  about thinking. It’s exhausting. You still playing the guitar, by the way? Haven’t heard you mention it in ages. Nah, not much. Been swamped with uni work, same as you, I suppose. Plus, the string snapped a couple of weeks ago and I haven’t gotten round to replacing it. It’s just… sat there, mocking me. Mocking you? That’s a bit dramatic, innit? Get a new string. You used to be obsessed. You were going to start a band! "The Rusty Sprockets" or something ridiculously named. Don't remind me. That was a phase. A very, very short-lived phase. Though I do miss it sometimes. It’s just… easier to watch Netflix, you know? Speaking of which, saw that documentary about… well, you won’t believe it. About that bloke, Jimmy Savile. Oh, God. Don’t. I can't even think about that. Makes my skin crawl. It’s awful, isn’t it? How people can… and get away with it for so long. It’s terrifying. Makes you question everything. And then you start… overthinking about everything, worrying about who you can trust. It's no wonder people are careful around everyone these days. It's just... awful. It is. Truly awful. We weren't kids ourselves when all that started coming out, were we? Still feels… wrong. Changes how you look at things, doesn't it? Honestly, I need a stronger drink. This shandy’s not cutting it. Tell you what, I’ll get the next round. And maybe we can talk about something… less horrible.

Seriously though, Montenegro? That’s…random. Like, why Montenegro? My Aunt Carol’s friend, Brenda, has a timeshare there. Offered it to us cheap. Apparently, it’s beautiful. Loads of mountains and beaches. Sounds…okay. Is it expensive to  get  there, though? Because “cheap timeshare” doesn’t cover flights and everything else. Yeah, that's the thing. It’s not exactly cheap to fly into Podgorica or whatever it’s called. But we’re looking at EasyJet, trying to find a bargain. Dad’s being optimistic, saying we can live off supermarket sandwiches for the next month to save up. Supermarket sandwiches all month? No thanks. I’d rather just… not go. You’re being dramatic. It’s just a bit of sacrifice. Although, supermarket sandwiches  are  pretty tragic. What about that Italian place on the high street? They do amazing pasta for like, six quid. Six quid a meal adds up, Liv. We're trying to fund a whole trip! And I’m still stuck on this EPQ. Seriously, ‘The Ethical Implications of Fast Fashion’? What even  is  that? Mr. Davies just chucked a bunch of readings at me and said “get on with it.” Sounds awful. Mine's way better – the history of skateboarding. Actual, interesting stuff. Though, finding primary sources is a pain. It’s mostly just old magazines and blurry YouTube videos. I'm doing mine on the representation of female characters in Shakespeare. Which is…fine. A lot of reading, obviously. But at least it’s something I actually care about. What about you, Jamie? Are you still struggling with all your A-Levels? It’s the Economics that’s killing me. Supply and demand, elasticity…it’s just endless graphs and numbers. I’m starting to think I should have dropped it and done Art instead. You’d be amazing at Art. Remember that giant drawing you did of Darth Vader in Year 9? That was epic. Yeah, well, Darth Vader doesn't exactly get me a place at university. Although, maybe there's a course in…Comic Book Illustration? That’s a bit of a jump from Economics, isn’t it? Have you even thought about what you want to  do  at uni? Honestly? No. Not really. I'm just trying to get through the EPQ and the A-Levels first. Then I can panic about the rest. What about you two? Any ideas? I’m leaning towards History.

Honestly, this kitchen is a disaster zone. Like, who leaves dirty dishes for  days ? It's grim. Tell me about it. I walked in earlier and nearly slipped on something… questionable. Honestly, I’m starting to think living in halls was cleaner. And that’s saying something. You both make it sound like a biohazard zone. It’s not  that  bad. Though I did find a rogue potato in the sink yesterday. A whole potato. My nan always says you gotta clean as you go. Says it’s the key to a happy life. Your nan sounds sensible. Mine just sends me passive-aggressive texts about how I should be saving more money. Like, thanks Mum, super helpful. Tuition fees, rent, food… where do you expect me to conjure cash from? Oh god, the money thing. Don't even get me started. I checked my bank account today and basically had enough left for ramen noodles for the rest of the month. Ramen noodles are a student staple, though, aren't they? It's practically a requirement for a degree. My parents are constantly asking about my budget. They’re convinced I’m living lavishly. My dad just keeps going on about how much I’m spending on energy drinks. Says I’ll rot my teeth. Mine's convinced I'm addicted to avocado toast. Like, I had it  once . Once! It was a treat. It's the principle of the thing, though, isn’t it? They think we have unlimited funds. It's the guilt trip, isn’t it? Like we’re somehow failing them by needing money to just, you know,  exist  as students. Right? My mum keeps bringing up how she worked two jobs while studying. Which is great for her, but times are different now, aren’t they? Rent's insane. Seriously. Did you hear about Sarah from the law course? Her landlord just hiked up the rent on her house by like, £150 a month! She’s having to get a second job. Fifteen quid a month? That's no joke. No way! That's ridiculous. I swear some landlords just make up prices. Speaking of ridiculous, have you guys seen Ben and Chloe arguing again? Oh god, what's it this time? Apparently, he ‘accidentally’ deleted all the photos from her phone. All of them. She’s absolutely fuming. Said he did it because he was ‘tidying up’.

Honestly, the kids are driving me round the bend with Christmas lists already. It’s only November! Leo wants a… a robotic dinosaur that  transforms  into a spaceship. Honestly! Where do they get these ideas? Oh, the lists. It never ends, does it? My grandchildren are the same. Little Amelia, she's eight, has requested a pony. A pony! I said, "Darling, where are we going to keep a pony in a semi-detached in Penarth?" She just shrugged and said, “In the garden, Grandma.” Oh, bless her! Leo’s just as practical. He said we could build a special ‘dinosaur pad’ in the garden. Apparently, robotic dinosaurs require dedicated outdoor space. They do, of course. It’s essential. Remember old Mrs. Higgins from the village? Her grandson wanted a llama for his birthday. A  llama . She nearly had a heart attack. Oh, I remember her! She was always such a character. Did she get him the llama? No, thankfully not. Her daughter put her foot down. Though I think the grandson spent the next six months sulking. Speaking of characters, have you heard anything from Sarah and Mark lately? I haven’t seen them since the summer. Not much. Sarah sent a Christmas card picture, looked like they were all having a lovely time in Thailand, though. Mark's been travelling a lot for work, apparently. Still doing that consultancy thing? That's the one. All over the place. He was telling me about a project in Dubai last time we spoke. Sounds exhausting. And Sarah’s still teaching, is she? She always loved that job. Yeah, still teaching little ones. She says it’s chaotic, but she wouldn’t trade it. She's brilliant with children. She’s thinking about doing a postgraduate course, something in special educational needs. That sounds like her. Always wanting to learn and help. Do you remember when she tried to teach old Mr. Davies to use a computer? Oh, goodness yes! That was a disaster. He thought the mouse was a real mouse and kept trying to shoo it away. And he kept calling the internet 'the information superhighway'! It was hilarious. You know, sometimes I miss those days. Simple things, good friends… This consultancy keeps me busy, but it's not the same as having a proper community around you. I know what you mean. Totnes is nice, but it takes a while to really feel settled.

So, how was the drive down? Any traffic nightmares? Not too bad, actually. A bit congested around Dartford, naturally. But nothing like I expected. Though, you wouldn’t believe how much that area’s changed. Everything’s…upmarket now. Loads of fancy coffee shops and those awful minimalist house builds. Crayford’s becoming unrecognisable. Really? I haven't been back in ages. Mum keeps sending photos - it  does  look different. All glass and steel. Remember old man Hemmings’ sweet shop? Gone, I presume? Demolished years ago. Replaced by a…a nail bar. Honestly. It’s a sign of the times, isn't it? Everyone wants their nails done, no one wants a humbug. You’re not wrong there. Did you see any of those new speed cameras they put up along the A2? Thought I might be getting a letter through any day now. Yeah, they're everywhere. They're really clamping down, apparently. A mate of mine got points last week, completely caught him out. Says they’re less about safety and more about revenue now. They’ll take your license for a sneeze. Typical. Right, so, work. How’s the call centre treating you? Still fielding complaints about broadband speeds? You have no idea. It's relentless. Honestly, I think I'm developing a twitch. People are…vocal, let's say. At least it's steady work. Trying to convince my manager I need a raise, though. No luck so far. Push for it! You deserve it. You've been there forever. I’m still loving the teaching, honestly. It’s chaotic, but rewarding. Just had a student email me to say she got into Uni. Felt pretty good. That’s brilliant! Proper feels-good stuff. You still thinking about moving to Brighton? Yeah, seriously considering it. Found a couple of promising flats. It’s just…a big step, you know? Leaving everything behind. But I need a change. I need the sea air. It'd be good for you. You always were a bit of a beach bum. Remember that trip to Tanzania? You spent the whole time sunbathing, while I was trying to photograph every bird in the national park. Hey, I did some sightseeing! Just…balanced it with crucial vitamin D intake. Speaking of which, I think I’ve put on a stone since I last saw you. Comfort eating lockdown got the better of me. You haven’t!

Honestly, the supermarket was  heaving . I just wanted milk and bread, and it took me twenty minutes to get through the checkout. Oh, don’t even. I braved it earlier for… well, I honestly can’t remember now. Something equally mundane. It’s always like that on a Saturday, isn't it? Everyone decided to do their big shop all at once. It's ridiculous. You'd think people had better things to do with their weekend. Did you see that article I sent you, the one about the PR stunt gone wrong with the influencer and the smoothie? The pineapple one? Yes! Absolutely disastrous. Trying to be edgy and ended up just looking…tone-deaf, I think is the word. She clearly hadn’t done any research into the company’s ethics. Exactly! It's just lazy PR, really. And then the backlash. Poor things. Though, you do wonder how these people get hired in the first place. It's horrifying, genuinely. It is. It speaks volumes about their internal comms, doesn't it? Like, what kind of briefing did they give her? Or did they not give her any at all? Probably none. Just ‘here’s some money, post this’. Honestly. It makes my job sound incredibly glamorous in comparison, doesn’t it? ‘Oh, you just lecture on Romantic poetry…’ Don’t undersell yourself. Romantic poetry  is  glamorous. And at least you’re dealing with Keats and Shelley, not trying to navigate the minefield of social media outrage. Speaking of glamorous… have you decided what you’re wearing to the gig on Friday? Ooh, good point. I was thinking maybe that black dress? The one with the lace? Though it might be a bit overdressed? It’s just The Static Hearts, not a full-blown orchestral concert. No, that’s perfect! It’s not  too  much. They’re a pretty cool band. Have you heard their new single? It's a bit different, more…synthesizer-heavy. I have! It’s growing on me. It’s not quite as raw as their earlier stuff, but it’s still good. Are we meeting anyone there? Just Liam and Chloe, as far as I know. I messaged them earlier, and they’re both up for it. We'll grab a drink beforehand at The Eagle and Child, shall we? Say around seven? Perfect. Seven at The Eagle and Child. That sounds lovely.

Right, so onions are softening nicely. Are you sure you don’t want a bit of garlic in this? It would be lovely with the tomatoes. No, no garlic tonight, please. My stomach's been a bit dodgy all day. Just keep it simple. Though, actually, simple is good. It’s been a long day. Fair enough. It’s just… everything feels a bit bland at the moment. Like the bathroom. Seriously, we  have  to do something about that shower curtain. It’s been looking sad for months. Sad shower curtain? You’re assigning emotions to bathroom fixtures now. Well, it’s true! It’s all faded and a bit mildewy. I was thinking maybe a nice navy blue? Or something with a subtle pattern? It would brighten the whole room up. Navy blue sounds… sensible. Though, let’s not get carried away with ‘brightening up’. Remember last time we tried to brighten the bathroom? The lime green tiles were a mistake. A  big  mistake. Okay, okay, point taken. No lime green. But seriously, the bathroom needs a little love. Maybe we could paint? Painting’s a whole undertaking. We’d have to move everything. It’d take a weekend. And honestly, the walls aren’t  that  bad. True, but new paint would make a difference. It’s just… I’ve been itching to do something creative lately. Everything’s been so… work, work, work. Transcribing endless interviews about sewage treatment plants is not exactly inspiring. Tell me about it. Another day spent wrestling with spreadsheets and endless emails. Honestly, I sometimes feel like my job is just anticipating the next fire to put out. Speaking of things that take ages… how's the bean bag coming along? Still knitting? Oh, don’t even ask. It's…slow going. I'm on the sixth panel. It’s going to take me until Christmas at this rate. I underestimated the sheer volume of yarn required. Six panels? Wow. That  is  slow going. It's a good job you’re not aiming for a bean bag sofa, then. Don’t even suggest it! I might have to abandon the whole project. Although, a bean bag sofa  would  be amazing… No, focus. One bean bag. One incredibly slow-knitted bean bag. Right well, tomatoes are in. Let's let this simmer for a bit and then maybe we can have a proper look at shower curtains online?

Right well I think that's enough of that then. Didn’t realise it was getting so late. It does fly by doesn’t it? Especially when we’re just chatting. Indeed. Good to catch up properly, you two. It's been a while since we all sat down like this. It has, hasn’t it? Not since… well, since before everything really, I suppose. Don’t start on that again, Arthur. We all know. Just saying. Everything feels… different now. Even a cup of tea isn’t quite the same. That's age, I suspect. Teas always tasted better when you didn’t have to worry about your prostate, eh? Oh, you two! Always with the medical complaints. Honestly. Well, it  is  a fact of life, isn't it? Comes with the territory. Although I reckon yours would still be going strong, Margaret, you always were a tough one. Flattery will get you everywhere, Arthur. Though my knees disagree. They haven’t been the same since that trip to Cornwall. Speaking of trips, did you two ever manage to sort out that weekend away you were talking about? To the seaside, was it? Oh, that. No. It just… fell by the wayside. Too much bother with the arrangements, really. And then the weather turned, and… well, it wasn’t worth the hassle. It wasn't just the weather, Arthur. You were worrying about leaving the house unattended. It's just sensible to think ahead, isn't it? You never know who might be about. You two and your concerns! Honestly, you'd think you lived in a hotbed of criminal activity. This is a quiet village, for goodness sake. That’s what they all say, David. Until it happens to them. Exactly! You can’t be too careful. I read in the paper just the other day about… Oh, here we go. Arthur’s news round-up. It’s important to be informed! It was about a burglary in a village not fifty miles from here. They took everything! Even the silver candlesticks. Oh dear. That’s awful. Still, doesn’t mean we have to live in fear. Maybe we should just concentrate on something happier. Like… cake? I made a Victoria sponge this morning. Now you’re talking! A Victoria sponge sounds excellent. Especially with a good cup of tea. Right. Cake. That's a sensible idea. As long as it doesn’t have too many currants in it.

Honestly, the price of sprouts this year is scandalous. Scandalous! I nearly didn’t bother. Sprouts are always scandalous around Christmas, aren’t they? It’s some sort of festive conspiracy. They know we feel obliged. It's true! It's like they add a Christmas surcharge to everything green and vaguely vegetable-related. I saw a jar of cranberry sauce – a  jar  – for nearly five pounds. Five pounds! You can make it yourself for a quid. Exactly! And it tastes nicer. Honestly, people just… are they that lazy? It’s convenience, love. People are time-poor. Plus, marketing. They convince you you  need  the pre-made, expensive version. Speaking of convenience, has anyone sorted out a food delivery slot for Christmas Eve? I was hoping to avoid a supermarket scrum. I tried, darling. They’re all booked. Solid. I looked at Tesco, Sainsbury’s, even Waitrose. Nothing. Blast. I was relying on that. I was hoping to get a nice ham, and all the trimmings delivered. I’m happy to brave the shops if it means we get a decent Christmas dinner. I’m fairly strategic in my supermarket attacks. You are, aren't you? You're like a tactical shopper. All angles covered. We might need your skills, Fiona. Seriously. I'm picturing hand-to-hand combat over the last turkey crown. What about going to that farm shop near Ashford, Claire? They usually have really good stuff, and it’s less chaotic than the big supermarkets. Oh, that’s a good shout, Dad! They do amazing cheeses too. Although, getting there on Christmas Eve might be a nightmare with traffic. True. But Ashford isn’t as bad as, say, Brighton on a Bank Holiday. Speaking of which, are we still thinking of going to Brighton for New Year’s? I’m up for it. It's always a good laugh, and a nice change of scene. Although I’m not sure I can face the crowds. We could always try a weeknight. Less of a crush if we go on the 2nd or 3rd. That’s a good idea. Plus, it’s more affordable. Hotels are extortionate over New Year. It’s just nice to get away for a bit. I feel like we’ve barely had a family holiday this year. Work’s been… well, you know. Utterly manic. It’s always manic, isn’t it? Especially this time of year.

So, have you been here in Northern Cyprus long then? I only arrived a few days ago, it's lovely so far. Oh, a few days! No, no, I've been coming here for… well, nearly twenty years now. My wife, bless her, discovered it and we’ve been wintering here ever since. Though, she passed a couple of years ago, so now I just come on my own. Oh, I’m so sorry to hear that. It must be lovely to have those memories though, coming back to a place you both enjoyed. It is, it is. Keeps me going, really. Though it’s not quite the same without her nagging me about the sun cream! She was very strict about that. I get a bit pink, you see. Used to be a right ginger as a boy. I can imagine. I’m already feeling the sun, even just sitting here. It’s a world away from Dorset this time of year. Have you explored much of the island? Oh, bits and bobs. I'm not one for rushing around, you see. Not like some of these tour groups that whizz about. I’ve done the usual – Nicosia’s interesting, if a bit… well, divided. Famagusta’s quite haunting, actually, walking through Varosha. Bit spooky. I've heard about Varosha. It sounds…intense. Is it easy to get around without a car? I was thinking of relying on taxis and dolmuşes. Dolmuşes are brilliant, absolutely brilliant. They're like little minibuses, very frequent. Taxis are alright, but they can add up. You will get ripped off if you don't agree a price beforehand, mind you. They think everyone’s a tourist. Good to know! Always a risk, isn't it? I was reading about the Karpaz peninsula, it sounds absolutely beautiful, very unspoiled. Oh, the Karpaz! Wonderful. Wild donkeys everywhere. Honestly, you can be driving along and suddenly there’s a donkey just… standing in the road, looking at you. They’re quite cheeky, too, will try and steal your sandwiches if you’re not careful. I can picture it! That sounds delightful. I was thinking of maybe taking a cookery course while I’m here, learn a bit about Cypriot cuisine. Good idea! The food's fantastic. Lots of meze, of course. And halloumi – you’ll be eating halloumi until it comes out of your ears! Though, be careful where you buy it.

Honestly, the students were dreadful today. Just absolutely dreadful. Didn’t read the assigned chapters, kept asking questions we’d already covered… it was exhausting. Oh, no. Really? Mine were… okay. A bit chatty, as usual, but at least they’d done the reading. Though, Liam tried to argue with me about Foucault  again . Honestly, you’d think he’d learn. Liam? Still? That’s… dedication, I suppose. Or stubbornness. Probably both. I swear, sometimes I feel like I'm just shouting into the void. They just glaze over. It’s frustrating, isn’t it? You put all this effort into preparing the lectures, trying to make it engaging, and then… nothing. It feels like a waste of time. Exactly! And it’s not even like they’re deliberately being difficult. They just… don’t seem to  want  to engage. I’m starting to wonder if I’m just a terrible lecturer. Don’t be silly. You’re brilliant. They’re just… students. It happens. Remember what Professor Davies used to say? “You win some, you lose some, and some just want a degree.” Oh, Davies. He was a cynic. A lovable cynic, but still. Gosh, look at the smog today. It’s even worse than yesterday. Isn’t it awful? I could taste it on the walk over. It’s ridiculous, really. You’d think they’d be doing more to tackle it. I saw an article about how… Let’s not dissect the environmental policies of China just now, shall we? My brain is already fried from battling undergraduates. Fair enough. Sorry. Just… it’s depressing, isn't it? Especially after being back in London for the conference. The air felt so clean. It did. I miss proper green spaces. And clean air. Though, the conference was good, wasn't it? It was nice to catch up with Sarah and Ben. It was. Sarah was telling me about their little one finally sleeping through the night. Apparently, it’s a miracle. Oh, fantastic! That's lovely. Maybe we should try and arrange something with them soon, have them over for dinner? Once I’ve recovered from this teaching trauma, of course. That’s a great idea. We could do a proper roast. Or maybe try that Sichuan hotpot recipe you found? Ooh, the hotpot sounds good. But maybe after a  very  quiet weekend. I just need to recharge. And avoid thinking about Foucault and unread chapters.

Right, so I was thinking, shall we do a big salad with this chicken? It's a bit boring just on its own, isn't it? Sounds good to me. Loads of stuff in it – tomatoes, cucumber, peppers… Maybe some avocado if we’ve got any that aren’t completely rock solid. Ooh, yes, avocado would be amazing! I can chop everything up if you want, Mum. I’m pretty quick. Oh, that would be lovely, thank you, darling. Saves me wrestling with the knife while trying to supervise Dad not adding too much chilli to everything. Hey! I just like a little kick! Speaking of which, did you see those photos I sent from the garden earlier? The chillies are actually starting to turn red. I did! They look amazing, Dad. You’ve actually managed to grow something edible this year. Progress! Don't be cheeky. I reckon I'll have a bumper crop. Enough to make a proper chilli jam, maybe. Oh, that would be nice. Though last time you made chilli jam, you nearly set the kitchen on fire trying to sterilize the jars. A slight exaggeration, dear. There was a bit of smoke, granted. But everything was fine! Famous last words. Honestly, it's a miracle this kitchen is still standing. Well, we've survived so far. Right, salad ingredients are out. Any thoughts on lunch tomorrow? I was thinking of going into town, maybe that new Italian place everyone's talking about? That sounds rather nice. As long as they don’t play that opera music too loud. It gives me a headache. I'm in! I've been needing a proper pasta fix. Any plans for tonight, apart from more culinary adventures? I was thinking of finally starting that new detective series on TV. The one everyone at work’s been raving about – “Happy Valley”? Oh, yes! I’ve heard good things about that. Quite gritty apparently. Ooh, perfect! I could snuggle up with a blanket and watch that. It’s been a pretty hectic day at work trying to finish off those copy decks. Oh, how was work, dear? Anything interesting happen? Not especially, just the usual deadlines looming. Though Mr Henderson did ask me if I'd considered a career in stand-up comedy. Apparently, my email subject lines are "unexpectedly amusing." No! Really? That’s brilliant. Oh, he always was a bit of a character.

Honestly, this new bus route is a joke. It’s supposed to make getting across town easier, but it just adds another twenty minutes onto everything. Really? I haven’t taken it yet. I usually cycle, but I might need to start relying on buses more when the weather turns properly nasty. What’s the problem with it? It goes completely the wrong way round! To get to the shops near Mill Road, you have to go all the way out towards Histon first. It makes no sense. And it stops like, every five minutes, which is supposed to be good, but it just means it’s constantly full of people. That sounds… inefficient. Cambridge is bad enough for traffic without buses making it worse. Did you see that protest outside Cambridge University Press bookshop yesterday? Oh yeah! I walked past it on the way home. Something about divestment, wasn’t it? A student chained themselves to the front doors, apparently. That’s what I heard. It caused a proper scene. A few people were getting really angry, trying to get in to buy books. I mean, I get the sentiment, but blocking access to a bookshop seems a bit… counterproductive. Exactly! Like, who are you trying to convince? People who are already buying books? I’ve always thought Cambridge students are quite vocal, though. Compared to Durham, it’s a completely different vibe. Oh, Durham? Is it really that different? I always pictured it as being super traditional and reserved. It is. Everything is very… collegiate. Everyone sticks to their college, and there’s a lot of emphasis on formal dinners and tradition. Cambridge is a lot more open, I think. More mixing between courses and colleges. People just seem a lot more… out there. That makes sense. Different types of universities attract different types of people, I suppose. I always felt a bit out of place at Imperial, actually. Everyone was so focused on their studies. I didn’t really fit in with the hardcore engineering crowd. See, that's the same with me and Oxford. I visited a friend there once and it just felt… cold. Everyone was so ambitious and driven. I felt like I needed to relax and breathe a bit! It's funny how much university shapes you, isn't it? Even just the environment and the people you meet. It's more than just the degree.

Honestly, the portions at that pub were ridiculous. I felt awful afterwards. So much butter on everything. You always say that, but you always finish it! Remember that lasagne in Keswick? You said you were going to leave half, and… Okay, okay, I have a weakness for carbs. Sue me. How was your weekend, Mum? Did you manage to get out at all? Oh, it was peaceful enough. A bit of gardening, a lot of reading. Though young Finn called, wanting to know if I could help him with his geometry. Honestly, the things they teach them now…it's not geometry, it's some kind of spatial reasoning nonsense. Finn's a bright spark though. He’ll be fine. It's just a different approach, that’s all. Different, is it? It’s like they’re deliberately trying to confuse the poor children. They can’t even memorise their times tables anymore! Everything’s a “visual aid” and a “learning journey”. Times tables  are  pretty brutal though, aren't they? I remember my mum drilling me until my eyes glazed over. Mum didn’t drill us! She always said it was about understanding the concepts, not rote memorisation. Well, times tables are foundational! You can’t build a house without foundations, and you can't do mathematics without knowing your times tables. It’s…logical! It's amazing how passionate you still are about maths, even in retirement. It was my life! Though honestly, having a bit of peace and quiet is rather lovely. Speaking of which, how's Sarah? Is she still seeing that…what was his name… the artist? Ben? Yeah, they’re still going strong. He came up last week, actually. They did that hike up Scafell Pike. Scafell Pike?! In February? Are they mad? Apparently not. He’s pretty outdoorsy. They were all geared up, layers and everything. They had a lovely time. Mum, you wouldn’t believe the photos! Honestly, these young people. No sense. Reminds me of your father. Always off climbing mountains, or sailing, or something equally reckless. He always said it was about the challenge. A challenge? It was about showing off! He always had to be the best at everything. Well, he  was  rather competitive. Speaking of challenges, I’m trying to teach Leo some basic French. It's…a struggle. He keeps saying “Bonjour” to the dog. Oh, bless him! That’s adorable.

Honestly, it’s just… endless concrete, isn’t it? I mean, it's nice to  see  the river, but they’ve just built all the way along it. It’s a shame. It is a bit, yeah. Though, that’s a good view of the O2, isn’t it? Still looks a bit like a giant golf ball plopped down. A very expensive golf ball. I still don’t understand why they put it  there . It just dominates everything. And the traffic around it is horrific. Glad we don’t have a car, honestly. Think of trying to get anywhere near here on a Saturday night. You’re right. We’d be stuck for hours. Though, I do sometimes envy people who can just… hop in the car and go. Remember when we tried to convince your brother to drive us to Cornwall? Oh, don't remind me! He was having  none  of it. Said his back couldn’t take it. Honestly, it’s just easier to wrestle the kids onto a train. Though, this year, even that feels… daunting. Trying to coordinate everyone’s schedules is a nightmare. Tell me about it. Everyone’s so busy. Are you still thinking about Brittany? I know you were looking at gîtes. Yeah, Brittany's still on the cards, if I can actually book one that isn’t already snatched up. It’s just… packing for a family of five is exhausting. And then someone inevitably forgets their favourite toy and it's a full-scale meltdown. You’re a saint, you are. Seriously. My sister went to America last year, and she was complaining about all the recipes being in cups and ounces. Said she couldn’t convert anything. Oh, that’s awful! I hate American measurements. It’s so imprecise. “A dash of this, a pinch of that…” What does that even  mean ? Give me grams and millilitres any day. It's just… inherently illogical. Exactly! It’s like they actively try to make it difficult. It makes you wonder, doesn’t it? Why do we cling to these arbitrary systems? Why do we define things the way we do? Now you’re getting philosophical on me. Honestly, sometimes I just want a cup of tea and for everyone to be quiet for five minutes. Is that too much to ask? No, not at all. A very reasonable request. Look, there’s the Cutty Sark.

Honestly, this rain is relentless. It’s been going for days. I feel like I’m living in a perpetual grey film. Tell me about it! I had to cycle to work this morning, and I was soaked through before I even  got  to the first client’s house. My waterproofs aren’t waterproof anymore, I swear. Oh, you poor thing! I wish I could offer you a lift, but with the kids… it’s just chaos getting them anywhere these days. Speaking of chaos, sports day is next week, and honestly, I'm dreading it. Oh no! Is Leo excited? Excited doesn’t even  begin  to cover it. He's been practising his running in the living room, knocking over everything in his path. And Maisie just wants to know if she can wear her princess dress.
