It’s going to be… an experience. They grow up so fast, don’t they? Seems like yesterday Leo was just learning to walk. Remember when he used to cling onto that teddy bear, Barnaby? Oh, Barnaby! He was ancient. So patched up he barely resembled a bear anymore. We really should have gotten rid of him years ago. Don’t you dare say that! Leo’s still attached to him, even if Barnaby is falling apart at the seams. Honestly, he'd be devastated. I’m thinking of taking them to Build-a-Bear soon, maybe that will distract from sports day. Oh, good idea! Maisie would  love  that. She’s obsessed with making things look pretty. Although knowing her, she’ll want to cover whatever bear she makes in glitter. Everywhere. Oh, glitter is the bane of my life. You find it for weeks afterwards. It’s like it multiplies! Speaking of things I find everywhere… have you managed to get Finn properly potty-trained yet? It's… a work in progress. We have good days and bad days. Mostly bad days, if I’m being honest. He seems to think the bathroom floor is an acceptable alternative. I’m seriously considering just sticking to nappies forever. Oh, I remember those days! It's exhausting. You just feel like you're constantly cleaning up. Remember how Mum used to say it was just a phase? She always did! “It’s just a phase!” That woman drives me mad sometimes. But honestly, she’s right most of the time. Still, wishing she wouldn’t offer unsolicited advice every five minutes.

Right, so, genuinely, what feels… good? Not ‘should’ feel good, not what looks good on paper, but what actually excites you for the next, I don’t know, six months? Beyond just surviving this house-sitting gig, because, let's be honest, palm trees are nice, but it’s not a life plan. No, it’s definitely not. Okay. Well, the PGCE feels… settled. I like teaching. It’s challenging, obviously, but I genuinely enjoy it. I think… I think I'd like to look at doing some more training? Maybe a specialism? Something in inclusion, perhaps? We talked about that, didn’t we? We did. And you’d be brilliant at that. It fits perfectly with your patience and… well, your general goodness, basically. Goodness is a skill in a classroom. Is that realistically achievable alongside everything else though? Thinking about marking, planning... It would be a bit of a push. But the school’s supportive. They offer funding for some courses. I’d need to look into it properly. What about you? Still obsessed with building this… empire? Empire is a strong word. Let’s call it a moderately successful online business. Honestly? It’s plateauing. I'm getting… bored. I think I need a project, a challenge. Remember Liam and Chloe talking about expanding their marketing agency? They were sniffing around for someone with my skillset. Oh, seriously? That's a tempting offer, isn’t it? Working with them would be… fun. Less solitary than what you're doing now, at least. And potentially more lucrative. But it would mean shifting everything again. Another new venture. Exactly. That’s what’s holding me back. The thought of ripping everything up and starting over is exhausting. But staying where I am feels… stagnating. It’s a proper dilemma. What about… us? Longer term? We haven’t really talked about… you know. Kids. You mean. Yes. It’s always looming, isn’t it? I… I want them. I do. But the timing never feels right. And with me being a teacher, and you flitting between projects… it feels selfish to bring someone into that. Flitting is harsh! I’m a dynamic entrepreneur! Okay, okay, fair enough. Look, if I joined Liam and Chloe, it would give us some financial stability. A proper base. We could… actually plan properly. Research schools, think about childcare… That's true. It would be a lot less stressful.

Honestly though, I still can't get over how different your accent is getting, Liam. It’s like, subtly shifting every week. Am I? Is it that bad? I've just been spending a lot of time with folks from Manchester, you know? It rubs off. No, it's not  bad , it's just… noticeable. You’re starting to sound like you've swallowed a tram. A tram! That’s brilliant! It’s alright, though. Still recognisably you. It’s just… less Warrington. Fair enough. I'll try to tone it down. It's not deliberate, honestly. Remember when Mark tried to do a Scouse accent after that stag do in Liverpool? That was a disaster. Oh god, don’t remind me. I thought I was going to have to stage an intervention. He genuinely believed he was mimicking a Liverpudlian. It was like watching a car crash in slow motion. Speaking of disasters, has anyone seen Ben lately? I haven’t heard from him in ages. He was talking about starting some crazy Pokémon Go challenge. Like, catching every single Pokémon in a fifty-mile radius. Think he's holed up somewhere remote, battling virtual creatures. Seriously? That sounds… exhausting. Classic Ben. Always with the extreme hobbies. Remember when he tried to build a fully functional replica of the Millennium Falcon out of cardboard boxes? And the council had to get involved because it was blocking the pavement! Good times. Say, anyone fancy popping to the shop? I'm craving chocolate. After Eights specifically. Oh, go on then. You're always getting us snacks. I’ll chip in. I'm good, thanks. I’m still full from that massive lunch. You know, it’s weird. I used to  love  After Eights, and now they just taste… artificial. It’s an age thing. Your taste buds are evolving. It’s a sign of maturity, darling. Like discerning a good Pinot Grigio from a mediocre one. Speaking of evolving, has anyone tried those new noise-cancelling headphones? Apparently, they’re amazing. They’re pricey though, aren't they? I'm still rocking my ancient earbuds. Actually, I think the wire's about to snap. My Fitbit keeps telling me I need to move more. It's so judgemental! I’m trying, okay Fitbit?! I walked to the bus stop. A whole thirty yards! Olympic effort. Honestly though, the amount of sugar and crap I’ve eaten since uni started… terrifying.

Well, that was a dreadful football match wasn’t it? Absolutely dreadful. Couldn’t understand a thing the commentator was saying either, mumbling away like he had a mouthful of marbles. Oh, don’t start on the football, Arthur. You say that every single week, regardless of whether you’ve actually  watched  the match! It  was  a bit of a slog, Dad. Not exactly a thrilling spectacle. At least the roast was good, Mum. Honestly, your Yorkshire puddings are legendary. They really are. You've outdone yourself, honestly. Best Yorkshire puddings I’ve had in ages. Oh, you say that every time, you two! Just trying to be polite, are you? I’m just glad everyone’s here. It’s nice to have a proper family dinner for once. Speaking of proper, have you seen what that Sunak’s up to now? Another tax hike. Honestly, it’s ridiculous. They’re bleeding us dry. Dad, please, not politics at the dinner table. Let’s try and have one meal without arguing about the government. Yeah, maybe we can avoid that this time? It’s nice to just… relax. Though, I did hear a rumour about potential strikes in universities if they don’t address the pay issues. It’s getting a bit tense at work. Oh, you too? It's the same where I am. Everyone’s worried. We're trying to organise something, but it’s slow going. It’s the administration, you see. Always the administration. University strikes? Oh dear. Sounds stressful. Are you managing alright, love? You do work so hard. I’m alright, Mum. Just… a lot. Marking essays, preparing lectures, and now potentially picketing. It feels like there’s never a quiet moment. Reminds me of when I used to work on the farm. Never a moment's peace! Always something needing doing. Though, mind you, at least you’ve got a pension these days. I never saved enough, always thought I’d have more time. You shouldn't worry too much about that, Arthur. You always looked after us all. Besides, we're happy to help out. Exactly. And we need to start planning for your birthday, Arthur. Seventy-eight, is it? What sort of fuss do you want to make? Fuss? Oh, don’t make a fuss. Just a quiet evening, a nice pint, and a bit of telly. That’ll do for me.

Honestly, I’m seriously considering just… chucking it all in. What? Like, dropping out? Properly? Yeah. I just… I don’t know what I’m doing here. Everyone else seems to have a plan, a career path, something. I’m just… existing. And accumulating debt. Oh, Liv. That’s rough. But you’re good at your course, aren’t you? History of Art? You got like, a first on that essay last term. Yeah, but enjoying something and being good at it are two different things, aren’t they? It's just… not sparking joy, as Marie Kondo would say. And all this reading, the essays… it feels pointless. I get that. It’s hard when it doesn't feel like it’s leading anywhere. But you’ve come this far. Remember how excited you were about uni? About getting away from Liverpool? I was escaping my auntie Brenda, mostly. She meant well, but she’d constantly ask me what I was going to  do  with a degree in art history. Like I needed a practical skill to justify existing. Brenda sounds… Brenda. You’ve always been creative though. Remember when we were kids, and you’d make those elaborate outfits for your Barbies out of, like, curtains and tea towels? Oh god, don’t remind me! Mum was furious about the curtains. She said I was ruining them. I thought I was a fashion designer! And you were always building forts. Massive ones, in the garden. You'd spend days in there. It was a simpler time. No essays, no student loans. Just sticks and blankets. Speaking of simpler times, look at your shoes. What about them? They’re… coated. In something. Mud? Is it mud? Probably. I walked across campus after it rained. It was a swamp. They look like you’ve been digging for gold. You're leaving muddy footprints everywhere. Dramatic much? Anyway, back to my impending life crisis… Have you ever considered dropping out? Briefly. After first year, when I realised how much work a psychology degree actually involved. But my mum would have killed me. She’s always been so proud of me being at uni. Honestly, it's a bit stifling. See, mine would probably just be relieved I didn’t become a performance artist or something equally unconventional. She's always wanted me to have a ‘sensible’ job. Sensible is overrated. Hey, your name is interesting.

Honestly, this risotto is amazing. You were right to recommend this place. Though, I'm feeling slightly judged for ordering it – everyone else seems to have gone for something lighter. Oh, don't worry about it! It  is  proper comfort food. And honestly, you deserve a proper treat. How’s work been? Still battling spreadsheets and project deadlines? You have  no  idea. It's been manic. We’ve got this new client, huge contract, and the scope just keeps creeping. It’s like, every time I think I’ve nailed the plan, someone adds another ‘essential’ deliverable. I’m seriously considering learning to say ‘no’ in five different languages. Oh, bless you. The eternal project coordinator struggle. I feel you. Pearson is… Pearson. Lots of meetings about meetings. It's all very corporate, which is fine, but sometimes I just want to scream into the void. Though, I did manage to sneak in a proposal for a new social media campaign focused on student wellbeing - which is cool. Oh, that's brilliant! See, you're making a difference. That’s what I need to remember – trying to find the little wins. Speaking of which… how’s Ben? Last I heard, he was thinking about a career change? He did it! He actually did it. He handed in his notice last month. He's enrolled on a coding bootcamp, ironically enough. Says he wants to build apps, be his own boss, the whole shebang. No way! That's huge! I'm so proud of him. He was so stuck in that dead-end job for so long. Is he… terrifyingly excited? Terrifyingly is the word. He’s all energy and enthusiasm, bouncing off the walls. It's brilliant, but also slightly exhausting to be around! He's already talking about pitching ideas for the next 'unicorn' app. He's a bit delusional, honestly. He always was. That’s what I love about him. Okay, this is a terrible segue, but… are you seeing anyone at the moment? You mentioned last time you were still 'exploring options'. Oh god, don't even. It's been a disaster. I went on three dates last month, each more spectacularly awful than the last. One was a conspiracy theorist, one talked about his ex for the entire evening, and the third just… kept ordering more and more expensive wine and trying to impress me with his wealth.

Right, now then, I’m having a look for that bird feeder, aren’t I? The one with the suet pellets in. Mum, you bought one last week. It’s still in the garage. Did I? Oh, did I now? Well, that’s a waste of money, isn't it? I could have sworn the squirrels had already demolished it. They’re crafty, those squirrels. They haven’t touched it. I checked. You just hadn’t put it up. Well, I’m looking for a  better  one. One they can’t get into. A squirrel-proof one. They’re advertised on the internet, you know. Yeah, but they never  actually  work, do they? Squirrels always find a way. Oh, don’t be so pessimistic. There’s one on eBay, looks like a cage around it. Right, let’s see… how much is postage? Oh, that’s a rip-off. Six pound ninety-nine for postage! What are they playing at? It’s usually cheaper on Amazon, isn’t it? Amazon… yes, but I don’t always trust Amazon these days. Had a rogue delivery once. Said it was delivered, but it wasn’t. Turned up three days later. That happens, though. Sometimes the drivers scan it too early. Still… it’s the principle. eBay, you deal with a person, you can message them if there’s a problem. Amazon, you’re just talking to a robot. It’s usually quicker though, isn’t it? Prime delivery and all that. Quick doesn’t always mean good, lad. I'm after quality. Right, let’s have a look at the reviews for this eBay one. Hmm, mixed. “Easy to assemble,” says one. “Squirrels chewed through it in an hour,” says another. See? Told you! So you'll just stick with the one in the garage then? No… no. I’ll keep looking. There must be one. A discerning bird feeder for discerning birds. Now, let me filter by ‘highest rated seller’… and look at this one. Solid metal. That might do it. It’s a bit pricey, mind. Twenty-five pound. Is that including postage? No… another four ninety-nine. Oh, for goodness sake. These people are robbing us blind. So, you’re still going to buy it? Well… it  looks  sturdy. And I’m determined the squirrels aren’t going to win. Right. Add to basket. Now, don’t tell your father.

So, how was the journey back then? Dreadful, I expect? It was… lengthy. Honestly, the M11 was a car park for about an hour near Stansted. Everyone clearly thought escaping London for the weekend was a brilliant idea. Sounds about right. Always the same. More people on the roads than sense, I say. Did you at least have a good weekend away with everyone? It was nice. Really nice. A bit too much rosé for some, perhaps. Aunt Carol was doing a particularly good impression of a flamingo by Sunday afternoon. Oh, Carol. She hasn’t changed then. Always did like a tipple, your aunt. Not a bad sort, though. A bit… boisterous. She's harmless. Just exuberant. It was good to catch up with everyone though. It feels like ages since we’ve all been together properly. It does, doesn't it? Time just runs away from you. Feels like yesterday you were a little thing, running around my feet. Now you're off working, production controller, is it? Sounds important. It's…a job. It’s busy, anyway. We’re launching a new product line next month, so it’s all a bit hectic at the moment. Lots of late nights and spreadsheet staring. Spreadsheets, eh? Sounds awful. Used to hate numbers myself. Always preferred a good book. Still do, even if my eyes aren’t what they used to be. You should come and visit more often, Grandad. We could have a proper catch-up, you could tell me all your stories. I would like that. I really would. It's just… getting out and about isn't as easy as it used to be, you know? And your mum, she worries. Doesn’t want me travelling on the buses on my own. Mum worries about everything. It’s her default setting. But I can come and get you, easily. Next weekend maybe? We could go for a nice lunch. Next weekend… that sounds good. Very good indeed. Let me check with your mum first though, don’t want to cause any fuss. I’ll text her now, actually. She’s probably already planning our lives for the next six months anyway. Oh, she’s replied. “Yes, that’s lovely! But please make sure he has his coat.” See? Told you. Always the coat. Always the coat. Alright, it’s a date then. Lunch next weekend. You choose where you want to go.

Right, so we’re actually nailing down Christmas plans now? Seriously? It feels a bit early, doesn’t it? No way! It’s practically upon us. If we want to do anything remotely interesting, we need to book things  now . Like, flights. Flights on Christmas Day? You’re mental. Who wants to spend Christmas Day in an airport? She's got a point. It's barbaric. Are you thinking of going somewhere, Liv? Well, my auntie in Melbourne keeps hinting she'd love us to come. It would mean flying on the twenty-fifth, admittedly, but imagine Christmas Day on Bondi Beach instead of… grey London? Bondi sounds a bit better than…well, anything here to be honest. Though, I’m perfectly happy just chilling here with you lot. Less hassle. I’m hosting this year, remember? So, you’re all coming  here . And I’m not flying anywhere. I’ve already started planning the menu. It’s ambitious. Oh, god. Ambitious how? Last year’s ambitious involved setting fire to the Brussels sprouts. That wasn’t my fault! The oven’s temperamental. This year, I’m going full-on Christmas. Turkey, goose, ham… the works. Plus, I'm attempting a Buche de Noel. A Buche de Noel? You’re brave. That’s a proper challenge. I can help with the carving. I'm a professional, remember? Years of slicing prosciutto. A turkey is nothing. Speaking of things getting sliced… did anyone see that story online? About the deer that wandered onto the M25 and got…well. Oh, dear god. No. Don’t tell me. Apparently, three cars swerved, one ended up in a ditch. Horrible. It makes you think, doesn't it? Driving around at Christmas. It does. Though, you're more likely to hit a fox around here than a deer. Saw one digging through bins on the way back from work last night. Utterly brazen. They're smart, foxes. Very smart. They know when people are feeling generous with leftovers. Right. Leftovers. That’s another thing. I’m ordering a massive ham, partly so we have enough for sandwiches for days. And partly because I fully intend to give bits to the foxes. You’re encouraging them! You’ll have a whole gang of foxes camped out in your garden. It’s Christmas. A little fox-feeding is allowed. Have you guys started thinking about presents yet? I need to get something for my nephew.

Honestly, I still can't place where she's from. That woman at the petrol station. It wasn’t London, definitely not Birmingham… maybe somewhere around Bristol? She just had… one of those vaguely South West accents, didn’t she? Like it could be anywhere between Devon and Gloucestershire. It’s the way they all kind of blend. I thought she sounded a bit Welsh, actually. Not full-on Cardiff, but like the bits closer to the English border. Welsh? Really? I didn’t pick up any of the lilting thing. Maybe I’m just bad at accents. You're the editor, aren’t you? You should be able to pinpoint these things. I’m good at  written  language, Leo, not necessarily spoken. And accents are deceptive. It’s all about subtle vowel sounds. Plus, people often modify their accents slightly. Yeah, like, I subconsciously tone down the 'Birmingham' a bit when I'm further south. Don't want to be stereotyped as a Peaky Blinder or something. Fair enough. Though you’d need a flat cap and a lot more aggression for that. Speaking of Birmingham… this car’s giving me flashbacks to Dad’s old Rover. Remember that thing? Oh God, the Rover. The one that smelled permanently of stale biscuits and pipe tobacco? And rattled like a box of spanners every time you went over 30. It was a medical miracle it actually stayed on the road. Exactly! This is… slightly more reliable. Though I’m still getting used to the automatic. Feels a bit weird letting it do all the work. You’ll get used to it. It’s far less stressful on a long drive. So, are we still planning on swapping drivers halfway? I’m happy to take a stint. Yeah, that's the plan. I reckon around Leicester? We can grab a coffee or something. Unless you and Jamie want to just push on and get the whole thing done in one go? I'm good to swap. I’ve been staring at a screen all day, my eyes need a break. And frankly, your music choices are starting to grate on me. Hey! This is a classic 80s playlist! Show some respect. Plus, you were happily singing along to Spandau Ballet ten minutes ago. I was being ironic. Always. Look, Leicester sounds good. We can check the traffic around there and decide. Is the sat nav set for the right address, Leo?

Right, so have you guys actually  listened  to the new Arctic Monkeys album? Like, properly listened? Yeah, bits of it. It's alright, innit? Bit different though. Not as good as  AM , obviously. Different is an understatement. It’s… lounge music. Arctic Monkeys doing lounge music. I don’t get it. It’s like Alex Turner decided to become his own grandad. Exactly! It’s so slow and… conversational. Like he’s just reading a poem over some jazzy chords. It feels wrong. I kinda liked the lyrics, though. They’re still clever, yeah? That bit about the satellite dishes and the… what was it, the disco lights? The lyrics are fine, I guess. But they don't  hit  the same without the energy, you know? It’s like taking the engine out of a Ferrari and just admiring the paint job. That’s a good analogy, actually. Speaking of stuff that doesn’t quite work… have you seen the new  Ant-Man  movie? Oh god, yeah. It was… a lot. Quantum Realm stuff is always a bit much, isn’t it? Like, they just make up physics as they go along. Seriously! I was trying to follow the time travel stuff and my brain just short-circuited. It’s like, if you're going to lean into the science, you have to at least pretend to understand the basic principles! Right? They were talking about multiverses and shrinking and expanding and it was just… chaotic. Like a GCSE physics lesson gone horribly wrong. At least Paul Rudd’s still funny, though. He’s the only reason I stayed awake for the second half. True. He’s a national treasure. He could deliver a lecture on thermodynamics and I'd still be entertained. Okay, quick change of subject before my brain implodes from bad superhero science and disappointed Arctic Monkeys expectations. Anyone got recommendations for new music? Something… energetic? Have you heard of Fontaines D.C.? They’re a bit post-punk, kinda like Joy Division but more… shouty? Oh yeah, they're decent. A bit bleak, though. Good if you’re feeling existential. Hmm, maybe. I need something to, like, counteract the Alex Turner grandpa vibes. Actually, what about IDLES? They're always a good shout for energy. IDLES are class. Properly angry lads. Perfect for winding down after a day of A-Levels. Yeah, I'm gonna stick some IDLES on the bus home.

…and then Mrs. Davies said, “Honestly, it’s like watching a baby giraffe learn to walk!” which was a bit harsh, don’t you think? Was it Leo? He  is  a bit wobbly. I’m not wobbly anymore! I did Balanceability! You  did  do Balanceability, which is amazing! And you were so much better than some of the others. Remember Ms. Riley saying how quickly you picked it up? Yeah! I got a sticker! A shiny one! Ooh, a shiny sticker! What colour was it? Blue! It had a bike on it. See? She was really impressed. And now you’re zooming around on your bike without stabilizers. It’s brilliant. It just shows what you can achieve when you try. Did anyone fall off? A few did. But everyone got back on. It’s all about trying, isn’t it? It reminds me of those assessments we have to do at school. Sometimes they’re hard, but you just have to give it your best shot. I don't like assessments. I know, darling, nobody does. But they help us see what we’re good at, and what we need to work on. Like with Balanceability – some kids needed a little longer, and that's okay. Mummy, can we have pizza tonight? Hmm, pizza sounds good. What kind of toppings? Pepperoni and pineapple! Pineapple on pizza? Are you sure? Yes! It’s yummy! I like ham and sweetcorn. Okay, we can definitely do ham and sweetcorn. Maybe a little pepperoni for you, and we can see about a tiny bit of pineapple for… experimentation. Did anyone talk about their holidays at school today? Thomas said his mum and dad are renovating their whole house! And they're putting in a swimming pool! Wow, that’s a big project. I heard they're even building a little… manmade waterfall. A waterfall? That sounds amazing! But swimming pools can be dangerous, can't they? They can be, yes. Especially diving. We always need to remember never to dive into water unless we know how deep it is. It’s really important. Ms. Johnson told us today that it's National Cat Day in Japan! Oh, really? That’s lovely. I wonder what they do to celebrate. Maybe they give cats lots of treats! Probably! Speaking of treats… what goes well with pizza, do you think? Garlic bread? Salad? Chocolate! Not chocolate, sweetie.

Honestly, I’m shattered. That spin class nearly killed me. Oh no! I thought you said you enjoyed those? I  do  enjoy them, usually. But the instructor today was… intense. Like, Olympic athlete intense. I couldn’t keep up! I was just trying not to fall off the bike, honestly. Oh dear. Well, at least you tried! I’ve been meaning to get back into running, but I keep making excuses. It’s so cold and dark in the mornings. Tell me about it. I had to practically wrestle myself into my leggings this morning. But honestly, it’s worth it afterwards, you feel so much better. You should find a running buddy, that helps. Maybe. I’m just… not sure I’ve got the energy for all of it at the moment. Work’s been a bit manic. And things with… well, you know, with Mark. Oh, right. How’s that going? Still the silent treatment? Pretty much. He’s being… passive-aggressive, mostly. Leaving little notes about whose turn it is to do the washing up. Seriously? Is that how grown men communicate now? Ugh. Men. Honestly. It sounds exhausting. Have you tried just, like, sitting him down and actually talking? I have! Several times. He just clams up and says I’m overreacting. It’s like talking to a brick wall. He says I’m always ‘analysing everything’ and that I need to ‘just relax’. Oh,  that’s  rich. The classic deflect and invalidation combo. Honestly, you deserve better. I know, logically. But it’s just… hard. We’ve been together for four years. It’s comfortable, you know? Familiar. Comfortable isn’t always good, though, is it? Especially if it’s comfortable being miserable. You deserve someone who actually  talks  to you. And doesn't leave you passive-aggressive notes about laundry. You’re probably right. I’m just… scared of being on my own, I think. It’s silly, isn’t it? I’m a fully functioning adult, I have a good job, I have friends… It’s not silly at all! It’s totally normal to be scared of change. But you’re amazing, you'd be absolutely fine. And we’re all here for you, no matter what you decide. Thanks. That means a lot. You always know what to say. So… shall we order a takeaway and watch something terrible on TV? Distraction tactics are needed.

Right, that was a good dominoes drive, eh? Didn’t half take old Mrs. Patterson down a peg or two this week. She thought she had me cornered, did she? Aye, she always thinks she's got someone cornered. She's proper competitive, that one. Did you see her face when you won? Oh, I did. Priceless. Honestly, she practically threw her dominoes across the room. More drama than EastEnders, that woman. More pizza, anyone? I ordered extra, knowing you two lot. Aye, please! This pepperoni's cracking. Better than the stuff they serve at school, that's for sure. School dinners, eh? Don’t get me started. Remember your mam used to pack you a proper feast, lad? Sandwiches the size of paving slabs. I do! And a Wagon Wheel every single day. Mrs. Davison used to glare at me somethin’ awful. Said it wasn't a proper packed lunch. Well, she had a point. A Wagon Wheel isn't a balanced meal, is it? Though I can’t blame you, they  were  delicious. Speaking of which, have you thought about what you want for Easter? Your auntie and I were talking. Not really. Haven’t really thought that far ahead. Maybe some new trainers? Mine are falling apart. Trainers, eh? Always trainers. In my day, we were happy with a pair of plimsolls and a bit of luck. You lads have it easy these days. Oh, don’t start with that "in my day" stuff, Arthur. It was different times. And trainers  are  practical, especially with all the running about you do. Did you manage to get that log sorted in the fireplace, by the way? I saw it looked a bit… precarious last week. Aye, got it sorted. Nearly slid right out while I was poking at it. Sounded like a landslide, it did! Gave me a right fright. Needed a cuppa and a lie-down after that. Wow. That  would  be scary. You’re not wrong. Right, I’m thinking of getting my hair cut on Tuesday. It's getting a bit too long, I think. What do you think, lads? Should I go for the usual bob, or something a bit different? Just keep it tidy, love. Don’t go getting one of those fancy styles. You suit a simple cut. Yeah, keep it simple. Don't want you looking like one of them pop stars!

Right, so milk first, or tea first? It’s a whole thing, isn’t it? My nan swore tea first made it stronger. Oh, tea first, definitely. It’s… science. I read something about it once. Seriously. It releases the flavour better. Or something. Science, eh? You and your science. Honestly, you’d think running experiments all day would be enough, but no, you need to scientifically determine the best way to make a cuppa. Hey, details matter. Especially when it comes to tea. Speaking of details, have you looked at pubs around here yet? We need a proper local. Somewhere… atmospheric. A bit, yeah. There’s the Eagle, obviously, tourist trap, but alright for a quick one. And the Maypole, which is a bit more… studenty. Though they do a decent Sunday roast. I was hoping for something a bit more…traditional. Like a proper old man’s pub. Ooh, like a proper dark wood and sticky floors kind of place? Yeah, I'm with you on that. The Maypole feels a bit too… bright. And full of people discussing their dissertations. Exactly! I don’t want to hear about Bayesian statistics while I’m trying to enjoy a pint. Though, talking of things I don't want to hear about… have you seen what’s happened with that bloke… what’s his name… the one from  Bridgerton ? Rege-Jean Page? Oh yeah, the drama. Apparently, he turned down the  James Bond  role. Can you believe it? No way! Mad. Absolute mad. He’d have been brilliant! Though, honestly, the pressure would be insane. Still, disappointing. Right, tea’s brewing. So, food plans for the week? I was thinking of attempting a vegetable tagine. Ooh, ambitious! You and vegetables… It’s a brave new world. Hey! I’m expanding my horizons! It’s just… I’m not naturally drawn to things that are green. But I know I  should  eat them. And tagine seems like a good way to disguise them. Mostly. Fair enough. I'm happy to do the shopping. And maybe… gently encourage the addition of a few more vegetables than strictly necessary. You're a lifesaver. Seriously. Actually, what about Brussels sprouts? Have you ever tried roasting them with balsamic glaze? It’s… transformative. Brussels sprouts? You're actively trying to scare me now, aren't you? Balsamic glaze doesn’t make them less… sprouty. Trust me!

Right, okay, my turn. Ugh, this is awful. Okay… “Famous explorers.” No, too broad. Right. Okay, you lot are not allowed to say Magellan! Or Columbus! Or… anything obvious. Oh, you’re pre-emptively banning words already? That’s not fair! It’s her tactic. She always does this. Makes it impossible. Now, now, let the lady play. Though I agree, it  is  a bit mean. Famous explorers… hmm… was it Shackleton? The Antarctic one? No! No, no, no! Too easy! Think… later explorers. More modern. Ooh, ooh, is it… Livingstone? David Livingstone, I presume? No! Honestly! You’re all thinking of the classics. This is a relatively recent explorer. Female. Female explorer? Oh, crikey. Is it…Junko Tabei? The first woman to climb Everest? Yes! Yes! Junko Tabei! Finally! You got it! Good grief, it took you all long enough. She gave absolutely no clues! “Famous explorers” is massive. And then banning everyone who’s even remotely well-known... It’s a strategy! It forces you to think outside the box. Your turn, Rhys. Don’t ban everything! Fine, fine. Okay… “Things you find in a garden.” Right. Easy peasy. Flowers! No! No flowers! A shed? No! A gnome? Keep going! Keep going! You’re getting warmer… A barbeque? No! But you’re almost there… think smaller. Things you  find … not things you  put  in a garden. Worms? Yes! Worms! Finally. You’re all terrible at this game. Absolutely hopeless. It’s a difficult game! It requires lateral thinking. And discerning clues. Which, frankly, some people aren't providing. Oh, here we go. Grandad being critical again. Oh, leave him be, he's enjoying himself. It's good to have a bit of healthy competition. Ok, ok my turn. “Things that are blue”. The sea! That's too easy. Bluebells! Nope. Blueberry? Getting warmer... Blue cheese? Yes! You got it! Blue cheese! I thought that was a good one. Honestly, you lot are obsessed with food. Well, it’s a good category! Everyone likes food. Right, alright, my turn again. “Books”. The Bible? Too easy. Think modern. Harry Potter! No! Think… something a bit older. A classic. Pride and Prejudice? Yes! Pride and Prejudice! Good. Okay, this is getting fun. It’s a good game, this. Gets the brain working. Reminds me of the old days, playing charades at the WI meetings. Oh, don't remind me of those, Dai.

Right, okay, so I’m going to put down a red seven. And then… oh, hang on. Rhys, you haven’t taken a card, have you? You’re just staring into space. Oh! Sorry, lost in thought. Beautiful countryside, innit? Absolutely stunning. My brain just… wandered. Go on, put your seven down. Stunning for sheep, maybe. It’s just… green. A lot of green. Oh, don’t be like that, Gareth. It's peaceful. And it’s lovely to get away, isn’t it? Especially after that half-term we’ve just had. Honestly, little Timmy nearly drove me round the bend. Tell me about it. My Year 6s were… energetic. Let's just leave it at that. So, red seven down. Anyone got a seven to beat it? Nope. Pass. And seriously, this game is intense. I feel like I'm back in university, calculating probabilities and trying to bluff everyone. You were terrible at bluffing at university, remember? You always went bright red. That's a low blow! I improved! Slightly. I’ve got a red seven, but… it’s a different suit. No good, is it? Nope, needs to be hearts. Right, my turn again. I’m going to play a… a green nine. Oh, excellent. Now we’re getting somewhere. Ooh, I can beat that! I’ve got a green ten! Take that! You always have a card up your sleeve, don’t you? It’s infuriating. You know, I remember playing this game with my nan. She used to always say, “A steady hand and a sly grin are all you need.” Your nan sounds like a card shark. She was! She cleaned everyone out at family gatherings. It was legendary. Once, she won enough money to buy a… well, it was a very small caravan, but still! A caravan! Incredible. Right, I’m thinking strategically now. I need to get rid of some of these high cards. Careful now. Don’t underestimate me. I’m feeling lucky. I've had a dodgy week at work, need to win something. What happened at work? Anything exciting? Or just the usual classroom chaos? Oh, you know… parent complaints, tricky behaviour… a miniature protest about the lunchtime menu. It's always something. One little boy refused to eat anything that wasn’t beige. Anything! Oh, that’s brilliant! Anything beige? Goodness me. They’re very specific these days, aren’t they?

Honestly,  Wednesday  is just… chef’s kiss. Have you guys seen it? It’s so good. Like, properly dark and funny. Ooh, I’ve heard about it! Is it on Netflix? I've been meaning to start it, but work’s been mental. Old Mr. Henderson's been particularly… demanding. Keeps wanting me to rearrange his cushions  exactly  so. Netflix yeah. It’s brilliant. Jenna Ortega is incredible. Way better than the last Addams Family attempts. Though, talking of work, I’m starting to think I really messed up choosing accountancy. It’s just spreadsheets and tax codes. It’s…sad. Spreadsheets are the backbone of civilization, Amelia! Don’t knock spreadsheets. Though, to be fair, my job involves a lot more blowing things up virtually, which is marginally more exciting. Still, tons of spreadsheets. Blowing things up? Seriously, Ben? Sounds intense. I just spend my evenings folding jumpers at Next and trying not to make eye contact with customers. It's…character building. Oh, you poor thing, Lily! Well, at least you’re earning money. I'm completely broke until student loan comes in again. Uni is expensive even with the loan, isn’t it? Tell me about it. I’m still paying off mine. I considered an apprenticeship instead, honestly. Might have been a better route. Less debt, more practical skills… Apprenticeships are a good shout. A lot of my team are ex-apprentices, and they are solid. I mean, I went the full university route, but it’s not for everyone. Costs a fortune. Speaking of costs, has anyone got any Christmas present ideas for Gran? She’s got everything. Last year I got her a foot massager and she just looked at me like I’d insulted her. Ooh, tricky. Maybe a really nice photo album with family pictures? She loves looking at old photos and going on about how cute we all were. Yeah, that's a good idea! Or a fancy box of biscuits. Gran loves a biscuit. Although, she  did  get a really bad cold last week… Mum was worried sick. Oh no, poor Gran! Is she better now? She’s on the mend, thankfully. Just a nasty bug. Mum's been forcing her to drink loads of lemon and honey. Honestly, Mum turns into a full-on nurse when anyone gets ill. Mothers are like that. Mine turned into a biohazard specialist when I got chickenpox at seventeen.

Honestly though, I don't know what’s happening with people these days. Just walking along, glued to their phones. Nearly walked straight into one earlier, you know? Outside the bakery. Oh, it’s awful isn’t it? You see it  everywhere . Like they’re living in a different world. Right, and they don’t even look up! Nearly got taken out by a cyclist doing the same thing last week. Headphones in, eyes down. Reckless, that’s what it is. Cyclists are the worst! I swear, they think they own the pavement. And going so fast! I nearly had a heart attack the other day, one whizzed past me on Mill Road, didn’t even ring his bell. Mill Road's a nightmare. It's just constantly busy. I cycle to work sometimes, and even  I  get stressed. You're dodging pedestrians, buses, other cyclists… You should get the bus, love. Safer, that is. I’d love to, but the bus routes are terrible. It would take me ages, and I need to get to work for nine. Cycling is quicker, even with all the chaos. Well, if you ask me, everyone should drive. It’s far more sensible. You’re in control, you can see what’s happening. But parking is a nightmare here, Gran. And it's so expensive! Plus, you're contributing to the pollution. She’s got a point there, Mum. Parking  is  a joke. Remember when we tried to drive into town for Christmas shopping last year? Took us an hour just to find a space. Hmph. Well, I still think driving is the safest option. I’ve been driving for fifty years, never had an accident. Touch wood! Fifty years is a long time, Gran. Things are a bit different now, aren’t they? More traffic, more people… Remember old Mr. Henderson? Used to cycle everywhere, rain or shine. Even in his eighties! Said it kept him young. Oh, Henderson! A lovely man. But he was a bit of a madman, cycling in that weather. Always had a waterproof coat though, bless him. Speaking of getting around, are you two still planning on coming to visit me next month? I was thinking we could walk along the river, maybe go for a picnic. We are, love. Looking forward to it. As long as the weather’s decent. Yes, a lovely day out. Perhaps we could take the bus, though?

It’s lovely isn't it, to be back? Feels like ages since I was wandering these corridors as a student. Absolutely. Though it all feels… smaller, somehow. Remember thinking everything was so grand and imposing? That's the trick of youth, my dear. Everything  is  smaller when you've had a few decades to grow accustomed to the real world. Though this faculty remains rather impressive. So, are you both alumni of the Law Faculty then? Yes, I graduated about five years ago. I’m a Language Research Coordinator now – a bit of a mouthful, I know. It’s fascinating work though, looking at legal language across different cultures. And I’m a Research Administrator. Bit more paperwork, a bit less language, but still good. Did you ever study any languages alongside law? I did! Spanish, actually. Spent a year in Barcelona. Absolutely fell in love with the city. Have you been? Barcelona? A beautiful city. Though I must confess, I found the Catalan independence movement a little unsettling while I was there. Fascinating linguistic situation though, isn’t it? The Basque country is even more unique. Such an isolated language family. I’ve always found linguistics fascinating. It’s amazing how much law is tied up in language and interpretation. I tried Mandarin briefly, completely failed. It's just… conceptually so different. Oh, Mandarin is a beast! I've dabbled a bit, but it's a whole different skillset. Have you travelled much in China? I did a sabbatical in Hong Kong years ago, lecturing on comparative law. Quite an experience. Very different legal traditions, as one might imagine. Though I spent most of my time trying to avoid the humidity! Reminded me of summers in London, honestly. London’s pretty humid these days, isn't it? Though not quite Hong Kong levels, I imagine. I haven’t been back to Cambridge since I graduated. I did spend a couple of years living in London after university, though. It’s changed a lot even in the last few years. It's definitely… busier. Did either of you ever venture into Wales during your time here? Wales? I did. Years ago. Went to watch a rugby match. Incredible atmosphere. Truly incredible. Though I confess, I didn’t quite understand all the rules. Oh, rugby! It’s a bit of a national obsession there. My dad’s Welsh, so I was practically raised on it.

Honestly though, seeing all those Ice Bucket Challenge videos pop up again on Facebook… it’s weird, isn’t it? Feels like a lifetime ago. Remember how everyone was doing it? Even Gran got involved, bless her. Oh god, Gran and the ice bucket. That was… a sight. She was complaining about being cold for a week afterwards. And Uncle Barry filming it all, of course. He  loved  that. Did you see Sarah’s engagement photos? They’re all over my feed. Oh, the ones in that ridiculous castle? Yeah, a bit much, even for Sarah. Still, good for her, I suppose. She's always wanted the full fairytale wedding. How’s your mum doing, by the way? Haven't spoken to her properly in ages. She’s alright, she's alright. Bit creaky, you know, the usual. Complaining about her knees. She keeps trying to get me to sign up for that pilates class with her. Says it’ll ‘sort me out’. Oh, Mum will try and fix everyone with pilates. It's her solution for everything! Remember when she tried to get Dad to do it for his back? He nearly strangled her. She’s a force of nature, isn’t she? Speaking of forces of nature… how’s teaching going, Ben? Still battling through the grammar tenses with bewildered students? It’s… a challenge. Honestly, sometimes I wonder if I made the right decision going to uni to do that. It’s not exactly a lucrative career path, eh? Plus, the paperwork. Endless forms to fill in. It feels like I spend more time doing admin than actually teaching sometimes. Tell me about it. Dental practices are the same. So many forms! And everyone’s got a ‘condition’ to note down. Honestly, you’d think everyone was on death’s door. Sounds grim. Recruitment isn’t  that  bad. Although… trying to convince people they’re perfect for jobs they clearly aren't is a skill. I had one candidate yesterday who swore he was fluent in Mandarin. Turns out he knew how to say ‘hello’ and ‘thank you’. Oh, brilliant. You always get those! Remember Mark from school? Said he was a black belt in karate. We found out he’d taken two lessons. Oh,  Mark . Don't even get me started on Mark. He was always exaggerating. Speaking of school…did you hear about Lisa’s little boy, Freddie?

Honestly, this coffee machine is driving me mad. It makes a perfectly good cup sometimes, and other times it just spits out lukewarm water. It's possessed, I tell you. Possessed! Maybe it needs descaling? You said you hadn't done it in ages. Descaling, cleaning, praying… I’ve tried it all! It's just… unreliable. Like half the politicians these days. Speaking of politicians, did you see what Starmer said about… well, everything? It was predictably bland. Honestly, where are the real idealists anymore? Nobody's fighting for anything properly. Oh, don’t get me started on politics. It’s just a mess. All sound and fury, signifying nothing. Though, to be fair, I’m finding it hard to care much since I retired. Less infuriating news headlines in retirement, I suppose. True. Though I find myself doomscrolling far too much. It's a bad habit. It is. Anyway, back to more pressing matters... have you gotten quotes yet for removing and storing some of the stuff from the attic? We really need to clear it out before winter sets in. I did. It’s absolutely outrageous, the prices! One company wanted nearly four hundred pounds just to  look  at it, let alone move anything. And the storage costs... Honestly, it's cheaper to buy a new house and fill it with new stuff. Four hundred pounds just to assess? That's daylight robbery! Did you try that man, Barry, from the village? He does removals on the side. Yes, I did. He’s busy until October, and even then he wants more than I was hoping to pay. He said everyone is clearing out before the cold weather. Apparently, everyone's suddenly realised they've accumulated too much junk. Well, we  have  accumulated a lot of junk. Let’s be honest. It’s a generational curse. Grandmother Moira was a hoarder, and it seems to be in the genes. Don’t remind me. I’m still finding her teacups in the most unlikely places. And her collection of commemorative spoons. Honestly. It's madness. Maybe we could have a clear-out weekend? We could all tackle it together? The more hands, the quicker it’ll be. That's a good idea. Though knowing us, we'll end up reminiscing over every single item and get nothing actually  done . Probably. But it’s worth a try. At least we can make a strong cup of coffee…if this wretched machine cooperates, that is.

Honestly, Mum, the thought of Christmas already fills me with dread. Not the actual day, but  getting  to the actual day. It's just… relentless, isn’t it? Oh, darling, you always say that. You say it every year. And yet, you always manage to pull it off, a delightful Christmas spread, everyone happy. You’re a natural. That's just forced cheer, I assure you. And a lot of Prosecco. This year, I’m seriously considering just eloping. You and Dad, maybe Jamie and Isla… and just disappearing somewhere warm. Eloping? Where to? Don’t be ridiculous. Your father would have a fit. Besides, what about your brother? He’d never forgive you. Or Auntie Brenda, for that matter. She’s already started hinting about wanting to carve the turkey again. Oh, God, Brenda and the turkey. A horrifying image. That's exactly what I’m trying to avoid. Maybe just a small Christmas, at my place? No extended family, just close friends? That sounds… sensible. Though, your father does love having everyone around. He gets so much joy from it. He secretly loves Brenda’s insistence on carving the turkey, you know. He pretends to be annoyed, but he isn’t. He’s such a softie. Right. Okay. We'll have family Christmas. But I’m delegating. Seriously delegating. I can’t be responsible for  everything  again. Last year, I practically single-handedly assembled ten Lego sets. Ten! Oh, the nephews. They are a handful. It's lovely to see their faces though, isn’t it? That pure joy. It is. But my fingers were aching for a week. And speaking of aching, how is your back? Still giving you trouble? It’s…manageable. I'm doing those Pilates classes, remember? Trying to. Although Mrs. Higgins keeps showing off, and it's terribly distracting. She was a ballerina, apparently. A  professional  ballerina. At seventy! Good for her! It’s good to keep active. You should get Dad to join you. He’s complaining about his knees again. He'd rather watch football. You know that. He's stubbornly refusing to admit he’s getting older. Keeps trying to chase after the dog. Oh, Dad. Always the sportsman. Listen, about work… I’m thinking of doing that CELTA course in January. Fully immerse myself, you know? Really boost my TEFL qualifications. Oh, that’s excellent, darling! Very sensible. You’re good at that, you are.

Honestly, I thought old man Hemmings was gonna have a heart attack last night. What, at the pub quiz? What happened? No, not at the pub quiz. At Sheila’s. He was going on  about  Geoff. Apparently, Geoff’s snoring kept him up all night. Said it sounded like a rusty engine trying to start. Oh, bless him! Geoff snores worse than a badger. Did he actually complain to Geoff? Apparently so. Sheila had to intervene. Said Geoff just mumbled something about needing a really strong whisky and rolled over. Hemmings was fuming. Honestly, some people. It’s snoring! A bit of earplug action and job done. Speaking of Sheila, did anyone get those cream cakes from Waterfields for her birthday? I did! Got a box of the little fancies. And a loaf of their sourdough. Proper good stuff, Waterfields. Oh, nice one! She’ll love that. She’s obsessed with their sourdough. Says it's the only bread that doesn't give her indigestion. Remember when Waterfields used to do those little sausage rolls with Richmond sausages in? Pure heaven. They stopped doing them ages ago. Tragedy. Oh my god, yes! Proper Richmonds, not that cheap rubbish they use now. Honestly, it's a crime against pastry. It is. It really is. Everything’s gone downhill. You can’t get a decent sausage roll anywhere anymore. Speaking of things going downhill, did you see Barry yesterday? He was walking around with a… a  handkerchief ! No way! Barry? The Barry who uses a whole roll of paper towel to wipe his nose? Apparently, his mum sent him one. Said he needed to “be more of a man” and stop wasting paper. Oh, his mum! She’s a character, isn’t she? Sending him a handkerchief! It’s the 21st century! I bet he was mortified. Imagine Barry trying to  blow  his nose into a handkerchief. It’s a mental image I didn’t need. I saw him trying to figure out how to fold it afterwards, too. Looked like he was wrestling with a small, patterned bird. Oh, this is brilliant. I need to tell everyone. Geoff, the rusty engine, and Barry, the handkerchief man. This is gold. So, quiz tonight then? Same teams? Yeah, sounds good. Just promise me we won’t get stuck on the music round again. I’m terrible with anything post-2000. Deal. Though, someone needs to stop Dave from shouting out all the answers.

Honestly, that was the busiest weekend ever. I feel like I haven’t stopped moving since Friday evening. Tell me about it. Though, mine was busy in a different way. Mostly involving stubborn sheep and fences that decided to give up their lives. Oh, no! Not again with the fences? You said the last storm really did a number on them. A number is putting it mildly. It was more like a total demolition. Spent most of Saturday patching things up, and then Sunday was spent checking they hadn't  immediately  fallen down again. It’s a never-ending cycle, honestly. Sounds exhausting. At least mine was… social exhaustion. I went to that art exhibition with Chloe, and it was surprisingly packed. Then a birthday dinner for Liam, which went on  way  too long. Liam, eh? Progress? Don’t push it, Dad! It was just a friendly dinner. He’s good mates with Ben from work, so it was a bit of a team thing. It was nice, actually. He's got a new puppy, a little Jack Russell, absolutely adorable. A puppy? You’re a sucker for a puppy, aren’t you? Shut up. It was cute! Anyway, then Sunday I was helping Mum sort through old photos. That was a whole saga. Apparently, I had a phase where I only wore bright orange, and she has photographic evidence. Oh, bless. Mothers and their photo albums. They’re a historical record of our shame. I remember your grandma had a photo of me in short trousers and knee socks… traumatizing. I bet. So, what about you? Aside from battling rogue livestock, anything else happen on the farm? Any breakthroughs with the new irrigation system? Not quite breakthroughs. More like minor victories. Got the pump working consistently, but the distribution is still a bit uneven. It needs another tweak, I think. I'm hoping to get a proper engineer out next week, if I can find one who isn't booked up for the next six months. That sounds frustrating. It always seems to be one thing after another. It is. But, you know, it's rewarding too. Seeing the crops come in, knowing you've played a part in that… it's a good feeling. Plus, you get to spend time with the sheep, which are always entertaining. Even when they’re escaping. Fair enough. So, are you free next weekend?

Honestly, the marking is just… relentless. I’m dreaming of essay titles now. And they all think they’re budding Zadie Smiths, honestly. Oh, tell me about it! Though at least English Lit essays are…readable, usually. Trying to decipher Year 9 French attempts at describing their weekend is a special kind of torture. “Je suis allé au cinema avec mon chien.” It’s always the dog. Always. Oh my god, that’s brilliant! They just throw in random vocabulary, don’t they? It's the same with Spanish, they just sprinkle in words they vaguely remember. I had one kid write about going to the beach with his grandfather…and then suddenly, a detailed description of making paella. The logic escapes me. How’s the new Head of Department? Is she as terrifying as everyone said? She’s…efficient. Let’s go with efficient. Very focused on data and targets. Definitely not a ‘warm and fuzzy’ leader. She keeps asking about ‘value-added’ and I just nod and pretend I understand. Honestly, I miss old Mr. Henderson. He just wanted us to enjoy teaching. Oh, Henderson was the best. Remember that time he accidentally locked himself in the stationery cupboard during parents’ evening? How could I forget! The parents were queuing up, wondering where he’d disappeared to, and then this muffled shouting emerged from inside. It was glorious. Anyway, enough about work, I'm starting to stress just  talking  about it. How are things at the language school? Still enjoying it? It's good! It’s just… different. A lot more responsibility. Managing the adult classes is surprisingly demanding. You get all sorts, you know? Retired engineers learning Mandarin for a cruise, diplomats brushing up on their Italian… It's fascinating, but tiring. Sounds it. Have you met anyone interesting? A few. There’s a lovely woman from Brazil, she’s learning English and wants to become a translator. And a very charming Italian man who’s constantly trying to get me to go for aperitivo. Ooh, dangerous! Speaking of charming men… how’s the baby hunt going? Any closer? No. Still nothing. We had another round of tests, everything’s… fine. Just nothing happening. It’s starting to feel a bit hopeless, to be honest. Oh, darling, I’m so sorry. That’s awful. Don’t give up hope though. Millie and Mark were trying for  years  before their little Leo arrived.

Right then, lovely bit of sunshine isn’t it? Good for the roses, though I reckon those sparrows are getting a bit too confident. See ‘em diving right in for the seed, cheeky little beggars. They are bold, aren’t they? I topped up the feeder this morning, you’d think they’d be grateful, but no. Always wanting more. Still, better than them building nests in the guttering again. Remember last year? A right mess. Oh, don’t remind me! I had to get young Mark to come round and clear it out. Dreadful really. All that mess… and the wasps! It’s a wonder we didn’t get stung. Beautiful nests though, when you actually  look  at them. Tiny pieces of everything. Aye, clever little things, the birds. Though I don’t understand why they pick such silly places sometimes. Especially with the cats about. Speaking of which, have you seen Tibbs lately? He’s been a bit quiet. He’s under the hydrangea. Having a snooze, I expect. Old boy needs his rest these days. Getting on a bit, isn’t he? Like us. Oh, don't start on that! We’re not  old , just… experienced. More time for cake, I say. Is there any left of that Victoria sponge? Marjorie, it was divine. Absolutely divine. Plenty left, I saved you a big slice. In the kitchen, with a cup of tea. Though you should be careful, dear. Remember what the doctor said about your sugar. Oh, pooh to the doctor! A little cake never hurt anyone. Besides, a bit of sweetness is good for the soul. I’ve been thinking… I’ve got those old puppets in the loft. The ones the grandchildren used to play with. Might dig them out. Puppets? Good heavens, you’re going to start putting on shows now are you? Well, why not? Keeps the mind active. I was thinking maybe a little puppet show for the neighbourhood children. It’d be good for them to see something a bit different than the telly. That's a lovely idea, Marjorie. Though you'll need a stage. And a script. Oh, I'll manage. I used to be quite good at improvising. It's just... it's a bit worrying, isn't it? Seeing some of the older folks around here. Old Mr. Henderson keeps forgetting where he lives. Awful. It is sad.

Right, I think I'm going to go for the grilled halloumi with the salad. It smells lovely. Are you having the kebab again, David? You know me too well. Can't resist a good kebab, especially out here. And the bread is just… incredible. Oh, look at that couple over there, arguing already! They’ve barely had their starters. Oh dear. It's always the same, isn’t it? You get all sorts in these places. Remember old Mrs. Higgins from the village? She used to come here on holiday every year, and she'd always complain about the seagulls stealing her chips. Oh, I remember her! A force of nature, that woman. Used to chase them off with her handbag. She was convinced they were deliberately targeting her. Speaking of targeting…my sister’s still going on about her dodgy online dating experiences. Apparently, the last one claimed to be a millionaire, but his car was held together with duct tape. Oh, you're kidding! Honestly, some people. I'm glad I’m happily settled with Mark. Though even  he  has his moments. Remember when he tried to build a fire in the garden using only twigs and a magnifying glass? It took him three hours, and he nearly set the rose bushes alight! Oh, yes! That was a sight. He’s a good man, though. Always trying. My hearing aid's playing up again, by the way. Everything sounds a bit muffled. It’s the humidity, I think. Oh, no! That’s frustrating. You really should get it checked. It’s such a pain when they don’t work properly. It reminds me of Grandad’s hearing. He refused to wear one for years, then when he finally did, he said all he could hear was the washing machine! He sounds a bit like my Uncle George. Stubborn as a mule. He always said modern medicine was nonsense. He was convinced dowsing could cure everything. Apparently, he could find water with a forked stick and predict the weather. Oh, really? That’s… interesting. My friend, Sarah, is quite into shamanism. She's been trying to get me to have a reading. She says it’ll help me unlock my true destiny. Destiny, eh? I think our destiny is to enjoy this kebab. Though learning a few Turkish phrases would be useful. I’ve managed “Teşekkür ederim” - thank you.

Honestly, the kids are driving me round the bend with the exams. It’s just… constant. Constant pressure. They’re all so stressed, and then it filters down to us. Oh, Mum, that sounds awful. Is it worse this year? It always feels peak stress time doesn’t it, around exams? It  is  worse. They’ve changed the specifications again, haven’t they? New content, new marking schemes… It’s a nightmare to keep on top of. And the appeals process! Don’t even get me started. Sounds like fun. Though I suppose someone has to do it. Reminds me of dealing with subsidies for the farm, always paperwork, always someone complaining. Though thankfully, no teenagers involved. Just grumpy farmers. Dad! You’re terrible. But seriously, Mum, can I get you a top-up of tea? You look like you need it. Oh, that would be lovely, thank you, dear. Just a little splash of milk, please. So, how’s work going? Still coordinating projects that are constantly on the brink of disaster? Pretty much! It’s… dynamic. We had a launch yesterday that went slightly sideways, but we managed to salvage it. It involved a lot of late nights and a lot of coffee. They’re talking about restructuring again, which is never a good sign. Restructuring. That’s just a fancy word for ‘someone’s losing their job’, isn’t it? Probably. I’m hoping I’m not one of them. I’m trying to be proactive, picking up extra responsibilities, being generally indispensable. Good for you, love. You always were a grafter. Speaking of indispensable, your Auntie Carol called. She was asking when you’re coming to see her. She's been doing up her garden, apparently. Oh, bless her. I really should. It's just… finding the time. I promised I'd help her with the patio, but weekends are always booked up. You need to make time for family, you do. It’s important. Your grandparents would have said the same. Remember old Grandad Ernie? Always said family came first. Even over rugby. Which was quite a statement, considering. He did love his rugby, didn’t he? I remember him trying to explain the offside rule to me. It went completely over my head. I remember him sneaking biscuits to me when you weren’t looking. He was the best. He was a good man. Now, about this house.

Honestly, I was proper howling at that catfish episode last night. Oh, the one with the bloke pretending to be a model? Proper mental, innit? I missed it! Was it good? I've been stuck revising all week, it's torture. Good? It was  gold . He'd stolen photos off some random American guy and built this whole life online. Then she flies all the way to meet him and… well, you can imagine. He was wearing like, padding everywhere! And a wig. A terrible wig. Honestly, the audacity of some people. No way! That's… that's next level. I can't believe people actually fall for that. They do though, don’t they? It’s mad. Makes you wonder what’s real online, doesn’t it? Everything's fake, love. Literally everything. That's why I stick to looking at cats on Instagram, at least  they  are what they seem. Mostly. Speaking of mental… did anyone watch Jeremy Kyle this morning? Oh god, no. I actively avoid that show. It's depressing. Pure, unadulterated misery. I caught a bit of it while I was making a cuppa. They had a woman on accusing her sister’s boyfriend of… oh, this is awful… using her garden gnome as a… well, let’s just say it wasn’t a respectful use of a garden gnome.  What?!  You’re joking! I wish I was! Jeremy Kyle was proper mortified. And the lie detector… oh, the lie detector was going  wild . Right, that’s it, I’m gonna watch it on catch-up. I need to see this gnome situation for myself. Honestly, people are bonkers. Honestly. It makes you feel better about your own life, though, doesn't it? Like, at least I haven't been involved in any garden gnome related scandals. Absolutely. Although, I did have a massive argument with my nan last week about her obsession with gnomes. So, maybe I'm closer than I think. Oh no! What happened? She's bought like, fifteen new ones, and they're all staring into my bedroom window. It's terrifying. I swear they move when I'm not looking. That’s proper creepy! You need to stage an intervention. A gnome intervention. Definitely. Maybe get Jeremy Kyle involved? He seems good at dealing with family drama. Oh god, no. Don’t tempt fate. Your nan might end up on the show with her army of gnomes.

Honestly, the WiFi’s been a nightmare all morning. I’ve been trying to upload this essay for ages. It keeps cutting out mid-sentence. It’s infuriating! Oh dear. You young people and your computers. It's always something isn’t it? When I was at university, everything was so… simpler. Though, of course, it wasn’t. It just  felt  simpler. We’d spend hours in the library with actual books. Sounds…peaceful, actually. Though I can’t imagine lugging around a stack of books for every essay. Speaking of university, I’m thinking of applying for a year abroad. Paris maybe? Paris! Oh, that’s wonderful! I haven’t been back in… goodness, decades. It’s changed so much, I hear. You should definitely go. Your French is very good, you know. Almost as good as my German. Though, admittedly, I haven’t spoken German properly in years. Well, I’ve been taking classes. It’s alright. I can order a croissant and ask for directions. That’s about the extent of it. You said you lived in Vienna, right? Was it very different from London? Oh, vastly different. Vienna is… elegant. It has a history, a weight. It’s practically built on music and coffee. And cake, of course. London is… busier, more chaotic. Though I do miss it, naturally. My sister still lives there, you know. She’s a Classics scholar. Always buried in ancient texts. Wow, that sounds intense! What does she actually  do  with all that knowledge? She teaches. And she translates. Very precise work. It’s quite a contrast to my painting, which is… rather messy. Speaking of which, I've been trying to capture the light on the lavender this week. It's proving difficult. You always make it sound so easy when  you  paint. It's always just… there. Speaking of things that are ‘just there’ have you seen the bees are back in the garden? I spotted one buzzing around the roses this morning. Oh, excellent! Yes, I saw them too. I’ve left out a little dish of sugar water. They need the energy. It reminds me of my grandmother's garden in Italy. We used to keep bees there as well. The honey was divine. Italy! Have you been back recently? Not for far too long. My cousin still lives in Florence. I promised to visit, but then… well, life gets in the way, doesn’t it?

Honestly, the way that man just pulled out… I thought he wasn’t going to stop! Nearly gave me a heart attack. Seriously! People are so reckless. It’s like they think those lines on the road are just suggestions, not rules. It’s awful. And you see them on their phones too, isn't it? Absolutely terrifying. I saw one woman practically steering with her knees while scrolling through something. It’s a wonder there aren't more accidents. Speaking of things that are a wonder… have you seen the state of some of these new builds? All crammed in, no gardens, looks like rabbit hutches. God, yeah. And expensive rabbit hutches at that! Remember when we drove through Slough? Honestly, one of the worst towns I’ve ever seen. Ooh, Slough is… an experience. Harlow’s not much better these days, sadly. They just keep building and building, no thought for the people who have to live there. You need space, you know? I’m glad we’re going to Dorset. At least it’s a bit more… green. Yeah, it'll be nice to get away. How’s work, Carol? Any drama? Oh, you know. The usual. Short-staffed, which means extra shifts. Managed to snag a couple of days off next week though. Doctor’s appointment and then hopefully just a bit of quiet time. Need it. Doctors, eh? Always a waiting game. I had to call my solicitor again yesterday. Still chasing up that paperwork. Honestly, they charge you a fortune and then take their time. Ugh, solicitors. Money-grabbing vultures. Are you still worried about Mum’s estate? Always. It’s just…a headache. And the car’s MOT’s due next month. Another bill to look forward to. Everything is a bill these days. I swear. Speaking of bills and headaches, how’s the dissertation going, darling? Still wrestling with that theory? It’s… progressing. Slowly. I’m trying to focus on the primary sources, but it’s all so dense. And then comparing it to everything else! Honestly, I feel like I’m losing brain cells. It's so academic, you know? Compared to what you do, it's like a different planet. You're being very hard on yourself dear. It's good work. I still can’t believe you had to learn how to use Windows 8 for it. Absolute nightmare of an operating system.

Right. Oh you’ve got your slippers on already. It’s only half past four. Well my feet are a bit chilly, aren’t they? Damp. Damp house this is. It’s not  that  damp. You say that every day. It is. Feels it, anyway. Did you put the heating on? Yes, I did. An hour ago. Are you sure you feel alright? Fine. Just cold feet. What’s on the telly tonight? Anything good? I think there’s that detective programme you like. The one with the… the fella who always wears a tweed jacket. Morse? Or Endeavour? Oh, it's Endeavour. The young Morse. Ah, good. Good. I like that one. Better than the other one, I think. I don’t know. They’re both quite gloomy. That’s Oxford for you. Always gloomy. Remember when we went to Oxford? Pouring with rain. Yes! And you lost your umbrella. Did I? Well, probably. I lose everything. You do. You lost your glasses three times last week. That wasn't  losing  them. I just put them down somewhere. On top of the fridge. Well, it was a good place to put them. Away from harm. Harm? What harm would come to your glasses? Dust. And… and cats. We don't  have  a cat. Well, if we had a cat… it’d knock ‘em off. It's just sensible thinking, isn’t it? Sensible. Right. Are you wanting a cup of tea? I just made a fresh pot. That'd be lovely, love. Lovely. With a biscuit? Of course, with a biscuit. What sort? Digestive. Can’t beat a digestive. Not too sweet. Alright. Coming right up. You just sit there and warm your chilly feet. Thank you, you’re a good woman. A very good woman. Oh, hush. You always say that when you want something. Well, it’s true. It is. You know… I saw Old Man Hemmings down the shops today. Looked right peaked, he did. Oh dear. Is he alright? Said his arthritis was playing him up. And his daughter… she's still not well, is she? No, poor woman. It's been a long illness. Aye. Makes you think, doesn’t it? About how quickly things can change. One minute you’re alright, next minute… you’re not. Don’t dwell on it. You'll give yourself a fright. Tea’s coming.

This pasta’s lovely, honestly. You’ve really outdone yourself. Better than any restaurant, pet. Aye, well, it’s a simple tomato and basil, isn’t it? Can’t go far wrong. Though sourcing decent basil in Cambridge isn’t always easy, is it? It always looks a bit…sad in the supermarkets. It’s nice when you get a good bunch though, smells amazing. Reminds me of Gran’s garden actually. She used to have the biggest basil plant ever. And tomatoes, well, she grew award-winning tomatoes! Your Gran was a proper gardener, wasn’t she? Mine just liked pot plants. A bit of geranium, a dusty fern. Not exactly the Chelsea Flower Show. She was more into music though. Always had Vera Lynn on. Oh, Vera Lynn! Blast from the past. You know, Liam was telling me about this new band he’s got into, “Wet Leg”. Have you heard of them? Wet Leg? Vaguely. Isn’t that the Isle of Wight band? I think I saw something about them on Twitter. Sounds a bit…indie, right? Seriously indie. But good! They’re really dry and witty in their lyrics. Liam’s trying to get me into them, but it’s a bit different from what I usually listen to. I was more into Florence + The Machine last month. Different strokes, eh? Speaking of different, did you manage to get hold of Sarah? I haven’t heard back from her about next weekend. I texted her earlier. She's still stuck in that data collection phase for her research. Apparently, she’s spending all day interviewing people about their attitudes towards… garden gnomes. Garden gnomes?! Right. That’s a niche. You’re telling me! She said she’s starting to dream about little ceramic men. Sounds exhausting. She says the weather is playing havoc with her outdoor interviews though. Apparently it's pouring and windy down in Devon. Awful. This weather’s been mental, hasn’t it? One minute sunshine, the next it’s threatening a downpour. Not ideal for discerning gnome opinions. No, definitely not! She’s having to reschedule everything. It's a good job she’s patient. Honestly, I couldn’t spend all day talking to people about gnomes. Me neither. Though, to be fair, I’ve spent the last six months reading about the socio-economic factors influencing the consumption of biscuits. So, who am I to judge?

Honestly, the amount of admin I had to do today just to  access  data… it's ridiculous. You’d think after three years, they’d have streamlined things. Tell me about it. I spent half of Tuesday chasing people for sign-offs on a report. Like, seriously? My job is  research , not project management. It's exhausting. It’s the funding, isn’t it? Everyone’s scrambling. Remember when we were moaning about tuition fees? Feels like a lifetime ago. Now  I’m  the one contributing to the system, and it feels just as… broken. Broken is a good word. Gran keeps going on about how she worked in the shipyards, left school at 14 and had a secure job for life. Can you imagine? Secure. It's such a foreign concept now. Completely. And then you have people being made redundant left, right and centre. Old mate Dave from the pub was saying his company’s just offered voluntary severance packages. He’s gutted, but also… kinda tempted. Says the stress is killing him. Oh, poor Dave. So rough. He always seemed so happy. Remember when he tried to learn the ukulele? Oh god, yes! He was terrible. Absolutely dreadful. He was convinced he was going to be the next George Formby. Then he gave up after a week and bought a shedload of garden gnomes instead. Classic Dave. It’s funny though, isn’t it? Everyone having these little side hustles or hobbies, trying to find something to fill the void, or just make ends meet. It's like, that feeling of being ‘settled’ is just…distant. Yeah. It's a weird pressure. You’re expected to be passionate, constantly ‘improving’ yourself, and simultaneously, you need a job that pays the bills. Speaking of passions... have you seen that  Wicked  is coming to Cambridge? No way!  Wicked ? Seriously? Yeah! Tickets go on sale tomorrow. I was thinking… we should try and get some? It’s cheesy, I know, but I've always wanted to see it. Cheesy is good! I love a bit of cheese. And Elphaba is iconic. We absolutely have to. Are we talking matinee or evening? Honestly, I'll take whatever we can get. It feels like we haven't done anything fun in ages. I was leaning towards evening. It’s a bit more… dramatic, isn't it? Plus, we can grab dinner beforehand. Although, knowing my luck, I’ll be fighting with website crashes all night trying to get tickets.

Oh, that’s lovely, isn’t it? The colours are really bright. Do you think little Leo would like it? It’s a bit… busy, maybe? Yeah, it’s good. I reckon he’d love the dinosaur on the front. He’s obsessed with them at the moment, everything has to be a dinosaur. He even tried to convince me his toast was a Stegosaurus this morning. Aye, that  is  a bright one. All those colours. When I was teaching, we had a book like that… kept the wee ones entertained for ages, just pointing at everything. It's a nice idea, the whole thing, isn’t it? About a little badger who loses his favourite toy? Reminds me a bit of when Liam – my stepson, you remember Liam? – lost his teddy. He was inconsolable for days. Yeah, I remember. You were telling me about it last time I was over. He carried that bear  everywhere . Boys and their teddies. My own son, Alistair, had a wee rabbit. Called it Reginald. Reginald went  everywhere  with him. Even to his football matches! Imagine. A rabbit on the sidelines. Oh, that’s brilliant. It’s funny the things they get attached to, isn't it? It makes you wonder what Leo will fixate on. Maybe a specific spoon? Or a sock? Probably. He’s got a thing for socks at the moment, keeps trying to put them on his head. It's… a look. They’re at a funny age, aren’t they? Full of surprises. It’s good you’re documenting it all, though. All these little moments. Well, I was thinking, maybe we could put a little story together, a proper book. With pictures. I've got loads of photos of Leo being… Leo. That's a really good idea, Mum! We could even get Gran to help with the… the storytelling bit. She’s brilliant at making up tales. Och, I’d be happy to. I've got a head full of stories, you know. All those years with the wee ones, you collect a few. We could build around his sock obsession. “Leo and the Lost Socks!” Has a ring to it, doesn’t it? It does! Or maybe something about the dinosaur toast? We could get creative. It'd be good for him to have something… a wee piece of family history, don’t you think? Especially with everything being a bit… split up these days.

Honestly though, I’m dreading going back to that cafe. Why? What happened? Did old man Hemmings give you grief again? Worse. Remember how I was saying they offered me more shifts? Yeah? The ones on Saturday mornings? Aye, well…Mrs. Higgins. She was  proper  intense about my arm hair. No way! Your arm hair? What did she say? She literally asked me, mid-latte art, if I planned on “cultivating a full-bodied forest” on my arms. A forest! Oh my god, she did not! That’s… aggressive. I know! She was all, “Health and safety, dear, think of the hygiene!” Like I’m single-handedly bringing down the entire cafe’s sanitation rating. Seriously? She’s mental. It’s just arm hair. Most people have it. Exactly! And it’s not even that bad. It’s just…there. I felt like I needed to apologise for being a naturally hairy human being. Ugh. Some people are just awful. I hate it when people comment on other people’s bodies. It’s so rude. Tell me about it. I nearly told her to mind her own business, but then I remembered I needed the money for textbooks. Fair enough. Student life, eh? Trading dignity for education. Basically. I’m seriously considering just shaving both arms every shift. Oh, don’t do that! That sounds awful. All that shaving. You’ll get ingrown hairs and it’ll be a nightmare. I know, I know. It’s a slippery slope to full-body hair removal. But the thought of another “forest” comment… Just tell her it’s a stylistic choice. Embrace the fluff! Hmm… maybe. Or I could just wear long sleeves. Even in summer. That's dedication. Although slightly concerning. Honestly, just ignore her. She’ll get bored eventually.
