You think so? She seems like the type who’d hold a grudge about arm hair for years. Well, even if she does, you’ll be earning money and avoiding awkward conversations. Win-win, sort of. Have you told anyone else about this? Just Liam. He thought it was hilarious. He’s suggested I start calling myself ‘The Woodland Nymph’. Oh, Liam. He’s awful. But yeah, Woodland Nymph has a ring to it. I hope this meets your requirements! Let me know if you’d like any adjustments or additions. I hope this meets your requirements! Let me know if you’d like any adjustments or additions.

…and honestly, the sheer arrogance of thinking you could just… invent a new letter. Like, what are you even  doing ? I know, right? He was so serious though! Said the current alphabet was ‘limiting’. Limiting! As if we haven’t managed perfectly well for centuries. Said it needed a symbol for… I don’t even remember what, some esoteric concept. Sounds like a postgraduate seminar gone wrong. Seriously though, the idea that you could just  add  something to something so fundamental… It’s like redesigning the wheel. Or deciding gravity needs a rethink. Exactly! Speaking of rethinking things… this pint is going down a bit  too  easily. Fancy another? Don’t mind if I do. Though, I’m already contemplating the impending hangover. I swear, Cambridge pubs have a way of making the alcohol sneak up on you. It's the scholarly atmosphere, I reckon, makes you feel less guilty. It’s a valid theory. Though, I think it’s just strong beer. You know, I was reading an article about the increase in spiking incidents… It’s terrifying. Makes you think twice about leaving your drink unattended. It’s awful. And it’s not just drinks, is it? There’s a worrying trend of people slipping stuff into… well, anything, really. It's a complete violation. Reminds me of that documentary I saw about the boxing scene in the nineties… the whole thing was riddled with dodgy promoters and substances. Oh, the boxing thing? I remember hearing about that. Terrible. All that pressure to win… and the shortcuts people take. It’s a really brutal world. Brutal is an understatement. Speaking of brutal, did you see that match on Saturday? The one in Italy? The racist abuse directed at that Black player? Absolutely sickening. I did. And it’s just… relentless, isn’t it? You think things are getting better, then something like that happens and you’re just hit with the reality of how much work still needs to be done. It’s especially frustrating because football  should  be a unifying force. It should. But it's become a breeding ground for that kind of behaviour. The authorities need to come down harder, and the fans... well, some fans clearly need a serious education. Honestly, it makes you question supporting the sport sometimes. I know. It feels almost complicit, contributing to something so messed up. But then you think about the players who  aren’t  involved in that, the ones who just want to play the game… it’s a tricky one.

…and the planning officer, bless her, was adamant. Absolutely adamant. No modern insulation, period. Said it would ‘compromise the breathability’ of the walls. Oh, they’re good, aren't they? The breathability argument. It’s become a bit of a mantra. Though, honestly, on a building of that age, you’ve got to consider it. Mid-18th century, right? Lime plaster is key. Exactly. Which is why I was leaning towards the lime render anyway, but she was still worried about it impacting the original façade. Said it needed to be ‘reversible’. Reversible is the watchword these days. They want everything to be able to be undone in, say, fifty years. As if anyone’s going to go ripping off painstakingly applied lime render! It’s madness. Have you showed her the detailed spec? The ratios of lime to sand, the aggregate size? Of course. Several times. I even included diagrams showing the layering process. Still wasn’t enough. She wants a full conservation statement, and an impact assessment… for a garden shed! A garden shed? Seriously? What’s the shed attached to, the crown jewels? Effectively! It’s within the curtilage of a Grade II listed farmhouse. Apparently, that changes everything. It’s driving me mad. I’m trying to steer the client towards a timber frame structure, sympathetic to the style, but she’s set on brick. Brick is…challenging. You’ll be fighting that one, I suspect. Have you considered sourcing reclaimed bricks? It’s expensive, obviously, but it ticks all their ‘authentic materials’ boxes. I have, but finding a sufficient quantity that matches the existing brickwork is proving impossible. It's a locally sourced, rather unusual colour. And the client's budget is already… tight. Tight, as in ‘barely covers the tea and biscuits’ tight? Something like that. She’s hoping to get a heritage lottery fund grant, but she’s woefully unprepared for the application process. She thinks it’s just a matter of filling in a form. Oh dear. Oh, dear, dear, dear. You need to gently, very gently, explain the level of detail they require. Business plans, long-term sustainability reports, community engagement strategies… it’s a full-time job to write those applications properly. Have you worked with them before? No. I've only dabbled. Mostly smaller applications for things like window repairs. This is a whole different level. I'm thinking of suggesting a specialist consultant, but she’ll balk at the cost.

Right, so I was reading this paper on dialect levelling in Yorkshire, and it’s  fascinating . They’re finding that younger speakers are adopting more standard pronunciations, but it’s not a complete loss of regional accent, it's more… a kind of smoothing out. Like, the really distinctive features are disappearing first, but there’s still a noticeable difference from, say, RP. Interesting. Is that purely down to social mobility, do you think? People wanting to sound ‘neutral’ to avoid being judged? It’s a huge part of it, I think. And the media, obviously. Exposure to standard accents on TV and radio. But also, the paper suggested increased internal migration within Yorkshire itself – people moving around, mixing up different sub-dialects. It speeds up the process. Makes sense. It’s happened a lot in Birmingham, hasn’t it? The Brummie accent is… let’s say, less prevalent than it used to be. My grandma used to sound completely unrecognisable to anyone outside the city centre. Exactly! It's the same with Geordie, actually. You get a lot of people around Newcastle who’ve moved in for uni or work, and their kids pick up a milder version. It’s a weird sort of linguistic blending. Which, obviously, is what I'm researching, although with a slightly different focus. Still, it’s amazing how much variation there is, even within relatively small areas. You spend your whole life thinking it’s just ‘an accent’ and then you start looking at the phonetics and the socio-linguistics and it’s a whole world of complexity. It really is. It’s why I love it. Honestly, sometimes I wish I’d done a proper linguistics degree instead of all the social policy stuff. Although, that's probably useful for the qualitative side of things. Anyway, tea almost ready – milk and sugar as usual? Please. You know me too well. Speaking of needing a break from research… any thoughts on holidays this year? I was looking at Italy, but it seems ridiculously expensive at the moment. Italy  is  pricey. We were thinking about maybe going back to Scotland. We had a brilliant time up in the Highlands a couple of years ago. It’s not cheap, but it’s a lot more manageable than trying to squeeze into Tuscany in August. Scotland… hmm. That’s a good shout. I haven’t been to the Highlands since I was a kid.

Mummy, at school today, Leo ate all his broccoli. Did he? Well done, Leo! That’s brilliant. You didn’t eat yours, did you, William? No. It was…green. It’s good for you though. It makes you big and strong. I’m already big and strong. You are very strong, aren’t you? Right. Are you both enjoying your school dinners? They’re okay. Sometimes they have chips. And sausages! Good. Is the food at school better than at Granny’s? Be honest. Granny’s is better. She makes really good roast potatoes. And gravy. And she lets us have pudding first. Oh, she does, does she? Well, that’s Granny for you. She’s a bit of a rebel. Now, about the school tennis tournament next week… Mrs. Davies sent a note saying they need £5 for William to participate. Do we have that handy? I think so. I put some money aside. Let me check my purse. Tennis is fun! I hope I win. I’m sure you’ll do your best, darling. And even if you don't win, it's good exercise. Now, Ronald, did you remember to tell Mrs. Davies about your allergy? Oh yes, I did. She said she’d make sure there are no nuts in anything you’re given. Excellent. Good thinking. I’m glad that’s sorted. You know, when I was little, school dinners were…well, they weren’t very good. It was all sort of grey meat and overcooked vegetables. Ewwww. Was it? It was. But then, Granny always packed me a little extra something. Usually a biscuit or a piece of fruit. I wish I could join the circus. The circus? What makes you say that? I want to be a clown! And ride a tiny bicycle. Oh goodness. Well, that would be something! Do you know what clowns do, William? It’s lots of hard work, you know. And you have to be able to make people laugh. I can make people laugh! Watch!  makes a silly face   giggles  Oh, you are funny. You are a very funny boy. But being in the circus would mean travelling a lot, and maybe not seeing us very much. Oh. Maybe you could just be a clown for a day? At a party? Yeah! I could be a clown at my birthday party. Now that's a good idea.

Honestly, the special effects were just… exhausting. Like, relentlessly bombarding you. It felt less like a story and more like a theme park ride. Oh, I know what you mean. All flash and bang. I preferred the older ones, more…character driven. Though, mind you, my eyesight isn’t what it was. Everything’s a bit of a blur these days. I agree with you both. It was visually impressive, no question, but it lacked substance. It felt like they spent the entire budget on the CGI and forgot to hire a decent screenwriter. Speaking of substance, did anyone catch that history debate at the Union the other night? Just bits and pieces. I tried to watch the livestream but grading papers…you know how it is. Was it as heated as I heard? Heated is putting it mildly. There was a real clash between the traditionalists and those pushing for a more…inclusive approach. A lot of talk about decolonizing the curriculum. Decolonizing? What does that even  mean ? History  is  about empires and conquest and all the messy bits. You can’t just gloss over that. It's not about glossing over it, Dad. It’s about presenting a more nuanced view. Recognizing the perspectives of the colonized, not just the colonizers. It’s about challenging the traditional narratives. Exactly. The argument, as I understood it, was that the current national curriculum still presents a very Eurocentric view of history. And frankly, it does. I mean, how much time do they really spend on pre-colonial Africa, or the complexities of Asian history? Not nearly enough. And it feeds into so many problematic assumptions. I try to address it in my lessons, but it's often a struggle against the prescribed syllabus. Honestly, this curriculum feels increasingly outdated. It's almost Victorian in its approach. Victorian? I went to a proper grammar school, you know. We learned our history, and it served me perfectly well. History is about dates and battles and kings and queens! All this talk about perspective…it's just wishy-washy. Dad, with all due respect, the world has moved on a bit since your grammar school days. And a good education isn't just about memorizing facts, it's about critical thinking. Remember how you used to complain about the rote learning at your school? That was different! We had discipline. These days, kids are just encouraged to question everything.

Terrible weather isn’t it? Keeps going and coming. Didn’t think we’d see rain like this in July. No, you wouldn’t. Reminds me of the summer of ’66, actually. Constant drizzle, but everyone was so happy ‘cause of the football. Happy despite the weather, more like. Though, I’ve been reading about the war again…the sheer scale of it. Makes you think about what really matters. Which war are you on about, Colin? There’s been a few, you know. Oh, the First World War, mostly. Grandad Reginald fought in that, you know. Never spoke about it, not a word. Mum said he just…changed. Came back a different man. They all did, didn’t they? Shocking what they went through. My old man was in the Second one, thankfully came back relatively unscathed, though he always had nightmares. Kept a pistol under his bed, apparently. Goodness me! I didn’t know that. Your mother never mentioned it. No, she didn't. Said it frightened her. He only used to bring it out if there was a particularly bad storm, she said. Thought the house was going to be invaded, I suppose. Crazy stuff, war does things to people. It does. It’s fascinating, isn’t it, trying to trace your ancestors? I’ve been digging into the family history and found we had a cobbler way back in the 1700s. A proper, old-fashioned cobbler. That’s interesting. Mine were mostly farmers. Hard lives, I imagine. Lots of toil. Speaking of hard lives, I saw PC Davies down the shops earlier. Looking rather grim. Apparently, there's been another burglary on Elm Street. Honestly, it's getting worse, isn’t it? It is. The police are stretched thin, I think. They need more resources. It’s just…disheartening. Makes you miss the old days, when you knew everyone on the street. Now it’s all strangers. Everything's changing too fast. That’s true. Though, I’m trying to embrace some changes. I'm finally getting around to sorting out the furniture in the spare room. It’s been piling up for years. Oh, good! What are you doing with it? Well, I'm thinking of donating some to the charity shop. That old wardrobe is taking up far too much space. It's a beast, a proper Victorian thing, but it’s just not practical.

Right, so just to be clear, you’ve got Auntie Carol’s number saved, yeah? Because she keeps asking me directly and I’m trying to deflect. She wants to know  exactly  when we’re getting the stuff over to her. Yeah, yeah, got it. I texted her this morning, said we’d be in touch next week with solid dates. Hopefully that buys us some time. She's relentless, isn't she? Like a terrier with a bone. Seriously. And then Uncle Barry’s got his opinions on the mortgage, apparently. Mum said he cornered her at the garden centre and was giving her a full breakdown of interest rates. Oh, Barry. He thinks he's an economist now, does he? Probably read something in the Daily Mail. Still, means well, I suppose. You sure you’ve got all the paperwork sorted for the removal guys? Don't want any surprises. Pretty sure. I’ve made a list, checked it twice, and then checked it again. It’s mostly books, to be honest. And that ridiculous armchair Mum insisted on buying five years ago. I don’t even think  she  likes it. Oh, that monstrosity? The floral one? Yeah, she’ll be glad to be rid of that. You feeling alright, by the way? You’ve been a bit quiet. Just… a bit weird, I guess. This is the last time we’re driving this route, isn’t it? Last time we’re driving Mum back to Bedford. Feels a bit final. It does. Bit sad, actually. But it’s a good thing, isn’t it? You and Chloe getting your own place. A fresh start. Though, Northamptonshire… you’re sure about that? Isn’t it a bit…quiet? Chloe’s family's there, which is a big thing. And it’s affordable, which is even bigger. It’s a compromise, obviously. And it’s not  that  quiet. It’s got a cinema, apparently. A cinema! Fancy that. Still, Bedford's got that little Italian place, you know, the one we always go to? Best pasta this side of Rome. You’re just saying that because you have a weakness for their garlic bread. It  is  exceptional garlic bread. Speaking of food, did you remember to pack any snacks? I'm starting to feel a bit peckish. I grabbed a couple of biscuits. There's a bag in the glove compartment.

Right, so we’re pretty much set on the menu then? Salmon en croute, obviously, because she loves it, and then that roasted vegetable medley and the dauphinoise potatoes? Sounds good, Mum. Though are you sure you're not biting off a bit much with the en croute? It’s quite fiddly, isn't it? Honestly, I watched a tutorial on YouTube. Apparently, the key is really cold pastry. I reckon I can manage it. Plus, it  is  her 80th. Needs to be a bit special. I’ve already ordered the salmon from Billingsgate Market, lovely bit of Scottish salmon, should be delivered Friday morning. Billingsgate! Fancy. She’ll love that. She always says the supermarket salmon tastes…well, you know. Exactly. Now, the seating plan. This is the tricky bit. I was thinking your Auntie Carol next to Dad, to keep her occupied. And your cousin, Emily, needs to be as far away from Uncle Barry as humanly possible. Remember last Christmas? Oh god, yes. The political debate. It lasted for hours. Emily was practically in tears. Definitely good segregation there. How's Grandad doing with remembering things? Should we put him next to someone who’s good at prompting? It’s…variable. Some days he’s completely lucid, other days he's asking where your father is – and your father  is  sitting opposite him! I think putting him next to me is best. I’m quite good at subtly steering conversations. And I can prompt him with names if needed. Good plan. Have you got enough candles? She loves all the ambiance. Loads! I went a bit overboard, actually. Got those lovely pillar candles in the cream colour, and some tealights. And those little hurricane lamps. It should look really cozy. I've also been trying to declutter the dining room. I've been attacking the cupboards, found photos from… well, ages ago. Oh really? Any embarrassing ones? Oh, you know the usual. Awkward school photos, questionable fashion choices. I’ve put a few out on the sideboard, hoping it'll spark some memories. Although, knowing her, she’ll probably just complain about her hair in all of them. That sounds about right. Have you seen the new series of Great British Bake Off? Oh, a little bit. Actually, I was thinking about trying to copy one of the cakes for her birthday next year. Not this year, too much on my plate already.

Right, so I genuinely think I’m dying. My mouth is absolutely killing me. Oh no, what’s up? Did you finally get them out? Your wisdom teeth, I mean. Aye, got ‘em out Tuesday. It was supposed to be straightforward, like, two little buggers. Turns out one was… impacted. And like, growing sideways. It’s proper agony. Ouch! That sounds awful. Are there…holes? Like, big holes? I always worry about that. My mum’s friend had hers out and she had massive holes for ages. There are holes. Not  massive  holes, thankfully, but yeah, like little caves. And the taste! Oh god, the taste is vile. Like, constantly rinsing, but it just… lingers. Ugh, sounds grim. You poor thing. Are you on painkillers? Yeah, loads. They make me feel like a zombie. I just wanna sleep for a week. Which, ironically, is what I need to be doing, ‘cos we’re going back to uni next week. Brilliant timing, innit? Tell me about it. I’m dreading it. Especially now we’ve had a blissful week of sunshine and croissants. It’s gonna be a shock to the system going back to lectures and instant noodles. Exactly! Honestly, I'm not even ready for it. I’ve barely packed. And Mum’s been on at me about moving all my stuff back, which is just…another stress. Oh yeah, how’s the house move going for your parents? Is it all sorted? Sort of. They’ve exchanged contracts, so it’s happening. But Dad’s panicking about everything. He keeps saying he’s gonna end up living in a tent. Dramatic, as always. Bless him. He always was a worrier. My parents are pretty chilled, usually. Though Mum’s been going on about redecorating the spare room and I’m like, “Mum, I haven’t even moved back yet!” They’re always like that, aren’t they? Planning your life for you. I told Mum no way was I bringing half my stuff back, I’m trying to minimise, be less of a burden. She didn’t even hear me. They’re just trying to be helpful. In their own, slightly overbearing way. Hey, are you still up for going into town tomorrow? Maybe we can get some ice cream and sit by the river? Distract you from the mouth pain. Oh, yeah, definitely. That sounds amazing actually.

Right, so for the acts of kindness, I was thinking… we could bake some cookies. But lactose-free ones, for Mrs. Peterson next door. She always says how nice it is when someone thinks of her. Can we make sparkly ones? With sprinkles! We can definitely do sparkly ones! And maybe some with little red envelopes tucked underneath, for Chinese New Year? Ooh, like treasure! Can we use the chess pieces as money? The pawns could be one pence, and the knights could be five pence! That’s a brilliant idea! Yes, we can use the chess pieces. We’ll need to make a little chart so we remember how much each one is worth. Can I be in charge of the chart? I’m  really  good at drawing charts. You absolutely can. And maybe we can write little notes to go with the cookies, wishing everyone a Happy New Year. Or a good Lunar New Year, because it's not  our  New Year just yet. What's Lunar New Year? It's like New Year, but it happens at a different time of the year, and lots of people in China and other countries celebrate it with fireworks and special meals and giving red envelopes full of money. Can we have fireworks? Not  real  fireworks, darling, that's a bit dangerous. But maybe we can find some sparkly decorations to put up? And we can watch videos of fireworks online. Can we give red envelopes to Grandad and Nana too? Of course! They’d love that. Although, instead of chess piece money, we’ll use real money for them. Speaking of which, I think I saw some red envelopes in the cupboard… let’s go and look. While we’re looking, can we talk about dying my hair? I want it to be rainbow colours! Oh, rainbow hair. We’ve discussed this. It’s a bit…permanent. I think rainbow hair would be cool! Like a unicorn! It would be very colourful. But maybe we could start with something a little less…intense? Perhaps just a few streaks? We could look at pictures online. But rainbows are  awesome ! They are awesome. We’ll think about it. First, let's find those red envelopes. And then we can brainstorm some more acts of kindness. Maybe we can help Mr. Henderson with his bins? He sometimes struggles. And make him cookies too!

So, did you see that car crash on the High Street yesterday? It was  awful . Right outside Boots. Oh, no! Really? I hadn't heard. Was anyone hurt badly? I was working late, didn't even venture out after six. Apparently, yeah. Someone was trapped, the fire brigade had to come, the whole thing. I was walking back from Sarah’s and just… saw it. It made me jump. It reminded me a bit of that bit in  Alice in Wonderland  when everything gets all chaotic and confusing. Oh, that's a strange comparison, but I get what you mean. A bit overwhelming, I suppose. Poor people. It’s just awful to think about, isn’t it? Were you alright after seeing it? Yeah, I think so. It just… stayed with me a bit. It made me look at my little scar again. You know, the one on my knee from when I fell off my bike? Oh, yes! The one you got trying to be a stunt cyclist, as I recall. It’s barely noticeable now, though. I know, but it just made me think about how easily things can go wrong. And that car crash… it just felt really close. Accidents happen, unfortunately. It’s good you weren't involved. Speaking of things happening, did you finish that music project for school? The one with the costumes? Almost! We’re doing a song from  Wicked , and we have to design and make costumes. Maya is doing really well with hers, it's amazing, but mine is…okay. It's just hard to find good fabric. I’ve been looking online, but everything is so expensive. Oh, online is good for ideas, but you're right, pricey. Have you tried that fabric shop down by the station? Old Man Hemlock’s? He has all sorts of remnants. You might find something perfect for a bargain. Oh, good idea! I forgot about him. I'll go tomorrow. What about you? How was work? Anything exciting happen? Not exciting, exactly. Just the usual. Mrs. Higgins complained that I hadn't booked her a theatre ticket for  Matilda  – apparently, I promised her I would months ago. I have no recollection! Honestly. Oh, typical Mrs. Higgins! She always complains about something. She’s a bit of a drama queen. You’re not wrong. And then I got ten spam calls today! All about PPI claims.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of paperwork they had to wade through was astonishing. They were quite panicked last night, bless them. All these solar panel applications popping up all over the place, just… blanket coverage. Exactly. It's the same playbook, isn't it? They try and overwhelm, hoping people just give up. It’s what happened, in a way, with the turbines here. Initially, there was a real swell of opposition, but it just… dissipated. People got exhausted. Exhausted and confused, more like. The council’s development control committee… it’s a farce. They’re not interested in preserving the landscape, or the character of the villages. They’re just ticking boxes, aren't they? Driven by targets, by the developers’ promises. And the appeals! That's what really demoralises people. They fight tooth and nail, get a refusal, then the energy company just appeals and suddenly the whole thing is back on the table. It’s like fighting a hydra. You have to be meticulously prepared for an appeal, though. That's what I tried to tell them last night. Photos, detailed objections, citing specific planning policies… not just “it’s ugly” which, let’s face it, it often  is ! It needs to be about demonstrable harm to the environment, to local amenities, visual impact assessments… the works. It's all about the research. And that’s where these groups are usually hampered. They’re well-intentioned locals, not planning lawyers. They haven't got the time, or the resources, to really dig into it. I mean, the amount of government money that goes into  subsidising  these things rather than  researching  genuinely sustainable alternatives... it’s obscene. Exactly! It’s all about quick wins. Throw some money at wind and solar, and you can say you're hitting your carbon targets. But what about energy storage? That's the real problem, isn't it? We can generate all the renewable energy in the world, but if we can’t store it efficiently, it’s useless when the wind doesn’t blow or the sun doesn’t shine. And the technology isn't there yet, is it? Not on a large scale, anyway. There's a lot of talk about hydrogen, but... it's still so expensive. And the infrastructure required! It’s the politics of it all, isn’t it? The planners are influenced, the energy companies have deep pockets, and the protest groups are left scrambling for scraps.

So, have you booked those driving lessons yet, love? Your mother’s been on at me about it. Saying you’re getting too old to be relying on buses. Dad! I’m thirty-two, not eighty-two. And yes, I’ve booked them. Started next week, Tuesdays at 10. Hopefully, I won’t stall on the roundabout near Tesco. That place is terrifying. Oh, it is a nightmare. Especially on a Saturday. Remember when your cousin, David, nearly reversed into a fruit and veg stall there? Thought your Auntie Maureen was going to have a heart attack. Good heavens, yes. A right kerfuffle that was. And expensive, I seem to recall. Speaking of expensive, have you looked at car insurance quotes yet? Don't want you ending up paying more for the insurance than the car itself. I have, and it's… grim. Apparently, being a London resident even though I’m visiting is pushing the price up. And the car I’m looking at, a little Fiat 500, is in insurance group… twenty-something. Oh dear. A Fiat 500 is nice though. Easy to park. Your grandfather had one of those, bright red. He called her ‘Rosie’. He used to drive her everywhere. He did. Even tried to take her across country lanes barely wide enough for a bicycle. Your mother nearly went spare. Anyway, back to the insurance. Have you tried comparing websites? MoneySuperMarket and the like? Yep, done the comparison thing. It's still a lot. I might have to add my mum as a named driver, which feels a bit… embarrassing. Nonsense, dear. It’ll bring the price down. It’s common practice. Better than driving around uninsured. We’re going to need a car for the holiday, aren’t we? That's right. We’re still on for Cornwall in August, then? I've been looking at cottages online. Found one in Padstow, looks lovely. Sea view and a garden. Sounds perfect! I’m really looking forward to it. Need a break from marking essays. Honestly, the things some of them write… It’s like they haven’t even  read  the texts. Oh, teaching. Always a challenge. I had a right character in court yesterday. Claimed he was allergic to the legal system. Said it gave him hives. Allergic to the legal system! You don’t hear that every day. So, what are your plans for this week then?

Honestly Dad, parking in Brighton is a nightmare. I spent twenty minutes circling yesterday just to drop off groceries. Twenty minutes? In my day, you just found a space, parked, and got on with it. Never had this bother. Though, mind you, there weren’t half as many cars on the road then. Everything's different now. It’s just relentless. Everyone has a car, and they’re all trying to squeeze into the same tiny spaces. Makes me almost want to get rid of mine. Don’t you dare! You’ll need it to come visit your old man, won’t you? Though, I don’t see you as often as I’d like, now you’ve moved. Brighton’s a long way. I know, I know. I will come more, I promise. It's just… life gets busy. And then there's this Facebook app, it's driving me mad. It keeps sending me notifications about everything. Facebook? What’s that got to do with anything? You young people and your…digital contraptions. Everything! It’s how everyone keeps in touch. But it’s constantly beeping and buzzing. I turned off half the notifications, but it still sends me loads. It's so distracting when I’m trying to work. Switch the darn thing off then. Simple. We managed without all this technology, didn’t we? Though, I did quite enjoy the wireless back in the fifties. That was a marvel. Easier said than done, Dad. It's how I get updates from uni, and keep in touch with friends. Anyway, I made a shepherd’s pie for dinner. Hope you like it. Shepherd’s pie? Lovely. You always were a good cook, just like your mother. She could feed an army. Remember those Sunday dinners? Everyone crammed around the table. Of course. Although, feeding kids these days is so expensive. Everything’s gone up. I heard they’re using food banks more and more. It’s a disgrace, it is. Politicians promising the world and… it’s all just talk. Back in my day, a man could provide for his family on a decent wage. These days… people struggling just to get by. It’s tough. Speaking of tough, how are your knees? Still giving you trouble? Oh, they’re a right state. Arthritis, you know. Makes it hard to get around. And the weather’s not helping.

…and then Old Man Hemmings, right, he’s the head groundskeeper, walks past and just  deadpans  “Looking a bit breezy out there, are we?” Like, mate, I'm actively battling gale-force winds to hit a tiny white ball into a slightly smaller hole. It's not a casual observation, it's a personal attack. Hemmings sounds… delightful. Honestly, golf just seems engineered to breed passive-aggression. The whole quiet contemplation thing is a lie. It’s just frustration management with expensive clubs. Exactly! And everyone pretends to be so zen about it. “Oh yes, well a slightly duffed shot is just a learning opportunity.” No, it’s a wasted five pounds and a dent to my fragile ego. Speaking of fragile egos, did you read Professor Davies' essay on  Hamlet ? Oh god, the one where he tries to argue that Hamlet is actually a deeply sarcastic comedian? The very one. He just kept going on about “subtextual wit” and “ironic detachment.” I'm pretty sure Hamlet's just profoundly depressed and wants everyone to die. Davies is convinced he’s the Richard Pryor of Elsinore. It’s his surname, isn’t it? Davies. He  has  to find irony everywhere. My uncle’s a Davies, and the man can’t accept a genuine compliment without questioning the motivation. “Oh, you like my tie? Is this some sort of subtle dig at my financial situation?” Classic Davies. My grandma's a Pritchard, and they're all fiercely competitive. Even over… well, everything. Apparently, family Christmas is basically the Hunger Games with board games. Sounds intense. What about nicknames? Did your family have those? We were all just called what we were called, no fun shortened versions. Loads. My cousin Rhys was always “Rhino” because he was built like a tank, even as a kid. I was… annoyingly, “Little Skip” for about five years. Don't ask. Something about me skipping everywhere when I was tiny. It haunted me through secondary school. “Little Skip”? Oh, brutal. I can see why you’d develop a sarcastic defence mechanism. I worked at that garden centre over the summer, remember? The one near the A38? God, yes. Full of pensioners and aggressively cheerful floral displays. It was soul-crushing. Mrs. Higgins, the manager, was convinced we were all secretly plotting against her. She kept asking us to write down exactly what we were doing, every fifteen minutes.

Honestly, this week has been  mental  at work. Like, back-to-back meetings, everything last minute. Someone pulled out of presenting at the conference, so I had to find a replacement at, like, ten o’clock on Tuesday morning. Nightmare. Sounds rough, yeah. I’m just… physical work, you know? Gets tiring, but it’s not mentally draining like that. Though today, unloading that van in the rain… my back is screaming. Oh, you poor thing! You need a hot bath and a serious lie-down. I had a surprisingly calm week, actually. Managed to get through all my reports without being interrupted once. Felt like a minor miracle. Although, Brenda in accounts keeps asking me about my “lifestyle choices.” Oh god, Brenda. What does  that  even mean? Apparently, coming in with a green smoothie every day is a “lifestyle choice.” And she made a comment about needing “proper food.” Honestly, the cheek! I just said I was trying to be healthy. Proper food is a roast dinner, that's what it is. Not rabbit food. Though, I gotta admit, I've been trying to cut down on the takeaways. Bank balance is taking a beating. Tell me about it! I’ve been trying this new diet, it's supposed to be amazing, but it's all kale and quinoa. I miss chips. So much. Kale and quinoa? Seriously? That sounds… depressing. I’m more of a “everything in moderation” kind of gal. Although, I did start going to that yoga class with Chloe. Oh, how’s that going? Is it all chanting and incense? A bit, yeah. But actually, it’s pretty good. Really helps to unwind. Better than scrolling through TikTok for three hours, which is what I usually do. Speaking of Chloe, she’s still looking for a flatmate, isn’t she? Yeah, I think so. She mentioned it last week. Said her last one was… interesting. “Interesting” is code for chaotic, isn't it? Chloe attracts chaos. Remember when her boyfriend tried to build a hydroponic farm in her living room? Oh my god, how could I forget? It was a disaster! The whole flat smelled like wet lettuce. Honestly, you guys have the best stories. My life is just… lifting things and getting wet. Although, I am thinking of finally getting that motorbike I’ve been saving for. Oh, that's awesome! You've been talking about that for ages.

Right then, well come on through, you can see the garden properly now. Bit overgrown, mind you. Didn’t get a chance to tackle it properly this year, what with everything. Looks alright to me, Arthur. A bit of nature never hurt anyone. Though your roses are looking a bit peaky. Need a good feed, they do. Lovely though. It’s so nice to have a garden, isn’t it? Makes all the difference. Especially with the eclipse coming up. Imagine being able to watch it from here. That's the plan, Doreen. Provided the clouds stay away. Though, knowing our luck… Still, even if we only get a glimpse, it'll be something. Remember the last one? Back in ‘99, wasn’t it? Vaguely. I was probably complaining about the telly needing a new aerial then. Speaking of which, has the TV licence renewal come through yet? Don’t want a visit from those chaps. Sent it off ages ago. Should be here any day now. More worrying is the state of old Mrs. Higgins' bamboo. It’s spreading like wildfire, it is. Soon be over the fence and into our garden. Oh dear. Have you said anything to her? Tried, but she’s a bit deaf, and keeps saying it ‘adds character’. Character! It’s a jungle, it is! And then young Kevin over the back… He’s putting up a new fence, but it's a foot over the boundary line. Trying to claim extra land, the cheeky beggar. People are getting away with murder these days. No respect for property rights. Though, I must say, that painting programme on last night was quite good. The chap showing how to mix colours… fascinating. Oh? I missed that one. Was it one of those ‘Bob Ross’ type things? Happy little trees and all that? Not quite. More about landscapes. Oils, mostly. And rather politically correct, actually. The presenter kept saying things like “we’re not going to  depict  the landscape, we’re going to  respond  to it”. Honestly! Politically correct nonsense. It's the world gone mad, I tell you. Still, a bit of art is good for the soul. Though, speaking of souls, have you been reading about these black holes? Makes you think, doesn't it? What was there before the beginning? Ah, now you’re talking. I've been watching a documentary on the cosmos. Extraordinary stuff.

Right, so I was thinking, for dinner, we could try that new Italian place, Bella Notte? Apparently, it’s where the old post office used to be, near the cathedral. Have you heard anything about it? Bella Notte… vaguely. I think Liam mentioned it. Said it was a bit pricey, but good. Though Liam thinks anything over a tenner is ‘pricey’ these days. He's still on a student budget in his mind, I reckon. Fair enough. Though, honestly, I’m starting to feel like  I’m  on a student budget. Rent’s gone up again. It’s ridiculous. They’re building those new flats down by the river, aren't they? The ones overlooking the Wear? Yeah, the ‘Riverside Residences’ or something? Dreadful name. They look… sterile. All glass and steel. No character at all. And they're charging a fortune for them. Exactly! They’re basically saying Sunderland’s become Dubai overnight. It’s just… houses are getting too expensive, you know? Even just decent terraces. It’s the same down south, trust me. Harpenden is… bonkers. Everything is overpriced. I was looking at places with my mum last weekend, even just a little bungalow, and they were asking for… well, let’s just say it would make your eyes water. Oh, I can imagine. Still, at least Harpenden is… pretty. Sunderland’s got its charm, but it's a bit rough around the edges sometimes. You know, like driving through Hetton-le-Hole last night? The potholes… Oh, God, yeah. It was like navigating an obstacle course. Seriously, the council needs to do something about those roads. You could lose a tyre down there. And the buses… don’t even get me started on the buses. I know! Always late, always overcrowded. I swear, sometimes I think it's faster to walk. Speaking of walking, did you see the scaffolding around the cathedral? They're doing some work on the west front, I think. Oh yeah, I noticed that. It looks… major. Wonder what they’re doing? Hopefully, not damaging the stonework. It's a beautiful building, even if it's not quite as grand as Durham. Definitely not Durham, but it’s got a history, hasn’t it? And it looks amazing lit up at night. Anyway, back to dinner. Bella Notte or… do you fancy Indian? There’s that place on Stockton Road, ‘Spice Delight’. Spice Delight… hmm.

…and honestly, it was insistent. Not a gentle little chirp, a full-blown announcement. I thought it was a robin at first, but it was too complex a song. Oh, you and your birdsong! You're becoming quite the expert, aren't you? I just hear ‘bird’, honestly. Though, I did manage to identify a blackbird the other day. Purely by process of elimination, mind you. They’re the common ones, aren’t they? They  are  common, but that’s no reason to dismiss the intricacies of their vocalizations! It was definitely a warbler, I reckon. A chiffchaff, maybe? I've downloaded an app now, you see. You can record it and it tells you what it is. It's utterly brilliant. Goodness me. Technology. I still struggle with setting the timer on the cooker. Speaking of which, I need to get a new alarm clock. Mine’s developed a habit of going off at 3 am. Wakes the whole house, it does. Oh, that's dreadful! Is it one of those digital ones with multiple alarms? Sometimes I accidentally set two, and then it's a cacophony. No, it’s an old-fashioned one. With bells. I’ve changed the batteries, but it still does it. I think the mechanism's just… given up the ghost. It's a sign, isn't it? A sign I need to embrace silence. Although, that's difficult when you’ve got a cat demanding breakfast at five. I know the feeling. And speaking of demanding feeders… the birds are going through a fortune. I’ve filled the feeders twice this week already. The blue tits are particularly greedy. They are, aren't they? Little bandits. I haven’t put much seed out recently, actually. I had a bit of a scare at the dentist last week. Oh no! What happened? Just a routine check-up, but he spotted a tiny erosion on one of my back teeth. Apparently, it's quite common with age… acidity. He had to do a bit of filling. Honestly, the thought of it! And I kept imagining the drill… It sent me into a bit of a state. Had a nosebleed afterwards, believe it or not. Oh, you poor thing! That sounds awful. Nosebleeds are always so alarming. They are. Thankfully it stopped quickly. Makes you think about looking after yourself, doesn’t it? I really should get back into the garden.

Honestly, it’s just… exhausting. The relentless scrolling. Everyone presenting this perfect version of their lives. It’s draining. Tell me about it. I deactivated my Facebook account last year. Best thing I ever did. Although, admittedly, it makes keeping up with some people… tricky. Like Auntie Mabel, she only communicates via Facebook now. Oh, bless her. Mine’s my cousin, Brenda. She sends me links to conspiracy theories about 5G. Honestly, I used to just ignore them, but then she started tagging me in them publicly. So embarrassing. Oh dear. It's like they forget you have a real life outside of that little blue screen. How is little Leo? Is he still a whirlwind? A whirlwind is putting it mildly. He's seven now, and… well, he’s all energy. I swear he doesn’t  walk  anywhere. It's either a sprint or a jump. It's wonderful, truly. But it's also… a lot, doing it all on my own. You’re brilliant, you know that. Honestly. Raising a child single-handedly, while also being a dedicated teacher… you’re a superwoman. Flattery will get you everywhere! Though, sometimes I do wonder if I made the right decision, you know? Going through IVF... it was so emotionally and physically draining. Then, when it didn’t work, and I realized I wanted to be a mum  so  badly… it just felt like everything fell apart. I remember. You were so strong throughout it all, though. I always admired that. Remember how we used to talk about having huge families? It's funny to think back on those naive dreams. Oh god, yes. Fifteen kids and a pony, if I remember correctly. Life had other plans, I suppose. Speaking of plans, how's the social work going? Still battling the system? Always battling the system. It's… rewarding, but utterly soul-destroying at times. The bureaucracy, the caseloads, the endless paperwork… I’m seriously considering a career change. Oh really? What are you thinking of doing? You always had a creative streak. I've been toying with the idea of becoming a yoga instructor. It's been such a lifeline for me, honestly. After a particularly horrible day with a case, just going to a class and stretching and breathing… it’s the only thing that keeps me sane. Plus, I’ve been documenting some of my thoughts and experiences, and a few friends have suggested I write a book.

Honestly, the traffic was dreadful getting over here. I thought I’d be stuck forever on the A38. Oh, tell me about it. It's getting worse, isn't it? They say they're going to do something about the flyover near Spaghetti Junction, but I’ll believe it when I see it. Used to be able to nip across town in fifteen minutes, now it’s forty if you’re lucky. It’s ridiculous. Though I suppose it’s a small price to pay for actually  living  in Birmingham. I still miss Hertfordshire sometimes, but there’s a…buzz here, isn’t there? There is, aye. And people are friendlier. Hertfordshire, didn’t sound very friendly to me. All those commuter belts and fancy houses… You’ve got me there. It’s definitely a different pace of life. So, how are you keeping, then? Still managing to get out in the garden? Trying to. My knees are playing up a bit, though. Doctor says it’s just wear and tear. Apparently, decades of marking essays doesn’t do wonders for the joints. Oh dear. You must have marked thousands over the years. My partner’s a teacher too, secondary school, and he’s the same. Always complaining about his back. It's a demanding job, teaching. Glad I’m finished with it, to be honest. Though I do miss the kids sometimes. Especially the ones who actually  wanted  to learn. You teach languages, don’t you? I do. French and Spanish, mostly. It’s lovely when you get a class that's really engaged. But you get a few who just… don’t see the point. Ah, the “When am I ever going to use this?” brigade. Heard that one more times than I care to remember. My subject was history, and you’d get the same. “Why do we need to know about the Tudors?” Exactly! You try explaining the importance of cultural understanding and they just glaze over. Actually, speaking of history…did you hear about that attempted robbery at the jewellery shop on the High Street? No! What happened? Apparently, they tried to smash the window with a hammer, but the alarm went off and they ran off empty-handed. Honestly, it's getting a bit scary around here. It is. Used to be a safe area, this. Seems like there’s more trouble these days. Though, knowing Birmingham, it'll be on the news for a day and then everyone will forget about it.

Right, so who’s bringing snacks for the film tonight? I’m happy to do a supermarket run if needed. Ooh, good thinking. I was planning on just bringing some biscuits, but a full supermarket haul would be much appreciated. Maybe crisps, chocolate…? I can contribute some dips and, like, veggie sticks. Trying to be vaguely healthy, you know? Though I fully expect to demolish a load of chocolate later. I’m happy to grab some drinks. Soft drinks, maybe some beers? Anyone got preferences? Beers would be good, yeah. As long as there’s some decent non-alcoholic options too, for the designated drivers amongst us. And definitely chocolate. You can’t have a film night without chocolate. Agreed. What are we even watching again? I was scrolling through Netflix earlier and got utterly lost in the options. We settled on that new sci-fi thriller, “Echo Protocol,” didn’t we? The one Leo was raving about? Ah, yeah, Leo said it’s brilliant. Apparently, the soundtrack is insane too. He’s a bit of a film buff. Leo always has strong opinions on everything. Remember when he tried to convince us that Abba were objectively the greatest band of all time? Oh god, yes! He was  so  insistent. I still think the Bee Gees are superior, sorry Leo. He’s a good lad though. Always up for a debate. Speaking of music, anyone been listening to anything good lately? I’ve been stuck in a 90s Britpop phase. Oh, nice! I'm revisiting some early Radiohead myself. “The Bends” still holds up incredibly well. I've been listening to a lot of jungle and drum and bass recently. Bit of a throwback, but it’s perfect for getting stuff done. Although, my neighbours might disagree. I can imagine! I've been exploring some Icelandic electronica - Sigur Rós, Björk. Very atmospheric stuff, good for winding down after work. Ooh, I’ll have to check that out. I’m always looking for new music. Right, so supermarket run, drinks, dips, biscuits... are we sorted? Should we coordinate who's getting what specifically? I’m happy to do the beer and soft drinks run. Let’s say I’ll grab those. I'll do the main grocery shop then – crisps, chocolate, maybe some popcorn. And I can pick up some extra biscuits if needed. Perfect! It’s going to be a good night.

Honestly, the gym was rammed this morning. Like, shoulder-to-shoulder rammed. Couldn't get near the squat rack. Oh, no way! That’s awful. I’ve been meaning to go back, but I’m dreading it. It was the same before Christmas, everyone making resolutions, suddenly deciding they're athletes. It’s always worse in January, isn’t it? Though, I’ve found if I go really early, like 6am, it's usually manageable. Painfully early, but manageable. Six AM? You’re a psychopath. I can barely  think  at six AM, let alone lift weights. I’m more of a lunchtime gym-goer, but even then, it’s getting busy. Yeah, lunchtime's a no-go. Too many people trying to squeeze it in. Speaking of squeezing things in, have you guys started thinking about summer holiday plans? A little. I was looking at Cornwall again. We went last year, remember? Had a decent time, despite the rain for the first three days. Cornwall’s nice. A bit… predictable though, isn’t it? I’m tempted by Italy this year. Somewhere in Tuscany, maybe. Just imagine the food. Tuscany sounds amazing. Proper sunshine too, hopefully. This weather we’ve been having is just… depressing. Grey, grey, grey. It’s like living in a black and white film. It is grim, isn’t it? I saw a forecast saying we might get a heatwave in August, though. Fingers crossed. I'm thinking of backpacking around Southeast Asia, if I can swing it. Oh, wow! That sounds incredible. Expensive though, surely? Yeah, it’ll be a stretch. But I've been saving, and I'm hoping to find some cheap flights. And hostels, obviously. Not looking for luxury. Smart. Hostels are the way to go. You get to meet people. Speaking of meeting people, has anyone heard anything more about that kids' camp for Leo? I emailed them yesterday, still waiting for a response. Apparently, they're really popular. Hoping he can get a place. It’d be a good break for everyone. A week of peace and quiet… It would be! Though, I’ll probably spend the whole week worrying about whether he’s having a good time. Mum-life, eh? Tell me about it. I’m still on the fence about getting a dog. It sounds amazing, but then I remember all the responsibility… Dogs are great. Just be prepared for early morning walks in the rain.

Oh, that was a dodgy tackle, wasn’t it? Right in front of the ref. Absolutely. Should have been a yellow, minimum. They’re letting them get away with murder today. Honestly, it's frustrating to watch. They always do this when it’s a big game. Give the benefit of the doubt. It’s ridiculous. I’ve got money on this, you know. You and your football bets. Honestly, you're addicted. How much have you risked this time? Not too much! Just a tenner on a Liverpool win. Seemed a safe bet at the start. Now I'm not so sure. A tenner is a tenner. It all adds up. Are you still hoping for a decent Easter weekend? We haven't really talked about plans. Yeah, definitely. I was thinking maybe a drive out to the coast on Sunday? Somewhere with a good pub lunch? That sounds lovely. Somewhere not  too  busy, though. Everywhere gets rammed over Easter. I’m half tempted just to stay in and binge-watch something. Oh come on! You’ve been cooped up working on that thesis for weeks. You need fresh air. And a proper pub meal. You’re right, you’re right. I need to embrace the outdoors, even if it's just for a few hours. What films have you been wanting to see? Anything good out at the moment? There’s that new sci-fi one, “Echo Bloom”. Everyone’s saying it’s visually stunning. But I'm also up for a rewatch. We haven't seen “Spirited Away” in ages. “Spirited Away” is always a good shout. Classic. Okay, coast on Sunday, “Spirited Away” sometime over the weekend. Deal. Deal! Right, pay attention. Looks like they're building up an attack... Oh! And he scores! About time. Finally! Okay, maybe your tenner isn't lost after all. Though I still think the ref is biased. Honestly, you're obsessed with the referee. Just enjoy the goal! Come on! Liverpool! Easy for you to say, you’re the one with skin in the game. I'm just a neutral observer subjected to questionable officiating. You choose to be a neutral observer. You secretly support Arsenal, don't you? Absolutely not! Don't be ridiculous. I’ve seen the evidence. The subtle sighs when they lose. The overly enthusiastic cheers when they unexpectedly win. That’s just… basic empathy for the human condition.

Ah, look at this one. Little terror, wasn’t he? Covered head to toe in mud after… what was that, a fun fair? Yeah! That was in Weston-super-Mare. He won a goldfish. Remember, Mum? It died after like, a day. Oh, the poor thing. He was heartbroken. He named it… Finley, wasn’t it? He was  convinced  it understood him. Oh, children and their goldfish. It’s a classic. I had a wee boy in my class once who swore his goldfish was a spy for the Russians. Said it kept staring at the map! That’s brilliant! He got that from somewhere, that one. Speaking of maps, does anyone remember when we tried to take him to Iceland? Iceland? Seriously? Oh, don't remind me. That was a disaster. He refused to get on the plane. Full-blown meltdown. He just kept screaming, “Too cold! Too many elves!” We ended up having to turn around. The airline staff weren’t thrilled, I can tell you that much. Oh dear! That sounds… stressful. Maybe Iceland wasn’t the best choice for a seven-year-old. Though, I suppose he wasn’t entirely wrong about the elves. They say Iceland is full of them, you know. He still talks about elves sometimes. He’s making a film at school about them. It’s supposed to be really cool. That’s lovely. He's always been imaginative. Look at this picture - he’s all kitted out for the London Marathon. Remember when your father decided he was going to run it? Don’t even get me started. He hadn't run a bath in twenty years, let alone a marathon! He barely made it to mile five. He looked  rough  at the end. Mum made him a banner saying "Go Dad… slowly!" I did! It was the least I could do. Although, I did suggest he just walk it. It would’ve been far more sensible. Sensible isn’t always the most fun, dear! Still, I admire his ambition. And look at that film he made, there. Remember when he filmed us all at the cinema? Honestly, it was wobbly, out of focus, and entirely too long. But it was  his  film. He was so proud of it. He made us watch it about twenty times. He's a good lad, isn't he? It’s crazy how fast they grow up.

Honestly, this shepherd’s pie is amazing, Mum. You’ve really outdone yourself. It tastes exactly like Nana used to make. Oh, well that’s lovely to hear dear. It's just the usual recipe, nothing fancy. Though, I did use a different lamb mince this time, a bit more flavour, I think. Your Nana always said a good mince was half the battle. She was right! And you’ve got the potato topping  just  right – crispy on top, fluffy underneath. It’s an art form, honestly. Remember when I tried to make it and it was just…soggy? Oh god, yes! It was like mashed potato soup with a bit of lamb in it. We teased you for weeks. I  know ! It was mortifying. I think I just didn't preheat the oven enough. It's a learning curve, isn't it? Speaking of learning curves, have you started that new knitting pattern yet? The cable knit cardigan? Not yet. I’ve been meaning to, but work has been absolutely manic. I keep staring at the yarn, willing it to knit itself! I did finish the little baby blanket for Sarah’s friend though. She had her little boy last week. That's lovely, dear. You always were good with your hands. I remember when you used to spend hours making little outfits for your dolls. What were those dolls called again? Oh, goodness. It was a whole saga. There was Penelope, and Beatrice, and then I had a Sindy, and later a Barbie. I used to make clothes for them out of old scraps of fabric. Awful things, looking back. That’s so sweet! I was more of a games person. Do you remember ‘French Cricket’? We used to play it in the garden for hours. Oh my god, yes! With the bat made out of a broom handle? And you were  fiercely  competitive. I was! I always had to win. It was a family trait, I think. Remember Uncle George and his obsession with Scrabble? Oh, George! That man could spell anything. Even words no one had ever heard of. He always had a dictionary hidden under the table. He swore it was for checking  their  spelling, not his! Honestly, it's a small world. I was talking to a client today, and her husband went to school with George! Apparently, he was still playing Scrabble competitively, even in his eighties.

Lovely bit of bread this, isn’t it? Proper crusty. It is nice. From that little bakery down the road, wasn’t it? The one with the queues. Aye, that's the one. Worth the wait though, I reckon. Much better than that sliced stuff, all soft and…well, lacking. Definitely. Remember when everything tasted of more? Everything seemed to have more flavour. Oh, you’re tellin’ me. It’s all these additives, I expect. Messin’ about with things they oughtn’t to. Used to be simple, things were. Flour, water, a bit of salt… And a lot of elbow grease! Your mother could bake a loaf that’d feed a family for days. She could, bless her. Used to say it was the secret ingredient – a pinch of love. Always said that. She was a good woman, your mother. Always had a kind word for everyone. She did. Miss her, you know. Still do, after all these years. Hardest thing, losing your mum. It is. Such a cornerstone. Everything feels a bit… unsteady afterwards. That’s it. Unsteady. I was thinkin’ earlier about that old garden she had. Full of roses, it was. Oh, I remember. And the smell! All those sweet peas climbing up the trellis. Aye. I’ve never been much of a gardener myself, mind. Always preferred a good read. Though I did try last year, with the tomatoes… And how did those go? Terrible! Blighted, they were. Little green things, all shrivelled up. Couldn't salvage a single one. Oh, that’s a shame. It’s always a bit disappointing when things don’t grow as you hoped. It is. Makes you feel a bit useless, doesn’t it? Though, I suppose readin’ a good book is a growth of sorts, eh? Growth of the mind. That’s a good way to look at it. What are you reading at the moment? I’ve started one of those detective novels. Old fashioned, you know, with a vicar and a missing will and all that. Oh, lovely. A bit of escapism. Just what you need. Exactly. And much easier than growin’ tomatoes, that’s for sure. Another bite of this sandwich? You want the crust? Oh, go on then. I do like the crust. Thank you. It really  is  a lovely sandwich. You’ve always had a good taste in bread. Learnt from the best, dear. Learnt from the best.

Honestly, the kids were  wild  today. Year twos are just… a different breed, aren’t they? One of them tried to convince me that a badger was a type of dinosaur. Oh my god, no way! That's brilliant. My year fives are obsessed with slime. Like, truly obsessed. Covered everything, including themselves. It's a nightmare to clean up. Oh, the slime. It’s a plague. My little cousin got it  everywhere  at Christmas. It was like a viscous, glittery alien invasion. Speaking of Christmas, have you guys figured out what you’re getting anyone yet? I'm completely stuck. I’m terrible at presents. I always end up getting people socks or… scented candles. It’s so boring. I was thinking of getting my mum a pottery painting session, she's been talking about wanting to try it. That's actually really thoughtful! I’m thinking a weekend away for my parents. They deserve a break. Although, honestly, just  planning  a weekend away feels like a full-time job. Coordinating childcare, booking trains… it's exhausting. Tell me about it! My aunt is convinced she needs a new car, which is code for ‘I want you to help me research new cars and then subtly convince my husband to buy it.’ It's a whole saga. Apparently, the current one's making a noise like a dying walrus. A dying walrus?! Oh, bless her. My uncle's car is always on the verge of collapse. He's perpetually 'just keeping it going' with duct tape and hope. And a lot of swearing. Sounds about right. Speaking of things falling apart, how’s work, Liv? Still battling the marketing briefs from hell? You have  no  idea. This week it’s all about ‘disruptive synergy’ and ‘leveraging core competencies’. I’m starting to suspect my boss just pulls words out of a thesaurus at random. Honestly, I’d rather be wrangling slime-covered year fives. Oh god, the corporate jargon. It’s horrific. I’m just trying to avoid parent-teacher conferences where I have to explain why little Timmy keeps drawing pictures of exploding toilets. Oh, the joys of primary teaching! Though, exploding toilets actually sound quite creative, to be fair. How's Ben? Still obsessing over his cat, Winston? Absolutely. He's convinced Winston understands complex philosophical arguments. He spends hours talking to him about existentialism. It’s… endearing, but also slightly concerning.

And then young Liam next door, right, absolutely plastered the front door with… glitter. Proper, chunky glitter. Saying it was a 'magical portal' for Harry Potter. Oh, bless him. He’s a good lad, Liam. Full of imagination, isn’t he? Though your door will be shimmering for weeks, won't it? Weeks! I tried everything. Washing up liquid, a hose, even a bit of white spirit. It’s  embedded , I tell you. Embedded. Oh, that’s awful. You'd think glitter would just wash off, but…it doesn’t. It’s the devil’s craft, glitter is. Mum, can I get another biscuit? In a minute, love. Let your dad finish telling us about the glitter attack. It sounds like a scene from a film. It  felt  like a scene from a film. A horrifying, sparkling film. It’s just… this whole street’s changing, you know? New families moving in. All well and good, but it’s not the same. It happens, doesn’t it? L8’s always been a bit of a melting pot, but it’s speeding up now, isn't it? More students, more young professionals. It's good for the area, really. Brings money in. But yeah, you lose that sense of… everyone knowing everyone. It was nice when Mrs. Higgins used to bring round her homemade pies. Exactly! Mrs. Higgins. A legend. And Old Man Hemmings, always patching up bikes for the kids. Now it’s all… estate agents and Instagram influencers. You’re painting a very bleak picture, you are. I’m just saying! I had a bloke knock on the door yesterday trying to sell me security cameras. Said there’d been a spate of… things. Things? What things? Didn’t say. Just “things.” Made it sound like ISIS had set up shop down the road. Bit dramatic, I thought. That’s awful. Makes you feel uneasy, doesn’t it? Dad, what’s ISIS? Right. Okay. We'll talk about that later. Let’s just say they're… people who cause trouble. Ignore them, love. Focus on your biscuits later. So, how’s work going, love? Still enjoying the reception job? It’s alright, Mum. Busy. A lot of phone calls, a lot of…complaints. People are always complaining. Mostly about paperwork. The eternal struggle. I’ve got a seminar on post-colonial literature next week. Trying to get my head around it.

…and honestly, the sausages at the Farm Shop are just…divine. They do a Cumberland one that’s just bursting with flavour. Not like the anaemic things you get at the Village Shop, bless ‘em. They try, but… Oh, I agree completely. Though I do pop into the Village Shop for a pint of milk if I’m desperate, it’s just…convenience, isn’t it? And Mrs. Higgins is always so cheerful. But for a proper treat, the Farm Shop wins every time. Did you try their coffee this week? They’ve changed suppliers. No, I haven’t. Is it any good? I’ve been trying to cut down, actually. All that caffeine…makes me jittery. Though, thinking of travelling, I need to be on top form for Nepal. It’s lovely! Properly strong, but smooth. Not bitter at all. And speaking of Nepal, have you finalised the itinerary, Brenda? Are you taking all those vaccinations? I remember when we went to Morocco, the list was endless! Oh, Morocco! Now  that  was an adventure. David and I went in… Oh, goodness, 1988, I think. Before the children. We haggled for everything. It was exhausting, but exhilarating. Nepal will be a whole other level, won't it? Proper mountains. Yes, well, the travel agent's been very thorough. Vaccinations are booked, visas sorted…mostly. I’m more worried about the altitude. And the food. I’m taking a supply of gluten-free biscuits, just in case. You know how it is. Oh, bless you. Always prepared! It reminds me of my Mother-in-Law. She was evacuated from Siberia as a child during the war, can you imagine? Her journey took her all the way to Africa! Absolutely extraordinary. She’d always pack a tiny tin of biscuits, no matter where we went. “Just in case,” she’d say. War habit, I suppose. Their diet was so limited then, you know. Everything was rationed. It’s hard to imagine now, isn't it? My mother used to tell me stories about making meals out of whatever scraps were left. No fancy gluten-free options then! Although, oddly, she always insisted on home-made bread. She said it was “wholesome.” Speaking of food, have you seen this new free school meals system? Apparently, they’re sending out packed lunches to kids who qualify. Honestly, the content is appalling! White bread, processed meat, a tiny bit of fruit… It’s a disaster waiting to happen.

Honestly, this week at work has been  mental . Like, genuinely questioning all my life choices mental. Oh god, tell me about it. I had a five-hour meeting yesterday solely about… spreadsheets. Spreadsheets! I swear to god, if I see another pivot table… You poor thing! Five hours? That's dedication to pointless tasks. Mine's been alright, relatively speaking. Just the usual admin chaos. Old Mrs. Henderson keeps emailing me asking how to attach a photo to an email.  Again . See, that I’d almost prefer! At least that’s… human. I’m coordinating this massive conference for tech CEOs, right? And they're all so specific, so demanding. One wanted all the water bottles labelled with  his  name on, another is convinced the room temperature needs to be precisely 20.3 degrees. 20.3! Oh, the entitlement. It's always the tech CEOs, isn't it? Think they're somehow above basic human needs. Remember that time Mark at [Previous Company] wanted a specific brand of oat milk, and when we didn’t have it, threatened to pull his sponsorship? Oh, Mark. The oat milk tyrant. Honestly, it’s exhausting. And then they all expect you to anticipate their every need, like you’re a mind reader. Honestly, I miss when I was at uni. Don’t we all? No responsibility, just… questionable life decisions and instant noodles. Exactly! Although, I think my questionable life decisions are following me into adulthood. I’m starting to think I need a proper holiday, just to disconnect. You should! Where would you go? Somewhere with no Wi-Fi, perhaps? Force them to actually…talk to each other. Ooh, tempting. Maybe somewhere in Scotland? I’ve always wanted to do the North Coast 500. Get properly lost in the Highlands. That sounds amazing! I’m just craving some sunshine, to be honest. This English weather is doing my head in. We should all go somewhere! A girls’ trip. What do you reckon? We could aim for… October maybe? When things quieten down a bit? Ooh, yes! That’s a brilliant idea. Where would we go? Somewhere cheap? My bank account is weeping just thinking about it. Actually, I was looking at flights to Barcelona the other day. They weren’t too bad. Plus, tapas! And sunshine! Barcelona sounds perfect! Okay, operation ‘Barcelona Getaway’ is a go! We need to start checking flight prices seriously. And maybe a group chat, so we can bombard each other with potential Airbnbs.

Honestly, the council are unbelievable. Demolishing the library? It’s just… short-sighted. I know, isn’t it? They’re saying it’s ‘underutilised’, but that’s because they've deliberately run it down. Reduced the hours, cut the budget for books… it’s a self-fulfilling prophecy. Exactly! And now they want to build luxury flats on the site. As if we need  more  overpriced flats. We need a community hub, a safe space for kids, a place people can access information. It’s just… infuriating. I was chatting to old Mrs. Higgins from number 38 yesterday, she’s absolutely distraught. She relies on the library for her book club and to use the computers. She doesn't have internet at home. See? It's the people who need it most who are going to suffer. Right, I’m serious, we need to do something. I was thinking about starting a petition. Online, and proper paper ones we can get people to sign in the shops. That's a good idea. A petition would definitely raise awareness. I'm happy to help. I can design something, maybe a little flyer to go with it? I’ve got some basic design skills. Oh, that would be brilliant! You're a lifesaver. We could focus on the impact on the community, the loss of a valuable resource… and maybe mention how much cheaper it is to  keep  a library running than to build luxury apartments. Definitely. And we need to get the local news involved. Maybe contact the  Greenwich Standard ? I used to know someone who worked there. That would be amazing! Speaking of things needing to be organised, my shifts this week are a nightmare. Three late nights, and then a super early one on Saturday. My brain will be fried. Ugh, that sounds awful. I’m on a similar rota, actually. All over the place. It’s exhausting trying to keep track of everything. I've started using mnemonics, ridiculous ones, just to remember what I need to do when. Mnemonics? Like what? Oh, don’t ask. One of them involves a purple penguin and a rubber duck. It helps me remember a specific coding sequence, don't judge. No judgement! I need to get on that. I'm hopeless with remembering things. Maybe I should try some of those brain training apps. Do you think they actually work? I don't know, honestly.

…and then young Derek, bless him, he was going on about this new scheme the council's got planned for the High Street. Says it’ll ruin the village. Honestly, you can’t please some people. He complained about the planters last year, remember? Said they were a “hazard to pedestrians.” Derek moans about everything. Always has. Reminds me of old Mr. Hemmings, down the lane. Never a kind word for anyone. Though Hemmings had a point about the parking down at Cromer last summer. Absolute chaos. Oh, don't even  start  on Cromer parking. We spent half an hour circling just to find a space, then ended up miles from the beach. And it cost a fortune! Honestly, you’d think they  want  to discourage tourists. It's a racket, that’s what it is. Pure and simple. They see holidaymakers coming and think “easy money”. Speaking of which, did you see that woman at the door yesterday? Jehovah’s Witnesses again. Oh, them. They come round every few months, don't they? Always very polite, though. Never pushy. Bit misguided, if you ask me. I just tell them I’m not interested. Saves embarrassment all round. Though I feel a bit sorry for them, really. Spending their Saturdays going door-to-door... must be exhausting. Exhausting, and a waste of time! Still, they're entitled to their beliefs. It's just a bit annoying when they interrupt my afternoon nap. How are your daughter and her husband getting on, Bernard? Still living in Ipswich? They are. She phoned last week. Said they’re thinking about fostering. Can you imagine? Little ones running around the house again. It’d be lovely, but a big responsibility. That’s wonderful! She always had a way with children. She was brilliant at helping me with the little ones I used to mind. Mind you, those days are long gone. My back wouldn’t cope now. Speaking of coping, I had my tax bill through this morning. Absolutely scandalous! They seem to think I’m earning a fortune in retirement. Honestly, all I do is potter around the garden and watch the birds. I tell you what, have you seen those starlings lately? Absolutely swarming in the trees. Hundreds of them. Quite a sight. Lovely, aren't they? Though they do make a mess. Reminds me, I must get some birdseed. Speaking of mess, have you seen Brenda’s garden lately?

Honestly, the state of that garden next door is appalling. Honestly, appalling. They haven't touched it since old Mr. Henderson passed, have they? It's just… gone to seed. No, it really has. It's a bit of an eyesore, isn’t it? Though, I suppose they're dealing with things. It must be difficult. It is, but a little trim wouldn’t go amiss. It makes the whole street look… neglected. And you know how Mrs. Peterson judges everything. Mrs. Peterson. Always a keen observer. Reminds me of a headmistress I once knew. Saw all, said little, but knew  everything . She does. She’s got eyes like a hawk, that woman. Speaking of which, have you tried that new Italian place on Elm Street? Apparently, it’s very good. No, not yet. Is it expensive? We’re trying to be reasonably careful with the budget, you know. I heard it’s mid-range. Not cheap, but not exorbitant. Apparently, their pasta is homemade. Homemade pasta? Now  that  sounds promising. Though, nothing beats a good, simple mashed potato, does it? Proper creamy mash. Oh, don’t even start, Arthur. You and your mashed potato. Honestly, you'd think it was the most exquisite dish in the world! It  is  a masterpiece, Margaret! A true test of a cook. Takes skill, you know. Getting the right consistency… the perfect amount of butter… It’s funny Dad, you always go on about mashed potato. I remember when I was little, you’d make a huge batch and I’d just sit on the floor and eat it with a spoon. I can picture that! You were always a messy eater. You were a delight, though. Absolutely delightful. Now, tell me, are you still doing all that transcription work? Is it keeping you busy? It is, yeah. It’s… reliable. Though they're talking about outsourcing more and more to India. It’s a bit worrying. Outsourcing again. It seems to be happening everywhere. My office is looking at it too. It’s just cheaper, isn’t it? They don’t care about quality, just the bottom line. The tragedy of modern business. Profit over people. Happened in education too, you know. With these school academies. Turning schools into businesses… it changes the whole ethos. Exactly! It's a dreadful trend. We had such wonderful teachers at my school. Dedicated, passionate… they wouldn’t have lasted five minutes in today’s climate.

…and then they had the cheek to send me a council tax bill  after  we’d already sold the house! Honestly, the bureaucracy is unbelievable. Aye, they do that, don’t they? Always a delay. It's a proper nuisance. I had a similar thing when we moved, though it wasn’t the council tax, it was… oh, what was it… water rates, I think. A month after we’d handed the keys over. It's just expecting you to know the future, isn’t it? They  know  you’ve sold it, they should just update their records. I was chatting to Doreen the other day, and she’s having absolute hell trying to sort out her mother's estate. Taxes all over the place. It's a nightmare for people, especially when they're grieving. Exactly! And it’s not like we’re hiding anything. It's all above board, everything declared. Makes you wonder what they’re playing at. Did you see what that Sunak’s up to now? Another tax hike, apparently. Bah. All the same. Politicians, always taking, never giving. Used to be you could rely on a decent state pension, now… well, you’d need to win the lottery as well. It's awful, isn’t it? They keep fiddling with the rules. Honestly, I'm glad I’m retired now; I wouldn't want to be starting out today. Still, speaking of fiddling… did either of you manage to finally get that recycling sorted? My bin is overflowing again. I did mine yesterday. Honestly, the amount of plastic people get through... it's frightening. I wish they’d just ban some of it, really. Though then they moan about the cost of everything going up. You can't win. Always a catch, isn't there? I keep meaning to, but then I see a perfectly good cardboard box and think, "That'll be useful for something…" and it just ends up piling up in the garage. Oh, I’m the same! I'm a hoarder, I admit it. I’ve got a box of wrapping paper in the attic that's probably older than half the people in this village. I was trying to use the Sat Nav to find Old Man Hemmings’ farm the other day, you know, the one up near Dereham? It kept taking me down these tiny little lanes… barely wide enough for the car.

Right, so the hard drive’s definitely gone. Completely toast. Not a peep out of it. Can’t you just… get another one? Like, from a shop? Of course I can, but it’s the principle of it, you know? It’s only six months old. Should be covered under warranty. I spent good money on that machine. Did you keep the receipt? You're usually so good with that sort of thing. I  think  I did. It’s somewhere in the ‘Important Documents’ pile. Which, admittedly, is less a pile and more a geographical feature in the study. I'll have a dig after dinner. Sauce! More sauce! Behave now, Finn. You’ve already got a mountain of it. And no talking with your mouth full. Speaking of sauce, anyone fancy fajitas tomorrow night? I picked up some chicken earlier. Yeah, fajitas sound good. Is that the Old El Paso one? The one that tastes like… well, like nothing much? Ha! You have a discerning palate, young man. No, I got the proper stuff this time. The one in the glass jar. Much better. Oh good. The Old El Paso is an insult to peppers. Right, Leo, have you finished your broccoli? Can I go and play rugby with Tom after dinner? Mr. Henderson said we can use the field. What time is it getting dark now? It'll be nearly pitch black. It won’t be. Not for ages. We’ll take torches. Torches are a good idea. Make sure you wear a proper jacket. It’s getting chilly. And be back before it  is  dark. We could all go for a swim after Tom’s rugby practice, if everyone's up for it? The pool's open until 8. Oh, I don’t know. I’m fairly knackered already. Running after Finn all day takes it out of you. You could have a nice relaxing soak instead? Tempting. Very tempting. Finn, look at your ears! They practically stick  out . They’re like Dumbo! Dum-bo! Leo, be nice! It’s not very kind. They’re perfectly charming ears. And they’ll get smaller, apparently. They give him character. Alright, let’s finish up here. I’ll start clearing the table. And then, operation ‘Find the Warranty Receipt’ begins. Before this house swallows it whole. I hope this captures the desired tone and context. Let me know if you’d like any adjustments!
