Right, pizza’s almost ready! Who’s excited? Me! Me! Can I have extra cheese? And pepperoni! Lots and lots of pepperoni! We'll see about the ‘lots and lots’… but yes, extra cheese for you, darling. Now, before we dive into pizza, let’s talk about using our words. Oscar, remember what we talked about this morning? Instead of grabbing Lily’s toy, you  ask  if you can play with it. But she never lets me! That’s not true, sometimes she does! And even if she says no, you have to say “Okay, thank you for letting me ask”. It’s all about communicating nicely. Like when I ask for pizza? Exactly! You asked politely, and now you’re getting pizza. See? It works! Can we do handstands after pizza? Like Daddy? Maybe, if you both eat your vegetables too. We need strong muscles for handstands! How many pieces of broccoli do you think you each need to eat? Let’s say two each. How many is that altogether? One, two, three, four! Four! Um… two and two is… four! I’m good at numbers. You  are  good at numbers! Alright, pizza's ready! But after pizza, we’re going to start on that fairy garden we talked about. I found some really pretty pebbles. Ooh! Can we make a house for the fairies? And a swimming pool! And maybe… a little Loch Ness Monster lives in the swimming pool! A Loch Ness Monster? In a fairy garden? That’s a brilliant idea! But is the Loch Ness Monster friendly? Maybe he just wants to play! And eat pizza! Well, maybe he could have a tiny piece. Okay, who wants the first slice? And while we're eating, let's brainstorm…if each fairy needs one pebble for a seat at their table, and we have twenty pebbles… how many fairies can join the party? Twenty! Twenty fairies! That's a lot! Can they all wear sparkly party clothes? Absolutely. Sparkly party clothes for everyone! Even the Loch Ness Monster. Now, eat your pizza before it gets cold. And remember – nice words! What would be the ideal menu for the fairies? Rainbow sprinkles! And tiny pizza! Excellent ideas. And maybe a little dewdrop tea? Yes and honey! Perfect! Now dig in. Mummy do you think the Loch Ness Monster is real? That is a very good question. Some people think so, some people don't.

Honestly, this Peka is unreal. Like, seriously good. I’m stuffed. Isn’t it? It's proper comforting food, isn’t it? And the portion sizes… massive. You’ll be needing a lie down after this, love. Can I have some more bread? Always, champ. You’ve got a hollow leg, you do. Though, I suspect we all do when faced with Croatian food. It's a different league. It’s just… the flavours. And it’s really tender. Did you see how long they had that cooking under the bell? Hours! It’s a labour of love, that’s for sure. Reminds me a bit of how your Grandma used to do her pot roasts, doesn't it? Slow and low. Grandma’s were better. Oh, don’t start a family feud now. Grandma could make anything taste amazing. So, Rovinj tomorrow then? I’ve heard it's absolutely stunning. Apparently, it’s full of these little cobbled streets and art galleries. That’s the plan! Though, I’m a bit worried about parking. We had enough trouble here in Motovun. Honestly, those roads are tiny. Honestly, I'd happily walk everywhere. The scenery is gorgeous, and it’s a good excuse to burn off some of this Peka. Can we go swimming? Does the apartment have a swimming pool? I believe it does, yes. It's a little complex, apparently, with shared facilities and a bit of a walk, but a pool nonetheless. Though, the sea here is so clear, I’m not sure we’ll bother much. Speaking of clear, did you hear about that outbreak of… well, I can’t even say it… back in Africa? It sounded a bit like… well, you know. Ebola? Oh, I saw something about that. Bloody terrifying. It’s just… with all the travel these days… It’s a valid concern. Though, I imagine the health protocols are extremely tight these days. You've got to remember the immigration officers are examining passports for more than just stamps. It's about tracking movement and potential illnesses. Did you see that dog on the way here? It was really fluffy! Yes! A huge, scruffy thing. Probably a local stray. Croatia is really good with animals, aren't they? I saw a lot of well looked after strays, mostly well fed. It’s very different to some places we’ve been. Speaking of different, have you seen the advancements in food technology they’re teaching kids in school these days?

Right then, finished that up, didn’t we? Good bit of ham, that was. Lovely. Though a bit salty, wasn’t it? Still, better than nothing. You’d think after all these years, I'd have perfected my ham slicing. You always say that, Margaret. Always. You've been slicing ham for… well, decades. Speaking of decades, did you see that article in ‘The Lady’? About the debt collectors harassing pensioners? Absolute disgrace. They’re preying on vulnerable people. PPI claims, mostly, ain’t it? They sold ‘em to ‘em, then flog ‘em again and again. Bunch of rogues, the lot of ‘em. I wouldn’t answer the phone to anyone I didn’t know, not these days. I get so many calls. Always about accidents I haven’t had. Or claiming I'm entitled to compensation. Honestly, it's infuriating. I just hang up now. Good. Don't give them the satisfaction. Old Mrs. Higgins down the road got caught out. Gave them her bank details. Lost a fortune. Poor woman. Terrible. Absolutely terrible. I was watching that show on telly last night, the one about… what was it called? ‘Rogue Traders’? They exposed a similar scam. Oh aye, I watch that one. Keeps me entertained. Though half the time, I can’t keep up with that fella, Matt Allwright. Talks a mile a minute. Still, good on ‘im for sticking up for the little man. I'm more of a ‘Call the Midwife’ woman myself. Lovely, gentle programme. Though it does get me all weepy. I’ve been trying to get the television sorted. Keeps losing the signal. I think it’s the aerial. Needs adjusting, probably. I need to get someone to climb up there. Not doing that myself, not at my age. I could take a look, David. I used to be rather good with aerials. Remember when we had that storm a few years back? I fixed half the street’s televisions. Would you, John? That’d be brilliant. You’re a lifesaver. You’re all too kind. Speaking of kindness, are we still on for the party at Emily’s? Saturday? Yes, definitely. I’ve got some new seeds I want to show her. Sweet peas. She loves sweet peas. Oh, good. Looking forward to that. It'll be good to see everyone. I’ve been trying to remember the words to that hymn we used to sing at Abbey.

Honestly, that was a  day . Three domestic cases back-to-back. It just… gets to you, doesn’t it? Och, aye. It does. I've seen a fair few over the years, you know. Doesn’t get easier, even after all this time. Though, truth be told, the sentencing today seemed a bit… lenient, didn’t it? For what he did? I thought so too. It’s frustrating. You hear the details, the impact on the victim, and then… well, it feels like it doesn’t quite match up. Do you think it’s because of the backlog? They’re just trying to get through cases quickly? Could be, lass. Could be. They’re stretched thin, that’s for sure. And the funding… don't even get me started. I overheard someone saying they’re cutting back on legal aid again. Makes it even harder for folk, doesn't it? Especially those who truly need it. It's appalling. And it just perpetuates the cycle, doesn't it? If people can't afford a decent defence, they're more likely to re-offend. It’s a systemic issue. Speaking of systems… did you see the traffic on the M40 this morning? Absolute chaos. Aye, I heard about it on the radio. Nearly didn’t bother coming in, frankly. I usually get the train, you see, but it was playing up. Signal failures or something. Ended up getting a lift with Margaret, but even that was slow going. They need to invest in the infrastructure, desperately. Tell me about it. I’m thinking of cycling to work more often, but honestly, the roads just aren’t safe enough. It’s a bit terrifying. Though, I’m trying to do my bit for the planet, you know? It’s just… overwhelming sometimes, the scale of the climate crisis. It is, it is. My grandson, Hamish, he’s very keen on all that. He's at university studying environmental science. Bright lad. Says we’re all doomed if we don’t change our ways. A bit dramatic, maybe, but he has a point. They all do, don't they? It's good he's passionate. My sister just had a baby – a little girl, Elsie. It makes you think about the world  they’re  going to inherit. Which is part of why I’m trying to be more mindful. Congratulations! A wee girl. Lovely.

Right, so we were talking about what makes people happy, weren’t we? What makes  you  happy, Poppy? Um… unicorns! And chocolate! And when you read me stories! Those are lovely things! Very good answers. And what about you, Leo? What makes  you  happy? Dinosaurs! And building LEGO! And… when I beat you at Monopoly! Oh, you  do  love beating me at Monopoly, don’t you? It’s a good thing to be good at stuff you enjoy. But is that  all  that makes you happy? No! Playing in the garden! And… and… having lots and lots of money! Ah, yes. Lots and lots of money. Why does money make you happy, Leo? Because then I can buy  all  the LEGO! And a dinosaur park! And a real unicorn! I want a unicorn too! A sparkly one! Well, sparkly unicorns are very expensive, aren't they? Money can buy things, definitely. But do you think having lots of money is the  only  way to be happy? Hmm… no. Why not? Because you can be happy even without LEGO. If you're playing with your friends. That’s a really good point, Leo. It’s true! And Poppy, what do you think? Can you be happy without having everything you want? Yeah! I can be happy playing with my dolls even if I don’t have a new one! And I can be happy singing silly songs! Like… um… Go on, what silly song? “Bananas in my pyjamas!” “Bananas in my pyjamas!” Very good! See, that makes me happy, listening to you sing. It doesn’t cost anything, does it? Nope. Sometimes the best things in life are free, remember that. It's about having fun, and being with people you love, and doing things you enjoy. Money can help with some things, but it doesn't buy happiness all the time. It’s much more about… well, about feeling good inside. Like when Mummy gives us cuddles? Exactly like that, Poppy. Exactly like that. And when Daddy makes pancakes on Saturday morning. Those are the things that really matter, aren’t they? Not how much money we have. Can we have pancakes tomorrow? We’ll see! Now, who wants to try and think of a rhyme? Let’s see… happy as can be… what rhymes with “be”? Me! Very good! "Happy as can be, happy as me!" Now you try, Leo.

Seriously though, have you thought about what you’re doing after this? Like, actual plans. Everyone's talking about Uni applications, but… what if Uni isn't the one? I know, right? Everyone's stressing over UCAS already. I'm leaning towards engineering, I think. My dad keeps going on about how it's a 'solid' career. Solidly boring, maybe. See, that's what I mean. Solid. Like a brick. I was reading about this guy who patented a self-folding laundry machine. A  self-folding  laundry machine! That’s… innovation. A self-folding laundry machine? Is that even necessary? Sounds expensive. Who's got the time to invest in something like that? That's the point! Someone did. And probably made a fortune. I was thinking, maybe something like invention is the way to go. Patent stuff, become a billionaire, retire at twenty-five. You're ambitious, I'll give you that. But you need money  to  invent things, right? And to get patents. It's not exactly free. Plus, most inventions are terrible. Remember that electric toothbrush that vibrated your whole face off? Okay, bad example. But still. Imagine inventing something that solves a real problem. Like, world hunger. Or… efficient recycling. World hunger is a bit beyond a school project, don't you think? Though, efficient recycling… that's actually a good shout. But China's basically got that locked down already, haven't they? They're processing like, 50% of the world's plastic. Yeah, but they're also  creating  a massive amount of plastic waste. It's a cycle. It’s all about investment, isn't it? If you invested in a company developing new biodegradable materials, you’d be set. Sounds risky though. What if it flops? My dad's always going on about 'safe' investments – like property. Mortgages and stuff. Super exciting. Property’s so… stagnant. It's just sitting there. It doesn’t  do  anything. You need something that grows. Like, a tech start-up. Or a self-folding laundry machine company. You're obsessed with that laundry machine. Honestly. I’m just trying to figure out if I want to do physics or mechanical engineering. And avoid having a complete meltdown trying to write my personal statement. Fair enough. Maybe we should both just invent things. No pressure of applications, no boring degrees… just pure innovation. And a lot of debt. Don't forget the debt.

Honestly, I think I'm going to stick to the blues today. My legs are screaming. You and me both! That red run we did yesterday… I thought my quads were going to detach. Honestly! And the lift queue for it was ridiculous. Twenty minutes just standing there, freezing. Tell me about it. Although, I did manage to spot Sarah and Mark in the queue for the gondola. Did you? Oh, that’s good. Are they having a good time? Apparently. Sarah said Mark nearly ended up in a snowdrift yesterday. He went a bit too far off-piste trying to show off. Oh, classic Mark! He always has to be the daredevil. Is he okay though? Perfectly fine. Just a bit bruised ego, I think. He’s convinced he was deliberately trying to go off-piste, not that he lost control. Of course he is! He'd never admit defeat. So, are they sticking around for the week like us? Yeah, they flew in on Saturday too. They’re bringing their kids out next year, apparently. Oh wow, that’ll be chaos! Remember when Mum and Dad tried to teach us to ski? Complete disaster. Don't remind me! Dad yelling instructions, Mum attempting a parallel turn and ending up going backwards…it was brilliant! Oh, amazing. Speaking of family, have you heard anything from Emily about Christmas? She said she was struggling to get flights. She messaged me earlier, actually. She managed to get a flight, but it’s a really awful connection. She’s going to be travelling for nearly twelve hours. Oh, poor thing. Still, at least she’s coming. It wouldn’t be Christmas without her. No, it wouldn’t. Right, I'm going to order another Aperol Spritz. I deserve it after yesterday's trauma. Want one? Oh, go on then! Yes please. I think I deserve one too. Maybe a little something to eat as well. My stomach is starting to rumble. Good idea. Let's see what they have... Oh, look, they do a really nice chicken salad. Ooh, that sounds perfect. We've definitely earned it after all that skiing - or attempted skiing, in my case. Absolutely! And we’ve got another few days of it yet. Hopefully, my legs will cooperate. Let’s just aim for the blues and don’t push it. We’re here to enjoy ourselves, not end up in A&E!

Right, now hold still. Just a little bit more off the side… oh dear. Oh,  dear . What? What is it? Don’t tell me you’ve… I think… I think I’ve taken a little bit too much off. And… oh, heavens. Is that… a stripe? A stripe?! You’ve given me a stripe in my hair! And… is that… a tiny bit of earlobe? Oh, Margaret! Oh, I am SO sorry! It’s the light, I think. It makes it hard to see. And honestly, you were wriggling. It’s very difficult to cut hair when the subject moves. Never mind the racket strings, this is a disaster! A stripe! It looks like a barcode! We need to focus. We were talking about the racket strings. The breaking problem. Right. Cable ties. Are you  sure  about the cable ties? Well, it’s a temporary fix, isn’t it? We're not claiming it's a permanent solution. Think of it as… emergency string repair. For a fiver, people will be thrilled! We could call it ‘String Savers’ or ‘Racket Rescue’. ‘Racket Rescue’… sounds a bit… dramatic. And five pounds? Considering the cost of materials… those cable ties aren’t free, you know. And the little instruction leaflet explaining  how  to tie them without snapping the frame? Oh, everything adds up, doesn't it? Okay, four fifty? No, three fifty. And the leaflet will be digital. A QR code on the packet. Much cheaper. We’ll need to trail the idea, of course. See how many breakages we get at the club. Phil’s strings always go. He’s a brute. Phil  is  a brute. And we’ve discussed this, Margaret. We need to market it properly. What about… a ‘fleet’ of String Savers? We could say, ‘Keep a fleet of String Savers in your kit bag!’ A ‘fleet’? That sounds… naval. Is it the right word for cable ties? It suggests preparedness! Being ready for anything! It's marketing language! Look, this could work. Especially for schools. Imagine – primary schools, kids breaking strings all the time… a quick fix for PE teachers. Primary schools… yes. Actually, secondary school as well. They play a lot of badminton. Higher impact, more breakage. Though they might be a bit more… discerning. Discerning? They're teenagers. They'll use anything that gets them back on the court quickly. We could even do a school package!

Lovely cuppa, isn't it? Just what you need on a grey afternoon like this. It is, Arthur. Though a biscuit would have gone down a treat with it, wouldn't it? I didn't realise we were all out. Mmm, it’s a good brew. Speaking of treats though, I saw this exhibition advertised in Norwich. It’s a retrospective of Maggi Hambling’s work at the Sainsbury Centre. Oh really? Hambling, she's the one who did the sculpture of Oscar Wilde, isn't she? Down on the Embankment in London? That’s the one! It’s supposed to be a really comprehensive collection – early sketches, her seascapes, everything. I was thinking of going next weekend. Maggi Hambling… doesn’t ring a bell, I’m afraid. I never was much one for modern art, you know. Give me a nice landscape, a Turner or Constable, and I’m happy. All that abstract stuff just looks like a mess to me. I know what you mean, Arthur. It can be a bit…challenging. But sometimes, if you look at it long enough, something clicks. I saw a Rothko exhibition once and found it surprisingly moving. Just blocks of colour, but it really got under my skin. It’s about what it makes  you  feel, I think. You don’t need to understand it intellectually. And Hambling’s work is quite visceral. It’s very emotional, very raw. She paints the sea a lot, and you can really  feel  the power of it. That's exactly it. And she’s Norfolk born and bred, which is nice. It’s good to support local artists. It’s not all just pretty pictures, either. Her work often deals with difficult themes – loss, sexuality, isolation. Sounds a bit gloomy for my taste. I like painting that cheers you up. All those daffodils and sunsets. Now  that’s  art. Though, I did rather like those Impressionists. Monet and all that. They could paint a decent water lily. Monet was lovely. Very soothing. You know, I tried a watercolour class a few years back. Thought I’d give it a go. And? Oh, it was a disaster! I’m terrible at watercolour. Everything just runs together, turns into a muddy mess. I prefer knitting, much more satisfying. You can actually  see  what you’re creating. It takes practice, Mum. You can't expect to be Monet overnight!

Honestly, Chloe just… ugh. She’s been going on about this guy, Mark, for  weeks , and then today she was like, “Oh, yeah, he’s started talking to this other girl.” Like, honey, you should have seen that coming. It’s textbook. Oh, the drama. Is it always this intense with her? I swear she manufactures conflict just to have something to talk about. It’s exhausting! And she had the  audacity  to ask  me  for advice. Like, I’m not a relationship guru, I can barely keep a succulent alive. You’re too nice. You should have just said, “Look, you created this mess, you deal with it.” I know, right? But I just… I ended up saying something vaguely sympathetic. I’m a pushover. Speaking of messes, have you seen the state of the bathroom? Please don’t. I’ve been deliberately avoiding it. My shift was  horrendous  today. Two sectionings, both related to substance misuse. It just drains you, you know? I really just wanted to come home and collapse. Oh god, that sounds awful. No wonder you’re avoiding cleaning. I feel bad complaining about Chloe when you’re dealing with actual, serious stuff. Hey, it’s all valid. We’re allowed to vent about ridiculous people and dirty bathrooms. It’s self-care. Good point. Okay, so, bathroom rota… we both conveniently “forgot” last week. Maybe we should just commit to Saturday morning? I’ll tackle the shower if you do the toilet. Deal. But can we put on some ridiculously cheesy music while we do it? I need to cleanse my ears after a day of… everything. Absolutely. And we’re allowed to procrastinate for at least fifteen minutes beforehand with tea and biscuits. It’s non-negotiable. You read my mind. You know, I was thinking about that email I’ve been putting off sending to the uni about my dissertation supervisor. I’m seriously considering just dropping him a vague “I’m finding things difficult” and hoping he magically fixes everything. Oh, the art of passive-aggressive communication. A classic postgraduate tactic. Honestly, the language people use in academia is just… bonkers. “Operationalising the paradigm shift…” What does that even  mean ?! Exactly! It’s like they deliberately try to sound pretentious. I swear they have a competition to see who can use the most jargon. It's a skill. A terrible, awful skill.

Honestly, the commute was… biblical. They’d closed the M4 again, so it was all A-roads and tractors. I swear, every single tractor in Berkshire was out for a drive. Sounds delightful. You’d think they’d schedule roadworks for, I don’t know, the middle of the night? Or a weekend when fewer people are trying to get to work. Exactly! It's just… basic common sense. Which, apparently, is a rarer commodity than intelligence these days. People can be incredibly clever, PhDs and everything, but utterly lack common sense. True. It’s like they’ve never had to  deal  with the real world. All theory, no practice. Remember old Mr. Henderson from Sixth Form? Brilliant physicist, couldn't boil an egg without setting off the smoke alarm. Oh god, yes! And then there was Bethany from university. She was arguing with me about feminism yesterday, completely missing the point because she’s lived such a privileged life. She was going on about how hard it is for women in tech, which is a valid point, but then completely dismissed my experience dealing with daily sexism in a completely different industry. It’s difficult, isn’t it? Trying to explain different experiences. People often assume their struggles are the only struggles. Exactly. They just don't ‘get’ it. It's exhausting sometimes. I needed a cigarette when I got in, I can tell you that much. Don't start. You know I hate it when you say that. We talked about this. I know, I know. It's just... stress. And honestly, seeing Sarah chain-smoking on her balcony this morning didn’t help. She’s completely back on them since her mum's been ill. Poor Sarah. It's understandable, grief does funny things. But still, it’s not a solution. It just… postpones the problem. Like my wine. You and your wine. Hey, it gets me through client calls with people who think ‘the cloud’ is a literal fluffy thing in the sky. It requires a certain level of detachment. Speaking of which, did you hear old man Peterson's daughter eloped with a yoga instructor from Bolivia? No! Seriously? Old Man Peterson, the one who spends his life complaining about ‘modern values’? The very same. Apparently, she met him on a retreat. He's absolutely furious. Says it's a cultural mismatch. Oh, the irony! It's brilliant.

Right, so the farm was… hectic, wasn’t it? Honestly, I think I need a holiday  after  taking you two to a farm. But it was  good ! I liked the piglets. They were really squeaky. And the tractor! Can we go on a real tractor ride again sometime? Not just the little one in the play area. We'll see. Maybe. It depends if Mummy can cope with the chaos again. You two were running off in opposite directions the whole time. Honestly, I felt like a sheepdog. I was looking at the chickens! They were laying eggs! I wanted to feed the sheep. But that boy kept pushing me. Oh, dear. Well, that’s not very nice. Did you tell someone? I told you. Yes, and you did. Good. And did you tell a grown-up at the farm? No. You should have, sweetie. That’s important. Sometimes you need to ask for help when someone isn’t being kind. Now, speaking of not being kind… how was school today? Okay. Miss Davies said I drew a  very  good picture of a rainbow. Oh, lovely! That’s wonderful, darling. Show me later. And you, my little whirlwind? Er… Miss Johnson sent a note. Oh? What did it say? That I was… talking too much. And distracting the other children. Right. Well, that’s not ideal, is it? What were you talking about? Dinosaurs! And if T-Rex could beat a Triceratops in a fight. Well, that  is  an important question. But school is for listening to the teacher, okay? You can talk about dinosaurs at playtime. Or when you get home. Can we watch a DVD after dinner? Please? Maybe. If you both promise to be sensible. What DVD would you like? Dinosaur Train! No! Horrid Henry! And Moody Margaret! Oh, dear. Negotiate. You have to decide together, or there will be no DVD. Remember what we talked about – sharing and taking turns. Now, who's hungry? I’m thinking pasta and sauce. Unless you two want to debate the merits of different dinosaur species with the Bolognese? Pasta! Yeah pasta! But can we watch Horrid Henry  after ? We’ll see. Let’s get this pasta on, and then we’ll discuss further DVD options. And maybe, just maybe, we'll all have a quiet evening after a very noisy day. Mummy, what does ‘sensible’ mean? It means using your words nicely, listening to each other and not running around like wild things.

Right, so three sugars for you then? Still haven’t broken that habit, eh? Never will. It’s a comfort. And you? Just the one, still trying to be… vaguely healthy? Trying. Failing spectacularly, probably. Speaking of comfort, look at this yarn. Honestly, it's like a hug in a ball. This is for the… well, I’m still deciding. Maybe a jumper for your mum? She always says she’s cold. She would love that. She’s been going on about needing a new cardigan for ages. You’re a wizard with the needles, you know. Unlike me, who can barely sew on a button. Oh, don't sell yourself short! You’re building a whole  world  with your research. That's way more impressive than a jumper. Did you see that thing about Benedict Cumberbatch doing that… weird art installation? Oh god, the one with the smashed pottery? Yes! It was horrifying, but also… compelling. Like, what was he  thinking ? Apparently, it’s supposed to represent the fragility of the male ego or something equally pretentious. Seriously? Classic Cumberbatch. He's got a knack for being both incredibly clever and utterly baffling. It’s a gift. It is. Though, honestly, I’m still holding out hope he'll reprise Sherlock. Need a bit of intelligent drama in my life. It’s all Bake Off and Olympic reruns at the moment. Oh, the Olympics were brilliant, weren't they? The diving was incredible. I could  never  do that. The sheer bravery… and the speedos. The speedos were… memorable. Right, tea’s brewed. You realize, it’s almost Easter already? Where has the time gone? I know! It feels like Christmas was five minutes ago. Are we doing anything special? Your family usually have a massive Easter egg hunt. We usually do. My niece and nephew live for it. I’m planning on hiding some of those ridiculously oversized eggs… the ones that cost more than a decent bottle of wine. It's all about the thrill of the hunt, you see. You're enabling a sugar rush of epic proportions. Precisely. It’s a tradition. Plus, it keeps them quiet for approximately five minutes. Which is a win in my book. Actually, talking of art… have you seen that new Hockney exhibition? Apparently, it’s on at the Fitzwilliam. No! I keep meaning to check it out. Hockney’s amazing, isn’t he?

Right, so the National Gallery’s shut on Mondays, isn’t it? Just double-checking. Don’t want a wasted trip all the way into town. Yep, Mondays. Always Mondays. Seems a bit daft, really. All that art, locked up. I know, eh? Still, we can do the Portrait Gallery, then. And I’ve been meaning to see that Hockney exhibition at the Tate Modern. Oh, Hockney. Is it any good? I saw a little bit on the telly, looked a bit… abstract for me, if you know what I mean. Oh, go on, John! It’s David Hockney! It’s brilliant! Colourful, lively, proper art. You might be surprised. And afterwards, we could pop into the British Museum, if we’ve got time. All that walking. My knees are playing up, you know. And the tube… honestly, it’s a nightmare on a Sunday. Packed like sardines. We can get the bus, if you like. It takes longer, but it’s more comfortable. Though, knowing London buses, we might be stuck in traffic for hours. Hmm. The tube’s quicker, I suppose. Just need to be prepared for a bit of a scrum. Remember that time we went to see that film at the Imax, near Waterloo? Oh, don’t remind me! That was chaos! And it was 3D, wasn’t it? Nearly gave me a migraine. All those things flying out the screen! And the price of the tickets! Highway robbery, I tell ya. For what? A slightly bigger screen and some dodgy plastic glasses? It was an experience, though. You have to admit. Though, I do prefer a good, proper theatre. A play, something with actual actors. Aye, me too. But a good film…a really good film…you can’t beat it. Speaking of which, should we think about what we're having for tea when we get back? I'm famished already just  thinking  about all that sightseeing. Don’t change the subject! We’re planning a posh cultural day out! We’re not just going to spend the whole day thinking about scran. Though… maybe a nice slice of cake at the National Portrait Gallery cafe? Now you’re talking. See, that's the way to plan a day. Mix a bit of culture with a bit of comfort. What about getting the tube to Euston, then a bus? Less walking from the station. Hmm, that’s not a bad idea.

Right, Christmas dinner. Operation Festive Feast begins now. You’re doing starters, I’m on mains, agreed? Sounds good. Though, honestly, I’m already stressed thinking about it. Last year’s smoked salmon mousse was… a learning experience. Let’s just say it didn’t hold its shape. A learning experience is one way to put it. It resembled more of a salmon puddle. But hey, you recovered admirably. Right, mains. Turkey? Goose? We’ve had turkey the last few years, haven't we? Yeah, a bit predictable, isn’t it? Goose is good. A bit…robust. But a pain to carve. Maybe a nice beef Wellington? Ooh, now you’re talking. Beef Wellington it is. Though, that pastry is a beast to get right. I’m already envisioning a soggy bottom scenario. Paul Hollywood would be horrified. Don’t even mention soggy bottoms. I still have nightmares about Great British Bake Off. Speaking of horrors, have you seen ‘Elf’ yet this year? It's practically mandatory viewing. Not yet! It’s on the list. I was more of a ‘Die Hard’ Christmas movie kind of guy, which apparently causes arguments. People get very heated about whether it counts. ‘Die Hard’ is  definitely  a Christmas movie! It’s set at a Christmas party, there’s family drama… what more do you need? Have you heard back from Mark and Sarah? Are they finally joining us this year? I texted Mark yesterday, haven't heard back yet. They’re always so busy over the holidays with family back in Leeds. Sarah’s mum is… demanding, shall we say. Keeps trying to set Mark up with her niece. Oh, bless. That’s proper northern matchmaking right there. My mum's the same. She’s convinced every single woman I introduce her to is ‘a bit too quiet’ or ‘not ambitious enough’. It’s exhausting, isn't it? The pressure! Remember when she tried to get me to go on a blind date with…what was her name… Brenda? The one who collected porcelain dolls? Brenda! Oh god, I’d almost blocked that out. She brought a  doll  to the pub. A full-sized one. In a pram. A pram! It was surreal. Anyway, let’s hope Mark and Sarah can make it. It's not Christmas without a proper argument about politics over gravy. Absolutely. And we need to rope in old Dave from down the hall.

Honestly, the state of Twitter right now. It's just… relentless negativity. I had to log off. It was impacting my sourdough starter, honestly. Tell me about it. Every single take is just so  loud . Like, no one's capable of nuance anymore. And the performative outrage is exhausting. I saw someone arguing about the correct way to make a cup of tea. A CUP OF TEA. Oh, don't even get me started on online arguments. I got a one-star review on Google today, and the  only  feedback was “too much atmosphere.” Too much atmosphere! What does that even mean? Oh my god, that's amazing. Is it like, it was too cozy? Too many plants? Exactly! It's a small café, I’ve made it all fairy lights and mismatched furniture, that  is  the atmosphere! I replied, obviously, asking for clarification, and they just...didn't respond. People are just looking for a platform to vent, aren’t they? They won’t actually  tell  you what’s wrong, they’ll just drag you down online. Reminds me of that awful guy who came into your bakery last week, demanding a gluten-free croissant. Ugh, don’t remind me. He was convinced I was deliberately hiding them from him. And then started lecturing me about the ethics of artisanal baking. Like, I’m using organic flour and local butter, what more does he want?! It's the entitlement. They think their opinion is gold dust. I had a woman yesterday complain her latte was “not Instagrammable enough.” No way. Seriously! Said the foam art wasn't symmetrical. I wanted to tell her to take a photography course. You should’ve! Honestly. I was thinking about doing a whole redesign of the bakery, maybe leaning into a more minimalist aesthetic. Less… ‘cottagecore,’ more… clean lines. Do you think it would work? That could be good. You've got such a strong brand already, but a bit of a refresh might be nice. It depends on the vibe you’re going for. I’ve been helping Mateo with some design stuff for his new web shop—he’s selling handmade ceramics now. It's looking really good. Very Scandi. Oh, that's cool. Mateo’s talented. Have you been to Margate recently? They’ve got loads of little independent shops popping up there now. I was thinking of doing a little weekend trip.

Honestly, Oisin, you’ve barely touched your peas. They’re lovely peas, honestly. They’re green. Yes, they  are  green. That’s what peas  are . They're good for you, make you strong like a superhero! My history exam was awful. I completely blanked on the dates for the Tudor monarchs. Utterly blanked. Oh dear. Well, you’ve still got revision tomorrow, haven’t you? Focus on those key dates, make flashcards. Flashcards? Seriously? Don’t dismiss flashcards, darling. They work! I used them for my Master's. Though, admittedly, remembering Tudor monarchs isn’t quite the same as remembering postmodern literary theory. Can I have some raspberries after? Yes, you can have raspberries after you’ve eaten some more peas, sweetie. Just a few more. They go beautifully  with  the raspberries, actually. A little savoury, a little sweet. We saw the most amazing robin’s nest when we were out walking this morning. Right in the hedge, little blue eggs. Oh, how lovely! Did you get a good look? It’s so exciting to see them building. We had a blackbird nesting in the garden last year, but the cats… well, let’s just say it didn’t end well. Speaking of cats, Mrs. Higgins’ gerbils escaped again. They were running around her garden all morning. She was chasing them with a dustpan and brush. Gerbils are cute! Can we get a gerbil? Absolutely not. We have enough on our plates, young lady. Remember the hamster? That was a disaster. You’re not wrong. He escaped, chewed through the sofa, and then disappeared into the wall. Don’t remind me. Right, who wants to go for a bike ride after dinner? The weather's supposed to be lovely tomorrow. Maybe. Depends how much revision I have to do. History’s killing me. Bike ride! And then ice cream? Chocolate ice cream? Perhaps. If you finish your peas. And maybe a small portion of broccoli. We need to get some greens into you, you know. We could walk to the shop for ice cream. Actually, I need to get more birdseed. And maybe some more compost for the roses. Gardening is so therapeutic, isn't it? It is, when the slugs aren't eating everything! They’re relentless. I swear they multiply overnight. They’re probably escaping from Mrs. Higgins’ garden after the gerbils. Possibly! It’s a conspiracy, I tell you.

Honestly, the supermarket was chaos this morning. Absolute mayhem. Everyone seemed to be doing their big shop. Oh, don't I know it. I went yesterday afternoon, thinking it’d be quieter. Still packed! Though, to be fair, I was after those reduced yellow sticker bits, so I was battling everyone else for bargains. Yellow sticker bargains are serious business, aren't they? In my day, we didn’t have all this ‘reduced to clear’. You just bought what you needed and that was that. Though, mind you, we didn’t  have  much choice! True enough. Mum, are you still managing alright with your shopping? I’m happy to pick things up when I’m doing my own run. Oh, I’m fine, dear. Old Mrs. Higgins next door is a darling, she pops to the shops every day and always asks if I need anything. Though she does try to get me to buy those awful custard creams… says they remind her of her late husband. Custard creams  are  awful! Though I suppose they’re a comfort food for some. They're just… dry. Anyway, speaking of needing things… my eyebrows are looking dreadful. I really need to get them sorted. I could do them for you, you know. I’m quite good with tweezers. Oh, would you? That would be brilliant! I’m dithering about whether to go to that new beauty salon in town, but it’s so expensive. Don't you waste your money on those places! They charge a fortune for a bit of plucking. Your friend here is perfectly capable. Honestly, these youngsters know everything! Flattery will get you everywhere, dear. How about next Tuesday evening? After work? Perfect! Thanks, love. We should also think about a proper meal out, just the three of us. It's been ages since we’ve done that. That sounds lovely. Not that fancy Italian place, though. Too much garlic, gives me indigestion. No, definitely not there. How about The Old Mill? They do a nice roast. Good shout. They also have a lovely garden, if the weather holds up. Ooh, yes. A roast sounds wonderful. And afterwards, a little stroll along the river… though I won’t be joining you if you both light up those cigarettes. We’ll behave ourselves, Mum. Honestly. I’m trying to cut down, anyway. It’s ridiculously expensive, and I’m coughing like an old chimney.

Right, so I think we’re officially down to two feeds a day now with Leo. It feels…strange. Like, a proper milestone, isn’t it? It  is  massive! He’s doing so well, though. Seriously, he's such a good little thing. And you’re doing brilliantly, honestly. It's a huge step, taking away those extra feeds. It just feels like I’ve got more time suddenly. Which is great, but then I feel guilty for thinking that! Like I  should  be missing those cuddles. Motherhood, eh? Always a guilt trip waiting to happen. Don't worry, the cuddles will still be there. He'll just be… more mobile, and wanting to investigate everything instead of just wanting milk. Exactly! Which is terrifying in itself. This week’s looking busy. Your dad’s coming on Wednesday, isn’t he? Yep. He wants to take Leo for a walk in the park. He’s been talking about it for ages. Said he wants to be a proper pushing-the-pram grandad. Oh, he'll love that. He’s already completely besotted, aren’t they? Then Sarah’s coming down on Friday, I think? Friday evening. She’s bringing Mark, and little Freya. It'll be nice. A bit chaotic, probably, with two under twos running around, but nice. It’s ages since we’ve all been together. It has been. And then I promised Auntie Carol I’d go for lunch with her on Tuesday. She’s been on at me for weeks. Oh, good for you. You deserve a bit of Auntie Carol time. She'll have all the local gossip, no doubt. Guaranteed! I need to book that baby sign language class, too. I keep meaning to. Oh, yes! Are you still thinking of the one at the community centre? Yeah, that one. It’s on Thursday mornings, apparently. I checked their website. It’s a six-week course. That sounds good. It’ll be really useful, won't it? Especially when he starts getting frustrated that he can’t communicate. Exactly. And I think it’s good for their brain development too, apparently. Someone at the baby group was saying it helps them with speech later on. Oh, that’s interesting. I might look into that for Freya when she's a bit older. I’ll let you know what it’s like. It starts next week.

It’s funny isn't it, how even a tiny rise feels like a proper hill after London. Everything’s so… flat there. Absolutely. You forget what proper undulation feels like. It’s just concrete and straight lines. This is proper countryside. Everything feels… softer. It’s the light too, I think. It’s different here. More expansive. London light feels… contained. Bouncing off buildings. Yeah, it’s definitely the light. And the smell. You can actually  smell  things. Not just exhaust fumes and coffee. Honestly. I was reading an article about how city-dwellers are losing their sense of smell. Apparently, our brains filter out the constant barrage of smells as a survival mechanism. That’s depressing. So we're slowly becoming olfactory-blind? Pretty much. Which is why a field of wildflowers is so overwhelming when you actually experience it. It is. It just hits you. Makes you feel…reset. Look, that village over there. Little Barningham, isn't it? I think so. We drove through there last autumn, remember? When we were looking at that antique shop? Oh, God, yes. The one with the terrifying collection of porcelain dolls. I still have nightmares. They  were  unsettling. But the shop itself was lovely. And the tea room next door was brilliant. That’s true. That Victoria sponge was… legendary. It’s amazing how these tiny villages manage to sustain a tea room, isn't it? Community spirit, I suppose. And tourists. We’re part of the problem, really. Descending and consuming Victoria sponge. We’re contributing to the local economy! That's what you tell yourself, anyway. Look at those sheep. Just dotted all over the field. So peaceful. It’s funny, isn't it? How something so…ordinary can feel so restorative. Walking. Sheep. Villages. It’s the absence of… urgency, I think. In London, everything is a rush. Here, you can just  be . Exactly. No one’s aggressively checking their phone every two seconds. No one’s trying to overtake you on a country lane. Though judging by that Land Rover coming towards us, some people are still trying to drive like maniacs. Oh dear. They're going a bit quickly aren’t they. Perhaps they're late for their Victoria sponge. Exactly. The stakes are high. We  must  come back here more often. Definitely. We absolutely must. Before we lose our sense of smell entirely. And before the porcelain dolls come for us.

…and then the ending, honestly, it just felt so… rushed. Like they’d realised they were over budget or something and just slapped something together. Yeah? I thought it was alright. Not amazing, but decent enough for a Friday night. What specifically didn't you like? Just everything felt…convenient. All the loose ends tied up  too  neatly. And the villain’s motivation? Non-existent! Honestly, worse than the second  Paddington  film and that’s saying something. Harsh. Okay, okay. I’ll give you that the villain was a bit cardboard. But it was a fun ride, right? Popcorn movie. Fun, maybe, if you switch your brain off entirely. Speaking of fun, how’s Liam settling into the new job? He was stressing about it loads last week. Actually, he’s loving it. He sent me a really long message yesterday. Apparently, he’s already working on some huge project with loads of responsibility. He’s proper thriving, which is brilliant. He was convinced they'd given him a load of grunt work to start with. Good! He deserves it. He was so stressed about leaving his old place, even though it was making him miserable. Yeah, it was awful seeing him like that. Sticking with awful things, though...did you see that cyclist just cut us up back there? Oh my god,  yes ! Nearly gave me a heart attack. No lights, no indication, just swerved right in front of us. It's insane, isn't it? Like they think the roads are their personal race track. Honestly, I wouldn’t cycle in this city. Too many drivers who don’t look. They’re just…arrogant. And it’s not all of them, obviously, but the ones who think the rules don’t apply to them are the worst. Especially when they’re wearing those ridiculous Lycra outfits. Okay, that's a bit harsh! No, it’s true! It’s like they’re trying to compensate for something. And they always cycle in groups, blocking the entire road. Alright, alright, I get your point. They can be…frustrating. It’s just, you’ve got to share the road, right? Everyone's just trying to get where they're going. Easier said than done when they’re actively trying to kill you! Honestly, if I was in charge, I'd make cyclists take mandatory lessons, like driving. And helmets, absolutely  mandatory  helmets.

It’s just… peaceful, isn’t it? Really properly quiet. London feels like a different planet sometimes. Completely. Though I did miss the hustle a little bit yesterday, actually. Needed a bit of that energy for marking. Felt… sluggish. Sluggish is a good word. I think my brain genuinely shuts down when I’m surrounded by this much green. It’s lovely, but not conducive to thinking about post-structuralism, you know? Tell me about it. Though, speaking of things not conducive to thinking… did you see that article about the new agricultural subsidies? Utter chaos. Apparently, they're pushing for more cash crops, but it’s going to completely decimate the wildflower meadows. Oh, I skimmed something about that. Ridiculous, isn’t it? Short-term economic gain for long-term ecological disaster. Classic. It’s always the same story. They don’t factor in the inherent  value  of biodiversity. Exactly! And it's not just about aesthetics, although these poppies  are  incredible. It’s about pollination, soil health, the whole system. It’s basic economics, really. Externalities and all that. You’re always bringing it back to economics. Well, someone has to. You’re off chasing Derrida and Foucault, I’m grounded in reality! Although… speaking of languages, I was trying to explain ‘externalities’ to Stefan yesterday, and it just didn’t translate. He’s brilliant, but some concepts are so culturally embedded. Oh, Stefan’s still struggling with the nuances of English economic terminology? Poor man. It must be exhausting. He’s fluent enough for everyday conversation, though, isn’t he? Absolutely. We were talking about football last night – apparently, the local team is doing really well. He's quickly learning the required vocabulary for that at least. “Offside” and “VAR” seem to be key phrases. Of course! That’s the priority. You know, it's funny, I was thinking about how different our research areas are. I’m dismantling the structures of language, and you're trying to understand how people  use  them to manipulate markets. It’s a symbiotic relationship, really. You break things down, I try and figure out why they’re broken, and then how to fix them, or at least profit from the wreckage. A very cynical view. Realistic! Come on, you know it’s true. Look at that field over there. Probably earmarked for rapeseed next year, knowing our luck. Pretty, for a brief period, but ultimately… just a commodity.

Right, so are we still on for Saturday then? You picking me up around… one-ish? Yeah, one's good. Unless something massively explodes at work, I’ll be there. What are we thinking for the football, watching it at yours? Aye, at mine. Mam’s out with her friends, so we'll have the place to ourselves. She’d kill us if we watched it at hers and started shouting. She’s very proud of her living room. Understandable. Your mam’s living room  is  rather… curated. Last time I was there felt like I was in a magazine shoot. Speaking of which, is it still a nightmare parking around your place? Oh, it’s a disaster. It's always a disaster. Especially on match days. You'll probably have to park about a mile away and we’ll walk. I keep meaning to ask the council about a residents' permit, but I always forget. Sounds fun. Good cardio at least. My car’s been making a weird noise too, by the way. I think it might be the exhaust. Sounds like a dying walrus. A dying walrus? You always have the best descriptions. Should you get it checked? Before it actually dies on the A1? Probably. I’ve been putting it off. It’s just… inconvenient. I’d have to book it in and take time off work. Though it’s not like anyone notices if I’m not around, really. Everyone's so busy with their projects. Don't be like that. You're brilliant at what you do. They’d notice if you weren’t there to sort out their messes. You’re sweet. Anyway, after the football, fancy grabbing some food? Or are you wanting a quiet night? Food sounds good! There's that new Italian place that opened up near the Metro station, apparently it’s amazing. We could go there? Perfect. Or we could drive out and see the Angel of the North on the way back. It’s been ages since I’ve been. Ooh, aye! That'd be good. It’s always a bit bleak but impressive at the same time, isn’t it? It reminds me of being a kid. Yeah, it’s a pretty iconic landmark. Have you seen that they’re building loads more flats near there now? Changing the whole landscape. I have! It’s a bit depressing, to be honest.

Honestly, I can’t believe what’s happening on that celebrity trial show. It's absolute chaos! Did you see what…oh, hello dear, good morning. Lovely to see you. Coffee’s brewing, help yourself to a biscuit. Morning, thank you. Oh yes, I saw a bit of it. That footballer…the one who used to be on the telly a lot? He screamed when a spider went near him! Screamed? Men! All show, they are. Back in my day, men were made of sterner stuff. Didn’t bother ‘em a bit, spiders. Well, times have changed, haven't they? Though I suspect a lot of it is for the cameras, to be fair. Anyway, it's all just a bit of fun, isn't it? Though I did feel a bit sorry for the politician. He looked utterly miserable. I prefer watching the wildlife programmes. David Attenborough is brilliant. I saw a program about geese migrating the other day. It's incredible, isn't it, how they know where to go? So far! It is astonishing. Hundreds of miles guided by…well, nobody really knows, do they? Some sort of internal compass, I think. We had a huge flock of Canada geese land in the field behind the house last autumn. Quite a sight, though they did make a mess! Mess is right! They're greedy things, geese. Come waddling along, honking and pooping everywhere. Used to have them on the allotments, they'd decimate the brassicas. I saw a buzzard circling over the park yesterday. Beautiful bird. So graceful. They’ve really increased in numbers around here, haven’t they? They have. It’s wonderful to see. We get kestrels occasionally, hovering over the garden. They're hoping for a vole, I imagine. It’s amazing what you notice when you just…look. Vole? We used to trap voles. Nasty little things they are. Ruined my sweet peas, they did. Used to set the traps overnight. It's a shame about the hedgehogs though, isn't it? I haven't seen one in months. They used to come into the garden all the time. That’s worrying. Apparently, their numbers are drastically down. Loss of habitat, garden tidiness…it impacts them all. I leave a little saucer of milk out for them every night, hoping one will come along. Milk? They don't need milk. They need bugs! Good, juicy beetles and slugs.

Honestly, this quiche is amazing. Did you make it? Thanks! No, I grabbed it from that little bakery on the high street, 'Flourish'. They do the best lunchtime deals. I was desperate though, completely forgot to bring anything with me. How are you finding things now you’re back from maternity leave? It's…a readjustment, massively. I underestimated how much my brain had turned to mush. Trying to remember verb conjugations after months of ‘goo goo gaas’ is surprisingly difficult. And the staff have all changed so much. Feels like starting from scratch. Oh, I can imagine. It’s brutal. It took me ages to get back into the swing of things after Ruby was born. Did you have a good interview for the head of department role, by the way? It was…okay. It was a lot more focused on data analysis than I expected. I felt a bit out of my depth, to be honest. They kept asking about attainment gaps and target setting. I’m good at teaching, inspiring kids, you know? This felt like a completely different job. Ugh, that sounds awful. So much pressure on data these days, isn’t it? It's all numbers and very little about actual teaching. They don’t want a teacher, they want a data manager. Exactly! And the person interviewing was so…intense. Kept staring at me, not really listening. I rambled a bit about creating a more inclusive learning environment, and she just raised an eyebrow and asked about spreadsheets. Oh, bless you. Sounds like they already had someone in mind, honestly. Don’t beat yourself up about it. It wasn't a good fit, clearly. Honestly, sometimes I think I’d rather teach monkeys than deal with school politics. Tell me about it! Although, monkeys probably wouldn’t ask you to justify every single lesson objective with quantifiable data. How’s little Leo doing, anyway? Is he sleeping through the night yet? Oh, bless him. Occasionally. He had a growth spurt last week, so it’s been back to hourly wake-ups. I’m running on approximately three hours of sleep a night. I’ve started hiding chocolate in the laundry basket. Don’t judge. No judgement here! I was doing the same with biscuits when Elsie was that age. It was a dark time. Oh, speaking of hiding things, have you tried that new cafe on Station Street?

Honestly, I’m starting to freak out a little bit about… everything. Like, properly. Everything? Big everything, or little everything? 'Cause little everything I can help with, big everything… well, that requires wine and potentially a very long rant. Big everything. Like, the future. My job. Whether I'm actually doing anything meaningful. The creeping realisation that I’m officially… an adult. Oh, the adulting crisis. Classic. I think we all hit that around twenty-five. It’s like suddenly you’re supposed to have a five-year plan, and all you’ve got is a vague aspiration to own a cat and not live in a shoebox. Exactly! Everyone at work is all ‘promotion track’ and ‘career progression’ and I’m just… thinking about if I should finally join a pottery class. It feels so… pointless. I feel like I should be building an empire or something, not scheduling deliveries of cardboard boxes. Hey, someone’s gotta schedule the boxes! It’s a vital role. Seriously. And look, I get the empire building thing, but not everyone  needs  to be a CEO. Remember Aunt Carol? She was obsessed with making artisan dog biscuits. Found her niche, absolutely thriving. True. She did smell perpetually of liver. A small price to pay for entrepreneurial success. But seriously, what about you? What  do  you want, aside from not cardboard boxes? I don’t know! I used to think I wanted to travel, but then I realised I hate airports. And I thought maybe a different job, but everything seems… hard. And I’m good at my job, actually. It's just... not  inspiring . Okay, okay. Deep breaths. You’re allowed to want a job that doesn’t set your soul on fire. It pays the bills, right? It gives you disposable income for pottery classes and cat food. That’s… a depressingly practical way of looking at it. Sometimes practical is good. What about side hustles? Have you thought about something creative? You were always brilliant at drawing. I haven't drawn since uni. I’m probably terrible now. And I don’t have time. I spend all my week trying to stay afloat at work, then collapse into a heap on the sofa and binge-watch terrible reality TV. Okay, new plan. We're limiting reality TV. One night a week, max. And we are signing up for that life drawing class down the art centre.

Honestly, I’m fuming with Liam. He’s been proper distant all day. Oh, not again? What’s he done this time? Is he still going on about that girl from his work? No, not specifically, but it's just… like he’s barely spoken to me. Just grunts and nods, you know? And he’s been on his phone  constantly . He didn’t even notice I’d got my hair cut! Ooh, that  is  bad. A haircut is a big deal. Men are clueless sometimes. Did you ask him what’s up? I tried! He just said he was tired. Tired?! We’ve been sat on a beach all day, doing nothing! How can you be tired from doing nothing? Boys. Honestly. It's always something. Remember when Mark pretended he had a work emergency to avoid coming to my birthday? Oh god, don’t even remind me! That was awful. You were so upset. Still makes me mad for you, actually. Yeah, it was rubbish. Although, looking back, he was a bit of a… well, you know. A complete waste of space, yeah. You dodged a bullet with that one, babe. I think I’m starting to think I need to dodge a bullet with Liam, too. It’s just… I saw him liking some girl’s photo on Instagram earlier. Not a super obvious like, just a quick double tap, but still. Right, well that’s a classic move. The sneaky little double tap. Ugh, the worst! It’s not the liking itself, it’s the  concealing  of the liking. Why not just be open about it, or not like it at all? Exactly! And Chloe’s been going on about how amazing her new boyfriend is all day. It’s just… rubbing salt in the wound, you know? Like, she’s showing off and I'm here, feeling ignored. Oh, Chloe always has to be the happiest person in the room. It’s exhausting. Don't let her get to you. Honestly, she's a bit competitive. She always has to one-up everyone. Remember when she claimed she’d already read all the books on our reading list for uni, and then admitted she hadn’t even started them? Oh my god, yes! The absolute nerve! I think I need a glass of wine. Or three. Now  you're  talking. I’m with you. Let's forget the boys and the Instagrams and the competitive friends and just enjoy being in France.

Honestly, this shepherd’s pie is amazing, love. You’ve outdone yourself. Thanks, Mum. It’s really good. Though, Mr. Henderson said Mrs. Davies makes a better one. Oh,  does  he now? Mr. Henderson clearly has questionable taste. Mrs. Davies uses ready-made mash, everyone knows. He’s just trying to get on your good side, Sarah. Classic Henderson tactic. Though, I will admit, the Davies’ do have a rather competitive streak when it comes to cooking. Did you see Liam’s goal in the hockey match today? It was mental! He just… flicked it over the goalie’s head. Yeah! I was there! Crazy, right? He’s gonna be so smug all week. Smug is an understatement. He’s been insufferable since Year 7. Still, good for him. Did you manage to speak to Emily’s mum about the weekend trip to Alton Towers? I did. She said Emily’s really keen, but has a Brownies meeting on Saturday morning, so we’d have to pick her up afterwards. We could maybe leave a bit later? That sounds perfect. We can grab a coffee while we wait, and then head straight over. Have you booked the fast passes yet? I don’t fancy queuing for Nemesis for an hour. Not yet, Dad. I was going to do it tomorrow. They release new ones, don’t they? They do, yes. Best to get on as soon as they’re available. It’s chaos otherwise. Are you still planning on going to Barcelona with your friends, Leo? Yeah, in the summer. Hopefully. We're still trying to sort out flights and accommodation. It’s proving harder than we thought. Everything’s so expensive. Barcelona is lovely, though. I went years ago with your Auntie Carol. We got completely lost in the Gothic Quarter one day. Ended up eating the best tapas of my life in some tiny little backstreet bar. Tapas? What's tapas? Little snacks, Leo. Spanish snacks. Lots of different things – olives, potatoes, little bits of meat... We spent hours wandering around, just soaking up the atmosphere. It was wonderful. You should definitely go, even if it means cutting back on some other things. Experiences are much more valuable than possessions. I guess. It’s just… we really want to go to the water park as well, and that’s another expense. Perhaps you could do a bit of fundraising?

Honestly, the size of these trees is just… mind-blowing. It makes you feel incredibly small, doesn’t it? It really does. I keep trying to get a photo that captures it, but it’s just impossible. Everything looks… miniature in comparison. Did you see that one we passed, the one you could literally drive a car through? Oh my god, yes! I couldn't believe it. It’s just… how old are these things, even? It's almost incomprehensible. Makes you think about everything, you know? All our little dramas. Totally. It puts things into perspective. Speaking of little dramas, have you heard anything from Amelia since she went to that pottery class? She was so stressed about it, worried she’d be terrible. I haven’t, actually. I messaged her a couple of days ago, just a quick check-in, but she hasn’t replied. Probably engrossed in shaping clay masterpieces. Or, you know, regretting her life choices. Knowing Amelia, probably a bit of both. She always overthinks everything. Remember when she was convinced Mark was going to propose on that disastrous camping trip? Oh lord, yes! The rain, the leaky tent, the badger trying to steal their biscuits… and she was scanning the horizon for a ring! It was hilarious. Poor thing. He didn't even bring the ring with him. Exactly! And she’d spent weeks subtly trying to drop hints about wanting a vintage engagement ring. It was all very carefully orchestrated, and then the badgers ruined everything. Speaking of relationships… how’s your cousin, Chloe, doing with Ben? Last I heard, things were a bit rocky after that awful Christmas with his mum. It’s… complicated. They're still together, but she's constantly complaining about his mum interfering. Apparently, she's started sending unsolicited baby clothes. Chloe doesn't even  want  babies yet. Oh my god, that’s awful! That’s such a classic overbearing mother-in-law move. I’d lose it. Chloe’s trying to be diplomatic, but I think she's reaching breaking point. She said Ben just shrugs it off and says his mum means well. Which is… not helpful. No, it really isn’t. Ben sounds a bit spineless, to be honest. You need someone who’ll stand up for you. Honestly, families can be exhausting. Makes you appreciate not having  too  much drama in your own. Tell me about it.

Right so, the Kievs were… remarkably good. Honestly. I wasn’t expecting much, Tesco value and all, but they were actually decent. Were they like, proper squirty inside? That's the best bit. Don't talk with your mouth full, darling. And yes, they were beautifully squirty. Though I think your father nearly scalded himself. A little bit, aye. Needed a moment to cool down. Speaking of needing a moment, did anyone catch the rugby today? Nah, I was playing FIFA. Ireland won though, right? I saw something on Twitter. Won comfortably enough. Sexton was on form, which is always a good sign. A proper thrashing of whatever team they were playing. Wales maybe? Italy, actually. A good win, but nothing to get overly excited about, is it? We need to see them beat a proper team before we start celebrating. True enough. Right, we need to firm up plans for Granny. Are we still going on Saturday? I think so. Unless she rings and cancels again. She has been a bit flakey lately. Said her hip was playing up. She always says her hip is playing up. It's a tactic. She wants extra attention. Don’t be giving your grandmother backchat, young man. Show some respect! She's a lovely woman and she misses us. I  am  being respectful. Just saying. She’s a bit of a drama queen. Like, remember that time she pretended to fall down the stairs? Oh, don’t even start. It turned out she’d just tripped over the cat. Honestly, she’s a character. She sent me a link to some photos earlier, she’s finally figured out how to use Flickr. Good for her! Though I swear, she keeps trying to send me things via Dropbox that are just… blank documents. She doesn't quite grasp the concept, bless her. She thinks you're meant to  put  the photos  in  the Dropbox folder, not share a link. It's a lost cause. Oh, and apparently there's a hedgehog in the garden. She's left biscuits out for it. A hedgehog? Cool! Can I go look? After you’ve finished your dinner. And no chasing it! They’re prickly little things. Actually, I'm feeling a bit of a headache coming on. All this excitement. Oh dear. Maybe you shouldn't have had that second Kiev. No, it wasn’t the Kiev.

Right, so I’ve put the potatoes on to boil. Are you wanting peas or green beans with this? Peas, definitely peas. Though, honestly, I could just eat a loaf of that buckwheat bread with some cheese and be happy. It's so much nicer than normal bread. Isn’t it? I was looking at some recipes online for making it myself, but it seemed… involved. Easier to just get it from the market. Much easier. And speaking of the market, did you see they’ve got that new stall selling those handmade chocolates? Apparently, they’re amazing. Ooh, no, I haven’t! I must have a look on Saturday. Oh! The cups arrived! The eBay ones? Already? That was quick. Yes! They’re in the kitchen, I’ve just quickly unwrapped them. Come and see. They’re even prettier than the photos. One’s a really delicate floral pattern, and the other is this amazing art deco style. Oh, lovely! You have a real eye for these things. I always think they look so much nicer than modern china. So much more character. I know, right? And they’re surprisingly affordable on eBay, especially if you’re patient. Though I did get slightly carried away and bid on another one… Oh, you! Don't tell me you're starting a collection? Well… maybe. It’s just, they’re so pretty, and it feels a bit sad for them to just sit in someone’s attic. It's like rescuing them. Anyway, back to dinner. Are you still up for going to Sarah’s leaving do on Friday? Absolutely. I've already booked a taxi. It’s a shame she's leaving, she was brilliant to work with. Though she did say she’s hoping to come back for a visit once she’s settled in. That would be nice. I didn’t realise she’d been there so long. It feels like only yesterday she started. Doesn’t it? Time flies. Right, can I help with anything, or are you fully in control of the potato situation? I can do the peas when they're ready. You can do the peas, that would be wonderful. And maybe set the table? I’m trying to finish this transcription before we eat, it’s a really long one about… well, it’s incredibly dull, actually. Something about agricultural practices. Sounds riveting. Well, I'll get the good cutlery out then, to make it a slightly more glamorous experience.

Honestly though, seeing how much paperwork you’re dealing with… it’s mental. And for what? A couple of extra quid? It's not a couple of extra quid, Liv. It's keeping the business afloat. Everything's going up, isn’t it? And people want everything cheaper. It’s a nightmare. You’re basically a professional paper pusher, aren’t you, Sarah? Don’t start, Tom. It’s not just paper pushing. It's compliance, risk assessment, knowing the regulations inside and out... It’s actually really… stressful. Sounds like a right headache. Remember when I used to just turn up to a building site, yell at a few lads and get paid? Those were the days. None of this “Know Your Customer” nonsense. Dad! You were doing dodgy stuff! Dodgy? No, streamlining! Adapting to the needs of the client! Semantics. Exactly the kind of attitude that lands people in trouble. Honestly, the amount of money laundering that goes on… you wouldn’t believe it. Especially through seemingly legitimate businesses. You seen those documentaries? They make it look so easy. Just funnel it through a few shell companies and Bob’s your uncle. It’s not that easy. Believe me. The banks are getting really, really strict. They’re flagging everything now. We had a customer whose account was frozen last week because they deposited a large sum of cash. Turned out their grandma had passed and left them an inheritance, but proving it was a legit source… it was a whole saga. So, like, what happens if you  do  get caught? Oh, huge fines. Criminal charges. Depending on the amount, potentially jail time. It’s not worth the risk. That’s why I'm so vigilant. It's my livelihood on the line. Speaking of livelihoods… how's little Leo doing? Is he showing any artistic flair yet? Heard he was obsessed with painting. He’s terrible. Absolutely terrible. It’s mostly just brown and green smudges. But he loves it, which is the main thing. Daniel’s trying to encourage him, says he was a bit of a mini-Picasso himself when he was younger. Picasso? You? Never. You couldn’t draw a straight line with a ruler. He claims he could. It's probably rose-tinted nostalgia. And speaking of kids… how’s Jess doing with her university applications? Has she decided what she wants to do with her life yet?

Honestly, this weather is doing my head in. One minute it’s sunshine, the next it’s chucking it down. Makes planning anything impossible. Tell me about it. I had a garden event scheduled for next week, a little coffee morning for donors, and I'm half tempted to cancel. Soggy bottoms aren't a good look for fundraising, are they? No, definitely not! Although, a bit of rain might discourage people from lingering  too  long, which could be a bonus if you’re trying to get through the pitch quickly. Mean! But true. Speaking of lingering, how’s the sign language class going, Mum? Are you still managing it with everything else? It’s…challenging. My brain feels like it’s turned to mush some days. Trying to remember all those hand shapes is harder than it looks! And then trying to recall the right one at the right time, it's a disaster. Old age, I suppose. Nonsense, love. You’re as sharp as a tack. It’s good you're doing something for yourself though, you deserve it. Yeah, it’s really good! And useful. I’ve already used a couple of signs with the kids at school, it’s brilliant when you see their faces light up when they understand. Honestly, it's such a thoughtful thing. Anyway, how are you feeling, Jess? Still morning sickness city? It’s…easing up slightly, thank goodness. Still not exactly enjoying food, but I can at least keep it down most days now. And the tiredness is still crippling. I feel like a sloth. Oh sweetheart, you just need to rest. Don’t push yourself. And eat what you can, even if it's just biscuits. Anything’s better than nothing. You’ve got a good support network here, you know. We’re all here to help. I'm happy to do more grocery runs or whatever you need. Same here. I'm on my feet all day at work, but I can always spare an hour or two. And I make a mean lasagna, if you fancy something a bit more substantial than biscuits. Lasagna sounds…amazing. Honestly, you guys are the best. It's just… it’s all a bit overwhelming, isn’t it? First baby, new job… feels like everything’s changing at once. It is overwhelming, darling. But you’re strong, you’re capable, and you're going to be a wonderful mum.

Honestly, the amount of emails I’ve had to sift through this morning is… startling. It’s like everyone decided Monday was the day to unleash all their queries. Tell me about it. I spent the first hour just deleting things. Mostly people who apparently haven't read the submission guidelines. It’s infuriating. Oh, same! I had three manuscripts where the formatting was just… all over the place. Double-spaced, single-spaced, random fonts. Like, seriously? It’s not that hard. You guys are lucky you get manuscripts. I’m mostly just spreadsheets and… well, more spreadsheets. And trying to figure out why the coffee machine is making noises again. Oh, the coffee machine. It’s a sentient being plotting against us, I’m convinced. It only works properly on Fridays, as a final act of passive aggression. It's a conspiracy, I tell you! Right, so, anyone actually manage to  do  any actual research today, or were we all just consumed by the inbox vortex? I got a little bit done on the dialect variation project. Found some really interesting data points in the Cambridge News archives. People use ‘round ‘ere’ a surprising amount, even now. Oh, that’s good! I'm worried my project is going to hit a wall soon. Trying to map regional variations in politeness strategies is… a nightmare. Everyone’s just so individual. Sounds intense. I was reading an article the other day about how politeness is culturally constructed. It makes sense, but it also makes everything so much more complicated to study. It does! And it’s all so nuanced. Like, is a dry, sarcastic comment rude, or a sign of affection? Depending on where you are, it could be either. Exactly! Then you get into the regional differences – what's considered direct in Manchester might be considered incredibly aggressive in, like, Norfolk. Precisely! And then you add age and gender into the mix… It's a logistical nightmare. I’m starting to think I should have just studied something simpler, like… astrophysics. Don’t even suggest that. At least language has everyday applications. Try explaining astrophysics to your grandma. Very true. Though, explaining what I  actually  do to my grandma is equally challenging. “So you… read books, and then tell people to change them?” Haha, pretty much. Mine thinks I just…validate spelling. Oh God, mine thinks I transcribe things. She asked me if I was writing subtitles for TV.

Right, so the visa application… absolute nightmare, innit? They want a letter from my nan stating I’m a good egg. A  letter . From my nan. Seriously? That’s mental. They just wanna make sure you’re not planning on defecting or something. Good luck getting Nan to type one up, she still struggles with sending texts. Exactly! She thinks ‘LOL’ is a medical condition. I’m gonna have to write it  for  her and get her to sign it. It feels a bit dodgy, doesn’t it? A bit. But needs must, eh? Mongolia isn't gonna let us in based on charm alone. Speaking of which, have you got the passport photos sorted? Nope. That’s another job for tomorrow. I’ve been putting it off. I look awful in passport photos. Like a criminal. They always make you look awful. It's the lighting. There’s that booth at the market, the one near the bakery. It’s alright. Quick, cheap. Yeah, I might give that a go. Better than trying to get a decent one at home, with my mum directing me like I’m auditioning for a police lineup. Ha! Right, donations… we’re still a bit short, aren’t we? I put another post up on Facebook, but it wasn't exactly inundated with pledges. Barely. People are tight. I was thinking… Gumtree? We could put an ad on Gumtree. “Two lads driving to Mongolia for charity, please donate!” Gumtree? That’s… optimistic. I’m not sure it’s the target demographic for charitable giving. But honestly, at this point, I’m open to anything. It’s worth a shot, I suppose? Exactly! We’re desperate. “Reliable car, experienced drivers, hilarious journey. Please help us reach our target for [Charity Name]!” We can add a picture of the car looking all muddy and adventurous. That's… marginally less embarrassing than I expected. Alright, I'll draft something up tonight. We need to emphasize the ‘Mongolia’ bit. People get more excited by exotic locations. Good shout. Oh, and I finally got a quote for the engine service. It’s… not cheap. How much? Don't tell me it’s another grand. No, not  that  bad. But six hundred and fifty. Which is still… a lot. Considering we’re relying on this thing to get us across half of Asia. Right. Well, we  have  to do it.

Right, honestly, I still can’t believe you ended up in A&E. Over an arm. I  told  you it was bad! It felt like it was going to fall off. And honestly, I was half-cut, which probably didn't help my assessment of the situation. Half-cut is an understatement, wasn’t it? You were practically horizontal by ten. Didn't even make it to Sugar. Hey, a girl needs to self-medicate sometimes. Uni is stressful! And you both were having a brilliant time, I didn't want to ruin it. Ruin it? You  did  ruin it, having to drag you to the bus stop, then having a waiting room full of judgemental looks. Honestly, what did the doctor even say? Just a sprain. A really dramatic sprain, apparently. They gave me a sling and told me to take paracetamol. Dramatic, I tell you. A dramatic sprain! Of course it was. Come on, let's get you some tea. You look absolutely grey. Kitchen time? Oh god, yes please. I haven’t properly hydrated since… well, since before the dramatic sprain. Lead the way.    So, anyone got any plans for tonight? Apart from you, obviously, being a medical marvel. Plans? I’m planning on existing. Maybe a gentle Netflix binge. Definitely avoiding anything vaguely resembling physical activity. I was thinking of going to the film screening in the Furness bar. They’re showing that new Wes Anderson one. Ooh, yeah! I heard it’s good. Though, honestly, I’m still recovering from last night. And thinking about lectures tomorrow is filling me with dread. Lectures. The bane of my existence. Honestly, I’m starting to question my life choices. Why did I pick this course again? You said you loved the creative writing aspect? I  did . Before the constant essays and the crippling sense of inadequacy. Speaking of choices, are you still seeing…what’s his name? The one from County? Liam? God, no. We had a massive row last week. He kept saying my accent was ‘too strong’. Honestly, the cheek. Too strong?! What an idiot. You've got a lovely accent. It’s proper. Unlike some people… Oh, are we gatekeeping accents now? Is Warwick considered acceptable dialect territory? Hey! It’s very refined. Very… neutral. And anyway, Liam sounds like a tool. He is. I'm officially single and focusing on my degree. And maybe… finding someone who appreciates a good Scouse accent.

So, did you have a good time at Gran and Grandad’s anniversary? Honestly, it was a bit chaotic, wasn’t it? Yeah, it was good. Loads of people though. Could barely move in the conservatory. Tell me about it! Auntie Brenda was holding court, as usual, with her stories about… well, I don’t even know  what  half of them were about this time. Something about a pigeon and a market stall? Yeah, I overheard a bit of that. She does love a good tale, doesn’t she? I mostly hung out with Tom and Charlie. We were raiding the buffet. Of course you were! That buffet was impressive, though. Your Grandma really outdid herself. Did you try the mini quiches? They were lovely. Yeah, the quiches were good. I had about three. And loads of the sausage rolls. They went  fast . Uncle David basically camped out in front of the sausage roll platter, I swear. Oh,  David . He's got a one-track mind when it comes to sausage rolls.
