Honestly, he’d probably fight you for the last one. Did you speak to Cousin Emily much? She seemed a bit quiet. Not really, no. She was talking to Great-Auntie Maureen for ages. Probably hearing about all her medical complaints. Maureen does love a good moan. She does, doesn't she? It’s exhausting just  being  near her sometimes! Poor Emily. I tried to corner her later, to ask about university, but she’d disappeared. Did you see Liam trying to help Grandad with the music? It was a disaster. Grandad was trying to explain how to work the playlist and Liam just kept pressing random buttons. Oh, that was hilarious! Grandad was getting more and more flustered. He’s a patient man, but even he has his limits. It ended up being a mash-up of opera and… I think it was heavy metal? Yeah! It was so random. Everyone was laughing. I think even Grandad started to see the funny side in the end. He did, eventually. It was a nice day overall, though, wasn't it? Just lovely to have everyone together. Even with the chaos. Yeah. It was good. Although, I'm still recovering from all the sugar. I feel a bit sick now. Well, that’s what happens when you have three quiches and a mountain of sausage rolls! Perhaps a walk later might help?

Honestly, Dad, you've got like, six water bottles in the door pocket. Six! What are you even  doing  with all those? Well, you know me, always prepared. One for now, one for later, one in case… you get thirsty. And one for emergencies. Plus, you always finish yours, so… I finish mine because I’m actually  doing  stuff! You’re just driving. And you had a coffee like, twenty minutes ago. It was a small coffee. And I might want another. You never know what the traffic's like further down. Need to stay hydrated, you know. Speaking of which, did you remember to pack your pens? For the journey? Yes! In my bag. Why does everyone always ask me about pens? It's like my entire personality is "girl who has pens." Just making sure. You were complaining last time about not being able to do the Sudoku. Right, lunch. We’re stopping near Exeter, yeah? That services place? Remember the one with the decent sandwiches? If ‘decent’ means slightly stale and overpriced, then yeah. Maybe we should’ve just brought a proper picnic. Too much faff. And who’d carry it? Besides, I was going to swing by Holland & Barrett in Exeter, see if they’ve got that stuff for… you know. Oh, not the IBS stuff again. Honestly, Dad, you worry too much. Just avoid the spicy food and everything will be fine. It's not  just  the spicy food. Remember what happened last year? It was a disaster. It's just good to be prepared. Okay, okay, prepared Dad. Just… let’s not spend half an hour reading ingredient lists. And please, no more stories about Mrs. Henderson’s move. We've heard it five times already. She’s a lovely woman! And it was a complicated move. And she’s got all that antique furniture… proper stuff, you know, from a manor house. They don’t make ‘em like that anymore. Right. Manor houses. That’s fascinating. Are we nearly at the M5 yet? This A30 is  slow . Nearly. And speaking of houses, if we ever moved, I’d want somewhere with a proper driveway. Not like that little postage stamp we've got now. And a garden big enough for a washing line. And a cat flap. Don't forget the cat flap for Winston. Of course, for Winston! He'd have a fit if he couldn’t patrol the garden.

Honestly, the amount of jargon they use in these medical reports… it’s a different language entirely. I spent half an hour today trying to decipher what ‘peri-orbital ecchymosis’ actually  meant . Peri-orbital… sounds painful. Is it… bruising around the eye? Yes! Exactly! Bruising around the eye. You’d think they could just  say  that, wouldn’t you? Oh, the medical profession. Always needing to sound important. It was the same when I was a headmistress, you know. Inventing terms to make simple things sound complicated. ‘Learning challenges’ instead of ‘struggling with reading’. Aye, it’s the same in my trade. “Optimised structural integrity.” Means “I nailed it straight.” Honestly. Keeps the punters thinking you’ve done something clever. Exactly! It's infuriating when it's just deliberately obfuscating things. I mean, I’m a graduate, I’m used to complex texts, but this is just… excessive. I get it. Work’s full of it too. We had a new initiative launched last month – “Synergistic Cross-Departmental Collaboration.” Turns out it means “everyone has to talk to each other more.” Oh dear. They certainly have a knack for turning perfectly sensible concepts into utter nonsense. Remember when ‘downsizing’ became ‘rightsizing’? Truly dreadful. They keep talkin’ about ‘streamlining’ where I am. Means someone’s gettin’ the chop, usually. Fancy word for firin’, innit? It feels like it’s designed to distance people from the reality of things. Makes it all… abstract. It does, doesn’t it? Like they’re trying to avoid taking responsibility. “It’s not a firing, it's a streamlining!” It’s a lack of honesty, plain and simple. I always told my pupils – and my staff – that clarity and directness were the most important qualities. Aye, that’s good advice. Straight talkin’ gets you further than all the fancy words. Sometimes I just tell a client, “Look, this’ll cost ya this much, and I’ll get it done.” No need for fluff. It’s refreshing to hear someone say that. I’m surrounded by legal and medical terminology all day, it's nice to come here and have a bit of… common sense. Definitely. A bit of reality. It’s good to just… chat. Does this fit what you were looking for? I tried to keep it natural and flowing, with each speaker contributing based on their implied backgrounds. Let me know if you'd like adjustments!

Right, Operation Mother’s Day is a go. What have we got so far? Leo, have you finished making your card? Almost! I need glitter. And I want to draw a really big dinosaur on it. A T-Rex! I’ve made mine! It’s got sparkly hearts all over it! And I wrote “I love you, Mummy” inside. Oh, that’s lovely, sweetheart. That’s  really  lovely. And Leo, a dinosaur is a brilliant idea. Just…maybe not  too  much glitter, okay? We don’t want to be finding glitter in our sandwiches for the next month. Okay. But dinosaurs are awesome! They ruled the world! They certainly did. And now, what about breakfast? I was thinking we could make pancakes. Ooooh! With strawberries? And chocolate chips? Maybe both! We can be very fancy. And then, after breakfast, we need to decide what we’re doing for the rest of the day. Can we go to Forest School? Please, please, please? Hmm, that’s a good idea. But Forest School isn’t on today, is it? It’s Sunday. Oh. Right. I forgot. Can we  pretend  it’s Forest School in the garden then? We can build a den! That's a fantastic idea! We can definitely build a den. We can gather sticks and leaves and everything. Maybe even find some feathers. Feathers! I love feathers! Me too. It'll be fun. Now, I was talking to Mrs. Higgins at school yesterday, and she was saying how you two are always getting into scrapes. She said you're “little monkeys.” What does that mean? Are we turning into monkeys? No, silly! It’s an idiom. It means you’re a bit mischievous, a bit cheeky. A bit… playful! Like playing hide and seek? Exactly like playing hide and seek! Sometimes adults say funny things that don’t  mean  exactly what they say. Like, if I said “it’s raining cats and dogs,” would you think cats and dogs were falling from the sky? YES! No! It just means it's raining very, very hard. It’s just a way of saying things. Oh. That's silly. It is a bit silly. But that’s what idioms are! Right, pancakes are calling my name. Let’s get cooking! And then, den-building and a lovely, relaxed Mother’s Day. Sound good? Speaker_3 & Speaker_2 : YAY! Mummy, can we have extra chocolate chips?

…and honestly, the guilt is awful, you know? Just knowing she wasn’t herself for so long before. We all just… accepted it, didn’t we? Accepted the tiredness, the withdrawal. Said she was ‘just getting old’. It’s so easy to do that, isn’t it? To rationalise things. To tell yourself it's just… a phase. With my dad, it was the coughing. He’d always had a bit of a smoker’s cough, but it just got… deeper. And we kept saying, “Oh, it’s just the winter.” Exactly! And then the diagnosis… it felt like a punch. It’s not that we didn’t expect something was wrong, but… the  cancer  word. It just changes everything. It does. Everything filters through that. You look back on every little symptom, every missed opportunity to push for something more. Do you think… Do you think she knew, your Nan? I honestly don’t know. She never said. But there were moments… moments where she’d just look at me, with this… sadness. Like she was already saying goodbye. Makes you wonder, doesn't it? Whether it's a sixth sense or just reading body language. It’s probably both. And grief’s a funny thing, innit? It doesn’t happen in stages like they say it does. It’s messy. It’s… exhausting. I still have days where I just completely fall apart, thinking about Mum. Me too. And it’s been nearly three years now. People say, “You should be over it by now.” Like there’s a deadline on heartache. Honestly, the ignorance some people have. It’s awful. It’s like they think you just… switch it off. Has Liam been okay? He’s usually so good at bottling things up, he must be struggling. He is. But he’s trying so hard for the kids. He’s been really quiet, though. He’s started running again, which is good, I think. A healthy distraction. I’m worried about him though, he's been having trouble sleeping. I think he needs to talk to someone, but he's so stubborn. Men are! My Andy won’t even consider it. Just brushes it off as stress from work. It’s just… they’re so afraid of appearing weak. Exactly. And it's not weakness to need help, is it? It’s strength. I’m thinking of suggesting he try that mindfulness app, Headspace.

Right, so I think I’ve finally cracked the dissertation timetable. Monday is solely literature review, Tuesday is methodology, Wednesday is data analysis… it’s ambitious, I know. Sounds…intense. You’ll be chained to your desk. Seriously though, good on you for actually  making  one. I’m still just… existing in a haze of reading. Did you finish that article on minimalist syntax I sent over? Minimalist syntax? Oh god, no. It was… dense. I got about three pages in and my brain started to leak out my ears. It felt like trying to assemble IKEA furniture with instructions written in Klingon. That’s pretty accurate. It was a bit of a beast. Though, Professor Davies was  raving  about it in the seminar yesterday. Apparently, it’s key to understanding the Chomsky hierarchy. Davies loves to throw curveballs. Remember that lecture where he spent half an hour discussing the socio-linguistics of pigeon English? Completely out of the blue! Oh, yeah! And then acted offended when everyone was confused. He's brilliant, but eccentric. Speaking of brilliance… I’m starving. What’s for lunch? Is it more lentil soup? Actually, I was thinking we could try that Korean bibimbap recipe we saw online. I picked up some gochujang yesterday. Ooh, yes! I’m in. Though I'm slightly worried about the tofu prep. It has to be  just  right, doesn’t it? Not too soggy, not too dry... I’ve watched, like, five YouTube tutorials. I think I’ve got it covered. And it’s infinitely better than more lentil soup, even if it  does  involve a surprising amount of chopping. True. Though to be fair, lentil soup is pretty economical. Tuition fees are looming, y’know. Have you checked your student finance yet? Don't remind me. It’s a black hole of bureaucracy. Apparently, there's been a "delay" in processing my application. Which translates to: they've probably lost it. Classic. Maybe we should just start a crowdfunding campaign? “Help Ben Survive University – Donate Now!” Tempting. Though I suspect my family would prefer I got a part-time job. They’re not huge fans of “online begging”. Speaking of family, have you heard from your Mum recently? Is she still trying to set you up with that… lawyer’s son? Please don’t. He’s a lovely guy, apparently, but the sheer  banality … He mostly talks about property prices in Kent.

Honestly, this pizza is saving my life. I swear, that physics problem set nearly broke me. Tell me about it! I was staring at that equation for a solid hour and then just…gave up. It’s like they  want  us to fail, isn’t it? Nah, they just want to see who’s actually paying attention in lectures. Though honestly, half the time I’m just mentally planning my next Sugarhouse trip. You and Sugarhouse! Seriously, you’re going to be on first-name terms with the bouncers soon. Speaking of which, remember when Liam tried to sneak in with a fake ID? Oh my god,  yes . And insisted it was totally legit? The look on his face when they confiscated it… Priceless. Remember the flooding a couple of years ago? I thought we were all going to be swimming to lectures. This house, especially, is built basically at water level. Ugh, don't remind me. My mum nearly had a heart attack. She was convinced we were all going to lose everything. She kept texting, "Are you on higher ground?!". Like we could just  climb  somewhere. She’s a worrier, your mum. Remember when she said backpacking in Africa was a ‘death wish’? Oh yeah! And then got really into watching those travel documentaries and said, "Oh, maybe it's not  so  bad." The flip-flop was amazing. Speaking of things that are amazing... anyone fancy a round of Articulate after this? I’ve got some scorchers ready. Ooh, yes! Head’s Up too? I always win at Head’s Up, just saying. You just shout random things and hope for the best! It’s not skill, it’s chaos. Like trying to follow the plot of  Cloud Atlas . Honestly. That film… try explain it to someone. And don’t even get me started on the  Chaos Walking  trilogy. I thought I’d lost brain cells reading those. I’m still recovering from Twilight, honestly. I was so young and impressionable. I can’t believe I ever thought Edward Cullen was… appealing. We all have our dark pasts. Mine involves watching  The Vampire Diaries  religiously for like, three years. Don’t judge. No judgement here. Mine's probably rewatching  How I Met Your Mother  every single summer. It's just comfort TV. Comfort TV is essential. Did anyone see Jack Whitehall’s Christmas special on  The Big Fat Quiz ?

And then she just…launched into it, right? About how the new coffee machine in the office is basically a personal attack on her. A personal attack? Seriously? Dead serious. Apparently, it doesn't froth the milk  exactly  how she likes it. Like, it’s a fraction off, and she claims it's a deliberate attempt to sabotage her morning routine. Wow. That’s… a level of dedication to being annoyed I didn’t know existed. Is she always like that? Oh, you have  no  idea. Last week it was the desk plants. Someone moved hers approximately three centimetres to the left, and she spent an hour trying to figure out who the culprit was, convinced it was passive-aggressive office politics. Three centimetres? Oh my god. It's like a sitcom. Honestly, it is. And the worst part is, she's really good at making everyone else feel bad for not understanding her struggles. She’ll be like, “You wouldn’t  get  it. This is  important ." Sounds exhausting. So, has anyone tried just…buying her a personal milk frother? Someone suggested it, but she said that would be “giving in to the tyranny of inadequate office equipment.” I swear, I'm not making this up. That’s…a very specific stance. You're better than me, I would’ve just bought the frother and quietly celebrated a moment of peace. I considered it. Strongly. But then I thought, that would just enable the behaviour. Plus, honestly, it’s good for a laugh sometimes, as long as she’s not directly interrogating  me  about the thermostat settings. Fair enough. It’s good to have office entertainment, right? Keeps things interesting. Speaking of interesting, did you manage to finish that article I sent you about the new quantum computing breakthrough? Oh, that one. I started it, but my brain sort of glazed over about halfway through. It's just… a lot. I’m good with words, you know, analysing language patterns and all that, but quantum physics… it’s another level. Yeah, it’s pretty dense stuff. It’s basically a whole new way of thinking about reality. See? That's why I stick to sentence structures and verb conjugations. Much safer. It doesn't threaten my fundamental understanding of…well, anything. True. Maybe we should stick to discussing office drama then. It’s far less likely to induce an existential crisis. Definitely.

This weather, eh? Proper miserable. Feels like it’s been raining for a fortnight. Tell me about it. My joints are aching somethin’ awful. Can’t be good for anyone, this damp. I swear it gets right  into  you. Mum’s right. It’s absolutely grim. I had to cycle in this morning, and I was soaked through before I even got to the university. Though, honestly, worse than the rain is the wind. Aye, the wind’s biting. Though I’m more concerned about my new telly. Bought a fancy OLED, all the rage apparently, and I’m worried about the humidity. Read online it can damage the panels. A telly, eh? What’s wrong with the one you had? Seems like you’re always buying new gadgets. It wasn’t an OLED, Dad. Massive difference. And the old one… well, it was getting a bit… fuzzy. Plus, the smart features just weren’t cutting it anymore. Keeps buffering, you know? Buffering? Is that one of those computer things? Honestly, I struggle with the remote control sometimes, let alone all this… technology. It means it stops and starts when you’re streaming things, Nan. Like when you're watching programmes online. Online? Why would you want to watch programmes online when you’ve got a perfectly good telly aerial? Because you get a wider choice, Dad. And catch-up services. Plus everything’s in HD. HD? Crikey. All sounds very complicated to me. Though I must say, that Dr. Turner on  Call the Midwife  is a handsome man. That’s a programme I can understand. Mum, you say that every week. Well, he is! And he’s always so kind. Unlike my Arthur… always moaning about something. Speaking of moaning, how's your back, dear? Still giving you gyp? It’s alright, it’s alright. Just stiff, that’s all. The rheumatologist said it’s just wear and tear. Everything wears out eventually, doesn’t it? Like this old body. You’ve got to look after it, Dad. Do your exercises. Exercises! At my age? Honestly, I just want to sit in my chair and watch Norwich get thrashed again. They were awful on Saturday. Absolutely dreadful. Oh, don't start on the football, Dad. It'll only ruin your afternoon. Ruin it? They  already  ruined it! Lost two-nil to Millwall. Millwall! It’s a disgrace. At least the tea’s good.

Honestly, the wedding planning is… a lot. I thought I was organised, but then you start looking at flowers and suddenly you're questioning all your life choices. Oh, tell me about it. Even picking a flavour for the cake felt monumental. Did you go for the lemon and elderflower everyone’s obsessed with? Ugh, lemon and elderflower is  so  last year. It's all about lavender and honey now, apparently. Though honestly, I’m just excited for the free cake. You lot are already stressing about the details?! It's months away! I’m just happy I managed to find a dress that doesn’t make me look like a lampshade. A lampshade! Oh, you’re awful. But seriously, it’s easy to get carried away. Mum's already offering to make canapés for a hundred people. A hundred! Your mum is a legend, but maybe gently steer her towards a slightly more manageable number. Remember Sarah? Her mum nearly took over her entire wedding. It was a disaster. Oh god, yes! She completely rearranged the seating plan the day before, because apparently Aunt Carol didn’t “vibe” with Uncle Dave. Bless Sarah. So, how’s Mark holding up? Is he coping with the flower arrangements and the seating charts? He’s… helpful. In the way that he says “whatever you want, honey” a lot. Which is sweet, but doesn’t actually contribute. I’m starting to think he just wants the free booze. Classic Mark. Speaking of boys, are we still on for dinner with Liam and Ben next week? I haven’t seen them in ages. Yeah, definitely. Though I’m warning you, Ben is  obsessed  with his new sourdough starter. Prepare for an hour-long lecture on fermentation. Oh, god. He’s the worst. Remember when he tried to explain the complexities of brewing kombucha at my birthday? I just wanted to drink prosecco. Oh, I’ve heard. Apparently, he’s considering opening a microbrewery. Oh please no. Another pretentious beer snob is the last thing we need. Anyway, I saw Chloe the other day. She’s talking about trying for a baby. Already?! They just got married, didn’t they? People are so quick to have kids now. It's terrifying. I know, right? I’m not even sure I want them. It feels like such a huge responsibility. Although, Mark keeps hinting… He’s started looking at prams online.

Honestly, this new telly… it’s got more buttons than a spaceship. I swear, I spend more time trying to  find  something to watch than actually watching it. Oh, you and technology, Arthur! You've always been a bit of a Luddite, haven't you? My grandson, Leo, he sets everything up for me, bless him. Still, I do wish things weren't so complicated. It’s the interfaces, isn’t it? Designed by people who think everyone’s a computer whizz. I had a parent complain the other day, said the online homework portal was “intimidating.” Intimidating! It’s learning to log in, basically. Intimidating! That’s a good word for it. Reminds me of when they first brought in those automatic checkout machines at the supermarket. Spent a good ten minutes trying to scan a tin of beans. Ended up having to call someone over. Speaking of beans, did young Emily ring about the horses again? She was asking if you’d seen old Mr. Henderson’s mare, Blossom. Said she hasn’t been looking right lately. She did, yes. Lovely girl, Emily. Always worried about those animals. Said Blossom seemed a bit off colour. Henderson’s a good man, looks after ‘em well enough, but he’s getting on, you know? Sometimes things slip his mind. It’s tough when you’re getting older, keeping on top of things. Especially with animals. My sister’s got a dog, and she’s constantly fretting about whether she’s giving it the right food, enough walks… It's like being a parent all over again, isn’t it? Except they don't talk back! Though sometimes I wish my charges  hadn’t  talked back so much. Remember little Thomas and his obsession with dinosaurs? “Roar!” all day long. Drove me round the bend. Ah, children. A handful, they are. Still, you wouldn't trade 'em, would you? No, you wouldn't. Though sometimes a quiet afternoon is a blessing. What about you, David? Still battling with the teenagers at school? More or less. Had a lad trying to argue with me today about the historical accuracy of a video game. Said it was “more truthful” than his textbook. Honestly! I tried explaining the importance of primary sources… didn’t get very far. Video games. Another thing I don’t understand. All that shooting and… well, I don't know  what  they do.

…and honestly, the teenagers were hopeless with the subjunctive. Hopeless! You’d think after three years of French, they’d grasp the concept of ‘if I were’ versus ‘if I was’ but no. It’s like their brains actively resist it. Sounds about right. Teenagers, eh? No respect for grammar, or anything else for that matter. Reminds me of dealing with some of the younger executives at the firm, always trying to cut corners. Proper cowboys, some of ‘em. It’s the instant gratification thing, I think. Everything’s got to be quick and easy now. No one wants to put the work in. What have you been up to this week, Arthur? Anything exciting happen? Not particularly. Bit of gardening, mostly. The roses are coming along nicely, though. Had a right battle with the aphids, mind you. Little blighters. And I finished that model railway section I was telling you about. The one with the viaduct. Oh, lovely! I remember you mentioning that. You must spend hours on that. Is it almost complete now? Nearly. Just needs a bit of weathering, and some miniature figures. Always something more to do, isn’t there? Speaking of things to do, are you planning anything nice for the weekend? I think we're just having a quiet one. My sister’s coming round with the kids on Saturday, so that'll be… lively, to say the least. They’re at that age where everything is a negotiation. Ah, yes. Little negotiators. My granddaughter’s the same. Brilliant child, but you have to be prepared to argue your case for everything, even the colour of her socks! Exactly! It’s exhausting. Though, it’s good to see them, isn’t it? Keeps you young. Have you been away anywhere this year, Arthur? I know you used to love your trips to France. Not this year, unfortunately. Been a bit… cautious, with everything that’s going on. The travel disruptions, you know. Too much hassle. I’d like to get back to the Dordogne eventually, though. Beautiful countryside. And the wine’s not bad either. Oh, I can imagine! I haven’t been abroad for ages. Perhaps next summer. I'd love to brush up my French if I actually had a chance to use it with native speakers again. It’s all ‘Bonjour’ and ‘Au revoir’ with the students, not much beyond that. Well, you could always come on one of my trips!

Honestly, that was the most uneventful Valentine’s Day ever. Like, seriously. Tell me about it! I was fully expecting, you know, a grand gesture, something romantic. Instead, I got a text saying “Happy V-Day ❤️” and a voucher for… Tesco. No way! Tesco?! That's…practical, I guess? Mine was even worse. My mum kept asking if anyone had sent me flowers. Like, Mum, I’m a student, I’m lucky if I get a text. Oh god, mums. Mine was on about marriage already. I was like, “Mum, I’m literally eating a toastie in the uni canteen, let’s not.” Exactly! It's just… a day. I mean, it's nice to be appreciated, but the pressure! Everyone’s posting these perfect couples pics on Insta. It's depressing. I totally deleted Instagram for the evening. It was just horrifying. All these people going to fancy restaurants. I just ordered a Deliveroo and watched a terrible movie. Oh, which movie? Spill the tea. It was one of those really bad rom-coms. You know the type? Predictable plot, awful acting, but you can’t look away. It was a disaster, but a comforting disaster. I feel that. I tried to be productive and watch a documentary about climate change. It just made me feel worse about everything. Oof, yeah, maybe stick to the comforting disasters. So, Friday then? Are we sticking with the cinema? Apparently, there’s that new horror film everyone’s talking about. Yeah, I’m in. I need a good scare to distract me from all the existential dread. But let’s get food  before  the cinema. I’m starving. That canteen pasta was… an experience. Oh, absolutely not another canteen pasta. It tasted like sadness. There’s that new Korean place near the library, have you tried it? Apparently, the bibimbap is amazing. Ooh, that sounds good! I’ve been craving something spicy. Although, my spice tolerance is pathetic. I once ordered a ‘medium’ curry and cried. Oh my god, same! I tried to be all adventurous and ordered a vindaloo and instantly regretted every life choice I’d ever made. Then I was moaning about my mouth for like, two hours. It’s a skill, honestly. Being able to handle spice. Also, have you noticed how different everyone's accents are here? Like, I met a girl from Scotland the other day

Honestly, the sheer audacity of him to say that. Like, genuinely. Did he not think anyone in the room would call him out? Right? It’s always the ones who’ve benefitted the  most  from the system who are the loudest about “meritocracy”. And then he has the nerve to act all surprised when people are like, “Um, systemic racism, hello?” It’s exhausting. It is. It really is. And the worst bit is, he wasn’t even saying anything particularly  original . It’s the same tired arguments, repackaged for a new audience. Did you see that article I sent you, about the housing crisis in Berlin? The one about the rent caps? Yeah, fascinating. Though, honestly, it feels like putting a plaster on a gaping wound, doesn’t it? Like, yeah, okay, stopping rent increases is good, but it doesn’t address the fundamental problem. Exactly! It doesn't tackle the speculation, the commodification of housing, the idea that a  basic human need  is just another investment opportunity. It's… it's bleak. This Dan Dan noodles are amazing though, right? Seriously, the sesame paste is perfection. They are incredible. Definitely needed comfort food after that work meeting. My editor basically told me I need to start pitching more “human interest” stories, less political analysis. Ugh, the pressure to dumb it down. What did you say? I tried to explain that people  are  interested in political analysis! That just because things are depressing doesn't mean they aren't important. But she just gave me that look… you know the one. The “we need to appeal to a wider audience” look. Oh,  that  look. The bane of every journalist’s existence. It's all about clicks, isn’t it? Doesn’t matter if it’s intellectually stimulating, just needs to be outrage-inducing or heartwarming. It’s all so cynical. Exactly! And then she wants me to write a piece about… wait for it… the best brunch spots in North London. Oh my god. Seriously? Seriously. It feels like I went to uni for three years to do  this . Though I guess rent in London isn't going to pay itself, is it? It’s just… demoralizing. This is why I'm obsessed with co-living spaces. At least then you're building community, not just lining the pockets of some landlord. It’s a good idea, in theory. But even those are getting absurdly expensive.

Honestly, the amount of forms they wanted filled in for nursery… it was ridiculous. Like, a full medical history, what his favourite colour is… honestly! Oh god, seriously? Sounds stressful. Is he settling okay though? He seems to be, yeah. Yesterday was a bit wobbly, a proper cling-on, but today he seemed much happier. Still, it’s just…weird, isn’t it? Leaving him. It must be. It's a big step. Are  you  okay with going back to work now? Not really, no. I mean, I need to. We need to. But I'm dreading the commute again. And the thought of missing…well, everything. Every little thing. It feels like he’s changing so fast. I know what you mean. It feels like yesterday you were telling me you were pregnant. Time flies. Doesn't it? Right, so, work. Two days a week to start with, which is…something. Then building up from there. I'm hoping I can still be vaguely useful after this long break. You'll be brilliant, Mum! You were always amazing at your job. Don’t worry about it. So, any plans for holidays this year? Maybe now things are…calming down a bit? We talked about Cornwall again. Your dad keeps going on about wanting to go back to St Ives. Oh, that'd be nice. He loves his art galleries, doesn't he? Obsessed! We were looking at cottages last night. Though, finding one that’s baby-friendly and dog-friendly… it’s a challenge. Yeah, that limits your options, doesn’t it? Speaking of challenges… how's the weaning going? Is he enjoying all the purees? It's a mess! Utter chaos. He mostly just flings it everywhere. Sweet potato is the worst. It stains  everything . But he's eating  some  of it, so that’s a win, I suppose. At least he's experimenting! It’s good he’s not refusing everything. I saw this thing online about baby-led weaning… Oh, I’ve heard of that. Letting them feed themselves chunks of food? No way! That feels like a disaster waiting to happen. Yeah, it's a bit…intense. Maybe when he's a bit older. What are you watching on TV at the moment? Anything good? Honestly, not much. I’m usually too exhausted to concentrate. We started watching  The Tourist  with Jamie Dornan… it’s quite gripping.

Honestly, the day has been… a day. I spent most of it giving a statement to the police. Oh, blimey. What on earth happened? Everything alright? It’s just… someone hit my car while it was parked. Small bump, really, but they didn’t leave a note. A witness got their registration, thankfully, so the police are dealing with it. Just tedious paperwork, mostly. That’s awful! So annoying. Happened to my Nan once, she was fuming. Sounds frustrating. At least you’ve got a registration number, that’s the main thing. Less hassle than trying to track them down yourself. Exactly. Although, trying to explain to the officer exactly  where  on the car it was… it’s not the most graceful thing trying to mime a dent on a wing mirror. I can imagine! Speaking of frustrating, I’ve just had my EE bill. It’s astronomical. They’ve somehow added another £30 on, claiming I went over my data allowance. I’ve barely used my phone this month! Oh, they do that all the time! It's a scam, honestly. You need to ring them up and argue. It’s a nightmare, but usually they back down. Yeah, happened to me too. Spent an hour on hold, then the guy tried to tell me I’d downloaded three films. Three! Sounds like they’re hoping you’ll just pay it rather than fight. You have to be firm with them, Dad. I will, I will. I’m just… bracing myself for the battle. It’s always so time-consuming. Right, what about you two? How were your days? Chloe, how’s the shop? Busy, busy, busy! We had a delivery of the new autumn stock, so it was a lot of unpacking and re-merchandising. Trying to make everything look all cosy and autumnal. Footfall was good though, so can't complain. And me? Work was… work. Endless meetings about budgets and projections. Honestly, sometimes I think I spend more time  talking  about doing things than actually doing them. Sounds familiar. I feel like half my job is writing reports about the work I’ve already done. So, any plans for the week? Anything fun lined up? Actually, I was thinking about going to that new Italian place in Lichfield on Wednesday. Anyone fancy joining? Wednesday's good for me. I’ve been wanting to try it. Ooh, yes, that sounds lovely!

…and then he just  launched  into a detailed explanation of Roman concrete. Like, full on, aggregate ratios, volcanic ash – the lot. It was a wedding reception, mate! Classic Uncle George. He's obsessed, isn't he? Always has been. Remember that trip to Italy? He spent three days just staring at the Colosseum, muttering about  opus caementicium . Oh god, yeah. And then tried to explain it to a group of Italian school kids. They just looked utterly bewildered. Speaking of bewildered, have you seen the new  Spartacus  reboot? Heard about it. Is it any good? The original was… well, it was a bit of a guilty pleasure. Lots of slow motion and oiled abs. It's… different. More historically accurate, apparently. Which means a lot less oiled abs, and a lot more political intrigue. And everyone dies really,  really  young. Like, seriously, these guys aren't even 30 before they're getting stabbed. Depressing, really. Sounds about right for ancient Rome, though, doesn’t it? Short life expectancy and constant backstabbing. So, how are you finding married life? Still feels weird coming back here and seeing everything so… you? It's good, it's good. Definitely an adjustment. She’s already re-organised the kitchen. Apparently, I wasn’t utilising the space ‘effectively’. Oh dear. The kitchen is sacred territory. You gotta tread carefully. Speaking of kitchens, I've been experimenting with making my own spice blends. Got a proper mortar and pestle now. Nice! Doing what, like Indian stuff? Yeah, a bit of everything, really. Trying to recreate some of the flavours I had when I was travelling. Got some proper Aleppo pepper, some good cumin, loads of coriander… I even managed to find some black cardamom. Black cardamom? Fancy. I just stick to paprika and chilli powder. You and your adventurous palate. What about those hazelnuts you were talking about last time? Did they come good? Yeah! I roasted them with a bit of rosemary and sea salt. Incredible. I've been putting them in everything – salads, pasta, even just munching on them straight from the bowl. And I'm thinking of trying to make my own hummus. Loads of chickpeas, tahini… Ooh, good shout. You have to get that sourdough bread from the market, though. It’s the perfect accompaniment. I got a souvenir on the train back from London last week. Terrible, gaudy little Chinatown dragon.

Ugh, honestly, English was  brutal  today. Mrs. Davies is on one, isn't she? Like, seriously intense about the poetry analysis. Tell me about it! I didn’t even understand half of what she wanted us to find in “Ozymandias.” It’s just a poem about a broken statue! Why does it have to be so…layered? Exactly! And then she spent like, twenty minutes going on about enjambment. Enjambment! Like we’re all going to be writing poems using that word in everyday conversation. It felt like she was showing off, honestly. Like, “Look how clever  I  am, knowing all these fancy terms.” Did you finish the practice questions? I only managed like, three. Three? I got four! But I had to look up half the definitions. I swear, she deliberately makes it hard. It's not like we’re all going to be literary critics. Well, you’re better at English than me anyway. I’m just praying for a C. What about art? Was that any better? Art was… okay. Mr. Henderson let us start painting our landscapes. I’m attempting a field of poppies. It already looks like a massive mess. I’ve got red everywhere. Oh no! That sounds like me last week with the watercolour. Remember when I accidentally turned my whole hand blue? Oh my god, yes! You looked like a Smurf! Mr. Henderson was trying so hard not to laugh. He always hides it so badly. Anyway, I’m dreading French on Monday. Madame Dubois is giving us a pop quiz on verb conjugations. Verb conjugations! Seriously?! That’s so unfair. French is already hard enough without having to worry about memorizing a million different endings. I can never tell the difference between  être  and  avoir . Me neither! It all just sounds the same. Have you seen Chloe lately? She's been really quiet. Yeah, I think she’s upset about something. I think it’s Liam? Apparently, he was talking to Sophie after school yesterday.  Liam  and Sophie? Oh no way! Chloe’s going to be devastated. He was telling everyone just last week how much he liked Chloe’s new hair. I know, right? Boys are so awful. Actually, speaking of awful, have you heard what happened in wind band rehearsal? No! What? Did Mr. Bell get angry again? Worse! Ben accidentally sat on the tuba!  The tuba?!  No! Was it damaged?

Honestly, lad, you've grown another foot since last time I saw you! Look at you, nearly towering over your grandad. Aye, well, I'm getting there. It's alright though, I can still reach the biscuit tin. That’s all that matters, isn't it? Speaking of biscuits, this café does a cracking shortbread. Have you tried it yet, love? Not yet, but it smells lovely. I had a scone earlier, though. Delicious. Though, honestly, the jam to cream ratio was  all  wrong. It's a cardinal sin, I tell you. Sounds serious. I’m just having a panini, plain cheese. Can’t go wrong. Safe bet. You’ve got to be careful with fancy fillings. Remember that time we went to Italy, and you ordered that one with the artichokes and… whatever else it was? Don’t remind me. It tasted like someone had washed a sock in olive oil and then shoved it in a bread roll. Oh, you were green for days! Poor thing. It’s always the adventurous ones who suffer, isn’t it? Though, it’s good to try new things. I was reading an article about how people in Japan are eating edible flags now. Edible flags?! What on earth for? Is this some sort of national pride thing? Apparently! They’re making them out of rice paper and food colouring. A bit tasteless, if you ask me. Literally. Sounds a bit daft, to be honest. I’d rather have a proper flag, and a decent football match to wave it at. Have you seen Newcastle doing this season? They're on fire! Oh, aye, I have! Your dad's been glued to the telly every weekend. He's practically forgetting I exist. Although, I wouldn’t put it past him to try and claim their success as his own – always was a bit of a glory hunter, your dad. He’s alright, just enthusiastic. He's been moaning about the price of tickets though. It’s getting ridiculous. Everything’s getting ridiculous. I was at the hospital last week with my arthritis acting up, and the parking charges are extortionate. Honestly, it feels like they’re punishing you for being ill. It's scandalous. They need to sort that out. They talk about wellness and preventative care, but then they make it financially impossible to even get to the appointments. Yeah. Miss is talking about preventative care in PSHCE lessons.

Honestly though, seeing the state of some people these days…it’s not natural. All this obesity. It’s just…laziness, isn’t it? And too much food. Now hold on a minute, Maureen. That’s a bit harsh. There’s more to it than that. Genes play a big part, you know. My nan, she always carried a bit of weight, and she never sat still all day, scrubbing floors and whatnot. Dad’s right, Mum. It's massively complex. There’s a genetic predisposition, absolutely, but it’s also the modern diet, the lack of exercise…and honestly, the marketing. It’s designed to make us crave unhealthy things. And don't forget the socioeconomic factors. Healthy food is  expensive . It's significantly cheaper to fill up on processed stuff. Oh, don’t start on that. Everyone can make choices. I grew up during the war! We didn’t have fancy ‘socioeconomic factors’ then, we ate what we were given and we were grateful. Different times, love. Different times. Though I will say, they didn't have all these takeaways popping up on every corner then, did they? Remember when a chip shop was a treat? Now it’s every night for some. It’s also about portion sizes. Everything’s bigger now. Even a ‘small’ coffee is massive. And it’s all normalized. It’s… unsettling, really. I was reading a study about the rise in childhood obesity and… Right, let’s steer clear of depressing studies during dinner, shall we? How’s your recovery going, by the way, Dad? Still feeling okay after the op? Yeah, not bad, not bad. Still a bit tender, but getting there. The surgeon said it was a success, thankfully. Though the hospital food…that’s a whole other conversation about societal failings. Honestly, a rubbery chicken and some mashed potato doesn't exactly promote healing. You need building up, that's what you need. Proper meals. Not that hospital slop. I'll make you a nice stew when we visit next week. That'd be lovely, Maureen. You always make a good stew. Though I'm trying to watch my cholesterol, the doctor's been on at me. Speaking of doctors, has anyone seen that article about the new allergy tests? Apparently, they're much more accurate now. Little Leo’s been having such terrible eczema lately, I’m wondering if we should get him tested for something he's eating.

Right so I’ve finally figured out why half my students couldn’t submit the essay last week. Oh really? Don’t tell me it was another Moodle glitch. That platform is actively designed to frustrate me, I’m convinced. It was, yes. But not a glitch, exactly. Apparently, the submission box wasn’t visible on mobile.  Seriously ? You’d think after all this time, they’d have made it responsive. So students trying to submit on their phones just… couldn’t? Exactly! And a surprising number of them tried. I’ve had a flood of apologetic emails this morning. I’ve extended the deadline, naturally. Of course. It’s always the tech. It’s never the students not doing the work. Though, admittedly, sometimes it is. True. But this was definitely Moodle being obtuse. I had one student who screenshotted their phone showing the blank space where the submission box  should  have been. It was pretty damning. Oh, that's good evidence. Did you report it to learning technologies? They're usually pretty slow to respond, but… Already done. Got an automated acknowledgement. We’ll see. It’s just… frustrating, isn't it? We spend so much time crafting the perfect learning experience, and then Moodle throws a spanner in the works. It really is. And the interface is still hideous. It looks like something from 2005. They need a complete overhaul. Absolutely. I was showing my first years how to navigate it yesterday, and they were all completely lost. Honestly, I felt like I was explaining hieroglyphics. It’s getting worse, too. Every time they ‘update’ it, they just move things around and make it less intuitive. I’m starting to think they actively  want  us to suffer. It feels that way sometimes. I’m seriously considering just emailing out instructions with screenshots next semester. It’ll be a pain, but potentially less painful than dealing with Moodle-related help tickets. That’s probably a good shout. Screenshot everything. Document everything. Just in case. You need a paper trail when you’re fighting Moodle. Precisely. It's a digital battleground, honestly. A digital battleground fought with confusing icons and invisible submission boxes. You’re not wrong. Maybe we should petition for a new platform. Something… simpler. Something humane. Oh, I'm with you. But knowing the university, they’ll probably just stick with Moodle because "it’s what everyone’s used to."

Honestly, I’m still wrecked from that flight. It’s not even the length of it, it’s just…the  time difference . I feel like a zombie. Tell me about it. You look it, actually. Though you're functioning, which is more than I would be. How was the conference itself, beyond the jetlag? Anything juicy in the medieval literature world? It was good, actually. Lot of interesting papers on female mystics. Very niche, but fascinating. Though mostly I just spent the breaks trying to stay awake and resisting the urge to nap in the keynote speech. Did you manage to get through all your marking? Most of it. Left a pile for myself to tackle this evening. The joys. Listen, about Saturday…are you still up for the play? “A Midsummer Night’s Dream” at the village hall. Old Mrs. Higgins is doing Titania, apparently. Oh, bless her! Yes, absolutely. It’ll be wonderfully awful, in the best way. What time does it start? Seven thirty. I was thinking we could grab something to eat beforehand, maybe at The Swan? It’s a bit of a walk, but… That sounds lovely. The Swan’s perfect. And we can discuss the eternal question of whether Oberon’s motivations are purely selfish, or if there’s a tragic element to his meddling. Of course. Can’t go to a Shakespeare without debating that. Right, practicalities. Baby’s bedtime…do we put Leo down early, or try and brave a post-theatre milk feed? Hmm…early might be best, poor little thing. He’s been so clingy since he’s been teething. He’ll probably sleep through most of it anyway. He’s getting so good at tuning us out. He has your selective deafness gene, I suspect. Still, an early bedtime means we can actually enjoy a full pint. Speaking of enjoying things… did you see Sarah’s post? About the new kitten. Oh, the fluffy ginger one? Adorable. Though she already has three cats. Is her flat turning into a feline sanctuary? Pretty much. She’s convinced it’s the key to happiness. I'm starting to suspect she's building an army of adorable overlords. Well, you can’t argue with that logic, can you? Right, I’m going to attempt to make some tea. Maybe caffeine will finally kick in. And then I face the mountain of emails. Good luck with that.

So, how’s Omar getting on with the visa application? Still a nightmare, is it? Absolutely. It’s… exhausting. He’s got all the documentation, obviously, proof of funds, letter from the university, everything. But they keep asking for more, little things. Like, they needed a certified translation of his birth certificate  again , even though he sent one last time. It feels deliberately obstructive, doesn’t it? Like they just don’t  want  to let people in. It often does, doesn’t it? Bureaucracy at its finest. Seems designed to wear you down. Is it the American visa, still? Yeah, to visit his sister in California. She's been there fifteen years now, settled with a family, and he hasn’t seen her since his mum’s funeral. It’s heartbreaking. He's trying to get over for Christmas, but… I doubt it now. That’s rough. You’d think family ties would count for something. It’s a long way to go, and expensive. You know, it makes you think about the politics of it all, doesn't it? So much of it circles back to oil. Absolutely. Everything does. You look at Libya, for example. Before Gaddafi, it was comparatively stable, reasonably prosperous. Then the oil money… and the Wahabi influence started creeping in. Honestly, it's a disaster. My cousin’s still there, trying to make a life, but it’s… scary. He sends messages, but you can always tell he’s censoring himself. It's terrifying. I was reading an article about the smuggling routes across the Mediterranean earlier, and the sheer desperation. My friend Anya’s involved with a refugee support group, she says the stories are just… unimaginable. It's awful. And it’s getting worse. My sister used to work for an NGO in northern Iraq, right on the border with Syria. She said even  before  all this latest stuff blew up, the young people were leaving in droves. No future, they said. No opportunities. Just… stuck. It’s the same here, in some ways. Not the same level of conflict, obviously, but finding affordable housing is impossible, decent jobs are scarce, and the whole political landscape feels… broken. We're thinking of moving further out, y’know? Away from the city. Where? You were saying something about Chester, weren’t you? Maybe. It's just an idea. Somewhere with a bit of green space, a bit of peace.

Honestly, that lamb was absolutely beautiful. You’ve really outdone yourself, Mum. Oh, it was nothing, dear. Just a simple roast. Though I did marinate it overnight, that makes all the difference you know. Old family recipe. It  did  make a difference. Perfectly pink. Though, having a TV on in the dining room still feels…odd. Odd? It’s brilliant! Means we can watch something while we digest. Though I did almost choke on a potato laughing at that program about competitive dog grooming. Competitive dog grooming? Good heavens. What will they think of next? Still, better than staring at the wallpaper, I suppose. Though I do miss proper conversation. We  are  having a conversation. About competitive dog grooming. It was incredibly elaborate. Little outfits, dyed fur… it was a spectacle. Reminded me of that Scottish tablet you brought back last time, Mum. Absolutely decadent. Ah, yes. Good quality tablet. Not like some of the stuff you get these days, all claggy and flavourless. I got it from a little shop in Pitlochry. They still make it properly there. Pitlochry… haven’t been there in years. Remember that disastrous cruise we took a few years back? We vowed never to set foot on a boat again. Don’t remind me! Seasickness, endless buffets and a magician who kept making the same rabbit disappear and reappear. It was a nightmare. Well, I thought it was quite relaxing. Apart from the roulette, of course. Lost a small fortune, I did. Relaxing for someone who doesn’t succumb to motion sickness. I spent the entire time feeling green around the gills. And then there was the issue with the landlord… Oh, don't even get me  started  on landlords. Ours is threatening to increase the rent again. Says it's 'market value'. As if market value applies to a damp, crumbling flat with a garden overrun with weeds. They all do that, don’t they? It's daylight robbery. You'd think after all these years, there would be some regulations in place. Honestly, renting is a terrible system. You're constantly at the mercy of someone else. I always believed in owning your own home, security for the future and all that. Easier said than done these days, Mum. Especially with house prices the way they are. I’m trying to do more workouts, at least. Trying to stay healthy is one thing I  can  control.

Right, so I genuinely think I could live off pasta forever. It’s the perfect food. Cheap, filling, you can chuck anything in it. You say that now, but give it a week. You’ll be craving a vegetable or something. Remember last time you did the ‘only beans on toast’ thing? That was a… a difficult time. I’m learning from my mistakes, I am. This is sustainable pasta-based living. You need to branch out, Liam. Seriously. My nan keeps trying to send me Tupperware containers full of stew. It's lovely, but… a LOT of stew. Bless her. She’s just looking after you, Sophie. It’s what nans  do . I know, I know. It’s just… I’m barely fitting my clothes in my wardrobe as it is, let alone massive containers of beef and potatoes. Speaking of living arrangements, are you lot still good to move into the new place at the end of the month? My landlord is already giving me  looks . He wants me out. Yeah, definitely. We’ve got the deposit sorted, and Finn’s dad is helping us with the van. Should be manageable. Are you sorted with somewhere else? Not exactly. I'm still crashing at me mam’s. It’s… cosy. Let's put it that way. She keeps asking about job applications too. It’s relentless. You need to get something lined up, mate. Even just a part-time job would be good to get you back into a routine. What about something in retail over Christmas? I’ve applied for a few things. Nothing’s come back yet. It’s frustrating, you know? I’ve got a degree, I shouldn’t be struggling this much. It's rubbish, the job market. I heard from Chloe - she's absolutely stressed about uni applications. She's got good grades, but she's worried she won't get into any of the places she wants. Oh yeah, it's brutal. Competition is insane. I’m still trying to decide whether to apply for a year abroad next year. It would be amazing, but I’d fall so behind with coursework. Do it! Year abroad is the best thing you can do. I’m so jealous I didn’t. Plus, think of all the stories you’d have. Imagine the pasta you could eat in Italy! Different pasta shapes, different sauces... the possibilities are endless.

Right, so I need to get the cupcakes iced before school tomorrow. Do you two want to help? Maybe sprinkle some hundreds and thousands on? Ooooh! Can I do pink ones? And purple? I want blue! And green! Like a swamp monster! A swamp monster cupcake, excellent! Okay, pink and purple for you, blue and green for you. But gently, okay? We don’t want icing  everywhere . It's for Year 3, remember? They’re learning about instruction writing, and we’re going to write instructions on how to make cupcakes. Are you going to  eat  them after? Of course! That’s the best part of instructions, isn’t it? Following them… and then enjoying the result. Though I might sneak one  before  they write their instructions, just to make sure they’re properly delicious. What are Year 3 doing now? Are they still doing that story about the giant? They finished the giant last week! We're onto poetry now. It's a bit chaotic, honestly. They all want to write about dragons and superheroes. It’s hard to steer them towards… daffodils. Daffodils are boring. They are a bit, aren’t they? But they’re spring! Sometimes you have to write about spring. Oh, I nearly forgot! It’s Leo’s half-birthday on Saturday! We need to get him a little something. Can we get him a Tomodachi Life thing? He really wants a new apartment for his Miis. A Tomodachi Life thing… okay, that’s a good idea. I was thinking maybe a new book. I saw a really lovely one in Morrisons yesterday - a pop-up dinosaur book. Dinosaurs are better than daffodils! Absolutely dinosaurs are better than daffodils. Although, I also saw a really nice one about… gardening. Ugh. I know, I know. But it had HUGE pictures of vegetables. Like, enormous carrots. Maybe we can get both? The dinosaur and the…slightly less exciting vegetable book? Can we read the dinosaur one tonight? Definitely! We’ll read the dinosaur one tonight. And then tomorrow, we’ll conquer these cupcakes. Now, who is ready for sprinkles? Remember, gentle sprinkles. No swamp monster incidents. I'm already thinking of a swamp monster one. It needs extra green. Oh dear. This is going to be a sticky afternoon, isn’t it? Mum, can you get the purple icing first? Please? It’s my favourite colour. Purple it is.

Honestly, the state of Facebook these days. It's just… relentless. Everyone’s performing their perfect life. You’d think no one ever had a bad hair day or burnt the dinner. Tell me about it. My Aunt Carol posted a photo of her garden this morning. Looked like something out of Kew Gardens. She spends all day out there, apparently. It’s exhausting just  looking  at it. Exactly! And then the political arguments. It used to be a way to keep in touch with people, now it’s just a shouting match. I nearly unfriended my cousin last week. He was going on about… well, it doesn't matter. It was ridiculous. I mostly just ignore it now. Scroll past the drama. Though, I did fall down a rabbit hole of classic car restoration videos yesterday. That was a good use of twenty minutes. Oh, cars! You were tinkering with yours again yesterday, weren’t you? I heard you out there, under the bonnet. Yeah, just trying to sort out a little… rattle. Nothing major. It's a '67 Mustang, you know. They need constant attention. It’s part of the charm. Though sometimes I wonder if I’m spending more time fixing it than driving it. It’s a beautiful car, though. Properly stunning. I always admire it when you drive past. You've really kept it in good condition. Thanks. It’s a labour of love, really. It’s just… finding the parts can be a nightmare. Everything's online these days. Which is convenient, but then you get stuck with dodgy sellers and inflated prices. Oh, the internet. Another mixed blessing. The ability to access information is amazing, obviously. But the whole online marketplace thing? It’s a minefield. Remember when we used to go to actual car boot sales? Do I ever! That’s where I found that vintage tool kit for the Mustang, actually. Bargain. You couldn't get that online. It’s all curated vintage now, overpriced and pretending to be ‘shabby chic’. Exactly! Everything's got a filter on it. Real life is messy and imperfect. It’s much more interesting, isn’t it? Definitely. Speaking of interesting… did you see Professor Davies’ post about the new digital humanities project? Sounds ambitious. Oh, yes! He emailed us about it. Seems like a lot of work, but potentially very rewarding. Though, honestly, after spending the day grading essays, the last thing I want to do is spend more time staring at a screen.

Right, pass us the remote will you? I can’t quite reach. Honestly, this sofa’s a bit far from the TV, isn’t it? Here. But you always say that. It’s not  that  far. You just… can’t be bothered to move. Harsh! Just offering constructive criticism, love. Right, pause it there. Did you see the bit with the giant spaghetti tornado? Mental. Yeah, it was good. But it's just a kids' film, innit? Don’t overthink it. I’m not overthinking it! I'm just saying, the whole thing is a metaphor for unchecked consumerism, isn't it? Like, everyone wanted more and more food, until it totally overwhelmed them. And the mayor just wants everything to be perfect and clean, suppressing all the… chaos. Woah. You've been reading too much into things. It’s just a funny film about food falling from the sky. I was enjoying the meatballs. You  always  say that. I'm allowed to have thoughts, you know. Speaking of food, I had a right nightmare at work today. Mrs. Higgins complained her sandwich was cut diagonally instead of straight. Diagonally! Honestly, some people. Oh, bless her. She's a bit…particular. You should've just remade it. It’s not exactly rocket science. It's the principle of the thing! I spent ten minutes explaining the difference between a diagonal and a straight cut to a woman who probably thinks the Earth is flat. Plus, I'm on minimum wage, I’m not a sandwich artist. Alright, alright, calm down. It's just a sandwich. Did you eat lunch then? You seemed pretty hangry earlier. Yeah, I had a packet of crisps. It doesn’t exactly fill you up, does it? You had a proper lunch at uni, didn't you? Something fancy? Nah. Just a pasta salad. Though, Liam tried to convince me that feminism is outdated because women have “already achieved equality”. Honestly.  Seriously ? Liam? He's still banging on about that? Bless him. He’s got a lot to learn. Tell me about it! I tried to explain intersectionality but he just kept saying “but men have problems too!”. It was exhausting. Ugh, men. Honestly. Anyway, back to the meteor shower of food… I wonder how much that cost them to animate? It must have taken ages. All that jelly and stuff. It looks like something a really dedicated artist would make.

Right so, you were saying about the match on Saturday? Didn’t sound like a classic, from what you told me. Classic? Nah, honestly, it were a right slog. Two nil, aye, but nothin' like a proper game. Just… scrappy. Like watchin' paint dry, almost. Mind, the atmosphere was decent enough. Full house, always is these days. Though half of 'em are probably tourists, payin' a fortune just to say they were there. Aye, that’s the Premier League for you now, isn’t it? More of a global show than a local… well, anything. Makes you wonder about the supporters who’ve been goin’ for generations. Gets priced out, doesn’t it? Gets priced out alright. And then you get these lads turnin' up wearin' Man U shirts, in Liverpool. Talk about lack of respect. I had a fare the other week, right, bleedin' Chelsea supporter. Startin' on about how good their manager is, while I’m drivin’ him through Anfield. I didn’t say nothin', but I was thinkin’ it. You held your tongue, then. Good lad. Though sometimes it’s temptin’, isn’t it? It’s the tribalism, I suppose. Still, football’s practically a religion in this city. Reminds me of the old days, back when New Labour were in power. Blair, ironically enough, was a bit of a football fan, wasn’t he? Blair… yeah, he was always tryin' to be seen at the matches. Bit of a poseur, if you ask me. Though, to be fair, it weren’t all bad under New Labour. Things were movin', were they not? Least, that’s what they told us. Now look at ‘em, all squabblin’ and fightin'. This current lot… honestly, I wouldn’t trust ‘em to run a bath, let alone a country. It's a mess, innit? I mean, the whole idea of “stakeholder capitalism” Blair was pushin'… it sounded good on paper, but it just seemed to benefit the already wealthy. And now, we’ve got this… this obsession with austerity. Talkin' about cutting public services while the fat cats are gettin' richer. It's disgusting. Disgusting is the word. They’re all in it together, the lot of ‘em. And don’t even get me started on the expenses. Remember that MP who claimed for a duck house? A duck house! What kind of a country are we livin' in? I’m workin' twelve hours a day, barely makin’ ends meet, and they’re claimin' for bleedin' duck houses!

Honestly, I’ve spent the entire morning wading through BNC recordings. It’s… a lot. Like, so many people saying ‘like’ every other word. It’s draining my soul. Oh god, the BNC. I remember those days. Proper linguistic archaeology, innit? Though, on the topic of people saying things, LinkedIn is a whole other level of…performance. Everyone's a thought leader now. Seriously! It’s just people patting themselves on the back. I scroll through and think, ‘Yeah, you went to a workshop, good for you.’ It’s exhausting. I need a social media detox. You and me both. I’ve been trying to limit myself, but it’s addictive. Speaking of needing escapes… how was your weekend? Did you manage to get out and about in London? It was nice! We went to Broadway Market. It was rammed, obviously, but we got some amazing pastries. And then just wandered around. It still feels so weird having proper weekends again, after so long working remotely. Tell me about it. I feel like I’ve forgotten how to ‘do’ weekends. Want to hear a ridiculous story? My aunt Carol is trying to convince me to move to Wales. She’s already found me a little cottage. Wales? Proper move-to-the-country vibes? Full on. Apparently, the ‘pace of life’ is much better. And she keeps talking about the stunning scenery. It’s lovely, but…it's Wales. I’d be miles from everything. It's a big shift! You’re a city girl. Although... have you ever thought about just… moving  abroad ? Like, properly? Oh, all the time. Spain, mostly. I've got a few friends living in Barcelona. The weather! The food! But then I get paralysed thinking about visas and learning another language. And honestly, the thought of flying terrifies me. Oh, I’m the same with flying. Properly terrified. I once had a panic attack on the runway and had to practically be dragged off the plane. Oh my god! That sounds awful! I just… overthink everything that could go wrong. It’s so irrational. I saw some photos of the Maldives online and was thinking ‘oooh’, but then immediately thought ‘no way’ – too much flying. The Maldives would be amazing! But yeah, the flying. Maybe a really long boat trip? Although that feels even more terrifying. Haha! True. It's a lose-lose situation. Have you seen Sarah’s pictures from her trip to Italy?

Right, so I was thinking, maybe a little more chilli in this? It feels a bit… tame. A little more, yeah. But not  too  much, remember what happened last time? You nearly set off the smoke alarm. Honestly, you’d think you were cooking for a dragon. Dramatic license, Mum. It needed a kick! Speaking of kicks, still thinking about getting that sleeve done? Oh, the watercolour one? Maybe. Still umming and aahing. It’s a commitment, isn’t it? Plus, I’m a literary editor, I should probably project a more… subdued image. Subdued? You? You dress entirely in shades of purple! A bit of ink isn’t going to ruin your gravitas. Touché. It’s just… what if it clashes with my book launches? Imagine me unveiling a groundbreaking novel with a half-finished phoenix on my arm.  Doorbell rings  That’ll be Sarah. Saved by the bell, eh? Saves you having to commit to dragon-level spice or permanent art.    Hello, you two! Something smells amazing. Is that Thai green curry? It will be. Mum was worried I was going to set the kitchen on fire. A slight exaggeration. Hello, darling. Come in, come in. Did you have a nightmare on the Central Line? It was absolute chaos earlier. You have  no  idea. Packed like sardines. Anyway, forget the tube, tell me about Christmas! Have you started planning yet? It’s practically November. Oh, don’t even mention it. I’m supposed to be hosting this year, which means battling supermarkets and attempting to create a festive masterpiece. Honestly, I’d rather edit a manuscript written entirely in emoji. Sounds stressful. You could just order everything from Deliveroo. Problem solved. You and your solutions. Though, honestly, that’s not a bad idea. How’s work, by the way? Still drowning in submissions? Drowning is a strong word. Submerged, perhaps. We’ve got a new intern, though. Bright as a button, but utterly clueless about the classics. I asked her if she'd read any Woolf, and she thought I meant wolf as in, the animal. No way! Oh, that’s brilliant! You’re going to have your work cut out for you. So, you’re still with the renovations, then? How’s the kitchen looking? It’s… ongoing. The builders promised it would be finished by October. October has come and gone. Now they’re talking about ‘unforeseen complications’ with the plumbing.

Right, so I was thinking, because you’re a proper food writer now, or editor, whatever… could you actually give me some decent recipes? I’m getting so bored of the same four things. Bolognese, chilli, pasta with pesto… and, honestly, sometimes just toast. Toast is underrated. But yes, I can definitely help. What kind of things are you  looking  for? Quick weeknight stuff? Something more ambitious for the weekend? And what do you actually  like ? Because I can send you a Jamie Oliver recipe for Moroccan tagine, but if you hate cumin… No cumin, definitely. I’m alright with spice, just not that particular spice. Quick weeknight is good. Something I can bung in a pan and forget about for half an hour while I mark essays. Honestly, marking Year 9 French is draining the life out of me. Oh god, Year 9. They’re at that delightful stage where they think they know everything, but actually know nothing. Right, okay. How about a one-pan lemon and herb chicken and veg? It's basically chuck everything in a roasting tin, drizzle with oil and lemon juice, throw some herbs on top, and bake. Minimal effort, maximum flavour. That sounds… genuinely achievable. I need achievable. I attempted a soufflé last month. It was a disaster. Looked like a deflated balloon animal. Oh no! Soufflés are evil. They’re designed to mock you. I’ve given up on them. Speaking of things that mock you, have you been to that new Pilates class at the community centre? I saw a poster! Is it any good? I’m trying to get back into some sort of exercise, but the gym just feels so… depressing. Lots of very fit people judging my lack of fitness. It's actually really good! It’s surprisingly intense, but everyone's at different levels, so no one's judging. And the instructor, Sarah, is lovely and really encouraging. I went on Tuesday, and I’m still feeling it. In a good way, mostly. Okay, you’ve sold me. I'll look into it. Maybe we could go together? Though, I warn you, my core strength is approximately zero. Definitely! We can suffer together. It’ll be brilliant. Right, this smells amazing now. I’ve added a bit of chilli flake to this… hoping it's not too much. Chilli flake is  always  a good idea. Unless it’s in a soufflé, possibly.

Honestly, the things they come up with in those essays. It’s like they haven’t even  read  the material. Tell me about it. I had one student today who argued that Confucius was a key figure in the French Revolution. No way! Seriously? I wish I was joking. I had to gently… redirect him. It’s exhausting, isn’t it? Trying to unpick those fundamental misunderstandings. It is. It really is. Sometimes I wonder if they’re just trying to see how much they can get away with. Like a game. Maybe. Or maybe they’re just overwhelmed. This is a huge culture shock for some of them, after all. True, that’s fair. Though I still maintain some of it is just… lazy. Oh! Speaking of overwhelming, have you seen Sarah’s photos from her holiday? Which Sarah? Sarah Miller, from the history department. She’s in Bali. Posing in front of every single rice paddy. And wearing a different floral dress for each one. Classic Sarah. She does love a good photo op. She’s always been a bit of a… performer. A performer is one word for it. It’s all very curated. And the filters! Honestly, she looks about twenty years younger. She always was very conscious of her image. Remember that phase she went through with the fake tan and everything? Oh god, yes! It was a disaster. She looked… orange. And she used to complain that her toenails were always getting broken. Oh, I’d forgotten about the toenails! She’d spend ages moaning to anyone who would listen. Apparently, it was a tragic saga. Apparently! It was a daily update. You know, it’s funny. We’ve known her for years, and she’s still… Sarah. Some people just don’t change. Have you heard anything from Ben lately? I haven’t seen him since the conference. He texted me a few days ago. He’s still completely buried in marking. Apparently, he’s got a particularly difficult group this year. He said they haven’t even attempted to define key concepts. Honestly, it sounds almost as bad as your Confucius and the French Revolution student. It's a universal struggle, isn't it? The woes of academia. Does this fit what you were looking for? Would you like me to continue the conversation, or perhaps focus on a specific aspect of it?

…and honestly, the whole thing was just  exhausting . Like, pretending to be enthusiastic about sourdough starters for three hours straight. You know Brenda? Brenda from the book club? She went on and on. Brenda. Right. The sourdough queen. God love her. Sounds… intense. How’s the teaching going, by the way? Still battling teenagers with questionable grammar? Oh, you know. A constant struggle. Year 10 are currently obsessed with slang I’ve never even  heard  of. Apparently, something is “rizzless” now? I had to Google it. It’s… depressing. It felt like learning a whole new language just to understand their gossip. Rizzless! Oh, that’s brilliant. See, you  are  still learning! Keeps you young. Speaking of learning, I had a meeting today with a guy trying to convince me to invest in some… crypto thing. Said it was the future. Oh, not again. You always get those. What was this one? Some sort of Dogecoin knock-off? Worse, apparently. Something involving NFTs and… simulated sheep farming. I kid you not. Simulated sheep farming. He had a whole PowerPoint presentation. Oh, that’s spectacular. The lengths people will go to. It’s always the ones with the PowerPoint presentations, isn't it? Extra points for a stock photo of a very happy sheep. Absolutely. And he kept referencing some conspiracy theory about the government controlling the wool market. Honestly, I just wanted my coffee. It reminded me of that documentary we watched about that bloke who thought pigeons were government drones. Oh, the pigeon man! He was convinced they were watching him. Slightly terrifying, actually. Makes you think, doesn’t it? You realize how easily people can get lost down those rabbit holes. It does. Though, I suspect most of them just enjoy having a good story to tell. It’s cheaper than therapy. Speaking of things that are expensive, have you seen what’s happened with ticket prices for the Taylor Swift concert? Don't even  start  me. I tried. I genuinely tried. My niece is obsessed. I spent two hours refreshing the page and ended up with nothing. Scalpers are charging a fortune. It’s outrageous. It is. Same with Beyoncé. It’s like you need a second mortgage to go to a concert these days. Remember when tickets were, like, thirty quid? Vaguely. Those were the days. Though, I suppose everything is more expensive now. Even coffee. So, how’s Sarah enjoying married life?

Dad, are we nearly there yet? Seriously, my legs are killing me. Nearly, love, nearly. Still a good few hours to go yet, though. Cornwall's a long way from Manchester, you know. Just look at the scenery, though. Beautiful, isn’t it? All these fields, and those wind turbines spinning away. They’re kind of… hypnotic. Like giant, slow-motion windmills. Do you think people used to think windmills were magic? Oh, I bet they did. Everything looked magical before we understood it, didn't it? Speaking of magical, remember that time we went to Jamaica Inn? That place felt proper spooky. All dark wood and stories of smugglers. Yeah! And the sheep were all black there, weren't they? That was weird. It felt like a film set. Like something out of a Sherlock Holmes story. Right you are. Proper atmospheric. You know, your great-grandad used to be a telegraph operator. He could send messages in Morse code, you know. Morse code? What's that? Is that like, tapping? Aye, tapping. Dots and dashes. Back in the day, before texts and phones, that’s how people sent urgent messages. Think about it, a whole language based on clicks and pauses! They even had telegraphs, wires stretched across the country. Your nan used to tell me about waiting for telegrams from her brother when he was in the army. It was a big deal. Wow. That’s so… slow. It would take ages to tell someone you were going to be late for dinner. It did! And before that, it was letters. And before  that … well, stories passed down through generations, like fairy tales. Do you think fairy tales started as a way of explaining things before science? Maybe. Like, why the sky is blue, or where babies come from. Although, some are just really weird. Like, why does the Wicked Witch of the West melt when Dorothy throws water on her? That makes no sense. Good question! Sometimes they don't need to make sense, do they? It’s the  feeling  of the story that matters. Look at the colours of the road! All the different shades of green and brown... reminds me of something Lewis Carroll would write about. Lewis Carroll? The Alice in Wonderland guy? That's the one. He was brilliant at describing details. Speaking of colours, fancy a chocolate biscuit? I’ve got a whole packet in the glove compartment.

Honestly though, the price of a cinema ticket now is just…criminal. Ten quid for a student? It’s daylight robbery. Ten quid? In my day, it was sixpence. Sixpence! And that included a bag of sweets. Real sweets, not these sugary things they have now. Proper, hard boiled ones. Sixpence, wow. You’re going way back, aren’t you Grandad? Though, I do agree, it’s getting ridiculous. I saw  Dune: Part Two  last week. Good film, but…expensive.  Dune?  Oh, I’ve been meaning to see that. Is it worth the tenner? Yeah, definitely. Visually stunning. But prepare for a long sit. Nearly three hours. Three hours! I remember when a film lasted an hour and a half, and you were grateful for it. We used to go to the Regal, down in Altrincham. Lovely place. Used to smell of popcorn and disinfectant. Sounds nice. I went to the Odeon in Sunderland, always felt a bit sticky underfoot, if I’m honest. Right? Cinema floors are a hazard. Speaking of hazards, did you see the price of petrol this morning? Nearly £1.50 a litre. It’s outrageous. Don’t even  start  me on petrol. It's ruining me. I'm barely using the car now, cycling everywhere, even with all the hills around here. Hills? You wouldn't get hills like the Pennines around here. Used to cycle to school, I did. Timperley to Altrincham. Uphill both ways, naturally. Naturally, Grandad. It’s always uphill both ways. Ha! Classic. Though this  is  hilly. I’m trying to get back into running, actually. But my stamina is…shot. How’s your swimming going, Mark? Slowly. I signed up for a charity event, trying to build up to a decent distance. Nothing like a Channel swim, obviously. Channel swim! When I was in the war, we used to see the boats going across. Dangerous work. Very dangerous. I was in signals, you know. Very important. Couldn't tell you what I did, naturally. Top secret. Top secret, eh? Sounds exciting. I used to be really good at geography in primary school. Knew all the capitals. Still remember most of them. Impressive. I was rubbish at geography. Always confusing Spain with Portugal. Portugal, Spain… don’t matter to me. I preferred building things. Used to be a right dab hand with a soldering iron, back in my BT days. Proper engineering, that was.

Right, so I’ve made a start on the list for moving stuff out of your spare room. It’s… extensive. Mostly old Christmas decorations and things you haven’t touched since, well, since I was a kid. Oh dear. Well, I did say I’d accumulated a bit. Don’t throw anything away without asking, though. There’s a perfectly good fondue set in there somewhere, I’m sure of it. We haven’t used it in years, but it's a perfectly good fondue set. A fondue set? Seriously? Mum, you haven’t had a fondue party since the 80s. That doesn’t mean it’s not a perfectly good fondue set! It was a lovely shade of avocado, you know. Very stylish. Anyway, have you managed to sleep properly since getting back from Japan? You looked utterly wiped yesterday. Honestly, no.
