Jet lag is brutal. I keep waking up at like, 3 am just convinced I need to be teaching a class. My brain is completely scrambled. I tried that melatonin stuff, but it just made me feel…fuzzy. Oh, that's not good. Your Auntie Carol swore by chamomile tea. Said it always settled her when she used to go on those cruise holidays. Though, to be fair, she’d also have a little brandy in it. Of course she would. Right, chamomile tea noted. Did you see Sarah and Mark last week? How’s the wedding planning going? Oh, it’s all consuming, darling. She’s got a spreadsheet for  everything . From the colour of the napkins to the precise angle of the fairy lights. Mark’s just trying to stay out of the way, bless him. She keeps asking me if I think teal and rose gold clash. What do you think? Teal and rose gold? Uh… I honestly don't have an opinion on wedding aesthetics, Mum. They both sound… sparkly. Men. They just don't understand the importance of these things. It’s a reflection of their future happiness, apparently. Speaking of happiness… Have you given any more thought to…well, you know. To…? To finding a nice girl. Settling down. Little ones running around. You’re not getting any younger, you know. Mum, we’ve been over this. I'm happy with my life as it is. Teaching in Japan was amazing, I'm enjoying being back, but I’m not rushing into marriage just because society thinks I should.

Honestly, it's just… baffling. Like, what’s the point of changing the A-levels  again ? They’ve barely settled down from the last lot of reforms. Aye, it’s a right mess, isn’t it? I was reading something about it online, they’re shifting the focus even  more  towards coursework. Which, fine, for some, but it just disadvantages kids who don't have, y'know, someone at home able to help them with it, or a fancy tutor. Exactly! It just widens the gap. And then everyone panics when results come out, and it’s all ‘grade inflation’ and ‘lowering standards’. It’s a self-fulfilling prophecy, really. It is. And the teachers are stuck in the middle, trying to navigate all this. Poor things. Did you see Mrs. Henderson’s hair at the garden centre? No! What’s she done now? Last time I saw her she was rocking a really… vibrant purple. Oh, that was a phase. Now she’s gone for a full-on beehive. Like, 60s style beehive. It’s… something. Oh my god. She’s a character, that one. Speaking of characters, have you checked on the peace lily? It was looking a bit droopy last time I looked. I watered it this morning. It’s a drama queen, that plant. Needs constant attention. Honestly, having all these plants is like having kids, eh? Haha, almost. Less expensive though, thankfully. Though I'm starting to think maybe it  is  expensive. All the compost, the plant food…it adds up. You're telling me. And don't even get me started on the cost of petrol now. Honestly, it's ridiculous. I filled up yesterday and nearly had a heart attack. It’s insane. Part of me just wants to cycle everywhere. But then Cambridge drivers… well, you know. It’s a death wish. Oh, it is. They’ve no sense, them lot. Remember that crisis last year? When everyone was panic-buying? It was bonkers. God, yes. Queues around the block. People arguing. It felt like the end of civilisation. It did. And the NHS is getting worse and worse, isn't it? Just read an article about the waiting lists for everything. It's horrifying. My aunt’s been waiting months for a hip replacement. She's in constant pain, and they just keep pushing it back. It’s the same story with everyone.

Right, so I genuinely think I’m gonna have to get a job over the summer. Like, actually  a  job, not just a few shifts here and there. Oh god, same. I’ve basically spent all my loan on… well, existing. And vintage shops. Mostly vintage shops. Tell me about it. I'm already dreading asking my mam for help again. She’s started giving me the ‘you need to understand the value of a pound’ speech every time I mention wanting a coffee. My dad's on one about me getting a ‘proper’ job, like, full-time. He keeps sending me LinkedIn links for accountancy firms. Accountancy! As if. Oh, brilliant. My dad’s just lecturing me about the importance of saving for a house deposit. As if a house is even on the cards in this economy. He doesn’t understand. Exactly! He’s like, ‘You should just give up the smoking, that’ll save you loads.’ As if that’s the answer to everything. It's a coping mechanism, Dad! Honestly, it’s always the smoking, isn’t it? Like, okay, maybe it's not  good  for me, but it’s the only thing keeping me sane during coursework. And besides, it’s the one vice I haven't relinquished to student life. I refuse to become a completely caffeine-fueled, broke, stressed-out mess that consumes nothing but instant noodles. I’m holding onto my cigarettes. Fair enough. I have been thinking about cutting down though, honestly. It’s just… expensive. It's like funding Big Tobacco with my dwindling funds. Speaking of dwindling funds, anyone else completely blank on their dissertation topic? I’m supposed to be researching something to do with feminist literature and I’m just drawing a complete blank. Oh, I’ve got a vague idea, but it’s basically just an excuse to read more Virginia Woolf. Which, admittedly, isn't the worst fate. I’m stuck on my history one. I was thinking about… wait for it… the Black Death. The Black Plague? Seriously? I know, right? It’s a bit morbid. But think about it! Social upheaval, economic collapse, religious questioning… it’s totally relevant to everything that’s going on now! Okay, that's… actually pretty insightful. Not what I was expecting. I'm over here thinking about comparing Charlotte Brontë to Taylor Swift. Wait, that's not a terrible idea!

It’s just…it’s exhausting, isn’t it? Maintaining friendships that have just…run their course. Tell me about it. Feels brutal though, doesn’t it? Like you’re a terrible person for wanting less contact. Especially when people  expect  a certain level of involvement. Exactly! Like guilt-tripping is their default setting. I was thinking about Sarah the other day, from uni. We used to be so close. Now…I dread her calls. It’s always a drama. Always. And she always expects me to fix it, or at least listen for hours. Oh, the ‘everything’s a crisis’ friend. I had one of those. Mark. He’d call me at, like, 10pm on a Tuesday to dissect some minor work disagreement. Like, seriously? I’ve got stuff to do! And then when you try to gently pull back, they act like  you’re  the one being unreasonable. Like you owe them your emotional labour. It’s the entitlement, isn’t it? I think I just…ghosted Mark eventually. Felt awful, but setting boundaries was impossible. He’d interpret politeness as encouragement. “Oh, you’re busy this week? No worries, I’ll call next week!” and then it would start all over again. Ugh. Ghosting feels horrible, though. I’m terrible at direct confrontation, ironically, given my job. I keep dithering with Sarah, thinking I need to have ‘the talk’. But what do you even  say ? “Hey, I value our history, but I can’t handle your constant crises anymore”? That sounds awful! You could try the slow fade? That’s what I did with a couple of people. Just…less frequent calls, longer response times, always having a ‘prior engagement’. It’s less dramatic than a full-blown confrontation. Hmm. That feels…less cowardly, definitely. But then you have to maintain the façade, which is exhausting in itself. It’s like a weird, drawn-out performance. True. But sometimes it’s kinder, I think. A sudden cut-off can be really hurtful. Especially if there’s a long history there. And honestly, sometimes people just won’t take the hint with a direct conversation. They’ll argue, they’ll manipulate… That’s Sarah to a tee. She's very…persuasive. I've been trying to convince myself it's just a phase, that she’ll grow out of it. But we’ve been friends for fifteen years, and the drama hasn't lessened.

So, how are things going at university, darling? Still enjoying the history course? Yeah, it’s… good. Intense, as always. We’re starting a new module on the Tudors next term, which I'm actually really excited about. It's a bit of a jump from medieval stuff, but a good change of pace. The Tudors! Oh, that’s fascinating. All that drama with Henry VIII. Such a colourful period. Did you ever know your great-aunt Matilda was quite obsessed with Anne Boleyn? She had a whole room dedicated to it, filled with books and portraits. No way! I never knew that. Aunt Matilda always seemed so… practical. Not the type for historical obsession. Oh, don't underestimate her. She had hidden depths, that woman. She used to say Anne Boleyn was a misunderstood genius. Though, truthfully, I think she just liked the scandal. Speaking of scandalous, have you spoken to your mother recently? She was on the phone yesterday, going on about your cousin David’s latest… venture. Oh god, David. What is it this time? Another “get rich quick” scheme? Last I heard he was trying to sell ethically sourced alpaca socks online. Worse, apparently. He’s decided to become a life coach. A “holistic wellness guru”, he called himself. Honestly, the things people do. Your mother was quite beside herself. Seriously? That's… incredible. He’s always been a bit of a drama queen, but this takes the biscuit. Has he actually got any clients? She thinks he’s mostly convincing friends and family to pay for sessions. She’s worried he’ll end up in debt again. He always was a bit hopeless with money. Though, he does have your grandfather's artistic flair, even if it manifests in… questionable ways. True. Grandad always had big ideas. Remember that time he tried to build a miniature replica of the Eiffel Tower in the garden? Oh, how could I forget? It collapsed halfway through and nearly took out Mrs. Higgins’ prize-winning roses. Your grandfather was never one for practical engineering. Anyway, enough about the family. How’s your own art coming along? Are you still sketching in those notebooks of yours? Yeah, I’m still at it. Nothing serious, just doodling really. I saw that exhibition at the Tate Modern last week, the one with the abstract expressionists. It really inspired me to try and loosen up a bit.

Right, so I was thinking, before the gym tonight, definitely need something proper. Not just a banana. Like, a proper meal. I'm gonna be wrecked. Absolutely. Remember that time in Prague? You tried to do a leg day on an empty stomach? The wobbling. It was… concerning. Don't remind me! I genuinely thought my legs were going to give way mid-squat. Humiliating. Seriously though, we need to find a decent supermarket soon. I’m craving something with protein. We passed a little shop back in Tarnow, I think. Looked quite well-stocked. Though, navigating the aisles with my Polish is… optimistic, to say the least. I’m better, I think. Managed to order coffee without ending up with hot milk and a bewildered barista. Small victories. It’s just…everything takes so long. Even the simplest tasks. Time just  moves  differently here. Or maybe it’s the roads. It’s a bit of both, I reckon. And the driving. Honestly, I'm starting to feel like a rally driver dodging potholes and tractors. You’re doing brilliantly, by the way. Navigating this beast of a campervan is no mean feat. Thanks. I’m mostly just praying I don’t take out a sheep. Seriously, they just wander onto the road like they own the place. Which, admittedly, they probably do. Speaking of owning the place…it's just…being English here is…interesting. How so? It’s just… subtle things. The way men look. The comments. Even well-meaning attempts at conversation often feel… weighted. It's hard to explain. You get used to it, I suppose. After a while you just build a wall. I’ve noticed it too, actually. It’s not overt, like shouting or anything, but there's… a presumption. Like, we need ‘helping’ or ‘explaining’ things to. It’s frustrating. And the gym… I dread to think what it's like there. Oh, it's a whole other level. The staring. The unsolicited advice. I had a guy try to adjust my form on a machine last week. I was lifting perfectly fine! Like, seriously? That’s beyond infuriating. It’s that ingrained sexism, isn’t it? The assumption that men know best, even when they demonstrably don't. It’s exhausting. It is. It really is. And then you feel bad for getting annoyed, because you think  am I being overly sensitive?

This mug’s lovely, isn’t it? Proper hand-thrown, you can feel the difference. Not like those mass-produced ones. Aye, it is a nice mug. Though I still miss my old blue one. The one with the roses. Simple, but it held the warmth, you know? More than just the tea, if you get my drift. I do. Though I remember you saying it chipped, and you were worried about cutting your lip. Oh, it did chip. Little sliver right on the rim. Had to retire it then, didn’t I? Can’t risk a poorly lip at my age. This milk’s a bit thin though, isn’t it? Not like the stuff we used to get from Old Man Hemmings’ farm. It's the semi-skimmed. I thought I’d try and be…sensible. Sensible! At our age? What’s the point? A bit of proper milk never hurt anyone. Though, speaking of sensible, did you see that spider in the garden this morning? Huge thing, dangling from the rose bush. Oh,  that  spider. Monstrous! I nearly walked into its web. I hate spiders. Absolutely hate them. They’re just getting ready for winter. Spinning up a cozy home. They’re useful, you know. Keep the flies down. Though, I agree, a big one swinging in your face isn’t pleasant. Did you get the tomatoes staked? It’s turned a bit blustery, hasn’t it? I did, yes. Though I think I need to go and check them again. The wind’s picking up. It's been such a funny summer, hasn't it? Sweltering one minute, then a downpour the next. Aye, very erratic. Remember that power cut last year? We were plunged into darkness for hours. Had to get the candles out, just like the old days. And we ended up telling ghost stories until the small hours. You nearly scared me to death with that one about Old Man Withers and the haunted barn! Oh, it’s a true story! Well, mostly true. I heard it from Mrs. Higgins, and she swore it was gospel! Have you seen many birds in the garden lately? Not as many as usual, no. The blue tits seem to have disappeared. Perhaps they've found a better source of food. Though, I did see a robin earlier. Bright little fellow. Robins are always around. They’re braver than most.

So, are we definitely going to Cornwall this year? That’s the plan, love. Unless your Grandad here decides he wants to go to Skegness again. Skegness was lovely! Good arcades. And the sea air. Though a bit bracing, mind you. Skegness is… not Cornwall, Grandad. I just said it was lovely. No need to be rude. He’s just teasing, darling. Cornwall it is. We’ve got the cottage booked, haven't we? Near Newquay? Yeah, the one with the little garden? That's good. Will Chloe and Maisie be coming with us again? I’ve asked Chloe’s mum, but she hasn’t got back to me yet. She said something about a family thing. Oh. That’s a shame. We always have loads of fun with them. Especially on the beach. Aye, they’re good girls, those two. Full of beans. Always wanting to build sandcastles. Maisie’s really good at decorating them. She always finds the prettiest shells and seaweed. We could always invite Sophie and Lily? They’ve been asking about going away with us. Ooh, yeah! That's a good idea, Mum. Sophie’s really funny. And Lily's good at… well, she's good at everything. Lily’s a bit of a know-it-all, if you ask me. Grandad! Now, now. She’s just bright. Don’t be grumpy. Just saying. She corrected me on the name of a Beatles song last week. A  Beatles  song! Maybe you got it wrong, Grandad. I  know  a Beatles song when I hear one! I saw them live, you know. That’s a lovely story, dear. Perhaps we can save the Beatles debate for the car journey? Are we going by car again? It takes  ages . Well, we could get the train, but then we’d have to get taxis to the cottage. And all your beach stuff… True. Plus, you always get motion sickness on long journeys, Mum. I do, don't I? Best stick to the car then. And stop worrying about it. It’ll be a lovely holiday. We can go to the Eden Project, and maybe try surfing. Surfing!? I don’t think so. I used to be a dab hand at surfing, you know. Back in my day... Of course you did, Grandad. Oh dear, here we go. Perhaps we’ll pack some earplugs for the car journey after all. Okay now I'm thinking.

Honestly though, Heath Ledger in that film… like, peak Heath Ledger. I could watch that scene in the football stadium a million times. Seriously! And the way he’s just… brooding. It's so good. Although, Patrick Verona is a bit of a manipulative jerk, isn't he? Like, paying someone to date you? Not cool. I know, right? But it's a  film . It's romanticized! And Kat Stratford is amazing. She's so fiercely independent. I wish I was that intimidating. You’re plenty intimidating when Mrs. Davies tries to give you extra homework. Remember last week? Oh god, don't remind me. She just  loves  to pick on me. I swear she has it out for anyone who asks questions. It’s ridiculous. History is already boring enough without her making it actively unpleasant. Tell me about it. Geography is killing me. Mr. Henderson just drones on and on about tectonic plates. Like, I get it, the Earth moves. Can we move on, please? Ugh, boring teachers are the worst. Speaking of moving on… are you still gutted about not being able to go to the London trip? Gutted doesn’t even cover it. My mum's being so unfair. She said it's ‘too expensive’ and ‘I need to focus on my GCSEs.’ Like, a weekend in London is going to  ruin  my future? That's so rubbish! Everyone’s going. It’s the theatre trip, right? Seeing Wicked? Yeah! And then walking around Covent Garden and maybe going to that vintage shop we talked about? I was already planning my outfit! Oh, that vintage shop is amazing. I got this jacket there last year. You’d love it. Maybe… maybe if you did extra chores or offered to help with something, your mum might reconsider? I’ve tried! I offered to clean the entire house for a month! She just said, “You’ll get bored and do a bad job.” Honestly, she just doesn't  want  me to have fun. That’s awful. I’m sure we can figure something out. Maybe we can save some money for you and you can meet us there on the Saturday? It might be a push, but… That would be amazing! But I don't want to put you guys out. It’s not putting us out! We’d love it if you could come. Let's look at train tickets later.

Honestly, Facebook is a minefield. I spent an hour last night arguing with someone about… well, I don’t even remember what it was about now. Just endless loops of misinformation. Misinformation? Always was a lot of nonsense on that internet thing. Never did trust it, myself. Too easy to say anything, isn't it? It’s the echo chambers, I think. People just surround themselves with people who already agree with them. It's awful, isn't it? My neighbour, bless her, she shared something about… I don’t even want to repeat it. It was something about vaccines and Bill Gates. I tried to gently explain, but she just wouldn't listen. It’s exhausting. It feels like everyone’s constantly shouting into the void. Reminds me a bit of young Arthur, always getting into scrapes. Terrible for collecting things, he was. Had to have everything  just so . Kept lining up his toy soldiers for hours. Oh, you mean his OCD? Poor Arthur. It was heartbreaking to watch. Remember when he refused to go to school because his pencils weren't sharpened exactly the same length? It’s a difficult condition. It’s good he got help eventually. Is it still… a thing? With Arthur? He manages it. Medication, mostly. Still a bit particular about things, mind you. Can't stand a crooked picture frame. But he’s a good lad. Works hard. He is. A lovely boy, always was. Remember when he had chickenpox? Covered head to toe. Poor thing was miserable. Oh god, chickenpox. I remember being absolutely  itchy . And my mum making me wear those calamine lotion socks. Sounds delightful. He had it bad, Arthur did. We used to have to tie his hands together at night so he wouldn’t scratch himself to bits. Ruth – my wife – she was beside herself. Always worried about her children. Though she wasn't one for much religion, Ruth wasn't. Said she didn't see much sense in it. No, she wasn't, was she? Though she always let us go to Sunday school. I think she just wanted us to learn some morals. It’s interesting, isn’t it? How different people approach faith. I was raised quite religiously, and… well, I’ve certainly had my questions. It’s a complex topic. Too complex for a cup of tea and a biscuit, I think. You're right about that.

Honestly though, Germany was… a lot. I mean, lovely country, beautiful scenery, but trying to order a simple coffee was a nightmare. Oh god, the language! I tried to learn a bit before we went, just the basics, but it all went out of my head the second someone actually  spoke  to me. It’s always the way, isn't it? You spend weeks memorising phrases and then when the time comes, you just end up pointing and miming. I remember trying to ask for directions in Italy once… ended up accidentally ordering a whole plate of snails. Snails?! Seriously? Absolutely. Beautifully presented snails. Didn't eat a single one. Dad, you’re awful! But that  does  sound like something you’d do. Remember that time you tried to fix Aunt Carol’s car and ended up… well, let's just say she had to call a professional. Now, hold on a minute! That car was a lemon. A complete and utter lemon. It was practically begging to be taken apart. It was begging to be replaced, more like! Carol was furious. Speaking of cars, anyone remember Gran’s old Morris Minor? That thing was indestructible. Oh my god, the one that smelled permanently of biscuits and lavender? That’s the one! And she drove it everywhere. Even took it to France once. In a Morris Minor? Brave woman. She was a character, your grandmother. No fear. Used to tell the policeman off for speeding, even when  she  was the one doing the speeding. That sounds exactly like her. I wish I’d asked her more about her childhood. She always had the best stories. Me too. She always had a story for every occasion. Remember when she told us about growing up during the war? Oh yes, the rationing and the evacuees. She said it was a hard time, but everyone pulled together. A different world, really. It’s funny, isn't it? How much things have changed. Still, family dinners were always the same, even then. Mum making a roast, Gran telling her stories, and Uncle Barry complaining about everything. Old habits die hard. Speaking of dinner, is anyone else starving? All this reminiscing is making me hungry. Definitely. What are we having tonight? I was thinking lasagne. It's easy, and everyone likes it. Sounds perfect to me. And maybe we can dig out some old photos afterwards.

So, have you been to any gigs recently? Anything good? Nah, not for ages, mate. Been slammed at work, you know? Long shifts, prepping for the weekend rush. It’s brutal. But I did catch a bit of that new IDLES album on Spotify. It's alright, a bit… shouty, even for them. Shouty’s kind of their thing, isn’t it? I thought it was pretty solid. Saw them at Rock City a couple of years back – absolute chaos. Proper good chaos though. Did you ever get into them much? I liked their first album,  Brutalism . That was something else. But I’m more of a… drummer’s perspective kinda guy. I listen specifically  for  the drumming, and Joe Talbot’s screaming kinda gets in the way of appreciating it, you know? Fair enough. Who are you listening to drumming-wise at the moment then? Anything inspiring your own playing? Been going back to a lot of early Radiohead, actually. Phil Selway’s brilliant. Subtle, really musical. And I've been digging into some older jazz too, Max Roach, Art Blakey... trying to broaden my horizons a bit. Yourself? Still hammering away? Still at it, yeah. Got a practice session booked with the band next week. We’re trying to write some new stuff, but it’s slow going. Everyone’s got uni stuff on, it’s hard to get time together. How’s Ben doing? Haven’t seen him in ages. Ben’s good, he started that internship at the restaurant in Plymouth, yeah? The one he was going on about forever. Seems to be loving it. Says the head chef is a bit of a perfectionist, but he’s learning loads. Apparently, he's plating things with tweezers now. Tweezers! That’s dedication. He always was a bit of a perfectionist, though, wasn’t he? What about Sarah? Still at uni? Yeah, she's finishing up her dissertation now, I think. She's stressing, naturally. Saw her at the pub last week, she was drowning her sorrows in cider. Said it's about… Victorian poetry, I think? Oh, wow. Sounds… intense. Any plans for after uni? You thinking of sticking around Devon, or heading off somewhere? I’m not sure, to be honest. I've been offered a full-time position at the restaurant, which is tempting. Good money, good hours, good food… But part of me wants to travel, you know?

Honestly, this place is rammed, isn’t it? Didn’t realise it’d be this busy for just a coffee. Yeah, it’s mental. Look at the queue for the drive-through. Absolute chaos. Old Mrs. Henderson’s in that white car, isn’t she? Probably wants a frappuccino with extra everything. Probably. She loves her fancy coffees. It’s just so noisy in here though. Are you alright? You seem a bit… distracted. Just thinking about Saturday. Jamie’s got that domino drive on, yeah? Said I could come. Oh, that’s good! You enjoy those, don’t you? Bit of a Geordie tradition, all that dominoes and chatting. I’m knackered just thinking about it. Work’s been a nightmare this week. What’s happened? Another parent complaining about homework? Worse. The head wants us all to participate in this new scheme – ‘Entrepreneurial Skills for Young Learners’. Honestly, I haven’t a clue where to start. Apparently, we’re supposed to get them thinking about business structures and profit margins. It’s Year 7! Sounds… ambitious. Maybe you could get them to sell cookies or something? I thought about it! But then you get the issues of allergies and parental permission and… oh, it's a headache. Anyway, enough about work. What are your plans for the summer? Have you thought about that yet? Not really. Liam wants to go camping again, but I don't know. Remember last year? The midges ate us alive. Oh, dear god, yes. And the rain! We ended up sleeping in the car for half the night. We need to think about getting some decent sleeping bags this year, and maybe proper bug repellent. I saw a deal at Go Outdoors last week. Sounds good. Maybe. It depends if I can earn some money. I was thinking of getting a paper round or something. That’s a good idea. It'll give you some independence. Did you finish that history project I asked you about? Almost. Just need to write the conclusion. It’s about the industrial revolution in Newcastle. It’s quite interesting actually. Did you know they used to have a massive shipbuilding industry there? I did! My grandad worked at Swan Hunter for years. He used to tell me stories about it. Hard work, but good money. Speaking of Newcastle, do you want me to drop you off near the station after this?

Right, so this place is… basically functional. Still got boxes everywhere, obviously. Welcome to the chaos. Fancy a beer? I think I've actually managed to locate some glasses. Cheers, mate. Functional’s good, functional's a start. It's a good size, though. Way bigger than that shoebox you called a room at uni, eh? Remember trying to fit, like, seven of us in there for pre-drinks? Don’t remind me. And the smell… a potent mix of instant noodles and desperation. Seriously though, it’s a massive step up. Rent’s a bit mental though, isn't it? Sussex is officially trying to bankrupt me. Tell me about it. Everything’s gone up. I’m still trying to figure out this whole ‘adulting’ thing. Paying bills, doing laundry… it's a conspiracy, I swear. Speaking of which, did you get that form for the council tax? Absolute nightmare. Ugh, yeah. I spent like an hour trying to decipher what they wanted. It’s like they actively  want  you to fail. What about you? How’s the assurance analyst life treating you? Still finding loopholes in systems? Still finding loopholes. Pays the bills, though. Which is the main thing, isn’t it? I mean, speaking of money... heard anything from Sarah and Ben? They were hinting about… well, you know. Oh! Yeah, actually. They announced it on Facebook yesterday. Tiny human on the way! Honestly, slightly terrifying. Remember how utterly hopeless Ben was at looking after that cactus at uni? Oh god, the cactus! It died within a week. He genuinely seemed surprised. So, a baby… a human being. That’s a level of responsibility he hasn't even begun to comprehend. Are you going to the reunion next month? I think so. Trying to sort out train tickets. It's been ages since I saw everyone. It'll be good to catch up, see who’s managed to completely fall apart and who’s faking it. Faking it till they make it, that’s the uni motto, isn't it? I’m hoping no one tries to get me to talk about my Spanish. I've let that completely lapse. Can barely remember "Hola". It’ll be alright. Someone will inevitably start talking about their incredibly lucrative career or getting married. It's tradition. Actually, talking of marriage… you and Chloe still going strong? Yeah, really good. We’ve been talking about… well, you know, the whole joint bank account thing.

…and honestly, the guilt is awful. I keep thinking I should have pushed her harder to go to the doctor sooner. Even though she kept saying she was fine, just tired. Oh, Sarah. Don’t do that to yourself. You  always  encouraged her to look after herself. She was just…stubborn. You can’t take responsibility for someone else’s choices, especially when they’re trying to be brave. I know, logically. It’s just…seeing how quickly it went downhill after diagnosis. If they’d caught it earlier… There's no point in ‘ifs’ now, is there? It wouldn’t change anything. And honestly, even if they  had  caught it earlier, it might not have made a difference. It was aggressive, what she had. You know that. I do. It’s just…Emily keeps asking about her. She’s handling it remarkably well, actually, for eight. But then she’ll suddenly ask if Grandma is just sleeping, and it breaks my heart all over again. Oh, bless her. That's…that's brutal. How are you even beginning to explain all of that? Gently. We talked about Grandma being very, very sick, and her body just stopping working. She asked if Grandma was in heaven, and I said…I said she was. And that she was looking after us. It felt so inadequate. It  is  inadequate. There  are  no good answers. Just…be there for her. Let her ask questions, and answer honestly, but age-appropriately. It’s all you can do. And don’t be afraid to show your own sadness. It’s okay for her to see you grieve. You’re right. I’ve been trying to be strong for her, but maybe I’m overdoing it. I don’t want her to think she can’t come to me with her feelings. Exactly. And speaking of feelings… how are  you  holding up? Really? Beyond the guilt and the Emily stuff? Honestly? Exhausted. And…terrified. It feels…precarious, you know? Like everything could fall apart at any moment. It’s stupid, I know. It’s not stupid at all. When something like this happens, it shakes everything. Makes you question everything. And you’re also dealing with your own grief on top of everything else. It's perfectly normal to feel like that. Have you been back to the doctors about your own anxiety? Not yet. I keep putting it off.

So, how was school today, you two? Anything exciting happen? Apart from the usual teenage dramas, of course. It was alright, Mum. History was boring as usual. Mr. Davies just reads from the textbook. Honestly. Mine was okay. We started doing practical stuff in science, which is good. Dissecting… things. It was a bit gross. Dissecting? Already? You’re moving quickly then. When I was your age, we were still labelling diagrams. Yeah well, Miss. Henderson’s a bit keen. She wants us all to be little surgeons, I think. Sounds ambitious! Speaking of ambitious, have you given any more thought to what you want to  be  when you grow up, Leo? Still aiming for professional footballer? Yeah, obviously. But Dad says I need a backup plan. He keeps going on about apprenticeships. Your father has a point. A good apprenticeship can set you up for life. It’s a proper skill, a trade. More reliable than relying on sporting talent, I think. Though, of course, anything’s possible. I don’t really know what I want to do. Everyone’s talking about university but… it seems like a lot of debt. It is a big commitment. And it’s not the only route. Your dad’s right about apprenticeships; they’re fantastic. Or you could even consider starting your own little business. I’ve been thinking, actually, about investing in that online marketing idea I mentioned. You mean the proofreading and content creation? That’s a good market, actually. Lots of small businesses need that kind of help. But careful with your investment, darling. It’s a risky world out there. I know, I know. I’m being cautious. It's just… I'm tired of working  for  people. I want to build something for myself. And it might be good experience for the boys, seeing how a business works. You mean, like, could we help? With the… the social media stuff? Exactly! You’re a whiz with TikTok, aren't you? And Ben, you’re good with computers. You could handle the website updates. Though first, you need to focus on your GCSEs! Speaking of focus, did you see that match on Saturday? Liverpool were awful. Absolutely awful. Don’t even get me started. It was a disaster. They need a new midfielder, desperately. Yeah, and a new goalkeeper. Alisson’s been sloppy lately. Honestly, you two and your football.

Right, so Lancaster station is… about forty minutes from here, isn’t it? Feels like we’ve been on this train  ages  already. Feels like it. It’s that weird feeling of knowing you’re getting somewhere, but not  being  anywhere yet, you know? I’m really looking forward to seeing Sarah though. It feels like ages since I last saw her properly. Me too. And her new flat! She makes it sound amazing. Apparently, it's right near the canal. I’m hoping we can maybe go for a walk along it. Ooh, that’d be nice. She said something about wanting to take us to Morecambe Bay too? I haven't been to the coast in  ages . Real proper seaside. Oh, yes! Morecambe. Apparently, the cockle disaster happened there. Remember reading about that? All those people getting stuck in the mud. Oh god, yeah! Horrible. Hopefully, we won’t be venturing  that  far out. I’m just picturing fish and chips on the prom though. Proper, greasy fish and chips. Oh, you’re speaking my language. That's essential Lancaster experience material right there. She also said she wanted to show us around the university. Lancaster Uni is gorgeous, isn’t it? All those brutalist buildings. A bit imposing, but pretty. I wonder if it would’ve been a good option for my Masters… Thinking about that now, won't you? You’re doing so well with the application process though! I know you’re stressed, but you’ve got this. It’s a really strong project idea. Thanks. It’s just… the dissertation feels so huge. Like, a whole book. And thinking about needing to justify it all and stuff... I keep getting stuck on the methodology section. You will. You’ll crack it. Remember all those late nights we did in the library during our undergrad? We got through worse. What about you, how's the research going? Still wading through endless transcripts? Oh, it’s brutal. Honestly. It’s fascinating stuff, but it’s  slow . And then trying to turn it into something coherent… Luckily, my supervisor is really good. She keeps me on track. What are you hoping to do after this project, anyway? Have you thought about careers stuff? I have been… Actually, my Aunt Carol mentioned something the other day. Apparently, someone at her firm is retiring, and they’re looking for someone with my skillset.

Did you see Liam at the gig last night? Proper wedged in, wasn’t he? Right at the front. Nah, I didn’t go. Was proper knackered from work. Sounded good though, judging by your Instagram story. Who were they again? The…Uh… Static Bloom? Yeah, Static Bloom. They were brilliant! Proper energetic. You would’ve loved ‘em. Bit indie, bit rocky. Reminded me a bit of The Kooks, but heavier. Oh, right. I do like The Kooks. Should’ve gone. Was it busy then, properly rammed? Mental. Seriously. Couldn't move. I nearly lost my phone about three times. Ended up clinging onto it for dear life. Liam was just…in his element. Head banging, the lot. Classic Liam. He lives for that stuff. What about Sarah and Josh? Were they there? Sarah was, but Josh had a family thing. Said his grandma wasn't feeling too well. Sarah was bouncing about though. She’s proper into them, apparently. Been following them for ages. Oh, that's a shame about Josh’s grandma. Hope she’s alright. Sarah’s always got her finger on the pulse with the music scene. I’m usually a bit behind, to be honest. You need to let me be your guide, lad! I’ll take you to all the best gigs. What have  you  been up to then? Besides slaving away? Not much, to be fair. Tried to get back into painting miniatures. Bought a couple of Warhammer figures, but I’ve just been procrastinating. Can’t seem to get motivated. Oh yeah? You were really good at that, weren’t you? Remember that ork you painted? It was proper impressive. Thanks. Just need to…start, I guess. It's a bit fiddly, and I end up just watching YouTube videos instead. Currently obsessed with this guy who builds scale models of spaceships. Oh, you and your nerdy hobbies! That's fair enough though. YouTube’s a black hole. I’ve been trying to learn to crochet, but it's…challenging. Crochet? Seriously? You? That's a surprise. Don’t judge me! My nan’s been trying to teach me for years. I figured I'd finally give it a go. It’s harder than it looks. I’ve ended up with a tangled mess of wool more times than I care to admit. I can imagine. Maybe stick to the gigs, then? Clearly, that's more your thing.

Right, okay, so I’m going to use my researcher to… build a research station in Atlanta. Because honestly, Atlanta is a disaster zone already on the board. Feels appropriate. Good call. Smart. I’m going to fly from Cardiff to… São Paulo. Need to get a handle on that outbreak down there, seems to be escalating. Right, draw two player cards. Oh, brilliant. One is a funding card… and the other is an epidemic card. Fantastic. Oh, come  on ! Seriously? We've only just started! Right, okay, epidemic. Which city are we going to lose first? Let’s not be fatalistic, Rhys. It's just the draw of the cards. I’m going to treat a cube in Essen, then fly to Milan. Gotta contain this European spread. Reminds me of that time in ‘87, during the bird flu scare. Everyone was convinced Cardiff was going to be wiped off the map. Mrs. Davies down the street started stockpiling pickled onions. Pickled onions! Said they had medicinal properties. Oh, Gwynn, you always have the best stories. She swore by them for everything! A cold, a headache, a broken heart… pickled onions were the answer. Okay, okay, everyone focus! Epidemic means we intensify. Draw the bottom card of the infection deck. Oh no… Kolkata. Another three cubes go onto Kolkata. Right, that’s looking grim. I can fly to Kolkata and treat, but it'll take my whole turn. Do it. Kolkata feels like it’s about to explode. I’ll try to mitigate the damage in South America, build a research station in Buenos Aires, maybe slow things down there. I’m going to share knowledge with you, Alun. Give you my eradication card for blue. We need to get that blue disease under control, it’s spreading too fast. Always happy to receive a gift. I’m just going to quietly fly around trying to clean up messes. Old man’s work, really. Okay, Alun, you've treated in Kolkata. Good. It's still a hot spot, but manageable. My turn again. Building a research station in Chicago. It's a central hub, plus if things go south…well, you know. Hang on, before you do that… Rhys, you’re a chef, right? Imagine trying to coordinate a global response to a pandemic  while  simultaneously ensuring everyone is properly fed. No pressure. You think a culinary crisis is worse than a literal pandemic?

Right, so, the CBeebies panto is on the 27th, which is good. It’s a Saturday. We’ll have to book tickets, won’t we? Remember last year how quickly they went? Ooh, yes! The one with the pirates! That was  so  good, Mummy! Can we sit near the front? Please? I want to see all the glitter! We’ll try, darlings, we’ll try. Though getting close to the front with you two is always a bit of a… tactical operation. Now, Leo, you are officially seven in the summer. Any thoughts on what you'd like to  do  for your birthday? I want a Lego castle! A  really  big one! And a party with all my friends! And cake with chocolate frosting! Okay, okay, we can talk about a Lego castle. And a party, definitely. Though perhaps not  all  your friends… the house isn’t enormous, remember. Elsie, you’re turning five. What about you? Do you have any big ideas? I want a princess party! With a real princess! And a rainbow cake! And…and… I want to wear my sparkly dress! A real princess might be tricky, darling. But a sparkly dress is  absolutely  happening. Rainbow cake, definitely. Right. Operation Birthday Planning begins now. We’ll need to check dates, because Nana and Grandpa want to come, and Auntie Sarah… Mummy, remember when Mr. Tumble said “Big hug!”? It makes me giggle. Yes, I do, darling. Mr. Tumble  does  say “Big hug” a lot, doesn’t he? He’s a bit of a saying machine, that one. “Something special is in the spotty bag!” Remember that? I like the stories on CBeebies! The ones with the little bear! What's his name…? Bluey! Bluey! Yes, you love Bluey. That's a good one. They're quite good at teaching little life lessons, aren’t they? Mummy, what are we doing for World Book Day? Can I be Harry Potter? We need to have a think about that, Leo. It's not for ages yet, is it? We’ll have a rummage through your books and see what inspires us. And then there's Mother’s Day next month… I'm not expecting much, honestly. Just a nice breakfast in bed would be lovely. I can make you a card, Mummy! With lots of sparkly bits! Oh, Elsie, that would be the  best  present ever. A sparkly card, made by my very own little artist.

Honestly, this weather is doing my head in. One minute it’s sunshine, the next it’s biblical rain. Makes planning anything impossible. Tell me about it! I was hoping to cycle to work today, but absolutely not a chance. Completely drenched just walking to the bus stop. It’s November in England, what do you expect? You’re both moaning! It’s…atmospheric. Perfect for curling up with a book. Though I will admit, the grey does get a bit much. Speaking of which, how’s the house hunt going, Ben? Any closer to escaping the North? Slow. So slow. Viewings are either booked solid or the places are…well, let's just say the photos were  very  flattering. Saw one yesterday that smelled strongly of damp and had wallpaper peeling off. Oh, the joys of house hunting. Remember when we were looking for this place? The one with the questionable plumbing and the garden that was mostly just weeds? Good times! We got lucky with this one, though. It’s cozy, and the location’s brilliant. Though, seriously Ben, are you sure you want to move  all  the way down to Hampshire? Seems a long way from everything. It’s the job, isn’t it? It's a really good opportunity and they’re offering a relocation package which helps. Honestly, I'm more worried about finding a decent internet provider down there. Apparently, it’s a broadband desert in some areas. Crucial for my work, obviously. You’d think in this day and age, broadband wouldn't be an issue! It’s ridiculous. I’m still battling with BT. They keep promising to fix the signal, but it’s been “scheduled for repair” for three weeks now. Don’t even get me started on tech support. Trying to explain to someone on the phone that my laptop won’t connect to the printer is a soul-crushing experience. They just read from a script. Speaking of soul-crushing experiences, I braved the world of online dating again last week. Oh no… how did it go? Let me guess, a lot of questionable profiles? You have no idea. One woman’s profile picture was a heavily filtered selfie with a tiger. A  tiger . And another was obsessed with crystals and claimed to communicate with dolphins. Oh, Ben! You really do attract the…interesting ones. Have you thought about giving up and embracing the hermit life?

Honestly, this book was… underwhelming. All that hype for… well, for beige. It felt beige. Like a really long, beige cardigan. Beige is a good word for it, actually. I kept waiting for something to  happen . And the characters… did anyone actually  like  any of them? I found them all terribly self-absorbed. I think I felt a bit sorry for the main character, actually. But yeah, the pacing was terrible. It dragged. Though, it did remind me a little of those long summer holidays we used to have as kids. Just… endless days stretching out. Oh, summer holidays. That takes me back. Do you remember those little plastic ponies? The Shetties? I was obsessed. I had a whole stable of them. And I’d give them all names and stories… Ooh, the Shetties! Yes! I preferred the My Little Ponies, though. The bigger ones, with the long manes you could brush. I’d spend hours doing their hair. My Nan bought me a whole set. It was proper luxury. I had both, actually. My brother was really into Action Force, and I used to try and sneak their figures into my pony world. They didn’t really fit, though. It was always a bit awkward. He wasn’t keen. Ha! Kids. My nephew’s all about dinosaurs at the moment. Apparently, he corrects me on the pronunciation of all their names. Apparently, I'm saying "Triceratops" wrong. Oh, the tiny experts. They’re the worst! Though, I suppose it’s good they’re learning. It’s funny, isn’t it, how different things are now? I was trying to teach my niece a bit of Lincolnshire dialect the other day. She just looked at me blankly. Lincolnshire dialect? What did you try and teach her? Just “tha knows” and “ay up.” Simple things. But she didn’t recognise them. Apparently, all the kids at school speak with this sort of… London accent now. Even in Peterborough! It’s mad, isn’t it? Everyone’s blending together. I mean, even I’ve probably lost a bit of my Essex twang over the years. Especially working in finance, you have to be… neutral, I guess. Absolutely. At work, I have to consciously tone down the Boston accent sometimes. People don't always get it. They think I'm speaking with a West Country accent, which is just… wrong. It's a very distinct accent, Boston.

So then, the satnav just completely lost it, didn’t it? Sent us down this tiny little lane, barely wide enough for the car. Honestly, Mum, you two and technology. It's always an adventure. Were you near any farms or anything? You always end up near farms. Oh, aye, a proper farm, pet. Sheep everywhere. And honestly, the smell! Not  unpleasant , mind, just… agricultural. Colin was convinced one of the sheep was judging him. He’s always been sensitive to livestock. No, really. Once, a goose chased him around a pond for a good ten minutes. Utterly terrified. Oh, that sounds brilliant! Did you get any good photos? Pictures of judging sheep? Please tell me you got pictures of judging sheep. I did! A right close-up. You can practically  see  the disdain in its eyes. I’ll show you later. We did manage to get to Whitby eventually, though. Beautiful place. Much nicer than getting lost in the countryside. Whitby was lovely. A bit too many tourists, admittedly. Couldn’t get a decent seat on the pier to eat our fish and chips. Ended up having to take them back to the car. Fish and chips in the car? Iconic. Did you at least get proper Whitby scampi? That's the main question. It  has  to be Whitby scampi. We did, thankfully. Massive portions. Colin nearly burst. Although, he did try to share some with a seagull… A rather aggressive seagull. Nearly took his hand off. I told him, “Colin, leave the wildlife alone!” He never listens. Classic Colin. Speaking of wildlife, how is Barnaby doing? Has he forgiven you for abandoning him for a week? He gave us the silent treatment for a good twelve hours when we got back. Full cold shoulder. Wouldn’t even look at us. Ah, cats. They hold a grudge, you know. He probably organised a feline protest while we were gone. Probably. He’s a drama queen, that cat. We got a little souvenir for him though. A little feather toy. He perked up as soon as he saw it. Good. He deserves a treat. So, what else did you get up to in Whitby? Did you go up the 199 steps? Oh God, no. Not with Colin’s knees. He managed about thirty before declaring it a “health hazard.” We mostly wandered around the shops and had a few pints in a pub.

Right, who finished the orange juice? Seriously? I just bought a carton yesterday. Not me! I had a glass with breakfast, but there was still loads left. Though, to be fair, I didn’t check  how  loads. Probably Ben. He's a juice fiend, isn't he? Though, he's not here yet. Maybe he snuck in early for a fix. It’s always Ben. Honestly, the man operates on 90% orange juice and 10% existential dread. Speaking of which, did you see that article about Elon Musk… honestly, the man is completely unhinged. Oh, the one about the Twitter rebranding? Utter chaos. I mean, X? Really? It feels… unfinished. Like he ran out of ideas halfway through. It’s just not catchy. It’s a branding nightmare. And the fact he’s actively encouraging people to call it “X” despite it sounding like a mathematical equation? It’s a disaster. I’m working on a piece about it, actually. The level of free publicity he’s getting for sheer absurdity is… impressive, I guess. He's a genius at self-promotion, that’s for sure. Even when it’s spectacularly bad. I’ve been wrestling with a problem at work all week, this control system for a new bit of machinery, it’s driving me mad. Keeps throwing up errors. Oh dear, that sounds stressful. What kind of machinery? Is it anything exciting? Not particularly. It’s for a bottling plant. Relatively mundane, but the tolerances are super tight. One tiny miscalculation and it’ll create a cascade of broken bottles. Which, obviously, isn't ideal. Sounds… messy. Are you getting support from your team? They're helpful enough, but it’s one of those things where you feel like you should just  know  the answer. It's frustrating. I need to spend the afternoon properly debugging it. Maybe with copious amounts of coffee. Speaking of caffeine, are we doing a grocery shop today? I'm almost out of coffee  and  tea. It’s a crisis. Also, I’m thinking of attempting that Portuguese custard tart recipe I found online. Oh, yes! The  pastel de nata ? You have to. I’ve heard they’re amazing. I'll happily be a taste tester. And yes, grocery shop. I'm out of everything remotely resembling fresh produce. I’ve been surviving on biscuits for the last two days. Biscuits are a perfectly acceptable diet.

Honestly though, I still don't trust satnavs. They always try to take you down roads that are clearly not meant for cars. They do, don't they? Remember when it took Dad down that farm track last summer? Thought we were going to get stuck. Ha! That was brilliant. Dad was fuming. He swore he could find it quicker on a map. Aye, maps were alright. Proper sense of direction you got with a map. None of this relying on a little screen telling you what to do. Though, Google Maps got me out of a right pickle in Saudi last year. Couldn’t have done it without it. Saudi Arabia? What were you doing in Saudi Arabia, Reg? Work, love. Bit of training with the Saudi National Guard. Hot as hell, mind you. Never known heat like it. Wow. That sounds…intense. Are you going to miss it though? Moving back here full-time? Not the heat, no. Though, I'll miss the lads. Good bunch. But I'm looking forward to a bit of peace and quiet, you know? Just pottering about. Maybe finally get around to decorating the spare room. Decorating? You and decorating? That'll be the day. Alright, alright, I'm no DIY expert. But it needs doing. Been saying that for five years now. You should get someone in. It's not worth the stress. We had that disaster with the wallpaper last year... Still finding bits of it behind the sofa. Yeah, you were proper stressed, Sarah. Remember? Don’t remind me! Speaking of stress, how’s the job going, Alex? Still project coordinating? Yeah, still at it. It's alright. A bit chaotic at the moment, but that's just the way it is, isn’t it? Long hours. Thinking about looking for something a bit less… demanding. You should, mate. Life's too short. I’m alright, though. Still doing the same. Hard work, but it pays the bills. And I get to be outside, which is a bonus. Good honest work, that is. Can't knock it. Have you heard from Mark recently? I haven't seen him in ages. Last I heard he was backpacking through South America. Sent a postcard from Bolivia. Said he was loving it. Good for him. He always did have the travel bug. He's a good lad, Mark. Always up for a laugh.

Honestly, I think I'm coming down with something. My throat feels a bit scratchy. It's probably this change in air, isn’t it? Stockholm air is…crisp. Could be. Or you're just finally feeling the exhaustion from all the rushing around we've been doing. You’ve been pushing yourself, haven't you, trying to see everything. He always does. He’s like a human hummingbird. Needs constant stimulation. Honestly, Hugh, you need to build in some downtime. You’ll burn out. I’m fine, I’m fine. Just need a good night’s sleep. Though, the hotel pillows are…suboptimal. Not the fluffy cloud-like experience I was hoping for. You and your pillows. Honestly. You'd think running a successful business would have allowed you to invest in decent bedding by now. It's a principle! I refuse to be held hostage by a good pillow. It shouldn’t dictate my happiness. That’s…a take. Anyway, look at this rhododendron. The colour is incredible. So much more vibrant than the ones we see back home. They must do something special with the soil here. Or the water. It's amazing what a difference good garden management makes. Remember old Mrs. Higgins’ garden back in Dorchester? Utterly dreadful. Always complaining about slugs. Slugs are the enemy. Absolute menace. I had a war with them in my vegetable patch last summer. Lost, utterly and completely. They won the zucchini. You grow zucchini? I didn’t know you had a green thumb, Hugh. Green thumb is a generous description. More like a beige thumb that occasionally flirts with green. It's mostly about sheer stubbornness, to be honest. And copious amounts of organic slug pellets. Speaking of stubbornness, have you been remembering to use hand sanitiser? Everywhere we go. You’re notorious for touching everything. I am not! Oh yes, you are. You were stroking that statue of Carl Linnaeus like it was a beloved pet. He  was  a fascinating man. Father of taxonomy, you know. And the statue was very smooth. Smooth doesn't mean sterile. Germs don’t discriminate based on surface texture. Honestly, I’m carrying extra wipes. Here. Use them. Just do it. Alright, alright. Mother hen. Fine. But I resent the implication that I’m a walking petri dish. It’s a loving implication. Seriously though, it's good you're being careful. I’ve got a meeting with a potential client next week, can’t afford to get sick.

Honestly, the way Gran talks now, you’d never know she was born in London. It’s all… smoothed out. Like she's been practicing Received Pronunciation or something. Don't be daft, love. Lived in Kent too long, that’s all. Picks things up, you do. Though, I s’pose when you’ve spent seventy years saying things, habits are ‘ard to break. It’s funny, isn't it? I can still hear my nan’s voice clear as anything. Proper Essex. You could pinpoint Harlow just from the way she said "butter." My mum’s gone the opposite way. She tries to drop all her Chatham, you know? Thinks it sounds common. It just comes out forced. Sounds… weird. It does. Like she's trying too hard. Remember when she tried to say "schedule" and it came out "shed-yool"? Oh, that was brilliant! She went bright red. Still won’t let me live that down. Though, she had a point about Chatham accents, back in the day. Rough around the edges, some of ’em. Speaking of rough around the edges… how’s Mark doing? Still… struggling? It’s bad, honestly. He hit a new low last weekend. Apparently, there was an argument with Carol. Something about… well, everything, really. But mostly about him not looking for work. Classic. Always the same story with him. Blames everyone else, eh? Says the jobs aren't there, but he doesn't actually  try  to find them. He needs help, that lad. Real help. Not just enabling him, letting him sit around all day playing Minecraft. That’s what I told Carol. I said, “He’s thirty-five, Dad! He can’t spend his life building virtual castles!” She said he finds it… therapeutic. Therapeutic? It’s avoidance, plain and simple. And honestly, the amount of takeaways they get… it’s no wonder he’s put on so much weight. It's a health hazard. Remember when we used to cycle everywhere as kids? Up and down those hills in Chatham? Proper fitness. Now, everyone just drives everywhere. Even to the shops. We didn’t have a choice, did we? Couldn’t afford to run around in cars. Bikes were it. Good for the legs, too. I used to deliver papers on my Raleigh. Built some real stamina. I’ve been trying to convince Carol to get Mark out on a bike, but she says he’s “not the outdoorsy type.”

So, did you manage to grate all the cheese for the baked Alaska? It’s a surprisingly large amount, actually. Yeah, Mum, it’s done. My hand’s aching though. Seriously, that was a lot of cheddar. Why does a baked Alaska need  that  much cheese? Cheddar? Oh, darling. It’s not cheddar. It’s supposed to be Parmesan. You’ve grated cheddar into a baked Alaska. What?! No way. Are you sure? It smelled like cheddar. I grabbed the block from the fridge… it was yellow… Right. Well, we’ll see how it tastes. It’s probably… an interesting flavour combination. Honestly. It will be a story, at least. Remember when your aunt Mildred tried to make profiteroles and used self-raising flour? Oh god, yeah! They exploded all over the kitchen. It looked like a bomb had gone off. Exactly. This is a slightly less dramatic version of that. Anyway, are you excited about the Halloween party on Saturday? Yeah, definitely. Ben’s going as a zombie, Liam’s being a vampire. I haven’t decided yet. Maybe a werewolf? A werewolf would be good. You’d pull it off. Are you going trick-or-treating around the village, or staying local? Probably local. Old Mr. Henderson gives out full-size chocolate bars, so that’s always a good start. Plus, it’s safer. There were stories last year about some older kids being a bit… rough with the younger ones. It’s a shame that happens. People can be so unkind. It reminds me of something that happened when I was recruiting for the graduate scheme at work… Oh, here we go. A work story. It’s relevant! I promise. We had two extremely qualified candidates, both really bright. But one was… significantly older than the others. And you could tell the other interviewers were subtly, but definitely, biased against him. Treating him differently, asking different questions. It was awful. That’s… not fair. No, it wasn’t. I had to pull them up on it, of course. But it just highlights how ingrained some attitudes are. Even when you think people are being progressive… It’s weird thinking about age, though. Like, how old is too old for… I don’t know… stuff? Oh, that's a very complicated question, darling. It depends on the "stuff" doesn't it. There are legal age limits for certain things, of course.

This coffee is absolutely lovely, you’ve got a good machine here. Much better than my instant, I confess. Oh, glad you like it! It was a bit of an investment, but worth it, I think. Helps get me going in the mornings, especially with marking looming. Are you alright for toast? There’s jam, marmalade… Marmalade’s perfect, thank you. So, New York! You must tell me everything. I saw a tiny snippet on Instagram, of that amazing rooftop bar, but that doesn’t do it justice, does it? Doesn’t even come close. Honestly, it felt like being  in  a film set. Everything’s just…bigger, bolder. The energy is incredible. We walked miles and miles, saw a show, ate far too much pizza… it was brilliant. I’m still exhausted, though. Sounds exhausting and exhilarating all at once. You’ve always been a bit of a city person, haven’t you? I’m more hills and dales, personally. Though, I must admit, I did feel a pang of… something, seeing all those skyscrapers. So, what’s the plan for today? I was thinking a walk along the beach? The tide’s supposed to be out this afternoon. Or we could potter around Mumbles? Oh, the beach sounds lovely. I haven’t had a proper seaside walk in ages. That’d be perfect. And then maybe a pub lunch? Absolutely. There’s a good one in Mumbles, overlooks the sea. We could do both, have a wander around the village afterwards. Unless you fancy something more…adventurous? Remember that conversation about flying lessons? Don’t even  start  on the flying lessons. It’s a mid-life crisis, pure and simple. Though, thinking about it... the view would be spectacular. No, no, let's stick to solid ground, thank you very much. Fair enough! Though honestly, after living in Japan for so long, I'm always up for trying new things. It changes your perspective, doesn't it? Everything feels…possible. It does. That’s what I loved about hearing you talk about it when we first met. It's funny, isn't it, how a place can do that to you. Though I remember when we first met, you were complaining about the tiny apartments and the constant politeness. Oh, I was. It took some getting used to! The politeness is lovely, truly, but sometimes you just want someone to be brutally honest!

Right, okay, my go. Ugh, seriously? Another vowel. This is hopeless. You’re just moaning, Leo. You’ve got loads of consonants. Play ‘quixotic’! ‘Quixotic’? Are you kidding me? That’s a triple word score waiting to happen, and you've been holding onto a Q all game! That's just… tactical villainy. Tactical brilliance, more like. Honestly, you lot are terrible at Scrabble. I used to crush my nan at this. She’d call it ‘word wizardry’. Your nan sounds intense, Ben. She  was  intense. She'd look up the origins of words just to make sure she was using them correctly. Once, she spent an hour arguing with my uncle about whether ‘literally’ could be used figuratively. Oh god, that sounds like a family gathering at my aunt’s. Someone  always  brings up the correct usage of words. Speaking of origins, I was reading about the word ‘scab’ the other day. Apparently, it comes from Old Norse, meaning a crust or a flake. Lovely imagery. Helps with the Scrabble, doesn’t it? Right, well, I need to use this ‘z’. Anyone got a word that needs a ‘z’? ‘Zebra’ feels… underwhelming. You could try ‘zizz’. It means to buzz or hum, apparently. I learned that from a children’s book, actually. A really weird one, about a bumblebee detective. A bumblebee detective? What did that involve? Sting-based interrogations? Something like that. It was wonderfully bizarre. Actually, thinking about kids’ books, remember those pop-up books? The ones with the incredibly intricate paper engineering? Yeah! The ones you were terrified to touch in case you broke them? Worth a fortune now, probably. More valuable than my student loan, I reckon. I’m still paying that off. Though, honestly, A-levels felt like a bigger scam. All that work for what… to pick a university course? Tell me about it. I’m seriously questioning my life choices right now. This Masters is… intense. I feel like I haven't slept properly in months. You need to come with me to the Chelsea Flower Show next weekend. Fresh air, floral displays, escaping academic doom. Oh, that actually sounds… idyllic. Is Ben coming? Because I need a witness if I start openly weeping at a particularly beautiful rose bush. I might be busy, prepping for a new menu at work. Trying to avoid anything involving Brussels sprouts. Apparently, they're ‘trendy’ now, which is a tragedy.

Right then, finished that crossword, didn’t I? Took me a good hour. And still one clue I can’t get. “Ancient mariner,” six letters. Any ideas? Oh, those are tricky. Is it…Sinbad? No, tried that. Doesn’t fit the crossers. It’s got to be a proper name, I reckon. Someone famous. Well, not much help, am I? I’m no good at crosswords. Always preferred a good jigsaw puzzle. More…visual, you know. Aye, you always did. Remember that massive one we did of that cathedral? Took us weeks! Oh, the one with all those tiny little stones? Nearly drove me mad, that one. But it was satisfying when it was finished, wasn't it? Felt like a real achievement. It was. Though my back ached for a week afterwards, bending over the table. Getting too old for these things, I suppose. Nonsense. You’re not  that  old. Just…experienced. Experienced at aching joints, you mean. Still, beats doing nothing. What have  you  been up to? Besides avoiding the crossword, of course. Just a bit of tidying mostly. Went through some old photographs. Found some lovely ones of the grandchildren. Little Emily's got her front teeth through at last. Looks like a little shark! Ha! She’s a clever one, that Emily. Always was. Reminds me a bit of you, when you were little. Always getting into mischief. Oh, I was a terror! My mother had her hands full with me, let me tell you. Always climbing trees, or disappearing into the neighbour’s garden. And always with a story ready to explain it all away. You were a silver-tongued devil, you were. Well, a girl’s gotta survive, doesn’t she? Though I don’t think I’ve got the energy for all that running about these days. A nice cup of tea and a bit of peace and quiet is more my style now. Me too. Though I still find myself pacing around, looking for something to do. Feels odd, being retired. After all those years of work. It does, doesn’t it? But it’s a good odd, I think. A chance to just…be. No deadlines, no bosses, no worries. Just us. And a particularly stubborn crossword clue. True enough. Still, “ancient mariner”...six letters… it’s driving me round the bend. Perhaps I'll just leave it for now. Have a biscuit.

Honestly, this is lovely. Just what I needed after all that driving. Your roast chicken is always spot on, isn’t it? Thanks, Dad. It's just a simple recipe, really. Good quality chicken makes all the difference, I think. And a generous helping of herbs. Mum, did you enjoy it? Absolutely delicious, dear. Lovely and moist. Though, I do wish I’d managed to get some decent parsnips. Everything in the shops seemed a bit… sad. Parsnips  are  tricky. You need to get them just right. Not too woody, not too bendy. It’s a skill. Speaking of skills, have either of you tried that new app, ‘FitFusion’? My neighbour, Brenda, was raving about it. Says it’s revolutionised her fitness routine. Ooh, no, I haven’t. What kind of thing is it? Is it one of those intense, bootcamp-style ones? I’m trying to get back into a bit of exercise, but I’m not sure I’m up for anything  too  strenuous yet. Apparently not. Brenda said it’s quite adaptable. You can choose different levels and types of workouts. Yoga, Pilates, even just walking programmes. It tracks your progress and everything. She’s lost a stone, she claims. Though Brenda always claims things. Sounds good. I might have a look. I’ve been meaning to do more walking, especially now the weather's been…reasonable. Did you hear they’re finally opening the new train station at Crediton? Oh, really? I thought that was a lost cause! It’s been delayed for  years . I remember when they first announced it. What, ten years ago? At least! Everyone was so hopeful. Then it just… stalled. Apparently, there were issues with the land acquisition and then something about archaeological finds. Honestly, you’d think they’d known there’d be something under there. It's Devon! It’s always something in Devon. Though it will be a huge benefit when it’s finally up and running. It'll make getting to Exeter so much easier. No more battling the A379. Absolutely. I’ve missed so many meetings because of traffic on that road. It's ridiculous. Though, knowing our luck, it’ll be chaos for the first month while everyone figures it out. Probably. Still, it's progress. Speaking of progress, anyone fancy another helping of potatoes? These are particularly good, even if we did struggle to find parsnips.

Honestly, that burger was…substantial. I’m genuinely worried I’ve entered a food coma. Tell me about it. I think I saw my life flash before my eyes halfway through that second patty. Worth it though, right? Best burger I’ve had in ages. Absolutely. Though, I'm starting to regret saying yes to the extra fries. I’m gonna be dreaming of potatoes tonight. Did you catch that new Marvel film then? Everyone’s raving about it. Yeah, went last night actually. It was alright. Bit… predictable, I thought. Good effects, obviously, but the plot felt a bit recycled. I’m more hyped for the next Dune film, to be honest. That first one was incredible. Dune’s good. Real epic scale. I’ve been mostly getting my kicks from gaming lately. Been properly hooked on that new RPG. What about you? Anything keeping you entertained besides near-death experiences via burgers? Been trying to finish that book my mum sent me. It’s… intense. Psychological thriller. ‘The Lie’ or something. Really messes with your head. Keeps suggesting things without actually  saying  them. Ooh, sounds good. I struggle to concentrate on reading sometimes. My attention span is practically nonexistent. Speaking of nonexistent, have you been following the football lately? Arsenal are looking… shaky. Honestly, it's painful. They had a good run, but it feels like it's all falling apart again. I’m a proper Spurs fan, so I'm secretly enjoying their suffering. Don't tell anyone I said that. Haha, your secret’s safe with me. Although, my cousin’s a die-hard Arsenal supporter, so I might be getting an earful later. He’s already started planning his mate’s stag do, and apparently, it’s going to be… ambitious. Ambitious how? Paintballing and a pub crawl ambitious, or full-blown recreating a medieval siege ambitious? Somewhere in between, I think. Prague. Apparently, there's a whole scene there for stag dos. He's determined to make it… memorable. I'm bracing myself for the photos. Prague sounds… intense. You’ll need earplugs. Uni stuff, how are seminars going? Still struggling with that Shakespeare module? Still struggling, yeah. That professor is brilliant, but he expects us to unravel centuries of literary analysis in an hour. I'm pretty sure he’s secretly a wizard. I saw that they were doing Hamlet on the telly last night.

Honestly, this cake is amazing. You  have  to try it. It’s lemon and poppyseed, but like, a really good lemon and poppyseed. Ooh, go on then.  takes a bite  Oh, wow. You weren’t kidding. So good! It’s been ages since I've been to Greens, it's nice to be back. Cambridge is… different. Different how? Still enjoying Pearson? It sounds pretty intense. It's good, genuinely. Challenging, but good. It’s just… everyone’s so focused on, like, climbing the ladder. It’s all very “where do you see yourself in five years?” and I'm just trying to figure out what I’m having for dinner. And Cambridge itself… it's just very… polished. Everyone seems to have been to Eton or something. You know? Oh, I can imagine. It’s a bit of a world away from Cambourne, isn’t it? Speaking of worlds away, how’s…Mark? Still causing chaos? Oh god, don’t even. He messaged me last week, trying to be all apologetic. Apparently, his mum’s been giving him grief about how he treated me. Can you believe it?  His mum ! Like she suddenly has a moral compass. Men. Seriously. Good on her though, at least someone’s holding him accountable. It's been nearly a year now, hasn't it? Are you properly over him? I think so. I mean, I still cringe if I think about certain things, but generally, yeah. I’m fine. Honestly, I’m more annoyed at myself for wasting so long on him. What about you? Any dating disasters lately? Ha! You know me. More like dating non-starters. I went on one date with this guy, Ben, who spent the entire evening listing his achievements. Like, I get it, you got a first in history. Good for you. But maybe try asking me about  my  life? Ugh, the worst. It’s like they think a monologue is a date. Exactly! Anyway, enough about terrible men. How’s your mum doing? She was feeling a bit rough last time we spoke. She’s okay, thankfully. Just a bit of a cold. She’s driving me mad though, constantly asking when I’m going to settle down and buy a house. I’m 26! Mine's the same! Although she’s more concerned with whether I’m eating enough vegetables. It’s like I’m five again.

Right, so I was on the phone to Mam earlier, and you will  not  believe what she's done now. Honestly, the woman is a menace. Oh dear. Let me guess… involved a garden gnome and a questionable life choice? Close! It wasn’t a gnome this time, it was her prize-winning hydrangeas. She decided they were looking “a bit peaky” and gave them… wait for it… fizzy juice. Fizzy juice? As in… Irn-Bru? Worse. Tango Orange. Said the sugar would give them a boost. I nearly choked. I tried to explain about pH levels and root rot, but she just said I was “overthinking things”. Oh, your Mam. She's a force of nature. Reminds me of my nan trying to cure aphids with washing up liquid. Didn’t end well. Exactly! They reckon they know best, don't they? Anyway, she’s convinced they’re already looking perkier. I’m half expecting them to start glowing orange. Speaking of plants, how’s your basil doing? Mine is…struggling. The basil’s actually thriving. I think the key is to just ignore it mostly. I water it occasionally and sing to it slightly off-key, and it seems happy enough. Sing to it? You're kidding. No, honestly. It's scientifically proven that plants respond to sound vibrations. Okay, maybe not scientifically proven, but it can't hurt. Plus, it makes me feel less pathetic talking to a plant. Fair enough. I might have to try that. Mine just looks permanently dejected. I think I’m actively stressing it out with my constant worrying. It happens. Plants are sensitive creatures. Right, tea’s almost brewed. Are you still attempting that Moroccan tagine recipe for Saturday? I am, bravely. Found a slightly less intimidating recipe online. It still has about fourteen different spices, but at least it doesn’t require me to trek across Cambridge for saffron. Good shout. Saffron is extortionate. And remember what happened last time you tried a complex recipe? The smoke alarm and the neighbours asking if everything was alright. Don’t remind me. Honestly, I think I’m better at simple things. Like toast. Though even that's a risk sometimes. You're not terrible. You just...enthusiastically experiment. It's endearing. Nearly ready? I’ve got the biscuits. Digestives, naturally. Perfect. You know me too well. And if the tagine ends up being a disaster, we’re ordering a takeaway.

Right dreadful weekend absolutely dreadful. Oh? What happened? Did the plumbing finally give up the ghost? You were muttering about it last week. Worse than the plumbing, Gareth. Much worse. My daughter decided to show me photos… photographs of all the offspring of modern footballers. Honestly, you wouldn’t believe the… the  outfits . Sequins, Gareth. Sequins on seven-year-olds. Oh, the perils of celebrity offspring. Keeps the paparazzi busy, I suppose. My weekend was… quiet. Very quiet. Marked essays. Seems the students haven’t grasped the concept of referencing. Again. The referencing! Don't even get me started. It's like pulling teeth. They copy and paste, then think they can just change a word or two and it'll be alright. It infuriates me. Reminds me of a student years ago who tried to pass off a passage from Dickens as his own. Dickens! Bold. Very bold. Did you catch any of the snooker on? O’Sullivan’s looking good, isn’t he? Still. Yes, yes he is. Remarkable, really. To maintain that level of concentration and skill after all these years. Though truthfully, I find it rather soporific. Puts me right to sleep. I prefer a bit more… action. Though not football, definitely not football. Fair enough. I’ve been trying to get my garden sorted. The rain hasn’t helped, obviously. It’s turned the whole thing into a bog. Trying to get some roses going, but the black spot is a nightmare. Any gardening tips from the Cairo-born professor? My gardening experience is limited to supervising the groundskeepers at my father’s estate. Though I did learn that a bit of strategic bribery with baklava goes a long way. Black spot though… that requires a specialist. Seriously, Gareth, you need to consult a horticultural expert. I might. Though my budget is more suited to a packet of weed killer and a prayer. Speaking of challenges, you heard about young Rhys from Tredegar? Tried to join the police force. Apparently, his eyesight wasn’t up to scratch. Ah, no. What happened? Failed the test. Then tried the army. Same problem. Turns out he’s severely short-sighted, always has been. His mother’s furious. Keeps saying they should have picked it up in school. These entry requirements are becoming increasingly stringent, aren’t they? Higher standards, more tests… It's a different world now to when I was applying for academic positions.

Right, so, the bunting… I’ve ordered the bunting, it should be here tomorrow. Pink and gold, obviously. Can it have sparkles on? Please can it have sparkles? Darling, everything has to have sparkles with you, doesn't it? I think it’s got a bit of shimmer, which is close enough. It’s got little flags, and everything. Your cousin Maisie's helping me put it up. Oh good. I'm still trying to figure out how I'm getting back up here on Saturday after my shift. The trains are a nightmare, especially weekends. Oh, well we can pick you up from the station, obviously. No problem at all. Don't worry about a thing. I’ve already asked your Dad to check the car’s ready. That’d be amazing, thanks Mum. Honestly, it saves so much hassle. I just… I really want to be there for the christening. It feels weird missing out on all of this. Will you bring your purple glitter? The really sparkly one? Maybe! If I can fit it in my bag. I'm not promising anything. Is Uncle Paul coming? Yes, he and Carol are already booked into the Premier Inn. They said they wouldn’t miss it for the world. He booked it weeks ago. He’s very excited, he keeps ringing asking about the cake. I want a chocolate cake! With pink icing and sprinkles! And a fairy on top! We’ve got a chocolate cake, darling, with pink icing, and  lots  of sprinkles. And a little sugar fairy. It’s from that bakery in Tamworth, the one we always use. Remember? Ooooh, yeah! The one that makes the really yummy biscuits too! That's the one. Now, about your birthday… have you given any more thought to what you want to do?
