I was thinking maybe we could go to that escape room in Birmingham? The one everyone’s talking about? Oh, that sounds good! Is… is that something your little sister would enjoy too? Probably not, she's a bit young. But she'd happily stay with Grandma and Grandad. She loves spending time with them. We could make it a proper sisters’ day out, just me and you. That sounds lovely. We can look at booking it. Your Dad’s been complaining about needing a new shed, though. Perhaps we could squeeze in a trip to B&Q as well?

Honestly, this weather is dreadful, isn’t it? Rain, rain, rain. Makes you want to just hibernate. Tell me about it! I had to cycle to work this morning, and I was soaked through before I even got there. My hair was completely ruined. You looked like a wet dog, Auntie Chloe! Very funny, Lily! Well, it wasn’t funny at the time. It’s just…everything’s a bit damp and grey. I’m already dreaming of sunshine. Me too. Speaking of dreaming, has any progress been made on the New York plans? Are we actually getting anywhere with finding flights? I’ve been looking, Mum. It’s…expensive. Shockingly expensive. Especially around Christmas. I’ve found a few options with stopovers, which would bring the price down, but they add so much travel time. Hmm. Stopovers aren’t ideal, but maybe we have to consider them. Lily would be exhausted. Wouldn’t you, sweetheart? I don’t mind a stopover, as long as there’s a park! With swings! See? A park will solve everything. I’ll keep looking. I’m thinking maybe early December, before the real Christmas rush hits. That sounds good. It'd be lovely to see New York all decorated for the holidays. Remember Uncle David and I went for our honeymoon? It was…different then. Much quieter, less touristy. I’ve seen the pictures! You looked so happy. And the outfits…classic 90s! Oh, don’t remind me! Big hair and shoulder pads. We thought we were so stylish. What’s shoulder pads? Are they like bouncy castles? No, darling. They're…well, they were put inside clothes to make your shoulders look bigger. It was a fashion thing. A  very  questionable fashion thing. How’s work going, Chloe? Still dealing with constant complaints? Oh, you know. The usual. Someone complained today that the biscuits weren’t fresh enough. Biscuits! Honestly, people. I swear, sometimes I think I should just become a hermit. They’re lucky to have you, honestly. You always go above and beyond. Maybe. It's just draining. I'm thinking of applying for that assistant manager position that opened up at the other store. More money, less biscuit-related drama hopefully. That sounds sensible. Do it! You deserve a bit of peace and quiet. And what are we doing this weekend? Anything exciting planned? I thought we could take Lily to Drayton Manor.

Right, so this… this is the initial proposal, yeah? For the dissertation. Professor Davies wanted it by Friday, which was a bit ambitious considering, but here we are. Ambitious is an understatement. Looks… comprehensive. What's the core argument again? Just trying to get my head around it all. Okay, so basically, I'm arguing that the perceived decline in regional dialects post-industrialisation isn’t necessarily a  loss  of linguistic diversity, but a reconfiguration of it. Like, it’s not disappearing, it’s just… morphing into something else, influenced by increased mobility and digital communication. Right, so not a dilution, but a… remix? Exactly! A remix. I’m avoiding ‘fusion’ because that implies a harmonious blending, and I don't think that's what’s happening. It's more chaotic and uneven. This section here – the bit with all the footnotes – is where I lay out the theoretical framework. I’m drawing on Bourdieu, obviously, but also some work by Labov about the social stratification of language. Bourdieu, naturally. Sounds… heavy. It is. But it needs to be. Davies is a stickler for theory. Then this part, which is already getting way too long, is the detailed methodology. I'm planning on doing a corpus analysis of online forum posts from around Lancashire, and then some interviews with people who’ve moved away from the area over the past decade. Online forums? That’s… a choice. Won't everything be riddled with intentional misspellings and slang? Yeah, that's the challenge. I’m going to have to develop a pretty rigorous coding scheme to filter out the intentional noise. And then the interviews will hopefully give me some qualitative data to back up the quantitative findings. I’m hoping to find evidence of linguistic features being retained or adapted even when people aren't physically in the region. Smart. So you’re looking for subtle indicators… like pronunciations slipping into standard English, or new slang being adopted from elsewhere? Precisely. It's about tracing the patterns of change. And this, the bit on the pink paper, is a preliminary literature review. I realised I needed to include a section on digital dialects, like leetspeak and internet meme language. It’s relevant, even if it’s a bit tangential. That’s good thinking. It shows you've considered the broader context. Honestly, it looks like you've pretty much got it nailed.

…and then I was trying to build a Lego castle, but all the pieces kept turning into slugs. Like, really slimy slugs. It was awful. Oh, that's brilliantly bizarre. Classic dream logic. I had one last night where I was giving a geography lesson… to a class full of cats. Cats?! I know, right? And they were  very  unimpressed with my explanation of plate tectonics. Just blinking at me and grooming themselves. Did they hiss? Cats hiss. I think cats are quite good at geography…they always seem to know where the sunbeam is. True. And they're masters of navigating a house. Though, speaking of navigating… yours sounds less stressful than mine. Slugs are marginally less judgemental than feline students. I dreamt I was flying! And I had sparkly wings! Ooh, lovely! Did you fly over Comberton? Yes! And over Grandma’s house! I waved! I dreamt I had a dog. A really big, fluffy one. Oh, you still want a dog, don't you? Yes! A golden retriever! Or a Labrador! We've talked about this, haven’t we? It's a big commitment. Especially with both of us working. And thinking about how much time we spend away… it wouldn’t be fair to a dog, really. But it would be  so  fun! We could take it to Grantchester meadows! It would be lovely. But it’s a lot of responsibility. Maybe when we have a bit more space… Or win the lottery. Now  there's  a dream. Imagine. Big house, massive garden, a dog for each of you… and a full-time Lego castle builder. And a bouncy castle! And a swimming pool! With a slide! And I wouldn’t have to worry about slimy Lego slugs anymore. Honestly, that was really disturbing. I woke up feeling quite…viscous. You’re a weirdo. But a lovely weirdo. Have you actually checked your lottery ticket, by the way? Oh, blimey, I forgot! It's still on the fridge. Hang on… Nope. No millionaire-making numbers, unfortunately. Just a free lucky dip next week. Aww. Maybe next time! We could buy loads of dog biscuits! That’s the spirit. Even without winning millions, a dog biscuit fund is a worthy cause. Though, maybe we stick to dreaming about the dog for now. And the geography-loving cats, obviously. And keeping the Lego slugs at bay. Definitely keeping the slugs at bay.

Honestly, the state of A&E these days is just… something else. You went again? What happened this time? Not  me  this time, thankfully. It was Gran. She tripped over the rug in the living room, proper went flying. Oh no, is she alright? Yeah, she’s okay now. They think it’s just a sprained wrist, but she was absolutely convinced she’d broken it. She was screaming the place down, apparently. Mum said it was mortifying. Poor Gran. She does have a habit of going for spectacular falls, doesn’t she? Remember that time she tried to get the cat off the curtains? Oh god, don't remind me! That was a disaster. Anyway, Mum took her to A&E and said it took  hours  to even be seen. She said the waiting room was packed, mostly people with things that definitely didn’t need A&E. It’s always like that, isn’t it? Everyone and their dog goes to A&E for a sniffle. Exactly! Mum said there was a lad there with a splinter, a  splinter ! And a woman who’d stubbed her toe. Seriously? Seriously. And then someone started arguing with the security guard because they were annoyed they had to wait. It was chaos. Mum said she nearly walked out. It’s ridiculous. They need to do something about it. Maybe triage things better, or redirect people to pharmacies or GPs. You’d think so. Apparently, they were seriously understaffed too. The doctor who eventually saw Gran was lovely, but she said they were completely swamped. That’s just a systemic issue, isn’t it? The NHS is constantly stretched. It is. And it’s scary, you know? What if it  was  something serious? What if someone needed urgent care and had to wait hours because of all the non-emergency cases? I know. It makes you think. Remember when I dislocated my shoulder playing football a couple of years ago? I was lucky to get seen quickly, but even then, the wait was pretty long. Oh yeah, that looked proper painful. Did they manage to pop it back in properly? Eventually, yeah. It took a couple of attempts though. The doctor said I was particularly… uncooperative. You? Uncooperative? Never! Hey, I was in a lot of pain, alright? And I was worried they were going to make it worse. It’s not exactly a pleasant experience, having your shoulder yanked around.

…and then young Timmy, bless him, asked if Putin was a wizard. A  wizard , Nigel! Honestly, the things they come up with. Had to explain international politics to a class of ten-year-olds. Felt like I needed a drink afterward. Good grief. A wizard, eh? They get it from somewhere, those ideas. Probably one of those TikTok things. Still, better a wizard than thinking he’s some sort of heroic figure, I suppose. Speaking of needing a drink… fancy another cuppa, or shall I raid the biscuit tin and we have something a bit stronger? A bit stronger sounds rather appealing, actually. This news is getting to me. The situation in Ukraine… it feels like it’s just grinding on and on. And now this business with the protests in France. It’s all a bit much. Tell me about it. Makes you feel helpless, doesn't it? I was reading an article this morning about the economic impact… supposedly it’s going to knock a good percentage off global growth. Not good for anyone, is it? Especially not for small businesses. Precisely. Which reminds me, how’s the antique shop doing? Still keeping busy? Busy enough. It’s… patchy, to be honest. People are tightening their belts, you see. Less spending on ‘luxuries’ like antique furniture. I’ve been thinking, though, about diversifying a bit. I’ve had an idea kicking around for a while now. Oh? Do tell. You always have a trick up your sleeve, Nigel. Well, I was talking to old Mrs. Henderson the other day – you remember her, always popping in for a chat and a browse - and she mentioned she’s struggling to find somewhere reliable to get her silver polished. Said she’s tried a few places, but they’ve either done a shoddy job or overcharged her. And…? And it got me thinking. We’ve got the space in the back room, it wouldn’t cost much to get the right equipment, and there’s clearly a demand for it. Silver polishing and repair. A niche market, I reckon. "Nigel’s Notions & Polished Silver," perhaps? "Nigel's Notions"! That's rather good. A bit alliterative, mind you. But a solid idea, Nigel, a very solid idea. It’s sensible. You’ve always been good with your hands. And Mrs. Henderson is a good barometer of local demand – she knows  everyone . Exactly my thinking.

Right, so are we thinking pizza tonight? Or should we try and be a bit more… grown up and do something with vegetables? Pizza sounds excellent. Honestly, after that day, I need carbohydrates. A full-on, cheesy, carbohydrate hit. You had a rough one, then? You have no idea. Spreadsheet hell, mostly. And Brenda decided today was the day to “restructure” her filing system. It involved a lot of passive-aggressive sighing and moving things into labelled boxes. Oh, Brenda. Still at it, then? Eternally. Speaking of things that are eternally frustrating, have you started the new series of  Happy Valley ? Not yet! I’m saving it for a proper weekend binge. Is it good? Good isn’t the word. It’s… intense. Sarah Lancashire is just phenomenal. Although, honestly, the scenery is pretty bleak. Makes Yorkshire look a lot less appealing. This place is pretty bleak, actually. Although, in a kind of… charmingly gritty way. Look at those stained-glass windows. Bit random for a pub in Woolwich, isn’t it? Maybe it used to be something else? A church, perhaps. Or a particularly grand waiting room for the ferries. Probably. It's got that vibe. You know, reminds me a bit of the student union bar at university. Oh god. The student union. Memories. Mostly of sticky floors and questionable music choices. What was your uni like, anyway? I never really got the full story. It was… overwhelming. A lot of very loud people with strong opinions. I mostly hid in the library. And the art shop. It’s how I ended up doing English, really. Anything to avoid proper science. Sensible. I did economics, which was basically just a glorified numbers game. I still shudder when I think about econometrics. Cold? You didn't bring your coat, did you? No, I thought it would be warmer. Looks like I underestimated the Woolwich chill. Here, use mine. It’s a bit big, but it’ll keep you warm. Thanks. What are they playing now? Sounds like… 80s synth-pop? I think so. Actually, it’s not too bad. It’s better than some of the stuff they had on in the student union. Remember that awful night they only played sea shanties? Oh my god, yes! I’d completely forgotten about that. That was a special kind of torture. Speaking of torture, have you seen Winston lately? He’s been shedding like crazy.

Aye, honestly, the light in Skye was just… unreal. I’ve never seen anything like it. Completely different to down here, even. Oh, absolutely. I was up in Lewis and Harris last year, doing a bit of coastal walking, and the light there is otherworldly. It changes every five minutes. Good for photography, obviously, but also just… stunning to  be  in. Stunning is the word. I was trying to get this shot of the Old Man of Storr, you know, with the mist rolling in. Spent ages waiting for the right moment, freezing my bahookies off. Sounds about right. Scotland and photography often involve significant discomfort. Did you get it, though? The shot? I think so. It’s alright. I’m still learning, you know? I’ve been messing about with long exposures lately, trying to get that silky smooth water effect. It's a pain, though. You need a tripod, filters… the whole shebang. Aye, it can be a bit of a kit obsession, can't it? I went through a phase of convinced I needed every lens under the sun. Realised pretty quickly I was just carrying a lot of expensive weight around! I mostly stick to prime lenses now. Simpler. Prime lenses, aye? I’ve been meaning to look into those. I’ve got a zoom, which is handy, but it’s not… sharp, is it? Not compared to a good prime, no. They force you to move your feet, though. No zooming in from the comfort of your spot. Makes you think more about composition. That’s true. I tend to be a lazy photographer, to be honest. Stand there and just click away, hoping for the best. We all do it! You were saying Skye was cold, though? Was it raining much? Honestly, it was a miracle it wasn’t. We had one shower, just a quick one, and then the sun came out blazing. But the wind… the wind was brutal. Nearly blew me off the cliffs a couple of times. I’m surprised the camera survived. Aye, the wind can be a killer. That’s why I always pack a waterproof cover for my gear, even if the forecast looks good. You never know. Good shout. I’ll have to remember that. I'm thinking about heading to Iceland next year, to try and catch the Northern Lights. Iceland! Now  that  sounds incredible. The landscape there is insane.

Right, so, nursery's confirmed for little Leo three mornings a week, starting next Monday. I've double-checked everything, packed the bag… honestly, it feels so weird! He’s actually going to be… somewhere without me for more than an hour. Oh, darling, you’ll be fine. He’ll be fine. It's good for him, gets him socialising. And it’ll give  you  a bit of breathing space. Are you dreading the drop-off? A little bit, yeah. I keep imagining him clinging to my leg, screaming the place down. Mrs. Davies at the nursery said they're brilliant with settling children in, but… still. What about you? Any plans this week? Anything exciting happening in Birmingham? Not particularly exciting, no. Same old, same old. I’m meeting Brenda for lunch on Wednesday, just a quick catch-up. She's been doing that pottery class and is convinced she’s a natural. You know how she is! And I need to get to the garden centre, the roses are looking a bit sorry for themselves. Oh, Brenda and her pottery! She  does  get obsessed, doesn’t she? Mum, could you maybe pop over on Thursday evening? I’d love you to meet Leo’s key worker, just for a chat, and maybe have a little play with him before he starts. It would really put my mind at ease. Of course, love. Thursday evening is perfect. What time? And what’s this key worker like? Is she nice? You know I'm a sucker for a good childcare professional. 6:30ish? And yeah, she seems really lovely on the phone. Very calm and reassuring. Apparently, she has loads of experience with separation anxiety. Which is exactly what I’m dreading! Honestly, it’s silly, isn’t it? I know he’ll be okay, I just feel… a bit redundant all of a sudden. Not redundant, darling. Just transitioning. You’ve done an amazing job looking after him full-time these last few years. It's natural to feel a bit strange about it changing. It’s a big milestone for both of you. True. I just feel like I haven’t had much time to myself lately. I was thinking of trying to watch that new drama everyone's talking about, ‘The Crimson Tide’ or something? Have you heard of it? Oh, yes! I've seen a few clips online.

This pasta’s lovely, honestly. You’ve outdone yourself, Anon. Cheers. It’s just a jar sauce, really. Though I did add a bit of chilli flakes. Gives it a kick. Definitely. A good kick. So, how’s the conference planning going, El? Still dealing with demanding speakers? Oh, you have  no  idea. This one professor, Dr. Ainsworth, keeps emailing me at like, eleven at night, demanding a specific brand of bottled water. Bottled water! Like, it’s Cambridge, it’s not the Sahara. Blimey. Sounds right posh. What did you say? I politely explained that we stock several varieties of bottled water and that he’d be perfectly able to choose one upon arrival. He hasn't replied. Probably composing another strongly worded email as we speak. You handled that well. You can’t give in to that sort of thing. You’ll just encourage it. How’s…Ben? Still being a bit distant? Ugh, don’t even. It’s been awful. He said he “needs space” again last night. I’m starting to feel like a houseplant he’s occasionally remembered to water. Space, eh? That's a classic. Honestly, that’s just a polite way of saying he's not sure. Have you asked him directly what’s going on? A million times! He just clams up. Says everything’s “fine” and then avoids eye contact for the rest of the evening. I told him if he can't be honest with me, I can’t keep doing this. Harsh, but fair. You deserve better than being left hanging. Exactly. You’re amazing, El. He’s lucky to have you. What about you, Finn? Still grafting away on building sites? Yeah, pretty much. It's cold, though, and the boss man is riding everyone's backs about getting the new estate finished. He keeps saying we’re behind schedule, but it's because half the materials haven't even arrived yet! That sounds stressful. You should unionise! I thought about it. But... well, you know. Gotta pay the bills. Plus, I need the money for clothes. Clothes? What’s wrong with your clothes? You always look perfectly presentable. Presentable for a building site, maybe. But Maya keeps going on about needing to get me “decent” clothes for meeting her parents next week. Apparently, jeans and a t-shirt are not cutting it. Oh dear. That’s…a challenge. Maya’s parents sound…particular.

Right then, who wants another cuppa? I’ve just made a fresh pot. Earl Grey, it is. Oh, go on then, Arthur. That  would  be lovely. Mine’s gone a bit cold now, actually. Been chatting so much. I’m alright for the moment, thank you. Though, I must say, this is a proper brew. Not like some of the…  disappointments  one gets offered these days. Oh, don’t get Malcolm started on the state of modern tea-making! He’s a purist, our Malcolm. Remembers a time when teabags were considered a scandalous shortcut. Not a bad shortcut, mind! Saves a lot of mess. Though, I do appreciate a good loose leaf, I will admit. Especially a nice Darjeeling. Expensive stuff, that is. I always thought you were a builder’s tea man, Arthur. Strong, with a good dollop of milk. Oh, I can manage a builder’s now and then, Maisie. When I'm feeling particularly… robust. But my tastes have refined with age, you see. A bit like a fine wine, I suppose. Though not quite as pricey! Refining tastes, eh? I always said a good Yorkshire Tea was the benchmark. Sturdy, reliable. Gets the job done. Doesn't mess about with fancy flavours. It’s all a matter of preference, isn't it? I’m a bit partial to a fruit tea myself. Raspberry and hibiscus is my current favourite. Fruit tea? That's… well, that’s not  tea  is it? That's coloured water! Only joking, Doreen, only joking. Oh, Arthur, you are a card. Though I have to say, I do agree with Malcolm. Proper tea needs to be, well, proper. None of this flowery stuff. It’s the tannins, you see. The tannins are what give it the… character. The bite. Fruit tea lacks that crucial bite. You're all so traditional! It’s good to experiment a little. Though, I do appreciate a good cup of Earl Grey, Arthur. Very civilized. Civilized, that's right! That’s what it is. Here you go, Maisie. Careful, it's hot. Now, is that enough milk for you? I always err on the side of caution. Perfect, thank you. You know me well, Arthur. Absolutely perfect. This is lovely. Just what I needed. You know, speaking of beverages, I tried that new ginger beer the other day. Quite potent stuff. Nearly blew my head off. Oh, I’ve heard of that one!

Honestly though, this roast is amazing, Mum. You’ve outdone yourself. Oh, it’s nothing, love. Just a bit of practice, that’s all. Remember when I first started doing roasts? They were…an experience. I vaguely recall a rather dry chicken, wasn’t there? And a lot of gravy attempting to compensate. You’re being kind. It was like eating sawdust coated in brown sauce. Speaking of experiences, anyone fancy venturing out to The Ship later? Apparently, they’ve got a new band on tonight. Oh, I don’t know. It’s a bit of a trek, isn’t it? And I’m feeling a bit knackered after the shopping this morning. We could get a taxi? It wouldn't be too expensive, and it’s ages since we’ve all been out. I’m in! I need a proper pint. Been stuck with soft drinks all week, prepping for that CRB check for the new job. It’s relentless. A CRB check for customer services? Isn't that a bit…much? Apparently so. Something about safeguarding vulnerable adults. It’s a lot to go through for just talking to people on the phone, if you ask me. It's the world we live in, sadly. Everything’s a risk now. Did you see that protest in London on the news? Absolute chaos. Oh, the one about the…circumcision ban? Awful. I can't believe people are getting so worked up about it. It’s a deeply personal decision for families. It’s all just political point-scoring, isn’t it? Stirring up division. Speaking of division, anyone else think the prices of petrol are ridiculous? I nearly had a heart attack filling up the car yesterday. Tell me about it. Trying to justify driving anywhere these days feels like a crime. I’m thinking of cycling to work more often, even though it’ll take twice as long. Good luck with that in November! You’ll be frozen solid. Remember that hotel we stayed in in Cornwall last year? The one with the leaky roof? Oh god, don’t remind me! Woke up with a drip on my face in the middle of the night. Thought it was raining indoors. Actually, talking of Cornwall, I saw this incredible exhibition of local art in a gallery down there last month. Really thought-provoking stuff. Lots of seascapes, obviously, but also some really abstract pieces.

Oh my god you are back! How was it? Did you have a good time? It was…intense. In a good way, mostly. Honestly, I needed that sun. I feel like a new woman. Though my bank account definitely doesn’t. Oh, tell me everything! Did you actually manage to get any proper relaxation, or was it all non-stop exploring? A bit of both. We did a ridiculous amount of walking, like, seriously blister-inducing amounts. But we also spent a good few days just lounging on the beach, reading and drinking cocktails. It was glorious. You are looking peak pale by the way. Rude! I’ve been working, okay? Unlike some people who bask in the Mediterranean sun… Speaking of work, how’s everything at the hospital? Still chaotic? Oh, you know. Always. We’ve had a spate of admissions this week, it’s been pretty full-on. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I’m just running around putting plasters on things that need serious surgery. It’s draining. Ugh, that sounds awful. You need another holiday already. Are you seeing anyone this weekend? Thinking of going for drinks with Chloe on Saturday. She’s already started planning her wedding, it’s… a lot. She’s got spreadsheets, honestly. Chloe and spreadsheets, name a more iconic duo. Have you heard anything from… you know… Liam? No. Thankfully. I blocked him on everything. It’s the only way to have peace of mind. I saw his mum at the supermarket last week though. That was awkward. She tried to make small talk about the weather. Oh, god. Awkward doesn’t even begin to cover that. Just breathe. Speaking of awkward, Mum asked about you. Specifically, asked if you’d “found a nice doctor yet”. Oh, for goodness sake. She’s still on that? I’m perfectly happy being single, thank you very much. I don't need a man to complete my life, I have a thriving career…and you! That’s my girl! Although… I did make pasta bake last night, there’s loads left over. I was hoping you’d be back to help me demolish it. Oh, you’re speaking my language now. Pasta bake? Don't mind if I do. Is it the cheesy one with the ham? The cheesiest. It’s calling your name. Also, I’m thinking of finally trying to tackle the garden.

Did you speak to Sarah today? How’s she doing? Yeah, I gave her a call this morning. She sounded… tired. Really tired. Said the chemo’s hit her hard this week. Mostly just sleeping, apparently. She managed a short walk with the dog, but that was about it. Oh, that’s rough. It’s just… awful, isn’t it? Even knowing it’s supposed to make her better, it sounds so debilitating. It is. She tried to be upbeat, you know, the usual “fighting spirit” stuff, but I could hear it in her voice. She’s really worried about missing more work. Feels like she’s letting everyone down. Bless her. She always was a grafter. Tell her not to worry about work, honestly. We all just want her to get better. The department will manage. I did say that. She mumbled something about student essays piling up. Honestly, that woman. Anyway… trying to focus on something else. Have you been looking at those houses in the village again? Oh, yes! I was scrolling through Rightmove during my lunch break. There’s one just come up on Old Orchard Lane. Three bedrooms, decent garden… it’s a bit of a fixer-upper, though. Needs a new kitchen. Old Orchard Lane? Isn’t that the one near the school? That can be a bit noisy at drop-off and pick-up time, can't it? It’s on the other side, thankfully. It backs onto the fields, so the garden would be really private. The photos look lovely. It’s asking for… well, it’s at the upper end of our budget, but not completely out of reach. And the planning permission for the extension? Did you manage to find out anything more about that? We don’t want to buy somewhere and then discover we can’t do what we want with it. I spoke to the planning officer at the council. Apparently, there were some objections from the neighbours to the previous application. Something about blocking their sunlight. She said it’s not an automatic rejection, but it would be an uphill battle to get it approved. Ugh, typical. People always have something to say. So, we’d have to scale back the plans, then? The whole reason we wanted a bigger kitchen was to have more space for entertaining. We could. Or… we could look at other properties.

Honestly, I’m starting a list. A list of things I absolutely do  not  like about this job. It’s getting long. Oh, go on then. Let’s compare. I’ve already got a mental catalogue, but a physical list sounds… therapeutic. Right, number one: the students leaving passive-aggressive notes about noise. Like I’m a miracle worker who can control other people’s social lives. “Could you  please  ask the people on the second floor to be quieter after 11pm?” As if I haven’t already tried! Ugh, the notes. They’re the worst. I had one the other day complaining about the smell of cooking.  Cooking!  It’s student accommodation, what did they expect? Michelin star dining? Exactly! And they always phrase it like it’s a personal attack on  you , like  you  personally made them lose sleep. It’s always couched as ‘just a suggestion’ isn’t it? ‘Just a suggestion, maybe the bins could be emptied more frequently?’ Like I spend my days deliberately letting the bins overflow. Oh, don’t even get me started on the bins. That leads into number two on my list: the sheer volume of cardboard. Seriously, where do they  get  all this cardboard? Online shopping addiction, that’s what it is. It’s insane. And they just… leave it. Piled up next to the bins. Like we’re their personal recycling service. I spent half an hour breaking down boxes yesterday. Half an hour! That’s a waste of your time. It should be their responsibility. And number three… the state of the common rooms after a Friday night. It’s like a bomb’s gone off. Pizza boxes, empty cans, questionable stains… Oh god, the stains. I’ve seen things, Mike, things I can’t unsee. It’s always sticky. Always. Sticky and… pungent. And don’t even get me started on the attempts at ‘art’ they leave on the whiteboards. It's just scribbles and inside jokes no one else understands. Right? It’s like they think they’re Banksy. Add to my list: students thinking they can just change the thermostat to Arctic temperatures because  they  feel warm. Oh, that’s a good one. It's always too hot or too cold. Never just right. It’s like they're deliberately trying to make our lives miserable. I genuinely think they are. And the constant requests for key replacements.

Honestly, it’s always the English you bump into, isn’t it? Wherever you go. Like when I was in Barcelona, three different groups in one day. Three! And all complaining about the paella. Sounds about right. Can't go anywhere without finding someone moaning about the food. Used to be the chips, now it’s paella. It’s a national pastime. It's true though. Remember that time we did that package tour of Italy? Half the coach was from Surrey. And they were all going on about how the pizza wasn’t ‘proper’ pizza. Honestly! Oh, package tours. Mum and Dad did one to the Christmas markets in Germany last year, didn’t you? We did. Too regimented for me, honestly. Up at six, on the bus, a quick look at a market, then back on the bus. No time to actually soak it in. Antwerp was nice though. A bit of free time there. Antwerp's lovely. I always thought I’d like to learn Dutch. Sounds…well, difficult. Good luck with that! I tried learning Spanish for uni, lasted about a week. All those conjugations…! You need to be young to pick up languages, love. My brain's too full of remembering where I left my slippers. Speaking of which, your Auntie Maureen was asking after you. She’s been down Herne Bay shopping again. Apparently, they've got a new garden centre. Oh really? She loves a good garden centre. I need to get a move on with my Christmas shopping. It’s nearly December! It feels like only yesterday it was August. Tell me about it. Time flies, doesn’t it? Speaking of which, Leo's birthday is next month. He’s turning eight. Can't believe how quickly he's growing up. He’s obsessed with puppies at the moment. Wants one for Christmas. A puppy? You and Jamie will be doing all the work! Remember raising boys? It’s non-stop. One minute they're building Lego, the next they’re trying to disassemble the sofa. Oh, I remember. My Daniel was a nightmare. Always getting into trouble. Though, he's turned into a good lad now, thankfully. They’re little terrors, but you wouldn’t trade them for the world. It’s just… losing Gran this year has made me think about time, you know? How quickly everything changes. It has, hasn't it?

Did you see about Ireland, with the vote? Oh yes, the equality vote. It’s about time, isn't it? Though, honestly, I'm surprised it took them this long. Yeah, it was pretty big news. Everyone at school was talking about it. Old Mr. Henderson even stopped a lesson to explain it, which was…weird. Mr. Henderson? Oh,  him . He probably wanted to share his ‘wisdom’ on the matter. Though, to be fair, it’s a pretty important thing. He went on for ages, honestly. Said something about traditions and… I zoned out. Anyway, everyone seems really happy about it. Good. It's a step in the right direction. It’s just… well, you see how much fuss is made about it over there, and it makes you realise how lucky we are, comparatively. Lucky? You mean with politics? Mum, you always say politics is awful. It  is  awful, darling, but at least we've had… some progress. Some movements. It feels like Ireland’s just catching up. Bit late, but better late than never, I suppose. Yeah. So, are we still on for Ben’s party on Saturday? Yes, although your father is already making plans to tell embarrassing stories about your childhood. Apparently, the one about the dinosaur costume is a ‘classic’.  No . Seriously? He promised he wouldn’t! He promises lots of things. Trust me, I've learned to take it with a grain of salt. It's practically tradition at these parties. Embarrass the child. It’s not funny! I was five! And the costume ripped! Oh, it was glorious. You were running around yelling like a tiny T-Rex, and then  rip . Everything was on show. Mum! Oh, alright, alright! I won’t tell it. Though, honestly, it’s a good story. Speaking of stories, Auntie Carol was asking me about your birthday. She wants to know what you want. Oh, not more socks. Please, not more socks. I have enough socks to clothe a small army. She always gets socks. It’s her thing. It's a terrible thing! Can't she just…give money? Or a video game? I’ll gently suggest a gift voucher. Though knowing Carol, she’ll say, “But I  like  getting you socks!” Then she’ll tell us about the time she tried to convince your grandfather to elope with her to Las Vegas. Oh god. She does love a good story, doesn’t she?

Right, well this ham's alright, isn't it? Not as good as Mrs. Patterson's down the road, mind you. She knew how to cure a ham, she did. Saltpetre and all. Oh, don’t start on Mrs. Patterson and her ham again, Harold. You’ve told that story a hundred times. It  is  a good ham, Dad. Though, admittedly, a bit thin on the fat. Thin on the fat! That’s the modern way, isn’t it? Everything’s gotta be lean. Back in my day, a bit of fat gave it flavour. Speaking of flavour, did you ever get that lathe tool sorted, David? The one I lent you? The parting tool? Yes, it’s fine. Cleaned it up, sharpened it. Used it for a little project, actually. Turned a small bowl. Good, good. Those tools need looking after, you know. They don’t make ‘em like they used to. Proper high-speed steel, that was. Not like this modern stuff. Honestly, you and your lathe tools. You talk about them more than you talk about your grandchildren sometimes. Well, they’re  useful  things, Ethel. Unlike… well, never mind. What sort of wood did you use for the bowl, Dad? Now, that reminds me of a story. Old Mr. Hemmings, from the village… he used to get wood from all over. One time, he brought back a load of what he  thought  was apple wood. Lovely colour, it was. Turned out, someone had been using his shed to… well, to house a hamster. A hamster? Harold! What are you talking about? A hamster, Ethel! And the poor little thing used the woodpile for, well, for its business. Mr. Hemmings nearly fainted when he started turning it. The smell… Oh, the smell! You're kidding! A hamster… in a woodpile? Not a bit of it. Swear on my life. Apparently, someone had thought it was a kind thing to do, letting it roam free in the shed! Then Mr. Hemmings went to turn some wood. It was a disaster. Goodness me. Honestly, Harold, where do you  hear  these stories? And you’re eating your ham as you tell it! Well, it’s a good story, isn’t it? And the ham helps. Reminds me… did you ever hear about Old Man Peabody and the microwave? He tried to heat up a… Dad, please! Let's just enjoy the ham, alright?

Honestly, the price of houses now… it’s just… ridiculous. I was looking online, just out of curiosity, at places in Guildford, and even a tiny little terrace is going for upwards of half a million. Half a million! It's the same everywhere, isn’t it? Driven by London, mostly. People commuting, pushing up the prices. We’re lucky we bought when we did, even if it means… well, you know. The mortgage hanging over us for the next decade? Yes, I know. Though, I did see something interesting about banks offering interest-only mortgages again. Is that… sensible? Sensible? Banks offering anything is rarely sensible, dear. It’s all about tempting people in, isn’t it? They learned nothing from the last time, of course. Interest-only… it just kicks the can down the road, doesn’t it? All that debt building up. It's a gamble, isn't it? Hoping house prices continue to rise. A very big gamble. I saw an article about someone finally clearing a debt they'd had since the 80s. Absolutely staggering. Oh, don’t remind me. We were talking about that cat the other day, the one that turned up in somebody’s Amazon parcel? Oh, yes! Absolutely extraordinary. How did that even  happen ? Apparently, the cat had snuck into the warehouse and just… curled up in the box. It travelled goodness knows how many miles. Amazing. Speaking of things travelling miles, I’m still trying to get my head around this mirror-writing thing. Apparently, Leonardo da Vinci did all his notes in mirror writing. Really? That’s… bizarre. Was it a security thing? So people couldn’t easily read his ideas? Possibly. Or perhaps he simply found it more comfortable. Some people are naturally left-handed and find writing from right to left easier. Though, scribbling everything backwards seems a bit much, even for a genius! Are you doing the cryptic crossword tonight? I’ve started it, but I’m stuck on 14 across. Something about a Parisian street and a colour. Oh, that’s a classic. Rue… and… azure? Rue Azure? That’s it! Wonderful. You’re a genius, you are. Unlike some politicians currently making a mess of things across the pond. Honestly, American politics is just… exhausting. Don't get me started. It’s all bluster and posturing. And speaking of things that irritate me… they’re still charging for plastic bags!

Right okay that’s enough screen time for today. Honestly, you’ve been on those things for hours. It’s a beautiful afternoon, isn’t it? Why don't you two go and build something with your Lego? But Mum, I was  just  about to beat the ender dragon! It’s a really good world, I've built a secret base under the waterfall. That sounds… complicated. But even complicated things need breaks. And your eyes need breaks too. Remember what the doctor said about looking at screens for too long. Can we at least finish this level? Kai’s about to unlock his Spinjitzu Burst! It’s a new Ninjago set, it’s really cool. No, no more levels. Ninjago is fine, it's good to be creative, but a little bit of reading wouldn’t go amiss either. Remember that book Grandma gave you, Alfred, about the knights? Ugh, that’s boring! It doesn’t  do  anything. It just… has words. Minecraft does everything! You can build anything you want and fight monsters and explore caves. It’s way better than a book. It’s not about which is ‘better’, Laurena. It’s about using your imagination in different ways. Books help you imagine the stories in your  head . Games show you everything. It’s important to do both. But my world is really good! I spent ages making a railway system that goes all around everything. It’s epic. I’m sure it is. And I’m sure Kai’s Spinjitzu Burst is very impressive as well. But sometimes, just sometimes, it's nice to switch off the screens and use your hands to create something. Lego's good for building, but books build worlds inside your mind. Can we at least save our Minecraft worlds first? Please? Alright. Five minutes. Five minutes to save, then screens off and Lego or books. Deal? Speaker_2 & Speaker_3 : Deal! Good. Now, hurry up before I change my mind. And try to remember there's a whole world outside of those glowing rectangles. Honestly I feel like I'm constantly battling with technology these days! It's wonderful for them to be learning, but it's so easy to get lost in it. Mum, can I have just  one  more minute? I nearly finished! Alfred! No. Absolutely not. Lego. Now. Fine. Mum, do you think I can build a secret base in the Lego world like the one in Minecraft?

So, was the journey back alright yesterday? No dramas, I hope? It was okay, Mum. A bit busy on the M6, as usual, but nothing too bad. Honestly, I was just so tired I think I could have slept standing up. How was your drive? Oh, you know, the M6. Always a gamble! I managed to time it fairly well, though. Not too much hold-up. Honestly, the best part was just getting back and putting my feet up. That Cornwall trip was lovely, but draining. Honestly, I need a holiday to recover from my holiday! You always say that, Mum! But it did sound amazing. All those beaches and the cream teas… I’m seriously jealous I couldn’t come. It was brilliant, honestly. We did try and bring you both back a little something, though. I’ve got them in the kitchen. Nothing massive, just a couple of little bits and bobs. Oh lovely! You shouldn’t have. Nonsense, I wanted to. Right, coffee refills anyone? What are you two up to today? Any grand plans? Not really. I was planning on doing some reading for uni, I’ve got a massive essay due next week about... honestly, it's so dull, something about post-structuralist literature. Sounds thrilling! I've got a staff meeting at two, then just a mountain of paperwork. Standard Saturday for a store manager, I suppose. I’m hoping to get to the garden centre later, though. Need some more bedding plants. Oh, good idea! I keep meaning to tackle the garden. It’s looking a bit of a state at the moment. Maybe we could go together next week, Chloe? It’s always more fun with company. Maybe! Depends how this essay goes. If I’m still pulling my hair out, I might need to stay indoors in a darkened room. Fair enough. You get stuck into that. Sarah, did you manage to book that dentist appointment for your toothache? Oh, yes, thank you for reminding me! I managed to get in for Tuesday afternoon. It’s not too bad, just a bit sensitive. Hopefully, it’s nothing serious. Good, good. It's always best to get these things checked out straight away. Now, have you both seen the photos from the Eden Project? Honestly, the biomes are just incredible. I took about a hundred… Oh, yes! I saw a few on your Facebook, they looked amazing!

This sandwich is… underwhelming. Seriously, five quid for this? It’s mostly bread. Tell me about it. I got the chicken and bacon and it tastes like it’s been sitting here since Tuesday. Honestly, I should have just gone to Pret. It's a bit further, but at least you know what you're getting. Did anyone see what Liam posted on his Insta story last night? No, I was busy trying to finish that history essay. What was it? Another one of his weird motivational quotes? Worse. He was going on about how his grandad fought in the Falklands. Like, okay cool, but what’s that got to do with anything? He was trying to look all… patriotic or something. Ugh, Liam. He does that all the time. My uncle was in the army, but he doesn’t go around shouting about it. It's just… awkward. Yeah, it’s like he’s trying too hard. Remember when he tried to argue with Mr. Davies about, like, international politics in Geography? Oh my god, yes! He was rambling about Taiwan and Mr. Davies was just standing there, looking completely baffled. And then he said something about needing to “defend freedom” which, honestly, was a bit much for a Friday afternoon. Did you guys hear about Maya getting picked as head girl? Seriously? Maya? I thought for sure it would be Tom or Chloe. Yeah, it was a bit of a shock. She's alright, but she's a bit… intense, isn’t she? I heard she was going around telling people what they  should  be doing for charity week. She does have a bit of a “do as I say” vibe. Speaking of intense, have you seen the new series of ‘The Watchers’? It's so creepy. No, is it good? I’ve been hooked on ‘Severance’ again. It’s just so… unsettling. ‘Severance’ is amazing! I binged it all in one weekend. ‘The Watchers’ is different, it's a proper horror. Like, jump-scare central. We should have a movie night next weekend? Definitely! We could order pizza and play some cards afterwards. Anyone up for a game of Exploding Kittens? I’ve been practicing my bluffing skills. I'm in. I always lose at that game. You guys are ruthless. Oh, and speaking of ruthless, did you hear Mrs. Peterson actually gave Ben a detention for talking during her lesson?

Honestly, Mr. Davies is the  worst  physics teacher ever. He just stands there and drones on and on. You can tell he doesn't even like physics, honestly. Seriously! I thought it was just me. He explains everything so… complicatedly. Like, he could say “the ball fell down” but he'd say “due to the gravitational pull exerted by the Earth’s mass…” Ugh. Exactly! And then he gives you this look if you ask him to repeat something. Like  you’re  the idiot for not understanding his super-complex explanation of something simple. He has that… condescending eyebrow raise, doesn’t he? Like he’s talking to a room full of toddlers. Yes! It's awful. Did you hear Mrs. Peterson is off sick again? No way! Again? That’s like, the third time this term. Who’s covering our form time? Mr. Harrison. Which is… okay, I guess. He’s pretty chill, but he always forgets to tell us important stuff. Like, last week he forgot to remind us about the deadline for the history essay. Oh no! I completely missed that. I’m still trying to finish it. It’s so long! I’m rewriting the introduction for the fifth time. Tell me about it. I’m stuck on the conclusion. I just can’t find a good way to sum everything up. Have you seen that film,  17 Again ? Ooh, yeah! I watched it ages ago. It's so funny! It made me think about school. Like, if I could go back and redo everything, I’d actually pay attention in physics. And maybe not leave my history essay until the last minute. Ha! Me too. Although, I’d probably just spend all my time eating snacks and avoiding PE. Good point. What are we reading in English at the moment? I keep forgetting.  Frankenstein . It’s… slow. I mean, it's good, but it’s a lot of description. And the language is so old-fashioned. Ugh, I know. It's hard to keep track of who’s who. And all the gloomy descriptions of the countryside. Have you seen Liam Davies in our year? He's started wearing those ridiculous bright orange trainers. They're so… noticeable. Oh my god, yes! It's like he's deliberately trying to attract attention. He's so weird. And he keeps staring at Ms. Jones, the art teacher.

Honestly though, Transylvania. You’re actually going? That’s…ambitious. Ambitious? It's a holiday, Leo! It's not scaling Everest. I found a really cute little Airbnb in a village, apparently it’s supposed to be amazing for hiking. And you know, Dracula vibes. Dracula vibes, eh? You taking garlic with you just in case? Very funny, Maisie. Seriously though, I’m a bit nervous about the language barrier. My Romanian is… non-existent. Fair dinkum. You’ll be right though, people usually manage. Just learn a few key phrases, you know? “Where’s the nearest beer?” is always a good start. Yeah, that’s solid advice, Ash. Though I reckon you could probably get away with just pointing at a menu in most places. So, Transylvania. That’s you sorted for the summer then? Any plans for the weekend just gone, anyone? I went to that new art exhibition in Shoreditch, the one everyone was raving about. It was… alright. Honestly, felt a bit pretentious. Oh, the one with the inflatable sculptures? I saw some pictures. Looked a bit silly. I spent the weekend perfecting my sourdough recipe. Managed to get a decent crust this time, which is a win. I had a nightmare. Old man Hemmings tried to complain that his latte wasn't hot enough. He's a regular, but honestly, he’s such a pain. Kept going on and on about it. Crikey. Sounds rough. Some people just want to have a whinge, don’t they? Speaking of rough, heard anything from Ben lately? He was talking about finally getting round to that laser eye surgery. Oh yeah, I think he had it done last week. He messaged me saying it went well, but he’s been a bit quiet since. Probably just resting his eyes. Good. He's been talking about it for years. It’ll be amazing for him, he hates wearing glasses. I saw Chloe yesterday, by the way. Chloe? Oh, the one who used to work at the record shop? What's she been up to? She's doing really well actually. She’s working as a florist now, apparently. And she’s seeing someone new. A musician, I think. Oh really? Who? Spill the tea! Apparently it’s Liam from “The Static Waves”. You know, that indie band we used to be obsessed with in uni? No way! Seriously? Liam? He was  fit .

Right, so the playlist for the party… I was thinking a bit of everything? Some 80s, some current stuff, a few of your favourites? Can we have Taylor Swift?  Please ? And maybe that song from the movie… the one with the dancing? The  Encanto  one? Absolutely! Good shout. And yes, lots of Taylor Swift. Your brother loves her too, apparently. He’s been practicing all the dances. I want the one with the robots! And the loud noises! Okay, some robot noises are allowed. Though maybe not  too  many, for Granny’s sake. Speaking of which, she asked if we're doing a photo shoot. She wants a ‘proper’ family photo. Oh, ugh. Do we  have  to? I look silly in family photos. Well, she's really keen. I was thinking we could do a silly one  and  a nice one? Maybe an  Alice in Wonderland  theme? I have that Mad Hatter hat. I wanna be the Queen of Hearts! And shout "Off with their heads!" We'll work on the phrasing, maybe? Perhaps "Off with their biscuits!" Less alarming. But good idea. We could get some props...though your dad will probably veto anything remotely flamboyant. He will. He hates having his photo taken. He says he looks like a startled meerkat. That’s… surprisingly accurate. Right, food. I was thinking pizza, obviously. And those mini sausage rolls you love. And a cake, of course. Chocolate, definitely chocolate. And crisps! Lots and lots of crisps! And dips! Yes, crisps and dips. Good thinking. Are you two being good? No swearing? I heard a little “bloody” earlier. It was  him ! He said it when he fell off the sofa! It wasn't  on  purpose! Okay, okay. Just try to keep it to a minimum, alright? Remember Auntie Carol is coming. She's… sensitive. Speaking of falling, how's the aerial hoop going? Are you still practicing? Yeah! I’m getting better. I can almost do a full rotation now. It looks like you’re a sparkly spider! A sparkly spider, that’s a fantastic description! I’m proud of you for sticking with it. It takes courage. Oh, and I signed us up for the muddy obstacle course next month. WHAT?! You did  what ?! Mud! Yes! Can I wear my wellies? Wellies are compulsory! It's going to be… an experience. Apparently, there’s a giant slide and a huge mud pit.

Honestly, this pizza’s lovely. Much better than that one we had last week, wasn't it? All soggy bottom and hardly any topping. It was dreadful, dear. Remember I said it tasted like cardboard? Though anything's good after that awful heat we had. Made you lose your appetite, didn't it? Speaking of appetite, this chocolate roulade is…well, it's a work of art, really. Did you make it, Margaret? I did, actually. Been practicing. Thought the girls deserved a treat after all the stress with those GCSE results. It’s amazing, honestly! Thank you! I was so stressed about History, but I actually got a 7! Ooh, well done! I got a 6, but I'm really pleased with my Art. Mr. Henderson said my perspective was excellent. A 7! That's smashing, love. Old man Henderson always had a good eye, didn’t he? Reminds me of old Mr. Davies, my woodwork teacher. Nearly flunked me, he did. Said my birdhouse looked like a prison. A prison for birds! That’s brilliant. How are the driving lessons going, then, Emily? Still terrifying your instructor? They're…going. I stalled at the roundabout again today. He didn’t say anything, just sighed really loudly. Oh, dear. It takes practice, love. Don’t worry. Remember when your father learned? He nearly drove into Mrs. Higgins’ flowerbeds! That was one time! And she  did  have ridiculously bright begonias. Distracted a man, they did. Did you see what happened in the girls’ football yesterday? Chloe tripped and everyone started arguing. It was a mess. Teenage drama, eh? Sounds about right. What are you girls thinking about for careers now that you've got your results? Any ideas? I’m thinking about maybe…photography. I really like taking pictures, and I'm pretty good at editing them. I’ve been tweeting them, actually. Got a few likes. Tweeting pictures? Goodness me. I can barely work the television remote. It's all this modern technology, Margaret. Makes my head spin. I saw a programme about blokes using drones to deliver takeaway food the other day. Honestly! It's changing rapidly, isn’t it? What about you, Sophie? Any thoughts? I'm not sure yet. Maybe something to do with animals. I volunteered at the animal shelter over the summer, and I loved it. But I’m worried about the science side of things.

Right, so if I move my horse here… checkmate? No, dear. Absolutely not. Your horse is beautifully positioned to be… taken. By my cannon. Oh, good move, Carol. Really good move. He didn’t see  that  coming, did he, Ben? I… I did, actually. I was baiting you. It’s a classic strategic misdirection. Oh, don't give me that. You looked properly flustered. Honestly, you're just like your grandfather, getting all red in the face when you're beaten at something. I am  not  like Grandad! He used to cheat at cards. I would  never  cheat. He accused everyone else of cheating, more like. Remember that holiday in Skegness? He swore old Mrs. Higgins was palming aces up her sleeve. Oh, that was a classic. Anyway, you’re still going down, young man. I’ve been practicing. I’ve watched hours and hours of tutorials online. Some Korean chap explaining the intricacies of Xiangqi. Honestly, the detail! You've been watching Xiangqi tutorials? Seriously? Why not? It’s fascinating! Far more strategic than chess, I think. Though, I may be biased. Did you have a good breakfast? I made those scones yesterday. Lovely scones, Carol. Absolutely lovely. Though a little bit dry, if I'm being honest. Needed a bit more jam. Dry? Oh, honestly! I followed the recipe  exactly . They were good, Mum. Really good. I had two. See? He appreciated them. Your father’s always a critic. Speaking of which, he’s been muttering about the weather again. Says it's going to rain all week. Well, it looks like it, doesn’t it? Grey as a mouse. Though it  was  quite mild this morning. I spent a good hour out in the garden, trying to prune the gooseberry bushes. Those thorns are vicious. Did you manage to get many berries? A few. Not as many as last year. And the slugs are having a field day. I need to get some more of that copper tape. It’s supposed to deter them. It doesn’t work, that copper tape. Waste of money. They just go over it. You need nematodes. Nematodes? What are those? Tiny worms that eat slugs? Precisely. It's biological control. Very modern. They’re amazing little creatures. You can order them online. Though, you have to get the right sort. Otherwise, they’ll eat your plants. Everything's complicated these days. In my day, you just chucked some salt at the slugs.

Honestly, some of the things they come up with… this one student, bless him, tried to tell me that “irregardless” is a real word. I had to gently explain… Oh, the bane of my life! It's not even… people just  make  words up and then insist they’re correct. It drives me mad. Same with “could of” instead of “could have.” Exactly! Though at least with the students, you can correct them. It’s harder when you overhear it on the news, you know? All this political rhetoric… it’s just… exhausting. Tell me about it. I try to avoid the news these days. It’s just a constant stream of negativity. Though I did read something about the pension age going up  again . Can you believe it? Ugh, don’t even. I’m already dreading thinking about that. I mean, I'm only just starting to pay into it properly now with the new job, and they’ll probably have it at seventy by the time I get anywhere near retirement. It’s outrageous. And then they wonder why people don’t save. It’s a vicious cycle. Speaking of money, how are you getting on with paying off your student loans? Slowly…painfully slowly. They keep changing the terms, and it feels like I'm just treading water. At least with the new job I’m earning enough to make a proper dent, but it’s still… a significant chunk each month. Oh, I remember those days. Though mine were paid off ages ago. Lucky me, I suppose. It feels a lifetime ago though, doesn’t it? Before all this… Polish adventure. It does! It’s so nice to get away. Right, shall we decide where we're driving tomorrow? You wanted to see the salt mine, didn’t you? Yes, Wieliczka. Apparently, it’s incredible. But… is it easy to get to? My Polish isn’t exactly stellar. And I haven't even attempted the MOT on my brain this trip, I'm a bit rusty. It’s fairly straightforward. I can navigate. It’s about an hour’s drive from here. We could combine it with a trip to Zakopane maybe further down the line, if we have time? That sounds wonderful. Zakopane’s been on my list for ages. Before we finalise anything, are you watching anything good on Netflix at the moment? I need something to binge on in the evenings.

So, Human Sciences… still leaning that way, then? It sounds… broad. Yeah, pretty much. It’s at Warwick, which is a big pull, obviously. It’s kinda like… psychology, sociology, anthropology all mashed up. Seems more… useful, than just straight psychology, you know? More career options, apparently. What about you? Still dead set on Maths? Yeah, pretty much. Got an offer from Bristol, conditional on A  in Further Maths. Which is… stressing me out a bit. Bristol’s good though, isn’t it? Good nights out, I’ve heard. Are you going to the rugby this weekend? Old Hamptonians are playing. Yeah, I’m supposed to be. Mum’s making me promise to “behave.” Which usually means “don’t drink too much and embarrass the family.” You coming? Probably. My old man’s going, so I’m basically obliged. He’s got season tickets. Speaking of drinking… they’ve got that new cocktail place in here, have you seen? Looks expensive. Yeah, saw it. Not for us, I reckon. Probably stick to pints. Orange juice for me tonight, actually. Gotta stay focused on this Further Maths. It’s killing me. Smart. I might have a cider. Need to practice the ‘university lifestyle’ before I actually get there, right? Although, I’m terrible at cooking. University’s gonna be a disaster if I have to actually feed myself. You and me both. My culinary skills extend to toast and potentially boiling an egg. I saw something on TikTok about a student who lives entirely on instant noodles. Seriously? That’s depressing. Actually, my sister went to uni last year, and she said the first few weeks are just a blur of introductory stuff and trying to make friends. Apparently, it’s exhausting. Sounds it. I’m hoping to room with Ben. We get on well, and he actually  can  cook. He makes a pretty decent curry, apparently. Lucky. I’m just hoping I don't end up with some weirdo who plays the bagpipes at 3 am. That’s my biggest fear. You think we'll actually  keep  in touch once we're both away? We should, yeah. Rugby, at least, gives us an excuse. And we’ve gotta plan a proper trip to somewhere decent during the holidays. Maybe Interrail? Interrail! Now  that  sounds good. Spain, maybe? I did GCSE Spanish, so I can at least order a beer.

So, you were asking about National Insurance contributions, weren’t you? Bit of a fiddle, it is. People think it just goes towards their pension, but it’s more than that, you see. Yeah, I was just trying to get my head around it all. It feels like a huge chunk of my salary just vanishes. It does, doesn’t it? But it funds the NHS, unemployment benefits, all sorts. It’s a contribution to the whole system. Now, back in my day, it was a simpler affair. Flat rate, pretty much. Now they’ve got all these tiers, depending on your earnings. I think I understand the tiers part, it’s the principle of it all that feels a bit… murky. Why does the government need so much money anyway? Good question. Well, look at the services they provide. Education, healthcare, defence… it all costs. And the population’s getting older, more people needing pensions and care. That puts a strain on the system, you see. But it feels like a lot of it gets wasted. I read an article about… well, never mind. It’s probably just sensationalism. There’s always some waste, unfortunately. Government isn’t known for its efficiency, is it? But it’s a necessary evil, I suppose. And think about tax avoidance. That’s a big problem. Large corporations finding loopholes to pay less tax. That means everyone else has to foot the bill. That’s what really frustrates me! Seeing those big companies get away with it while I’m diligently paying my income tax. Exactly. And it's getting harder to close those loopholes. They’ve got teams of lawyers dedicated to it. The government tries to clamp down, but they’re always one step behind. So, what about inheritance tax? That seems especially unfair. Taxing people after they’ve already… well, you know. That’s a tricky one. Designed to prevent huge amounts of wealth being passed down through generations, creating even more inequality. But it understandably upsets people. It feels like the government is coming after their hard-earned money, even after they’re gone. I can see both sides, I suppose. But I always wonder where that money actually  goes . Largely back into the pot. Funding public services, reducing the national debt… though, as we’ve said, there's always room for improvement in how it's managed. It's a constant balancing act, really.

Honestly, this project is just… consuming my life. I feel like I’m living at work. Oh, darling, you always say that. But you're good at it, aren't you? You thrive under pressure. Though it's not healthy, is it? I  think  I’m good at it. It’s just… non-stop. New requests coming in every five minutes. And everyone thinks it’s urgent. Like the world will end if their report isn’t on my desk by lunchtime. People, honestly! They have no concept of a reasonable workload. What’s Sarah been up to? Haven’t heard from her in ages. She’s good! She’s still going strong with the pottery, apparently. Posted some pictures on Instagram – absolutely beautiful stuff. She’s thinking of doing a little market stall, which is brilliant. Oh, that’s lovely for her. She’s always been so creative. Remember when she tried to make that dress for the school play? It was… ambitious. Ambitious is one word for it! It involved a lot of safety pins and questionable fabric choices. But she gave it a go! That’s Sarah all over. It’s good she's found something she loves. Makes all the difference. How’s your mum doing? I meant to ring her last week. She’s okay. Bit grumpy, as usual. Complaining about the neighbour’s cat getting into her garden. Apparently, it’s been digging up her prize-winning petunias. Oh, dear. That  is  annoying. She loves those petunias. She does. She’s threatening to get a sprinkler system just to deter it. Dad's trying to mediate, but you know how she gets. He just sighs and makes her a cup of tea. That’s your Dad all over. The silent peacemaker. Speaking of peacemakers, have you heard anything more from Liam? He hasn’t been answering his phone. Oh, him. No, not a peep. I think he’s gone off-grid again. He does that sometimes. Gets overwhelmed and just disappears for a bit. It's frustrating, but… it’s Liam. It is, isn’t it? Well, you know he's always welcome here if he needs to escape for a while. Though your mum might not appreciate him moping around the house. Probably not. She's not a fan of moping. So, back to work… I need to start drafting this email. It’s going to be a long one, I can feel it.

So, did you two manage to get yourselves sorted with dinner last night? I was meaning to ask. Yeah, it was alright. We just went to that Italian place down the street, ‘Bella Notte’. Nothing fancy. It was decent. A bit loud though, loads of families in. Still, good pasta. How about you, Mr. Thompson? Did you have a nice quiet night in? Quiet as a mouse, lad. Had a bit of a stew on, leftover from Sunday. Nothing to write home about, but it filled a hole. Though I did try that new red wine Marjorie brought round. Bit too fruity for my liking, honestly. Oh, the one she got from France? I thought it sounded nice. It wasn’t  bad , mind. Just not my cup of tea. She’s got a good palate, Marjorie, always finding these interesting bottles. She was asking after you, by the way, Emily. Said she hasn’t seen you since… well, Christmas, I think? Oh, right. I must give her a ring. She's always wanting to play bridge, but I’ve been so busy with work. This new project is mental. Speaking of busy, I’m still slogging through job applications. Seems like every company wants five years’ experience for an entry-level position. It’s ridiculous. Tell me about it. Even after retiring, I get lads asking for my advice on CVs! Says a lot, doesn’t it? Have you seen Liam recently? I haven’t bumped into him for ages. Now you mention it, no. Haven't. He was talking about going to Spain with some mates, a while back. Maybe he’s still over there soaking up the sun. He always was a bit of a wanderer, Liam. Remember when he tried to learn Spanish just before that trip? He lasted about a week, then went back to ordering everything in English with a Geordie accent. Oh, God, yes! It was hilarious. He thought he was fluent! He’s a good lad, though. Always up for a laugh. We should try and get him round for a games night. You fancy that? Yeah, that’d be good. We haven’t done a proper games night in ages. What have you got on your iPod at the moment, by the way? Need some new tunes. Oh, that's a good question. I've started getting into some older stuff. Rediscovered Fleetwood Mac actually.

Honestly, the whole thing was just…a lot. Like, a  lot . Oh, the conference? Tell me about it. Was it awful? I was bracing myself for a full debrief. Awful isn’t even the word. It wasn’t  bad , exactly. More…pointless. So much focus on blended learning, integrating tech, and I’m just sitting there thinking, “I teach teenagers in rural Spain. They’re lucky if the internet works consistently!” Oh, classic. They always do that, don’t they? Assume everyone’s got access to cutting-edge resources and a fully equipped smart classroom. Exactly! And the keynote speaker? Went on for an hour about gamification. An hour! I’m pretty sure half the room fell asleep. Ugh. Gamification. I swear, it’s a buzzword that just refuses to die. Did they at least have decent coffee? That’s usually my benchmark for conference success. The coffee was…adequate. Lukewarm, instant, and served in those tiny paper cups. But the  worst  part was the networking sessions. So much awkward small talk. Oh god, the networking. I hate the networking. It’s always the same questions. “And what do you teach?” “Oh, that’s interesting.” “Right…”  awkward silence . Precisely! And everyone’s trying to look important and insightful. I ended up cornered for twenty minutes by a guy who wouldn’t stop talking about his meticulously crafted online quizzes. Oh, the quiz masters. They're a special breed. Did you manage to escape? Eventually. I pretended I saw someone I knew across the room and made a dramatic dash for freedom. Seriously, I felt like I was in a spy movie. Ha! I can picture it. I’ve done similar things. Using the ‘urgent phone call’ tactic is a good one too. Oh, that’s a good one. I’ll add that to my arsenal for next time. Though honestly, I'm starting to think I’m going to actively avoid conferences in the future. I get it. It can feel like a waste of time and money. Though, they do provide a good opportunity to get out of the classroom for a bit, don't they? Even if it’s just to people-watch the quiz masters. That’s true. And the free pens are always a bonus. But this one… this one just felt particularly draining. How’s work been for you? Any exciting teenage dramas unfolding? You know it.

Right, so according to this, we need to take the E40 towards Krakow, but then  before  Krakow, take a slip road for Rzeszow. Does that make sense? Sounds… vaguely terrifying. I mean, navigating around Krakow sounds like a nightmare. Everything seems to funnel  through  Krakow. Are you sure that’s right? Pretty sure. It’s what Google Maps is telling me, and it recalculated when we left Tarnow. Plus, I checked a couple of different routing apps just to be sure. Unless you fancy a detour through, like, the Ukrainian border? Oh god, no. Krakow sounds preferable to accidentally ending up in Ukraine. Although… part of me is slightly intrigued. Still, let's stick to the plan. Speaking of plans, are you still hoping to squeeze in that hike tomorrow? Your legs must be killing you after all that walking in Tarnow. They're a bit achy, yeah, but I’m hoping a good night’s sleep and a bit of stretching will fix that. I really want to see that national park they were talking about at the hostel. Apparently, the views are amazing. You could come too, if you're feeling energetic. Oh, no, I think I’ll pass on the strenuous activity. My knees are starting to creak just thinking about it. I’m much more suited to gentle ambling and admiring the scenery from a cafe, thank you very much. I’ll be the designated tea-drinker and book-reader. Have you finished that novel you were telling me about? Not yet. It's a bit slow-going, actually. All descriptive prose and very little plot. I’m starting to wonder if it’s worth the hype. It’s one of those ones everyone on BookTok was raving about. Should have known better. BookTok. Honestly. It’s a minefield. Everyone recommending terrible romance novels with ridiculously ripped men on the cover. I saw one the other day where the hero was a Viking… and a doctor. A Viking  doctor . Oh, that’s… impressively ridiculous. I’m sticking to slightly more realistic fiction, I think. Although, thinking about ridiculously ripped men… have you seen the gym next to the hostel? It’s full of them. Polish men take their fitness seriously, apparently. Oh, good for them. I prefer a man with a good book, myself. And preferably one who doesn't spend all his time flexing. Although, I suppose a bit of muscle is never a bad thing.

…and the thing is, the pyramids, right? Everyone looks at them as tombs, grand tombs for the Pharaohs. But there’s increasing evidence they were actually enormous energy accumulators. Focused energy. Remember that fella, Erich von Däniken? Controversial, aye, but some of his ideas… there’s a kernel of truth there, I reckon. They weren’t just dragging stones, you know? They understood something about the Earth’s magnetic field, about harnessing power. That’s…quite a leap, isn’t it? I mean, I always thought it was impressive engineering, obviously, but to think of them as power stations… Engineering is part of it, of course. But look at the precision. Look at the alignment with Orion’s belt. The angles. It’s not just building, it’s…orchestration. And it ties into this whole thing about telomeres, you see. Telomeres? Oh, like, the things that shorten as you age? I read a bit about that, trying to find a miracle cream, naturally. Didn't work, obviously. Leo’s still waking me up five times a night. Ah, the joys! But the telomeres, they're not just about creams. They’re about energy. Maintaining cellular energy. And these ancient civilizations, I think they understood how to do that. How to prolong life. Not necessarily immortality, mind, but extending the lifespan beyond what we consider normal. So, you’re saying the pyramids somehow…charged people’s telomeres? Well, I’m hypothesising! It’s a stretch, I admit. But consider the Vikings. They raided all over Europe, navigated by the stars, built incredible ships… they were resilient, weren’t they? And a lot of their mythology is steeped in cosmic events - comets, auroras… Maybe they tapped into something too. Something ancient. They were also pretty brutal. Not exactly a model for healthy aging, all that pillaging. Fair point. Though, arguably, risk  is  invigorating. A little bit of danger keeps you sharp. But look, shifting gears… we were supposed to be planning a weekend away. Remember? Before we get lost in ancient energy sources and Viking longboats. Oh, right! Yes. I was thinking maybe County Clare? We could do some kayaking. It’s been ages since we’ve been out on the water. Clare sounds grand. I've a friend, Seamus, he runs a fantastic little B&B near Doolin. Stunning views of the Cliffs of Moher. And kayaking? Perfect. As long as it’s not gale-force winds.

This coffee is really good, actually. Did you get a new blend, Dad? Nah, same as always. Just made sure I cleaned the coffee maker properly this time. It makes all the difference, you know. That build-up of… stuff… ruins the flavour. You’re right, it's lovely. Though, I still think we need to think about getting a proper espresso machine. A little one, for the kitchen. Oh, don’t start that again, love. We don’t  need  an espresso machine. We've got this one, it does the job. Think of the money! Speaking of money, did you get those vouchers for the restaurant sorted? The Italian one near the pier? We were talking about going next week. Yes, I downloaded them onto my phone. They’re for two people, so you and your dad can go. I’m not really feeling up to a big meal out right now. Oh, good thinking. We'll go midweek, quieter. I’ve been meaning to try their seafood pasta. Ooh, yummy. Have you seen that new baby chair Auntie Maria bought for Leo? It's so fancy. Like a spaceship. Yes! It’s very… modern. Maria always goes a bit overboard, doesn't she? Spending all that money. She likes spoiling the little one. Can't blame her. Still, that's a lot of money for a chair. Remember when we just used a high chair that your grandma had? Yeah, it was pretty rickety though. It was! And covered in questionable stains. Right, well, times change. Speaking of changes… did you two see that result of the referendum? Ugh, don’t even. It's so depressing. It’s… complicated. I still don’t understand why people voted the way they did. It feels like such a backwards step. Aye, it is a bit of a mess. Still, can't change it now. I’m more worried about the price of eggs these days. Honestly! I was thinking of getting some chickens. Chickens?! In the garden?! Well, it'd save a bit of money, wouldn't it? Fresh eggs every day. Plus, they're good for the garden. Maybe not the best idea, darling. Where would they sleep? And the smell? Oh, I'd build them a little coop. It'd be alright. I saw a nice one online. You’re obsessed with saving money, Dad! You were complaining about the price of sunglasses last week.

Honestly, I don’t know what’s happened with Sarah recently. She’s just… different. Different how? Still going on about Dave? No, not Dave. Well, a bit. But it's more… withdrawn, isn’t it? She used to be so bubbly, always organising things. Now she just seems…flat. Maybe she’s just stressed with work. That marketing firm sounds intense. Could be. She did mention something about a big deadline. Oh, look at the tree! It’s looking lovely now, isn’t it? I’m glad we got a real one this year. It smells amazing. Much better than those plastic ones. Though Dad nearly had a meltdown trying to get the lights on properly. Men and fairy lights. A classic combination. Did you see Mrs. Henderson across the road putting up inflatable Santa’s? Oh god, yes! It’s… a choice, isn’t it? A slightly terrifying choice. It's a competition with the Millers, I reckon. They always try to outdo everyone. Speaking of competitions, how are your nails looking? All ready for Christmas parties? They’re okay. I’m going to do a sparkly red, I think. I tried that gel stuff, but it wrecked them. Oh, I know. It looks lovely when it’s on, but the removal process is a nightmare. How’s work going? Still churning out copy for everything and anything? Pretty much! It’s alright, honestly. A bit chaotic, but I’m learning a lot. They’re making me write about… German Christmas markets, actually. Oh, how interesting! You know, your Grandad was stationed in Germany during his National Service. Always loved talking about it. He said the Christmas markets were magical. Really? That’s cool. I might have to ask him about it when we see him. He’s usually good for a story. He is. And speaking of seeing people, have you made any plans with Ben for your birthday? We're thinking of going to that new Italian place in Tunbridge Wells. He said he'd book a table. He's being really lovely, actually. He even offered to put up the tree, but I said no. Good. Let Dad have his fun. He needs something to occupy him. Anything exciting happening this weekend otherwise? Not really. Just catching up with Millie on Saturday, and then probably a cosy night in. She's been reading a ridiculously long book about Prussian history.

Right, so… officially residents! Feels a bit weird, doesn’t it? Still smells like…newness. And paint. It does! It’s actually really nice though, way nicer than the photos made it look. And so much light! Did you manage to wrestle with the curtains? Managed, yes. Though I nearly took the whole rail down with me. Honestly, these things are never straightforward. It’s the little things, you know? Like, I’ve already spent an hour trying to figure out how the heating works. Oh god, heating instructions. The bane of my existence. I’ll have a look later, I’m slightly better at deciphering cryptic manuals. Right now, urgent priority: food. I’m starving. What’s the kitchen situation like? Pretty good!
