It's small, obviously, but functional. There’s a… vaguely clean oven. And a fridge that seems to be working, which is a win. I haven’t unpacked the food box yet, it’s currently residing in the living room, looking judgemental. Judgemental boxes are the worst. Okay, mission: unpack food, then assess what culinary masterpieces we can conjure. I’m thinking something easy. I’m not feeling particularly ambitious after the journey. I’m definitely leaning towards easy. Maybe pasta? I saw some pesto in the box. Honestly, I'm mostly just relieved the internet guy is coming tomorrow. I can't function without Netflix. Crucial. Absolutely crucial. Have you figured out the rubbish collection situation yet? It's always the thing people forget about. No, not yet. I saw a couple of bins outside, but no schedule. I’ll have to check the council website later. It's a whole new world of local bureaucracy, isn’t it? It always is. Remember that time in Bristol when we couldn't figure out how to recycle anything? Oh god, yes! We just ended up throwing everything in the general waste. Felt incredibly guilty. Anyway, I think I’ve spotted a Sainsbury’s local down the road. We could walk and grab some milk, maybe a loaf of bread? Perfect. Before we brave the outside world, though… do you have any cigarettes? I feel like I deserve one after all this moving chaos. Yeah, in the box, with the judgemental food. Though, honestly, you’re going to be smelling like paint and smoke. Not a great combination. I’ll risk it. A tiny bit of vice is allowed on moving day.

Honestly, this halloumi and harissa burger is  amazing . You absolutely made the right choice. Oh, it's good! Really good. I was torn between that and the chicken, but the harissa just… called to me. How’s your steak? It’s perfectly medium-rare, exactly how I asked. It’s been ages since I’ve just… sat and  enjoyed  a proper meal. Work’s been mental. Tell me about it! This placement is… an experience, let’s put it that way. So much more hands-on than uni ever was. And the office politics! You wouldn’t believe it. Oh, the politics. Always the politics. Is it all… spreadsheets and meetings? Pretty much! Though I did actually get to go on-site to a new development last week, which was cool. Seeing everything being built from the ground up. Reminded me a bit of that civil engineering module we did. Remember horrifying ourselves trying to calculate load-bearing walls? Oh god, yes! I think I genuinely considered switching courses after that. So, are you still thinking about applying for grad schemes after the placement? Yeah, I think so. Though I’m starting to question everything, honestly. Maybe I should just run away and become a travel blogger. A travel blogger? That’s… a bit of a switch. Where would you even start? I don't know! Somewhere warm, probably. Maybe Thailand? Remember our trip to Thailand after second year? That was insane. Insane doesn’t even  begin  to cover it. Getting lost in Bangkok, almost getting scammed buying a monkey… good times. Your mum was  furious  about the monkey. She was convinced it had rabies! She’s still going on about it, actually. Speaking of mums, how are your parents? Still trying to set you up with every available single man in Essex? You know it. Apparently, the neighbour's son is “a lovely young man, works in finance, very stable”. It’s exhausting. They just want me to settle down, I think. Mine are the same. Though they've backed off a bit since I started the placement. They’re impressed I’m “doing something with my life”. Apparently, a degree in History isn't enough on its own. Oh, don't even get me started. Everyone asks what you’re going to  do  with a History degree. It's like it’s useless. It’s not useless! It teaches you critical thinking and research skills!

Honestly, the amount of times I have to explain to people where Sunderland  is . It's not just… near Newcastle, you know? It’s a whole separate city. And with actual personality, might I add. I get it. Birmingham gets lumped in with ‘the Midlands’ constantly. Like we're all just interchangeable industrial towns. Which, okay, historically… but it’s got a vibrant music scene, incredible food… it’s a proper place. Exactly! People assume ‘North East’ and immediately think grey, industrial, and depressing. Which, look, some bits are, but there are beaches, gorgeous countryside… and the people are brilliant. Proper warm and friendly. You don’t get that same vibe down south, do you? It  is  different. More reserved, generally. Though Cambridge is a bit of a bubble. Everyone's either a stressed-out PhD student or a ridiculously well-adjusted undergraduate. Not much middle ground. How’s the research going, by the way? Still battling with the statistical analysis? Don’t even  start  me on the statistical analysis. It's like trying to wrestle an octopus. I swear, every time I think I’ve got a handle on it, another tentacle wraps around my leg. But yeah, it’s… progressing. Slow progress, but progress nonetheless. It’s fascinating stuff, though, genuinely. The impact of social media on political engagement. Sounds intense. I’m mostly staring at computer screens trying to model complex ecological systems. Equally thrilling, believe me. Speaking of intense things, I saw someone wearing Crocs  with socks  earlier. I honestly thought I was hallucinating. Oh god, no. That’s a fashion crime against humanity. The absolute audacity! I saw someone in a full tracksuit in town this morning. A  full  tracksuit. Like, ready for a marathon, not a Tuesday afternoon shopping trip. It's a bold look. Maybe they're starting a trend. A very, very questionable trend. Remember when everyone was obsessed with those awful slogan jumpers? ‘I’m not bossy, I’m the boss’? Oh my  god . Don’t remind me. I think I owned one. I was very young and easily influenced. You know what I miss, though? Proper indie music. Like early 2000s. Arctic Monkeys, The Strokes… Yes! Now  that  was a good era. Actually, there’s a band playing at The Junction next week, a sort of indie-rock revival thing. I was thinking of checking it out. You fancy it? Ooh, potentially.

So, like, Mr. Henderson in history was going on about the election, right? And he was saying how, like, all politicians are the same and just tell you what you want to hear. Aye, well, there's a grain of truth in that, lad. A good grain. They’ve all got to get voted in, haven’t they? Promises, promises… I remember when Wilson promised us all a land of milk and honey. Never quite materialised, did it? Wilson? Who's that? Oh, goodness me. Prime Minister, a long time ago. Before your dad was even a little lad. A Labour man, he was. Tried to modernise things. A decent fella, I thought. Though, he did have his problems, like they all do. Mr. Henderson said it doesn’t matter who you vote for, the country just gets worse. He said, like, it's all rigged. Rigged? Now, that’s a strong word. I wouldn’t go that far. But it’s true to say things are… complicated. It's not as simple as picking the best person. There’s a lot of things going on behind the scenes. Interest groups, wealthy people pulling strings… it all plays a part. So, like, what’s the point then? Why bother voting? Oh, you always bother voting. Even if you’re just voting against someone. It’s your right, see? My father, he fought in the war for that right. For us to have a say in how the country's run. He wouldn’t have taken kindly to me saying it wasn’t worth it. What was he fighting for exactly? To stop those awful Nazis, mostly. They didn’t believe in freedom, they didn’t believe in letting people have a voice. They wanted to tell everyone what to do. That’s why so many good lads went off to war. To protect our way of life. And voting is a part of that. Okay. But, like, even if you vote, they still build on green fields, don't they? And the trains are always late and stuff. Aye, they do. And the trains are a disgrace. They were better when they were nationalised, you know. But you have to try and make things better, don’t you? You can’t just give up. You've got to use your voice, even if it feels like nobody’s listening. Mr. Henderson said the Conservatives are all about money and the rich getting richer.

Now, Liam, put down the fork when you’re talking, will you? It’s not a very good look, son. Like you’re stabbing the air with it. Sorry, Dad. It’s just… this pasta's really good. He’s right, it  is  good. Your Uncle Seamus sent it over, remember? That pesto is fantastic. Though maybe a little heavy on the garlic for a Tuesday. Garlic keeps the vampires away, dear. Though I doubt you’ll be needing to worry about them with this blood moon coming up. Have you seen the photos? Extraordinary. Aye, I saw a few. Not much good for looking at the stars in Cork city though, too much light pollution. I read it's gonna look all red and stuff. Like in the movies. Can we go outside and see it, Granny? Oh, I’d love to, pet. If the clouds hold off, we’ll bundle up and have a look. Though I suspect it won't be quite as dramatic as the films, dear. They like to exaggerate things, you know. Just like they do with Irish hospitality! That’s true. So, Liam, have you finished your homework for tomorrow? Nearly. Just the maths. It’s really hard. Fractions. Fractions aren’t so bad. It's all about understanding the pieces, like a good puzzle. They used to teach fractions with apples in my day. Slicing apples into halves, quarters… rather messy, as I recall. Though it did make it rather concrete for the children. Good idea. Maybe we can try that with Liam tomorrow, after school. It’s important to have family meals, isn't it? Proper sit-down meals, like this. It’s getting harder to manage with little Alfie, but I’m trying. It is important. We always had family meals when I was growing up. Even if it was just a bit of bread and cheese, we were all at the table together. Can we go to Fitzgerald’s Park tomorrow, Granny? After I finish my homework? Oh, that sounds lovely, darling. We could feed the ducks. And maybe get an ice cream if you're a good boy and finish your fractions! Don’t promise him an ice cream if he doesn't earn it. He'll be expecting it then. Oh, relax, Michael. An ice cream won't hurt. Besides, Granny’s got a soft spot. I do!

So, did you catch any of that Scottish referendum coverage last night? Absolute chaos, wasn't it? A bit of it. Flicked through the news. Honestly, I thought it was going to be closer. Seemed rather decisive in the end, didn't it? Remarkably so. Still, good to see democracy in action, I suppose. Though all that arguing… exhausting. Speaking of exhausting, I had a truly bizarre interview today. Oh? For what? Still looking for someone to cover your classes while you’re… sorting things out? Exactly. And this chap… honestly. Said he'd 'revolutionise' the department. All talk, I suspect. No real substance. He kept using the word 'synergy.' Made my eyes glaze over. Oh, the dreaded synergy. Always a red flag. Sounds like you dodged a bullet. What was he like, generally? Young? Old? Mid-fifties, I reckon. Trying desperately to appear younger, though. Brightly coloured tie, slicked-back hair… and a habit of finishing your sentences. Maddening. Sounds a character. Worse than old Mr. Henderson, then? Remember him? The history teacher who smelled perpetually of mothballs? Oh, far worse. Mr. Henderson was just… eccentric. This one was actively irritating. Honestly, I'd rather have no one. Though head’s putting the pressure on. It'll come right. You always manage. How's your daughter doing, by the way? Haven’t heard much about her lately. She’s good, she’s good. Actually, rather brilliantly, as it happens. Got offered a place on a postgraduate course at Bristol. Bristol! Wonderful! What’s she studying? Marine biology. Always been fascinated with the sea, ever since we used to drag her to the beach as a little girl, protesting all the way. Now she can’t get enough of it. That's fantastic news. She’s a clever one, that girl. You must be proud. Terribly. Though it's a bit… bittersweet, I suppose. Means she’s further away. And with everything else that's going on…well. You haven’t mentioned it much, but… how  are  you holding up, old friend? You seem a bit… subdued lately. Just a bit overwhelmed, to be honest. The job uncertainty, the divorce… it’s a lot. Trying to navigate everything, keep a brave face. It's a bit like trying to bail out a sinking boat with a teacup. It sounds that way. Listen, you know you can talk to me, right? About anything.

Right, so we’re officially leaving Bedfordshire, then. Feels a bit… weird, doesn’t it? It does. Though, honestly, I'm just glad we’ve finally got everything shifted. That kitchen was a nightmare. All those boxes of china your grandmother collected! Seriously, a lifetime supply of floral teacups. Did she  ever  actually use them? Never. Strictly for display. Your mum always said she was saving them for “best.” Best what, no one ever knew. Right, well, Sat Nav says another hour and a half. Anyone fancy a biscuit? I grabbed a packet from the supermarket earlier. Ooh, go on then. Jammy Dodgers? You know me too well. Jammy Dodgers it is. Ann, you okay? You’ve been quiet. Just thinking about Buster. Leaving him with Sarah feels awful. He's been with us for twelve years, you know. He’ll miss the garden. He’ll be fine, Mum. Sarah adores him. And she's got that huge garden, remember? He'll be living the life. Chasing squirrels all day. Yeah, and think of the walks she’ll take him on. Proper countryside walks. He’ll be in his element. I suppose you’re right. Still… feels like leaving a family member. It’s funny how attached you get, isn’t it? Absolutely. It’s amazing the bond you form. Speaking of bonds, did you two manage to sort the tuition fees out? Aaron, you were stressing about it last week. Nearly. I’ve applied for the extra loan, but I’m still waiting to hear back. It’s a bit of a stress, to be honest. It's ridiculous how much everything costs. It is. I’m lucky I’ve got a bit saved from working over the summer, but it won't last forever. Teaching doesn't exactly pay the big bucks. Oh, don't talk about money. Makes my head spin. I was at the supermarket the other day, and I swear a loaf of bread is nearly £2 now. It’s daylight robbery! You wouldn’t believe how much art supplies cost either. Seriously, if I had to pay full price for everything, I’d be bankrupt. Don't even get me started on petrol prices. They’re going through the roof. It’s a wonder anyone can afford to drive these days. This little trip is costing me a fortune already. Speaking of journeys… did you see that documentary about that bloke who tried to break the world record for the longest continuous car journey?

Right, nearly there then, isn’t it? Just past this roundabout. Honestly, this traffic’s been mental since we left Durham. Mental? That's a bit strong, lass. It's a bit busy, aye, but mental… you young ‘uns and your exaggerations. Back in my day,  that  was mental traffic. You couldn’t move for hours, all the way to Manchester and back. Factories belching smoke, it was a proper smog. He’s got a point, actually. This isn’t  that  bad. Still annoying though, especially when you’ve got a schedule to keep. Are we still aiming for lunch at one? Yeah, should be good. Unless, you know, we hit another tractor. Or a flock of sheep. Seriously, the number of times I’ve nearly taken out a sheep on these country roads… Sheep are daft creatures. No road sense at all. Always wandering onto the road, thinking they own the place. Used to be worse when I was a lad, though. Farmers didn’t bother with fences as much. Just let ‘em roam free. That sounds… chaotic. Imagine trying to drive anywhere! Chaotic is an understatement! I once saw a whole herd of cows just blocking the A1. Honestly, a line of cows, just staring at the cars. No one knew what to do. Aye, cows. They’re stubborn beasts, those. More sense than sheep, mind you. They know what they want. And they usually want grass on the other side of the road. I can imagine. Speaking of animals, did you two see that alpaca farm we passed back on the A66? Oh my god, yes! It was brilliant! Alpacas! What’s that even  about ? They looked so fluffy though. I wanted to stop and take a picture, but we were already running a bit late. Alpacas, eh? Fancy that. Never seen an alpaca in me life. Used to know a man who kept pigs, though. Dreadful smell, pigs have. Truly dreadful. I’ve smelled a pig farm before. You’re not kidding. It’s… memorable. You learn to appreciate city smells after that, honestly. Exhaust fumes and questionable takeaway food suddenly smell like roses! Roses? You have a strange idea of roses, lass. Give me the smell of fresh-cut hay any day. Now  that’s  a proper smell. Reminds me of me grandad’s farm. Good times, those. Simple times. Sounds idyllic. Alright, are we turning off here?

Honestly, this shepherd’s pie is lovely, Margaret. You’ve outdone yourself. It is really good, isn’t it? Better than anything I could manage. Though I've been experimenting with sourdough lately…it's a disaster zone, mostly. You know, your mother used to make a shepherd’s pie just like this. Right down to the little potato swirls on top. A proper artist with a potato masher, she was. She was, wasn’t she? Always said presentation was half the battle. Though she’d kill me for saying it, she hated any kind of fuss. Speaking of mothers, have you heard from Auntie Brenda lately? She promised to call about the family get-together in August. Not a peep. Brenda and her punctuality issues. You’d think after seventy-odd years she’d have mastered the concept of time. Oh, don't even start. She was the same in school. Always late for parents’ evening. Mrs. Higgins, my Latin teacher, used to have a vein popping in her forehead every time Brenda strolled in ten minutes after it started. Oh dear. Was Mrs. Higgins as terrifying as everyone says? I’ve heard stories. Terrifying is putting it mildly. She could silence a room with a single glare. And she  detested  latecomers. Said it showed a lack of respect - for her, for the subject, for everything. Latin’s a lost art, isn’t it? I remember struggling with it at school. All those declensions and conjugations… completely baffling. Though I suppose it’s good for the brain. It is. Builds discipline, if nothing else. And the logic is quite elegant, once you get past the initial hurdle. Though to be honest, I haven’t used a single declension since I left teacher training. I'm thinking of joining the local choir. They're always advertising in the village newsletter. It could be fun. And good exercise, I suppose. That’s a lovely idea, love. You always had a good voice. Remember that school production of ‘Oliver!’? You were a fantastic Nancy. Oh goodness, do  not  remind me! The nerves were awful. I nearly lost my voice during ‘As Long As He Needs Me’. But it was good fun, overall. Though I’m quite happy to listen now rather than perform. I was thinking about volunteering somewhere too. I’ve got a lot of free time now I’m not rushing around with deadlines.

Right, so parent’s evening was… interesting. Mr. Davies said you’re really engaged in English, which is lovely, and your writing is fantastic. He was really impressed with your story about the dragon. I  love  dragons. Mine was a sparkly purple one. Mine would be green and fire-breathing! And really, really big. Goodness, yes. Very impressive. But… Maths. Oh. He said you’re really struggling with times tables and you’re getting quite flustered when he asks you questions in class. He suggested we do some extra practice at home. Times tables are boring. They are, aren’t they? But they’re important. We can make them less boring. Maybe some games? Or we could use that app I showed you? The one with the little monsters? That’s the one. We could do ten minutes every night after dinner, okay? Before pudding. Hmm… okay. But can I have extra sprinkles on my pudding if I try really hard? We'll see. Now, eat your broccoli. Broccoli looks like little trees. It does, doesn’t it? Little green trees. And speaking of things that are green… World Book Day is coming up! Have you thought about what you want to dress up as? I want to be Hermione Granger! With the wand and everything. That’s a brilliant idea! And Jackson? I want to be… a pirate! With a sword and an eye patch. And a parrot! Excellent! We’ll have to raid the dress-up box. Right, after school tomorrow, Mrs. Peterson said she’s taking Lily and a few others to that little circus that’s set up near the park. Are you happy for her to take her? Yes! I love the circus! Will there be elephants? I don't think so, darling. It's a small circus. But there will be acrobats and clowns and maybe a tightrope walker. Can  I  go? Hmm, that's a bit tricky. It's mostly for Year 2, and you're still in Year 1. Maybe another time. We can book tickets for a proper circus during the holidays. Oh. Okay. We could go to the cinema instead? There's that new film… what's it called? The one with the penguins? Pingu! No, not Pingu! This is a proper film, with penguins who go on adventures. Ooh, penguins! Okay, maybe cinema. Although… I was reading this thing online last night and it was really weird.

So, did young Leo manage to get that shift at the curtain shop this week? He was keen enough on earning a few bob. He did, actually. Mrs. O’Malley, the owner, said he’s a good boy, very polite. Mostly he's folding fabrics and sweeping floors, but she let him help measure a window for a customer yesterday, apparently. He was delighted with himself. More peas! Always a priority, young man. Always a priority. So, folding fabrics, is he? Good practice for a future interior designer, maybe? Don't put ideas into his head now, Margaret! He’ll be wanting velvet wallpaper and chandeliers next. Anyway, we really need to nail down the details for Oisin’s birthday. It's creeping up on us quickly. I was thinking we could book the community hall again? It’s a good space, and he loved having all his friends there last year. A good idea, dear. Plenty of room for running about. Though, last year, half the entertainment was watching  you  trying to control them! A slight exaggeration, perhaps. We could get a bouncy castle again? They all adored that. Bouncy castle booked. Consider it done. But we need to think about food. I’m not a fan of all those sugary party treats. Perhaps some fruit skewers and… And a healthy selection of crisps? Let’s be realistic. Alright, alright. A controlled selection of crisps. Speaking of controlled, have you noticed how Oisin’s speech has developed? He’s started using phrases he definitely picks up from somewhere… Oh? What kind of phrases? Well, yesterday he told me, very seriously, that I was “absolutely scandalous.” I nearly choked on my coffee! Scandalous! That's fantastic. Where on earth did he hear that?! No idea! I suspect Leo’s been watching too many of those old movies. He's got a thing for black and white films. I tell you what, have you managed to sort out being the treasurer for the garage owners’ association? They’re a handful, those lads. Always looking for a shortcut. It's a thankless task. I'm trying to get them to properly account for everything. It’s like pulling teeth. And then there’s the whole issue of tax on the rental houses… It’s a nightmare, the paperwork involved. Don’t even get me started on the paperwork. It’s enough to drive you mad.

Right, I’m telling you, Scrabble is rigged. Absolutely rigged. Rigged? How so? It's just a random draw of letters. No, no, it's the distribution, innit? You  never  get the good letters when you need them. Like, I had a double word score space, and all I could pull was a J, a Q, and three vowels. A J and a Q! Who builds words with those? Aye, that’s classic. You’re always hoarding them, hoping for the perfect moment, and the perfect moment never comes. It’s the Scrabble curse. You’re both just having bad luck. The distribution is designed to balance high and low scoring letters. It’s a mathematical thing, probabilities and all that. Oh, probabilities, is it? Well, probabilities clearly favour people who enjoy building words like “za” and “qi”. I’m trying to build proper words here, like “beautiful” and “incredible”, and I’m stuck with consonants nobody’s ever heard of. I had a similar situation last week. Holding onto an X for ages, waiting for an opportunity, then ended up using it to make “axe”. Axe! It felt… underwhelming. Okay, but an X is a high-scoring letter. You maximized your points. That’s the whole point, isn't it? It’s not  just  about points, is it? It's about the artistry! The linguistic challenge! Making a beautiful, complex word. She's got a point, actually. It feels a bit… soulless just going for maximum points with the lowest effort. Like, just slapping down a "za" for a quick win. I’m just saying, strategically, it’s the best move. I used to play with my Gran, and she was ruthless. She’d use every single tile just to block you, even if it didn’t score her anything. Your Gran sounds terrifying. She was. She took Scrabble very seriously. It was a… competitive environment. Have you guys ever tried Boggle? That’s a bit more frantic, less strategic. It's just a race against the clock to find words. Boggle’s good, aye, but it’s just shouting words at each other. There’s no finesse. No careful planning. So you  want  the careful planning, even if it means you end up staring at a rack full of useless letters? Absolutely! Suffering builds character. And then, when I  finally  manage to unload all my tiles in one go, it’s glorious.

Honestly, I napped for like, four hours solid today. Four. I feel like I've wasted the entire day. No way! Four hours? You needed it though, didn't you? You were flagging at Hannah's party. You were practically horizontal by ten. I was  resting my eyes . Strategic resting. But still, it feels wrong. It’s a Saturday! I should be…doing things. Like what? More uni work? Don’t torture yourself. You deserve a nap. Speaking of which, remember that time Liam fell asleep  standing up  at pre-drinks before Sophie’s birthday? Oh my god, yes! He genuinely just…toppled. Like a tree. And he didn't even wake up! Holly had to physically hold him upright while she ordered him a Red Bull. It was the funniest thing. I've got a picture somewhere, I'll send it. Hold on… scrolling on phone … Aha! Here. Oh, bless him. He looks so peaceful, completely oblivious to the impending doom of being woken up. He was wearing that awful Hawaiian shirt too. The one his gran got him? Iconique. He swore he’d burn it if he ever had to wear it again. Honestly, he's such a drama queen. Have you spoken to Chloe recently? I haven’t seen her since that…incident at the quiz night. Oh, god. Don’t even mention that. She's still mortified. Apparently, she's blocked Ben on everything. Wow. That escalated quickly. What exactly  did  he say? I only caught the tail end of it. Something about her general knowledge being…questionable? It was worse than questionable. He said she thought Marie Curie invented the microwave. And then he just kept repeating “Microwave Curie!” It was awful. Oh, cringey. Classic Ben. He doesn't realise when to stop. She's got a right to be furious. Exactly! And then she tried to argue back with facts no one had ever heard of. It was a mess. It's why I avoid pub quizzes now. Too much potential for disaster. Honestly, same. They’re just…stressful. Plus, the music's always terrible. Remember that time they played nothing but ABBA for two hours? Don’t remind me. I nearly walked out. I mean, I like ABBA, but there's a limit. And then  they  started a singalong. It was horrifying. It was like being trapped in a Mamma Mia! musical against my will.

Right, so I’ve been through the agenda for the council planning committee meeting again. And honestly, it’s a mess. A mess how? Is it the volume of applications, or is it… Councillor Davies being particularly verbose again? Both, actually. But mostly the structure. It’s just all over the place. They’ve got the outline for the new housing development slotted in  after  the retrospective application for the garden shed. A garden shed? Seriously? They’re dedicating committee time to a garden shed? Apparently, it’s a ‘substantial structure’ that’s been erected without planning permission, and a neighbour has complained it’s blocking their light. Honestly, the drama. Incredible. So, the housing development—the thing that will actually impact the entire area—is being dealt with almost as an afterthought? Precisely. And they’ve scheduled the public speaking slots for the housing development  before  the presentation of the plans. Which means people will be speaking about a plan they haven’t even seen yet. That’s… spectacularly bad planning, even for them. Is anyone going to point this out? I’m planning to. I’ve drafted a few points, but I’m worried it’ll come across as overly critical. I don’t want to alienate anyone. Especially not Councillor Henderson. Henderson’s a lost cause. He’ll support anything as long as it involves ribbon-cutting. Just be firm. Highlight the logical inconsistencies. Explain how having public speaking before the presentation undermines the whole process. You're right. It’s just… I’ve been on this committee for two years now, and it’s consistently frustrating. It feels like they’re deliberately making it difficult. They are. It's a combination of incompetence and a genuine desire to avoid anything resembling transparency. Remember the battle over the verge planting? Don't remind me. Still can’t believe they approved the concrete bollards. Anyway, back to the agenda. I’m also concerned about the wording of the recommendation for the community centre refurbishment. It’s incredibly vague. Vague how? It just says “improvements should be made to enhance the community benefit”. No specifics about what those improvements should be, or how they’ll be funded. They’re essentially giving the contractors free rein. That’s… worrying. Have you looked into the contractors at all? Briefly. They’ve got a pretty patchy record, apparently. Lots of projects running over budget and behind schedule.

Honestly, I am  starving . I’ve been surviving on biscuits all day. And instant coffee. It’s a tragic state of affairs, really. Sounds about right for a Monday. I managed to grab a sandwich at work, but it was… underwhelming. Turkey and cranberry, but the cranberry sauce tasted suspiciously like jam. Oh, no. That’s a crime against sandwiches. What are we having then? I was thinking pasta? I could really use some carbs. Pasta sounds good. Although… Mrs. Higgins was having a full-on shouting match with someone on her phone in the garden again this morning. It’s always something with her, isn’t it? Honestly, you’d think she’d run out of people to yell at. Oh, bless her. She’s a gift, that woman. Remember when she accused old Mr. Davies of letting his cat poo in her flowerbeds? And it turned out to be a badger? Oh my god, yes! The outrage! She was furious. He was practically in tears trying to explain it wasn’t his cat. Speaking of outrage, have you seen what happened with… oh, never mind. It’s depressing news. Lay it on me. I need a distraction. Is it more political nonsense? Sadly, yes. Another MP caught doing something… questionable. Honestly, it’s just endless. Anyway, enough doom and gloom. Did you manage to get that dress you were looking at online? The blue one? I did! It arrived this morning, and it fits perfectly. I'm planning on wearing it on Saturday. We’re going to that new cocktail bar with Chloe and Sarah, remember? Oh yes! Perfect. That place looks really nice. Though I’m dreading the inevitable conversation about men. Last time we all went out, it was  all  anyone talked about. Tell me about it. Sarah was going on about how ‘all good men are taken’ and Chloe was dissecting every single text message she’d ever received from anyone even remotely attractive. It’s exhausting. Honestly, sometimes I think I’m better off just adopting seventeen cats. Although, then  I ’d be the crazy cat lady. You’d rock the crazy cat lady look. Seriously. You’d have amazing cardigans. Have you heard from Gemma lately? From school? I was trying to find her on Instagram, but I couldn’t find an account. Oh, Gemma! I think she’s living in Australia now? I saw something on Facebook a while ago, she was posting pictures of beaches and koalas.

Right, honestly, the state of this place. I swear, dust multiplies when you’re not looking. You say that every time. It’s not  that  bad. Not that bad? The coffee table’s practically a geological dig site. Remember when Gran came round? She practically needed a hazmat suit. Gran exaggerates. She’s lived through two World Wars, a bit of dust doesn’t phase her. Besides, I’ve been busy. I had that meeting with Mr. Davies today about the new autism assessment protocols. Oh aye? How'd that go? Sounds proper head-wrecking. It was…lengthy. He’s got this weird obsession with using NLP techniques. Says it can unlock hidden potential in kids with communication difficulties. NLP? Seriously? Feels a bit…woo-woo, doesn’t it? Like something you’d see advertised on late-night telly with that bloke promising to make you a millionaire. Remember those adverts? Exactly! It's all about ‘anchoring’ and ‘reframing’ and all this jargon. I tried to explain the neurobiological basis of dyslexia but he just kept going on about positive affirmations. Blimey. Sounds like he’s been reading too many self-help books. Speaking of telly, did you see that advert for that new washing machine? The one where it’s cleaning someone’s muddy football kit? It’s amazing how they make everything look so…perfect. Everything's staged, isn't it? And filters. It's all filters. I saw a TikTok the other day showing how much editing goes into those 'natural' makeup looks. It's ridiculous. Don’t get me started on TikTok. It's a total time suck. I was scrolling through it for an hour yesterday. Found myself looking at videos of people organizing their spice racks. Spice racks! You and your spice racks. You'd be brilliant at a car boot sale, honestly. You’d haggle the price of a rusty bucket down to a tenner. I have a gift! My dad practically raised me on car boot sales. He could sniff out a bargain a mile away. Remember that time he got that antique clock for a fiver? Turned out to be worth a fortune. Oh God, yes! And Mum was furious because it took up the entire hallway for weeks. She kept tripping over it. Good times. I'm thinking of trying to get rid of some stuff on eBay actually. My phone’s full of photos of things I need to list.

Honestly, the traffic was  brutal  getting here. I left ages ago and still ended up circling the Aston Expressway for about twenty minutes. Oh, tell me about it. I took a back route, hoping to avoid the worst, but even those were jammed. Birmingham seems to have permanently entered peak hour. It’s just getting worse, isn’t it? They keep promising improvements, but… well, you know. Speaking of worse, has anyone tried that new Thai place near the Mailbox? I heard mixed reviews. Ooh, no, not yet. Is it authentically spicy, or that watered-down ‘British Thai’ flavour? That’s the crucial question. I had a disastrous Pad Thai last month that was basically noodles in sweet tomato ketchup. Oh, the horror! You're right to be discerning. I’ve been trying to eat more healthily lately, which is proving…challenging. I downloaded one of those meal planning apps, you know, to track calories and all that, but it’s just so dreary. Which one did you get? I’ve been tempted by MyFitnessPal, but I’m worried it’ll just make me obsessed. It’s called ‘PlateJoy’ or something. It’s…intense. It tells you to eat things like quinoa and kale for breakfast. Honestly, I need something more substantial to get me through the day. I’m a Yorkshire woman, I need a proper breakfast! Ha! Fair enough. I’ve finally started using Spotify properly. I was so late to the party, but it’s brilliant for discovering new music. They’ve got these curated playlists that are actually really good. Oh yeah, Spotify’s great. I’m still a bit old-fashioned and cling to my vinyl, though. It’s just…different, isn’t it? More tactile. I get that. I've been on a documentary kick lately. Watched one about the history of journalism the other night, and it was… grim. Basically, it was a lengthy explanation of how everything’s terrible and my job is slowly disappearing. Oh,  don't  say that! You're brilliant at what you do. The industry's changing, that's all. It needs good journalists like you. Exactly. And there’s still a demand for good writing. I’m working on a feature about the impact of local radio on communities. It's proving harder than I thought, sifting through all the council reports! Speaking of changes, any progress on the house hunt?

…and honestly, finding anywhere to live was a nightmare. Everything was either a poky little flat above a shop, or a crumbling Victorian terrace that needed a fortune spent on it. We ended up renting, of course. Couldn't possibly afford to buy back then. What was it like for you, David? Coming down here as a dentist, must have been a shock from Birmingham. A shock is an understatement! I remember driving down the M5, thinking, “Good Lord, what have I let myself in for?” The interview itself was… interesting. The hospital was ancient, practically falling apart. One of the senior surgeons had a pipe that he constantly relit with a lighter that smelled faintly of disinfectant! Anyway, I got the job, obviously. Then the  real  fun began – finding somewhere to live. Ah, yes, the housing market of the 60s. A truly bizarre landscape. I remember when I first came to the university here, a friend and I shared a house, well, a glorified shed really, with a family of six. It had no central heating, and the bathroom was outside. Still, it was cheap. Very cheap. We were lucky, I suppose. We managed to find a semi-detached house in Filton. It hadn't been modernised, to put it mildly. Avocado bathroom suite, orange shag pile… it was a sight to behold. But it was ours, eventually. And it was a good area for the kids, which was the main thing. Avocado bathrooms… oh, the memories! We had one of those. It was the height of fashion, apparently. Then everything went brown in the 70s, didn't it? Remember brown Formica? Oh, don’t even get me started on Formica! It was everywhere. The waiting room in my surgery was completely covered in the stuff. Made it look like a particularly depressing cafe. Where did you meet your wife, Arthur? Now that’s a story. I met Margaret at a conference in Leeds. She was teaching English as a foreign language, and I was presenting a paper on… well, something terribly academic that nobody understood. We ended up arguing about it, naturally. And the rest, as they say, is history. What about you, Roger? I met Brenda at a teacher training college in Bristol. She was training to be a primary school teacher, and I was doing my PGCE. We bonded over shared horror stories about difficult pupils and endless marking.

…and then of course, the whole thing with the ceramics. Honestly, people would bring me things, dreadful things, thinking they were valuable! I had to learn very quickly how to politely tell them their grandmother’s “antique” was actually made in the 1970s. Oh, you must have some stories. I imagine a lot of disappointment. It’s funny, isn’t it, what people assign value to? Sentiment, mostly I suppose. Exactly! Sentiment and wishful thinking. It was a good life though, a very good life. Kept me busy. What about you, dear? Speech therapy… that must have been incredibly rewarding, but also quite draining, I should think. It was. Both, actually. Massively rewarding to see a child finally communicate, to unlock that for them. But you carry their stories with you, you know? The struggles, the families... Especially the ones with acquired brain injuries. So much loss. I can imagine. Losing the ability to speak… horrifying. It’s a strange thing, speech, isn't it? We take it so for granted. I often think about my own childhood, and how much I  didn't  say. My mother… well, she wasn’t one for a lot of conversation. Oh? Was she a quiet woman? Quiet doesn't quite cover it. More… distant. She'd had a difficult life, I think. Lost her own mother young. She threw herself into the farm, really. Just worked and worked and worked. Never much room for silliness or, well, feelings, really. We lived out near Exmoor, beautiful countryside, but awfully isolated. I used to spend hours wandering the fields, making up stories in my head. That’s probably where the art came from, I suppose. Escapism. That makes sense. A way to create your own world. I grew up in Sydney, very different. Lots of noise, lots of people. My father was a shipwright, building yachts. He was a boisterous man, always laughing, always telling stories. A real character. Though, looking back, he expected a lot. I felt quite a bit of pressure to… succeed. Succeed in what way? Oh, he wanted me to be a doctor, or a lawyer. Something “respectable”. He wasn't terribly keen on the speech pathology, thought it was a bit…fuzzy. Not concrete enough. Typical, I suppose. But I loved it. Really loved working with people. Did you always know you wanted to be an artist? Goodness, no. I dabbled.

Right, so onions are caramelising nicely. You sure we’ve got enough balsamic? Last time felt a bit… lacking. Yeah, I got a bigger bottle this time. It’s lurking somewhere in that cupboard of doom. Honestly, it's a black hole in there. I think I saw a bag of marshmallows disappear in there last month. Marshmallows? What were marshmallows doing in the cupboard of doom? Don’t ask. It was a late-night impulse buy. I was stressed about the bake orders and suddenly needed…fluffy sugar. I barely remember it. Did you ever end up getting that new stencil for the cake decorating? Oh, yeah! It arrived yesterday. It’s the snowflake one, for Christmas stuff. It's  really  intricate. I tried it on a practice cake board, nearly had a breakdown. So fiddly. Ooh, send me a picture! I need some inspo. Christmas orders are already starting to roll in. People are going mad for mince pie macarons this year. It’s ridiculous. Mince pie macarons? That’s… a choice.  A knock at the door. Speaker_3 enters, carrying a large box.  Alright, you two! Sorry I’m late, the delivery driver was having a “moment” with his sat nav. And look what I’ve snagged! Oh my god, is that…the gingerbread house kit?! The one and only! Found it in a little shop near the market. They were selling out fast, apparently. I thought we  needed  it for our Christmas tradition. You are a legend. I was mentally preparing to construct one from scratch, which would have ended in disaster. No way! We're aiming for a festive masterpiece, not a structural engineering failure. So, what’s for dinner? Smells amazing. Caramelised onion and balsamic tart, with a side of…Christmas planning. We were just talking about the ridiculousness of mince pie macarons. Oh, don’t even get me started! People request the weirdest things. I had someone ask for a cake shaped like a Brussel sprout last year. A  Brussel sprout ! Seriously? Dead serious. Anyway, Christmas decorations. Have you guys thought about it yet? I’m thinking maximalist this year. Fairy lights  everywhere . I'm on board with maximalist. I bought a giant inflatable snowman. It's currently taking up half my hallway. An inflatable snowman? You’re really going for it, aren’t you? I think I’ll just stick to a tree and maybe some tasteful garlands.

Honestly, Cambridge feels… smaller every time we come. Don’t you think? It's lovely, of course, but just… contained. Yeah, I guess so. It’s definitely not London, that’s for sure. Feels a bit like a bubble, especially when term’s not running. More like a particularly posh village. A very  expensive  posh village. Though, thinking about it… have you actually started looking at houses properly yet? Not just scrolling Rightmove on your phone, but genuinely looking at estate agents? Mum, we talked about this. I’m finishing my thesis. That’s… kind of the priority. I know, I know. Of course. But the thesis  will  finish eventually. And then what? You can’t just drift, darling. You need a plan. Even a vague one. Vague is good. I’m good with vague. I’ve been looking, a little. Mostly at places… well, just outside Cambridge, really. Somewhere with a garden, ideally. Outside Cambridge? Why? You spent three years getting a degree  in  Cambridge. Surely you want to be closer to the action. London is always an option, you know. London’s… a lot. And expensive. Even more than Cambridge, I think. And I don’t know if I want to jump straight into  that . Plus, I’d like a bit of space. Somewhere to… breathe. Breathe? You sound like your father when he was having a mid-life crisis and wanted to buy a smallholding in Norfolk. Don't go buying a smallholding, please. No smallholding, I promise. Just a house with a garden. Maybe a shed. For… thinking. Right. Thinking in a shed. Sounds… idyllic. What about Oxford? Have you considered applying for post-doc work there? It's closer to London, better transport links. Oxford… I hadn’t really. It feels a bit… competitive. And, honestly, a bit…  Oxford . What does that even mean? You know. Pretentious. Overly polished. It’s not exactly a vibe I'm going for right now. I'm not sure I have the stamina for another round of intense academic rivalry. Well, you’ve certainly handled Cambridge. And, speaking of stamina, have you spoken to Aunt Carol recently? She was asking about you. Said she was worried you weren’t eating properly. Oh, Carol. She always worries. I told her I was fine, just… busy. And probably surviving on instant coffee and biscuits. That’s not a diet, darling. Honestly. Your grandmother would be appalled.

It’s just…it’s amazing to be back, isn’t it? It feels so different seeing it all through alumni eyes. I barely recognised the Squire Law Library after five years! Completely. I feel like a visitor. Everything’s so shiny and new. I remember it being… well, a bit more worn, shall we say? Did you have Professor Armitage for Land Law? Armitage? Oh, yes. A formidable man. Kept us all on our toes. He’d start a lecture mid-sentence, expecting us all to be perfectly up to speed with the previous week’s nuances. I’ve probably forgotten more about Land Law than either of you have learned! Oh, I definitely remember him! He was…intense. I did his module on Property Rights, actually. It was fascinating, though. Though, honestly, I’m using very little of it in my current role. I’m a Language Research Coordinator now. Oh, interesting! I’m an administrator in the same department. It’s a bit less academic, but still involves a lot of language work – mostly transcribing interviews and data analysis. It's a good fit. Language work? Fascinating. I spent a year excavating a village in Syria back in the…oh, must be forty years ago now. Absolutely crucial to have someone on the team who could understand the local dialects. We uncovered a trove of incredibly old pottery, but it was the stories the villagers told us, the local folklore interwoven with the archaeological finds, that truly brought everything to life. Wow, that sounds incredible! I studied Mandarin Chinese as part of my undergraduate degree. It's so different to anything I’d encountered before. The characters, the tones…it was a challenge, but a rewarding one. Do you speak any other languages, Professor? A little French, a smattering of Arabic – picked that up during my time in the Middle East. You learn quickly when you’re trying to negotiate for water rights in the desert! Arab culture is so deeply rooted in oral tradition, in storytelling. Their historical understanding is often preserved through poetry and elaborate narratives, not just written texts. That’s a really good point. It's easy to get caught up in focusing on the written record and forget that a huge amount of history is passed down through generations verbally. It must’ve been a completely different experience excavating in Syria compared to, say, somewhere in England.

Honestly, this uni workload is insane. I’m genuinely starting to question my life choices. Like, did I  need  a Masters in…well, whatever this is? Tell me about it. Baking’s physically exhausting, yeah, but at least you finish a loaf and you’re like, “Right, tangible result.” You guys are just…writing essays that no one reads. Haha, true. It’s the same with the café. Long hours, but at least people are enjoying a coffee or a cake. Feels productive. Though, I had a customer yesterday who tried to pay with Monopoly money? No way! Seriously? That's… peak post-lockdown behaviour. You get all sorts, don't you? Speaking of peak behaviour, have you seen that video going viral of the guy trying to parallel park a boat? Oh my god, yes! It's incredible. The commitment to failure is just… inspiring. Makes my essay deadlines seem a little less catastrophic. It’s the little details, isn’t it? The way he just keeps  steering  into the lamppost. And the guy filming is just cackling. It’s funny ‘cause it’s relatable. We’ve all had moments like that, where we’ve just stubbornly continued down a disastrous path. Absolutely. It’s the human condition, basically. You know, it makes me think about how weird it is that we all put ourselves through so much education just to end up…doing stuff like this. I mean, I spent three years learning how to make films, and now I spend half my time trying to convince people to fund my weird art projects. It’s class, isn’t it? Like, my dad keeps saying I’ve got it easy because I went to uni, but then he started work at fourteen and built a business from nothing. It’s just… different expectations. Yeah, my mum always says education is the key, but she left school at sixteen and got a really good job. It just feels like the rules keep changing. And some people just aren't built for the academic system. My cousin, Liam, he’s brilliant. Properly clever. But he’s dyslexic and absolutely  hated  school. He’s a mechanic now, and he’s fantastic. He can fix anything. He’s way more skilled with his hands than I am. That’s so true. Actually, I know a couple of people who were diagnosed with dyslexia later in life, and it suddenly made so much sense why they’d struggled at school.

Honestly, this pint is… okay. But it’s not the same as it was last time, is it? They’ve changed something. You say that every time, darling. It’s the same beer. You're just being critical. You’ve been critical about everything since that email from the university. Well, it  is  unsettling! They’re talking about restructuring the whole department. Restructuring! What does that even  mean ? It sounds ominous. And after I just got tenure track. It probably means they’re shuffling some admin around. They always do this. It’s bureaucracy. Don’t catastrophize. Easy for you to say, you're in the safe zone with the History department. They practically worship you over there. Mine’s… Literature. Perennially underfunded and always “under review”. That’s not true! You're brilliant. They’d be mad to let you go. Though, honestly, the whole thing is a symptom of what’s going on with funding in general, isn't it? This government… Honestly, the tax hikes are just ridiculous. Tell me about it. We’re barely breaking even this month with the mortgage rates the way they are. And don’t even get me started on the energy bills. It’s practically daylight robbery. I know. And then they have the audacity to talk about “fiscal responsibility”. I saw a thing on Newsnight last night, they were interviewing some economist… Oh god, don’t. I can barely handle the thought of another political debate. I switched off  Question Time  last week. It was just shouting. Pure shouting. And that Fiona Bruce… she just lets them get away with everything. She does, doesn’t she? Completely ineffective. Did you catch that new drama on BBC?  The Silencing ? No, I haven’t had a chance. Been too busy worrying about my job security and impending financial ruin. Is it any good? It's… captivating. Bit bleak, admittedly. A lot of grey skies and secrets. But really well-acted. It’s about a small coastal town and a series of disappearances no one seems to care about. Sounds cheerful. Maybe I need something a bit lighter. I saw an advert for that baking competition,  The Great British Bake Off . That’s harmless enough. You and your baking shows. Honestly, you'd think you'd be inspired to actually  bake  something. I might! Maybe. If I'm not too busy panicking about losing my livelihood.

Honestly, this quiche is lovely, Margaret. Did you use that cheddar from the farmers' market? It is good isn’t it? And yes, I did! It makes all the difference. Though, it was a bit pricey, even for a good cheddar. Everything seems to be going up these days. Everything  is  going up, Beatrice. It’s scandalous. Still, a good quiche is worth a little extra, wouldn’t you say? Reminds me of your mother’s, actually. She made a mean quiche Lorraine. Oh, she did. She always had a little nutmeg in hers, I remember. Never told a soul, it was her secret ingredient. I’ve tried to replicate it, but it’s never quite the same. Maybe you should ask her? If you can get through to her on the phone, that is. She’s become quite the technophobe lately, hasn’t she? Don’t I know it! I tried to show her how to use FaceTime last week, and she nearly threw the iPad at me. Said it was ‘the devil’s work.’ Your mother always was a character. Remember when she insisted the television was making the cat go cross-eyed? Oh, good heavens, yes! We practically had to hide the remote control from her. Speaking of television, have you two seen that new David Attenborough series? The one about coral reefs? I’ve recorded the first episode, haven't had a chance to watch it yet. Is it good? Wonderful, absolutely wonderful. The photography is stunning. Though it’s rather depressing to see how much damage has been done. Makes you feel helpless, doesn’t it? It does. Though, I do find it comforting to know there are people like Attenborough who are dedicated to raising awareness. It’s far better than burying your head in the sand. Definitely. It’s easy to get overwhelmed, though. I was reading an article about microplastics the other day… it’s scary stuff. Made me think twice about using glitter at Christmas this year. Glitter! Goodness me. You are a conscientious girl, you are. Now, I was talking to young Thomas yesterday – my grandson, you remember? – and he was telling me all about this new game he’s playing, something called ‘Fortnite.’ Utterly baffling. Apparently, you shoot people with… well, I didn't really understand. Oh, I’ve heard of that one. All the children are playing it, apparently.

So, what were you up to all afternoon, Leo? Still glued to that… whatever it is you play? It's called ‘Realm of Champions’, Dad! And I wasn’t  glued  to it. I paused it to have lunch. And then I was talking to Ben online. Oh, Ben from school? That's nice. It’s good you’re keeping in touch with your friends, even when you’re inside. Are you remembering to take breaks, though? Eyesight and all that. Yeah, Mum, I know. Every twenty minutes. It tells me to. It’s got a timer. Smart game. I suppose they have to think of everything these days. Did you win any epic battles? Or slay any dragons? I got to level 17. And I almost beat Gareth in a duel, but he disconnected right at the end! It's so annoying. Oh, that  is  annoying. Deliberate, probably. Sounds stressful. Much more peaceful over here. Finn has been… relentless with the teddy bears today. Absolutely relentless. Oh, he loves his teddies. Did you manage a walk with him? We did. Around the park. He insisted on “riding” Bartholomew - the big brown one - like a horse the entire time. My arms are killing me. Bartholomew? It's his name. Finn named him. He’s very serious about it. Anyway, Bartholomew nearly took me down a few times. He’s a powerful steed, apparently. It's lovely to see him so happy though. They grow up so fast, don't they? It feels like yesterday he was tiny and just cuddling them. He always tries to grab my teddies when I'm home for visits. He thinks they're his. He tries to claim all visiting toys as his own. Ruthless negotiator, that one. That's a good way to put it. He's learning from the best – you and your bartering skills in the shops! Hey! I get good deals. It's an art form! Can I have some dessert? In a minute, Leo. Finish your dinner first. Honestly, you'd think a growing boy was starving. He's got your appetite there, alright. I'm not surprised he wants dessert. Oh look at Finn, he’s trying to feed Bartholomew his broccoli. He’s a kind little soul, isn’t he? He is. And Bartholomew seems very appreciative. Though I suspect he’d prefer a biscuit. Does this conversation fulfill the requirements?

Right then, so the turkey’s ordered, is it? From Thompson’s? Yes, lovely bird. A proper one, not one of those frozen ones. Though frankly, I doubt anyone could tell the difference once it's covered in gravy. That’s the truth of it, isn’t it? It’s all about the trimmings. Though I'm bringing the stuffing, as always. My secret recipe. Ooh, yes! Your stuffing is the best. It really is! It's got… what’s in it, Mr. Davies? Sausage meat? Sausage meat, cranberries, apple, a little bit of nutmeg… the precise proportions are a closely guarded secret, naturally. Ha! A secret, eh? Well, you can’t take it with you. Though speaking of taking things with you, the drive down here was a nightmare. Traffic backed up all the way from Attleborough. Oh dear. That A11 is a menace. Is the car still behaving itself, dear? I keep saying you need to get it serviced. It's alright, it’s alright. Sound as a pound. Though I did notice a little rattle. Probably just a loose biscuit in the door pocket. Always a biscuit, isn't it? Gran, did you see Ethan’s new horse? It’s absolutely huge! It's a proper shire horse. Oh, is it? Lovely boy, Ethan. Always had a way with animals. Though rather distracted by young ladies these days, I hear. He likes Chloe! But she doesn’t really like him back. She’s got a boyfriend. Yeah, Liam. He’s in my art class. He's really good at painting. Liam, eh? What sort of painting does he do? Landscapes? Portraits? Mostly abstract stuff. Really colourful. It's good. Though I prefer drawing. Good to have a creative outlet. Keeps you sane. I've got a class doing a still life at the moment. Apples and oranges. Surprisingly difficult, actually. Getting the light right. Oh yes, still life. It's all very well, but give me a good biography any day. I’m reading one about Queen Victoria at the moment. Fascinating woman. Queen Victoria, eh? A bit serious for my taste. I prefer a good war story. Though I can't remember what I was reading last. My memory's going. It’s just age, Arthur. Don't worry about it. Although, perhaps you should get the car serviced. A rattling biscuit might just be the tip of the iceberg.

Honestly, work was… something else today. Old Mrs. Higgins decided she was a professional opera singer in the middle of her medication round. Oh, bless her. She's a character, that one. Still, you’ve dealt with worse, haven't you? Remember Mr. Peterson and the time he insisted the pigeons were government spies? Don’t remind me! That was a  long  shift. It’s just… exhausting sometimes, you know? People being lonely, or scared, or just needing someone to talk to. It’s more than just giving pills and checking charts. Sounds rough, Mum. You deserve a massive glass of wine and a night in. Not another shift, definitely not. Tell me about it. Though, speaking of needing someone to talk to, I bumped into Sharon from school today. She’s… well, she’s not doing great. Her husband's been made redundant, and she’s really worried about everything. Oh, poor Sharon. That’s awful news. Have you offered to help in any way? I did. Just listening, mainly. She said she doesn’t want to burden anyone. Classic Sharon. We’re going for coffee next week. She just needs to vent, I think. That’s kind of you, Mum. It’s the little things, right? Hey, did you decide what you’re getting Dad for his birthday? It’s creeping up on us quickly. I’ve been racking my brain. He says he doesn’t  need  anything. Which, translated from Dad-speak, means he wants something expensive but doesn’t want to admit it. Honestly! Maybe some nice leather gardening gloves? He’s been complaining about his hands getting cold. A bit… practical, isn’t it? He used to go on about wanting a telescope. Still does, actually. He thinks he’ll spot aliens. He does, doesn’t he? He's convinced. Though, a telescope might be pushing it. It's a fairly sizeable birthday present. We could pool our money? Or maybe a subscription to a stargazing magazine? A compromise? Good idea! Or... I saw this incredibly tacky alien-shaped garden gnome online. Just as a joke. Please, no. My gardening reputation is barely intact as it is. Actually, what are we all doing this weekend? Anything planned? I fancy a pub lunch. I’m free. I might need a pub lunch to recover from Mrs. Higgins’ arias. I’m in! I finished that big project at work, so I'm officially free to do absolutely nothing, or graze in a pub.

Well I was talking to Margaret yesterday and you wouldn't believe what she told me. Apparently, old Mr. Henderson… his wife found out about his… well, his mistress. And apparently, it’s been going on for  years . Years, you say? Goodness me. Him? Always seemed a quiet sort. People are rarely what they seem, aren’t they? Though honestly, infidelity isn’t exactly news-worthy these days. It’s practically a national pastime. It’s more sad than anything, really. All that deception. I imagine it's awful for the wife. Poor woman. She’s absolutely devastated. Apparently, she’s threatening divorce. After forty years! Forty years! That's a long time to be carrying on like that. Makes you wonder what goes on behind closed doors, doesn’t it? It does. Though, thinking about it, remember that awful party at the Vicarage last summer? The atmosphere was dreadful. Mrs. Abernathy was practically glued to young David, the new curate. Oh, don’t remind me. Awkward doesn't even begin to cover it. She barely spoke to her husband all evening. Speaking of awkward, have you lot managed to get all your Christmas shopping done? I’m dreading going to the shops. It’s always such a scrum. I’ve got most of it sorted. Got little Timmy that train set he wanted. Though I’m still struggling with a present for your daughter. She's so difficult to buy for. I offered to take her shopping but she said she preferred to browse herself. Typical. It’s that age, isn’t it? Knowing exactly what they want, but wanting you to guess. Absolutely. Reminds me of when we had that power cut last winter. We were all stuck in the dark, freezing, and your daughter was complaining she couldn't charge her phone! Oh, the youth of today. Can’t live without their gadgets. I remember a time when we entertained ourselves with a game of cards and a bit of storytelling. Simpler times. Speaking of simpler times, did you see that Big Brother is coming back? Oh, honestly. Is there anything new on television? It was terrible the first time around, and I can't imagine it’s improved. The dog's been going on all day. Reckon he senses the cold coming. He’s curled up by the radiator like a little sausage. Goodness, he's a spoilt pooch.

Right, so then Gran just… completely lost it. Honestly, it was over the Christmas lights. Over the Christmas lights? What happened? Did she fall over them again? She does that every year. No, no. Worse. Auntie Brenda put up those fancy ones, you know, the ones that project patterns onto the house? And Gran swore they were summoning demons. Oh, my god! Seriously? Your Gran thinks Christmas lights are demonic? Apparently. She said they were “unnatural flickering” and “an affront to the Lord.” She tried to unplug them, but Brenda wouldn't let her. There was a full-blown shouting match. Brenda’s the one who’s all about the sparkly, isn’t she? She’d probably have lights up in July if she could get away with it. Absolutely. And she just stood her ground, telling Gran she was being ridiculous. It was… a lot. Mum had to intervene and make everyone hot chocolate. That usually calms Gran down. Hot chocolate is the answer to everything. Honestly. Did you get to see much of your Dad over Christmas? Not as much as I wanted. He was busy with his work, apparently. Something about a big contract he’s trying to land. He was on calls half the time. Ugh, work following you even at Christmas. That’s rough. Is he still enjoying it though? He seemed really stressed last time I saw him. He says he is. But I think it's taking its toll. He keeps saying it's ‘rewarding’ and ‘challenging’ but he looks permanently exhausted. I tried to suggest he take some time off, but he brushed it off. Men, honestly. They think they're invincible. You should tell him again, even if he doesn't listen right now. Maybe it’ll sink in eventually. Anyway, enough family drama. What are we watching tonight? You picked the film. I was thinking that new one with Florence Pugh? The historical one? Oh, the one you were telling me about? Yeah, sounds good! Is it a sad one? I'm not in the mood for a proper tearjerker. I think it's more... bittersweet. Apparently, it’s really beautifully shot. And Florence Pugh is amazing in everything. Fair enough. Right, I’m just gonna finish chopping these onions. Then we can get the popcorn on. And maybe hide the Christmas lights from your Gran if she ever visits.

Aye, well, it's a right pickle, isn't it? This Scottish referendum. Mum, you say that every time it comes up. I do, don't I? But it's true! It's a proper mess. All that talk of independence, and what it’ll mean for everything… it's a big decision for them, massively. I know, but Mr. Davies in History said it’s really complicated. Like, loads of things are linked to it, and it’s not just about being Scottish or not. Your Mr. Davies has got a head on his shoulders, that one. It  is  complicated. And people get so passionate about it, don’t they? Reminds me a bit of the miners’ strikes, actually. That same feeling of wanting control, wanting to decide your own fate. The miners’ strikes? You've never really talked about those. Oh, it was a long time ago, love. Before your time. But there was a lot of tension then, a lot of anger. Folks felt unheard, you know? Like their lives were being dictated by people who didn't understand them. Same sort of feeling, this Scottish thing. So you think it’s about more than just, like, being proud to be Scottish? Oh, definitely. Pride’s a part of it, aye, but it’s about power, too. And money, let's be honest. All that oil…that’s a big pull. And everything to do with the borders, like, the army, the currency… it's a tangled web. What do you think will happen? Goodness me, if I knew that, I'd be running a betting shop! Honestly, it’s too close to call. I reckon it’ll be a narrow ‘no’, if I had to put money on it. But a lot can happen in a week, can’t it? Mr. Davies said if they vote yes, there'll be loads of negotiations. Like, years of them. He's right. It won’t be a quick fix, whatever happens. And even if they  do  become independent, it's not like everything will magically be better. There'll be challenges. Massive challenges. It sounds stressful. It is stressful, for everyone involved. But it’s their decision, isn't it? They have to decide what’s best for themselves. And we have to respect that, whatever they choose. Even if I don’t entirely agree with it. Now, are you finished with your tea?

Honestly, I can’t believe she thinks  he’s  the father. Look at ‘im! I know, right? Jeremy Kyle finds these people, doesn't he? He’s like a magnet for absolute chaos. And the accents, honestly. It's a linguistic goldmine, init? It is, though, isn’t it? You can pinpoint exactly where they’re from just by a couple of words. Listen to ‘er, the way she drops her ‘h’s. Proper East Midlands. Nah, it’s more than just dropping ‘h’s, isn’t it? It’s the vowel sounds. That woman from last week? She sounded like she was from Grimsby, but she swore she was from Scunthorpe. You could tell! You’re all proper linguistics nerds, aren’t you? I just enjoy the drama. Though, I do like how they all get proper angry. It’s the elision! They’re just smooshing all the words together! Listen, she said “gonna” instead of “going to” like five times in one sentence. It's fascinating! Ooh, good one! And the glottal stops. Loads of glottal stops. I’ve been trying to consciously  not  use them since uni. My mum keeps telling me I sound posh, though. Your mum’s just jealous! You’ve got a lovely accent. It’s proper Scouse, isn't it? Very distinctive. I reckon it's getting less distinctive, though. Everyone’s accents are sort of blurring together now, aren’t they? All that telly. Yeah, true. I heard a kid in Wakefield the other day talking like he was from London. It was weird. It's awful! Like, embrace your Yorkshire-ness! It’s brilliant! You can tell a proper Yorkshire person a mile off. It's the flat vowels innit? That's a bit sweeping, isn’t it? Not  all  Yorkshire accents are the same. It depends where you are, doesn't it? You sound different to someone from Hull, for example. True! My grandma from Derby sounds nothing like your grandma from Wakefield. It's all so complex. It is, though, it's fascinating, like a puzzle. It's all to do with historical migrations. Guys, focus. Jeremy Kyle’s about to do a lie detector test! This is the good bit. Right, right. But seriously, the linguistic variety on this show is unreal. I should be taking notes. This is better than a seminar! You’re joking, but you probably would get marks for it!

Honestly, that was a terrible tackle. Absolutely reckless. You’d think they’d learn, wouldn't you? Especially this late in the season. Yeah, a bit overzealous. Ref didn’t even look bothered though, did he? Just waved play on. Honestly, sometimes I think they just enjoy seeing a bit of a ruckus. It’s madness. My dad would be  fuming . He’s convinced all the refs are biased against Sunderland, naturally. It’s a lifelong affliction. Sounds about right. My old man's the same with Villa. Thinks every decision goes against them. It’s part of the fun, I suppose. Distracts from the, you know… actual football. True. Speaking of distractions, I finally finished that scarf I was knitting. Remember? The ridiculously long one? Oh yeah! The one that could double as a blanket? Is it actually wearable, or just a monumental crafting achievement? Wearable, I think. It’s… substantial. My mam's already claimed it. Said it’s perfect for keeping her knees warm while she’s gardening. Classic mam. Always practical. I keep meaning to learn to knit, though. Seems so… therapeutic. All that repetitive motion. It is, actually. Really good for winding down. You should give it a go. I could teach you. Although, I'm pretty sure I mostly just followed a YouTube tutorial. Maybe. Though I suspect my attempts would end up looking like a tangled mess of yarn. Probably best I stick to, uh, complicated statistical modelling. Probably wise. Ooh, did you see anything about the Olympic knitting competition? Apparently, it’s a thing now. No way! Seriously? What do they even judge it on? Speed? Artistic merit? The sheer length of the scarf? Apparently, everything! There’s a design element, a technique element, and a ‘wow’ factor. It sounds insane. It’s brilliant. Absolutely brilliant. Right, changing the subject completely… have you started thinking about baby names yet? Don’t even  start  me. It’s a minefield. I’ve got a list of about five that I like, but then Ben vetoes them all. What’s his problem? Are his suggestions any good? Oh, they’re…  unique . He’s really into old Norse names. Like, really really into them. I’m trying to steer him towards something slightly more… normal. Old Norse? Oh dear. That could be interesting. Maybe compromise with something Welsh? A little nod to your heritage? Hmm, that’s not a bad idea.

And then Barry Bee… honestly, it’s a surprisingly poignant film, isn’t it? About bees and… existentialism. It was funny when he went to the shop! And he pretended to be a human! Yeah! And he got all the nectar! Exactly! Though, it did make me think… all that talk about honey and queens… it kind of bleeds into this whole Royal thing, doesn’t it? What Royal thing? Well, we were talking about going to Hampton Court Palace, and it’s just… expensive. Really expensive. To walk around somewhere because someone  used  to live there. But it has a maze! It does have a maze, which is brilliant, but still… I feel like if we were a Republic, we could have a really lovely, well-maintained maze, and  everyone  could enjoy it without needing to remortgage their house. What’s a Republic? It’s… well, it’s when we don’t have a King or Queen. It’s like America. Want to be King? Oh, goodness no! Absolutely not. Too much responsibility. And all the waving. I’d rather be a politician, actually. Less waving, more arguing. You’re already good at arguing! Am I? Oh, dear. Well, that's… helpful. Anyway, all this Royal talk makes me think of Granny’s old house. Remember all the fruit trees in the garden? Yeah! The plums were the best! And the apples! Granny made apple crumble! She did. She always said she had ‘Royal’ plums. I think she just meant they were really big and juicy. She loved a bit of exaggeration, Granny did. Did she have a crown? No, silly. But she did have a very fancy hat. Speaking of things we need… have you both been taking your vitamins? I had my gummy bear vitamin this morning! I forgot! Honestly. You need to be strong and healthy for the Olympics! I managed to get tickets for the diving! Diving! Yay! Will it be splashy? Very splashy. But it's also… silent. They really want everyone to be quiet when the divers are competing. So we need to practice being very, very quiet. But what if I need to tell you something? You can whisper,  very  quietly. Or we can write notes. Which reminds me, taking you two to restaurants… it’s like a military operation. "No shouting, no running, use your inside voices…" I like restaurants! You do, when you behave.

Honestly, that tip was chaos. Absolute chaos. People just dumping everything with no regard. And the smell! Tell me about it. I swear I saw Mrs. Higgins from number 14 trying to sneak a sofa in disguised as garden waste. Hilarious. She’d do that, wouldn’t she? Strategic discarding, that's Higgins. Though, honestly, the amount of perfectly good stuff people throw away... it’s criminal. It is! I saw a perfectly serviceable rocking chair. Solid wood. I nearly rescued it, but then I remembered the state of the attic. No room for rocking chairs, sadly. The clear-out continues…it’s a mammoth task. Oh, the attic. Don't even get me started. We're doing the same. Mountains of boxes. Mostly filled with things my mother-in-law "might need someday." Sounds thrilling. Is that the reason for the Thirsk trip next weekend then, Mum? A strategic rummage through Auntie Brenda’s hoard? It's not  just  about Brenda’s hoard! We’re visiting Ethel, and Thirsk has that lovely little auction house…I saw a mention of some antique silverware. Honestly, I'm hoping for a Georgian teapot. An auction? You and your teapots! Remember that hideous porcelain shepherdess you bought last year? Still haunting the hallway. She has character! And she was a bargain. Speaking of bargains, has anyone seen that new garden centre on the A64? Apparently, they’re doing amazing deals on winter bedding. Are you seriously talking about gardening now? Can we talk about something… relevant? Like, have you seen the new gaming console? He’s got priorities. Rightly so. It’s a good distraction from the attic, at least. Though I’m dreading the sheer volume of Christmas decorations we’re going to unearth. Don't even mention Christmas. Although, speaking of events, did you hear about Carol and Brian’s daughter getting married? Massive stag do planned in Blackpool. Apparently, it involves inflatable guitars and a mobility scooter. Blackpool! That sounds… eventful. I'm surprised Brian's letting him get away with it. He’s usually quite stern. Blackpool's known for that sort of thing. It's practically a tradition. I saw a documentary on the history of seaside resorts the other night, very interesting. Apparently, they were originally designed as places for the upper classes to "take the air" and show off their wealth. Fascinating. Restorative air! Honestly, all that fried food and donkey rides.

Right, so I was thinking, for Saturday, we could actually go to the museum. Proper one, not the maritime one this time. The Walker Art Gallery. Oh, yeah? That's a good shout. I haven't been in ages. But parking's a nightmare around there, isn't it? Remember last time we tried? Ended up ages away and had to walk like twenty minutes. Aye, it was a disaster. We could get the train, yeah? It's dead easy from Lime Street. Actually, that’s brilliant. I hadn’t even thought of that. Dead easy and no stress. Good thinking. How was work today? Any little terrors in your class causing havoc? You would not BELIEVE. Little Liam decided to serenade everyone with a rendition of 'Baby Shark' for a full five minutes. Refused to stop. Honestly, I felt like losing it. Afterwards, he tried to trade me a half-eaten biscuit for extra playtime. Oh, Liam. He’s a character, that one. I swear, some kids are just born with a knack for chaos. Mine were interesting today too. Had one little lad who kept insisting he could talk to spiders. Oh, God. That sounds…intense. Speaking of intense, Auntie Carol practically interrogated me about wedding plans on the phone last night. Apparently, I need to have the guest list finalised by… next Tuesday? Carol being Carol, eh? She’s already planning the buffet, probably. Don’t let her overwhelm you. We’ve got ages yet. I know, I know. It’s just...it feels like everything’s happening at once. The wedding, thinking about moving, your interview for the Masters next week… It’s a bit much. It is, isn’t it? But it's good stuff, y’know? And the interview’s just a formality, you’re brilliant. You'll get in. And moving… we need to actually start looking. I spent hours online last night, and the prices are mental. Tell me about it. I saw one in Oxton, looked decent, but it was practically needing a full renovation. And the price? Ridiculous. We need to save more money, don't we? We do. I’m putting a bit aside each month, but it’s slow going. Christmas is going to murder our finances, as usual. Don't even talk about it! I already promised little Maisie a pony. Joking! Sort of. I’ve got no idea what to get your mum this year.

Honestly, this canteen pizza is criminal. It’s like… cardboard with a vague tomato scent. Tell me about it! I swear they just leave a box out in the rain and then charge us three quid for a slice. Speaking of, are you going out tonight? Liam's organising something, I think. Ooh, where? I’m so tempted. I massively need a night out. Uni's just been non-stop essays and lectures. I feel permanently exhausted. I think I actually dreamed about footnotes last night. He said something about “The Vault”. Apparently, it’s got a decent DJ and cheap drinks. Though knowing Liam, “cheap” is relative. He thinks £6 a pint is a bargain. Classic Liam. He’s convinced he’s a financial guru. I might go, yeah. I need to distract myself.
