I’ve been scrolling through Instagram for hours every night, which is, like, a terrible habit. All I see is everyone having amazing lives and going to amazing parties. Oh, the Instagram vortex. Don’t fall in! It’s all fake anyway. Everyone filters everything. Remember Chloe’s “spontaneous” trip to Paris? Turns out it was a heavily planned photoshoot she’d been saving up for for months. Oh god, yes! And then she pretended she’d just randomly decided to go. Honestly, the lengths people go to for likes. What about you? Any weekend plans besides potentially The Vault? My mum keeps trying to get me to come home. She’s convinced I’m wasting away here and need a “proper meal”. Apparently, university food is starving me. She doesn't understand pot noodles are a valid food group. Oh, mums! Mine’s the same. She’s constantly sending me links to recipes. Like I have time to make a soufflé between seminars! Have you seen that new show everyone’s talking about, “Heartstopper”? No, not yet. Is it good? Someone at the library was raving about it. They said it’s really sweet. I've been rewatching old Disney movies to de-stress. "The Little Mermaid" is my go-to. Oh, "Heartstopper" is  so  good. It's honestly adorable. Very feel-good. You should definitely watch it. And Disney is always a good shout. Honestly, sometimes I just want to live in a Disney movie. No essays, just singing animals and magical adventures. Exactly! Although I’m not sure I’d fancy being a princess.

Right, so I got Charizard! Finally! After ages of trading. Oh, that’s brilliant! Charizard's a good one, isn’t he? Leo was obsessed with Pokémon for a while, remember? He used to try and catch them in the garden. Char-zah! Zoo! He thinks Charizard’s a zoo animal. He's a clever one, isn’t he? Getting all the sounds mixed up. Are you Skyping Gran tomorrow? Yeah, supposed to be. But I’ve got a double maths lesson first. It’s gonna be brutal. Oh dear. Well, maybe you can do a quick hello before or after. She misses you, you know. I know, I know. I’ll try. She keeps asking about my guitar lessons. Are you still going? Yeah, but it’s slow going. Barre chords are  impossible . They are tricky at first. Don’t give up! It takes practice. Oisin’s been trying to say “ice cream” all day. It comes out more like “i-shee-cream.” I-shee-cream! That’s adorable! Honestly, it's exhausting trying to decipher. He’s got a new pair of skinny jeans, have you seen? They’re ridiculous. He looks like a little sausage. Skinny jeans? On a toddler? I know, right? Leo bought them. He thinks they’re “cool”. Honestly, the things he buys. What about those bright yellow wellies? Don’t even get me started. He’s impossible. Oh, and he's lost one of his slippers again. I swear they just vanish into thin air. Slippah! Gone! Maybe Charizard took it. Maybe. Speaking of vanishing, are we still on for Ramen on Saturday? Definitely! I’ve been craving it all week. Is Leo going too? Probably. He’ll want to try and order something ridiculously spicy and then complain he can’t handle it. That sounds about right. Typical Leo. Ramen! Yummy! He's already excited. I'll try and get Oisin to wear proper shoes this time, rather than just his socks. It’s freezing out there. Sounds good. I’ll text you if I can’t Skype Gran tomorrow. And I'll keep an eye out for any rogue Charizards stealing slippers. Does this meet your requirements? Let me know if you’d like any adjustments or further dialogue. Certainly, here is my answer:Right, so I got Charizard! Finally! After ages of trading. Oh, that’s brilliant! Charizard's a good one, isn’t he?

Honestly, it’s just…dust. And bits of string. And things I haven’t seen in decades. You wouldn’t believe the state of it. It’s like a time capsule of bad decisions and forgotten hobbies. Oh, go on, what did you find? Anything exciting? I’ve been meaning to have a clear-out of my attic, but honestly, I’m terrified of what I’ll unearth. It’s easier just to leave it. Well, I found… the gardening set. Remember? The little metal ones. With the tiny watering can and the rake? Oh,  my  goodness! Yes! I’d completely forgotten about that. We used to spend hours ‘gardening’ in the garden with those. Mum hated it when we dug up her flowerbeds. She did, didn’t she? She’d give us that look. The one that said “I love you, but you are absolute terrors.” And we’d just carry on, meticulously rearranging her petunias. Oh, and we'd pretend the weeds were exotic plants we were carefully nurturing. We were so imaginative. Were all the pieces there? I remember losing the little spade almost immediately. Surprisingly, yes! Everything was there. A bit rusty, naturally, but all accounted for. It’s funny, isn’t it? Such simple things bring back such vivid memories. It’s a bit sad, too, really. It is. It’s like a little piece of childhood rescued from oblivion. Did you find the Bako set? We were obsessed with that. All those colourful plastic bricks… Not yet. I think that might be lurking behind the Christmas decorations. That cupboard is a monster. The deeper you go, the more you find. It’s a black hole of forgotten possessions. Oh, dear. You’ll need a full day, at least. And a strong cup of tea. It’s all so overwhelming, isn’t it? Part of me just wants to shut the door and pretend it doesn’t exist. I know! But Mum said – well, she said it needs doing before… before everything gets sold. And I want to find some photos. I’m sure there are some hidden away in there somewhere. That's a good idea. We should have a proper rummage through everything together when you’re finished. Maybe we can have a ‘memory lane’ afternoon. That sounds lovely. Though brace yourself. It's not pretty in there. It’s started raining now, isn’t it?

Honestly, I think I've got about fifteen mosquito bites. Fifteen! And it’s only May. Really? I haven’t noticed any. Though I suppose they’re more attracted to you than me. You’re sweeter, you see. Very funny. I’m not sweet, I'm delicious. Apparently. To tiny, bloodsucking insects. It's infuriating. I'm slathering myself in repellent and they’re  still  getting to me. Maybe it's the washing powder? Something about the scent attracting them? Oh, don't start with the laundry theories again. It’s just… mosquitoes. It’s a natural phenomenon. A deeply irritating natural phenomenon. Just trying to be helpful. Though, speaking of irritation, the traffic was dreadful getting here. Absolutely gridlocked on Mill Road. Oh, tell me about it. I thought we’d be late getting back. Little one was starting to get a bit fidgety in the sling. It’s always bad on a Saturday, isn't it? Everyone heading to the park, or into town. Or both. It is. Though we did manage to get a space right outside, which was a small victory. True, a win is a win. Did you see that band, ‘Static Bloom’ are playing at The Junction next month? Oh, are they? I think I've heard of them. Are they any good? Apparently, really good. A bit indie, a bit electronic. A friend of mine saw them at a festival last year and raved about them. Hmm, maybe we could look into it. Depending on childcare, obviously. And whether my mosquito bites are driving me insane by then. We’ll figure it out. It’d be nice to get out for a proper gig, wouldn’t it? Something that isn’t… lullabies and nursery rhymes. Definitely. Though, honestly, some of those nursery rhymes are surprisingly catchy. “Baby Shark” is stuck in my head again. I think it’s a form of torture. I feel your pain. I caught myself humming the “Wheels on the Bus” earlier. It's a slippery slope. A very slippery slope. Look, there’s old Mr. Henderson with his terrier. Hello, Mr. Henderson! Morning, Mr. Henderson! See? Even the locals are wishing we had some peace and quiet from the children’s songs. Probably. Although, he does seem to enjoy a good chat. He’ll be over in a minute telling us the latest gossip from the gardening club. Then we’ll be hearing all about his prize-winning dahlias.

Right, that was… a day. Honestly, my shoulders are screaming. Four hours on the range, then another three on the course. Ouch. That  does  sound brutal. I managed… well, I managed to avoid most physical exertion today. Primarily involved staring at a laptop and feeling increasingly hopeless about job applications. Still nothing then? Anything come back from that recruitment agency? Nada. Zip. Zero. They said they’d get back to me “within the week.” That was last Thursday. I’m starting to think I need to learn to code or something. Become a hermit coder. Don’t do that. You’re brilliant at what you studied. It just takes time. The market’s a mess right now. Did you at least get out for a walk? Need to get some fresh air after all that screen time. I did, actually. Posted a letter – the last one to my aunt, I think – and walked around the park. Saw a toddler dressed as a tiny ghost. It was… premature. It’s still almost two weeks till Halloween. Ha! Dedicated little ghost. Speaking of premature, Old Man Hemmings is already putting up his spooky decorations. Giant inflatable spiders everywhere. It’s terrifying, honestly. He’s always been a bit extra, hasn’t he? Remember last year when the wind blew his Frankenstein over into Mrs. Peterson’s rose bushes? Oh god, yes! She was  fuming . Anyway, I tried to watch a bit of TV tonight, but my phone kept buzzing. It’s the tournament organisers, apparently. They want to ‘discuss potential media opportunities.’ I just want to eat dinner and sleep. Ugh, the price of being vaguely successful. What did you have for dinner? I just microwaved some pasta. Don’t judge. No judgement! I had that jerk chicken thing you made, reheated. It was amazing, still. Though, seriously, you need to write down that recipe. It’s a crime against humanity that it exists only in your head. I will, I will. I keep meaning to. It's just…writing feels like  work  right now. Everything feels like work when it’s related to finding a job. It’s so demoralising. I can imagine. Look, maybe we should go to the theatre next week? There’s that new play at the Wycombe Swan. Distraction is key. That actually sounds lovely. Anything but another evening staring at job postings. Are you free on Tuesday?

…A-B-C-D-E-F-G! Right, that's enough of the alphabet for now, little man. Dinner’s getting cold. He's got a good set of lungs, hasn’t he? Honestly, it's non-stop singing. It’s lovely, but… exhausting. It's pretty good actually. Better than my singing, definitely. Though I haven’t really practiced lately. You should join in with him! It’d be… entertaining. Oh, please no. Just imagine the two of you. My ears couldn't take it. Harsh! Speaking of taking things, are you sure you don’t want more potatoes? You barely touched them. No thanks, I’m stuffed. Honestly, that was lovely. You’ve really perfected that shepherd’s pie. It is really good, Dad. Best shepherd’s pie ever. Ah, stop it. I’m just glad someone appreciates it. So, any plans for the evening, Finn? Besides subjecting us to musical performances, of course. Not really. Just thinking of watching a film. Thinking maybe that new Marvel one, if everyone’s up for it? Oh, I don't know. Superhero films… they all seem the same these days. Endless explosions and not much plot. Now, now, don’t dismiss it completely. They can be quite clever, you know. Plus, it’s a good distraction. I’ve got that looming cloud of work hanging over me tomorrow. Big meeting with the team. Oh, that sounds stressful. What’s it about? Mostly budgets, unfortunately. Trying to get approval for some new software upgrades. It’s always the same story - trying to convince management that investing in better technology will actually  save  them money in the long run. Sounds… dull. It is. Terribly dull. But someone has to do it. Right, Leo, no throwing your peas please! Honestly, are you trying to redecorate the kitchen? He's just exploring his artistic side. We all did it at that age. Remember when you used to paint the walls with your crayons, dear? Don't remind me. Your mother was not impressed. So, movie after dinner, then? What about you, love? Any preferences? As long as it’s not another superhero film, I don’t mind. Preferably something with a bit of romance. Or a good mystery. Ugh, romance? That’s boring. Alright, alright. We'll have a democratic vote. Finn, you get to choose the genre. But no explosions, understood? Fine. But if it’s boring, I’m blaming you.

Honestly, the state of him. Sleeping in his pants  again . It’s a wonder he doesn’t overheat. It’s just comfy, isn’t it? He says it’s the best way to ensure a proper night’s sleep. A full commitment to relaxation. Daddy sleeps silly! In his undies! It’s weird. Why doesn't he wear pyjamas like me? Mine have dinosaurs on. Dinosaurs are far superior, agreed. It’s a lifestyle choice, apparently. A very…  warm  lifestyle choice. Anyway, look at this. I was sketching out some ideas for the extension. Oh, go on then! Let’s see. Are we finally tackling the kitchen? It’s… snug, to say the least. Snug is generous. It’s a postage stamp. This idea opens it up into the back garden. A proper kitchen-diner. Bi-fold doors, the whole shebang. Is there going to be a slide? Can we have a slide from the kitchen to the garden? That’s a brilliant idea! A super-fast slide! We’ll see. Maybe a smaller, more… practical slide. This part here… I was thinking of making the utility room bigger. And maybe a downstairs loo, so we don’t have to trek upstairs every five minutes. Sensible. Very sensible. Although, a wine fridge in the utility room wouldn’t go amiss. Just saying. For, you know, chilling the whites. A wine fridge? Now you’re talking. But we’d need to re-allocate funds from the slide budget. Nooooooo! Slide is more important! Yeah! Slide! And a bouncy castle! Right, okay, calm down. We'll explore all options. Potentially a mini slide integrated  into  the bouncy castle. Compromise. That actually sounds… amazing. Okay, I’m officially on board with the extension. But we're definitely having a wine fridge  somewhere . Deal. Though I’m starting to think we need a bigger house altogether. One with a dedicated slide room. And a wine cellar. And a room just for toys! A  huge  toy room! With robots! And spaceships! One step at a time, kids. One step at a time. First, we conquer the kitchen. Then, world domination… with a slide. And a well-stocked wine cellar. Don’t forget the wine cellar. Never. Never forget the wine cellar. Now, who wants breakfast? I’m thinking pancakes. Possibly while discussing architectural plans. Speaker_3 & Pancakes! Yes! Pancakes sound perfect. Though, honestly, watching your husband sleep in his underwear is a surprisingly good start to the day.

Right dreadful business this water company stuff isn’t it? Absolutely scandalous. Oh aye. Proper daylight robbery. They’re leaking more water than they’re delivering, from what I read. And then blaming us for usage? Unbelievable. Makes you wonder where all the investment’s gone, doesn’t it? Exactly. All lining pockets, I suspect. Speaking of investment, any luck with that funding bid for the particle physics project? Not yet. Still waiting to hear back. Apparently, they’re swamped. Everyone and their dog seems to be applying for grants these days. It’s a cutthroat world, this academic life. Tell me about it. I’ve had two rejected in the last month. One for the excavation in Turkey, the other for the… well, the study of ancient pottery. You’d think there’d be money for pottery! Pottery! Honestly. Though, thinking about it, I saw a rather fine bit of pottery on my trip to Italy last year. Florence, lovely place. You ever been? Oh, Florence is… magnificent. I went years ago with my wife, before she… well, never mind. We stayed in a tiny little hotel near the Ponte Vecchio. The art, the architecture, the food… fantastic. We’re thinking of going back. You should. It’s a tonic for the soul. I was there for a conference, actually. On, ironically enough, the ethical implications of large-scale scientific projects. All that talk of the Hadron Collider and its energy consumption. Goodness. Heavy stuff. Sounds like a debate that could go on forever. It rather is. Though, truthfully, I spent most of the time searching for decent coffee. That’s a serious concern in Italy, you know. Some of it is… questionable. Questionable? Italian coffee? Blasphemy! I’m telling you. I found a little place, though. Hidden away down a side street. Now  that  was coffee. Proper strong, proper flavour. I’ll have to make a note of that. If we do go, I’ll want a detailed itinerary, focusing exclusively on caffeination. Speaking of which, this coffee’s rather weak, isn’t it? I swear they’re watering it down. They probably are. Still, it’s warm. And keeps us awake. Have you made any progress with that decorating at home? You were talking about redoing the living room. Oh, don’t even ask. It’s a disaster. I thought I could handle painting the ceiling myself, but it’s a complete mess.

Mummy, can I have another chocolate egg? Please? No, sweetie, you’ve had three already. It's nearly bedtime, remember? We don't want sugar rushes. I haven't had  any  chocolate eggs yet! That’s not fair! You had one after lunch, darling. A big one, with a dinosaur inside. But it was a small dinosaur! I wanted a T-Rex! Alright, alright. We’ll see. Now, are we making any progress with the Lego sorting? It looks like a rainbow exploded in here. I’m building a castle! It needs all the grey bricks. That’s brilliant. And what are you building, Leo? A spaceship! It’s going to fly to Hogwarts! Oh, Hogwarts! Are you going to see Harry Potter? Yep! And Hermione and Ron! And fight Voldemort! I like Hermione! She's clever. She is very clever. You both love Harry Potter, don’t you? Do you remember when we went to see the film at the cinema? Yes! With the big screen and the popcorn! Exactly. We could go again soon. There’s a new film coming out, isn’t there? Not Harry Potter, but something with superheroes… I want to see the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles! They’re way cooler than superheroes. They  are  pretty cool. Leo, are you sure you want all these yellow bricks for your spaceship? That looks a bit… sunny. It’s a  special  spaceship. It runs on sunshine! Of course it does. Very clever. Oh, speaking of building things, did Granny say how the renovations are going at her house? She said the builders are making a mess! And Grandpa keeps getting in the way. Oh, they're a pair, aren’t they? I bet. She was complaining about the wallpaper choices, last time I spoke to her. Granny likes pink. She does, doesn’t she? Although, she said she’s thinking of something a little more… muted this time. Less Barbie, apparently. Can we watch The Simpsons after story time? Please? Maybe. If you’re both very good at tidying up this Lego. It's like a minefield! And then, it's straight to bed. No more chocolate eggs. Deal? Speaker_2 & Deal! Mummy, can I have  one  tiny piece of chocolate then? Just one? Oh, Leo… okay.  One  tiny piece. But that’s it! I want one too! Okay, okay. One piece each. Now, let's get this Lego sorted before Homer Simpson comes to life and starts causing trouble.

Oh my god, you are back! How was Greece? Honestly, fill me in. Did you actually manage to relax, or was it full-on tourist chaos? It was… a mixed bag. Beautiful, obviously. The sunsets were insane. But yes, chaos. So. Much. Chaos. Honestly, the sheer number of people trying to get the perfect Instagram shot was exhausting. Did you have a nice weekend? Anything exciting happen here while I was gone trying to find inner peace amongst the hordes? Exciting? No. Tranquil? Also no. Liam messaged me, which was… a choice. Apparently, he’s “doing really well” and wanted to “catch up”. As if. I immediately blocked him. Honestly, the audacity. Ugh, Liam. Still? Honestly, good riddance. Block is the only way to go. Did you tell him where to shove it before blocking? I feel like that's a necessary step. No, I didn’t give him the satisfaction. Just… gone. Poof. Anyway! Tell me more about Greece. Did you eat loads of amazing food? I'm starving, by the way. I’ve literally lived on toast for three days. Oh, the food was incredible! So much fresh seafood, and the gyros… don’t even get me started. I think I gained about half a stone just from gyros alone. And yes, I'm officially craving Greek salad. We should make some. Tonight? Yes! That sounds perfect. I can pick up some feta and olives on my way home from work tomorrow. Speaking of work, oh my god, I have a mountain of emails to get through. My boss is already breathing down my neck. Project X is apparently “slightly behind schedule” which translates to “completely falling apart”. Oh, project X. The bane of your existence. You’ll be fine. You always are. But seriously, take it easy. You need to de-stress. You’ve been working so hard. What about Sarah and Ben? Did you two manage to meet up while I was away? Yeah, we went for drinks on Friday. They’re good. Ben's still obsessed with rugby, naturally. He was trying to explain the offside rule to me for a solid hour. It's completely lost on me. Honestly, I think he just likes the sound of his own voice when talking about it. Classic Ben. Honestly, he could lecture on the intricacies of shoelaces if given the opportunity. How's your mum? Have you spoken to her recently?

Right, now then, have you managed to get the washing line sorted, love? It's blowing a gale out there. Not yet, Gran. Dad said he’d do it tomorrow. It's just… one of the posts is a bit wobbly. Wobbly, you say? Your grandad was a dab hand with a bit of cement, he was. Never a wobbly post in all his days. Aye, cement and a good sturdy pole. None of this flimsy stuff they sell these days. Back in my time, things were  built  to last. They certainly were. Now, are you warm enough, you two? I’ve put the fire on, but it takes a while to warm up this old house. I'm alright, thanks. It's cozy in here. Cozy indeed. Reminds me of our old place in Hull. Though, yours is a bit bigger, isn’t it? Well, it’s got an extra bedroom, aye. Needed it for when your Dad’s lot come to stay. It's always full to bursting. Reminds me, I need to change the sheets on the spare bed. Full to bursting? Sounds like my childhood! Six of us crammed into a two-bedroom house. You didn’t have room to swing a cat. Six?! Wow. Don’t believe everything he tells you, lad. He exaggerates. It was four. Though it  felt  like six. Four, six, what's the difference after eighty years? Both were a right squeeze. I used to have to share a bed with my brother. Oh, that must have been awful! Imagine sharing a bed! No way. Anyway, I made a pot of tea. Anyone fancy another cup? I’ve got biscuits too, shortbread, your favourite, Mum. Oh, go on then. A nice cup of tea and a biscuit. Can't say no to that. Though, don’t make it too strong, my heart isn't what it used to be. I’ll have one too. Though I can handle a good strong brew. Keeps the old engine running, you know. Always the same, you two. Right, you stay put, I'll get the kettle on. Oh and, have you finished that maths homework, young man? Your GCSEs are looming. Nearly. I'm stuck on quadratic equations. They make no sense. Quadratic equations? Oh those. They are a beast. I'm marking papers full of them at the moment. Absolute carnage. We'll have a look at them after tea, shall we?

Right, so we’re all agreed, movie night is definitely happening this weekend? Yes! Can we watch  Tinkerbell ? The sparkly one! No!  Peter Pan ! The one with the pirates! And Captain Hook! He’s really scary, but cool. We can definitely watch  Peter Pan . It’s been ages. Though, you know, it's a bit different to the original story. What’s different? Well, the version most people know is based on the play by J.M. Barrie, but the original story is… a bit darker, actually. And a lot longer. It has all sorts of adventures the film doesn’t show. Darker? Like, scary darker? A little bit, yeah. More about lost boys and growing up and… well, it's complicated. It's why it's a story that appeals to adults as well as kids, I think. Did you know Great Ormond Street hospital gets all the money from  Peter Pan ? Oh, that's right! J.M. Barrie gave the copyright of the play to the hospital! Isn't that lovely? He didn’t have any children of his own, so he wanted to leave something good behind. He used to spend a lot of time with the children there. Wow. So when we watch it, we’re helping sick kids? Exactly! You're helping sick kids. It makes it even more magical, doesn't it? It does! But I still want to watch  Tinkerbell  too. She’s so pretty. We can watch both! We can have a Peter Pan and Tinkerbell double feature. Though, have you seen the film  Pan ? The one that came out a few years ago, telling Peter’s origin story? I think so… didn’t it have pirates and stuff? It did. But it's…different. It’s not everyone's favourite. Some people really liked it, but it changed a  lot  of the story. It's a bit of a mess, really. Oh. Maybe we shouldn’t watch that one. Probably not. Stick with the classics, I’d say. The Disney one is a good starting point. And then maybe we can read some of the original story together when you're a bit older. Can we pretend to be pirates after the film? I want to be Captain Hook! You can absolutely be Captain Hook! And I’ll be… well, maybe I’ll be Peter Pan! I’ll be Tinkerbell and make sparkly dust everywhere!

Honestly, this M5 is a nightmare. Even on a Sunday afternoon. Used to be you could fly down this, but look at it now. Just solid. It’s always like this, isn't it? Especially heading towards Exeter. Everyone going to Cornwall, I suppose. Still, we’ve got plenty of time, right? Flight isn’t until… what, three? Three fifteen. Plenty of time, Dad. Just try to relax. Are you even remotely used to getting up this early again? You were a night owl in retirement, remember? Relax? Relax when I’m potentially missing  Songs of Praise ?! It’s a ritual, you know. And yes, I’m not used to it. I was having perfectly good dreams about… well, I can’t remember, but they were perfectly good dreams! You two young’uns have no appreciation for a lay-in. Oh, Dad. You and your dreams. Seriously though, how are you coping with the commute now, Mum? Back to Taunton every day must be exhausting. It is. It really is. It’s not the driving, surprisingly. It’s just the sheer amount of time  lost . Two hours a day! I feel like I’m living in the car. Remember when we lived in Sidmouth? It was only thirty minutes to Exeter then. Bliss. Sidmouth… now  that  was a nice little spot. We had some good times in that little cottage, didn’t we? Before it turned into a tourist trap. And before your mother decided she needed a garden big enough for a small agricultural operation. It wasn’t a small operation! I wanted to grow my own vegetables. And remember the view? Spectacular. Though, to be fair, the house in Crediton had its charms too. Just a bit… remote. Remote is an understatement! You could only get Deliveroo if the driver was feeling particularly adventurous. So, Christmas at our place this year then? We’ve got the spare room all ready. Absolutely. Though, you'll have to promise me there won't be any of that modern music. None of that… thump-thump-thump nonsense. We’ll try our best, dear. Though your granddaughter does have… strong opinions on music. We might need earplugs. Speaking of which, have you two started thinking about Sarah’s house-warming? She’s really excited about it. Wants to make it a proper party. A party? Oh, good. Something to look forward to. I’ll volunteer to be in charge of the cheese and biscuits.

Oh, honestly, my back is just  killing  me. All this bending over those herbaceous borders…you wouldn’t think a bit of deadheading could be so strenuous. Tell me about it. I used to think retirement would mean putting my feet up, but it’s been one working party after another. Good work, mind, for the village, but…my knees aren’t what they were. Though, nothing like the pain my Margaret was in at the end. Oh dear, I’m sorry to hear that. Was she…ill? For years. Started with a sort of…fatigue. Doctors couldn't put their finger on it. Eventually, she ended up in a hospice. Wonderful place, actually, the staff were angels. She had a Swedish massage once a week, said it was the only thing that gave her any relief. Cost a fortune, mind. A Swedish massage  does  sound lovely. I used to give them to clients when I had the gallery, as a little added touch, you know? Though, I’m more of a sports massage person myself. Gets right into the knots. It's a shame it took illness for her to experience something like that. It’s important to prioritise self-care, isn’t it? Especially as we get older. She always put everyone else first. Taught nursery education for forty years. Bless her, she was brilliant with the little ones, but never had a moment to herself. Always fighting for better funding, better resources… Nowadays, they're obsessed with inclusivity and all that, which is good, but back then, it was a proper struggle. Fighting for female equality, she was, before it was fashionable. It’s funny how terminology changes, isn’t it? Nursery education…we used to call it ‘playgroup’ when my children were small. And ‘female equality’ – my goodness, the battles we’ve all had! Though, I always felt it was less about equality and more about recognising the inherent  difference , wouldn’t you say? We bring different things to the table. Difference, maybe. Though, I always thought it was more about being given the same  opportunities  to bring those things to the table. Margaret certainly had to fight tooth and nail for every promotion. They kept saying she wasn’t ‘assertive enough.’ Assertive! She was a force of nature! Precisely! It's always been a double standard. A man is ‘strong’ and ‘decisive,’ a woman is ‘bossy’ and ‘difficult.’

Right, so I was thinking, for Italy, obviously we’ve got the flights sorted, but have you had a look at trains at all? Between Rome and Florence, and then Florence to Venice? A little bit. Honestly, the Italian train system… it looks a bit daunting, doesn't it? All those different classes, and different types of trains. Frecciarossa, Intercity… it’s a bit much to take in. It  is  a bit much, but it’s actually really efficient once you get your head around it. Frecciarossa is the high-speed one, that's what we want. It’s just a bit more expensive. I was looking at booking in advance, which seemingly saves a fair bit. Advance booking sounds sensible. Though I do worry about being tied down. What if we want to be spontaneous and stay an extra day somewhere? We can get flexible tickets, they're just… significantly more. Or we could just risk it and book closer to the time, but they say those get REALLY expensive, particularly during peak season. We’re going in August, remember. Oh, August. Right. Peak everything. Okay, flexible tickets sound best then, even if they sting a little. Less stress. So, Rome to Florence first… about three hours, isn't it, on the Frecciarossa? Roughly, yeah. A little over. I was looking at hotels near the station in Florence. Easier for transferring luggage, you know? Especially with my…enthusiasm for overpacking. You  do  take an awful lot. Though I’m not exactly minimalist myself. Near the station is practical. As long as it's not too… dodgy. Florence can be a bit rough around the edges sometimes. I’ve checked the reviews, don’t worry! Nothing too dodgy. It's got good ratings, and it’s only a 15-minute walk to the Duomo. Then from Florence to Venice… that one’s a bit longer, isn’t it? Yes, I think it’s closer to two and a half hours. And Venice is… complicated. All those bridges! Are you sure your shoulder will be okay with all the walking? It's a lot better now, honestly. The physio really helped. And I’m taking painkillers just in case. Plus, Venice is pretty flat! No hills to contend with. We can always get a vaporetto – a water bus – if I need a break. A vaporetto! Oh, that sounds lovely. We  must  do a gondola ride, though.

Right so I’ve just checked my bank, and apparently I spent forty quid on Deliveroo last night. Forty quid! Forty quid? What on earth did you order, a banquet? Nah, just…bits and bobs. Burger, some fries, a milkshake. And a couple of cookies, alright? Don't judge. It was a stressful day of essay writing. Needed the sugar rush. Fair enough. Essays are brutal. Though forty quid could have bought you a lot of sugar. You know, a whole bag. I know, I know. It’s just…convenience, innit? Couldn’t be bothered to go to the shops. Convenience tax. They get you every time. Speaking of things getting you, did you see the cricket yesterday? England absolutely hammered them. Did I! Root was on fire. Proper class innings. I was watching it with Liam and Ben. Ben was getting proper het up, shouting at the telly like he was the captain. Ha! That’s Ben all over. He's got that competitive spirit, even when just watching. Reminds me of my cousin, Dale. He used to get like that watching dominoes! Dominoes? Really? Serious business in Barbados, trust me. Anyway, how’s your mum doing? Haven’t spoken to her in a bit. She's good, she’s good. Still complaining about my aunt Carol. Apparently Carol brought a fruitcake to the book club and it tasted like cardboard. Oh, Carol. Always a drama. Your mum's book club sounds… lively. It is. It's basically just an excuse for them to all gossip and judge each other’s baking. Sounds perfect, really. I used to have a fruitcake from my grandmother, that was pretty solid. Took a chisel to get through it. See! It’s a common problem! What about work, how's it going? Still dealing with…what’s her name…Brenda? Brenda. Don't even get me started. She tried to take credit for my presentation again. I had to gently, but firmly, remind her who had actually done the work. It's tiring, y’know? Oh man, that’s awful. You gotta stand up for yourself though. I know. It's just…I don’t want to make things  difficult . It’s a small office. But I also don’t want to be walked all over. It’s a tricky one, yeah. You gotta find that balance. Have you spoken to your brother recently?

Oh, it’s lovely to actually  see  you both, not just hear your voices crackling. This Skype thing is a godsend, isn’t it? Though the picture keeps freezing… Aye, it’s alright. Better than nothing, I suppose. Though I still reckon a good old phone call is best. You can actually  hear  proper, then. Not all choppy like this. Mum, Dad, you both look well. Though Dad, you’ve got that ‘thinking hard’ face on. What’s got your brain ticking? I was just looking at that globe, that little one I got years ago. Remember when we went to that shop in Cromer? And I couldn’t decide between that one and a bigger one? Should’ve got the bigger one, really. You always say that. You always regret not getting the bigger globe! Honestly, it’s a running joke. Well, it  would  be more useful! You could actually see the little places better. Like, where we went on holiday to Yorkshire. Remember Scarborough? Lovely place. Though your mother nearly broke her ankle on those steps down to the beach. Nearly! And you were no help at all, muttering about needing proper shoes. I was perfectly capable of managing in sandals, thank you very much. Sounds like a typical holiday. Anyway, talking about Yorkshire… little Timmy at school is doing a project on it. I’m trying to help him find interesting facts, but it’s mostly just about sheep and dry stone walls! There's more to Yorkshire than sheep and dry stone walls, lad! There’s history. And proper puddings. And folk who talk proper. Oh, don’t start on the accents, Arthur. Everyone has their own way of speaking. Though I do agree, Yorkshire pudding is superior. I’m trying to get him to look at the industrial side of things, the mills, the history of Leeds. But he’s more fascinated by the Bronte sisters. Teenage girls, eh? Ah, the Bronte sisters. Good literature, that. We stayed in a youth hostel near Haworth once, years ago. Dreadful place. Damp. And the food… well, let’s just say I wouldn't feed it to the pigeons. Oh, the youth hostels! We did a few of those, didn’t we? Before we had the money for proper hotels. That one in the Lake District was lovely. Though you complained about the bunk beds. My leg, you see.

Right, so I’ve been looking at flights again, and honestly, it’s just…criminal. Tell me about it. I tried to book a train ticket back to London last weekend and it was practically the price of a plane. What are you looking at, anyway? Barcelona. For, like, the end of October. Just a long weekend, you know? Bit of sun before winter properly kicks in. But it’s all coming up at like, four hundred quid return. Four hundred! Ouch. That  is  steep. Have you tried Ryanair? They're usually a bit…optimistic with their baggage charges, but the base fare is often alright. Yeah, of course. They’re the first ones I checked. It’s the baggage that bumps it up, and then you add a seat selection because you don’t want to be stuck in the middle seat next to a screaming toddler, and suddenly it’s, like, five hundred. Ugh, the Ryanair tax. It's a thing. Remember that time we went to Prague and you ended up paying extra for a cabin bag that was like, two centimeters too big? Don’t remind me! I was fuming. The woman at the desk was so smug about it. Honestly, they just make it up as they go along. They do. Honestly, sometimes I think they just pick a random number and hope for the best. Have you looked at EasyJet? They're sometimes a bit better. Yeah, similar really. I think it's just the demand, isn't it? Everyone wants to escape the grey. I’m starting to think maybe Tenerife’s a better bet. It’s usually cheaper. Tenerife’s good. It’s a bit…British, though? Like, you’re surrounded by people from Hull. Yeah, that’s the downside. But sunshine is sunshine, right? Anyway, what about you? Any holiday plans brewing? Besides the extortionate train fares back to civilisation, obviously. Not yet. I was thinking about maybe a weekend in Edinburgh. It’s easily doable by train, and I haven’t been in ages. Plus, I really want to see the Christmas market. Ooh, that sounds lovely. Edinburgh’s gorgeous. Though you’ll probably need about five layers of clothing. Probably. I’m used to it. Actually, talking about layers…this lasagne is  amazing . You’ve outdone yourself. Oh, good! I was a bit worried it was a bit bland, but you seem to be enjoying it.

Honestly, the price of everything at Sainsbury’s now…it’s daylight robbery. A tin of peaches, used to be sixty pence, now it’s over a pound twenty! It is mad, isn’t it? I’ve been trying to switch to Aldi, but it’s a bit out of my way and sometimes the quality…well, it’s not quite the same. Aldi’s alright, you just have to know what to buy. Their bread is surprisingly good. Though I did have a terrible experience with their customer service last week. Tried to return a faulty kettle and the woman just shrugged! Honestly, shrugged! Shrugged? You wouldn’t get away with that in the old days. People had some respect. It all comes down to training, doesn’t it? And wages, of course. You pay peanuts, you get monkeys. Exactly! And then they wonder why people complain. Though, complaining is a lost art. I tried to lodge a formal complaint with my mobile phone provider – Three – and it’s just endless automated messages. You can’t actually  speak  to anyone. Oh, don’t get me started on mobile phones! My daughter’s got a new contract and they’ve charged her twice for the set-up fee. She’s been on the phone for hours and they keep saying they’ll look into it. It's a disgrace. It’s all these computer systems, isn't it? Take the bank, for example. Used to know Mr. Henderson at the branch, lovely man. You could walk in, have a chat, sort things out. Now it’s all call centres and endless security questions. My building society is the same. They keep trying to get me to use their app, but I’m just not comfortable with it. I like seeing a real person, knowing who I’m dealing with. I’m worried about all this online banking, honestly. All that data floating around. Makes you wonder what they’re doing with it all. They say it's secure, but who knows? I’ve been watching a nature program about hedgehogs. Apparently, their numbers are dwindling because of all the development and the loss of habitat. Makes you think, doesn't it? We're all losing something. That's so sad. We saw a fox in the garden last week, which was lovely. Though our neighbour complained it was frightening his cat.

Right, so we’re doing favourites, yeah? Like, ultimate favourites. I’ll start. Holiday-wise, definitely South Africa. Obvs. It just… feels like home, even though I didn't grow up there permanently. The sunsets are insane. What about you, Chloe? Ooh, tough one. I think… Italy. We did a road trip last summer and it was just amazing. The food, the scenery, the people. It was just perfect. Plus, I’m obsessed with pasta. Italy is lovely! I’d have to say Ireland. Wild Atlantic Way. It’s breathtaking. Literally. The wind nearly blew me off a cliff a few times, but it’s worth it. And the pubs, obviously. Wales, naturally! Honestly, the coastline is just unbeatable. Especially the Gower Peninsula. You can walk for miles and miles and it’s just…peaceful. Though, a good beach holiday in Spain is a close second. Ooh, Spain is good! I’m a sucker for a good all-inclusive. But, yeah, probably Cornwall. I know it’s a bit predictable, but I just love it. Proper cream teas and little fishing villages. Bliss. Right, animals? Who’s got a favourite? Okay, this is easy. Lions. Always lions. Majestic, powerful… they’re just the best. I'm a massive dog person. Always have been, always will be. Specifically, Golden Retrievers. They're just so friendly and fluffy and… perfect! Horses. Definitely horses. Grew up riding, and I still try to get out whenever I can. There's just something magical about them. And Galway ponies are the best. Small but mighty! Otters! They’re so playful and clever. I went on a kayaking trip in Scotland and saw a family of otters swimming alongside us. It was the highlight of my year. Cats, definitely cats. Low maintenance, cuddly…they just judge you silently, and I appreciate that. Especially Scottish Folds. They look like little owls! Okay, last one: food. Absolute favourite food. Go! Pizza. 100% pizza. Any kind, any toppings. Pizza is always the answer. Shepherd's Pie. Proper Irish Shepherd's Pie. With lamb and loads of gravy. It’s comfort food heaven. Welsh rarebit. It's basically glorified cheese on toast, but it's  so  good. Especially with a dollop of chutney. Curry. Indian curry. Specifically, a madras. Bring on the spice! Ooh, good choice! I’m going with boerewors. It's a South African sausage, proper grilled and… just amazing.

Honestly, I just… I can’t even  think  about writing this essay. It's on post-structuralism and honestly, it feels like they just made up words to sound clever. Tell me about it. I’ve been staring at a blank page for like, three hours. It’s supposed to be about Baudrillard, right? And simulations? My brain is officially fried. Yeah! Baudrillard. It’s just… layers and layers of abstract nonsense. Like, what even  is  reality anymore? It’s probably all just computer code anyway. Which actually, that kinda makes me wanna just play Sims instead. Ooh, Sims. Good shout. I was thinking of firing up Animal Crossing later. Bit more chill, you know? Though, even  that  feels performative sometimes. Like you’re curating a perfect little life for internet points. Exactly! It’s like, are we even allowed to be messy anymore? Everything’s gotta be Insta-worthy. Makes you wonder what old age is gonna be like. Everyone trying to look 25 with filters and surgery. Ugh, don't even go there. Seriously. I saw a TikTok the other day of a woman who looked, like, 60 but she’d used a filter to make herself look… ten? And it was genuinely horrifying. Like, just embrace the wrinkles, you know? Right?! I'd rather just… be authentically ancient. I mean, imagine being properly old, like, 90 or something. You’ve seen so much, done so much. You get a pass on everything. True. You can just sit in a corner and judge everyone without consequence. Though, thinking about being that old… it’s a bit bleak, isn’t it? Just… waiting? Maybe? Or maybe you spend all your time painting. I was looking at that Hockney exhibition online, the one with all the iPad paintings. It's stunning. Really bright and colourful. Makes getting old look kinda… vibrant. Oh, I love Hockney! He’s amazing. Actually, I saw a little gallery in town the other day selling prints of local artists. Mostly landscapes. It was nice, properly calming. We should go check it out sometime. When we finally finish these essays. Definitely! That sounds perfect. Honestly, just escaping the library for five minutes feels like a win right now. I think I need chocolate to power through though. And maybe another hour of procrastinating on TikTok. Sounds like a plan. I’m gonna go make a cuppa.

Right, so I was thinking…pasta? Again? We’ve had pasta like, three times this week. Hey, don’t look at me! You were the one who bought that massive bag of penne. And honestly, after a twelve-hour shift, I don’t have the brainpower to devise a culinary masterpiece. I know, I know. It's just…it feels like all we eat is beige. I saw Chloe posting pictures of this amazing Thai green curry she made. Chloe always makes everything look amazing. It’s a curated Instagram life, that’s all. Probably spent three hours prepping. Besides, remember her attempt at a soufflé? Disaster. Okay, valid point. Still, maybe we should try and be a bit more adventurous? Like, actually  use  that spice rack? Maybe. Though I’m still scarred from the chilli incident last month. My mouth was on  fire . Okay, okay, point taken. Low spice levels only. Speaking of fire, how was your shift? Rough one? Ugh. So rough. Had a patient who was convinced the hospital was secretly a spaceship. Took a good hour to de-escalate that. It’s days like those I question all my life choices. Oh no, that sounds… intense. Honestly, you're a saint. I just spent my day trying to get a presentation to format correctly. The stakes are so much lower. Don't downplay your work! Project coordinating is stressful in its own way. All those deadlines and people relying on you… It's just...it doesn’t feel like I’m  helping  anyone, you know? You’re literally making a difference in people’s lives. We all contribute something, even if it doesn't feel like it sometimes. Besides, someone has to keep everything organized, otherwise chaos reigns. Which reminds me, have you heard back from Liam? Oh! Actually, yeah. He texted earlier. He’s free on Saturday. He said he was thinking we could go to that new escape room? Oh, nice! The pirate one? I’ve heard good things. Count me in. It'll be good to catch up. I haven't seen him in ages. Yeah, ages. He’s been super busy with his new job. Apparently, his boss is…demanding. Classic Liam. Attracting all the intense people. He always had a knack for it. Tell me about it. Remember Sarah from uni? The one who made him write her poetry every day? Oh god, don’t remind me.

Right, so have you both had a chance to look over the speaker consent form? Just want to make sure we’re all clear on what we’re signing up to with this event. I have, yes. Seems fairly standard, doesn’t it? The usual clauses about recording, usage of materials, that sort of thing. Though the bit about image rights feels a little… broad. I agree about the image rights. It says they can use photos for “promotional purposes” but doesn’t specify  where  those promotional purposes might be. Social media, university website, press releases… it's a bit open-ended. Aye, that’s what I thought. I’m not against them using images, but I’d like a bit more clarification. Perhaps we should email the events team and ask for specifics? Before we sign anything. Good idea. We don’t want to inadvertently agree to having our faces plastered all over, say, a recruitment brochure without knowing. Definitely. Okay, while we’re on details, let’s quickly run through the structure for the seminar again. I’ve been tinkering with my section on non-verbal communication across cultures. Lovely. I was thinking I’d start us off with a broad overview of the challenges in international business communication. Setting the scene, if you like. Highlighting the reasons why misunderstandings happen. Sounds good, Brenda. That’ll give a good foundation. Then I was planning to focus on written communication - email etiquette, avoiding jargon, the importance of clarity. I’ve got a few examples of disastrous emails to share, always goes down well. Oh, excellent! People love a good disaster story. Following on from that, I’ll tackle the non-verbal side, as I said. Body language, proxemics - how close you stand to someone, that sort of thing. And then a bit on cultural concepts of time. Sounds like a really solid structure, actually. Will there be time for a Q&A at the end? I think so, if we’re fairly disciplined with timing. They’ve allocated us an hour and a half. We should aim for about 30 minutes each, leaving 30 for questions. Agreed. And we need to leave some space for interactive elements. Maybe a quick case study, something where the audience can discuss potential communication pitfalls? Ooh, I like that. I have a couple of scenarios I used in a previous module. They're based on real-life examples I’ve encountered.

Honestly, that seminar was… a lot. Old Man Hemmings really outdid himself today. Just rambling, completely lost his thread three times, and then tried to claim it was  deliberate  ambiguity. Sounds about right. He thinks being incomprehensible is intellectual. Did anyone actually ask a question? Just poor, brave Amelia. She tried, bless her, but he just sort of batted the question back at her with a vaguely condescending “And  what  do  you  think, my dear?” and then moved on. It's exhausting being in the same room as him. You’d think after fifteen years lecturing he’d have figured out a coherent structure. It feels like he just… thinks aloud. Is he still going on about post-structuralism? Worse. He's moved onto deconstruction, which, frankly, feels like just making things deliberately confusing for the sake of it. I spent the whole hour fighting the urge to just doodle little angry faces in my notebook. You should have. I bet half the class were. Still, at least it's nearly the end of term. True. Just a few more weeks of Hemmings and then glorious, blessed freedom. Though then I have to start marking all those essays… Don't even. We agreed - strict no-work talk after 6pm. This is our decompression time. Speaking of decompression… how did the plumber go today? Did he actually  find  the leak? Ugh. Don’t even ask. He spent two hours poking around, declared it was “definitely a pipe,” charged us a diagnostic fee bigger than my grocery bill, and then said he needed to “get a specialist in.” A specialist? For a leaky pipe? What kind of specialist? A pipe whisperer? Apparently. He said it might be a more “complex issue”. I suspect he just didn’t want to deal with it. It’s always the way, isn't it? They come and diagnose the problem, then vanish and you’re left with another bill and still a dripping ceiling. Absolute cowboys. We need to find a reliable one. It’s just… finding anyone willing to come out to this end of town seems impossible. Everyone's booked solid or charges a fortune for the "journey". It’s the same with everything. Gardeners, electricians… It’s like they think we live in some remote rural wilderness. We’re ten minutes from the city centre! Exactly. It’s infuriating. Maybe we should just learn to do everything ourselves?

Honestly, the amount of food people waste is just… infuriating. I had a parent complaining today about the school lunches, saying her son ‘doesn’t like’ the fruit salad. Doesn’t  like  it. Meanwhile, kids are going hungry. It's ridiculous isn’t it? Like, a bit of picky eating isn’t a valid reason to contribute to a massive global issue. Did you explain that to her? I tried! Gently, of course. I said we try to encourage them to try everything, but we can’t force them. And that there are children who really benefit from a nutritious meal. She just huffed. Classic. They think their little Timmy is the only one who matters. Reminds me of Nan and Grandad, though. They never wasted a thing. Everything was used, repurposed, pickled… Oh God, yes! Their house was…maximalist, to put it mildly. Every surface covered. And everything had a story attached. Do you remember that horrifying floral armchair? Horrifying is an understatement. It was like a floral explosion. But comfy, I'll give it that. And it smelt of mothballs and Werther’s Originals. But seriously, they didn’t believe in throwing anything away. They lived through the war, you know? That generation were just…different. Completely. It makes you think about how easy we have it now, doesn't it? Anyway, I started binge-watching that new series, ‘Severance’… have you seen it? Oh yeah! It’s brilliant isn’t it? Super creepy. I’m only a couple of episodes in. It’s got that kind of ‘Black Mirror’ vibe. Exactly! It’s making me question my entire career. Teaching is… draining. I'm thinking maybe I should’ve followed you into engineering. At least you're building things. It’s not all glamorous, believe me. Lots of spreadsheets. But yeah, it feels useful, I guess. Though the whole industry is becoming increasingly automated. They're talking about replacing engineers with robots within twenty years. Seriously? That’s terrifying! What's the point of all that study then? It’s like, what careers are even going to be  safe ? It's a good question. That's why I think they need to focus more on practical skills in schools. Less abstract theory, more work experience. Let kids see what real jobs are like. Definitely. And stop pushing everyone towards university. It’s not for everyone. Remember old Mr. Henderson?

Right, so I think I’ve got everything chopped for this curry. Just need to start frying it off. How was your day? Absolute chaos, I assume? You have no idea. Honestly, the amount of safeguarding concerns that landed on my desk today… It's exhausting. It feels like everyone is dealing with something. Little Timmy’s grandma is having a breakdown, Sarah’s parents are splitting up, and Mark… well, Mark just needs a lot of support. Wow, that  is  a lot. Sounds like you’re holding everyone else together. Is there any actual assessment work getting done amidst all that? Barely. It’s all reactive firefighting. I swear, sometimes I think my job description should just be ‘Professional Worrier’. At least it feels that way. What about you? Any breakthroughs in the world of health psychology? Not exactly breakthroughs. More like… incremental steps forward. Still wrestling with the data from the intervention study. It’s just… messy. So many confounding variables, it’s a nightmare trying to isolate anything meaningful. I’m starting to think the whole thing was flawed from the start. Oh, no. Don’t say that! You put so much work into it. Remember you were practically living in the lab for weeks? I do. And I'm worried it was all for nothing. Maybe the sample size was too small, or the control group wasn't really a control group. All those “maybes” keep looping in my head. Well, you're a scientist, you know that's part of the process. It's not a failure if you learn something, even if it’s ‘this approach doesn’t work’. Besides, you’re brilliant at what you do. You’ll figure it out. Easy for you to say, you’re the calm and collected one. I overthink everything. It’s a skill, honed over years of wrangling teenagers. Speaking of things I overthink, I’ve been worrying about Mum and Dad again. Dad's been really quiet on the phone lately. Oh really? That’s not like him. He usually has a story about the garden or some local gossip. Exactly. And Mum just brushes it off, says he’s “just tired”. But I know him. He’s probably just not wanting to worry me. Maybe give him a call directly? Just a quick chat, see how he’s truly doing. Sometimes they just need someone to listen.

It’s funny, isn’t it? How a bit of sea air can… well, not  fix  things, but… you know. Just makes you breathe a little easier. Though Margate’s not what it was, is it? All those amusement arcades. Used to be proper rock shops, selling traditional sweets. It’s changing everywhere, isn’t it? Harrow’s unrecognisable. Used to know everyone on the street. Now it’s just flats, and people rushing about, never a hello. Makes you feel a bit… well, invisible. Aye, that’s a feeling I know. Though Birmingham’s got its own pace, that’s for sure. Still, kids keep you grounded. Even when dealing with a Year 8 class feels like herding cats. Cats are easier, I reckon. Remember when Doreen wanted to buy that little house down by the beach? Said it would be our retirement dream. Little did we know… Oh, don’t start on that again, Arthur. It wasn’t Doreen’s fault the market crashed. And it was a lovely little place. Lovely, and completely unaffordable after the first six months of mortgage payments. Took years to untangle that mess. She tried, bless her, but… relationships, aren’t they? Built on sand, sometimes. They can be. It's funny, though, isn't it? You carry those things with you. I’m still trying to sort out some financial stuff with my sister. She always struggled, and now… well, she's hit a really rough patch. It's draining, honestly. It is. Supporting family can. Are  you  alright, though? You sound a bit… low. Just tired, I think. School’s been tough, lots of kids struggling with anxiety. Hard not to absorb some of that, you know? Makes you wonder what the point of it all is sometimes. That sounds a bit like… well, like my Geoff used to get. Proper down in the dumps. Wouldn't talk to anyone. Didn't seek any help either. Stubborn as an old mule, he was. You have to encourage them, Arthur. That’s the hardest part. You can offer support, but you can’t  make  them take it. Have you thought about volunteering, maybe? It can give you a bit of purpose. That's actually… a good idea. There’s a tutoring program at the local library. Might be something. It’s just… finding the energy. Little things help. I’ve been watching a pair of baby blue tits building a nest in the garden.

Honestly, this stuff is amazing. Look at the difference. It’s like… instant smoothing. Ooh, let me have a look. Wow, yeah, that’s pretty good. Is it expensive? Everything good always is. It's not  terrible . It was about £25, but I got it on a three for two offer at Boots. So, kind of manageable. I've been using it under my foundation and it just makes everything look… less crepy, you know? Crepy is definitely the word. I’m starting to get those little lines around my eyes. Stress, mostly. Dealing with Mrs. Higgins all day doesn’t exactly help the wrinkles, let me tell you. Oh, bless you. She sounds… challenging. I had a student yesterday who kept trying to barter with me for extra lesson time. Offered me a bag of biscuits. Oh, no! A bag of biscuits? That’s… something. Well, better than Mrs. Higgins, I suppose. She once tried to pay for her stamps with foreign currency. Honestly. Speaking of challenging, have you seen Sarah lately? She’s completely changed her hair again. It’s bright purple now. No way! Purple? Really? She was just blonde a few weeks ago. That girl is obsessed. She can’t leave her hair alone for five minutes. I know! It’s… a commitment. And it always looks a bit patchy, doesn’t it? I mean, I admire her boldness, but I could never. I’m too boring for bright hair. Me too. I tried a slightly lighter shade of brown last year, and I felt so self-conscious. I looked like a different person. I just stuck with what I know. Though, I  am  thinking of getting my nails done. Maybe a nice, neutral colour. Ooh, yes! That’s a good idea. I had a gel manicure last week. It’s so much better than regular polish. Doesn't chip after like, five minutes. What colour were you thinking? I don't know. Maybe a pale pink? Or a sort of…dusty rose? Something subtle. I saw a really nice shade in the window of that new nail place on Elm Street. The one near the bakery. Oh, ‘Polished’? Yeah, they seem good. A bit pricey though, isn’t it? Probably. But I deserve a treat, don’t I? After a week of Mrs. Higgins. Maybe we could go together? Next week? That’s a great idea!

Honestly, the parking around here is a joke, innit? Five quid for an hour! Robbery. I nearly just drove back home, honestly. Tell me about it. I was circling for twenty minutes last week trying to find a spot near the Women’s Hospital. Ended up having to pay a fortune. More expensive than the coffee, probably. Definitely. So, how’s work been? Still dealing with absolute chaos, I imagine? You have no idea. Had a case yesterday… a family, really struggling. Mum’s addicted, kids are bouncing between care and relatives. It just… gets to you, you know? Brutal. You’re a good egg for doing that, though. Seriously. I mean, I teach teenagers how to say "the" correctly, you’re actually making a difference. Yeah, well, someone’s gotta. How’s the teaching going anyway? Found any future Shakespeare’s yet? Nah, mostly just kids who want to learn enough English to order a pint on holiday. Still, beats a proper job, eh? Seriously though, I’m thinking about applying for that Masters at Uni. The one in Applied Linguistics. Oh, that’s brilliant! You’ve been talking about that for ages. Go for it, man! You’d be amazing. Have you looked at the entry requirements and stuff? Yeah, just need to get a good reference from the head of department, which shouldn’t be too bad. And then the interview… that’s the scary bit. They want to know what your ‘research interests’ are. I just wanna teach people to speak proper, not dissect the Oxford English Dictionary! You’ll be fine. Just talk about how you want to help students, how you're passionate about language. Sell yourself! You’re a natural. Speaking of scary, I’m going to Sarah’s wedding next month. You going? Yeah, booked the train already. Hoping it doesn’t cost me another five quid just to park near the station! It’ll be good though, won’t it? She's been planning it for ages. Ages. She's got spreadsheets and everything. It’ll be massive. And then she’s talking about moving house afterwards... can you believe it? Really? Where to? Somewhere out in the Wirral, apparently. Got a dog now, needs more space. She’s obsessed with that little mutt. Good on her. I’m still toying with the idea of getting a cat. But then, I’m never home, are I?

It’s just… frustrating, you know? He keeps saying he wants us to be a ‘team’ with the kids, but a team does things  together . It feels like I’m constantly managing his involvement, making sure he actually follows through with things he says he’ll do. Oh, I know that feeling. It's exhausting, isn't it? It’s like you end up doing double duty – parenting your own kids  and  subtly parenting their dad. Exactly! And it's not like he's a bad person, honestly. He's lovely with the kids when he  is  present. It’s just… the consistent follow-through is missing. And I find myself getting resentful, which is awful. I don’t  want  to feel resentful. It's so easy to fall into that trap, though. Especially when you’re the one picking up the pieces. It's bound to happen, and it doesn't make you a bad person for feeling that way. It’s a really tricky balance, step-parenting. You want to be supportive, but you also need to protect your own kids, and your own sanity. Sanity is the key word! And it's not even about the big things necessarily. It’s the little things. He’ll say he’ll pack Leo’s swimming kit, and then the morning of, it's me frantically digging through the laundry. Or he’ll promise to help with homework, and then gets distracted with… well, anything. Men! Honestly. Though, Leo’s lucky to have you, at least you get it done. I’m completely losing my brain cells with this toddler. She’s at that lovely stage of saying “no” to everything, and then crying when you actually let her have her way. Oh, the tyranny of the toddler! I remember those days. It feels like your entire existence revolves around snacks and preventing minor disasters. It absolutely is. And it's…isolating. I feel like I’ve lost a part of myself. Before, I had a career, a social life… now it’s just endless wiping and nappy changes. I know it’s temporary, but it feels like forever. It's hard not being… independent, you know? I get that. It's a huge shift. We’re so used to being capable, self-sufficient women. And then suddenly, you’re completely reliant on someone else to… basically keep a tiny human alive.

Honestly, I’ve been sucked into Pinterest again. It’s a total time void, isn’t it? One minute you’re looking at a recipe for sourdough, the next you’re deep-diving into minimalist Scandi interiors. Oh God, Pinterest. The black hole of aspirational living. My sister’s absolutely obsessed. She's planning a whole garden makeover based on what she's seen on there. It’ll look amazing, if she ever actually gets around to building it. Exactly! It’s all planning, no doing. I’ve got like, twenty saved wedding ideas, despite not even being remotely close to getting married. It’s just… pretty pictures. The power of pretty pictures. Speaking of things that consume your life, have you started watching ‘Severance’ yet? Everyone at the department is talking about it. Oh, I have! Ben told me to ages ago. It’s utterly bizarre, isn’t it? Like…what  is  going on? It’s properly unsettling. And Adam Scott is brilliant. Right? Brilliant. It's the kind of show that makes you question everything. I finished it last week and I’m still thinking about it. It’s giving me serious ‘Black Mirror’ vibes. Definitely. Though, ‘Black Mirror’ feels almost… tame now, compared to the stuff that's coming out. It's like we’re all bracing for dystopia. Tell me about it. Oh, and a quick reminder - it’s Liam’s birthday next week, isn’t it? Have you got him anything yet? Oh, crikey! I completely forgot! I’ve been so swamped with work, it’s flown by. I was thinking maybe a voucher for that craft beer place he likes? Or is that too boring? No, that’s good. He loves that place. Maybe with one of those fancy glasses? He’s always going on about needing proper beer glasses. Good shout. I'll pop and get that sorted tomorrow. How’s Sarah doing, by the way? Haven't seen her in ages. She said she was starting a new pottery class. She’s good! Absolutely loving the pottery. Apparently, she’s making these incredibly wonky, but endearing, little plant pots. She sent me a picture, they’re genuinely hilarious. She’s thinking of selling them at a local market. That's brilliant! She’s always been so creative. We need to get a proper meet-up sorted soon. It feels like ages since we’ve all hung out properly.

Oh, look at this one. It’s… a bit much, isn’t it? All sparkly glass. Reminds me of a ballroom.  Scoffs  Ballroom in the hallway? No thanks. I thought we said something… industrial? Matte black, maybe? We did, we did. I just… it was only £39.99. And it  is  pretty. Just… not right. Scroll down. There’s one a bit further down that's more… us.  Clicks mouse  Hmm. That's… functional. Looks like something you’d find in a garage. It’s modern! And it’s only twenty quid. We can't spend a fortune on a light fitting, remember? Especially when we might be… moving. True. Speaking of moving… did you see that one on Rightmove? The one near the park? The one with the wonky bay window? Wonky is character! And it’s got a garden. A proper garden, not just a patch of grass. And it needs a complete gutting. The kitchen looks like it hasn’t been touched since the seventies. Avocado green everywhere, I bet. We’d get to choose everything, though. Make it exactly how we want it. Plus, it's in catchment for that school we were talking about. It’s just… the price. It’s a bit optimistic, isn't it? For the amount of work it needs. Everything is optimistic these days. People just seem to think their houses are worth a fortune. We could always offer lower. Maybe. But I don’t want to get into a bidding war. Remember what happened with the last one? It drove me mad. That was different. That one was already lovely, just needed a bit of painting. This one's a project. Which is what we said we wanted. I know, I know. It’s just… daunting. It’s a big decision, isn't it? It is. But a good one, I think. Let’s save the listing, and maybe go and view it next weekend? If they have any viewing slots left. Alright. Let's do that. Oh, wait – this light fitting! This one’s actually quite good. It's got those Edison bulbs. Edison bulbs? Aren't those ridiculously expensive? No, you can get LED ones now. They look the same. And it's only… fifty-nine ninety-nine. Fine. Fifty-nine ninety-nine. But if we buy a house, and it needs a new kitchen, I’m blaming you and your sparkly lights.

Honestly, the shift was  mental  yesterday. Mrs. Henderson decided she was a professional opera singer at 3am. Full volume. Oh, bless her! She does love a bit of drama, doesn’t she? Still, you’re a nurse, you’re used to emergencies, aren’t you? A surprise concert must be mild in comparison. It’s different when you're trying to  sleep  on a night shift! And then Mr. Davies decided he needed a midnight snack and tried to make toast. In his room. With a blanket over the toaster. Oh my god! Seriously? Seriously! I had to wrestle the toaster away from him. The fire alarm went off, obviously. It was chaos. Honestly, I need a holiday. You deserve one. You always get the interesting ones, don’t you? I had a relatively quiet day. Old Mr. Peterson just kept asking for his cat, Winston. Apparently, Winston ran off years ago. Poor Mr. Peterson. Is he… alright, mentally? He's mostly okay, just very lonely, I think. Dementia’s creeping in. It’s heartbreaking, really. Makes you appreciate your own families, doesn’t it? Speaking of, how’s your mum doing, Sarah? She’s good, she's good. Still nagging me about finding a ‘nice young man’. Apparently, being a dedicated nurse isn’t attractive enough these days. My nan’s the same. Constant questions about if I’m seeing anyone. I just tell her I’m ‘focused on my career’. That usually shuts her up for about five minutes. Smart move. It's a diplomatic answer. Have you heard anything back about that job you applied for, Chloe? The one at the residential home? Not yet. I’m trying not to get my hopes up. It sounds really nice, though. More consistent hours than my agency work, and I really like the look of the residents. Though, honestly, after hearing your stories, I'm starting to think every care job involves some sort of emergency! It does have its moments! But it’s rewarding, you know? Making a difference, even in small ways. I'm actually thinking of doing some extra hours at the day centre. They’re desperate for cover. That’s good of you, Helen. You’ve always been a natural with people. I’m dreading going back to the ward after this coffee, honestly. I need to start looking at houses again, too. This flat is just…too small.

…and apparently, the big thing now isn’t blackout curtains or white noise, it’s temperature. Like, a really cool room. Apparently, your core body temperature needs to drop by a couple of degrees to get proper deep sleep. Really? That’s… surprisingly simple. All this money I’ve spent on fancy pillows and eye masks… and it's just about being cold? Seems that way. They were talking about it on this podcast. It’s all about signaling to your brain it’s time to shut down. Though, you’d think our brains would have figured that out by now, wouldn’t you? After, you know, millennia. You’d think so. It's a bit frustrating. Though, actually, I  do  tend to sleep better when it’s a bit chilly. Remember that camping trip to the Lake District? I was freezing, but slept like a log. Oh god, that camping trip. That was… an adventure. You nearly impaled yourself on a tent peg in the dark. Don’t remind me! And then getting completely lost trying to find the pub. Honestly, that village was a labyrinth. Every lane looked exactly the same. We spent a good hour circling that one field, didn’t we? I was convinced we were going in a big loop. And the map… utterly useless. Useless is an understatement. It looked like it had been drawn by a toddler. Speaking of getting lost, remember that time in Rome? Trying to find the Trevi Fountain? Oh, that was a disaster. I thought I had a good sense of direction, but those tiny, winding streets… it was impossible. We ended up wandering around for hours, ending up near the Pantheon, which was lovely, but not what we’d intended. We should have just asked for directions. I was too proud. Insisted I could navigate. My pride nearly cost us a gelato. It always comes back to gelato, doesn’t it? Anyway. Cool rooms. Must remember that. Speaking of navigation, did you read about that pilot who landed a plane at Farnborough with no landing gear? I saw something about it! Incredible. Apparently, his control was absolutely phenomenal. Must be so stressful though, knowing you're coming in to land without wheels. Apparently, it was a training exercise gone wrong. Something with a simulated failure during a touch-and-go. Still, landing a plane like that… it takes serious skill.

Honestly, I’m convinced Hamish thinks he’s a tiny human. The way he stares at you when you’re eating… it's judgemental, I swear. Oh my god, you're right! They  do  have such little personalities, don’t they? Mine, Pip, just spends his entire life stuffing his cheeks until they look like golf balls. You’ve got to be careful with the stuffing, though. Old Man Tiberius – my grandad’s hamster when I was little – got impacted and had to go to the vet. It was a whole saga. A hamster vet visit? That sounds…intense. Did he pull through? Eventually! But Grandad was beside himself. He’d built Tiberius this amazing multi-level cage with little tunnels and everything. He was very dedicated. That’s sweet. Hamish has a wheel, obviously, but he mostly uses it to… store food. Like a tiny, furry pantry. They’re weirdos. Honestly, they're like tiny, fluffy hoarders. Did you see that video going around of the hamster who’d hidden like, a whole bag of crisps in his bedding? Oh my gosh, yes! It was incredible. They’re so determined. Speaking of determined… have you two seen that new lad in the library, the one with the bright red hair? Oh, Ethan? Yeah! He's… striking. Striking is one word for it. He’s completely rocking the ginger aesthetic, isn't he? I saw him with a little Van Gogh sunflower pin on his bag. He's alright. A bit...intense, maybe? Keeps staring out the window like he's writing poetry about the rain. Ha! That sounds about right for a ginger. No offence to gingers, obviously. My cousin’s a ginger and he’s lovely, but they all have that… artistic brooding vibe. It’s just a stereotype, isn't it? But it’s a  strong  stereotype. I mean, Ron Weasley. It's ingrained in our culture. True. And honestly, it’s kinda endearing. It's like they come pre-packaged with a certain melancholy. It’s probably just the pale skin and freckles. Makes them look perpetually thoughtful. Whatever it is, he’s certainly noticeable. I think Maisie's got a bit of a crush on him. She keeps ‘accidentally’ sitting near him in the refectory. Oh, Maisie! Bless her. She’s very… direct. I reckon he knows. Probably. But hey, good for her! You gotta shoot your shot, right?

Right, okay, so if I move three armies from Iceland… and then… oh, hang on. Mum, are you sure this map is right? Greenland looks ridiculously small. It's a Risk map, lad, not a National Geographic spread. They simplify things for… well, for world domination, I suppose. Though, honestly, I always thought Greenland was bigger. It’s all that ice, innit? Makes it  seem  bigger. Honestly, you two. Still battling over Greenland? It’s been two hours. Aaron's parties were less strategically complex than this. And quieter. Hey! Aaron's parties required a different kind of strategy. Namely, avoiding eye contact with Brenda and her endless cat stories. Brenda's a harmless soul. A bit… enthusiastic. Speaking of enthusiastic, you’re building a massive force in Kamchatka. What’s the plan there? World domination via the Pacific Rim? It’s a defensive move! I’m anticipating your inevitable push from Asia. Remember last time? You steamrolled me. You left Australia completely undefended, darling. That was your downfall. Honestly, you need to read the instructions more carefully. They do have a logic to them, you know. I  have  read the instructions. Several times! They just... contradict themselves. Like, ‘Fortify your borders!’ and then, two lines later, ‘Aggressive expansion is key!’ Sounds about right. Life’s like that, innit? Contradictory. You need your glasses, maybe? Everything looks a bit fuzzy. I  am  wearing my glasses! And it's not fuzziness, it’s artistic licence. Look, can we just play? I want to conquer North America before dinner. Speaking of dinner, I'm smelling something burning. Is that the chocolate brownies? I put them in ages ago. Probably. You tend to put things in and forget about them. Reminds me of when you tried to learn Mandarin. A promising start, then… silence. It was complicated! And I had a lot on. Plus, the tones! It's impossible to get the tones right. Anyway, play your game. I'm checking on the brownies. And turning up the music. Something a bit more upbeat. This is depressing. Good, something without bagpipes. Okay, roll the dice. This is for North America… six, four… yes! Take that, Asia! Hold on, hold on. You’ve forgotten about me in Brazil. You think I've been sitting here admiring the scenery? Oh, right. You. Blast. This is why I hate Risk. Pure, unadulterated luck. It’s not about skill, it’s about rolling a six.

Honestly, I’m starting to seriously doubt this whole uni thing. Like, what am I even  doing  here? Everyone else seems so…focused. They’ve all got five-year plans and I'm just… existing. Oh, come  on . Don’t be so dramatic, Liv. Everyone pretends to have a five-year plan, they don’t actually stick to them. Trust me. My cousin swore she’d be a solicitor by now, she’s working in a dog grooming salon. A very posh dog grooming salon, admittedly, but still. Yeah, but that’s different. She  wanted  to groom dogs! I haven’t even figured out what I want to do. Is marine biology even a real career? I’m starting to think I just liked the David Attenborough documentaries. It’s a real career! Loads of people do it. Though, yeah, maybe think about the job prospects  after  all the studying. What about something…adjacent? Like, marine conservation? Or environmental stuff? You’re really good at campaigns, remember that petition you organised about the plastic on Gylly Beach? Okay, yeah, that was a good day. But still…it’s all so much pressure. And then everyone’s talking about internships and placements and I’m worried I’m already behind. Honestly, you're not. You're a first year, everyone's fumbling around. And besides, you're way smarter than you give yourself credit for. Remember when you explained photosynthesis to Mrs. Higgins in biology? She was baffled! She always was a bit slow. Speaking of baffled, did you see that picture of Harry Styles with a tiny baby? Online? No! Is it true? Is he a dad?! Oh my god. The internet is going to  explode . No one knows! It's all rumours, apparently. But people are losing their minds. Some are saying it’s his sister’s baby and he's just holding it. It’s chaos. Honestly, imagine Harry Styles changing nappies.
