It’s a vibe. It's a whole mood. Though, it makes you think, doesn't it? Like, what if  we  had babies one day? Woah, slow down! We're barely capable of keeping a cactus alive, let alone a human. Actually, remember Brenda the cactus? What happened to Brenda? Oh god, Brenda! She met an unfortunate accident with the vacuum cleaner. It was a tragedy. A prickly, dusty tragedy. But seriously, babies… nah. Not for a long,  long  time.

Honestly, this Geography project is killing me. Like, "Assess the impact of socio-economic factors on urban decay in Slough." Seriously? Who even  cares  about urban decay? It's alright, innit? Mr. Davies is just trying to make us think about stuff. It's actually kinda interesting once you start looking into it. Interesting? I’ve spent the last three hours staring at photos of abandoned buildings and reading council reports. It’s depressing, not interesting. And it all comes down to people just being…poor, doesn’t it? Well, yeah, partly. But it’s more complicated than that. Like, businesses leaving, people moving out...it’s a whole cycle. My uncle Raj works with the council, he says it's about investment, too. Or lack of it. Investment? Right. So, rich people decide where to put their money and if Slough isn’t shiny enough, they go elsewhere and everyone else is left with…this. It's a bit unfair, isn’t it? Life's unfair, man. You know that. It's not like we're exactly living in Beverly Hills. Remember old Mr. Henderson? His flat got flooded last year and the council took ages to help him. Yeah, that was awful. He barely had any money as it was. Did they ever fix it properly? I think so. His daughter sorted it, she's pretty sharp. But that's the thing, isn't it? Some people have someone to help them, and others don’t. It makes you think, though. Like, we’re all just buying stuff all the time, chasing the newest trainers or phone...and there are people genuinely struggling to get by. Tell me about it. My mum's always going on about consumerism. Says we're all slaves to it. She’s always reading those articles about how companies manipulate us into buying things we don't need. Your mum is hardcore. Still, she's got a point. I saw an ad for those limited-edition comics today. Fifty quid for a  comic ?! No way! What comic? I need to know if I need to save up! The new 'Cosmic Crusaders' one. Apparently, they only made a thousand copies. They’re already selling for like, a hundred online. Seriously?! That's mental. I'm trying to save up for that new graphics card, though. It's gonna take me ages. Yeah, those are expensive.

Honestly, the recording session yesterday was a nightmare. Absolute nightmare. Oh no, really? What happened? I thought you were really excited about it. I was! I  am  excited about the project, but the sound engineer… honestly, he was like a teenager playing with buttons. Kept asking me to do things again and again, changing the microphone, moving me around… it was exhausting. And he kept talking about “levels” and “compression” like I was supposed to know what he meant. Ugh, sounds frustrating. Did you get anything usable in the end? Eventually, yes. But it took hours longer than it should have. And then old Mrs. Higgins next door decided to start mowing her lawn  during  a quiet take. Honestly, the woman has no consideration. Oh, no! Mrs. Higgins? She seems so… sweet. Sweet as pie to your face, but a menace to peaceful existence. Honestly, I’m considering writing her a very politely worded, but firm, letter. Maybe. Though knowing her, she’ll probably just invite you in for tea and complain about the postman. You’re probably right. Speaking of aches and pains, I had my physiotherapy appointment this morning. My knee is still giving me grief. Oh, still? That’s rubbish. Is it getting any better? A little. The physio says it’s just age, really. Bad joints, apparently. It's all going. The whole system is just… deteriorating. Don't say that! You're not  that  old. Oh, I feel it, love. I feel every single year. I was looking at clothes online last night, and everything seems to be designed for teenagers or people who look like they’ve never eaten a carb in their life. Tell me about it. I went shopping last week, and everything either didn't fit or made me feel like I was trying to dress like a child. Exactly! And don’t even get me started on diets. I tried that new… what was it… the cabbage soup diet. Utterly miserable. I lasted two days and ended up ordering a takeaway. Cabbage soup diet? Oh god, no. That sounds horrific. I tried a juice cleanse once. Another disaster. Just made me feel weak and grumpy. It's all nonsense, isn't it? I mean, a little bit of healthy eating is good, but these extreme diets are just pointless. I’m much happier having a nice piece of cake. Preach! Though I am trying to cut down on biscuits… somewhat.

Right, so I reckon another splash of wine is needed, yeah? This pasta’s… good, really good actually. Better than I expected, considering I basically chucked everything in. “Chucked everything in” is a bit of an understatement, wasn’t it? You’ve actually managed a vaguely coherent Italian dish. I was bracing myself for disaster, I’ll be honest. Hey! I’m a culinary genius in the making. You just don’t appreciate my…rustic style. Honestly though, did you get enough courgette? I felt like I was slicing it for a lifetime. Plenty of courgette. I think you might have slightly overdone the garlic, but hey, that's you. It adds character. Speaking of character, how was your week? Still battling the conference centre chaos? Oh, you have  no  idea. We had a bridal exhibition on, and honestly, the drama. You wouldn’t believe the demands. One bride wanted the entire hall re-arranged at 3pm because the floral arrangements weren’t “vibrant enough." Vibrant enough! Like, lady, we’re in a beige conference centre, what did you expect? Oh god. Bridezillas are a special breed. I’m used to chaos at work, obviously, with production, but it’s usually the ‘shut down the set because the lightbulb is flickering’ kind of chaos. Not ‘my floral arrangements aren’t  vibrant  enough’ chaos. Exactly! And then her mother started complaining that the canapés were too small. Too small! They were perfectly normal-sized canapés. I swear, some people just want to create problems. Sounds exhausting. I feel for you. I had a bit of a nightmare with a supplier this week. They promised us a crucial piece of equipment would be delivered on Tuesday, and it didn’t show up until Thursday afternoon. Cue a frantic scramble to re-schedule everything and a very angry director. Ugh, the worst. The supplier blame game. Classic. Did you manage to smooth things over? Eventually. Lots of apologies, promises of future discounts, the whole shebang. Honestly, I'm starting to think I need a full-time job as a crisis negotiator. I swear, this week aged me ten years. Tell me about it. Fancy ditching all this responsibility and just…opening a flower shop? Or a bakery? Something peaceful. Ooh, a bakery. That actually sounds amazing. Imagine, just surrounded by the smell of warm bread all day. No frantic deadlines, no demanding clients...pure bliss.

Right, okay, so we’re doing film night, yeah? What are we thinking? I’m open to suggestions, honestly, I've been staring at Netflix for an hour and just scrolling. Ooh, I saw a trailer for this horror film, ‘The Blackwood Curse’ or something? Looked proper jump-scare-y. No way, no horror. I swear, if anyone suggests another haunted house flick, I’m heading to the pub. I need a good laugh, something light. I’m with Liam on that. I’m really in the mood for a comedy. Remember ‘Booksmart’? We need something like that. Smart, funny, not… terrifying. Has anyone seen ‘Everything Everywhere All At Once’? I heard it’s amazing, like, properly mind-bending. Oh! I’ve been meaning to watch that. Everyone keeps saying it's incredible. Is it sad though? I’m not really in the mood for a cry-fest right now. It's got bits of sadness, yeah, but it's mostly just completely bonkers in the best way. Like, martial arts and hot dog fingers. You gotta see it. Hot dog fingers? Right, okay, you have my attention. Hot dog… what now? Honestly, that sounds exactly like something Aisling would recommend. It’s wonderfully weird, isn't it? It is! And it's got amazing action sequences too. Michelle Yeoh is a queen. Okay, okay, I’m convinced. ‘Everything Everywhere All At Once’ it is! But we’re getting snacks. Proper snacks. Like, popcorn  and  chocolate. I'm on snack duty! I’m thinking a full-on cinema experience. Popcorn, sweets, maybe even those little boxes of raisins no one ever actually likes. Raisins are a crime against snacking. Absolutely not. Agreed. Raisins are an insult. Get some crisps. Proper crisps. Salt and vinegar. Ooh, good shout. Salt and vinegar  and  some chocolate digestives. Essential. Can we maybe order a pizza as well? I’m feeling properly hungry. Slow down, you lot! We’ve just decided on a film! Pizza can be negotiated. Let’s at least get the film started first. Okay, so ‘Everything Everywhere All At Once’ it is. Who's got the login for Netflix? I do! I’ll get it up and running. And I’ll start mentally preparing the snack haul. This is gonna be a good night. Hot dog fingers. Honestly. It’s gonna be a memorable night, that’s for sure.

Honestly, my feet are  killing  me. Paris is beautiful, don’t get me wrong, but all that walking… I swear I’ve done a month’s worth of steps in three days. Oh dear! You did go on a bit of a rampage, didn’t you? I remember you saying you wanted to see absolutely everything. Did you at least manage to find that little patisserie you were talking about? The one with the macarons? I did! It was amazing. Absolutely worth the blisters. But seriously, I think I’ve got a proper one on my heel. It's throbbing. Let me see.  examining Speaker_1’s foot  Ooh, yeah, that looks… substantial. You’ll need to get some proper blister plasters, not those flimsy ones. Did you take any decent shoes, or were you determined to wear those cute but utterly impractical boots? They  looked  cute, okay? And I thought I could get away with it. Lesson learned. Never underestimate Paris’s pavements. Honestly, I think I hobbled more than I walked by the end of it. Oh, you’re sounding like your grandfather! Always complaining about his feet. Though, to be fair, he did spend a lot of time on them. Did you manage to see the Mona Lisa? Was it as crowded as everyone says? Crowded doesn't even  begin  to cover it. It was like trying to fight your way through a rugby scrum just to get a glimpse. I ended up just taking a picture of the picture, which is probably all anyone does anyway. Sounds stressful. I would have just people-watched. That's my preferred Parisian activity. Cheaper, and much more comfortable. Speaking of comfortable, I’m going to collapse on the sofa. I'm starving too. What's for dinner? I need something that requires minimal effort from my feet. I was thinking of a quick pasta bake. I’ve got some leftover chicken we could throw in. Unless you’ve developed a craving for snails or something while you were gallivanting around France? Snails are… not my thing. Pasta sounds perfect. Although, last night, Chloe was telling me about this amazing fondue place she went to with Ben… Oh, Chloe and Ben. How are they, by the way? Are they still pretending everything’s perfect? That's the million-dollar question. She was putting on a brave face, but I think things are still really rocky.

Morning! You look… remarkably awake for a Monday. Did you have a good weekend? Surprisingly, yeah. Actually really good. Went to Chichester with my sister. It was lovely. Proper seaside vibes, even if it was a bit chilly. How about you? Anything exciting happen? Oh, Chichester! Nice. I haven't been in ages. My weekend was… decidedly less glamorous. Mostly grading papers, unfortunately. A couple of essays on passive voice were… a struggle, let’s say. Seriously, they just didn’t  get  it. Oh, the passives… the bane of every linguistics student’s existence. I remember struggling with those during my Masters. Grading must be awful right now, the deadline's looming isn’t it? Looming is an understatement. It's a mountain. Honestly, I need pay day desperately. I’m existing on instant coffee and the sheer willpower to not scream at grammatical errors. Did you get paid already? You’re on a different schedule, aren't you? I got paid on Friday, thankfully. Retail life means regular income, which is a blessing. Although, being a supervisor isn't always sunshine and roses, you know? Old Mrs. Higgins tried to return a firework she bought last November. Said it was faulty. No way! A firework? Seriously? People are… something else. Tell me about it. It took twenty minutes to explain why that’s not exactly a valid return. Anyway, enough about my retail adventures. How's the TEFL course going? Any particularly memorable students? It’s good, it’s good. Challenging. I’ve got one student from Malaysia, and her English is fantastic, but the dialect is… fascinating. Completely different sentence structure sometimes. It’s making me rethink everything I thought I knew about grammar. Oh, interesting! I love that stuff. My dissertation was partly on dialect variation. It’s amazing how much it affects things. Exactly! I keep wanting to “correct” her, but then I realise it's perfectly valid within her linguistic framework. It’s a constant learning curve. Oh, and I saw Sarah from the office on Saturday. She was with… a ring. A very shiny ring. No! Sarah? Seriously? Is she engaged? Oh my god, that’s amazing! I didn’t even know she had a boyfriend! Apparently, he proposed on Friday. It was all very hush-hush. She was showing it off to everyone in the coffee queue. She looked ridiculously happy. Wow. That’s… a lot.

Right, so you put in… about one and a half cups of water for every cup of rice. See? Like this. One and a half? That seems like a lot. Won't it be all soggy? No, trust me. It absorbs it. It  needs  that much. We used to mess this up all the time when your Dad and I first moved in together. He'd just guess, and it was always either rock hard or… well, paste. Dad and guessing. Sounds about right. So, one and a half. And then we just… boil it? Boil it, then turn the heat right down, put the lid on, and let it simmer for about fifteen minutes. Don’t lift the lid! That’s the key. All the steam stays in. You lift the lid, you lose the steam, you end up with crunchy rice. Right, lid on. Fifteen minutes. Got it. What about the curry sauce? Is that ready? Nearly. I warmed it up, but it could do with a bit of a kick. I was thinking a finely chopped jalapeno? Ooh, yeah! Good idea. They're pretty hot though, aren't they? They are. That's why we only need a little bit. Though honestly, the sauce is a bit bland. I think they skimp on spices now. Remember that amazing Indian place we went to in Bristol? Yeah! The one near the harbour? They did the best naan bread. Exactly! And everything tasted…properly spiced. This stuff… feels like it’s got a lot of salt. I’m trying to be more aware of that kind of thing, you know? All that hidden salt and fat. Yeah, Mum’s always going on about that. She used to read all the labels, checking everything. It's important. It all adds up. Did you see that documentary about… oh, what was it called? About how much sugar is hidden in everything? It was horrifying. No, I missed that. Was it on Netflix? I think so. Anyway, back to the rice. Just keep an eye on it. Don't stir it. Honestly, it's the hardest part, resisting the urge to stir it. Okay, okay. No stirring. It’s like… willpower training for cooking. Precisely! Speaking of willpower, I saw Mrs. Henderson from next door at the butcher's today. She was complaining about the mince going off quickly. Apparently, it went grey yesterday.

Right, so I was thinking, you know, about getting a telly for the room. Not a massive one, just something for… for watching stuff. A telly? Seriously? You’ve been saying that for six months. You haven't even  looked  at prices. I have! Sort of. I saw one in Argos, it was… fifty quid? Maybe seventy. But then I remembered I hadn’t sorted the broadband thing. You need to sort that, honestly. You’re living in the Stone Age. How do you even… exist without internet? I use your Wi-Fi when I’m here. And sometimes I go to the library. It’s fine. It’s not fine, Liam. You’re supposed to be actively looking for work, and you need internet for that. Applications, research… everything. I know, I know. It’s just… finding the money. And then actually sorting it. It’s a whole thing. Have you even  applied  for any jobs this week? Honestly. Don’t start, okay? I sent off two yesterday. Both at the pub. Bar work. Pretty sure I won’t hear back. Pub work again? You have a degree, Liam! Yeah, well, a degree in… Medieval History. Not exactly in high demand around here, is it? Look, I get it’s frustrating. But you can’t just keep applying for the same thing and then being surprised when it doesn’t work. Maybe look at something completely different? Like, I’m looking at taking a course in social media marketing. Maybe something like that could open some doors. Social media marketing? You? I thought you hated social media. I do, mostly. But it's a skill, and it pays. And my work are actually funding it, so it’s a no-brainer. It's a bit stressful though, I'm swamped at work. Old Man Hemmings is breathing down my neck about everything. Said I wasn't “proactive” enough on my last report. Hemmings is awful. He makes Mrs. Higgins from school look nice! Speaking of school... How are your A-Levels going, Chloe? Are you stressing about applications yet? It’s starting. I’ve got to write my personal statement. It's terrifying. Everyone says it has to be  so  perfect. Just write about what you enjoy, yeah? Don't try to be someone you're not. And mention your volunteering. That always looks good. He’s right. And don’t be afraid to ask for help.

Honestly though, I’m beat. This conference was… intense. Like, back-to-back meetings, constantly fixing things, dealing with speakers who decided they needed a completely different AV setup five minutes before they were due on stage. You know the drill. Sounds stressful, love. You always take on too much, don’t ya? You've got to learn to delegate more. It’s alright saying yes to everything, but then you end up knackered like this. Are you even enjoying the job anymore? I do, actually. When it’s  good  it’s really good. Meeting interesting people, seeing an event come together… it's satisfying. It's just… the sheer volume. And the people. Honestly, the egos. You wouldn’t believe. Egos, eh? Always a problem. You get all sorts, don't ya? Remember old Mr. Henderson from down the road? Thought he was God's gift to gardening. Won a rosette at the village fête and acted like he'd won the Chelsea Flower Show. Oh, I remember! He used to lecture everyone on the proper way to prune roses. Bit of a character. But yeah, similar vibe at these conferences. These academics, they think because they’ve published a paper on, I don’t know, the socio-economic impact of garden gnomes, they’re suddenly royalty. Garden gnomes! That’s a bit niche, even for academia. You need a holiday, that’s what you need. A proper one. Somewhere hot. Somewhere you can just lie by a pool and not think about logistics or AV equipment. That sounds… amazing. I was thinking maybe a weekend away with the girls? Maybe Brighton? It’s not exactly the Maldives, but it’s a start. Brighton’s good. Good for a laugh. Have you been keeping up with your running, by the way? You said you were trying to get back into it. I try. Honestly, after work, the last thing I want to do is go for a run. I just collapse on the sofa with a glass of wine and Netflix. It's a vicious cycle. Everything in moderation, eh? Although, you could try running  instead  of the wine occasionally! It’s good for the head, you know. Gets the endorphins going. Easier said than done. You’ve always been good with the discipline, haven't you? Actually, how  are  you keeping? Still doing the daily walks? Yeah, religiously. Keeps me sane.

Right, who’s doing the dishes? I’m not doing them again tonight. Honestly, it's like living with a pack of…well, never mind. Not me. I’m revising for history. Big test tomorrow on… um… the Second World War. Ah, the Second World War. A fascinating, albeit horrific, period. Remember, boys, history isn’t just dates and battles. It’s about understanding  why  things happened. And the consequences. Can I just say, Hitler was a proper villain. Like, the worst. Yes, darling, he absolutely was. A truly awful man. Now, back to the dishes. Nathan? I said I’m revising! It's about the appeasement policy and the… Leave him, love. He’s studying. I’ll do them. Honestly, you two, you'd think I was asking you to single-handedly build the pyramids. Thank you, dear. Honestly, sometimes I wonder where they get it from. I mean, look at that beard you’re cultivating, Daniel. It’s… substantial. It’s distinguished! I’m aiming for a George Clooney vibe. Besides, your mother likes it. Don’t you, darling? It’s… a conversation starter. Though I do worry you look like a slightly disgruntled woodsman. It looks cool, Dad. Yeah, it’s alright. Though, everything you post on Instagram with it looks like a meme. Everything I post? You’ve been monitoring my Instagram, have you? No! I just... saw it on Lily’s feed. She follows you. Oh, Lily. How  is  Lily? You haven’t mentioned her much lately. She's good. We... we’re not really talking at the moment. Oh. Oh dear. What happened? It’s just… stuff. She’s been hanging out with Sophie a lot, and Sophie… well, Sophie thinks I’m a bit immature. Sophie thinks everyone’s immature. She's fifteen. You're fourteen, right? This is all perfectly normal. Heartbreak, misunderstood feelings, questionable fashion choices… it’s all part of the teenage experience. Daniel, don’t trivialize it. It's hard when a girlfriend dumps you. Even if it  is  because of Sophie. I'm not trivializing it! I'm saying it’s a learning experience. It builds character. It prepares him for… well, for the nuanced world of adult relationships. Did you used to get dumped a lot, Dad? Let's just say I wasn’t always the smooth operator I am today. Your mother… she was very patient with me.

Honestly, the sofa… it’s just  massive . Didn’t realise how much space it would take up. Did you get rid of the old one then? Or is it just… sofa city in your living room now? Took it to the tip yesterday. Massive effort, that. Honestly, the queues were insane. Everyone clearly decided yesterday was ‘get rid of all your junk’ day. The tip at High Lane is always rammed on a weekend. Absolute chaos. They need to sort that out. It's always busy. I went a couple of weeks ago with some cardboard and had to queue for like, twenty minutes. Twenty minutes for cardboard! Exactly! And then, the man unloading, he was just… grunt-y. Barely said a word. Just pointed at where to put it. Rude. Oh, they can be like that. Doesn’t pay much, I suppose, dealing with other people’s rubbish all day. Still, a bit of politeness doesn't cost anything. Speaking of dealing with other people’s stuff… did you hear about Sarah’s friend, Karen? Oh, Karen? No, what’s happened? Her husband’s still poorly isn’t he? Yeah, he’s… not great. But apparently, her washing machine broke down, and she ended up getting her mum to do all her washing. Like,  all  of it. Including… you know… things. Oh, goodness me. That’s a bit much isn’t it? I mean, a few loads of normal clothes, fine. But everything? Right? My mum would have a fit. She’s very particular about her washing machine. And who’s washed what in it. Apparently, her mum was complaining about having to wash her son-in-law’s socks. Oh, bless her. Family, eh? Always something. Remember Auntie Brenda and the Christmas pudding incident? Oh god, don’t even  start  me on Auntie Brenda. She always got me those awful knitted tea cosies. Bright orange ones. Every. Single. Year. My nan was the same with the scented candles. Lavender. Everywhere. You could smell it before you even got to the house. It’s the thought that counts, I suppose. Though sometimes you wish people would just… ask what you want. Your Grandad Harry was always good for that. He used to ask me straight: “What do you need, love? Don’t want to waste my money on something you don’t like.” He was a good man, Grandad Harry.

Honestly, Mum, the whole thing with work is just… draining. I mean, they’re calling it a “restructuring,” but we all know what that means. Redundancy, love. It always means redundancy, doesn't it? Such a horrible word. Are you alright though? You sounded a bit stressed on the phone earlier. Yeah, I’m okay. Just… processing. It’s not  definitely  happening yet, there’s a consultation period, but it doesn’t look good. They’re basically streamlining the project management roles. And I’ve only been there just over a year! Oh, that’s awful, darling. After all the hard work you put in. You’ve always been so good at organising things. Honestly, I don't understand these companies sometimes. What are you thinking about doing? Honestly? I have no idea. Start applying for everything and anything, I guess. It's just… demoralising. I was actually starting to enjoy it. Well, you won’t be short of options, you’re bright and capable. You’ll find something else. So, enough about all that doom and gloom! How was your week? Did you manage to get to the gym? I did! Went Tuesday and Thursday. Still feeling it, though. My legs are screaming. You should come with me sometime, it'd be good. Oh, I don't know about that. I’m a bit past the energetic gym phase, I think! Though, I did walk to the shops instead of driving the other day, so I'm making  some  effort. Speaking of which, have you remembered to call Grandad? He was asking after you. Oh, shoot! No, I haven’t. I meant to this morning, it completely slipped my mind. I’ll do it now, as soon as we get home. He was talking about forgetting to eat again, which is worrying. He does that, doesn’t he? He gets so absorbed in his books. You need to remind him to at least have a proper lunch. And speaking of eating… I’m trying to cut down on biscuits. It’s a losing battle, I tell you. I know the feeling! I’ve been craving chocolate all week. Stress-eating, clearly. What are your plans for the weekend? Anything exciting? Not particularly, just a bit of gardening, maybe pop to the shops. Your Dad’s been talking non-stop about the house extension again. He’s got a whole Pinterest board dedicated to garden design now.

Right, nearly finished. Nearly finished. Just gotta get this… okay, there we go. Pasta’s on. You hungry? Yeah, a bit. Is it just pasta again? Well, what did you want? You didn’t say anything earlier. And Leo’s already eaten most of a banana, so…    I dunno. Something… different? Like, proper dinner?  sighs  It’s pasta with tomato sauce and some bits of chicken in. It’s not exactly gruel, is it? Honestly, you’re a nightmare sometimes. I didn’t ask for gruel! Don't be ridiculous. Did you watch ‘Stick with Mick’ today? Yeah, it was alright. He went to that… farm, didn't he? With all the sheep. Good. Good for you. Keeping up with your cultural programme. Leo loves ‘Mick’. He shouts “Mick! Mick!” at the telly like he’s his best friend. Want to go swimming tomorrow? Nah. Too crowded. Not if we go early. We could be there for ten, before everyone else turns up. Ugh. Too early. Can I just… stay in and play on the Xbox? No. You need to get some fresh air. It’s the summer holidays! We need to  do  things. Your friend, Ollie, said he was going to the park with his dad. Ollie’s dad is really boring. He just makes him dig holes. He’s teaching him gardening! It’s good to learn things about nature. Speaking of which, I asked Mr. Doherty if you could maybe help him with his garden for a bit, earn a few quid. What?! No way! I’m not weeding old man Doherty’s garden all summer. That’s… slave labour. Don’t be dramatic. He said he'd pay you. It’s just a bit of tidying. Honestly, you spend too much time glued to that screen.    Careful, little man! Okay, okay. What are you saying? Do you want to help mummy make dinner? See,  someone  wants to be helpful. He’s three. He doesn't know any better. He understands more than you give him credit for. Have you been practicing your guitar? A bit. I’m trying to learn that… Japanese song. Japanese? Where did you learn about Japanese songs? On YouTube. It's…complicated. Lots of fast strumming. Right. Well, maybe after dinner you can play me a bit. And then, we’re going to make a list of things you can do this summer.

Right, so he’s just about to, isn’t he? This bit’s always good. The tension’s building… you reckon he actually gets away with it this time? Nah, never. They  always  catch ‘em at the last minute. It's a bit predictable, innit? Still a good film though, proper classic. Reminds me of when I was a kid, always wanted to be a jewel thief, proper Ocean’s Eleven vibes. Aye, everyone does. I wanted to be an archaeologist, digging up dinosaur bones. Then I realised it’s mostly just…dust. And paperwork. This is way more glamorous. Speaking of glamorous, have you seen that new Ridley Scott film? The one about Napoleon? Heard bits and bobs. Joaquin Phoenix, yeah? Is it any good? My mam was on about it, said it’s historically inaccurate. It's… a film, alright? Historically  inspired , let’s say. Phoenix is brilliant, as always, but it’s a bit of a mess. Like, they gloss over a lot of stuff. And the battle scenes are just…loud. Reminded me of that time I went to the dentist. All drilling and shouting. That’s a mental comparison! Dentist and Napoleon’s battles. You’re alright, you. Though, yeah, a dodgy dentist is pretty terrifying. I had one years ago, proper creepy bloke, kept staring at my fillings like they were aliens. Ooh, that’s rough. Mine just talks at me incessantly about the state of my teeth. Like I don't know I need to floss more? It's patronising. Right, he’s about to rappel down. See? Told ya. Right on cue. See, predictable. Still, good fun. So, are you still planning on going to that gig next week? The indie band at the O2 Academy? Yeah, definitely. Got the tickets ages ago. You still up for it? Fancy getting a pre-gig scran somewhere? I've been meaning to try that new Vietnamese place down by the docks. Oh yeah, I’m in! Vietnamese sounds class. And I’m always up for live music. Although, knowing my luck, I’ll spend the whole night trying to decipher the singer's accent. Gets right on my nerves, people mumbling. Fair enough. You, the English language teacher, being annoyed by accents. The irony. Hey! It’s different when it's deliberately obscure for artistic effect. Makes me wanna shout “Speak up, lad!” Plus, you wouldn’t believe the accents I’ve had to deal with teaching in Liverpool.

So, how was your week? Anything exciting happen at school? Other than the usual chaos, of course. It was…busy. Honestly, prepping for Easter has been manic. We’re doing an Easter bonnet parade next week and the parents are going all out! Honestly, some of them are professional level. It’s a bit intimidating for the kids whose parents aren’t crafty, you know? Oh, bless them. It's always the way, isn’t it? Someone always tries to outdo everyone else. Did you bake any Easter cakes? I attempted one, and it looks…well, let’s just say it’s structurally unsound. I did! A simple Victoria sponge with a chocolate egg on top. Nothing fancy. The kids loved decorating them, though. It was messy, but fun. You should have seen little Leo, covered head to toe in sprinkles! Oh, that sounds lovely. I’m hopeless in the kitchen, honestly. I always end up making a mess. Speaking of kids, have you finalised details for little Alfie’s christening? Is Auntie Carol still offering to do the buffet? Yes! Everything is pretty much sorted. The church is booked for the 28th, and we’ve got the reception at The Plough. Auntie Carol’s definitely doing the buffet, and she’s threatening to make one of her enormous chocolate fountains. Oh lord. That woman and her chocolate fountains! They are… an experience. She means well, but it's a bit much sometimes. Have you sent out all the invitations? Almost. Just a few more to post off today. It's getting quite real now, isn’t it? I’m so excited, but also a little bit overwhelmed with all the planning. It always is. Don’t worry, you'll be fine. You’re such an organised person, you’ll have it all under control. How’s the new job going, by the way? Settled in okay? It’s good, really good. The school is lovely, and the kids are fantastic. It’s just… a lot more responsibility than my previous role. Year 3 is a whole different ball game to Reception. I can imagine. You're a natural with children though, you always have been. So, are you taking any time off over Easter? Any plans for a little break? We were thinking of going to Cornwall for a few days. Just a little coastal escape. Nothing too ambitious. We need a bit of a recharge after this half term.

Honestly, the Year 9s are driving me round the bend this week. Absolute chaos. They’ve decided conjugation is a personal attack. Oh, teenagers! It’s always something, isn’t it? I thought after lockdowns they’d be grateful to just  be  in school, but no. More rebellious than ever. You’d think! I’ve tried everything – games, songs, even bribery with extra credit. Nothing sticks. And the parents… don’t even get me started. Apparently, it’s  my  fault their darling little Timmy isn’t grasping subjunctive mood. Oh, the parents! That's a universal truth. Mine are starting to drive me mad, too. My son, Daniel, is suddenly decided he wants to be a… well, not a doctor, not a lawyer, but a professional gamer. Oh dear. That sounds… challenging. Challenging is an understatement. He’s convinced he can make a living streaming himself playing Fortnite. I’ve tried to explain about the instability, the competition… but it’s like talking to a brick wall. He’s spent all his Christmas money on a new graphics card! Oh, bless him. My niece, Chloe, is obsessed with makeup. It’s all contouring and highlighting. She’s practically running a beauty business from her bedroom! I tried to steer her towards, you know, books. Good luck with that! It's all TikTok and Instagram these days. Speaking of which, have you tried that new face serum everyone’s raving about? The one with the retinol? Oh, the one Fiona was going on about? I was tempted, but honestly, I just lather myself in factor 50 and hope for the best. I’m terrible with routines. I can barely remember to water my fern, let alone a seven-step skincare regime. See, that’s where I’m organised. It’s all about discipline. Though, my husband keeps saying I spend more time on my face than I do talking to him. Oh, they always say that! It’s the classic husband complaint. How’s Michael doing, anyway? Still busy with the… antique business? Still busy, yes. He’s got a lovely little collection of Victorian jewellery at the moment. He’s hoping to sell it at a fair next month. It's stressful, though. He's always worrying about authenticity. He had a scare last week with a brooch – turned out it was a very good imitation. Oh, no! Those things are always worrying, aren't they?

Right, so seriously, Auntie Sylvia, you’ve never had gefilte fish? Never? Honestly, darling, it’s just…not my thing. The texture. It’s…suspiciously smooth. Reminds me of something one wouldn’t discuss at a dinner party. Suspiciously smooth! That’s brilliant. It’s an acquired taste, definitely. Mum’s is the best, obviously. She puts a little bit of carrot in to give it colour, makes all the difference. It’s alright. I’m still on the fence, to be honest. I feel like I  should  like it, because of…well, you know. But it's just…fishy. It's a cornerstone of the Seder! A symbol! You're basically rejecting centuries of tradition, mate. Oh, don't be dramatic, Leo. I’m embracing the matzah ball soup.  That  I can get behind. It’s lovely and fluffy. Reminds me of a cloud. A savoury cloud. Speaking of clouds, has anyone booked flights for Italy yet? I was looking at flights to Rome, then maybe train up to Florence? I’ve had a look, yeah. Prices are going up, predictably. I can probably get something decent for around…£150 return, give or take. Italy sounds good. I need a proper holiday. Exams are killing me. Literally. It’s like a slow, academic death. Speaking of things that are killing me, I watched this documentary last night about Ortolan… Oh,  don’t . …you know, the little songbird they used to eat in France? Covered in salt and everything. Appalling. Absolutely appalling. Oh dear god. I’ve heard about that. Utterly barbaric. Even for a foodie like me, that’s a step too far. Sounds…intense. Did they at least season it well? Seasoning doesn't excuse…the essence of the bird! It's a metaphor for privilege and excess! Anyway. Back to happier topics. This charoset is amazing, Mum. What’s the secret? Chopped apples, dates, walnuts, and a little bit of Manischewitz wine. Don’t tell anyone, it’s a family secret. Though frankly, everyone probably already knows. It  is  rather good. Though I still prefer a nice crumble. So, Leo, how’s the Hebrew coming along? Are you at least managing to stumble through the blessings? It's…challenging. It's just so different from anything I’ve ever learned. And trying to pronounce everything correctly? Forget it. I sound like a strangled cat. You'll get there. It’s all about practice.

Right, so, who's seen the latest episode of ‘The Tourist’ then? Honestly, Jamie Dornan is just… wow. Though I did spend most of it shouting at the TV, telling him  not  to trust that woman. Oh, I haven't gotten around to that one yet. It's on the list though. I've been completely hooked on ‘Happy Valley’. Sarah Lancashire is phenomenal. A bit grim, but brilliant. I watched the first couple of episodes of ‘Happy Valley’ but I couldn't handle the intensity. I needed something a bit fluffier. I’ve actually been…knitting. You? Knitting? I didn’t know you knitted! It’s a new thing! My nan taught me over lockdown, and it's surprisingly therapeutic. I’m making a blanket for my niece’s new baby. It’s a bit wonky, but it's made with love. That’s lovely! I tried crocheting once. Ended up with something that looked like a disfigured octopus. Gave up after that. Oh, my mum loves knitting too. She’s made us all Christmas jumpers over the years. Some are… questionable. Remember the one with the reindeer that looked like a badger? Oh God, yes! And the flashing lights! Nearly blinded my Uncle George. Speaking of questionable, has anyone read that new novel everyone’s talking about, ‘The Midnight Bloom’? I’m about halfway through and… it’s slow.  Really  slow. I downloaded it onto my Kindle, but I haven’t started it yet. I’m still stuck in a historical fiction phase. Just finished a really good one about Eleanor of Aquitaine. I'm a proper book person, I have to have a physical copy. I just don’t get the appeal of eBooks. You can’t  smell  a Kindle. And there's nothing like turning the pages. I get both, honestly. eBooks are great for travelling, and I can read in the dark without disturbing anyone. But I agree, there’s something special about a real book. Plus, they look better on the shelf. Exactly! It's the aesthetic. My bookshelves are my pride and joy. Though my husband keeps threatening to get rid of some… says I have too many. Men. They just don't  understand . Have you seen that new film adaptation of ‘Little Women’? I'm thinking of going next week. Ooh, I've heard good things! I love Greta Gerwig. Have we decided on next month’s book yet?

Right, so this is the… the thing, isn’t it? Bit shiny. And cold. Feels proper Scandinavian this place, even the pub. It  is  freezing, isn't it? Proper Nordic chill. Ooh, look at the box, it’s all minimalist and… well, Finnish, I suppose. So, how easy is this supposed to be? You’ve had a play already, haven’t you? Minimal play. I managed to turn it on, and that was about the limit of my technological prowess. I’m honestly bracing myself for a two-hour battle with settings menus. Remember when Nokia ruled the world? Brick phones, nearly indestructible. You could probably build a small house with one. Oh god, yeah. And the Snake game! Hours wasted on Snake. It's ironic, isn’t it? Nokia, Finnish invention, and now we’re in Finland trying to figure out a  different  phone. Though, to be fair, Nokia isn’t what it was. No, it really isn’t. It's a sad story, really. Anyway, where’s the SIM ejection tool? Always the fussiest little thing to find. I swear they design them to deliberately get lost. It’s in the little tray underneath the…blister pack stuff, I think. Here. Honestly, the packaging alone is a crime against trees. Cheers. Right, SIM card in… oh, hold on. Is this… a different size SIM than the ones we usually get? It looks… smaller. Nan-o-SIM, I think it’s called. They keep making them smaller and smaller. Like they’re trying to make them invisible. Good luck with your fingers, by the way. You’re gonna need them. Right. Okay, that’s in. Now… what does this button do? Is this the power button? Or the… ejector seat button? Definitely not the ejector seat button. It's power. Though, honestly, some of these interfaces are so illogical. Okay, let's go through it step-by-step. Language selection first. You want English, obviously. Naturally. I’m not trying to learn Finnish phonetically through a new phone setup. That's a recipe for disaster. Okay, good. Now it's asking about data privacy… terms and conditions… all the usual legal garble. Just accept it all, we haven't got all day. Feels morally questionable, blindly accepting all that, but you're right. Time is of the essence. And besides,  everyone  does it. What’s next? Wi-Fi? Yeah, connect to the pub’s Wi-Fi.

Right, so Leo’s party. Are you still thinking superheroes? Yeah! Definitely. It’s cool. Maybe…Spider-Man? Or Batman? Mmm, those are good. We need to send out invites soon, you know. Mrs. O’Malley was asking after you at the shops, said she was wondering if Leo would be invited. Of course! He’s my best mate. I’ll make him a special one. With loads of glitter. Ga! Ga! Oh, hang on a sec, sweetheart. What’s this? A car? You like cars, don’t you? Mum, can we talk about the party again? I was thinking, maybe we could have a bouncy castle? A bouncy castle… That might be a bit much for the garden, don’t you think? It’s not exactly huge. But it would be  amazing ! We could all jump on it. Even…even Finlay. Finlay might prefer to watch from the sidelines, love. He’s still a little one. Speaking of little ones, what about birthday presents? Have you thought about what you want to get for Charlie? Oh, yeah. He loves… Red Pandas, doesn't he? He does! He’s absolutely obsessed. He told me yesterday they're his favourite animal in the whole world. Right. Maybe a Red Panda cuddly toy? Or a book about them? That’s a lovely idea. We could look online tonight. What’s  your  favourite animal then? Malamooches. Malamooches? What on earth are Malamooches? They’re like, huge fluffy dogs. From Alaska! They pull sleds and stuff. They're really strong. I saw one on a documentary. Oh, you mean Malamutes! Alaskan Malamutes. They are beautiful dogs, aren’t they? Much bigger than Poppy. Yeah! Poppy’s good though. Even if she sheds everywhere. Poppy! He loves Poppy too. He’s always trying to pull her tail. Not allowed, of course. Anyway, back to the party. We need to decide on food. Sandwiches? Pizza? Pizza! Definitely pizza. And cake. A big Superhero cake! Okay, pizza and a superhero cake. Sounds good. I was thinking we might be able to fit in a trip to Granny’s during the school holidays. Are you excited about that? Yeah, but it’s ages away. And I don't want to miss anything here. I know, it feels like a long time. Maybe we can watch one of those Japanese films you like on the train? The one with the robot cat?

Honestly though, Christmas at Nana’s was  always  mental. Not in a bad way, just… chaotic. Chaotic is a polite word for it. It was a full-on assault on the senses. Like, three generations crammed into that tiny house, smelling of sherry and roasting Brussels sprouts. Oh, the sherry! Your grandfather, bless him, thought it was his civic duty to offer everyone a glass the moment they walked through the door. Even the children. A tiny splash, of course. And the arguing! Always the arguing. Not proper fights, mind you, just… spirited debates about absolutely everything. Politics, the weather, whether gravy should be lumpy or smooth. The gravy debates were  intense . I remember once, Uncle Barry nearly stormed out because someone said lumpy gravy was superior. Barry? Seriously? He’s the most laid-back person I know now. Oh, he was a different man back then. Much more… fiery. Your Nana brought that out in him, I think. She had a way of provoking people with the most innocent-sounding questions. It was a very… English Christmas, wasn’t it? All that tradition and formality. Completely different from how things are done elsewhere, I imagine. Completely. I was talking to a girl at uni from Nigeria the other day, and she was telling me how Christmas is this massive street parade, music everywhere, everyone dresses up… It sounded incredible. It’s amazing how different things can be. My mum’s side of the family, they're Filipino, and their Christmas starts  way  earlier. Like, September earlier. And the food... oh my god, the food. Lechon, bibingka, puto bumbong… forget turkey and stuffing. Lechon? What’s that? It's a whole roasted pig. Seriously. They turn it on a spit for hours. It’s amazing. But it's a lot of work, and my aunt always ends up stressed out about it. Sounds a bit much for me, to be honest. I prefer a simple Christmas dinner. Though, I do remember one Christmas in Devon, we stayed at this little pub, and they did the most incredible seafood platter. That was a bit different. Devon? You’ve been to Devon? Oh, yes. Many times. Used to go down there every summer as a boy. Beautiful countryside. Though, the accents… took me a while to get used to them. The accents are wild. It's like they speak a different language down there.

Honestly though, I’m completely hooked on ‘Happy Valley’. Have you started it? No, not yet. It's on the list, honestly. So many things on the list. We were watching that Nordic Noir one, the one… oh, what was it called? With the sheep farmer? ‘Trapped’? Yeah, ‘Trapped’! That was good, really twisty. Though a bit bleak, wasn’t it? All that ice and snow. Bleak is good! That’s what I like. ‘Happy Valley’ is just…Sarah Lancashire is phenomenal. And the storyline. It's just gritty and real. I've heard. I'm waiting for a quiet week to start it, something where I can really focus. I hate it when I start something good and then have to pause it for days. Exactly! It ruins the momentum. Speaking of needing focus, how is work going, David? Still drowning in spreadsheets? You have no idea. It’s been manic. They’re implementing a new system, and it’s a disaster. Apparently, it will ‘streamline processes’. It’s just created chaos. Oh, the bane of all office life. New systems. Always a nightmare. Tell me about it. I had a new transcription client this week, and their audio quality is atrocious. I’m spending half my time deciphering what they’re even saying! And they want it all turned around in 24 hours. The joys of freelancing, eh? You get the volume, but no support. It pays the bills, though. Are you making any progress with the new novel, Eleanor? Slowly, very slowly. I’ve got the basic outline, and I’ve done a bit of character work, but actually sitting down and  writing … that's the hard part. Life keeps getting in the way. Life always does. Are you still meeting up with the book club, Eleanor? Yes, next Tuesday. We’re discussing that new Kate Atkinson. Apparently, it’s brilliant. I’ve downloaded it onto my Kindle, but haven’t started it yet. Kindles are the best, aren't they? I love being able to carry a whole library around with me. Though sometimes I miss the smell of real books. I’m more of a physical book person myself. I like the feel of the pages. And the sight of a full bookshelf. It’s different experiences, isn’t it? Both good. We should all go out for dinner soon. It feels like ages since we’ve properly caught up.

Right well I’ve been thinking about this boiler business, you know. Oh dear. Not again, Arthur. What's the trouble now? Well, young Derek came round didn’t he, from British Gas. Lovely lad, Derek. But he said it’s getting on a bit, needs a service, could pack up any time, all that sort of thing. He's just trying to sell you a new one, Arthur. They always say that. It’s their job. No, no, he seemed a genuine lad. Said it was getting a bit… temperamental. And the cost of a new one, John, it’s frightening. Absolutely frightening. It is a lot of money, but you can't go on forever with an old boiler. Remember last winter? We were freezing half the time. That was just a bit of a cold snap, Mary. Nothing a thicker jumper couldn't sort. And a hot water bottle. Don't underestimate the hot water bottle. Arthur, you were complaining about the damp then. A faulty boiler can cause damp, you know. Damp? A bit of condensation, more like. And it’s a very old house, John. Old houses have damp. It’s part of their charm. Charm doesn’t keep the grandchildren warm when they come to visit, Arthur. They complained. Remember little Emily said she could see her breath in the living room? Emily exaggerates. She always has. She’s a dramatic child. It's a trait she gets from her mother. Oh, don't start on that now. Look, why don’t you get a couple more quotes? Just to see what you’re looking at. Then you can make an informed decision. Don't commit to anything straight away. I suppose. But all that hassle. Phone calls, people coming round, trying to baffle you with technical terms… it’s exhausting. I can help with the phone calls, Arthur. I’m quite good at dealing with those salesmen. Firm but polite. You are, aren’t you? You've always been good at that. Right, I’ll get on the phone tomorrow then. But I have a feeling it’s going to be a very expensive feeling. Don’t worry too much about it just yet. We’ll sort it out. We always do. And remember, a reliable boiler is worth the investment for peace of mind. Especially with the winter coming. Peace of mind… yes.

Right, so, Friday. Is everyone still good for Friday? Seven-thirty at The Eagle? It's the only place I could actually book for a group our size on relatively short notice, sadly. Seven-thirty’s brilliant, yeah. Sorted for me. Though, fair warning, I’ll probably be talking about my nan the entire evening. She's convinced she saw Paul McCartney in Tesco. Oh, bless her! That’s amazing. I'm in. Though I might need rescuing from a lengthy discussion about the merits of different types of biscuit with Sarah. Last time it went on for a full twenty minutes. Biscuits are  serious  business, Lindsay. Don't underestimate the debate. I'm good for Friday, though. Seven-thirty works perfectly. I’ve already mentally prepared a list of embarrassing anecdotes about fieldwork. Sorry, just finishing up a call. Friday sounds great! The Eagle? Oh, good choice. It’s… charmingly Cambridge. I’ll be there. I promise to  try  not to dominate the conversation with stories about my eccentric aunt in Montana. Excellent! Okay, so The Eagle, seven-thirty. Should we maybe do a little whip-round for a deposit or something? Just to be safe? Yeah, good shout. I can collect the cash on Friday. Unless someone prefers to bank transfer? I’m happy either way. Happy to just give you cash, Claire. It’s simpler. Speaking of simpler… look! Oh, the poor thing! It’s trying so hard. It’s a tiny hawk-moth, I think. They’re nocturnal, so it's probably got completely disoriented by the lights. Oh, those are beautiful moths. We get them in Pennsylvania too, though they're a bit bigger. Right, operation rescue moth is now in effect. Anyone got a piece of paper? I’ve got a notepad and pen. Here. Good work, Amy! Hero of the hour. It felt good. It really did. Like, I saved a life. A tiny, fuzzy, winged life. You are a saint. Okay, back to party planning. Should we think about a theme? No pressure, but… A theme? Oh goodness. That sounds… ambitious. How about just ‘celebrating the end of Horace’? It’s a pretty strong theme in itself, given how much of our lives he’s consumed these last few months. Yes! Absolutely. "Horace Freedom Day." That’s perfect. I’m on board with that. Though I might come dressed as a corpus. Just to be topical.

Ugh, history was  brutal  today. Mr. Davies decided to spring a quiz on us. A quiz! On the Tudors! No way! Seriously? He said he wasn’t going to do any more quizzes this term. I know, right? Total backstab. And it wasn't even like, normal quiz questions. It was all, like, "Explain the socio-economic impact of Henry VIII’s dissolution of the monasteries on the peasantry." Like, who  knows  that off the top of their head? Oh my god, that sounds awful. I actually kinda… enjoyed history today. We started looking at the suffragettes. Oh, nice! That's way more interesting than Henry and all his wives. Did you learn about Emmeline Pankhurst? Yeah! She was amazing. So brave, even though what they did was… well, a bit extreme sometimes. Like throwing things and setting things on fire. I know, but desperate times, right? They weren’t getting anywhere just politely asking. It's just… Mr. Davies makes everything boring. He just reads from the textbook, monotone. Yeah, some teachers are just… like that. Mrs. Peterson in English is amazing though. She actually makes Shakespeare understandable. True! She’s the best. Did you finish the Romeo and Juliet essay? I'm still stuck on the intro. I keep rewriting it. Almost. I finished it this morning, actually. I argued that Romeo was actually really immature and that's why everything went wrong. Ooh, good point! I was thinking of going for the whole ‘fate’ argument, but yours sounds way more interesting. Maybe I should change mine… You totally should! It’s way easier to write when you actually believe what you're saying. Speaking of essays, did you hear old Mrs. Higgins assigned a ten-pager on the causes of World War One?  What?!  Ten pages?! She’s insane! That's practically a novella! I know, right? Everyone's freaking out. Apparently, she said it's to 'prepare us for university.' Like, seriously? We're fifteen! Ugh. School is just… the worst sometimes. Maybe if we just run away and join the circus… That’s a good plan. I could be a trapeze artist. And you could… train the lions? Definitely not the lions! Too scary. Maybe I could be the one who throws the glitter. That's a respectable circus job. Okay, glitter thrower it is! But first, we have to survive Mrs. Higgins’ essay. Don't remind me…I'm starting to panic again.

Honestly, this lasagne is lovely. Proper comfort food, this is. Though a bit too much cheese for my liking, mind you. It is nice, isn't it? I was starving. Work was absolutely chaotic today. Old Mr. Henderson decided  today  was the day he needed twenty different spreadsheets altering, and all at once. Sounds about right for Henderson. He's a nightmare. How's the new intern settling in? Still asking basic questions every five minutes? Worse! She asked me how to save a document yesterday. Save! A document! I nearly choked on my tea. I tried being nice, showed her, but then she asked how to open it… Oh, bless her. She’ll get there. Remember when your dad first got a computer? Took him a week to figure out how to send an email. Spent the entire time thinking he was shouting at people. Oh, I remember! He’d just type everything in capital letters. Thought it made it sound more important. It’s just frustrating when you're already swamped. And on top of that, Sarah’s been moaning all week about her mum being ill. It’s awful for her, of course, but it’s endless complaining. It’s draining. Family stuff always is, love. Always. My sister’s been having trouble with her grandson. Apparently, he’s refusing to eat anything but beige food. Beige! Can you believe that? Beige food? What, like…potatoes and biscuits? Pretty much! She’s at her wit’s end. Says he won’t touch a vegetable. I told her, “Just hide them in something!” Blend ‘em up, mix ‘em with mashed potato. He’ll never know. Good plan. Maybe Sarah should try hiding some positivity in her complaints for a change. Speaking of family, are we still on for Grandma’s birthday next weekend? I promised I’d help set up the garden. Yes, definitely. I’ve already booked a table at that Italian place she likes. Remember, the one with the ridiculously oversized portions? Oh, excellent. She loves that place. She'll want the tiramisu, mind. She always does. And tell your Uncle Barry to stay away from the wine. Last time, he started singing opera. Oh dear. That sounds… eventful. It was. Very eventful. I'm already dreading it, to be honest. But it’s Grandma, so you can't really say no, can you? Absolutely not. Family is family.

So, how was your week? Honestly, it feels like it’s flown by. And how’s young Thomas doing? Still causing mayhem at school? Oh, don’t even start me on Thomas! He had detention  again  on Tuesday. Something about… well, honestly, it was a bit vague. Just ‘disruptive behaviour’. I swear, that boy has a limitless supply of energy. I don't know where he gets it from. He was moaning something awful about it, said everyone else was being worse, but of course, they never see  that  side of it. Boys will be boys, I suppose. But detention already? He’s only fourteen, isn’t he? It feels a bit early for that level of… rebellion. Tell me about it. His dad’s losing his patience. He keeps saying he needs a firm hand, but I just think he needs to be understood a bit better. He’s been really down since Sarah moved away. You remember Sarah, from down the road? Oh, yes, the lovely girl who was always drawing. That's a shame. It's hard when friends move. Does he ever go and visit? She moved all the way to Norwich. It’s a bit far for regular visits, unfortunately. He FaceTimes her, but it’s not the same, is it? Anyway, that’s enough about Thomas, he's a whole saga on his own. How are things with you? Still completely swamped with work? You have no idea! It’s been manic. We’re trying to close this big deal with a company in Manchester, and the politics are… intense. Honestly, sometimes I think I should just take early retirement. Although, then what would I  do  with myself? You'd be bored within a week, knowing you! You need the challenge. Though, seriously, you need to look after yourself. You were looking a bit pale last time I saw you. Are you eating properly? I try. It’s just… hard to switch off. I keep worrying about things. It’s stupid, I know. Actually, speaking of worrying… I had a phone call from my Auntie Maureen last week. Oh dear. Not good, is it? No. She’s been diagnosed with cancer. Lung cancer. She’s starting chemo next week. It’s just… awful. Oh, no, that's terrible news. I'm so sorry to hear that. Maureen is such a lovely woman. She is. I’m trying to be strong for my mum, but it’s hitting her really hard, naturally.

Honestly, last night was  mental . Proper rammed. You wouldn’t believe the amount of students trying to pre-drink in there before heading to the clubs. Oh god, sounds chaotic. Was it a busy student night or something? I’m glad I’m just stuck with essays at the moment, sounds way more stressful than trying to understand post-structuralism. It's always busy on a Thursday, but it was particularly bad. And honestly, the mess people leave… I spent half an hour just clearing sticky rings off the bar. Honestly, you'd think people had never seen a coaster before. Ugh, that's the worst. People are just… inherently messy. I worked a summer job at a garden centre a couple of years ago, and the state some people left the potting benches in was horrific. Like, actual soil  everywhere . Oh, that sounds grim. At least a bit of spillage at the bar is mostly just…liquid. Though sticky liquid is a nightmare. Did you get decent tips at the garden centre though? I mean, bartending  can  be good for that. Not really, no. Mostly just grumpy people complaining about the price of petunias. It wasn’t exactly a lucrative summer. How’s the tip situation at your place? Enough to, you know, actually survive on a postgrad loan? Sometimes. Weekends are good, student nights…sort of. Depends how generous everyone is. I'm mostly relying on the loan, and a bit of help from Mum and Dad, if I’m honest. Trying to save up for a proper holiday next summer, though. Somewhere  not  in the UK. Yeah, I get that. I’m hoping to do some temping over the summer to boost my funds a bit. Thinking maybe something admin-y, just to get a bit of experience on my CV. It’s terrifying thinking about actually having to get a proper job after uni, though. Tell me about it. I'm starting to panic a bit. Everyone keeps going on about “transferable skills,” but what even  are  transferable skills from pulling pints? “Excellent customer service”? “Ability to withstand loud music”? Exactly! “Proficient in crisis management during spillage-related incidents”? You could put that on your LinkedIn. Maybe I will! Honestly, it’s good to vent, you know? Keeps me from quitting on the spot every time someone asks for a complicated cocktail. Definitely. Sometimes you just need to complain to someone who understands.

Right, honestly, I need a holiday. I’m dreaming of beaches already. Tell me about it! This term's been relentless. Everyone cramming before deadlines, the noise… I swear I aged five years in September. Where are you thinking of going, then? Somewhere exotic? Exotic? Oh, you’d kill for a quiet week in County Clare, I’m telling you. Fresh air, the cliffs, a good book… bliss. Though, last time I went, my cousin Maureen tried to teach me how to play the bodhrán. Nearly drove me to madness it did. A bodhrán, eh? Sounds…intense. I’m hoping for a bit of culture, myself. Florence, maybe. All that art, the food… I’ve been trying to learn a few phrases in Italian, but it’s a disaster. I keep accidentally asking for a herd of elephants. A herd of elephants?! How? It’s a long story involving a mispronounced vowel and a very confused online translator. Let’s just say “un’elefante” and “un’erba” are dangerously close when you’re a Londoner trying to sound Italian. Oh, that’s brilliant! I once tried to order a coffee in Spain and ended up requesting a small horse. You’re all terrible! Though, to be fair, Irish and Italian do sound a bit alike to the untrained ear. It's all that rolling of the 'R's, isn’t it? I’m thinking something a bit less…linguistically challenging. Maybe Portugal. Nice weather, not  too  expensive. My girlfriend's been wanting to go for ages. She keeps showing me pictures of the Algarve. Oh, the Algarve's lovely. We went a few years ago. The beaches are gorgeous, and the seafood is amazing. Just watch out for the timeshare touts. They’re relentless. Timeshare touts. The bane of every holiday. It's like they've got a sixth sense for stressed-out tourists. Aye, it’s the same wherever you go. They could spot a naive soul a mile off. I remember being in Lanzarote once, and this fella tried to convince me I needed a holiday home… in the middle of a volcano! Honestly? In a volcano?! He said it had “geothermal heating”! Honestly, the cheek of him. I nearly offered him a piece of my mind, but then I thought, “No, get me a pint of lager instead.” That’s always the better option. Definitely the better option. Speaking of options, has anyone booked their flights yet?

Honestly, that was a terrible call by the referee. Absolutely dreadful. Aye, a bit harsh, wasn't it? Looked like a clean tackle to me. He’s always been a bit… biased, that one. Biased? He’s actively ruining the game! They were building momentum, properly stringing passes together, and then  that . A perfectly good goal! Well, it’s football, innit? You get those decisions. Part of the fun, almost. Though, admittedly, less fun when it's  your  team getting shafted. Fun? It's infuriating! I swear, I spend half my weekend yelling at the television. And all I get for it is a headache and increased blood pressure. Sounds about right. Need a distraction, then? I was thinking of ordering a takeaway. Fancy some fried chicken? There's that place on Mill Road that does a decent one. Ooh, now you're talking. Fried chicken would definitely improve this situation. Though, I'm not convinced anything can truly mend the injustice we’ve just witnessed. What sides are they doing? They do proper chips, like proper chunky ones. And coleslaw. Maybe even those little… what are they called… hash browns? Hash browns, yes! Essential. And garlic mayo. Don’t forget the garlic mayo. It’s the law. Garlic mayo is non-negotiable. Okay, ordering now. They reckon about forty minutes, so we can get thoroughly enraged at the football for a bit longer. Forty minutes? That’s an eternity. Honestly, this game is going to give me an ulcer. And are you sure about fried chicken? I was kinda craving a burger, to be honest. A burger? After you just said fried chicken would improve things? You're a fickle woman, you are. I am allowed to change my mind! It's a free country. Though, maybe a combo? A burger  and  some fried chicken? Is that too much? You’re ambitious, I'll give you that. Alright, alright. I'll check if they do a combo. But if it takes an extra twenty minutes because of your indecision, you're doing the washing up for a week. Deal. Now, focus on getting that food ordered and less on my perfectly reasonable desire for both burgers and fried chicken. And maybe yell at the referee with me? It feels better in company. Fine, fine. He  is  a complete donkeys ears, isn’t he? Right, let me add a burger to the order... and prepare for a lot of shouting.

Right, so the meeting went… okay. Honestly, it felt like talking to a brick wall half the time. Old Mr. Henderson just kept going on about deadlines like they’re set in stone. Men. Always deadlines. Your grandfather was the same. Wouldn’t budge an inch, even if the sky was falling. He was stubborn, your grandad. But a good man. Did you see that new film, the one with… what’s-his-name? The one we were talking about? You mean ‘Dune’? Yeah, I went last week. It was… visually stunning, definitely. A bit slow though, wasn’t it? All atmosphere and not enough, you know,  happening . Oh, I saw that years ago, the first one. With that lovely young man, what was his name? Can’t recall it now. Much preferred the old black and white ones, myself. Proper stories they were. David Lynch directed it, Grandma. That’s why it’s a bit… strange. And the new one is part two. Oh, a sequel! Well, they do churn them out, don’t they? Speaking of churning things out, I tried that new recipe for shepherd’s pie, the one you sent me. It was a disaster! Oh no! What went wrong? I used lamb mince instead of beef, thought it would be nice. It wasn’t nice. It was… gamey. And I put too much Worcester sauce in. Your grandfather would have had a fit. He liked a simple shepherd’s pie. It's always the little things, isn't it? Like when I tried making a Victoria sponge and forgot the baking powder. Flattened as a pancake! Sounds about right. I was thinking of getting a new car, actually. The old one’s starting to make some worrying noises. Oh, a new car! Splashing out, are we? You don't need a fancy one, just something reliable. Remember when your father first got a car? A little Austin Seven. We thought we were the bees knees! It was bright green, wasn’t it? And always breaking down. Your father spent half his life under the bonnet of that car. I’ve heard stories. I’m thinking of an electric one, actually. Trying to be a bit more… responsible. Electric? What will they think of next! I still swear by a good petrol engine. More reliable, I reckon. Although, I suppose it's good to think about the environment.

Right, nobody is leaving this table until you’ve both eaten at least  some  of your pancakes. Honestly, Leo, you’ve barely touched yours! And Freya, you’ve had one bite and are now rearranging the sprinkles. But Mummy, I don’t  like  sprinkles. They’re too… sparkly. Mine’s too hot. It’s burning my tongue. It’s not that hot, Leo. I tested it. And Freya, you liked sprinkles yesterday. Honestly, you two. It's Pancake Day! You’re supposed to enjoy it. It breaks my heart knowing some children don't even  have  pancakes, or anything much to eat, full stop. Mrs. Davies was telling me today about a little boy in my class… Is he sad? Sometimes, yes. It’s hard when you’re hungry. That’s why we should all appreciate what we have, and try to eat at least a little bit of our pancakes, okay? Okay.  takes a tiny bite  Still hot. It's cooling! Speaking of school, Freya, how was assembly today? Was it the Year Sixes doing their presentation? Yeah! They did it on space. It was really good. Emily fell over though, during the Saturn bit. Oh dear! Was she alright? Yeah, Miss Jones helped her up. She was a bit embarrassed, but it was funny. I want to go to the Science Museum. Can we go, Mummy? Please? We talked about that, didn't we? Maybe next weekend. We’re going to Grandma and Grandpa’s this weekend, remember? Though we could check what’s on at the Festival Hall… they sometimes have family things. I want to go to Paris! Paris is a  long  way away, sweetie. We’ll see. Now, before we talk about any more exciting places, have you both brushed your teeth properly this morning? Yes! I even did two minutes! I brushed and brushed and brushed! Excellent! That’s my good boys and girl. You know, when  I  was little, growing up in Dartford, we didn't go on fancy holidays like Paris. We used to go to the beach at Southend. Building sandcastles was the highlight of my year. Actually, it was pretty magical. Have you ever read ‘Green Knowe’ by Lucy Boston? No. Oh, you should. It's about a little boy who goes to stay with his great aunt and discovers the house is full of the ghosts of children from the past.

This is actually really good. Better than I remember. Told ya. Best Chinese in town, hands down. Though I still maintain Old Man Lee's used to be better…before he retired. Oh, Old Man Lee's was  the  place. Remember when we were kids and we’d sneak in there after school? And he’d always give us extra prawn crackers, even though Mum would kill us for having them. Good times. Speaking of Mum…did anyone hear back about Auntie Carol’s funeral arrangements? Yeah, Mum sent a WhatsApp. It’s next Friday, two o’clock. She wants us all there obviously. Bit grim, isn’t it? Grim is an understatement. She was…a character. Always had a story, even if half of it was made up. Absolutely. Remember that time she claimed she’d met Mick Jagger? And she had a grainy photo as “proof.” It was clearly a cardboard cutout. Classic Carol. Still, it’ll be nice to see everyone. Haven't seen cousin Dave in ages. He's still living up in Manchester, right? Yeah, last I heard he was still battling with his housemates. Apparently, one of them leaves dirty dishes in the sink for  weeks . Oh, the horror! That’s a dealbreaker. Reminds me of living with Ben in uni. He thought the washing up fairy was real. Haha, classic Ben. Always living in his own little world. Did you see that thing on the news about… what was it? The rising cost of… everything? Yeah, depressing stuff. At this rate, we’ll all be living in cardboard boxes. Speaking of which, remember when Leo was obsessed with Bob the Builder? Oh my god, yes! He’d run around with a little hard hat and shout "Can we fix it?" at everything. He even tried to ‘fix’ the garden fence with sticky tape. Kids are brilliant. Hey, are any of you free to watch the cricket on Saturday? England are playing Australia. Could be a good game. I might be up for that. Depending on how much gardening Mum ropes me into. I’m in, definitely. Need a bit of sport in my life. Been stuck writing bids all week. It's soul destroying. I'm free too. Though I wouldn't pretend to understand the intricacies of cricket. Mostly just enjoy the atmosphere and the snacks. Perfect! We can order pizza, make a day of it.

Honestly, Old Man Hemmings next door to Mum… he used to sunbathe in his garden wearing  nothing  but a pair of Wellington boots. Honestly! Mum was horrified, apparently, she’d draw the curtains religiously. Wellington boots, you say? Goodness me. People were different then, weren't they? Less…concerned with appearances. I remember old Mrs. Pritchard down the road in Wolverhampton. Always had a parrot on her shoulder when she went to the shops. A bright blue thing, squawking away. Caused absolute chaos in Woolworths, it did. Oh, that’s brilliant! It’s the sort of thing you only read about now. Remember Auntie Mabel's obsession with rice krispy cakes? She’d eat a whole packet in one sitting, then complain she couldn't do up her shoes. Oh, God, yes. And she’d always offer you one, even  after  you’d politely declined ten times. It was a compulsion. She said they were ‘good for your tummy’. My sister Beatrice, now she had a peculiar habit. She collected thimbles. Hundreds of them! Filled drawers and drawers. Said each one had a story. I never understood it. She’d spend hours polishing them. Never understood where she got the time, always busy with the children. It’s funny the things people latch onto, isn’t it? I’ve got a weird thing about scan-as-you-go at the supermarket. I actively avoid the self-checkouts. I feel like I'm being accused of theft every time I use one. I get that. It's so impersonal. And it  always  needs assistance. Remember when we went to that new build estate near Plymouth, looking at houses? The insurance was ridiculous because of ‘potential flooding’ even though it was on a slight hill! The whole thing was overpriced, anyway. And that tiny garden! I wouldn’t pay half what they were asking. Much happier with the slightly wonky fences and overgrown roses here. At least you feel like you're actually  in  a garden, not a postage stamp. Gardens are important. My father, he was a keen gardener. Grew the most magnificent tomatoes. Said the secret was talking to them. I always thought he was a bit mad, but they  were  lovely tomatoes. He wouldn’t have trusted those driverless cars either, you know. Absolutely not. Said his driving was perfectly safe, thank you very much. He probably was a very good driver, actually.

Right, so this is the year of the dragon, apparently. Did you guys know that? Dragons are  amazing ! I drew one at school! It had, like, a million scales! Mine had fire! Proper big flames coming out of its mouth. It was the best dragon ever. Oh, fantastic! I’m glad you both enjoyed the drawing activity. We need to do more of those. It’s good to be creative. Did you learn anything else about Chinese New Year? Miss Davies said it’s really lucky! And everything is red! That’s right! Red symbolises good fortune and happiness. That’s why we're having noodles and spring rolls tonight – they're proper Chinese food! Though, I admit, I'm mostly making it because  someone  requested sweet and sour chicken. It’s my favourite! Can we have extra prawns? We’ll see. Let’s focus on being good first. Speaking of good, how was school today? Anything exciting happen? We learned about planets! Saturn has rings made of ice! Isn't that cool? That  is  cool! Which planet is your favourite? I like Jupiter! It’s the biggest! And it has a giant red spot. It looks like a big eye. That’s a good observation! You’re both little scientists. Now, remember we talked about practicing your instruments? How’s the piano going, Lily? I learned a new song! It’s a really fast one, but I keep messing up the bit in the middle. That’s okay, practice makes perfect! And you, Leo? Any progress with the drums? Are you still trying to be a rock star? Yes! I can do a really loud roll now! It makes the windows shake. Oh dear. Maybe not  too  loud a roll. We don’t want to upset the neighbours. Actually, did you remember to book Leo’s aerial hoop class for next week? Oh! I forgot! Right, I'll do it now. It’s getting so popular, they fill up quickly. It’s good you’re both trying different things. Keeps things interesting, doesn't it? Oh! Before I forget, did you guys watch Barbie and the Great Adventure on Saturday? It was good! Barbie found a secret kingdom! And she had a pet unicorn! It was  sparkly ! Ah, wonderful! Glad you enjoyed it. Now, who wants to help me chop the spring onions? It’s almost time for our Chinese feast!

Honestly, this is…perfect. I needed this. London was just relentless for a bit there. Rain, deadlines, the general vibe… Tell me about it! Though, I’m starting to miss the rain a little. This heat is…intense. I feel like I’m melting into my Aperol Spritz. You two city folk. You complain about everything! It’s Rome, it’s  warm . Embrace it! Though, yeah, it’s a bit much even for me. Still, beats Birmingham weather any day. Mate, you’re all soft. This is nothing. Try a summer in the Outback. You’ll be begging for a bit of drizzle, I tell ya. Easy for you to say, you’re practically built for heat! Seriously though, this AirBnB was a steal. Right near the Pantheon, can’t beat the location. It  is  lovely. Though, the host did warn us about the noise from the street. We’ll see how restful it actually is tonight. Noise is part of the Rome experience, isn’t it? Just soak it up! So, dinner plans? I’m starving. I saw a little trattoria down the street that looked amazing. Family-run, proper Italian. Sounds good to me. I’m up for anything, as long as there’s pasta involved. Honestly, I’ve already eaten my weight in carbs since we landed. I’m in! I’ve been trying to brush up on my Italian, mostly just sticking to “Grazie” and “Prego” so far. It’s harder than it looks. You’re doing better than me. I just point and smile a lot. It’s surprisingly effective. My Italian sounds like a strangled cat. It’s the accent, love. No one will understand you! Although, honestly, most people here speak English anyway. Yeah, and the ones who don’t are just happy you’re  trying . Makes a big difference. Speaking of accents, I had a bloke try to tell me this morning I was actually American. Said I sounded like someone from California. No way! You've got the strongest Aussie accent I’ve ever heard. Tell that to the bloke! It’s the sun, I reckon. It messes with people’s ears. Maybe. Though, I've noticed I'm starting to pick up little bits of Italian just from listening to people. It's like osmosis. It does happen. My Nonna, she lives just outside Venice. I spent summers with her as a kid and even now, bits and pieces just come back to me.

Honestly, the planning for Chloe’s hen do is stressing me out. It’s just…a lot. Tell me about it! Everyone has such strong opinions. I just want it to be fun for her, you know? Not a Pinterest-perfect disaster. Exactly! My cousin’s hen do last year was  intense . There were itineraries, colour schemes, choreographed dances… I nearly died of second-hand embarrassment. Oh god, choreographed dances are my nightmare. Chloe would hate that. She’s more of a relaxed pub quiz and cocktails kind of girl. That’s what I keep saying! But then her mum is suggesting a spa day, and her aunt wants a fancy dress theme, and… it’s endless. I’m trying to steer it towards something manageable, like maybe a crafting afternoon?
