Ooh, a crafting afternoon! That’s a good shout! We could do flower crown making, or macramé… Or even decorate cupcakes! Cupcake decorating sounds fun! I’m surprisingly good at icing, if I do say so myself. I made a three-tiered cake for my nephew’s birthday. It was…a learning experience. A learning experience? That sounds ominous. Hopefully it didn’t end in a kitchen covered in frosting. Let’s just say there was a  significant  amount of leftover icing. And a very sticky floor. Okay, maybe stick to individual cupcakes then. But the crafting idea’s good! We could do everything at Rosie and Ali Bonds, right? Plenty of space. Definitely! They do amazing coffee and cake there anyway. And it’s pretty central for everyone. Perfect! I can take on sourcing the craft supplies. I’ve got a friend who owns a craft shop, I’m sure I can get a discount. Oh, you are a lifesaver! That would be amazing. Okay, crafting at Rosie and Ali Bonds…that feels much more Chloe. Have you guys heard from Sarah lately? She was meant to be sending me a list of people who are definitely coming. I think she was baking a cake yesterday, so she was probably covered in flour and ignoring her phone. That’s Sarah. Classic Sarah. She gets so absorbed in baking. It’s adorable. Though I did hear she tried to make macarons and they completely collapsed. Oh no! Macarons are the ultimate baking challenge. I tried once. It was a disaster. They looked like sad little pancakes. Okay, we'll circle back with Sarah later.

Right, so you reckon this much chilli is good for a curry for four? Seems a lot, doesn't it? Nah, it's fine. You were a bit stingy last time, remember? Mum complained it wasn't spicy enough. And she  loves  spice. She just likes to complain, that's her hobby. Honestly, I thought I put loads in. Still, better too much than not enough, I suppose. Are you sure we’ve got enough rice? I feel like we always run out. Yeah, there's a big bag in the cupboard. I checked. You worry too much, you know? It's just rice. Speaking of running out of things, I think I’m coming down with something. Oh no, what’s up? You sound a bit croaky. Yeah, my throat’s killing me. And I've got a headache, and I feel all achy. I was hoping to get a decent night's sleep before teaching tomorrow, but it doesn't look like it. Blast. That’s awful. You need to look after yourself. Maybe take some Lemsip? You were saying you were thinking about going to Berlin next month, right? Is that still on? It is, but if I’m still feeling rough then… I don’t know. I've already booked the flights, though. And the hotel. It’s a weird little place, apparently, like a converted warehouse. Oh yeah? Sounds cool. Better than another chain hotel, eh? I stayed in one in Manchester last week, absolutely soulless. Little plastic everything, all beige. Beige is the enemy. That’s a good motto. This place in Berlin has exposed brick and everything. Apparently, it's right near a really good market. I’m hoping to try some proper German sausages. Now you’re talking! You need to fuel up for all that sightseeing. You’ll be walking miles. You and your need to “experience the culture”. Hey! It’s important! Plus, I need to practice my German. Although, I’m pretty sure I’ll just end up pointing and smiling. Speaking of fueling up, are you chopping those onions or just staring at them? Chopping! Chopping! Just… contemplating their spherical perfection. They’re making my eyes water, though. It's a conspiracy, I tell you. Onions are trying to defeat humanity. Dramatic much? Just wear your glasses. And maybe a gas mask. Seriously though, how did you get on with that presentation you were doing for work?

Right, shopping list. Milk, definitely. And eggs. How many eggs do you think? A dozen? A dozen's good. We'll use them for the quiche, won't we? And I fancy a victoria sponge. Oh, and apples. Braeburn, if they have them. Braeburn it is. Anything else immediately springing to mind? Oh! Biscuit tin's looking rather empty. Digestives? Yes, digestives. And those nice ginger snaps. You know, the ones that crumble everywhere? The ones that get into the carpet for weeks! Yes, I know them well. Speaking of things that crumble… did you see Brenda’s birthday card? She put she was 65! She’s clearly lost track. She’s at least seventy, if not more. Oh, Brenda. She’s always been a bit… optimistic. Remember when she insisted she was younger than me, even though we’re twins? Goodness, yes! That was a stand-off. It’s ridiculous, isn’t it? The age on the card. It’s just a number, really. It is. Though, I did feel a bit put out when Ethel sent me one with “70 and fabulous” on. Seventy! Still feels… a lot. Oh, don't. We're getting there, aren't we? Anyway, I was thinking of getting those calendar fobs for the grandchildren. The ones with their pictures on? Oh, lovely idea. They always like those. Little Leo would adore one with his dinosaur on. Exactly! It’s a useful present, as well. They can put them on their keyrings. It reminds me, when I was volunteering at the school, they were doing such lovely art. All the glitter and paint. It was a complete mess, of course, but so creative. They used to do that at my school. Remember making those paper chains? Always ended up covered in glue. And the smell of plasticine… Oh, the plasticine! Absolutely vile smell, but we loved it. And the hockey boots! Remember being made to polish those things until you could see your face in them? Horrendous. My fingers were always aching. And the smell of the leather polish! Ugh. It’s a wonder anyone took up hockey. It truly is. Oh, I was reading about that chap, David, from university. He’s working at the computing museum now. Apparently, they're desperate for volunteers. Really? That sounds interesting. They've a huge collection, haven't they? All those early computers… Apparently, they’re getting people to help catalogue everything, and sort of… document their history.

So, Old Man Hemmings next door, apparently he’s been complaining about the lights on the shed. Says they’re too bright. Oh, really? He’s always moaning about something, isn’t he? Honestly, a bit of light isn’t hurting anyone. Especially not in December. You'd think, wouldn't you? It’s not like you've installed a landing strip! Though knowing him, he’d probably complain about that too, if it brought more traffic. Did he actually  speak  to you, or just to…well, anyone who’d listen? Spoke to Margaret, apparently. She told Brenda, who told me. So it’s gone the full Holsworthy rumour mill route. Said he couldn't sleep. Dramatic, really. Men. Honestly. What did you say when you heard? I just laughed. Margaret said I should probably just dim them a bit to keep the peace. Which I’ll probably do, rather than a full-blown feud with the most miserable man in Devon. Still, seems a bit much. It does. Especially considering his garden looks like a jungle. You could lose a small child in there. A little shed light isn’t exactly a hazard. Speaking of gardens, have you had a chance to have a proper look around yours yet? Is it…overgrown, like everyone says? Overgrown is an understatement. It’s been…neglected. The previous owners clearly weren’t gardeners. It’s mostly brambles and weeds at the moment, but there are some lovely old apple trees. And a surprisingly productive rhubarb patch. Oh, rhubarb! Wonderful. You’ll have to make crumble, won’t you? Definitely. Though I’ll need a machete to get to it first. Seriously, I spent an hour just clearing a patch so I could see where the fence actually  was . You’ll get there. It's a project. You and I can do a gardening day together, you know. I'm fairly good at weeding. Though I wouldn't say I'm a gardener, exactly. More of a…weed assassin. That would be fantastic, actually. I’m not sure I’m up to tackling it all on my own. It feels a bit daunting. It needs a proper plan. Have you met the lady from number seven yet? The one with the roses? They’re absolutely stunning. She’s a proper gardening guru, apparently. No, not yet. But I’ve seen her out and about.

Right, so I’ve been looking at getting a new graphics card, yeah? For the PC. Oh aye? Which one? Don't tell me you're finally upgrading from that… fossil you’ve got. Harsh, but fair. It’s seen better days. I was thinking the RTX 4070. Saw a review online, seems decent. And it’s only… well, only £550.  Only  £550? You’re mental. You’ve been skint for weeks, moaning about not being able to afford a takeaway. I’m prioritising! A takeaway is temporary satisfaction. A graphics card is… investment in my future! Potential stream content! Potential stream content that nobody will watch because you'll be too busy complaining about lag on a £550 graphics card. You’re a real ray of sunshine, you know that? Anyway, I found this website, ‘TechDealsUK’ or something. They’ve got it on offer, but the reviews are…mixed. Lots of complaints about delivery times. Of course they are. It’s always the way. Everything online is either a scam or takes three weeks to arrive. Remember that phone case I ordered? Still waiting for it. Oh god, yeah. The one with the glitter? That's been months now. I swear it’s circling the globe. Probably. Speaking of online shopping… did you see that advert on TikTok for those weighted blankets? Apparently they're like, the best thing ever for anxiety. Weighted blankets? Sounds…claustrophobic. I get anxious  thinking  about being weighed down. No, it’s supposed to be comforting. Like a hug. I was thinking of getting one. Might help me actually get some sleep before these exams. Fair enough. You've got proper stuff to worry about, unlike me and my…gaming ambitions. What are you watching on telly tonight? Anything good? There’s that new crime drama starting, ‘Silent Shadows’ or something. Seems alright. Mum’s already claimed the living room though, she's got that baking show she’s obsessed with. Oh, 'Great British Bake Off: Professionals'? She's been banging on about that for weeks. The drama! The pastries! Exactly. It’s more exciting than my actual life right now. Seriously though, you should actually apply for some jobs. That online application for the supermarket was easy enough. I did, remember? They haven’t even  looked  at my application. It’s been two weeks. They probably think a history degree is a threat to their business model.

So, have you managed to get any of the heating sorted then, Dad? It must be freezing in here still. Oh, it’s a right palaver, I tell you. The bloke came round, said it needs a new pump. A new  pump ! Sounds expensive. He’s coming back on Tuesday, said he might be able to get one quicker if he knows I’m desperate. Desperate is an understatement! It’s like living in a fridge. Oh, you poor thing. That sounds awful. Can’t you put the electric fire on in the living room, just to take the chill off? I can, but it’s expensive, isn’t it? Not the way to run a house, relying on electric fires. I’m hoping this pump thing doesn’t cost the earth. It's all these old houses, you know? Built to last, they say, but everything falls apart eventually. Mum, are you making lunch? I’m absolutely starving. Walking around looking at paint samples works up an appetite, you know. Just finishing off some soup. Tomato and basil. It’s simple, but warming. Bit of crusty bread with it. Will that do? Sounds perfect, thanks. So, Dad, you’ve been planning this coastal walk, haven't you? When are you thinking of doing it? I was thinking next week, sometime. Depends on the weather, of course. And the heating! Can’t go traipsing around the coast if I’m shivering. Maybe Wednesday? Wednesday could be good. I'm free. We could pack a picnic. I’ve got that new rucksack. That sounds lovely. Where are you planning on walking? I was looking at the stretch from Hartland Quay to Clovelly. It’s about eight miles, I think. Not too strenuous, but some lovely scenery. We could stop at Clovelly for a cream tea. Ooh, a cream tea sounds good. Though Clovelly is rather…touristy, isn’t it? It is, but it’s part of the experience. Besides, a good cream tea is worth a bit of tourist nonsense. Now, about furniture. I need a new armchair. Mine’s on its last legs. Literally. The springs are poking through. We could go to that place in Exeter on Saturday? The one with all the second-hand furniture? They sometimes have some really good finds. Excellent idea. We could make a day of it. Have a look around, have some lunch… maybe even find you a decent armchair.

Right, that was…needed. Honestly, I think I was operating on fumes by the time I got home. That meeting this morning… Oh, don’t even  start  on meetings. Mine was a disaster. Honestly, I spent the entire hour trying to explain to Brenda why standardised testing isn’t the be-all and end-all. It’s like talking to a brick wall. Brenda, huh? Still fighting the good fight then? It sounds exhausting. Mine was just…endless. Professor Davies went on a tangent about the ethical implications of AI in psychological research. Which, fine, important stuff, but…at nine in the morning? Before coffee had properly kicked in? Oh, the agony. The absolute agony. I swear, some people just enjoy hearing themselves talk. Did you at least manage to get any actual work done afterwards? A little. I managed to crunch some numbers on the anxiety study. Still not seeing the patterns I’d hoped for, though. It’s frustrating. I keep thinking I’m missing something obvious. You’ll crack it. You always do. Remember that glitch with the data back in…January? You spent days on that, and you figured it out in the end. True, but that felt…different. This feels more fundamental. Like maybe my whole approach is flawed. Don’t be so hard on yourself. It's research. It’s  supposed  to be challenging. And honestly, you've been working flat out. How’s your mum coping, by the way? You said she was feeling a bit off last week? She’s…okay. She’s refusing to go to the doctor, naturally. Insists it’s just a bit of a cold, but she’s completely lost her appetite, and she's always eating. She’s proper stubborn. I tried to convince her, but she just gave me that look. You know the one. Oh,  that  look. The one that says, “I’m older than you, I know best, and you’re worrying over nothing.” Exactly. It's… it’s just worrying, you know? Everything feels precarious at the moment. Work’s stressful, Mum’s not well… I get it. It's a lot. Hey, listen. We’re going to need a proper weekend. No work talk, no family crises allowed. Just…us. Maybe that new Italian place? I hear the pasta is amazing. That sounds…perfect, actually. A complete escape. No AI ethics, no stubborn mums, no frustrating data.

Honestly, the price of everything is just… ridiculous now, isn’t it? Even cat food. Jasper’s turning his nose up at the cheaper stuff. He’s a right little snob, that one. Cats are like that. My old tabby, Winston, wouldn’t touch anything that wasn’t tuna flavoured. Cost me a fortune. Still, better than having a dog, all that walking… Walking’s good though! I’ve been meaning to get a dog, a little rescue one. But then I think about the travel, and honestly, my flat’s barely big enough for me, let alone a kennel. You’d manage. You always do. Remember when you tried to keep those chickens in the garden?  That  was a disaster waiting to happen. Oh god, don’t remind me. Mum nearly had a heart attack when she found out. Said the whole garden smelled like, well, you can imagine. They’re messy animals, chickens. Thankfully, nursing is mostly just humans. Though some days, you wonder… Tell me about it. Had a patient today who insisted he was allergic to the oxygen mask. Honestly. You get all sorts, don’t you? Remember old Mrs. Higgins, said she could predict the weather by the ache in her left knee? Of course. And she was usually right, ironically enough. Though it was probably just the arthritis acting up. This is why I write copy, everything is far less… chaotic. Though ads for cleaning products can be surprisingly cutthroat. It's amazing how many cleaning product ads there are, isn't it? It's always a race to say yours is the 'sparkliest' or 'most hygienic'. It’s interesting thinking about language though, isn't it? How we use words to convince people. I’ve been doing this linguistics module as part of my nurse practitioner training… it's fascinating. Apparently, even the way a doctor phrases a diagnosis can affect a patient’s outlook. Fancy that. I always thought it was just common sense. Softly, softly, catchee monkey, as they say. Speaking of common sense, has anyone figured out why I keep finding random left-handed objects around the house? It's like a conspiracy. Maybe it’s a ghost? A left-handed ghost? Don’t encourage her. No, it’s probably just Amelia. She started writing with her left hand last week, apparently. She's a clever girl, Amelia. Though don’t tell her I said that, she'll get a big head.

Honestly though, that crumble was unreal. Proper comforting, you know? After a day like today, battling spreadsheets… it was exactly what I needed. Crumble, eh? Used to make a lovely crumble myself, back in the day. Rhubarb mostly. Had a proper rhubarb patch, we did. Though, you wouldn’t get rhubarb like that now. Everything tastes… different. Less flavour. Grandad, you say that about everything! It’s just your tastebuds changing. It's a scientific fact. Nonsense! It's the  soil . The soil's changed. They don’t use proper manure anymore, all these fancy fertilizers. Ruins everything. You get a flavourless tomato, a flavourless strawberry… even a flavourless crumble! Maybe a bit of both, eh? You’ve always been a stickler for good soil. Speaking of growing things, did you manage to get any good tomatoes this year? I remember your greenhouse being legendary. Well, I  tried . But the blight got to them. Nasty stuff, blight. Came on quick as you like. Lost the lot. Had to dig ‘em all up, heartbreaking really. Spent months nurturing those plants. That’s rough, Grandad. You always put so much effort into your garden. It kept me busy, you know? After I retired. Better than sitting around moping. Though, I’m starting to think travelling might be a better use of my time now. Always wanted to see Italy. Oh, Italy! That would be amazing! Have you been looking at places? Just brochures mostly. My eyesight isn’t what it was, can’t really manage the internet properly anymore. Though your aunty Margaret, she’s been doing some research for me. Says there’s a lovely little town called Orvieto, built on a cliff. Sounds rather picturesque. Sounds brilliant! You could visit Rome while you’re there. Loads of history. And the food… obviously. Rome, eh? Bit too busy for me, I think. I like a bit of peace and quiet. Somewhere I can just sit and watch the world go by. Maybe sip a little wine. That sounds perfect. You deserve a good bit of peace and quiet. You've earned it! Have you ever been anywhere really exotic, Grandad? Before your retirement, with BT? Exotic? Hmm. Not really. They sent me up to Scotland a few times, fixing telephone lines after storms. That was cold! And once, to Wales. But that’s hardly exotic, is it? Always had a family to get home to, you see.

Right, so for the Monday class, I’m still thinking of doing the introductory session on post-structuralism. You said you were happy to cover the Derrida stuff? Yeah, absolutely. I've got a good little breakdown of  Of Grammatology  I can adapt. Maybe focus on the supplement, that’s usually a good entry point. Keeps it relatively… digestible. Good. Digestible is key. They're bright, but most haven’t encountered this kind of stuff before. I'm worried about overloading them on day one. I was thinking of maybe pre-circulating a very short excerpt from Foucault, just to prime them? Hmm, okay. Which essay? The one on power/knowledge? That could be a bit…dense. Maybe something from  Discipline and Punish ? The opening describing torture is fairly gripping, even if they don’t grasp the theoretical implications immediately. Oh, good shout, that’s much better. The torture bit always gets a reaction. It’s a good palate cleanser after the programme introductions, too. Less… institutional. Exactly. What about Thursday? Are you still aiming for the feminist film theory seminar? Yeah, but I'm a bit stuck on how to structure it. I don’t want to just be name-dropping Laura Mulvey all afternoon. Trying to make it interactive, but it’s tricky. I was thinking maybe showing a short clip and getting them to deconstruct it? That sounds good. What clip did you have in mind? Something classic, like a bit of  Vertigo ? I was leaning towards  Rear Window , actually. I think it’s slightly more accessible. The voyeurism theme is pretty blatant, which helps with initial analysis. Plus, it’s Hitchcock, so they’ll recognise it. Good thinking. You could get them to focus on the male gaze, obviously, but also maybe push them a little on the implications of the female characters’ relative passivity. Yes! That’s exactly what I was hoping to get at. Okay, that’s good. I’ll prep some guiding questions. Honestly, I’m just craving a proper roast dinner after planning all this. I'm so over noodles. Tell me about it. I saw a post on Facebook for a British food shop that’s just opened near the university. Apparently, they’ve got Yorkshire puddings. No way! Yorkshire puddings… that's almost worth the trek. Although, knowing this city, it’ll be ridiculously expensive. Probably. But desperate times, desperate measures.

Right, so I got a quote back from that storage place near Penrith. It’s…ouch. More than I was hoping, honestly. How much are they wanting? For a container, roughly the size we need…£180 a month. And that’s  before  you factor in the removal costs to get everything there in the first place. £180? That’s daylight robbery! We paid less than that for a garage near Birmingham, and that was a proper city. Cumbria’s supposed to be cheaper. Apparently not. I got a quote for removal too, and it’s looking like around £600 - £800 just to get it all loaded, transported and unloaded. Honestly, it’s cheaper to just…get rid of half of it. Isn’t it? Though, admittedly, that’s a depressing thought. It is, but practical. What exactly are we storing anyway? Grandma’s china? Boxes of old school reports? Be ruthless, you two. There's…a lot of books. Yours mostly, Mum. And a surprisingly high number of Christmas decorations. Well, the books are important! Some of them are first editions. Though even  I  admit the Christmas decoration collection has gotten out of hand. Remember when we tried to decorate the entire garden shed? Oh, don’t remind me. The neighbours thought we’d lost it. Speaking of lost…did you catch Newsnight last night? Utter chaos in the Labour party. Fragments of it, yeah. Something about Starmer being…ineffective? Honestly, I can’t keep up. It changes week to week. Ineffective is putting it mildly. He's trying to be everything to everyone and ends up appealing to no one. Remember Kinnock? He had fire in his belly. This one just feels…beige. It’s all so cynical now, isn’t it? Back in the day, people genuinely believed in something. Socialism, community, a better future. Now it's all about soundbites and…polling data. That’s probably a bit romanticised, Dad. There was always cynicism, even back then. Perhaps. But there was idealism too. A real sense of wanting to change things. Now, it’s just…careerism. Everyone’s climbing the ladder. And look at the state of things! The cost of living, the NHS…it’s a mess. I’m making another coffee, anyone want one? This machine is still a godsend, even if it does make a ridiculous amount of noise. Please, yes. And while you’re at it, can we revisit this storage situation?

Right, so basically, I’ve decided I’m going by “Rex” for the whole holiday. Just… Rex. No questions. Rex? Seriously? That's… a choice. Sounds like a dinosaur. Proper villain name, innit? Like, a Bond villain. “Rex… and I will control the world’s supply of… sourdough!” Fair dinkum. Rex. Bit much, mate. Just stick with what ya got. Nah, I need a fresh start. A clean slate. Plus it’s really ironic considering my flatmate’s dog is called Tiny. It’s a power move. Okay, okay, Rex it is. So, anyone actually know any interesting river names? I was trying to impress a customer at the bakery earlier, talking about the Thames, and realised I couldn’t name another one. The Severn’s a good one. Longest in the UK. Bit boring though. Got that whole, ‘reliable British river’ vibe. The Murray! Back home, the Murray-Darling Basin’s a big deal. Huge river system, bit of a mess environmentally these days though. Speaking of systems, did anyone see old Mr. Goldstein down by the canal yesterday? He was going absolutely mental about someone mooring a boat too close to his prize-winning hydrangeas. Apparently, it violates some ancient canal boat etiquette. Oh, him! He’s always moaning. He’s got more rules than kosher law, that man. You can’t even  look  at his hydrangeas directly. Remember when he tried to tell that group of students off for having a picnic? Said they were ‘disrupting the flow of the spiritual energy’ or something? Crikey. Sounds intense. We should have a picnic just to annoy him. Maybe later. Right now, I’m thinking about dinner. Anyone fancy Italian? I found this place online that supposedly does proper pasta. None of that pre-made, gloopy stuff. Ooh, Italian sounds good. Although, I'm bringing my own chilli oil. Their condiments are always rubbish. Honestly, you get bland tomato ketchup and watery mayonnaise. It’s a disgrace. You and your chilli oil. You carry that thing everywhere. It's like your emotional support condiment. It  is  emotionally supportive! It makes everything better. Even microwaved leftovers. Microwaved leftovers? You're a baker! You should be ashamed. Everything you make is amazing. Yeah, seriously. A proper bakery. That's a skill. I just push buttons on an espresso machine all day. Though, I can make a mean flat white. You make a mean flat white, and you’re a top bloke, that’s what matters.

Honestly, Tinder’s been a right disaster zone lately. Just endless lads asking for… well, you know. It’s exhausting. Tell me about it! I deleted mine last week. It was just a constant stream of “hey” and then instantly wanting to meet up. Like, hello, conversation first? Seriously! It's all about instant gratification, isn’t it? I matched with this one guy who, in his bio, literally said he was “looking for a good time.” Subtle. Oh my god. You're kidding! That's… bold. I’ve had a few offering to “Netflix and chill” within five minutes of matching. It's the same at uni too, isn’t it? Like, blokes just think if you make eye contact for more than three seconds you’re offering them… something. Exactly! And the uni boys are  worse . They all think they’re God’s gift. There was one in my seminar last week who kept ‘accidentally’ brushing his arm against mine. Creep. Ugh, the arm brushers. The  worst . Did you say anything? I moved seats. Honestly, I just couldn’t be bothered with the drama. I just want to focus on my dissertation. Wise move. Dissertation stress is already high enough without adding unwanted attention to the mix. Speaking of which, how's yours going? Mine’s a total mess. I’m stuck on the literature review. It’s like, there’s so much out there I don't even know where to start. Oh, I feel that. I’m battling the same thing. Mine’s on Victorian poetry, and it’s just… endless. I’m starting to dream in iambic pentameter. I’m okay, I think. I’ve actually got a decent chunk done, but now I’m worried it’s not… good enough. You know? That imposter syndrome hits hard. Oh yeah, totally. I constantly feel like everyone else knows what they're doing and I’m just pretending. Me too. It’s a student staple, isn’t it? Right, anyone else struggling with their housemates? Oh. Don’t even  start  me on mine. Liam leaves dirty dishes everywhere, and he plays his music at ridiculous volumes. I'm close to losing it. Mine are alright, thankfully. A bit messy, but generally respectful. I had a nightmare housemate last year though. Literally used the kitchen sink as a laundry basket. No way! Seriously?! I am not even joking.

Honestly, the state of it. Utterly ridiculous. What is now, Arthur? Don’t start. My tea’s barely touched. This whole benefits thing. They're just giving it away, you know they are. I saw a bloke on the news, living like a lord, never lifted a finger in his life. Oh, honestly, Arthur. You always say that. There are people genuinely struggling. Struggling? They're all struggling to find a bigger telly, that’s what they’re struggling with! It’s a scandal, I tell you. A scandal. Back in my day… Here we go. Back in your day, everyone was working down the shoe factory and coughing up dust. Not exactly a picnic, was it? It was honest work! And we didn't expect handouts. We built things. Bridges, roads… things that lasted. Not this…this dependency culture. It's just not that simple, is it? Jobs have changed. Things are different now. Plenty of people  want  to work, but there just isn't anything available. Nonsense. There’s always work. They just don’t want to do it. Too busy playing on their phones. You’ve got a short memory, Arthur. Remember old man Hemmings? Worked his whole life, lost his job at sixty and couldn’t find another one. Ended up relying on the state just to eat. It happens. Hemmings was a special case. A bit of a… well, he wasn't the sharpest tool in the shed. Oh, Arthur! That's unkind. Just stating facts. Anyway, did you see that program on last night? About the housing crisis? The one with that presenter who always looks like he’s smelling something unpleasant? That’s the one. It’s all these immigrants, driving up house prices. Now, Arthur, that's a rather sweeping statement. It’s a complex issue, not just down to immigration. It’s a contributing factor, surely. They're all crammed into these tiny flats, and who pays for it? The taxpayer! And what about the landlords raking in the money then? They don’t get a mention. They’re the real villains. They're all villains. The whole lot of 'em. It’s… infuriating. I swear, if I was in charge… Oh dear. If you were in charge, we’d all be living in bunkers and wearing ill-fitting hats. I’d sort it all out, you’ll see. A firm hand is needed.

This pasta’s lovely, isn’t it? You’ve really outdone yourself. Thanks. It’s just a simple tomato and basil sauce, really. Though I did use that posh balsamic vinegar you got. Makes all the difference. How was your day? Anything exciting happen at… well, wherever you were today? Exciting is… a strong word. It was  a day . The usual meetings, endless emails. Old Mr. Henderson was on one again, complaining about the font size on the internal newsletter. Honestly, you’d think we had bigger fish to fry. Henderson. Always Henderson. Doesn't he have anything better to do? Fundraising is stressful enough without dealing with font size complaints. Did you manage to get any of that grant paperwork finished? The deadline’s looming, isn't it? Almost. I’m stuck on the impact assessment. They want quantifiable evidence of everything, which is, frankly, impossible when you’re talking about supporting vulnerable families. How do you quantify 'hope', David? Honestly. You don't. You fudge it. A little. Tell them you’ve seen a 7% increase in applicants reporting positive mental wellbeing. Something vaguely believable. They just want to tick boxes. You rogue. I suppose you’re right. They don’t actually want to  understand  the work, just see the numbers look good on a spreadsheet. How was your day? Any big donors bite? One promising lead. Lady Worthington. Huge estate, supposedly very philanthropic. Spent an hour on the phone with her assistant trying to schedule a meeting. Apparently, she only does mornings and doesn’t appreciate being contacted before 10 am. Oh, the aristocracy. Always rules for everyone else, aren't they? Still, it’s a lead. Worth pursuing. Did Lily call about this weekend? She was supposed to confirm if she and Ben can come down. Not yet. I texted her earlier. No reply. I’m hoping they can make it. It’ll be nice to have some family time. This house feels a bit empty with just us two sometimes. I know. I miss the chaos, honestly. Even when they’re driving us round the bend. What are we watching on TV tonight? I saw there’s something new on Channel 4. That detective drama everyone’s talking about. Oh, “Shadows”? I've heard it's good. Actually, I was thinking we could finally start that documentary about the Antarctic. You’ve been talking about it for months.

Honestly, this weather is grim, isn’t it? Constant drizzle. I feel like I haven’t seen the sun in weeks. It's a good job I brought a proper coat, though. Remember that time I went to Scotland with just a cardigan? Disaster. Oh, yes! You were absolutely freezing. You looked like a drowned rat. Though, to be fair, even I’m feeling a bit under the weather. Just a bit off, you know? Not properly sick, just… blah. Oh no, not good. Are you sure you're not coming down with something? You’ve been a bit quiet since I got here. Poland isn’t exactly known for boosting immune systems, is it? Not with all this grey. I think it's just the stress of everything, really. Going back for Aunt Margaret’s funeral… it was awful. It felt so strange being back in Cambridge. It just didn't  feel  like home anymore. I can imagine. It’s weird, isn't it? What 'home' even  is . I've been thinking about that a lot lately. Is it where you grew up? Where your family is? Or where you feel… settled? Exactly. I don’t feel particularly settled anywhere now. I mean, I’ve made a life here, and I like it, generally. But it's not… England. Being back reminded me of that. And it’s not like I can just  go  back, is it? No, not really. Not with the job situation. Though, even if you could, do you actually  want  to? What did you enjoy most about your teaching days, before all this? Was it the TEFL stuff? That was alright, yeah. The one-on-ones were good - really seeing someone grasp something. But I miss the bigger picture stuff, the curriculum development, the academic side. University lecturing, that was my dream job. I get that. I love the classroom, but the paperwork… and the politics… Ugh. That's why I jumped at the chance to teach abroad. Less admin, more actual teaching. See, I'm looking at Bethany’s Instagram… oh, she’s in Santorini. Again. Honestly, that woman has an endless holiday fund. Makes me feel distinctly un-glamorous. Oh, don't. Instagram is a highlight reel, remember? She probably spent three months saving to afford that. Plus, she's got that horrible boyfriend. It's not all sunshine and cocktails, trust me. You're probably right.

Honestly, this tea is a lifesaver. I was starting to feel properly wilted after that client meeting. They wanted  everything  changed. Like, the whole campaign. Oof, sounds rough. What was it this time? Too… punchy? Not punchy enough? They’re always so vague. Too… ‘youthful.’ Apparently, describing washing powder as ‘vibey’ doesn’t resonate with their target demographic of… retirees. Oh,  god . Seriously? ‘Vibey’ washing powder. You're a genius. They should be paying you extra for sheer creativity. Tell that to Brenda from marketing. She just kept saying it didn't feel ‘aspirational.’ Aspirational washing powder. It's washing powder, Brenda! Brenda sounds exhausting. How’s the rest of work? Still battling the Christmas catalogue deadlines? Oh, it's a bloodbath. Everyone’s frantically trying to finish things before the end of the month. I’m writing descriptions for about a million different scented candles and luxury bath oils. It's… fragrant, but also soul-crushing. Sounds about right. I’m mostly coding surveys at the moment, which is less fragrant, but arguably less soul-crushing. It's just… repetitive, you know? They want to know everything about people’s biscuit preferences. Everything. Biscuit preferences are important! Don't underestimate the power of a good digestive. Speaking of which, I’m starving. Have you eaten? Not really. Just had a yoghurt this morning. I was planning on grabbing something from that little market near Waterloo after this. They do amazing sourdough. Oh, that sounds incredible. I’m completely useless at food shopping, by the way. I just end up buying ready meals and hoping for the best. I need to take a leaf out of your book. It's not that hard! It’s just… making a list. And then sticking to it. Mostly. Though I did buy three different kinds of olives last week. Don’t know why. Olives are always a good choice. Honestly, you’re a far more organised human being than I am. Do you think Chloe's still coming tonight? I haven't heard back from her. She said she might be late. Something about a last-minute rehearsal for her band. Apparently, they’re covering a really obscure Bulgarian folk song. Chloe and her obscure Bulgarian folk songs. Never a dull moment. Right, another sip of tea then. Fuel for the fragrant candle battles. Do you want me to continue the conversation, or would you like me to generate a new one?

Mummy you woke me up. Did I? Oh, sorry darling. I didn't mean to. I was having a really good dream. Were you? What were you dreaming about? Dragons. And spaceships. I was dreaming about unicorns with rainbow manes. Oh, lovely! Right, well, good morning officially then. What shall we do today? It’s Saturday! Can we go to the park? Yes, the park! And then can we practice juggling? Juggling? Oh, are we still on for that circus skills thing? Yeah! Dad said he'd teach us to juggle. Right, well, maybe after breakfast. I'm starving. What does everyone want? I want toast. With jam. Lots of jam. Pancakes! Can we have pancakes? With blueberries? Pancakes it is! Though maybe not  too  many blueberries. Remember what happened last time? Blue faces! Exactly. Now, I need coffee. And then we can get this show on the road. Oh, and your Dad’s mentioned something about Neon Moon tonight. What’s Neon Moon? It’s like… a sort of market, but with vintage clothes and music and things. It’s at The Cattle Market. Can we go? Maybe. It depends if we can find someone to look after you two. It gets very busy. Your Dad's mentioned asking Auntie Carol. But I want to go! Me too! It sounds cool. We'll see. Okay, pancakes. While we’re waiting, did you know that in Australia, they say “arvo” instead of “afternoon”? Arvo? That’s silly. It sounds like a dinosaur. Arvo-saurus! That's brilliant! See, learning  is  fun. Right, who wants to help me get the pancake mix out? Me! Me! I want to stir! Okay, okay, one at a time. We'll both stir. We'll need to be careful not to make a mess. Remember when we tried to make cookies last month? Flour everywhere! Flour  absolutely  everywhere. Let’s try for a slightly less chaotic pancake situation shall we? I hope this conversation fits your criteria! Let me know if you’d like me to continue it, or make any changes. Okay okay one at a time we'll both stir we'll need to be careful not to make a mess remember when we tried to make cookies last month. Flour everywhere. Flour absolutely everywhere let’s try for a slightly less chaotic pancake situation shall we. Make a mess. Flour. Good idea let's not do that let's watch out for the flour

Honestly, the state of things… you’d think after all this time, they’d have figured out a coherent strategy. It’s all just… flailing, isn’t it? Flailing and soundbites. You’re talking about the new housing bill, I presume? I read a fairly scathing article in the  Guardian  this morning. Utterly short-sighted. They keep saying it's about ‘levelling up’, but it feels like it’s just benefiting developers and ignoring the actual needs of communities. I saw something on Twitter about it. A lot of really angry responses, especially from young people. Nobody can afford to buy anywhere. It feels like the goalposts are constantly moving. Aye, that’s precisely it. The whole concept of home ownership feels… mythical, almost, for your generation. It wasn’t easy for us, mind, back in the 80s. Interest rates were sky-high. But at least there was  some  hope. This feels…different. It  is  different. And it’s not just house prices. It’s the cost of everything. Energy bills, food… even a simple trip to the cinema is a luxury now. I’m increasingly worried about what things will look like in ten, twenty years. It’s definitely a worry. I’m working three part-time jobs just to cover rent and student loans. Doesn’t leave much for… living, you know? That's… appalling. Absolutely appalling. It's a disgrace, frankly. Reminds me a bit of the situation in Nantyglo when the mines started closing, actually. Different industry, same desperation. People felt utterly abandoned. My grandfather, he lost his job then. Never quite recovered, he didn't. Spent the rest of his days working odd jobs, bitterness eating away at him. That’s a stark comparison, Gareth. But I see your point. And it’s a history we shouldn’t forget. It’s easy for those in power to lose sight of the real-life consequences of their decisions. They don’t feel it. It's easy to get cynical, isn't it? Feels like nothing ever really changes. Cynicism is a reasonable response, lad. Perfectly reasonable. But it’s also… debilitating. You have to engage. You have to hold them accountable. Even if it feels like shouting into the void. And vote. Always, always vote. Even for the least worst option. Absolutely. And remember the power of local activism too. Community groups, campaigning… it all makes a difference.

Right, so the brave knight, Sir Reginald… he didn’t have a shiny helmet, did he? He had a… a bucket on his head! A  bucket ? A silver bucket? No, a rusty old bucket! He found it in the garden. And it wobbled when he moved. Wobbled? Like… when I run really fast and my head shakes? Exactly like that! It wobbled and clanged. And he was trying to rescue Princess Penelope… but she wasn't very impressed with his bucket helmet. She’d say, “That's a silly bucket!” She definitely would! She'd say, “Sir Reginald, you look ridiculous! A proper knight has a  gleaming  helmet!” And then what happened? Did a dragon come? Hmm… not a dragon, exactly. A very grumpy goose. A goose who guarded the princess’s tower. A goose?! What did the goose do? Did it honk really loud? It honked  incredibly  loud. And it tried to peck Sir Reginald’s wobbly bucket!  Clang!  It made a terrible noise. He would have had to duck! Really, really fast! He did! He ducked and the bucket fell off. And underneath… he wasn’t wearing chainmail! He was wearing… pyjamas! Striped pyjamas! Pyjamas?! A knight in pyjamas! A knight in striped pyjamas! Princess Penelope was  very  amused. She couldn't stop laughing. Did the goose chase him? The goose chased him all the way back to his garden! Honking and flapping its wings! He had to hide behind the rose bushes. That's a really funny story! Is it like Helen Moss’s stories? When the heroes are a bit silly? It is a bit like Helen Moss, isn't it? Although her heroes are usually a bit more… prepared. Remember when we went to Linton Book Festival and met her? Yeah! And she signed my book! She did! And she told us all about where she gets her ideas. Maybe we need to go again this year? Ooh yes! Can we? Can we go and see her again? We'll have to see. But for now, let’s think about what happened  after  Sir Reginald hid behind the rose bushes… He had a very embarrassing walk home, I think! Maybe his mum told him off for wearing pyjamas to rescue a princess! She  definitely  told him off! A very stern talking-to. And the goose probably told all the other geese! Absolutely. The goose gossiped to all the other geese, and Sir Reginald was the laughingstock of the village!

Right, so I was reading this article about lab-grown meat, like, actual “shmeat” as they’re calling it, and it’s… it’s weirding me out a bit. Oh, yeah? I thought it sounded amazing! Like, potentially solving so many problems. No animal cruelty, smaller environmental impact… It’s still meat though, isn’t it? Like, fundamentally. Just grown in a vat. Feels… off. Exactly! And the ethical side of it feels muddled. Like, we're trying to avoid hurting animals, but isn’t there something… unsettling about creating life just to, well, consume it? But isn't the current system  worse ? The conditions in factory farms are horrific. And the amount of land and water used… It's massively unsustainable. Surely, a controlled environment, even if it  is  a vat, is the lesser evil? I guess. It just feels like we’re just shifting the problem, not solving it. Like, who regulates these labs? What are the long-term effects of eating this stuff? Oh god, don’t even get me started on the long-term effects. And it’s not like everyone’s suddenly going to become vegetarian. People  like  meat. This feels like a way for them to have their steak and eat it too, without actually confronting their consumption. That’s a bit cynical, isn’t it? Some people genuinely want to reduce harm but still enjoy the taste. It could be a good compromise. I mean, I’m mostly vegetarian, but I do sometimes crave a good burger. It's the whole hunting vs. abattoir thing for me. I understand people hunt to eat, there's a level of respect for the animal, it’s a quick death. But the sheer scale and impersonal nature of abattoirs…that’s what gets me. Still doesn’t make cultured meat appeal though. True. Okay, moving away from existential dread, and back to actual cooking. Are you putting enough turmeric in this? It needs a kick. I thought I did… it’s just a little bit. Don’t want it overpowering. Speaking of overpowering, did you catch the latest  Curb Your Enthusiasm ? Larry David is on  form . No! I’m behind. I’ve been working pretty much non-stop. What’s happening? Oh, it’s glorious. He gets into a dispute with someone about… I honestly can’t remember the specifics, but it involves a charity donation and a very passive-aggressive note.

Right, so I’ve put the chicken in to marinate, should be lovely with those roasted vegetables. Are we still doing dauphinoise potatoes? Absolutely. Though I’m having a crisis of confidence about my layering skills. Last time they were… well, let's just say unevenly cooked. More like potato surprise. Oh god, I remember! You were complaining about it all Boxing Day. It wasn’t  that  bad, darling. A little bit crunchy on top, admittedly. But edible. Have you sorted the washing machine, by the way? It’s been making that awful rumbling noise again. I called Brenda. You know, my cousin Brenda, the one who’s obsessed with appliances? Apparently, it’s probably just a sock stuck in the drum. She said to run an empty cycle on hot. A sock? Seriously? That's classic. It’s always a sock. Or a tea towel. It's the Bermuda Triangle of laundry. Honestly. It’s like they vanish into another dimension. Speaking of Brenda, did you hear she’s finally throwing out her mother’s china? The stuff she’s been ‘saving for best’ for fifty years? No way! Old Mrs. Higgins’ dreadful floral china? That’s a monumental event. She’s a hoarder of epic proportions. I remember when she made us all use it at Christmas, even though half of it was chipped. It felt so… precarious! Like one wrong move and the whole thing would shatter. Exactly! Remember Uncle Geoff trying to sneakily swap his plate for a paper one? She saw him and gave him such a telling off. Oh, brilliant. That man. He’s got a knack for winding her up. So, New Year’s Eve... still thinking of just a quiet one at home? I am leaning that way, yeah. I saw what happened in Edinburgh. A bit much, honestly. Too many people. And the internet's been full of complaints about the transport being a nightmare. Sensible. I’m happy with a nice bottle of fizz and a good film. Although… I did see something about that new detective series on ITV? ‘Hidden Depths’ or something? Oh, the one with the ex-military investigator? Apparently, it’s excellent. I’ve recorded the first two episodes. Though I've been trying to sort out the broadband all day. It keeps dropping out! Honestly, you’d think in this day and age… Tell me about it.

Honestly, a butterfly fork. Who invents these things? It’s just… needlessly complicated. What’s a butterfly fork? It’s… it’s a fork with sort of split prongs, shaped like butterfly wings apparently. Elsie’s grandmother sent one with her birthday gift. Apparently, they’re “very elegant” for peas. Elegant peas? That sounds… pointless. Does it actually work? It does, actually. It holds a surprisingly small amount of peas. But it’s so fiddly. You spend more time manoeuvring the fork than actually eating the peas. Sounds rubbish. Is Elsie happy with it? She politely said thank you. I think she’s wondering why her grandmother thinks she needs a specialized utensil for legumes. Speaking of Elsie, did you two finish the history homework? It’s about the Russian Revolution, isn’t it? Nearly. I’ve got the timeline done, but I’m stuck on explaining why the Tsar was so unpopular. It just seems like… a lot of reasons. Yeah, it’s a bit overwhelming. So many revolts, and reforms that didn’t really work, and then the war… It’s complex. Remember what Mr. Davies said about looking at it from lots of different perspectives? The peasants, the workers, the aristocracy… everyone had different grievances. Right, okay. I need to remember that. It’s just… Russia feels so far away and a long time ago. It’s hard to connect it to anything. I know, it does. It’s funny, isn’t it? How things that happened centuries ago can still cast a shadow over what’s happening now. Look at the situation with Ukraine. You can draw a direct line back to centuries of Russian expansionism. It's scary, though, isn’t it? Everything happening. Mr. Henderson was talking about it in assembly today. He said we’ll be observing the two minutes silence on Friday. That's good. Important to remember. It’s so easy to get desensitized when it’s constantly on the news. Do you think things will ever… get better? That’s a big question. I hope so. I really do. Sometimes it feels like history just repeats itself, doesn’t it? It kind of does. Anyway, back to Elsie's birthday. She’s having a proper party this weekend, isn’t she? She is. She’s invited nearly the whole class. I’m already dreading the sugar rush. We’re having a bouncy castle, which will probably be her highlight.

Right, so Adventure Island, series three, is officially the most requested thing this summer. And honestly, after last year’s Cornwall trip… I’m a little hesitant. But Mummy, it’s got a  real  pirate ship! And a volcano! And they find a secret treasure! Yeah! And the girl, Isla, she’s really good at climbing. Can we go to a place with climbing? Like Cornwall? Cornwall was… eventful. Remember the seagull incident, darlings? And the seven-hour car journey where you both asked ‘are we there yet?’ approximately five thousand times? But the beach was nice! And we built a really big sandcastle! I liked the ice cream. Even though it made my tummy rumble. Yes, the ice cream. Which reminds me, have you two been good about avoiding the dairy, with your intolerances? Or have you been sneaking biscuits again? No! Maybe a tiny bit… Tiny bit? Right. Well, we need to be careful. A rumbling tummy on holiday is  not  fun. Okay, so Adventure Island is on the table, but let’s explore other options too. I was thinking maybe a few days in London? There’s that V&A exhibition on pirates, actually. Pirates  again ? Well, it’s a different kind of pirate! It’s about real pirates, and treasure, and old maps. It's rather good actually. Can we go on the London Eye? Possibly. Depends if we can find somewhere affordable to stay. Everything in London is so expensive. I’ve got a mountain of exam papers to mark this week, though, so I won't have much time to research. Honestly, it’s relentless. Year six sats are the bane of my existence. What are sats? Oh, you don't need to worry about that yet. They’re just… grown-up tests. Very boring ones. Right, back to holidays. What about a cottage somewhere? Somewhere quieter, with a garden? Can we take Buster? Hmm. That depends on the cottage. Not all of them allow dogs. We'll need to have a look. And maybe, just maybe, we can revisit Cornwall next year. But we're definitely packing seagull repellent this time. And a very large supply of dairy-free ice cream. And a treasure map! We  need  a treasure map! And a volcano! We’ll see, we’ll see. First, exam papers. Then, holiday planning. It's going to be a busy week. Now, who wants a dairy-free biscuit?

Honestly, Mr. Davies is taking the absolute mickey with the history coursework. Like, fifteen sources? Who has time for that? Tell me about it! I'm still trying to find three decent ones. He just wants to make our lives miserable, doesn’t he? Mrs. Patel is alright though, actually gave us an extension on the English essay. Patel’s a legend. Davies just…ugh. Remember when he gave Ben a detention for yawning? A  yawn ! Seriously! And then he tried to justify it by saying it was “disrespectful.” It’s a yawn, not a political statement. Did you see Liam nearly fall off his chair laughing? Yeah, but then Davies gave  him  a look. Speaking of falling over, I nearly bailed it on my bike earlier. Went over a pothole on Elm Road. Oh no! Are you alright? You didn't smash anything, did you? Nah, just my pride. And nearly my face. That pothole is massive, someone needs to report it. Still, beats walking. True. Hey, are you going to Josh’s party on Saturday? Yeah, definitely. Promised I’d go. Are you? Yeah, I think so. Mum's being a bit iffy about it. She’s worried about… well, you know, with everything. All those rumours about what happened at Mia’s party last week? It was just a bit loud, wasn't it? Everyone makes it sound like a riot. That's what I said! But she's still not convinced. Plus she’s heard Josh’s older brother’s gonna be there, and apparently he’s a bit… intense. Right, the one with the motorbike? Heard he’s a bit of a show-off. Anyway, should be alright. I’m more worried about what to wear. I haven't even thought about that! I need something that doesn't look  too  new. Don’t want to look like I’m trying too hard. Exactly! Oh, have you seen the new Marvel movie?  Cosmic Chaos ? No! I’ve been meaning to. Is it good? It's insane! The special effects are mental. But, uh, heads up, apparently there is a scene with loads of peanuts. Like, everywhere. Oh, fantastic. You know I’m allergic, right? Yeah, sorry! Completely forgot. I’ll try to warn you if we end up watching it. Maybe cover your eyes or something? That's…helpful. Maybe we just watch something else. Anyway, did you hear they’re making Ethan a prefect?

This road is absolutely mental, isn’t it? Honestly, the traffic is building up for no reason. It always does at this time, doesn’t it? People just seem to decide to merge into one lane for fun. It's baffling. Aye, it’s daft. Remember when we were trying to get to Durham for that cricket match and we were stuck behind that tractor for ages? Oh god, yes. That was… an experience. I thought we were never going to make it. Was a good game though, wasn’t it? Root absolutely smashed it. He did! I was proper buzzing. It’s just getting there is the nightmare. I think next time, I’m getting the train. Less stress, you know? Probably a good shout. Though then you miss all the scenic… roadworks. Seriously, they’re everywhere. Haha, true. Speaking of getting places, are you still planning on cycling to Brighton next month? Yeah, still on. Doing a bit more training now, trying to get some decent mileage in. It’s further than it looks on a map. I bet! You’ll be knackered. Have you got all your gear sorted? Proper padded shorts and everything? Yeah, got the shorts, the helmet, the repair kit… the whole shebang. My mate, Ben, lent me a really good bike pump. Apparently, it makes a huge difference. Oh, good! You don’t want to be stuck halfway with a flat tyre and no way to fix it. That’s a disaster waiting to happen. Exactly. Ben’s done the ride a couple of times, so he’s been giving me loads of advice. He says the hills are killer. Hills? Where? Brighton’s pretty flat, isn’t it? Apparently, the approach from the north is a bit… undulating. He said there’s one particularly nasty one just before Devil’s Dyke. Oh, lovely. Sounds… fun. You'll need a massive energy gel supply then. Definitely. And a strong coffee at the top of every hill, I reckon. Perhaps I should start practicing eating energy gels whilst cycling. Now  that  would be a sight to see. Just don’t fall off! Honestly, you're a brave man. I’d rather sit and watch the cricket. Reckon we should take the A19 instead? It might be a bit quicker even with the roadworks. Hmm, good shout. Let's check the traffic on my phone. It looks like the A1 is backed up for miles.

Right okay, so who's actually going to  do  the ordering? Because last time, Leo, you spent ten minutes debating the merits of different spring roll fillings and we ended up with nothing. Hey! I was being thorough. A man's gotta know his spring rolls. Besides, you were busy scrolling through TikTok. Guys, guys, can we just choose a place and get this done? I'm starving. I had a really rough day crafting bids, seriously, the amount of jargon… it's exhausting. Fine, fine. Let's go with Golden Dragon. They’re usually pretty reliable and their Kung Pao chicken is divine. Golden Dragon? Seriously? They skimp on the chips! Remember last time? I practically had to ration them. Oh, don't even start with the chip rationing. That was a dark day. I was forced to share mine with you, Leo, and you devoured them in approximately three seconds. They just weren't giving us enough! It’s a fundamental right to have a decent portion of chips with your Chinese. Okay, drama queen. We’ll  request  extra chips. Happy? I’m calling. Right… hello? Yes, Golden Dragon? Er, takeaway please. While you’re on, could you ask if they do that special fried rice with the shrimp and pineapple? I'm craving it. Yes… and, um, could we have a special fried rice with shrimp and pineapple, please? …Yes, wonderful… Right, what else are we getting? I was thinking Kung Pao chicken… Definitely that. And a portion of ribs. Proper ribs, not those pathetic little things some places serve. …and ribs, yes, please. Proper ribs… He's giving me a weird look. Just tell him we know our ribs. It's important. …yes, we  know  our ribs. Okay… and some spring rolls. Just… standard spring rolls. No lengthy debates. Actually, can you ask if they do those duck spring rolls? The crispy ones? They’re amazing. …hold on a moment… Seriously?! What? They're good! Don’t judge me. …yes, hello? Sorry, um, do you do duck spring rolls? The crispy kind? … Oh, you do? Fantastic… See? Fantastic. You are  enabling  him, you know that? …Okay, so that’s Kung Pao chicken, ribs, duck spring rolls, special fried rice with shrimp and pineapple, and… standard spring rolls… and could we have extra chips,  please? … Yes, thank you very much… What's the postcode? … Yeah, 28 Acacia Avenue… Okay, great.

Honestly, the state of the NHS right now… it’s just relentless, isn’t it? I was talking to a colleague, Dr. Hayes, and she was saying the waiting lists for even basic things are just… astronomical. Tell me about it. I'm seeing it firsthand every day. We're constantly triaging, trying to prioritize, but people are suffering, waiting too long for even essential care. It’s heartbreaking, really. I had a woman in today, Ms. Doherty, been waiting six months for a hip replacement. Six months! She’s practically immobile. Six months? That’s… appalling. I mean, I teach Shakespeare, and even  that  feels more immediately valuable than trying to navigate the bureaucracy of it all sometimes. Though, honestly, I’m starting to wonder if a sonnet about the NHS waiting times would raise more awareness than any petition. You might be onto something there! A tragic verse, perhaps? Though I suspect even Shakespeare couldn’t cut through the red tape. It’s not just the waiting, it's the sheer  exhaustion  of the staff. Everyone's completely burnt out. It's a system under immense strain. I’ve been reading about the Finnish healthcare system, you know? They seem to have a much more preventative approach. Less firefighting, more… well, actually looking after people  before  they get to crisis point. Finland. Always held up as the ideal, aren’t they? Everything seems to work so well there. I wouldn’t mind a trip, just to see it in action. Though even then, I suspect it's a different cultural mindset as much as anything. Absolutely. It’s not as simple as just transplanting a system. Speaking of different cultures, have you had any more trouble with the neighbours? The ones with the… enthusiastic karaoke? Oh, don't even  start  me on them. It was worse last night. They were belting out some German oompah band song at two in the morning. Two! I considered calling the police, but honestly, what are they going to do? It's just… constant. Oh dear. That does sound… energetic. I recognise the feeling, though. When we first moved here, Mrs. Higgins next door decided to take up bagpipes. Bagpipes! The noise was unbelievable. It took a while, and a very carefully worded letter, to gently persuade her to limit her practicing to reasonable hours. A letter? I've tried being polite. I’ve tried leaving a note.

…and then young Kevin, bless him, says to me, “Sir, is ‘ironic’ really using a word you don’t know to sound clever?” Cheeky bugger. Honestly, these students. Ha! Good lad, that one. Sounds like a bright spark. They’re alright, the youngsters, if you give ‘em a chance. Though, mind, they don’t know the value of a hard day’s graft, do they? Everything’s handed to ‘em on a plate these days. It’s a different world, isn’t it? Though, to be fair, finding that ‘graft’ ain’t exactly easy. I was reading about that new welfare scheme… the one where they expect folk to apply for a hundred jobs a month. A hundred! What’s the point of that? You’ll spend more time filling in forms than actually  doing  a job. It’s just a way to wear people down, make ‘em give up. They want to push ‘em all onto Universal Credit, that’s what it is. Seems that way, doesn't it? My wife was saying the same. She works at the Citizen's Advice Bureau, so she’s hearing it all first hand. The stories are… grim. Grim, aye. Grim. Back in my day, if you wanted work, you went to the docks. Hard work, mind, but it were honest. Now… it’s all call centres and temporary contracts. And these agency fellas taking a cut of everything. Robbing buggers, the lot of ‘em. Speaking of robbing… did you hear about old Mrs. Patterson down the road? Someone tried to break into her house last night. No! Old Maggie? That’s terrible! Is she alright? The police caught ‘em, thankfully. Apparently, a couple of lads from down the street. Said they were “looking for quick money.” The police were round all morning, forensic team and everything. Always the same. Lazy buggers. Never worked a day in their lives. It’s this immigration, you know. They come over here, don't bother learning the language, just cause trouble. Now, now, that’s a bit harsh, isn’t it? I’ve got several international students, lovely lads and lasses. Work hard as anything. It’s not fair to tar everyone with the same brush. Oh, I don't mean  all  of ‘em. But there’s too many, that’s what I say. Too many coming over here, taking our jobs, stretching the resources. It weren't like this in my day, you know.

Right, so I genuinely spent half of yesterday afternoon trying to explain to my nan what a corpus actually  is . It was… a challenge. Oh god, the grandparents question. I’ve been there. Mine think I just… write dictionaries? Or something? It's close enough I suppose. My mum just nods and smiles. I think she thinks it sounds important, even if she hasn’t a clue. She asked if it involved a lot of numbers. That's a classic. My family mostly just assume anything related to language is vaguely related to teaching English to people, which… isn’t  wrong,  exactly, but also isn't  right . It’s a simplification. I tried explaining the concept of collocation to my dad, a retired mechanic, and his eyes just glazed over. Then he asked if it was anything like ‘finding the right spanner for the job’. I gave up. That’s brilliant, actually. A good analogy. Though horrifyingly inaccurate. Did anyone catch the email about the new server space? Seems a bit… limited. I did. It's definitely tight. I’m already concerned about the next big data dump from the ‘Teen Talk’ project. We’re going to be scrambling for room. It's always the Teen Talk data, isn't it? They just  talk  so much. Everything is documented. It’s a researcher’s dream and a server manager’s nightmare. It’s amazing data though, honestly. The shifts in slang are fascinating. Have you noticed the resurgence of ‘rizz’? I saw it used in a academic paper the other day. A  serious  academic paper. Oh god, 'rizz'. It makes me feel ancient. I’m pretty sure I saw someone using it unironically on LinkedIn. The world is ending. LinkedIn 'rizz'? Oh no. That  is  a bad sign. Right, so, lunch plans for Friday? Thinking that new Thai place near the station? Apparently, the pad see ew is phenomenal. Ooh, yes! I've heard good things. Count me in. I need a proper spice fix. Sounds good to me. I’m free. I'm in too. Although, fair warning, I’ll probably order everything on the menu and then complain I’m too full. It’s a habit. You and me both, honestly. Pad see ew sounds amazing. Perfect end to a week of dealing with metadata. It's truly a glorious thing. Okay, pad see ew it is. And a preemptive apology to our stomachs.

…and honestly, the recommendations algorithm on that platform is just… broken. It keeps suggesting me stuff I’ve already watched, or documentaries about competitive cheese rolling. Seriously. Competitive cheese rolling? That’s a niche interest. Though, I did fall down a YouTube rabbit hole of extreme ironing once. Don't ask. Extreme ironing? Right. That sounds… exhausting. It's just, I'm trying to broaden my horizons, you know? I want to watch something internationally acclaimed, something  subtitled , and it just keeps offering me repeats of “Homes Under the Hammer.” Subtitled, eh? Good for you. Trying to embrace other cultures. I tried learning Mandarin for a bit. Utterly failed. The tones… my brain just couldn’t grasp it. Mandarin is notoriously difficult. I attempted Spanish a few years ago. Got to the stage where I could order a beer and ask where the bathroom was. That felt like a success. That’s genuinely useful! Better than anything I achieved with Mandarin. It’s funny, isn’t it? How language learning highlights cultural differences? It’s not just about the grammar, it’s about how people  think . Absolutely. It’s like, some languages even have different ways of conceptualizing time. And I've been thinking about teaching, actually. My uni department asked if I'd be interested in assisting with the first-year undergrads next semester. Oh, really? That’s good, isn’t it? A bit of experience outside your PhD work. You’d be good at that. Remember how patient you were explaining statistical modelling to my aunt at Christmas? She thought a p-value was something you ordered at a pub. That was… a challenge. But yeah, I think I'd enjoy it. It might even make me better at explaining my own research. Which, let's be honest, is something I desperately need to work on. It all feels so… abstract sometimes. I know the feeling. I spent an hour today trying to explain my work on protein folding to my mum. She just kept asking if I was finding a cure for cancer. Oh dear. The pressure! You need to give her a very carefully worded explanation. I tried! Honestly, she's convinced I'm secretly working on something world-changing. I should just let her think that. It makes her proud. Actually, speaking of things academic... are you free next week? There's a talk at the Royal Geographical Society on cultural representations of the Amazon rainforest.

Right, now then, have you managed to get that leak sorted in the bathroom, love? It’s been dripping for a week now, and it’s driving me round the bend. Nah, not yet. I said I would, didn't I? Just haven't had the time with mock exams and everything. It's just a slow drip, isn't it? Not massively urgent. Not massively urgent? It's wasting water, lad! And it’s dripping onto the good floorboards. Those are proper oak, you know. Cost a pretty penny. Your Grandad would have had it fixed in five minutes flat. Aye, he would. Always fiddling with something, your Grandad was. Never a dull moment. Remember that time he tried to fix the television with a pair of pliers? Nearly blew the house up. Don't remind me. Fried the whole system, he did. Took me a week to get a man in to sort it. Said he was 'just having a look.' A look that cost me a hundred quid! He meant well, though. Always did. Now, about that leak… Can you promise me you’ll tackle it this weekend? Alright, alright. I promise. Saturday, definitely. Unless Mr. Thompson decides to give us another three hours of revision. That man's a menace. I swear he thinks we live to do maths. Did you get that shopping list I left you? We're almost out of biscuits, and your Nana is arriving tomorrow. There'll be hell to pay if there aren't digestives. Oh, don't worry about me. I’m not fussed about biscuits. Just happy to be here. Though a nice cup of tea would be lovely. Earl Grey if you've got it. Earl Grey? Fancy. I’ll have a builder’s tea, strong as you like. And a slice of fruitcake, if there is any. Footcake should be in the tin. I made it last week. Though your Grandad ate a good chunk of it while watching the cricket. Said it helped him concentrate. It does. Gives you something to chew on while you’re shouting at the telly. You two are both terrible! Using the biscuit tin and cake as excuses. Now, have you checked the spare room? I want to make sure Nana and Grandad are comfy. Fresh bedding, clean towels… the works. Yeah, it’s all done. I even dusted. Though I think dust just reappears magically.

Oh, look at this one! Remember Sarah’s wedding? We looked so young. And hopelessly jet-lagged, clearly. Oh god, yes. That was…a trip. Flying back from Australia the day before felt criminal. But worth it for Sarah, I suppose. She looked incredible. Is that…is that Ben attempting to do the worm in the background? It absolutely is! Ben always thinks he’s a better dancer than he is. Poor Sarah had to gently steer him away from the dance floor a few times. He really commits though, doesn’t he? Full enthusiasm, zero coordination. It’s endearing, in a way. It’s been ages since we’ve seen them, hasn’t it? Too long. They’re so busy with little Leo now. I keep meaning to organise something, a proper catch-up. But life just keeps…happening. Tell me about it. This marking is relentless. I swear, sometimes I dream in essays. Though, to be fair, they  are  some pretty interesting essays. Some of the students have really grasped the postcolonial theories. That’s good to hear. It makes it all worthwhile, doesn’t it? When you see them genuinely engaging with the material. It's easy to get bogged down in the admin and the endless emails. Absolutely. Though, sometimes I wonder if they’re just trying to impress me. They know I’m a sucker for a clever argument. You  are  though. You love a good debate. Remember that argument you had with Professor Chen about Deleuze? It went on for ages. Don’t remind me. He’s brilliant, don’t get me wrong, but he’s incredibly stubborn. It was like talking to a brick wall. Still, it was a good intellectual workout. It was hilarious to watch, honestly. You were so animated! Speaking of travel… I was looking at flights to Vietnam. Just daydreaming, really. Vietnam? That sounds amazing! We haven't really explored Southeast Asia much. We did Thailand, but that was…well, a long time ago. Exactly. I saw some photos of Ha Long Bay and I just thought…wow. Imagine kayaking through that. And the food! I’ve been craving pho for weeks. Pho…now you’re talking. Maybe when the semester finishes? We could really use a holiday that  isn’t  marking-related. Definitely. Just a little adventure. Somewhere completely different. We could try and meet up with Maya and David while we’re there?

Honestly, my face is  killing  me. I swear, glitter is the herpes of festivals. You just get rid of it and it keeps coming back. Oh my god, that's so true! I'm still finding sparkles in my hair. Did you see Leo last night? Absolutely plastered, trying to explain football to everyone. Oh,  please . Leo doesn't know a corner flag from a condiment. He was just shouting "GOAL!" at random intervals. Though, bless him, he did try to buy a round for the security guards. Classic Leo. Honestly, I thought Maya was going to murder him when he spilled his drink all over her new top. She's been planning that outfit for weeks! She was so stressed about it. Oh, the pink one? Yeah, that was a disaster. She kept dabbing at it with wet wipes. Didn't seem to help much. Speaking of disasters, did you see Chloe trying to flirt with Finn? Oh, god, don't even. It was  painful . She was doing that weird little laugh-snort thing she does when she's nervous, and Finn just looked… confused. He was way more into talking to Sarah about her cat. He likes cats?! I did  not  know this information. My whole world is crumbling. He’s been ignoring my DMs all week. Honestly, he just seems like a cat person, doesn’t he? He was asking Sarah about its diet and everything. Did you eat anything substantial last night, by the way? I just had like, three chips and half a donner kebab. Regretting it now. Literally nothing. I was too busy trying to avoid Leo and the security guards. I had a tiny bit of pizza off Liam’s plate, but he was hogging it. He's convinced he needs to "bulk up" for football season. Honestly, he already looks like a brick wall. He’s been going to the gym every day. It's a bit much. I’m trying to get back into it myself, but I just can't be bothered. All I want to do is lie in bed and eat biscuits. Same. My mum keeps sending me Instagram posts about 'glow-ups' and 'self-care'. Like, Mum, I just want to sleep. She’s constantly asking when I’m bringing a boyfriend home too. Ugh, mums. Mine keeps trying to set me up with her friend’s son.

Right, so have we actually finalised when your mum’s coming? I keep forgetting to ask. We’ve provisionally got the 17th, but I need to double-check with her about the train times. She said she wants to come up on the early train, but those are always a bit… dicey, aren’t they? Dicey’s an understatement. They're perpetually delayed. Remember when your dad tried to come up last year? He ended up getting in at nearly lunchtime. Oh, don’t remind me. He was fuming. He’d planned to help you with the garden. He's a good man, your dad. Always willing to lend a hand. Though, he does have a habit of lecturing me on the proper way to prune roses. He’s a bit of a gardening evangelist, isn't he? Though, to be fair, his roses  are  spectacular. They are beautiful. Still, I can handle my own roses, thank you very much. Speaking of handling things, have you seen the state of young Leo’s FIFA skills lately? He's convinced he's going pro. Oh god, don’t even. He was boasting to me about winning some online tournament, but I suspect he was playing against eight-year-olds. Probably. He's got a bit of a competitive streak, that one. Though, I must say, I’m impressed he’s even interested in football. I was always more of a cricket man myself. Each to their own. Though, all this talk of competition reminds me of that neighbour of ours. Old Mr. Henderson. Honestly, the way he blames everyone else for his overflowing bins… Oh, him? He's a character. He’s always muttering about the council, the foxes, even the  wind  being responsible for his mess. It’s never his fault, is it? Always somebody else. You know, it’s interesting how people avoid taking responsibility. It's a curious thing. It really is. I saw him arguing with little Maisie yesterday, accusing  her  of letting her ball bounce into his garden. She's five! Honestly! Some people have no sense of perspective. It’s a kind of… deflection, isn't it? Passing the buck. Easier to blame someone else than to admit you've made a mistake. Makes you wonder about the bigger things, doesn’t it? Political culpability, for example. Oh, don’t get me started on politics. It’ll ruin my peas and chips.

Right, well, that was lovely wasn’t it? Thanks for coming down, it's good to actually  have  a proper sit-down. Feels like ages. It was really nice. Proper tea and biscuits, the works! Makes a change from instant coffee and a rushed sandwich. Aye, good cuppa. Though, a bit sweet for me, I’m used to just a dash of sugar these days. Everything's getting sweeter, isn’t it? Even the bread. Don’t start on the bread, Dad. You say that every time. It’s just… flavour! And it’s good to see you all, honestly. It’s a bit of a trek down from Essex, but worth it. It is good to have you both. How’s the job going, Sharon? Still… eventful? Eventful is one word for it. Old Mrs. Higgins tried to feed me her dinner yesterday. Said I looked ‘peaky’. Lovely woman, but… you know. And there’s another bin strike looming. Honestly, it's ridiculous. The smell! Oh no, not another one! Brighton’s bad enough as it is without mountains of rubbish piling up. Did you manage to get down to the seafront this weekend? It was surprisingly warm. We walked around the Lanes on Saturday. Found a really dodgy shop selling didgeridoos. Like, a shop entirely dedicated to didgeridoos. It was surreal. Didgeridoos? What in the world for? I have no idea! Just… there they were. Loads of them. And expensive ones, apparently. I wouldn't have a clue. Maybe someone’s trying to start a trend. Though I can’t imagine anyone wandering around Brighton playing a didgeridoo. It’d block up the entire pavement. You’d need a permit for that, I reckon. Speaking of permits, are you still trying to get that water company to sort out the leak? You said it was dripping for weeks. Still at it. Apparently they're 'experiencing high call volumes'. High call volumes because everyone else has leaks! Honestly, it's infuriating. It's like they want us to live in a swamp. You wouldn’t believe how much water we're wasting. It's not as if water is limitless. Back in my day, you’d just call the plumber yourself. None of this automated nonsense. Give a man a job to do and he’d do it. Different times, Dad. Everything's so… layered now. You need a form for a form.

Right, have you checked the football? Any idea how City did? I completely forgot to look last night. Oh yeah! They absolutely smashed it, 4-1 against… um, let me see… Bournemouth. Haaland scored two, obviously. It was a good game, actually. Quite open. Oh, lovely! That's good to hear. It’s just… everything feels a bit grey at the moment, isn’t it? Even here. I think it’s the light. Proper SAD kicking in. This Polish November is  bleak . I know what you mean. It’s not helped by being away, is it? I’m starting to miss proper Sunday roasts. Not the Polish version, lovely as everyone is trying to be… it’s just  different . Exactly! Different isn’t always bad, but sometimes you just need a proper Yorkshire pudding. Speaking of which, how's that new student, the one with the really strong accent? Still struggling? Anya? Yeah, she’s getting there. It’s just the idioms, isn’t it? I tried to explain “raining cats and dogs” yesterday and her face… pure confusion. I feel so responsible, you know? These exams are coming up and I want them all to do well. It's a lot of pressure.
