I can imagine. It  is  a lot. It's good you care, though. You’re a good teacher. It reminds me of helping with that harvest once, back in Cambridgeshire. Felt the same pressure, everything relying on you. Except instead of grammar, it was potatoes. Potatoes are important! Though, slightly less stressful than exam results, I suspect. This coffee’s actually really good, by the way. Have you tried the latte macchiato here? Not yet, I’ve been sticking to cappuccinos. I’ll give it a go. Oh, actually, I just got a message from Sarah. She sent a photo of Winston, my nephew's dog. He's wearing a little raincoat. Aww, that's cute! He looks utterly miserable though, doesn’t he? All those Labradors look perpetually mournful. He does! Bless him. It’s that face. Sarah said he refused to go for a walk until he had it on. Typical Winston. Have you been watching much news? Honestly, it's all so depressing. Not really, I've been trying to avoid it. It’s just a constant barrage of… everything. I’ve been reading a lot instead. Finished that book you recommended, the one about the birds?

Honestly, this event I'm planning next month is going to be the death of me. Three hundred delegates, all expecting five-star treatment, and the venue keeps changing things on me! Sounds stressful. What’s the biggest pain point right now? Is it the catering again? It's the AV, actually. They promised a specific setup, and now they’re saying it’s not possible with the room layout. I spent ages convincing the client this venue  could  deliver, and now… Oh, that’s awful. You’re always so good at smoothing things over, I’m sure you’ll figure it out. Though, maybe you need to start building in a ‘disaster contingency’ budget, just in case. You're probably right. It's just… exhausting. Anyway, enough about work. How's the dating scene been, Leo? Still swiping endlessly? Still swiping. Honestly, it’s a bit grim. Everyone just seems to want Instagram-worthy dates, you know? Like, can we just go for a pint and have a normal conversation without someone taking photos for their story? Tell me about it! I deleted all the apps last week. I was spending more time crafting witty profiles than actually  meeting  people. Good for you, Maya! Seriously. They’re such a time sink. Honestly, I'm starting to think I’ll meet someone randomly, like, queuing for a Greggs. You never know! Though, Greggs is a bold move for a first impression. I saw this  amazing  outfit in Urban Outfitters the other day. Like, a really oversized blazer and wide-leg trousers. I’m trying to justify the expense to myself. Ooh, send me a pic! I’m terrible with clothes. I just stick to black jeans and jumpers, basically. It's efficient. You look good in black, though. Suits you. I’m still wearing the same two pairs of work trousers I've had for about five years. They’re practically part of my uniform. Stop that! You need a wardrobe revamp. We could go shopping next weekend? We’re free, right? Ooh, I might be on call for the event, but I could potentially sneak away for a few hours. We’ll have to see. What are we watching after dinner, by the way? I was thinking that new horror film,  Gloomhaven . Apparently, it’s genuinely terrifying. Ooh, yes! I've heard good things. I’m a bit of a wimp, though, so I’ll probably be hiding behind a cushion.

Honestly, this square is…odd. It’s all these straight lines, isn’t it? Like someone just sliced it out of the city. Not a natural flow at all. Yeah, bit brutalist. Though I quite like the lime trees, actually. They smell amazing this time of year, don’t they? Reminds me of…well, actually, reminds me of China. They had them everywhere. China? You still in touch with those folks you taught over there? The ones who came to visit? Yeah, Wei and Lin. Lin sends me birthday messages on WeChat still. It’s always…complicated. Trying to translate birthday wishes that are culturally specific. They were talking about pandas the other day, naturally. Apparently, they’ve got a new cub. Oh, lovely. Pandas are brilliant. Though I always get a bit uneasy thinking about the wider picture, you know? Bears in China…they’re farmed, aren’t they? For bile. Horrible. It is. That’s…that’s the tension, isn’t it? Incredible landscapes, incredible wildlife, unbelievable food, but then underneath… So, Wei was telling me about travelling through Sichuan province. Apparently, the landscapes are breathtaking. Mountains, forests, all that. Said it’s nothing like the tourist trail. Proper rural then? I tried to do the ‘proper’ rural Devon last year, and honestly, the lanes were terrifying. Single track, barely enough room for a bicycle, let alone a car. And every corner, a tractor coming the other way. It's the same in a lot of China. Though obviously, the scale is different. I’ve never driven there, thank goodness. Train journeys are the way to go. Though getting to the Isle of Wight seems simpler sometimes! Seriously, the logistics… Don't even  start  me on the Isle of Wight. Right, so, Wei and Lin. Still teaching TEFL, are you thinking? It’s a solid option, isn’t it? Particularly with the demand in Asia. Yeah, a few people I know are still doing it. One fella said he's in Vietnam now. Apparently the money’s better. I'm more focused on this research grant, though. Secure that, and I’m good for another few years. God, have you spoken to Professor Davies recently? He's been…difficult. Difficult? How so? Still hovering? Asking to see drafts every five minutes? Worse. Asked me if I’d considered “re-framing my entire methodology.” After six months of work. Six months! Nearly threw my coffee at him.

Right, so are we still on for Friday then? You said you might be working late, didn’t you? Yeah, possibly. It depends if this report gets signed off. Old Mr. Henderson is being particularly… thorough. He's questioning everything, down to the font size. Oh, brilliant. Sounds delightful. Well, if you  are  stuck, just let me know. We can always push it back to Saturday. No, no, I'll make every effort. I promised I’d help you with… what  were  we doing again? The bookshelf? The bookshelf, aye. And then the painting in the hall. It's driving me mad being wonky. Right, the hall. Okay, I can definitely give you a hand with that. I've got that laser level thing, remember? Makes it foolproof. Oh, that'll be amazing. You’re a lifesaver. Honestly, I’ve been staring at it for weeks. It’s just… off. It'll be sorted in half an hour, tops. We can get it done before we go out, maybe? Yeah, that’s a good shout. We could go for that Thai place we were talking about, isn’t it? The one near the theatre? Sounds perfect. They do a wicked Pad See Ew. Oh, I know! I’m craving it already. We haven’t been in ages. It’s been too long. Right, I’m just checking the sat nav. This traffic is ridiculous, isn't it? It's barely moving. Tell me about it. I left an extra twenty minutes early just in case, and I’m  still  going to be late for my meeting. What meeting is that again? The one with the uni people? Regarding the corpus? Aye, that’s the one. They want to go over the metadata and the tagging. It’s all a bit… dry, to be honest. But it’s important. I bet. Still, you’re brilliant at that sort of thing. All that meticulous detail and coding… it’s beyond me. It’s alright. It keeps me busy. Gets me away from wonky paintings, at least. Fair enough. Okay, looks like we’re starting to move again. Just another ten minutes, should be there. Do you want me to put some music on? Oh, yeah please. Something upbeat. I need a boost before facing the academic scrutiny. Right. Let's see… how about some Arctic Monkeys? Perfect. You know me too well. Now, don't you dare start questioning the font size of my playlist though.

Honestly, I feel like I’ve been run over by a bus. This cold is proper awful. You look it, lass. Proper pale. Should’ve wrapped up warmer yesterday, shouldn’t you? Even with the sun, it was a proper nip in the air. You always underestimate the Cambridge chill, don’t you, Chloe? It sneaks up on you. I mean, it’s practically the sea here. I thought I was alright! I had a coat on! It’s just…it’s hit me proper hard. And I’ve got that conference next week… I can’t be ill next week. What’s it for? Another fancy dress one, is it? Remember that medieval one? The outfits people wore… No, thankfully not. It’s for the university, a sustainability thing. Lots of academics, potential sponsors…it needs to go well. Sounds stressful. You coping alright with everything then, besides the plague? How’s…Ben? Oh, Ben. That’s… complicated. He’s being… distant. Again. Distant how? Like, “I’m going to the pub with the lads” distant? Or “I’m avoiding eye contact and pretending you didn’t just speak” distant? Honestly? The second one. He’s been really quiet. Barely says two words to me. And he’s been on his phone constantly. I asked him about it and he just said he was “busy”. Busy doing  what , though? Hmm. Textbook avoidant behaviour. Has anything specific happened? An argument, a disagreement… Not that I’m aware of. That’s what’s so annoying! I’ve been racking my brain to try and figure out what I’ve done wrong. I even asked his mum, but she said she hadn’t spoken to him much lately either. Blimey. That  is  odd. He’s usually glued to his mum’s hip. Maybe he’s just stressed about something at work? Has he mentioned anything? No. He works at that warehouse, doesn’t he? I can’t imagine it’s  that  stressful. It can't be. Don’t underestimate warehouse stress, love. It’s long hours, heavy lifting…plus his gaffer's a right grumpy git. I heard him shouting at young Liam the other day just for asking for a break. Still, completely shutting you out? That’s not fair. You deserve better than that, Chloe. Have you tried just… sitting him down and asking him directly what’s going on? Like, a proper, serious conversation?

Honestly, the week has been… a lot. I need a holiday. Or a new job. Maybe both. Oh no, what’s happened? Spill. Is it still Mark being… Mark? Worse. It’s Sarah. She’s… she’s broken up with Ben. Apparently, it was pretty messy. No way! Sarah and Ben? They seemed so solid. What happened? Apparently, he was messaging another girl from accounts. Sarah found out on his phone. Classic, right? The whole office is buzzing. It's awful because everyone really liked Ben, but… yikes. Oh, that’s brutal. Poor Sarah. She always seemed so happy, though. I can’t believe Ben would do that. He always struck me as being… sensible. Sensible? That’s… optimistic. He’s always had a bit of a wandering eye, apparently. Everyone’s tiptoeing around her at work, trying not to mention him, but it’s just so awkward. I had to present a project update  with  him this morning. It was excruciating. Oh god, that sounds awful. Did you… say anything? Just kept it strictly business. Short and sweet. I felt so bad for her, but also I didn’t want to get involved. It's a workplace drama bomb waiting to explode, you know? I just wanted to escape to my desk and pretend it wasn’t happening. Totally. Workplace break-ups are the worst. Speaking of work, I had a really difficult patient today. He was… incredibly distressed. It took hours to de-escalate things. It just really got to me. Oh, that sounds exhausting. You’re such a good nurse, though. You always handle things with so much compassion. But you have to look after yourself too, you know? You can't take all that negativity home with you. I know, I know. It’s just… hard. Sometimes it feels like I’m just absorbing everyone else’s pain. And then on top of that, my manager is being completely useless about staffing levels. We’re constantly short-staffed, which just adds to the stress. Ugh, managers. Mine's the same. She spends more time in meetings about meetings than actually  doing  anything. Honestly, it’s like she actively avoids making decisions. It’s so frustrating when you’re trying to get things done. It’s the absolute worst! It feels like you're banging your head against a wall. So, how are you coping? Besides avoiding Sarah and her ex-boyfriend?

So, the thing about dragons isn’t  always  that they’re bad, you see. It depends on the story. Some dragons are really clever and help people. Like Toothless? Exactly! Like Toothless. He was a really good dragon, wasn’t he? But in a lot of old stories, they’re guarding treasure, and they’re scary and breathe fire… and that’s because they’re trying to protect something important. But they  eat  people! In the books at school! Sometimes, yes. But even then, it’s usually because someone tried to steal from them. It’s a bit like… if someone came and tried to take all your Lego, wouldn't you try and stop them? Yes! I’d shout! Exactly! And the dragon is just being protective. It’s like, good and evil aren’t always… clear cut. They’re messy. What about the Green Man? Miss Henderson told us about him. Is he good or bad? Oh, the Green Man! That’s a really old story. He’s… complicated. He’s the spirit of the forest, the wild places. He isn’t good  or  bad, he just  is . He reminds people to respect nature. If you respect the forest, he's happy. If you hurt it, he can be… well, he can be a bit grumpy. Grumpy like Grandpa when you wake him up too early? A little bit like that, yes. He’s a powerful force. And that’s what lots of these old legends are about, understanding those forces and living with them. So dragons aren't always mean and the Green Man isn’t always angry? That’s right. Sometimes things aren’t as simple as they seem. It’s all about looking at things from different points of view. Now, who wants toast? I'm making some. Me! With jam! And sprinkles! Can I have sprinkles? Okay, okay. Toast with jam  and  sprinkles. But only because you’re both very good at thinking about difficult questions. Now, go wash your hands. And maybe while we’re eating, we can talk about other legends? I know a great one about a mischievous little fairy… Yes! Tell it! Tell it! Yesss! Fairy! Alright, alright! After hands are washed, then fairy tales. I’m washing my hands now! Me too! Super fast! Good, good. That’s my clever pair. Now, get going. I’ll get the toaster on.

So, how was the filming trip today, Lily? Did you have a good time? It was REALLY good! We went to the museum, and they let us dress up as Romans! I was a centurion! A centurion, eh? Very impressive. Did you get to poke anyone with a pretend spear? No! Miss Davis said no poking. But I had a shiny helmet! That sounds brilliant. Leo, did you enjoy it too? It was okay. I wanted to be a gladiator, but they didn’t have enough gladiator costumes. I was a peasant. A peasant is important too! Someone has to grow the food for the centurions. Absolutely. Did you learn anything interesting? We learned about how they built the roads, and about Boudicca! She was a really fierce queen! She certainly was. Right, I’m off to the gym. Thinking of attempting the treadmill. Wish me luck. I haven’t done one in… well, a long time. Oh, brave you! Don’t push yourself too hard. Remember what happened last time? Let’s not talk about the aching legs. I’ll just stick to a gentle walk, maybe. Though, that new donut shop opened near the gym… it’s tempting. Doughnuts?! Can we get doughnuts after school tomorrow? Yeah! With sprinkles! We’ll see. Perhaps if you both behave yourselves and finish your homework. Speaking of behaving, Leo, are you sure your leg is feeling better? You were limping a bit earlier. It’s a little bit sore still. I bumped it on the table in the classroom. Oh, poor darling. Did you tell your teacher? Yep. She put an ice pack on it. Right, well I better get going before the gym gets too packed. It’s still pretty warm out, isn’t it? Even in the evenings. I hope we don't have another heatwave. It is unusually mild for September. Still, I’m glad the nights are cooling down a bit. It was too hot to sleep last week. Can we have a duvet tonight then? The thin one? Yes, we can. You’ll be snug as a bug. Right, you two, homework time soon. And Leo, try not to bump your leg again! Alright, wish me luck with the treadmill. And try not to spend all your pocket money on doughnuts! See you later. Have fun at the gym! And don't think about the doughnuts too much!

So, how are things with the knee? Still giving you gip? Oh, it’s a right nuisance, honestly. Best days are when it’s dry, you know? Damp gets right into it. I’ve been trying those glucosamine tablets, but can’t honestly say I’ve noticed a huge difference. More expensive wee, that’s about it. That’s the downside of those, isn’t it? Emptying the wallet faster than your bladder. Seriously though, have you spoken to the doctor again? Maybe a stronger painkiller? Yeah, saw him last week. Said it’s just “wear and tear.” Lovely. As if I didn’t already know that! Offered me a referral for physiotherapy, but the waiting list is…well, you know. Months. I’d sooner just hobble on, to be honest. I hear you. The NHS is stretched to breaking point, isn’t it? Speaking of stretched, did you see that horrifying result for the Green Party in the local elections? Honestly, I thought they’d finally make some headway. Did not. Shocking, is it? Bit of a kick in the teeth. I thought more people would be waking up to the environmental crisis. Seems they’re more worried about bin collections. Exactly! Shallow as a puddle. Though, I suppose when people are struggling to make ends meet, environmental concerns tend to take a backseat. Old Man Hemmings retired from the builders, you know. Apparently, they’re struggling to find someone to take over his team. Really? Hemmings was a good builder. Reliable as clockwork. It's tough finding good tradesmen these days. All chasing the money, none wanting to do a proper job. Tell me about it. My roof needs looking at, and I’m dreading the hassle. Still, at least it gives me something to put off. Sounds about right. I’ve been meaning to clear out the garage for months. Thinking of doing a boot sale, get rid of some of this junk. Good idea! You always find some treasure at boot sales. I picked up a lovely little teapot last month for a quid. A quid! You and your teapots. Speaking of finding things... how’s things with Carol? Still seeing her regularly? Oh, Carol. It’s…complicated. We’re taking things slow. She’s been through a lot recently, you know, with the divorce. It’s hard for her. Yeah, I can imagine. It's never easy, is it?

Honestly, I’m convinced my fiddle leaf fig is actively plotting my demise. It’s just  drooping . Despite everything. I’ve rotated it, misted it, talked to it… the whole shebang. You’re giving it the full therapy treatment, then? They are dramatic, aren't they? Mine just sits there, judging me silently. It’s a snake plant, though, so it’s basically built to withstand nuclear fallout. It’s judging me too, I swear. I think it’s mocking my lack of green fingers. And it’s expensive! I paid a fortune for that thing. It’s a status symbol, apparently. Which is ridiculous. Everything is a status symbol these days. Even having a functional bank account, probably. Speaking of which, have you sorted out that ISA yet? The deadline for the allowance is looming. Oh god, that’s right. I keep meaning to. It’s just… numbers. They make my brain hurt. I'd rather obsess over the foliage situation. Is it greed, or is it genuinely sensible to be hoarding money like that? Sensible, mostly. It’s future-proofing. Although, honestly, with the way things are going, I’m starting to think burying it in the garden is a more secure option. Remember when everyone was saying Trump would never win? Don't even go there. I’m trying to have a nice evening. It’s scary that someone like that could even  get  anywhere near power. It just feels so… absurd. It's like the whole world's gone mad. It is. It really, really is. Though, I heard his legal fees are absolutely astronomical. Serves him right, really. Siphoning off all that money just to avoid accountability. Good. Maybe he should spend less on lawyers and more on, I don't know, basic human decency. Anyway, let’s talk about something less soul-crushing. What are you wearing to the conference dinner next week? I’m stressing. Oh, that. I’m just going to wear a suit. I’ve got a dark blue one that fits alright. No point overthinking it. You? I’ve been scrolling through ASOS for hours. There’s this lovely jumpsuit but I’m worried it’s too… much. It’s bright green. Bright green? Bold choice. You pull it off. You always look amazing. You're sweet. I just don't want to look like I'm trying too hard, you know?

Honestly, the students this term are… something else. I had one genuinely ask me if Plato was a real person. A  real  person! Oh, you’re joking. I wish I was. And another one tried to argue that all historical interpretation is inherently subjective, which, fine, a valid point for a seminar, but this was in a first-year introductory lecture. A first year! They’re getting younger, aren’t they? Or maybe just bolder. I had a student accuse me of perpetuating patriarchal structures because I assigned a reading by a male author. Oh, good grief. That’s… a lot. I find myself spending half the lecture just clarifying basic concepts. It’s exhausting. At least it's a change from the endless essay crises. Remember last year with the plagiarism? Vaguely trying to block it from my memory. It felt like a full-time investigation. Though, thinking about investigations, did you see that documentary about the squatters in London? Briefly. Is it any good? It was fascinating, actually. They were incredibly resourceful. Re-wiring electricity, building little gardens… it was almost admirable, even if completely illegal. It made me think of that awful programme ‘Homes Under the Hammer’. They’re always finding dodgy electrics and damp. It’s horrifying. I think those shows glamorise property speculation a bit too much. Anyway, speaking of resourcefulness, you remember Blue Peter badges? Oh, absolutely. The holy grail of childhood. I desperately wanted one. I sent off so many applications, meticulously collecting bottle tops and foil, but never got one. I got one! One glorious, shiny Blue Peter badge. For a painting of a killer whale. A truly terrible painting, looking back. Mostly blue, naturally. A killer whale? Ambitious. I was aiming for a simple paper plate model of a spaceship. Apparently, that wasn't badge-worthy. Speaking of things that are slightly terrifying, have you noticed how violent children’s TV is now? Even the cartoons! It's awful. I was watching  Paw Patrol  with little Leo the other day and even that had a tense chase sequence involving a runaway train. A runaway train! For preschoolers! Where have all the lovely, gentle art programmes gone? Lost to the algorithms, probably. Everything’s about drama and conflict now. Though to be fair, I'm pretty sure even  Blue Peter  had its fair share of near-disasters. Remember the exploding volcano kits? Oh, don't remind me.

…and then young Timothy, bless him, decides to paint the dog. With glitter. Honestly, glitter everywhere! Took me hours to get it out of Buster’s fur. Glitter, eh? Nightmare stuff that is. Gets into everything. Reminds me of when Elsie decided to decorate the kitchen with flour. Thought she was a baker, she did. More like a blizzard, covering everything. Sounds like you’ve had your hands full over the years, both of you. My lot are a bit more…contained. Though, I’m eternally explaining the concept of homeostasis to a fourteen-year-old who thinks it’s a trendy skincare brand. Homeo-whatsit? Honestly, the things they learn in school these days! When I was at grammar school, it was all proper English and sums. No fancy science mumbo jumbo. Proper sums, that’s what we needed. Not this new-fangled math, where they don't even teach you your times tables. Elsie’s granddaughter, she's struggling somethin’ awful. Said she needs a calculator just to add up ten and five. It’s a shifting landscape, isn't it? They’re trying to focus on problem-solving rather than rote learning, but it feels like the foundations are missing sometimes. I’ve got a student who can explain the theory of relativity, but can’t balance a chequebook. Relativity! Goodness me. All sounds awfully complicated. I remember Arthur trying to manage that hostel down by the seafront. Now  that  was complicated. Every Tom, Dick and Harry turning up needing a bed, all sorts of stories. And the state some of them left the kitchens in! Hostels. Good money to be made, I suppose. My brother, Harold, he ran a little engineering workshop after the war. Always grafting, building things. He could fix anything, that man. Cars, washing machines, anything. Sounds resourceful. My grandfather was similar. Had a little corner shop in Birmingham. Always working, always providing. Long hours. It was tough back then, but they were a hardworking lot. Hardworking they were. My mother, she ran a little sweet shop. Remember the smell? Sugar and boiled sweets. And the abattoir down the road… not such a pleasant smell, mind you. Though, Arthur used to get his meat cheap from there. Abattoirs. Always a bit grim. Old Man Hemmings had one out near Costessey. They used to say he knew every animal by name. Strange, that. Though, you needed good food back then.

So, you were a recruiter before this, right? That’s quite a jump to lecturing, isn't it? Yeah, a pretty massive one, actually. Six years in recruitment. Corporate recruitment, mostly. Headhunting, the whole shebang. It paid well, honestly, but… it was draining. Soul-crushing, sometimes. I can imagine. It always struck me as a very…results-oriented profession. Not much room for nuance, I’d have thought. Exactly. Everything was about filling the role, hitting the targets. People were just… commodities, really. I felt awful about it, quite often. I started doing a Masters part-time, just to have something else to focus on, and that’s when I realised I wanted to be  in  academia, not just supplying it with bodies. Smart move. So, what did you recruit for? Mostly finance and accounting. High-end stuff. Investment bankers, CFOs… the types who think the world revolves around them. You wouldn’t believe some of the demands they had. One guy insisted his office had to face directly north for feng shui reasons. Oh, my goodness. You're kidding! I wish I were. And the egos… Don't even get me started. This job is much more rewarding, even with the marking. Speaking of which, I’m currently wrestling with assessing academic literacy on the lecturer course. Oh, that’s a tricky one. How’s it going? Honestly? It’s a mess. Some of them are brilliant, naturally gifted writers. But others… it’s like they’ve never written anything longer than a tweet. They just don’t understand the conventions of academic writing. Paraphrasing is a complete mystery to some of them. It’s astonishing, isn't it? You’d think, being lecturers themselves, they’d have a grasp of it. You’d  think . But they’re experts in their subject matter – history, engineering, whatever – not necessarily in  how  to communicate that knowledge effectively in an academic context. I’ve had papers submitted with direct quotes used as entire paragraphs. No citation. Nothing. Oh, that's… bold. Have you had to give some pretty harsh feedback? A lot of it. And it’s hard, because you don’t want to crush their confidence. They're already feeling vulnerable putting their work out there for scrutiny. But you also can't just let poor scholarship slide. It sets a bad example for their students, doesn't it? Absolutely. It's a very delicate balance.

Right, so you’re saying you’ve never actually  been  to Blackpool? Never. Sounds… intense. All the arcades and donkey rides and… well, everything. Intense is one word for it. Chaotic is another. It's a sensory overload, honestly. You  have  to go sometime. It's a rite of passage, being from around here. I'm still getting used to the ‘rites of passage’ here. Everything is so different from Mumbai. No one tries to sell you anything on the beach! Mumbai? Oh, are you new to the uni? I don’t think I’ve seen you around before. I’m Aaliyah, by the way. Hi Aaliyah! I’m Priya. Moved here just last month for my Masters in Environmental Science. It’s…cold. You get used to it. Sort of. I’m Liam. And this is Chloe. Hello! So, Environmental Science, that's brilliant. We need more people sorting out this mess, don’t we? Priya: Exactly! Back home, the pollution is… dramatic. I wanted to learn the best practices here and hopefully take them back. That's amazing, Priya! What did you study for your undergrad? Botany, mostly. Lots of fieldwork. Now it’s all lectures and… books. And trying to decipher the northern accent. It’s a challenge! Hey! What’s wrong with our accents? It’s charming. Honestly. It’s just… direct. No beating around the bush. Direct is putting it mildly! My nan once told a shop assistant they needed to “pull their finger out” when they were being slow. Oh, that’s brilliant! My grandma just sighs a lot. Passive-aggressive sighs of judgement. Mine just comments on how much weight you’ve gained. It’s a loving gesture, apparently. Oh wow. Indian grandmothers are…very different. They just want to feed you everything. Constantly. It’s a sign of affection. Same! My Nani would literally chase you around with a plate of samosas. You couldn't escape. Actually, talking of food… anyone fancy grabbing a coffee and a biscuit? This library air is making me hungry. Ooh, yes please! I could really go for a chocolate digestive. Priya: That sounds lovely! I haven’t tried a chocolate digestive yet. Is it…digestive? Oh, you’re in for a treat. It’s definitely…more than digestive. It’s a whole experience. Come on then, let’s go fuel up!

Honestly though, seeing that documentary about the Falklands… it’s just… bleak. All those lads, so young, sent clear across the world. Yeah, it’s awful isn't it? My grandad was in the Navy, not the Falklands specifically, but he never really talked about it. Just…distant, you know? You could tell it stuck with him. Exactly! Like, they’re glorified in films sometimes, all heroic and stuff, but it’s just… trauma, really. Proper trauma. Have you seen that new Top Gun film? Oh, yeah! It was… fine. Visually stunning, obviously, but a bit… much? A bit like a recruitment advert dressed up as a blockbuster. That’s exactly what I thought! It felt… unearned? Like, nobody’s facing actual consequences. It’s all just… stunts and swagger. Makes a mockery of the real thing, doesn't it? Totally. Speaking of things that feel a bit… hollow, I’ve been trying to find a decent magazine lately. Everything’s just endless lists of things to buy. Oh, tell me about it. I used to love those fashion magazines, but now it’s all influencers and fast fashion. It’s exhausting. Remember  Smash Hits ? Now  that  was a magazine.  Smash Hits ! Oh my god, the posters! I used to cover my entire bedroom wall in them. Remember the free cassette tapes they’d give away? Oh, the tapes! Hours of my life were spent recording over those with stuff off the radio. Speaking of old stuff, I’ve been trying to get my old computer working again. Seriously? What, like a proper ancient one? Pretty much. It's a dinosaur. I just want to play some of those old games again, you know?  SimCity 2000  mostly. Pure nostalgia. It’s refusing to recognise the hard drive though. Ugh, computers. They’re the bane of my existence. I spent three hours on the phone with IT at work yesterday trying to get the projector working for a presentation. Three hours! Oh, that’s brutal. IT people… they speak a different language, don’t they? All jargon and condescension. They’re actively trying to wind me up, I swear. Anyway, have you managed to book those cinema tickets for Friday? For that new Wes Anderson film? Yes! Got them for the 7:30 showing. I thought that would be a good time, give us a chance to grab some food beforehand. Perfect. I’m starving just thinking about it.

Honestly, the state of dating apps right now is… a disaster. It’s just endless scrolling and everyone’s photos are clearly five years old. Tell me about it. I matched with someone last week who described himself as “outdoorsy” and then admitted his idea of the outdoors is sitting on a balcony with a cigarette. Oh, that’s brilliant! My last date was… an experience. He spent the entire time complaining about the government. Like, I get being politically engaged, but it wasn’t exactly a vibe. Ugh, the political monologues. It's a classic. It's like, can we just talk about… anything else? What music do you like? Have you seen any good films lately? Speaking of films, I’m trying to get funding for this short I’ve been writing. It’s a bit…dark. Deals with racism in the north, subtle stuff, you know? Really trying to avoid being preachy. That sounds amazing, honestly. Really important stuff. Have you had much luck with funding? Nah, not really. They always want something… easily digestible. Want a “feel good” story. But those stories aren't always  real , you know? It’s infuriating. Everything feels so sanitized lately. Like everyone’s afraid to say anything remotely challenging. Honestly, sometimes I think London's bubbles are the worst. Oh god, yes. My cousin’s coming up from London next weekend. She’s already started asking about “cool, underground” places to go. Like, honey, you’re in Sheffield. It’s already pretty underground. Exactly! They think anything outside the M25 is a rural wasteland. I’m visiting my parents next month - dreading the inevitable questions about my career. "So, are you seriously still an architect? Is that a  stable  job?" Oh, the parental interrogation. Been there. My mum keeps trying to set me up with the daughter of her friend's dentist. Apparently, she's a “lovely girl.” Oh no. The dentist’s daughter. That's a whole other level. Right? I’m thinking of just lying and saying I’m engaged to someone incredibly unsuitable. That’ll shut them up. That’s a bold move. I like it. What are you both doing next week anyway? I was thinking we could check out that new indie cinema. I’m free most of next week. Sounds good! I need a film to distract me from the endless application forms. I’m  still  trying to find a proper job.

So yeah, the flat's pretty small, isn’t it? But it’s ours, and it’s in a good location. Close enough to Brighton for a day trip, but quiet out here. Small is good. Less to dust. Though, you two seem to fill it with… stuff. More stuff than you need, if you ask me. Dad! We like our things. And it's cozy. It’s very nice, dear. Very modern. Though, I do feel a bit lost without a proper kitchen garden. All those spices… a bit much, aren’t they? I stick to salt and pepper, myself. Well, I do a lot of cooking. Trying new things. The kitchen's the heart of the flat, really. Though, yeah, maybe a bit cluttered. I've been meaning to sort through the drawers… Drawers, eh? That's where all the lost socks go. And spare batteries. And the things you 'might need someday.’ He’s not wrong. We’ve got a drawer full of phone chargers for phones we haven’t owned in five years. You should take those to a recycling centre. All this plastic… it’s terrible. I’ve started taking my own bags to the shops, you know. They look at me funny, but it’s the right thing to do. Good on you, Mum. We try to recycle as much as possible. Though, honestly, the council makes it so difficult. Different bins for everything. It's a nightmare. Councils are all the same. Taking your money, promising the world, delivering nothing. Speaking of money, how are you two managing? Still teaching, are you? Yeah, still at the language school. It’s… alright. Not brilliantly paid, but it keeps me busy. I'm finishing my Master's. It's a lot of work, and a lot of stress, but it'll be worth it. Hopefully. A Master's degree! Fancy that. I left school at sixteen. Factory work was more important then. Though, I always regretted not staying on. Don’t fret about that. You did what you had to do. My old man never saw the need for education. Said it wouldn't put food on the table. Ended up working on the docks his whole life. Hands like sandpaper. It's different now, isn't it? You really need a degree to get anywhere. Even a basic job. It seems that way. Though, I've seen a few youngsters with degrees, working behind the counter at Tesco.

Honestly, the internet was dreadful at my mam’s last week. Absolutely dreadful. She was trying to Facetime my nephew and it kept cutting out. She was fuming. Said it was the router, but I reckon it's just the whole system down there. It’s ancient. Yeah, rural broadband is…optimistic, at best. We were talking about it at work. Apparently, they’re finally rolling out some better stuff to some of the villages, but it’s taking  years . And it’s expensive. It’s a joke. You pay the same as someone in Cambridge for a connection that barely loads a webpage. How are people supposed to work from home or anything? It’s not fair. Work's been alright though, busy as always. The new undergraduate applications are flooding in. Endless checking and verifying. Ugh, sounds…thorough. I’m swimming in reports at the moment. Site investigations, soil analysis, the whole shebang. It’s good work, genuinely, but the sheer volume is a bit overwhelming. Though, better that than being out on site in  this  weather. It's chucking it down back home, apparently. Oh aye? It's a bit grey here, but not too bad. Though, they were saying it’s going to get colder next week. Proper winter chills, apparently. Trying to convince myself that the central heating bill won't be astronomical this year. It feels like everything is going up! Tell me about it. I was looking at house prices in Kent again, just… having a nose. Absolutely insane. A tiny little terraced house in Tunbridge Wells is going for half a million. It's ridiculous. How are people ever going to get on the property ladder? It’s a scandal, honestly. My cousin’s trying to buy in Newcastle, and even there it’s crazy. She's been saving for years, and it's still looking like she’ll need help from the bank of mam and dad. Which is just… sad. It is. It just feels like the goalposts are constantly moving. Speaking of things that are expensive, I tried making sourdough bread last weekend. Disaster. Utter disaster. Oh no! What went wrong? Everything. The starter wouldn't activate, the dough was like concrete, and it ended up looking like a hockey puck. I just ended up ordering a pizza. Oh dear. Sourdough is notoriously difficult. I tried once, and it was a similar story.

Honestly, this shift was  mental . Old Mrs. Higgins decided she was a mermaid again, and insisted on being wheeled to the window to "call her pod." No way! Seriously? You get the best stories, don't you? It's way more exciting than writing ad copy for dog food. Tell me about it. I had to deal with Mr. Peterson today. He swore his tea was poisoned because it tasted “too orange.” It was just a bit of lemon. Oh, bless him. My nan does that sometimes. Thinks everyone’s trying to swap her biscuits. Speaking of, did anyone see Sarah’s photos from the party on Saturday? Oh, the one at The Swan? I saw a few. Looked… lively. She really went all out with the decorations, didn’t she? Lively is an understatement! I heard Mark tripped over the fairy lights and took out half the buffet. Classic Mark. He always was a liability, that one. Still, good on Sarah for throwing a good party. I’m starting to feel ancient just hearing about it, though. I was in bed by ten! You deserve a lie-in! You work so hard. How’s little Leo doing? Still obsessed with dinosaurs? Utterly. He spent the entire morning roaring at the postman. Apparently, the postman was a “big, scary T-Rex.” It's exhausting, but adorable. It flies by, honestly. They grow up so quickly. Little Emily's started asking about the dentist already. I'm dreading that appointment. Oh, that’s the worst. I remember being terrified. Mum bribed me with a Barbie doll. My mum just threatened to tell Father Christmas. Worked a treat. Speaking of, have you heard anything from Auntie Carol? She said she was going to call about her hospital appointment. No, not yet. I texted her earlier, just checking in. She’s been having trouble with her knee, hasn't she? Says the doctor’s being useless. Oh, that’s awful. Sometimes you just need a doctor who actually  listens , you know? Mine’s brilliant, thankfully. Always takes the time to explain everything. You're lucky! I haven’t found a decent GP since I moved. Keeps trying to push me towards online consultations. What’s the point in that? Exactly! You need to be seen, especially if you’re actually unwell. What are your plans for the summer, by the way? Any holidays booked?
